content.text: The urban environment in Berlin is a concept for analysing older residential areas. In older residential areas of the inner city areas, often with urban planning measures (renovation, new construction, modernisation etc.) without guaranteeing the security or improvement of the living conditions of the inhabitants. As far as the urban areas are concerned, where social and spatial conditions are closely intertwined, changes in the residential areas that relate to the spatial dimension must fail in social policy terms. The work therefore develops a proposal on how the social-spatial conditions of such districts can be adequately described and from this strategies of renewal can be derived. Essential milieu properties are recognizable in characteristics of the district history, the use structures and local social relations. They can be examined primarily with the help of qualitative methods of social research. Analyses of this kind can be used in the context of the rehabilitation and construction planning as well as social work and a newly understood municipal cultural policy. The guide for an empirical examination of the subject of milieu context is led by interviews and groups of the Berlin authors.
content.title_en: Urban environment: a concept for analysing older residential areas

content.text: Civil Service Conservativeism and Modernization : Studies on the Prehistory of the Conservative Party in Prussia 1810 - 1848/49. Klappentext: The beginnings of the Conservative Party in Prussia lie in the first half of the 19th century, in the period between reform and revolution (1810 - 1848). Different concepts of modernization for the state and society lead to fractionation processes within the ruling bureaucracy in these decades. The present investigation follows the efforts of the conservative civil service faction to secure the decisive position of power both internally and externally. Almost casually, important impulses are given that contribute to the constitution of the conservatives as a party during the period of revolution.
content.title_en: Civil Service Conservativeism and Modernization : Studies on the Prehistory of the Conservative Party in Prussia 1810 - 1848/49

content.text: Model studies of the variability in the flow system of the European North Sea. Processes are taking place in the European North Sea which play an important role in the climate system of the ocean and atmosphere. For example, the European North Sea serves as a sink for the northward heat transport in the North Atlantic. The warm Atlantic water flowing through the Greenland-Scotland ridge into the European North Sea is cooled down strongly there. Together with other processes, this can increase the density of the water to such an extent that deep water is formed. This water flows through the Framstraße or over the Greenland-Scotland ridge again from the European North Sea and forms an important component of the deep water in the North Polar Sea and North Atlantic. The northward heat transport in the European North Sea serves as a heat source for the North Polar Sea and the Barents Sea, thus making the spread of the ice cover to the south more difficult.
content.title_en: Model studies on variability in the European North Sea flow system

content.text: Enlightenment and technology: Basic problems of an ethics of technology. In detail, the work tries to explain a concept of application-oriented ethics in the concreteization of the project of Enlightenment for technical development. A limitation to the normative principle level is criticized as well as the new naturalism, which is not least represented in Hans Jonas' principle responsibility. By considering the control problems of modern, functionally differentiated societies, the social-theoretical sterility of the current ethics discussion is to be avoided. By discussing the institutionalization of the technology evaluation, the work aims at possibilities of indirect control, which avoids the front position according to the motto "The economy develops, the state prohibits" as far as possible already in the approach.
content.title_en: Education and technology: basic problems of a technology ethics

content.text: Gas chromatographic and mass spectrometric analysis of organic substances in Elbe, flushing field and groundwater. From the preface: This dissertation examines the influence of the flushed-up harbour sediment with its high cargo of various organic substances on the occurrence and distribution of lipophilic ingredients of adjacent water bodies (stau, ground and surface water) in Hamburg's Elbe March using the example of Hafenschlick-Spülflächen: Moorburg-Mitte, Ellerholz, Moorburg-Ost, Francop, Feldhofe, Kirchsteinbek.
content.title_en: Gas chromatographic and mass spectrometric analysis of organic substances in Elbe, rinsing field and groundwater

content.text: The basic prerequisite for a targeted urban development policy is knowledge of the relevant socio-economic determinants of urban development and the spatial development trends.In order to determine the main causes of the different demographic and economic growth of cities, an overview of the determinants of the economic development process of cities is given.In addition, individual partial analytical explanatory approaches from the economic theory are presented and examined for their insight into an operational theory of urban development.In the main part of the study, a theoretical-empirical analysis of the determinants of urban development potential, the entrepreneurial location and the investment activity of the municipalities is carried out.For 57 major cities of the Federal Republic of Germany, the structural and development differences existing in the period 1950 to 1970 are presented and analysed quantitatively and analysed using statistical data on the natural and spatial population movement, the commuter volume, the labour market participation, the job and production structure, the municipal tax power and debt, as well as on location and structural factors.
content.title_en: Socio-economic determinants of urban development

content.text: Architecture as a symbolic fall: the steamer motif in architecture. Klappentext: The avant-garde among the architects of the 1920s was the steamer motif symbolizing a social utopia. At the same time, the model of form and the form of living fascinated it as a multi-layered symbol. The fact that and how it came to the image of failed hope illuminates the decay of an architectural language in which society should recognize itself.
content.title_en: Architecture as a symbolic fall : the steamer motif in architecture

content.text: Employment policy with sustained low economic growth: an analysis of the employment effects of low growth rates in the longer term and possible economic policy compensation strategies. From the introduction: In view of the rather subdued growth prospects for the economy of the Federal Republic of Germany, the question arises from the economic point of view, which effects a longer-term weakened economic growth would have on important economic objectives and which scope for manoeuvre economic policy has to compensate for possible negative effects. In this work, a partial aspect of this problem is highlighted: the consequences of a longer-term slowdown in growth for employment and employment policy are discussed.
content.title_en: Employment policy with sustained low economic growth: an analysis of the employment effects of low growth rates in the longer term and possible economic policy compensation strategies

content.text: The civil law assessment of human research. Klappentext: Human research is at the intersection of social, ethical and legal problem dimensions. The interdisciplinary study analyses the social relationship of researchers-proband, shows its specific distribution of interests, power and benefits and transforms the findings of the civil law experiment contract with specific primary duties. The work then concreteises the general obligation of protection of the researcher, among other things, in the enlightenment, deception and voluntaryness of the subject.
content.title_en: The Civil Law Assessment of Human Research

content.text: Calculation and interpretation of nut-boiled extruders. From the summary: The design of extruder screws has been a central topic of plastics processing for many years, in which the methods of theory and practice have been little supplemented. This work presents a self-contained design system for nut-boiled extruders, in which all criteria of screw design can be calculated. These are throughput behavior, performance requirements and homogenization capacity. The influence of geometry and material data on the process parameters can be calculated using analytical and approximate equations. The basis of the equations are physical analytical model concepts, which lead to realistic statements with the sum of the minimum possible simplifications. With this work, nut-boiled extruders can be optimized; this is discussed as an example and pointed to the implementation of a proposed procedure methodology in a calculation program. This could help to bridge the gap between mathematically analytical models and an exclusively empirical interpretation methodology in the future.
content.title_en: Calculation and design of grooved extruders

content.text: Reading motivations and readings among pupils: theoretical basics and empirical findings. "What is the starting point for what to read and continue reading under what circumstances?" - For this question, the author develops an action-theoretical motivation model that understands "reading" as an "instrumental act" that is directed towards multi-layered objectives. In an empirical pilot study, the author addresses two aspects of his model of action and motivation: a) Purposes of reading generally in contrast to other leisure activities and b) Expectations systems towards texts («psychological text types»). One of the didactic and pedagogically relevant results of his pilot study: reading is assigned the "status of a above all rational activity" as school is becoming increasingly school-time, "that attracts little emotional energies".
content.title_en: Reading motivations and readings among pupils : theoretical basics and empirical findings

content.text: The central and peripheral city centres have been concerned with spatial planning and spatial research for more than a decade. State and municipal action in the context of spatial development was primarily directed towards this area of tension. Problems of district and district centres, however, were only little noticed. Nevertheless, they are particularly important in ensuring the supply and housing quality of the inhabitants of urban regions. This work follows these problems and shows in particular the effects of individual determinants of the development of the centre over time. In order to overcome the usual isolated approach, the author developed a life cycle model of centres, which was presented in the theoretical part of the work and was often reviewed in the empirical part. On the one hand, status quo analyses and forecasts with this compacted presentation were given a special significance. On the other hand, for the practitioners of urban planning and development, action requirements can be derived from this from the various departments of the city centres and from the various departments of the city.
content.title_en: Centre development in single-core metropolitan regions

content.text: Computers and verbal data: opportunities for the innovation of social science research techniques. Qualitative research methods have become increasingly attractive over the last decade; in particular, in the interview, open approaches are increasingly used in data collection. However, the techniques for the evaluation of verbal data have not developed to the same extent; there is still no method canon that finds general recognition. The large extent and lack of structuring are the characteristics of this type of data. Can the computer be used effectively here? In this work methods and concepts for computer-assisted evaluation are developed, which are based on methodological and theoretical considerations in the context of the understanding sociology in the tradition of Max Weber. The connection of qualitative and quantitative analysis methods and a controlled method of type formation are the focus of the presentation.
content.title_en: Computers and verbal data: opportunities for innovation in social science research techniques

In this work landscape images are inventoryed nationwide, explained and their possible dangers analyzed. The results of this study are intended to provide information data for future planning as well as to represent a contribution to discussion about goals and methods of nature and landscape protection. Example area: Wittgensteiner Bergland (North Rhine-Westphalia).
content.title_en: Characteristics, potential danger and need for protection of landscapes of the Federal Republic of Germany

content.text: The aim of this publication is to automate part tasks of assembly planning such as the program development for industrial robots or the assembly-oriented design of components. First, the planning task is structured. Various model formations are discussed, which are suitable for developing the joining process - as an example of an assembly process - and the connection to a common optimum. Finite element simulation and object-oriented experiment are selected as suitable models, numerical optimization methods as suitable methods of process development. Methods and models are provided to the planner in a "development environment for automated assembly processes". With the tools created, joining processes for a flexible assembly cell are optimized in terms of different target criteria. The connections to be manufactured are designed in an appropriate manner.
content.title_en: Computer assisted development of flexible automated assembly processes

It should be applicable for the frequently encountered case where no drainage observations are available and therefore models that include a structural identification are not eligible. All data necessary for the determination of the flood peak discharge should be derived from topographic maps and precipitation data, which are assumed to be given.

content.text: The education of the good mother: medical-educational instructions for motherhood in the 18th century. In the process of shaping and spreading the specifically modern norm of maternality, medicine plays a decisive role: In the second half of the 18th century, academic medicine and approved doctors developed a program for the education of the mother to legitimize and control their behaviour towards their children. Only in this process does the idea of motherhood prevail as the central female principle of life and become the mother universally responsible and responsible for her biological infant. In the medical advisory literature for the >> mothers of the moral and educated states << < and in the obriginal state writings of >>Medical policy < < with their unique interweaving of medicine, pedagogy, philosophy and state science, the doctors formulated and propagated the social image of the >> good mother <<< . Although the doctors initially only addressed the numerically small group of women from the upscale bourgeoisie, but with the enforcement of the bourgeois family ideal, this good mother became the ideology and the guiding image for the <> women of all layers.
content.title_en: The education of the good mother : medical-educational instructions for maternity in the 18th century

content.text: Numerical methods of solving the transmission problem in special billiards and their application to the construction of quantum cascade lasers. The physical modelling of semiconductor lasers leads via the Maxwell equations to a 2-dimensional transmission problem, in which a solution of the Helmholtz equation inside a limited area with wave number n k and in the exterior a solution with wave number k is sought, so that both solutions are continuously differentiated over the edge. In this work a predictor-corrector algorithm is presented, which allows, in contrast to previous methods, to calculate all self-values in a given area directly, successively and efficiently, so that the development of search strategies as with previous algorithms becomes obsolete. The procedure relies on a margin-negral discretization of the respective Helmholtz operators, whose discretization errors in the calculation of the own functions or self-values are exponentially smaller. When the initial area is surrounded by a billiard curve, which is described by a family of p-periodular quadrbels, the two of these solutions are described by the binoculars.
content.title_en: Numerical methods for solving the transmission problem in special billiards and their application for the construction of quantum cascade lasers

In this work, the so-calculated surface-barriers phenomenon is investigated for hydrocarbons entering silicate zeolites. Using molecular simulation methods (transient and equilibrium molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo, reactive flux simulations) and comparison to experimental data from literature, conditions (systemic, thermodynamic, and chemical) were identified and determined.

content.text: The liability of intermediaries in international intellectual property law: specifications and limits of territoriality principle and land-based protection. The book deals with the liability of intermediaries from the point of view of international private and civil procedural law. The focus is on the question of which law decides on cross-border situations, as typically arise on the Internet, the liability of the intermediary, which enables an infringement of intellectual property rights by providing a platform or access service. Based on the requirements of the principle of territoriality in material property law and the land-based connection of protected areas and their limits, the requirements of Union law and the material law design of various forms of liability for the possibility of infringement of intellectual property rights in German, French and US law, an independent connection of the liability of intermediaries, which leads to the application of a foreseeable law, is advocated for the liability of the intermediaries

content.text: The so-called reading space barrier (§ 52b UrhG) is intended to enable libraries, museums and archives to make their analogue collections digitally available. It is based on the European Information Directive and was only implemented in 2008 in the German Copyright Law.The author comprehensively examines the reading space barrier, as it is difficult to handle in application practice and is highly controversial in science. Moreover, the ECJ has only recently decided on the scope of reading place privilege.Because the current legal situation does not meet the basic need of education and science for a modern information supply, alternatives are to be identified and a solution proposed for the next copyright reform is to be formulated. In this context, the plans of the Federal Government to introduce a general education and science barrier will also be taken into account.
content.title_en: The reproduction of works in electronic reading stations

content.text: The work examines in detail the need and legitimacy of a right to protection of public service for press publishers. In the sensitive field of public information, the creation of an exclusive right requires an in-depth examination because of the resulting reduction in the freedom of information. The study is intended to contribute to the debate on the right to protection of public service for press publishers by revealing their dogmatic foundation. It builds on the arguments put forward by the advocates of the new right to protection of public service. At the same time, the work comments on the results of this study, the drafts presented during the debate, including the draft government, which should thus provide impetus for the continuation of the debate even after the completion of the legislative process.
content.title_en: A right to protection for press publishers

content.text: The price-cost squeeze in European competition and national postal law. The work examines price policy measures that lead to so-called price-cost squeezes, for the first time according to both symmetric and asymmetric competition regulation standards. Concrete reference areas are European competition and national postal law.The author examines in detail the question of the method to be used in determining a price-cost squeeze against the background of the feedback effects and interdependence resulting from this context. It is shown that this question has to be answered differently in the relevant reference areas, due to the more intensive use of the sector-specific postal regulation. Since the battles for price-cost squeezes are currently being fought both before the BKartA and before the BNetzA for the postal sector, the practical relevance of the mentioned method discussion will continue to increase in the near future.
content.title_en: The price-cost squeeze in European competition and national postal law

content.text: From »oikos« to cyberspace: the private in political philosophy Hannah Arendt. Why are our data and private things worth protecting? This question arises especially in times of the fourth industrial revolution, the Internet of Things and political change. Julia Maria Mönig shows that Hannah Arendt's concern to preserve the private is necessarily, from her understanding of the ancient household to the violation of informational privacy in totalitarianism, providing insight into current debates - for example, about cyberbulbing. The book is aimed at philosophers as well as data protectionists and privacy researchers from various disciplines as well as all who are concerned about the future and present of democracy. Hannah Arendt 2.0 - This book links Hannah Arendt`s understanding of the personal with the current debate about the protection of data and privacy in the digital age.
content.title_en: From »oikos« to cyberspace : the private in political philosophy Hannah Arendts

content.text: Intensity of feed processing: influence on nutritionaldigestibility; performance and health of food. Therefore, the effects of mixed feed with different technical treatment methods on nutrient digestibility and animal health were tested in two pig fattening trials. The results showed a feed component-dependent increase in nutrient digestibility by increasing the digestion rate of the feed. However, positive effects in fattening performance were largely based on the avoidance of feed waste. By physical-chemical changes in feed by treatments, characteristics of chymus were changed, which in addition to the risk of stomach lesions are influenced by the intestinal immune system.
content.title_en: Intensity of feed processing : influence on nutrient digestibility, performance and health of growing-finishing pigs

content.text: Performance on creative and routine tasks : the role of context. This dissertation deals with behaviour during and after performing routine and creative tasks in different contexts. While research on routine tasks in experimental economic research is very advanced, there are hardly any studies on behaviour in creative tasks. One reason for this may be that economics is generally more focused on the final result, which results from a creative creative process than on the underlying innovative processes and achievements. Another reason could be that traditional research methods, such as empirical studies in the field of creativity research, can only be used for limited purposes. However, the process of creative thinking itself is of immense importance for the creation of innovation and therefore deserves more scientific attention. In psychology, creativity has long been researched on the basis of field and laboratory experiments. Field experiments offer a high external validity, but on the other hand, they are very costly and usually require sustainable cooperation between private companies and academic institutions. However, laboratory experiments are a promising alternative to field experiments. Although these experiments enable the researchers to perform less efficiently in the field, they also have a more extensive control over the field experiments.
content.title_en: Performance on creative and routine tasks : the role of context

content.text: The administrative act as a form of action for the award of contracts and concessions. The administration has various forms of action available to it to carry out its tasks. In the area of procurement, according to the express wording of § 103 para. 1 GWB, the applicability of the procurement law depends on the existence of a "remunerated contract". The study examines whether, in addition to the form of the contract, the administrative act can also be used. In this respect, both procurement law and administrative law questions arise. Against this background, the author analyses the possibilities of designing a procurement management act and describes for four selected procurement sectors whether and under what conditions administrative acts can trigger the applicability of the procurement law consequences.The investigation is directed at all parties affected by the procurement law. Public clients and potential bidders benefit from reading as well as lawyers and the award chambers and Senates.
content.title_en: The administrative act as a form of action for the award of contracts and concessions

content.text: Software tools for the phase and domain-wide design. This work contributes to improving software support in early stages of product development. Two problem areas were identified and worked on in particular. On the one hand, it is a phase-wide design concept for motion systems based on a bidirectional linking of product features in models of different abstraction levels. On the basis of this solution, a process was developed that allows the manipulation of CAD models in VR environments. On the other hand, a software tool was designed that allows a domain-wide modeling and simulation of heterogeneous systems. On the other hand, thanks to the component-based software architecture it is expandable to any domain and related calculation methods. In contrast to existing domain-wide tools, it offers user-centred access to the product model, which takes into account domain-specific representations and concepts. The development of both concepts was accompanied by a software-technical implementation that proves their feasibility and allows a demonstration of their working methods using different application examples.

content.text: Exploitation of music rights: a copyright study on the way of use, using the example of reproduction in the online field. Progressive harmonisation versus traditional rights exploitation: The exploitation of music rights is subject to a constant change, which the European legislator increasingly and with particular attention to the exploitation in the online area. Music rights are no longer licensed by collective and from one source via collecting societies, but increasingly repertoire-related and separate in reproduction and performance rights. In particular, the major Anglo-American music publishers are pioneers here, who license their reproduction rights directly to online music services. According to German law, it is above all disputed whether the reproduction for subsequent public access (so-called upload) constitutes an independent way of use which can be licensed independently from the law of public access.
content.title_en: Exploitation of music rights : a copyright study on the way of use using the example of reproduction in the online area

content.text: Laser spectroscopy of uploaded bismutations for the test of quantum electrodynamics. The work deals with a test of quantum electrodynamics in strong fields with the help of laser spectroscopy of the basic state hyperfine structure of uploaded bismutations. The experiment was carried out and evaluated at the ESR storage ring of the GSI Helmholtz Center for Heavy Ion Research in Darmstadt. Space charge effects were systematically investigated and the wavelength measurement of the laser was verified by absorption spectroscopy of iodine. Ion speed determined by an in-situ measurement of the electron cooler voltage could be reduced by more than one order of magnitude the greatest systematic uncertainty of the previous experiment. This showed the necessity of establishing a permanently installed high voltage measurement on the electron cooler, which was advanced in the context of the work. The specific difference determined from the measured wavelengths deviates so significantly from the theoretical prediction that none of the investigated systematics is considered a cause of the deviation. In addition to doubts about the values from the theory, the literature value of the magnetic core moment of bismut-209 is cited as a possible cause and illustrated in the forecast, how this puzzle could be solved in the following experiments.
content.title_en: Laser spectroscopy of uploaded bismutations for quantum electrodynamic testing

content.text: The work develops an approach to empirically capturing long-term media effects. By reconstructing media effects from the subjective perspective of the recipients, access to media effects phenomena that have not been studied so far becomes possible. The study also contributes to research on media and collective memory. The qualitative application study investigates the often neglected question of the effects of television representations of the Holocaust on the recipients. The results show the importance of television from the point of view of different age groups for its mental and collective representations of the Holocaust. The book is of interest to communication scientists as well as to scientists interested in the field of media memory.
content.title_en: Long-term media effects from the perspective of recipients : on the importance of television for mental and collective representations of the Holocaust

content.text: The political construction of irregularity in Germany and South Africa: a comparison of access to legal residency and public health care. What factors and actors determine the access of migrants to legal residence in Germany and South Africa? And what does illegality of residence mean for the accessibility of public health care in the two countries? State sovereignty is not only reflected in the enactment of laws and the rights of migrants defined in it, but is also dependent on policy implementation processes. The present book extends the regional focus of migration research to the present and places South Africa at the centre of interest. The comparison clearly shows the factors and actors determine the access of migrants to legal residence in Germany and South Africa. And what are the characteristics of legal regulations, existing resources, municipal political engagement and cooperation networks called state and non-state actors as examples of the existing law and the outcomes of the migration policy.
content.title_en: The political construction of irregularity in Germany and South Africa : a comparison of access to legal residency and public health care

content.text: Non-consent genetic diagnostic investigations: Analysis of the criminality § 25 para. 1 no. 1 GenDG. The present study deals with the criminality of non-consent genetic investigations. The focus of the work is the analysis and evaluation of the criminality created by the Gendiagnostikgesetz in 2010 § 25 para. 1 no. 1 GenDG. -- The author deals with the legal situation before the act enters into force and then looks at the new criminality of the GenDG in the overall structure of the normation. The work is devoted to the individual criminality of genetic investigations and analyses for medical purposes. The subject is also comprehensively considered the special dangers that exist during a foreign-country examination. The new criminality is used to treat general problems of consent theory and the law of criminal application. -- The topicality and relevance of the subject of genetic investigations and the associated dangers for the general personality right are already hardly to be underestimated and are still worth increasing with progressive research in the field of human genetics.
content.title_en: Non-consent genetic diagnostic investigations : Analysis of the offence § 25 para. 1 No. 1 GenDG

content.text: The dream of sleep in the 20th century: knowledge, optimising fantasies and resistance. Sleep: the subject of myths, stories and images for millennia. Man sleeps a good third of his life. The time we spend in sleep is an unconscious, unproductive and inactive time, but also a life-necessary and longed for time. How does a society in which scientific understanding, rationality and efficiency play a central role deal with such a stubborn phenomenon as sleep? Hannah Ahlheim's study of the development of "sleep-knowledge" in Germany and the USA since the late 19th century consistently combines the history of a science with the history of modern society. It shows that not only the image of the sleeping body, the dreaming soul or the dreaming brain has become another. Work with continuous machines, soft boundaries between day and night, advances in science, the development of synthetic sleeping aids and the experiences of war have led to new demands on the everyday organization of sleeping and promoted the fear of losing sleep.
content.title_en: The Dream of Sleep in the 20th Century : Knowledge, Optimization and Resistivity

content.text: The contribution of the Nursing Time Act to the better compatibility of care for relatives and work. With the Nursing Act, the legislator reacts to demographic change in Germany. Unfortunately, the implementation has largely failed and causes the legal user to break his head. So what contribution does the massively criticized law actually make to the better compatibility of work and care for relatives? Is the legislator, for example, shot above the target by the introduction of special notice protection for workers-like persons? These questions are examined and examined on the basis of the open legal questions and weaknesses, how the regulations fit into the system of existing regulations of labour, social and civil law. content.text: The belief in the great in modern architecture: large structures of the 1960s and 1970s. Large structures are a distinctive architectural heritage of the second half of the 20th century and are always highly controversial. Complexes such as the Ruhr University Bochum, the Klinikum Aachen or the Nordwestzentrum Frankfurt still divide the spirits. But the belief in the great is a constituent element in the architecture of modern societies. Large residential settlements, shopping centres, universities for thousands of students, conference centres or hospitals around the world testify to this as typical building tasks. The buildings became large as whole cities and should function as efficiently as machines. Three dominant concepts for the giants emerged: large-scale form, construction system and megastructure. This new book for the first time systematically presents the theory discourse on large structures. It opens up new perspectives for dealing with the much-mowed inherited giants and impressively shows how current debates on building on a large scale are today.
content.title_en: The belief in the great in the architecture of modernity : large structures of the 1960s and 1970s

content.text: Investigation of the behaviour of thermoresponsive polymers on electrodes in interaction with biomolecular systems. This work deals with the production and characterization of thermoresponsive films on gold electrodes by fixing an already synthesized thermoresponsive polymer. The basis for the development of the responsive interface was three different copolymers (polymers I, II and III) from the group of thermally switchable poly(oligo(ethylene glycol) methacrylates). The turbidimetric measurements of the copolymers in solutions have shown that the turbidity point depends on the pH value, the presence of salts and the ion strength of the solution. After characterization of the polymers in solution, experiments of covalent coupling of polymers I to III to the surface of the gold electrodes were carried out. While in polymers I and II the coupling was based on an amide bridge, in polymer III a photoinduated connection was chosen simultaneously with the connection of the crosslinking process.
content.title_en: Investigation of the behaviour of thermoresponsive polymers on electrodes in interaction with biomolecular systems

content.text: Virtualization of consulting services: The basics of digital transformation in corporate consulting. Megatrend digitalization is fundamentally changing companies. The result is the far-reaching virtualization of services, processes, organizational structures as well as entire business models. Business consulting supports their clients in advancing virtualization and exploiting associated potential. Some business consulting companies have already recognised that virtualization is strategically important for their own business model and services offered. In this dissertation, the author analyses the developments in this still diffuse field and constructs tools to support business consulting in the digital transformation process. For example, well-founded information on the state of research and practice is also the subject of his research, as well as factors for analyzing the virtualization potential or for selecting suitable technologies. In order to achieve equally relevant and rigorous results, business consultants and clients were interviewed in qualitative and quantitative studies. For example, a large-scale empirical study with the German Business Consultants Association (BDU) e.V. was conducted in order to determine the importance of virtualization today in research and in business consulting, which barriers to the use of virtualization are now understood by the business and the business.
content.title_en: Virtualization of consulting services : Basics of digital transformation in consulting

content.text: The optical system integration and function integration of optical components are being discussed in addition to micro-electronic, mechanical and fluid components. The optical system and function integration provide the necessary tools in the form of concept and optical design approaches as well as manufacturing processes. The focus of this work is on the research of innovative methods for the realization of highly functional integrated, miniaturized and robust optical free-beam systems. By folding the beam path, an interesting compromise of system size and functionality can be achieved for many applications. As one of the central challenges in the optical design of such systems, the present work addresses both established and innovative methods for the start-up system finding in detail. From theoretical considerations it is clear that optimal performance of folded optical systems can often only be achieved with complex surface profiles that are different from rotational symmetry. The integration of additional optical functions is further enhanced. In order to meet the increasing technological requirements of integrated optical systems, the optical processing process can be achieved in a wide range of applications.
content.title_en: Innovative methods for optical system and function integration

content.text: Influence of the electrophonon interaction onto electronic transport in metals. The present work combines the influence of the electron-Phonone (E-Ph) in the influence of the electron-Ph on the electrical conductivity and the thermopower. The calculations are carried out using ab initio methods based on flat waves and pseudo potentials as well as the influence on the transport properties are discussed using a model system. It is shown that the electrical conductivity decreases while the thermopower increases. Furthermore, an expansion of the electronic states is to be observed.
content.title_en: Influence of the electron-phonon interaction onto electronic transport in metals

By combining the highly electron-poor tetraazaanthracene with diarylamin donors, very narrow band gaps (energy gap between the highest occupied and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital) of 0.7 eV can be generated. The combination of the azaacene with 4-aloxythiazoles leads to dyes with NIR absorption and low LUMO energies from up to 4.8 eV are associated with a single-dose fluorption-resparability.

content.text: Photoelectron spectra with quantum trajectories beyond the plain dense field approximation. The strong field approximation (SFA) is used to calculate photoelectron spectra (PES) in the field of strong laser-matter interaction. We investigate various extensions of this theory to analyze features of PES beyond pure SFA. We consider systems in which additional forces influence the emitted electrons. Appropriate methods are derived and used for the calculation of PES. These are compared with numerical solutions of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation or PES from literature and analyzed by quantum trajectories. We investigate different extensions of that to analyze specified areas beyond the sphere of the dimension of the dimension of the dimension.
content.title_en: Photoelectron spectra with quantum trajectories beyond the plain strong-field approximation

content.text: Stress-related work analysis of clinicians in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. The working conditions at 18 clinics in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern were investigated, resource and stressor prevalences were recorded and compared with age, subject area and gender. Doctors felt less participation than doctors. Younger doctors were more exposed to stressors and felt less resources than older doctors. Special divergences did not exist. Among the strongly pronounced stressors, particularly time pressure, uncertainties in work and bureaucracy were mentioned. Resources, especially social support, were well developed.
content.title_en: Stress-related work analysis of clinicians in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern

content.text: Personal branding on social media : predictors of self-presentation and relationship management of German academics. The disintegration of traditional working structures distinguishes today's society and has led to the need for proactive attitudes towards one's own career. Against this background, the study examines how scientists use social media for professional self-presentation and networking. The study, bundled under the term Personal Branding, investigates this question and also investigates possible determinants of the use of social media for personal branding. The idea of social capital and the impression management theory form the theoretical basis of the study and provide a model with the determinant of personal branding. The study showed that the use of social media for professional self-presentation and networking is related to personal, social and environmental factors. However, the use appears to be more of static information presentation than of dynamic interaction.
content.title_en: Personal branding on social media : predictors of self-presentation and relationship management of German academics

content.text: Targeted influence of the liquid deterrence in the heat treatment of metallic components by means of previous turning. In this work a novel approach to the influence of the groove-like surface structure of the heat treatment material on the deterrent kinetics in evaporating liquids was investigated. It was shown that the specifically inserted surface structuring can significantly influence the deterrent kinetics. The main reason for this is the rapid local cooling of the groove tip. Surface structures with deep grooves and materials with low thermal conductivity are of advantage. The orientation of the groove structure is important.
content.title_en: Targeted influence of liquid deterrence in the heat treatment of metallic components by means of previous turning

content.text: The characterization of gravity waves and tides from LiDAR measurements in the middle atmosphere. The investigation of atmospheric waves is of great importance for understanding the circulation in the atmosphere. The day-to-day LiDAR in Kühlungsborn provides continuous time series of temperature profiles or relative density profiles in the middle atmosphere depending on the weather. The challenge in data analysis was to explicitly separate heavy waves and tides. In this work, various parts of the heavy wave spectrum were characterized in terms of their year-end and during an exceptionally long 10-day measurement. <ger> The knowledge of atmospheric waves is crucial to our understanding of the circulation in the Earth. Depending on the weather conditions the daylight capable Rayleigh-Mie-Raman lidar at Kühlungsborn provides continuous time series of temperature and relative density profiles between 30 and 75 km altitude in the yard yard and mid-range separately.
content.title_en: Characterization of gravity waves and tides from LiDAR measurements in the middle atmosphere

content.text: The time of prevention: being modern means to be able to perform prevention. Starting in the age of enlightenment until the recent past, the common history of prevention and modernism can be demonstrated by the history of the emergence and interdependence of the two genealogical studies. The study, which is based on the example of disease prevention in Germany (and beyond), shows how our culture has learned to treat potential health damage as current problems in the future. To this end, the two dominant cultures of prevention in the age of enlightenment are examined. While dietetics tried to contribute to the formation of a preventive self-relationship, the Medicinalpolicey laid the foundation for public health policy. Individual and population-related prevention forms were still comparatively unconnected at this time. The analysis illustrates, by means of the categories of infectious disease, social pathology and hereditary disease, that only in the years between 1848 and 1945 a systematic connection between individual and collective health was established. In addition, the realignment of biopolitical governance after the Second World War is discussed, in the consequence of which the restriction of individual freedom rights was increasingly perceived as a problem-free- to the use of the term of prevention.
content.title_en: The time of prevention : a genealogy

content.text: Risks of social media and user-generated content: social media stalking and bullying as well as data protection issues. The topics of internet-based crime in the context of social media and the topic of data protection are currently not only highly controversial in terms of legal policy, but also have a considerable practical relevance. The author takes into account the dogmatic aspects of a criminal classification of social media stalking and bullying. On the other hand, she is dedicated to the data protection requirements in the creation of user profiles and subjects the current legal situation to a critical consideration. content.text: Theologically conservative: Studies on genesis and concerns of the evangelical movement in Germany. In contrast to previous studies, Jörg Breitschwerdt develops the genesis of the evangelical movement not only in connection with the Bultmann controversy since 1941, but also places it in a wider context. In particular, the view of the theological debates of the 19th century provides astonishing theological and structural parallels. What were the theological concerns of the "theologically conservative" movements of both centuries and how can they be systematized? Breitschwerdt makes it clear that the evangelical movement is better understood in the context of a "theologically conservative" movement that emerged in comparison with a "modern theology" which emerged primarily through the development of the historically critical method during the 18th century. As an isolated phenomenon of the 20th century, the evangelical movement cannot therefore be seen as an increasingly visible phenomenon. The study contributes to the conservativism concept of the profane history (Valjavec, Epstein, Kondylis) to make it fruitful for church history and to be increasingly observed.

The comparative study of the existing terminology complements the comprehensive analysis of the development of the ecosystem approach in global and regional international law with reference to the Northeast Atlantic. Links to the law of the sea and the organ practice of the United Nations are shown. At European level, the focus is on the Marine Strategy Framework Directive. Of particular relevance to manufacturers, distributors and especially consumers is the problem of the extent to which the handling of the e-cigarette entails criminal consequences. Practical importance for consumers is gained by the steaming of the e-cigarette within the framework of the non-smoking protection and occupational safety law. content.title_en: The e-cigarette in the focus of criminal law

content.text: The principle of purpose limitation in data protection laws : the risk-based approach, principles, and private standards as elements for regulating innovation. The work examines the principle of data protection in relation to purpose retention from the perspective of research into innovation in the field of legal science. The purpose limitation principle therefore not only protects the autonomy of the data subject, but also leaves sufficient scope for processors to implement protection in the context of their innovation processes. In this sense, the processor's obligation to specify the purposes of processing is to be regarded as an instrument of preventive protection. It aims to identify specific risks arising from the processing of data for the fundamental rights of the data subject at an early stage. In contrast, the requirement that subsequent processing should not be incompatible with the original purpose is aimed at controlling the additional risks arising from subsequent processing. This interpretation approach shows a way of effectively protecting the data subject from the risks of data processing, but also enables processors to use the compliance with the regulatory advantage of innovation as a competitive advantage.
content.title_en: The principal of purpose limitation in data protection laws : the risk-based approach, principles, and private standards as elements for regulating innovation

content.text: A parallel algorithm for computing the flow complex : theory and applications. We present a parallel algorithm for calculating the Hasse diagram of the flow complex of a point cloud in Euclidean space. Known algorithms in two and three dimensions first calculate its geometric realization and must first calculate the Delaunay triangulation. Our algorithm only calculates the Hasse diagram of the flow complex, which, provided with sufficient geometric information, enables the same topological multiscale analysis as the alpha-shape filtration. We show with experimental results for medium dimensions that our algorithm scales well with the number of available cores on a multi-core architecture. We use our algorithm to sketch the carrier of a probability measure on the basis of points drawn from the Euclidean space. Furthermore, we apply our algorithm to scatter diagrams, which are used for correlation analysis, but are also a useful tool to understand the distribution of high-dimensional point clouds.
content.title_en: A parallel algorithm for computing the flow complex : theory and applications

content.text: Monitoring of offshore liability arrangements : Investigation into monitoring of liability and cost-sharing arrangements for the grid connection of wind turbines at sea. "Monitoring of offshore liability schemes" examines the compensation mechanism that applies to the delay, disruption or maintenance of the grid connection of offshore wind farms and its monitoring. Offshore liability schemes protect offshore wind farms against investment risks and limit the liability risks of transmission system operators who are obliged to establish and operate the interconnection lines. The compensation payments finance the last consumers via an offshore liability levy. The private-law support scheme is carried out by the beneficiaries themselves and is therefore vulnerable to conflicts of interest. Using a principal agent consideration, the work examines whether the arrangements are adequately monitored to ensure the protection of the last consumers against excessive levy payments. On this basis, it develops ways of improving the future design of transfer mechanisms.
content.title_en: Monitoring of offshore liability arrangements : study on monitoring of liability and cost-sharing arrangements for the interconnection of wind turbines at sea

content.text: Lévy hybrid models : modeling, valuation, calibration. Abstract: This thesis deals with hybrid modeling of stock and interest market in a common model environment. Two models are developed that are driven by independent inhomogeneous Lévy processes. They allow the valuation of stock, interest rate and hybrid options. A performance basket, a portfolio of stocks and bonds, is explicitly evaluated in both models. Both models allow an excellent adaptation to real market data. The calibration was carried out in two different model configurations.
content.title_en: Lévy hybrid models : modeling, evaluation, calibration

content.text: The management power of spatial planning: the example of acceptable conflicts in wind energy planning. The thematic access, content and intensities of spatial planning have considerably expanded in recent years. Spatial planning can now directly influence the building capacity of a land and determine the inability/admissibility of a space-significant outdoor project.This does not lead to demarcation issues within the overall planning, but also puts the property right and its constitutional requirement at the centre of the consideration. Sufficient planning appropriations are necessary. Wind energy use and its acceptance conflicts are engines of the intensification of spatial control access. Acceptance is a dazzling concept that has not been classified as legal until now.
content.title_en: The steering power of spatial planning: using the example of acceptable conflicts in wind energy planning

content.text: Optimization of technological parameters for minimizing the formation of 4-vinylbenzene (styrol) during the brewing process while preserving the typical aroma of wheat beer. This dissertation developed a minimization strategy for styrene in wheat beer. For this purpose, besides styrene, phenolic flavourings as well as the overall aroma were investigated, as well as the influence of each brewing process step on the formation of styrene and phenolic flavourings. Last, malts were investigated, the source of the precursors of styrene and phenolic flavourings. By selectively affecting the malting parameters, a styrene reduced wheat beer with high levels of phenolic flavourings could be produced.
content.title_en: Optimization of technological parameters to minimize the formation of 4-vinylbenzene (styrol) during the brewing process while preserving the typical aroma of wheat beer

content.text: This work deals with the questions whether rules of procedure (of the Executive Board, the Supervisory Board and the Annual General Meeting) are reserved for associations alone or can also use partnerships of such as content they have and who ultimately has the right to set up the organisation. Based on the law of the stock company, the registered association, the GbR, the OHG, the KG and in particular the eG are also taken into consideration.
content.title_en: The grounds for application and the limits of the rules of procedure of company law

content.text: The "conversion ban" as a border of non-contractual cooperation in the EU. The increasing tendency of European policy to move away from a single Europe in which all Member States move together has reached its preliminary peak with the "Brexit". For a strong and sustainable Europe it is therefore all the more important that the Member States set uniform European law within the Union treaties and not agree on international treaties outside the Union treaties, as last happens with the Fiscal Treaty. Its analysis clearly shows the problem that a threat to Union law does not arise per se through the individual international treaty in accordance with the law of the Union under international law, but can only result from a large number of international treaties. The author examines the effects of this cumulative approach, which has not yet been taken into account in the legal literature and offers concrete solutions to the limitation of a legal idea from cartel law.
content.title_en: The "conversion ban" as a limit of non-contractual cooperation in the EU

content.text: The work concerns the legally dogmatic and practically interesting institute of confirmation of countervailable resolutions of general meeting pursuant to § 244 AktG. First, the conditions of confirmation are explained. The confirmation presupposes that the decision of the final decision is countervailable, that a confirmation decision is taken and that it grows in force. Afterwards, the confirmation effect is discussed. In the work the thesis is represented that the confirmation – contrary to the h. M. – is equipped with a material-legal retroactive effect. This is based on legal dogmatic reasons, however, has practical consequences. In this context, the possibility of annulment of the decision of the final decision for the time before the confirmation decision according to § 244 S. 2 AktG. In the third part of the work the application of the confirmation in the registry law (registration traffic and release procedure) is analyzed.
content.title_en: Confirmation of countervailable resolutions

content.text: The processing of body substances into autologous tissue products according to § 950 BGB. Human trachea or heart valves from the laboratory are no longer mere future music. Research groups have already succeeded in producing these complex tissues from human body cells within the framework of the so-called tissue engineering and successfully implanting humans. Generally, the production of patient-owned cells is aimed at, since after implantation of the tissue there is no repulsive reaction of the body.The production of human tissues can lead to a legal acquisition of ownership of the manufacturer according to § 950 BGB. However, when the patient-owned cells are used there is a conflict between the resulting property of the manufacturer and the patient's personal right. The work first examines when the requirements of such acquisition of property are met.
content.title_en: The processing of body substances into autologous tissue products according to § 950 BGB

content.text: Development and characterization of dyes as probes for the determination of the solvent properties of molecular and ionic liquids. The dissertation deals with the characterization of solvent properties by means of spectroscopic methods. The dye N-methyl-6-oxyquinolone used was characterized by UV-vis, fluorescence, IR spectroscopy and DTF methods. From solvent-dependent studies, evaluation routines were developed using spectral signatures to determine solvent polarity and acidity. To improve the handling in ILs, a novel IL with implemented dye was synthesized, fully characterized and the application was proven as probe.
content.title_en: Development and characterisation of dyes as probes for the determination of the solvent properties of molecular and ionic liquids

content.text: Structural and kinetic investigations of the zeolite collapse. This work is dedicated to the study of the zeolite collapse, taking into account two main aspects. First, the question is examined whether the amorphised zeolite represents an approximation to the perfect glass according to the Kauzmann paradox. This cannot be approached as much as possible on the classical way of undercooling a melt, so that the amorphization of a highly symmetrical crystalline structure is an interesting alternative. However, it can be shown that the completely xenophobic end phase in its structural properties corresponds to a classical melted glass. Since the collapse process of Greaves [1] is postulated as two-stage, the second question is the existence and nature of the first phase of transition. As a decisive step, the general multi-stage of the collapse process can be seen with the help of molecular dynamics simulations and fluorescence investigations on Eu3+-exchanging zeolite.
content.title_en: Structural and kinetic studies of the zeolite collapse

content.text: Reflexive interaction - extending peripheral interaction by augmenting humans. The concept of reflexive interaction is presented as a specific manifestation of peripheral interaction. It is conceivable that a reflexive interaction can be performed without significant cognitive effort as a secondary task, while allowing the user to perform tiny interactions that are shorter than microinteractions without proving the main interaction channels of the primary task. To underpin the proposed concept, series of research studies were conducted that exploit our sensory and motor skills. <ger> The concept of a reflexive interaction is presented, which can be seen as a specific cognitive response of Peripheral Interaction. In contrast, a reflexive interaction is defined to be executed at a secondary task with involving substantial cognitive efficiency, while affecting the user tiny, the smaller the impossible of the microinteraction.
content.title_en: Reflexive interaction - extending peripheral interaction by augmenting humans

content.text: Analysis of the energy flows of biogas plants and development of efficiency parameters for energy plant fermentation. The operation of biogas plants does not meet the requirements of a power plant process. Thus, uniform evaluation standards and guidelines derived from these are missing, which the biogas plant as a power plant analyze in the narrow sense and offer optimization approaches. In this work an analysis of the energy flows of biogas plants is carried out by means of methods of energy and power plant technology to the biogas sector. Since anaerobic degradation processes can only implement part of the organics, a correction factor for the anaerobic usable energy potential is proposed.
content.title_en: Analysis of the energy flows of biogas plants and development of efficiency parameters for energy plant fermentation

content.text: The present dissertation is a theoretical work with several main areas of focus. Introductory is shown how the mechanical performance follows the concepts of vibration isolation and vibration style and the influence of system boundaries. The basic chapter deals with the conversion of power and energy storage in reluctance machines. The development chapter also describes the magnetic energy in polarized systems and is presented in the flow-flow level. The function of the reluctance machine is explained by force characteristics that follow from the integral force fields. The development chapter describes an iterative method for calculating control signals, with which the volume of reluctance machines is reduced. For this purpose, the course of the magnetic flow over the position of the rotor is gradually changed according to various criteria. As a result, the communication tables are available, which are optimized for minimal acoustics, minimal torque waveness or maximum energy efficiency. The research chapter begins with the question of how many phases a reluctance machine must have. An inverse design shows that two phases are sufficient to achieve a general position in order to produce a large number of rotor polarities.
content.title_en: Vibration reduction and reluctance machines

content.text: Efficient integration on Riemann surfaces & applications. This thesis deals with the efficient algorithms for the numerical integration of differential shapes on Riemann's surfaces and their application on problems in arithmetic geometry. The main topics are the calculation of periodic patterns, which describe the (analytic) Jacobic of an algebraic curve up to isomorphy, as well as the calculation of Abel-Jacobi figure. These objects are defined by integrals of holomorphic differential forms and can be approximated by numerical integration. The Riemann area is given by a level (singular) affine equation over a number body or by a superelliptic model. <d.> This is conned with efficient numerical integration.

content.text: Metaanalysis of the detection and the absence of sedating methods. The aim of this dissertation was to examine the significance of the detection and the absence of sedating methods. A literature research was conducted for this purpose. The elimination times were calculated using the formula of KIETZMANN (1983). The standard deviation was included in the calculation of the elimination time using the confidence interval calculation according to KIETZMANN et al. (2006). An estimation of the absence time was made using the model of TOBIN et al. (2013). The substances Detomidine, Medetomidine/Dexmedetomidine, Romifidine, Xylazin, Acepromazine, Ketamine, Buprenorphin, Butorphanol, Tramadol and Methadon were described more closely with the help of a literature analysis. The studies were selected according to a specific point scheme. All publications, which achieved a sufficiently high number of points, were described and used for the calculations. As a result, a comparison of the resulting elimination times with the data of individual horse sport associations was not possible. However, the results of the use of the most cases were not widely used in the association.
content.title_en: Metaanalysis of detection and waiting times of sedating agents

content.text: Analysis, design and optimization of the transport of partial loads in intercontinental maritime transport. Basics for planning transport networks -- Practical problem -- Modelling and optimization of transport networks -- Optimization models and application Cornelia Warmer uses quantitative methods to implement strategic network planning for designing a company-internal consolidation network for partial loads in intercontinental maritime transport. For this purpose, various practical mathematical formulations of the hub location problem are modelled from the perspective of a shipper and presented two different formulational variants to illustrate a practical problem: a path and a step-oriented formulation. Furthermore, an analysis of the individual models is carried out using different study scenarios (network configurations) regarding the solution behaviour, robustness in the event of fluctuations in different input sizes and scalability for practical orders of magnitude. The content Basics for planning transport networks Practical problem Modeling and optimization of transport networks Optimization models and application The target groups Dozierende and students of business administration with the focus on logistics, supply chain management and operations research Practitioners and practitioners from the University of Applied Sciences.
content.title_en: Analysis, design and optimization of the transport of partial loads in intercontinental maritime transport

content.text: Hafen versus Stadt: Conflict analysis of the land competition between port economy and urban development in Hamburg. Klappentext: Oliver Lieber examines the conflict between the port economy and urban development in Hamburg. He shows in detail that difficulties of urban use at the interface of port and city are underestimated in public debate and that the conflict is associated with loss of benefits for all sides. The author explains the complex legal framework of port planning in Hamburg and discusses urban investments in the port. In addition, he examines the framework conditions with regard to the Federalimmission protection law and to the protection of incidents as well as their effects. The detailed empirical investigation of the conflict shows that the conflict has been significantly intensified since 2000, to which concrete reasons for the development of the city, e.g. the Olympic competitions, contributed. The content: Introduction ; Historical development of the relationship between city and port; Deconstruction of the myth of Hamburg port; investigation of the conflict in Hamburg; analysis of the causes of the conflict and the course of the conflict; Possible solutions for the conflict. The target groups: Dozierde und Studieren der Stadtentwicklung, Politikwissenschaften; Konflikenzforschung; Responsible in den Bereichen Hamburg Assater, Hafen der Hafenwirtschaft der Hafen.
content.title_en: Port versus City : Conflict analysis of the land competition between port industry and urban development in Hamburg

content.text: Labour market and pension policy in Germany and France: Actors' constellations between executives, parties, trade unions and employers' associations. Extensive reforms of labour market and pension policy were implemented in Germany from the mid-1990s onwards, but in France only from the end of the 2000s onwards. It becomes clear that the French labour market and pension reforms of recent years have important parallels with Germany. Florian Steinmüller shows that the different development of both welfare states and the convergence of France with the German reform model are due to the country-specific patterns of relations between executives, parties, trade unions and employers' associations and their dynamics of change.The content Presentation of the actors, the analysis framework and the analysis model Fundamentals of labour market and pension policy in Germany and France Development of labour market and pension policy in the Franco-German comparison Change of welfare state and change of actors' constellations in the Franco-German comparison The target groups Lecturers and researchers of comparative welfare state research, France research, policy analysis Experts and experts of unemployment and pension insurance The author Florian Steinmüller is a public speaker at the German association.
content.title_en: Labour market and pension policy in Germany and France: stakeholder constellations between executive, parties, trade unions and employers' associations

content.text: The termination of copyright rights: a dogmatic analysis of the effects of termination on the rights derived from the rights chain. The legal consequences of the termination of copyright rights are always highly controversial. The author undertakes a dogmatic analysis of the legal consequences and takes a position on the application and scope of the causality or abstraction principle as well as the effects on the rights granted in the rights chain. The starting point are the decisions of Reifen Progressive, Take Five and M2Trade, in which the Federal Court of Justice has for the first time declared itself in favour of the continuation of a derivative right independent of the main right.In this work, therefore, the positions represented in the law and case law are critically reviewed and assigned to a separate solution, oriented to the dogmatic principles of German copyright law, which can be used as a generalizable basis for copyright law.
content.title_en: Termination of copyright rights: a dogmatic analysis of the effects of termination on rights derived from the rights chain

content.text: Federal climate protection legislation in Germany in the light of well-ordered law. Climate change has also provoked activism in Germany. Individual federal states have adopted their own climate protection laws with their own climate protection goals.But what contribution can these federal climate protection laws make in the federal multi-level system in Germany? How are they designed? What areas of action do they have? And what can they not do?In this work, the state climate protection laws of North Rhine-Westphalia, Baden-Württemberg and Rhineland-Palatinate are comprehensively presented, compared with each other and evaluated with a view to a well-ordered law. The study also includes approaches of the other federal states, the federal level and selected European countries with their own climate protection laws. Taking into account the federalism and the guiding principle of well-ordered law in Germany, the advantages and disadvantages are determined and ideas for the further development of the state climate protection laws are developed.
content.title_en: Federal climate protection legislation in Germany in the light of well-ordered law

content.text: Experimental development of a test method for the evaluation of the oxidative deposition tendency of diesel fuels on a laboratory scale. The content of this dissertation is the comparative, quantitative evaluation of the deposition tendency of different diesel fuels on the basis of the results of a modified laboratory test method. Critical deposition layers on metallic components of common-rail injectors can influence the injection image/needle dynamics of the injector and lead to functional impairments/default of the injection system. The findings and methods obtained should provide solutions for reducing fuel-related deposition on metal injector components.
content.title_en: Experimental development of a test method for the evaluation of the oxidative deposition tendency of diesel fuels on a laboratory scale

content.text: Acoustic resonators for the analysis and control of vibrational systems using the example of string instruments and dielectric elastomers. The sound properties of musical instruments are determined by the interaction of the acoustic vibration modes which can be excited on them, which in turn result from the geometric structure of the resonator in combination with the materials used. In this work the vibrational behaviour of string instruments was investigated by the use of minimally invasive piezoelectric polymer film sensors. The combined phenomena studied include the so-called wolftone and vibration stylators used for attenuation of the latter, as well as the mutual influence of arc and instrument during the playing process. At dielectric elastomeric membranes, the effect of the elastic properties of the membrane material on acoustic and electromechanical vibration behaviour was shown. The dissertation is divided into three parts, the main results of which are summarised below. Part I was the functioning of a tuning-stimmable vibration-stylizer for the attenuation of wolf tones.
