content.text: Electromagnetic modelling and optimization of through silicon vias. This work describes the simulation and design of through contacting in silicon substrates (TSVs) as used in the construction and connection technology for integrated circuits. Numerical methods of comparatively high numerical efficiency are developed and applied to simulate realistic arrangements with large numbers of TSVs. The presented methods are correlated with alternative approaches and parameter variations are derived from design recommendations. Furthermore, several measurement structures are developed with TSVs and measurement results are compared with simulation results. This thesis presents the simulation and the design of vertical interactions in silicon substrates known as through silicon vias (TSVs) which are applied to a component of 3D integration of integrated circuits. Numerical methods of interconnected highly efficient and applied in alternative parameters.
content.title_en: Electromagnetic modelling and optimization of through silicon vias

content.text: § 3a UWG: Market behavioural regulations for the protection of minors. The answer to the question which primary standards qualify as market behavioural regulations for the protection of minors and thus can be transformed into the law of integrity has always been difficult. At the latest since the entry into force of the UGP Directive, the literature increasingly believes that the child and youth protection regulations have no protective function in favour of minors and therefore no competitive relevance.In this work, we examine which children and youth protection regulations fall within the scope of the law of the breach. In addition, we discuss whether the applicability of § 3a UWG in the event of violation of a market behavioural regulation for the protection of minors is contrary to the claim of the UGP Directive for full harmonisation of consumer protection-related integrity law.
content.title_en: § 3a UWG: Market behaviour rules for the protection of minors

content.text: Screen scraping and freedom of information. Freedom of information and digital economy: Using the example of the phenomenon Screen scraping, the work examines for the first time the commercial handling of publicly accessible information and data on the Internet from an information-free perspective.First, the author discusses the points of contact between screen scraping procedures and constitutionally protected freedom of information by referring to European law requirements.The core of the investigation is a comprehensive, simple-law assessment of screen scraping. Information-free influences are particularly taken into account. The focus is on contractual, database and competition law issues as well as discussions on so-called virtual house law. Finally, the author develops general admissibility criteria of screen scraping software based on the established findings and information-free considerations.
content.title_en: Screen scraping and freedom of information

content.text: Media and Europe: European Union regulatory practice, competences and action in the field of media. Development lines, competence standards and current areas of action of the European Union in the field of media. What competences does the European Union have in the field of media? In times of increasing activity of transnational media groups and the emergence of novel media manifestations which seem to require a European response to regulatory questions, this question is of high topicality.Based on the finding that a special authorization for media-related special authorization is lacking in the European treaties, but the media there are included as an implicit cross-cutting objective, the competence standards to be granted to the European Union are examined on their normative content.This study is then applied to four current fields of action. These include European media concentration law, detailed questions of regulation of search engines, consideration of media diversity in European competition law and the state of broadcasting
content.title_en: Media and Europe: European Union regulatory practice, competences and action in the field of media

content.text: Road traffic and social visibility: the mass medium of road in Chicago 1900-1930. Urban roads serve as mass media for the creation of social visibility of persons, groups and their concerns even in the digitalized present. The study traces the history of this medial dimension of road traffic using the migrant and media metropolis Chicago from 1900-1930. Especially in the example of this rapidly growing city, contemporary reformers, writers, journalists and sociologists addressed the mediality of the phenomena on the road. Their texts make micro-historically condensed with photographic material and self-certifications multifacetedly illustrated how streets shaped as socio-technical setting visual constellations, perceptions and appearances of traffic participants. The encounter of countless (non)verbal articulations, competing self-images and demands of individual and communities led to stereotyping projections that ended in extreme cases in dynamics such as the Race Riots 1919
content.title_en: Road traffic and social visibility: the mass medium street in Chicago 1900-1930

content.text: The liability of host providers for immaterial rights violations. For several years, a clear tendency towards increasing use of host providers for the infringement of intellectual property rights committed by users has been evident. This trend is reflected in a steadily increasing number of court decisions at both European and national level. The liability system for host providers is particularly complex and controversial. It is characterized by an interlocking of regulatory levels in Union law and national law. The work subordinates the European legal framework of provider liability and the national dogmatic bases of indirect liability to a comprehensive and critical legal analysis. Union legal guidelines for intermediary liability are developed, which are then integrated accordingly into the national liability system.
content.title_en: The liability of host providers for IPR violations

content.text: Concepts for best-point-optimized combustion engines within hybrid drivetrains. Design of engine concepts with extended expansion -- Validation and coordination of submodels -- Simulation and evaluation -- Overall system simulation The subject of this study are combustion engine concepts for hybrid drivetrains. Using simulations, Morris Langwiesner examines three concepts with extended expansion. This process management allows a significant increase in expansion ratio and consequently an increase in efficiency with consistent compression ratio. A challenge in the simulation is the consideration of all concept-specific effects that influence effective efficiency. Therefore, the correct choice of submodels is crucial for the necessary predictive ability. The validity of the submodels in focus has been demonstrated by the author with the help of validation experiments. The overall system simulations carried out show that the choice of hybrid topology has a significant influence on the utilization of the best-point range. With a combined P2/4 topology, the potential for reducing consumption in the WLTP driving cycle is greatest compared to a conventional engine. The content of the design of engine concepts with extended expansion validation and coordination of the submodels has a significant influence on the utilization of the best-point range of the vehicle simulation of the research and the research group of the University of the University of Stuttgart.
content.title_en: Concepts for best-point optimized combustion engines within hybrid drive lines

content.text: Waste reduction in food retailing : Solutions by mathematical optimization and simulation-based evaluation. Branch logistics in stationary food retail -- Microperiodical order quantity models -- Goods redistribution for waste reduction The present book provides a direct link to the waste problem of stationary food retailing and provides two different logistical solutions for waste reduction in retail. Larissa Janssen proposes a twice daily order quantity planning with delivery or a goods redistribution. The used methodology leads to a reduction in the average stocks of perishable goods in stores of a food chain without reducing the degree of customer service. The simulation studies clearly show that the two approaches can be more efficient than the classical daily inventory management in food retailing. The content Store logistics in stationary food retailing Microperiodical order quantity models Product redistribution for waste reduction The target groups Dozierende and students from the fields of logistics, operations research, simulation technology Employees from food retailing from the fields of logistics and operations research The author Dr. Larissa Janssen has been a PhD student at Prof. Dr. Jürgen Sauer at the Chair of Systems Analysis at the University of Applied Sciences and Business Administration at the University of Applied Sciences.

content.text: Paper production in the German Southwest: a new trade in the late Middle Ages. The introduction of paper production is considered a central prerequisite for the enforcement of paper use in late medieval Europe. However, in large parts it is unexplored how papermaking established itself and how papermakers integrated themselves into society as representatives of a new profession. The study therefore examines the establishment process of this new trade using the example of the German Southwest, which early first paper mill districts in the Reich north of the Alps trained. The first part deals with technical historical aspects. It examines paper production from the material side by asking which traces in historical papers point to the production process. The second part focuses on paper mill foundations in Basel, above all on social and economic aspects. The Basel case study is embedded in an overall presentation of the early South West German paper mill sites. With the systematic evaluation of the sources, the present volume enriches paper-layer research in terms of the beginnings of paper production in the German area.
content.title_en: Papermaking in the German Southwest : a new business in the late Middle Ages

content.text: Liquid Democracy in Germany : on the future of digital political decision-making after the fall of the Pirate Party. The rocket-like rise of the Pirate Party followed its equally rapid decline. Is the experiment of political will-building - Liquid Democracy - just as failed? On the original path of Grounded Theory, Anja Adler approaches the recent German political history in order to deal with the ambitious proposal for the development of a new operating system for politics. Through numerous interviews with the actors of internet-based advisory and decision-making procedures, she draws a vivid and well-suited portrait of both the concrete procedures and the attitudes and visions of democracy developers Taking the most recent history of German politics as an example, this first comprehensive study about liquid democracy shows that algorithms of democratic decisions hamper as well as enrich politics
content.title_en: Liquid Democracy in Germany : on the future of digital political decision-making after the fall of the Pirate Party

content.text: Partitioned solution strategies for strongly-coupled fluid-structure interaction problems in maritime applications. Coupled multi-field problems occur in a variety of engineering applications. This work pursues a partitioned solution approach that not only allows the use of different discretization schemes for the individual sub-problems, but also the use of specialized and efficient solvers, which improves modularity, performance and software reusability. A framework for partitioned analysis of general multi-field problems is presented and implemented in the generic software library comana, which is reviewed using benchmark problems and applied to challenging problems of fluid-structure interaction from the maritime sector. Many engineering applications are governance by coupled multiple problem problems. In this thesis, a partitioned solution approach is followed to solve these problems, which does not enable the diffusion of conflicting problems.
content.title_en: Partitioned solution strategies for strongly-coupled fluid-structure interaction problems in maritime applications

In the age of communication on social networks, the generation of personal data is an element of everyday personality development. At the same time, third parties can generate a comprehensive profile of the person concerned by the analysis of the data. While the Federal Constitutional Court has developed a differentiated case law on "analog" communication, it still grants the data subject a general right to informational self-determination. Christoph Gieseler transfers the thoughts of self-responsible privacy and self-representation to the special dangers caused by automated data processing. Afterwards, personality and data protection on social network platforms presents itself as a protection of free communicational personality development against permanent storage, compilation and evaluation of the resulting data. / "Public Communication on Social Network Personnel" -- While the German Constitutional Court has developed judicial information on "analogue" consent by the consent it.

content.text: The copyright use of third parties between reproduction, processing and free use. Interventions in the copyright of the author can take place in different ways. While the use of a work in identical or almost identical form can be qualified as reproduction, there is an adaptation or other transformation in the case of a further change. However, the new work is so far removed from the original that it is almost "failed", this represents a free use which the author can no longer prohibit. These copyright uses and their delimitation from each other are the author's work. On the one hand, the current legal situation as well as the legal provisions and literature available for this purpose are presented. On the other hand, the questions are examined whether the current legal provisions are suitable and necessary to resolve the conflict of interest between authors and users and whether they are in accordance with the requirements of Union law.

content.text: The representation of the other: an investigation of images in thematic exhibitions on migration since 1974. What is conveyed about images in thematic exhibitions on migration and what effects are called upon about the formal image design? These are the two central key questions of the study, for which a total of 814 exhibitions were collected. The study provides a first comprehensive overview of these exhibitions, within which the topic of migration has been discussed since 1974, especially at a pictorial level. Although the number of pictures examined in total 13.049 appears high, it becomes clear on closer examination that the selection of the opened perspectives is limited to the topic. In addition to conclusions for curatorial practice, the findings also provide impulses for the educational activity of mediation.
content.title_en: On the Representation of the Other: an investigation of images in thematic exhibitions on migration since 1974

content.text: The team's own organizational processes in team development. The understanding, presentation and analysis of team development processes based on the premises of dynamic, unstable and nonlinear systems. As in the life history of people a certain sequence of typical phases of life can often be found, teams change their externally perceptible "character" and their inner thinking, feeling and behaviour over time. In particular, the linear, mechanistic world view, which was long based on research of teams (and still is partly still located), however, brought many statements about straight, predictable development processes in teams to light that are not durable from a system-theoretical point of view. The research of teams as social systems with a system-scientific perspective allows a deeper and, for the complex nature of the matter, more appropriate investigation to be made. The development process of teams in organizations is therefore presented in the present study on the basis of the premises of a system-scientific research approach and with a system-scientific method inventory. It is described whether and when phases of pattern change of team development occur in the context of team development.
content.title_en: Self-organisation processes in team development. Capture, display and analyze team development processes based on the premises of dynamic, unstable and nonlinear systems

content.text: Heat treatment of SiCr-alloy, oil-closing-coated spring steel wire. This work deals with the question of to what extent the combination of the heat treatment steps of wire and spring production can increase the mechanical load capacity and the life of screw pressure springs. An analytical model is presented which enables the calculation of temperature – time – curves of wire remuneration. Laboratory tests determine optimal regimes for each partial process of heat treatment, determine the parameters for the analytical calculation and validate the calculation model. Various factors affecting the structure of the wire material as well as the effects of all process phases on the mechanical properties of the treated spring steel wire are discussed. It is explained that torsion-loaded springs made of optimized material have a significantly reduced set amount and an increased life span in the time-strength range in the context of continuous vibration tests.
content.title_en: Heat treatment of SiCr alloy, oil-lubricated spring steel wire

content.text: Social space High-rise building: Neighbourhood and everyday living in Swiss large-scale residential buildings. The large-scale residential buildings, which fundamentally changed the Swiss settlement landscape during the construction boom of the 1960s and 1970s, have become increasingly discredited over the years. But how do the realities of life in this building stock – beyond the widespread clichés – shape themselves? Eveline Althaus focuses on the neighborhoods of high-rise residential settlements in Switzerland. Using house biographies, she examines social space dynamics and highlights how diversity and difference are experienced and (re-)produced in the residential environment. This opens up new perspectives on how to deal with this built heritage and forms of coexistence in heterogeneous settings.
content.title_en: Social room high-rise house : Neighborhood and everyday living in Swiss large residential buildings

content.text: Development of a calculation method for the determination of capacity in light signal controlled access roads with additional setup lanes with simultaneous release time. content.title_en: Development of a calculation method for the determination of capacity in light signal controlled accesses with additional ramps with simultaneous release time

content.text: Anion receptors based on hydrogen and halogen bonding. The development of selective anion receptors, which enable the targeted detection and binding as well as the transport of relevant anions, has been one of the most important research areas of supramolecular chemistry for many years. So far, these receptors have been based mainly on the donation of hydrogen bridge bonds, but recently also on halogen bridge donors. Unlike the hydrogen bridge, the halogen bridge closely related to it has a higher directionality, a greater covalent bonding component and a stronger interaction with a Lewis-basic partner, thus enabling the construction of potentially more selective receptors. An important heterocycle, which enables a simple implementation of halogen bridge bonds into various systems through its modular access, is the halogenated 1,2,3 triazole or the corresponding triazolium salt. This component allows a strong polarization of the halogen and thus a very efficient halogen bridgedonation.
content.title_en: Anion receptors based on hydrogen and halogen bonding

content.text: 50 + 1 in the relegation fight?: the principle of §§ 16 c No. 3 DFB-Stattung/8 No. 3 DFL-Stattung in the light of the TFEU. Now the 50+1 rule is more on the test stage than ever before, but many parts of the literature increasingly express legal concerns, which in particular refer to the European fundamental freedoms and the Union law banning of cartels. This book examines the relevant European standards and subordinates the regulatory subject matter of a proportionality test, in order to the question of any European law illegality of the currently extremely controversial 50+1 rule, which refers to the German fundamental freedoms and the prohibition of the German law of the German anti-trust law.

Julian Gulden examines determinants and context factors of acceptance and use of investment management FinTechs. content.text: The design potential of the driver's field of activity in the field of driving is: how complexity, display position and stereoscopic 3D determine the perception and driving performance of the driver's field of activity.The impact of different display types depending on the display position -- recording the perceptibility of stereoscopic depth stimuli during real-time travel -- potentials of autostereoscopic displays for the driver's workplace Johanna Sandbrink identifies design potentials that can improve the visual representation of infotainment displays in the vehicle in order to enable drivers to access advanced information during manual travel in a safe manner.The author illustrates from her central findings that using a suitable display position and the use of stereoscopic depth stimuli can achieve significant benefits for the visibility.In particular, the stereoscopic depth stimuli represent an effective parameter for the design of displays that is discreetly integrated and does not cause any negative effects on driving. content.text: The predictive quality of crash calculations is an important prerequisite for their ever-increasing use in body design. Even if the imaging quality of the calculations with steel structures has already reached a high level, a continuous improvement and further development of the simulations of highest importance for vehicle development is still essential. Philipp Wellkamp's research study contributes to the methodological analysis of joined steel body structures. These are used for the understanding of the system behaviour and, on the other hand, for the evaluation and improvement of the conformity quality between simulation and experiment. The author conducts these comparative studies on various levels of complexity along a validation hierarchy. content.text: The study focuses on the development and validation of a competence model for historical teaching. The individual phases of the test validation are detailed and reflected in relation to the quality of the developed vignette test. Results from a cross-sectional survey provide information on factors that can influence the history didactic competence in the formulation of tasks for prospective historical teaching staff. The study thus contributes to the research on professionalisation in the field of history didactics.

content.text: The evaluation of the benefits of medicines according to the AMG and the SGB V: an investigation into the generation of administrative knowledge bases and their judicial control. Karsten Engelke examines how knowledge about medicines is generated and received in the law on risk management: in clinical trials preliminary and revision-oriented knowledge about the new medicine is generated in accordance with medical methodology; the regulatory authority takes the risk decision about the marketing. At the same time, an extensive and complex, independent evaluation of the medical benefit begins in the German health insurance system. Engelke works out how the legal areas deal with the same medical knowledge that is behind the value decisions and how risk management law always generates new knowledge. The work concludes with an analysis of the BSG's case law on the handling of medicines and proposes an extension to the specific procedural review of the production of methodological standards.
content.title_en: The evaluation of the benefits of medicines under the AMG and the SGB V : an investigation into the production of administrative knowledge and their judicial control

content.text: On-demand streaming platforms: the role of copyright in new business models for the distribution of digital content. Social change and technical progress have led to a growing reduction in the role of physical media in the distribution of content. Streaming platforms, where content can be accessed directly from the provider's server without the need for permanent storage on the user's device, are about to replace "classic" distribution on physical media or as a data package for downloading. The work examines the role of copyright in new business models for the distribution of content in digital form and whether the current legal framework is flexible enough to take sufficient account of their specificities.
content.title_en: On-demand streaming platforms: the role of copyright in new business models for the distribution of digital content

content.text: The relevance of statistical methods in the case law and possible implications for legal education. Basic knowledge of statistical methods and methods of quantitative data analysis are now considered to be important in almost all professional fields - this is also true for the language-dominated legal professions. Both the methods of statistics and the legal sciences are aimed at reducing uncertainty in decision-making processes as far as possible. Not only because of this fact are statistical procedures increasingly incorporated into the case law. This is followed by the conclusion that quantitative statistical methods should be part of the legal education in order to correctly apply this right-wing external knowledge and to interpret its results clearly. The legal decision-making process thus has the possibility of being enhanced, while the legal science opens up for the import of knowledge of other disciplines. Basic knowledge about statistical thinking and argumentation, as well as methods of quantitative data analysis.
content.title_en: The relevance of statistical methods in case law and possible implications for legal training

content.text: Measuring mortality trends and dynamics in an era of continuous mortality deciline. The observations of the continuous mortality decline, the change in the age profile of mortality decline, and the potential for the expansion of the life span in the highest age levels form the basis of the articles in this work. The developed approaches and the consideration of the limits of age-specific mortality illuminate some of the challenges facing demographers, but also the general public at present and in the future. <ger> Three key observations – the significant continuity of mortality improvement, the changing age patterns of mortality improvement, and the location of longevity expansion potentials at the highest ages – are the basis for the individual articles of this thesis. The articles expand challenges are caused by the occurrence and the absence of the population prospects.
content.title_en: Measuring mortality trends and dynamics in an era of continuous mortality deciline

content.text: This is the first time that the law of international law has been adopted by the UN International Law Commission on the Law of Transboundary Aquifers in the context of international water law. In view of the global water crisis, the importance of groundwater resources as a water resource is steadily increasing. Groundwater resources – also called aquifers – are highly vulnerable to pollution and depletion. The majority of aquifers are also cross-border. Against this background, a legal regulation of this important water resource appears essential. This work is based on the extent to which the recent development of international groundwater legislation – the UN International Law Commission's draft articles on the law of cross-border aquifers – is capable of effectively regulating the protection and conservation of cross-border groundwater resources and of adequate use and distribution of the resource. The subject of the study is questions about the legal framework, the management of cross-border aquifers and current challenges in international water law. / »Groundwater and Public International Law« -- Groundwater is one of the world's most important water resources. Although it is the highest priority and prevent in international law.
content.title_en: Groundwater in international law: an investigation of the draft articles of the UN International Law Commission on the law of cross-border aquifers in the context of international water law

content.text: Legal issues of fertilisation: a control and legal analysis against the background of the obligations of the legal entity and of international law and policy objectives on environmental and resource protection. The fertilisation is a prerequisite for the nutrition of a growing world population, but also for the cause of massive environmental pollution. Against the background of the failure of numerous environmental objectives enshrined in international and EU law and the infringement procedure against Germany regarding the EU directive on nitrate, the work critically examines the fertilisation-specific agri-environmental law on its control effect and Union law compliance. The focus of the study is on fertilisation (means) law, which is the subject of profound legal changes with the current discussion on a fertilisation regulation at EU level and the latest amendment of the national legislation on fertilisation.
content.title_en: Legal issues of fertilisation: a governance and legal analysis against the background of Union and international obligations and policy objectives on environmental and resource protection

content.text: The object of the work is tensegrity structures with several stable equilibrium configurations, so-called multistable tensegrity structures. The focus of the work is on the development of algorithms with which such structures can be designed, investigated and designed in a targeted manner. To this end, possibilities for determining the equilibrium configurations of multistable tensegrity structures are considered. Furthermore, it is examined how tensegrity structures can be designed in such a way that they have predetermined properties. To this end, parameters for characterizing these properties are defined. Optimization problems are derived for both tasks. To solve these optimization problems, algorithms are designed, tested and analyzed. Based on these theoretical studies, another focus of this work is on the consideration of the possible uses of multistable tensegrity structures in gripper technology. Various concepts for the development of grippers from these structures are discussed. Further consideration of selected concepts is given, among other things, to the inclusion of dynamic analyses.
content.title_en: Form and parameter finding of multistable tensegrity structures by means of optimization algorithms and applications in gripper technology

content.text: Multifunctional fibre metal laminates with improved load bearing capacity. In order to increase the mechanical properties and the life of a bolt joint compared to conventional glass fibre reinforced plastics (GFK), multifunctional fiber metal laminates (FML) with permeable and surface treated metal layers are investigated. In addition, a new approach to damage detection is developed in FML. Laminates are produced in resin injection process. The subject of this work is the investment of multifunctional fiber metal laminates (FML) with permeable and surface treated metal particles to improve the mechanical performance and bolted joint fatigue lifetime compared to conventional glass fibre reinforced polymers (GFRP). In addition, a new approach for health monitoring to detect damage in ML is being developed.
content.title_en: Multifunctional fibre metal laminates with improved load bearing capacity

content.text: In search of attachment: the Japanese approach to the tsunami catastrophe 3.11 and an implication of the theology of cuddle. 20,000 people lost their lives on 11 March 2011 in a devastating tsunami on the north-eastern coast of Japan. Hundreds of thousands became homeless and had to live in transition settlements. To mourn for dear people came the pain of uprooting. What gives people the strength to live with hope in the face of such disasters? What role does the Church play in this? The focus of this study is on reports by victims of the tsunami disaster and the discussion of how Japanese pastors are pastorally responding to the suffering of individuals. In doing so, a Japanese concept of "cuddles" proves to be a viable size and expression of God's love in the face of the experienced suffering
content.title_en: In search of connectedness : the Japanese handling of the tsunami catastrophe 3.11 and an implication of the theology of cuddle

content.text: The Jungneolithic ceramics of Ergolding "Fischergasse" and Aiterhofen-Ödmühle: their significance for the definition of the Altheim culture. Abstract: The late Jungneolithic period, which lasted about 600 years, is characterized by the Altheim culture in southern Bavaria. This takes up a large part of the fourth pre-Christian millennium and is mainly spread between the Danube and the Alpine foot from Lech to the Inn. Since its exhibition as a separate group by J. Driehaus in the 1950s, the material gathered around the findings from the Altheim in Lower Bavaria formed a uniform block without any recognizable internal chronological development. Based on two major finds complexes of the last decades from Lower Bavaria, the dissertation is working on a three-stage chronology of the Altheim culture and shows its respective references to the neighbouring cultural areas. At the same time, the embedding of the Altheim culture is on the one hand into the regional neolithic cultural development and on the other hand into extensive supra-regional currents a part of the study.
content.title_en: The Jungneolithic ceramics by Ergolding "Fischergasse" and Aiterhofen-Ödmühle: their significance for the definition of the Altheim culture

content.text: Laboratory astrophysics : spectroscopic and instrumentation for the gas phase and the solid state. Laborastrophysics is a bridge between investigations of atoms and molecules in the interstellar medium, which we can identify by astronomical observations, and investigations of this species or its analogues, which we can generate in the laboratory and measure in situ. Laborastrophysics provides spectroscopic fingerprints of species needed to decipher observed astronomical spectra and allows the modelling of physical-chemical processes under the conditions of the interstellar medium. It helps to understand these processes in their entirety and to establish resilient astrochemical models that, supported by astronomical observations, can reveal our astrochemical past and future. One of the fundamental questions that arises regarding the interstellar medium is the nature and frequency of the detected species. To answer this question, three essential prerequisites are to meet: (a) species in interstellar analysis, to identify the interstellar models and to identify the interstellar models, to identify the interstellar models and to explain the interstellar parameters of the present species.

content.text: Social inequality in flexibilised vocational training: extended skills requirements and milieu-specific adaptations in training companies. Teaching companies are a new model of vocational education in Switzerland. The author shows that the project-shaped organisation of this form of basic vocational education, where learners change the training company several times, constitutes new mechanisms of social inequality in the field of basic vocational education. This is because teaching companies' associations, compared to traditional vocational teaching, place substantial higher demands on the self-organisation and flexibility of the learners. A sovereign handling of these requirements requires specific conditions and resources that are unequally distributed in social structure. Nevertheless, teaching companies also offer the opportunity to reduce social inequality. The condition for this is that teaching companies' associations do not require the key competences, which are fundamental to their working life, such as flexibility and self-organisation, but systematically impart them as skills. In addition, frameworks must be created, thanks to which the challenges of the combined training can be addressed to learners from less privileged backgrounds.
content.title_en: Social inequality in flexibilised vocational training: extended skills requirements and milieu-specific adaptations in training associations

content.text: Strategic Modeling of the Heuristic Solution Examples: Studies of Solution Procedures and Strategy Knowledge of the Mathematical Modelling Process. Modelling as part of a general mathematics teaching -- Teaching mathematical modelling competence -- Solution Example Learning from a cognitive psychology perspective -- Heuristic solution examples to promote strategic action in the modelling process The teaching of mathematical modelling competence is a central goal of competence-oriented mathematics teaching. Since only isolated specific mediation aspects have been investigated to promote this competence, Natalie Tropper investigates this topic in a qualitatively designed study. She considers the influences of strategy-oriented heuristic solution examples on the modelling processes and the modeling-related strategy knowledge of students. The results of her empirical study show the potential of the selected instructional material to support modeling-related learning processes and at the same time suggests implications for its educational embedding.

content.text: Local energy production in the energy transition: problems and options for designing the local energy system, using the example of renewable energy generation as compared to the private sector. The energy transition and the progressive liberalisation of the energy market pose enormous challenges for private and public energy companies. They require a strategic realignment, especially in the value-added stage of energy generation. Although municipal and private companies are active in the same economic sector, they are subject to different legal requirements, which sometimes result in significant legal and actual advantages and disadvantages for municipal companies. These differences can be derived mainly from constitutional determinants, which restrict the scope of the country's legislative authority. Local regulations, in particular in the field of over-local activity and public welfare, are sometimes in conflict with these constitutional requirements. Thus, it is necessary to adapt the municipal framework to the challenges of the urban energy transition without disregarding the constitutional requirements.
content.title_en: Local energy production in the energy transition: problems and design options in the case of electricity generation by renewable energy compared to the private sector

content.text: The wilfulness of the island of Rügen. From the preface: The basis of this study of the wilfulness of the island of Rügen is its detailed recording, which is included in the register of this work in a shorter version. After three introductory sections, the periods determined from the time of the wilfulness are treated separately. In this context, it is attempted to reconstruct the settlement of the island of Rügen for each period and to show the causes of the transformation. A summary of the periods indicates the position of the investigation space compared to other areas of Germany. Finally, conclusions on the settlement of Rügen and the main causes of the negative transformation of the settlement picture are presented.
content.title_en: The deserts of the island of Rügen

content.text: The old military and commercial roads of South Hanover and adjacent areas : represented on a geographical basis by archival material : with a map. The present work first deliberately places the emphasis on the younger period (16th-18th century) - especially for the more precise course of the military roads - for which a rich documentary tradition exists, and then tries to show, on the basis of older materials, that or to how far those roads existed already in the Middle Ages. However, to the fundamental historical exploration of the old roads it is essential to associate the geographical assessment. Only it is able to live up to the nature of the old military roads and preserve from impossible constructions.
content.title_en: The old military and commercial roads of South Hanover and adjacent areas : on a geographical basis, by archival material : with a map

content.text: The construction ground and the construction of Hamburg: the influence of the natural underground on the development of a world port city. The research of the Hamburg building ground is a matter of geologists. The description of the construction of Hamburg is a historical topographical task, the consideration of the buildings an architectural topic. The question of the relations between the building ground and the building is interested the engineer. Numerous investigations of the problems indicated here can be found in the respective literature. The aim of the present work, however, is to combine this variety of ways of looking at the building ground and the construction in a geographical overview.
content.title_en: Building ground and development of Hamburg: the influence of the natural underground on the development of a world port city

content.text: Business centres: Use and intensity as a measure of urban scale; an empirical-methodical comparison of 15 cities in the Federal Republic of Germany. This study tries to develop quantified comparable model concepts and to provide decision-making aid for the future with the help of 15 cities selected in the Federal Republic of Germany to trace the regularities of their internal structure. The most important urban functional link in cities of all sizes is the most valuable business area for this city, which is therefore to be considered in this study. Spatial codes of conduct of these business centres are to be used as a measure of urban scale. The business centres of Augsburg, Bensheim, Bonn, Darmstadt, Essen, Flensburg, Frankfurt am Main, Freiburg im Breisgau, Gießen, Heidelberg, Herne, Münster in Westphalia, Stuttgart, Worms and Würzburg are examined.
content.title_en: Business centres : Use and intensity as a measure of urban size; an empirical-methodical comparison of 15 cities in the Federal Republic of Germany

content.text: The study focuses on mapping the vegetation along off-road roads (Bundesstraßen u. Autobahnen) of five Hessian highway districts with consideration of the woody areas. In addition to the influences of the road-roads on the species living there and their diversity, the study also considers the effects that arise from the respective use of the side turned away from the road. Other location factors such as nutrient content, acid content of the soil and the water budget are also taken into account. The data obtained from this study is used to assess the importance of the road-render vegetation for nature conservation. The author is working on recommendations for the design and ecologically meaningful care of the road-roads and thus makes suggestions for their implementation into practical planning work. The work is aimed at botanist, forest biologists, etc.
content.title_en: Vegetation and flora on the road network of West Germany : Locations - Nature conservation value - Care : with 43 tables attached

content.text: The late and postglacial development of the Wood and Liefdefjord region of Nordspitzbergens. The topic of this work is the exploration of glacier fluctuations and their effects in a fjord system of Nordspitzbergens. With the help of acoustic, sedimentological and oceanographic methods, the deglazation history of the area was developed from the current status. (FWG)
content.title_en: Late and postglacial development of the Wood and Liefdefjord region of Nordspitzbergens

content.text: Employment systems as a sum of individual transitions on the labour market. Classification: I. Introduction: Labour market transitions as a scientific and theoretical problem field. - II. Labour market transitions, welfare state, transitional labour markets and employment systems. - III. Indicators for the recording of transition dynamics (1. Current indicators. - 2. The development of a "benchmark" as a basis for comparisons). - IV. Empirical implementation of the analyses of transitions in Germany and the Member States of the European Community (1. Data basis. - 2. The components of the German employment system - a descriptive analysis. - 3. Multivariate analysis of individual transition probabilities in Germany. - 4. A European comparison: The dynamics of transitions into and out of self-employment. - 5. A European comparison: transitions in the field of dependent employment and unemployment. - V. Summary and outlook The study refers to the period 1985-1999. (HoF/Text taken over)
content.title_en: Employment systems as a sum of individual transitions on the labour market

content.text: Self-presentation as an instrument in competition between universities: a contribution from a regional scientific point of view using the example of the University of Hanover. The present study examines the questions of how competition could be integrated into the higher education system and whether self-presentation could be an appropriate instrument in competition between universities. A model approach is presented based on system theory considerations and examined on its applicability based on case studies: On the one hand, the student demand and the regional catchment areas of universities with regional scientific analysis methods are examined, on the other hand, the leaving of a university institute by means of primary data. Concepts of action developed from the results show the applicability of the instrument self-presentation. At the same time, the publication of institute-related graduates data creates transparency and an exemplary form of self-initiated evaluation. (PHF/ übern.)
content.title_en: Self-presentation as an instrument in competition between universities: a contribution from a regional scientific point of view using the example of the University of Hanover

content.text: The time of society: on the way to a sociological theory of time. One can observe modern society from a factual point of view - and encounter the differentiation of functions. One can look at it from a social point of view - and encounter stratification, collectivities and distribution structures. One can also examine it from a spatial dimension - and then encounter reciprocal observational relations of places and perspectives. In this "modern classic" of system theory, modern society is knocked down in terms of its temporal order and dynamics. One then encounters the simultaneity of all the dimensions mentioned above: the simultaneity of functions, layers, collectivities and spaces and the problem of its synchronisation. In addition to a sociological study of a sociological theory of time, a draft of a social theory of time is presented in this study.
content.title_en: Society's time: on the way to a sociological theory of time

content.text: Infrastructural investment in large cities: problems and possibilities for optimising consumer infrastructure investments. As public services are recognised as an integral part of the local authority's remit, planning of consumer infrastructure becomes a permanent municipal task. However, in the absence of suitable planning objectives, the development of social infrastructure is now usually oriented towards ad hoc objectives or pragmatic benchmarks. The study starts from the analysis of this state and attempts to clarify the various practical and theoretical problems and causes of this poor planning. On the basis of this, a solution proposal for planning social infrastructure oriented to the needs of urban residents is developed. However, the proposed method of scientific and participatory target planning, in which the activities of citizens, scientists and politicians are meaningfully integrated, is so complex and complex that it cannot be carried out in cities of any size class.
content.title_en: Infrastructure investments in large cities: problems and opportunities for optimising consumer infrastructure investments

content.text: Stability of frying fat during storage and thermal stress : analytical detection of fat changes, possibilities of stabilization by natural antioxidants and their quantification. From the summary: The changes in unused frying fats (palm fat) for batch operations, which occurred during a minimum shelf life of 10 months at a temperature of 16ʿ C, were analyzed using chemical and physical measurement methods. It could be determined that the influence of storage led to loss of fat stability.
content.title_en: Stability of frying fat during storage and thermal stress : analytical detection of fat changes, possibilities of stabilization by natural antioxidants and their quantification

content.text: The Transfiguration of the Medieval Past made Romanesque churches in the 19th century a major building site. National pathos dressed in a historical garment. What impact did this historical enthusiasm have on the famous Romanesque buildings in the Rhineland? What remained of the medieval building substance? What influence did politics have on the preservation of monuments in the Prussian Rhine province? What role did Emperor Wilhelm II play, who understood the neuromanic developed from the Rhenish style as his mastery architecture? These questions of equally interest to building history and history are answered here after extensive archival research. Using nine carefully selected examples, the study leads the reader from Cologne and Neuss to Koblenz and Trier.
content.title_en: Rhenish Romanesque style in the 19th century : Monument conservation in the Prussian province of the Rhine

content.text: The technical drying of wood is now an indispensable process and is carried out in different plants and processes depending on the wood material. The drying air released from wood dust and water vapour also contains organic substances, such as low molecular alcohols and carbon acids, phenols and terpenes, as well as other compounds that are not yet identified. While the wood dust can be removed from the drying air to a sufficient extent, the light volatile substances continue to cause the so-called "blue haze" as well as odour problems in the environment. - Within the scope of this topic, the diploma thesis systematically describes the current and in the future perhaps possible methods for cleaning the exhaust air from drying plants in the wood industry, taking into account the special function and performance of organic hydrocarbons.
content.title_en: State of play and future prospects of exhaust air purification techniques of wood drying plants

The study presents aspects of the life of Turkish female students in Germany. Using qualitative interviews, the author presents the conditions for successful life of third generation migrants. The book makes it clear that neither the role of victims nor the generally acknowledged cultural conflict is decisive for the situation of young women. The study presents aspects of the life of Turkish female students in Germany. The author presents the conditions for successful life of third generation migrants in qualitative interviews. content.text: The importance of urban supply and disposal for sustainable urban development in Brazil: the case study Curitiba; with ... 42 tables. In his dissertation, Frank Zirkl deals with questions on sustainable urban development in Brazil, with a focus on problems of urban waste disposal in the southern Brazilian metropolis Curitiba. In particular, studies on population participation in municipal waste collection were in the foreground.
content.title_en: The importance of urban supply and disposal for sustainable urban development in Brazil : the case study Curitiba; with ... 42 tables

content.text: Bike and Ride: a concept for combined passenger transport; case study Darmstadt. Bike and Ride - the combined use of bicycle and public transport - has not been adequately perceived in the Federal Republic of Germany. The promotion of bike and ride offers the opportunity to contribute to the reduction of the suffocation of our cities in car traffic and to an ecologically oriented transport concept that gives us space and air again. Using the Darmstadt Commune as an example, the problems of traffic development and the deficits in traffic planning can be identified. An ecological planning approach often only exists on paper; in practice, car traffic is still promoted. A number of municipalities would certainly have good opportunities to move their citizens to "change" by providing an acceptable infrastructure for cycling, offering modern B+R facilities and a generously expanded public transport offer. The planning conditions for an ecologically oriented, integrated transport planning exist - now it is time to concreteise and implement it. <dt.>
content.title_en: Bike and Ride : a concept for combined local passenger transport ; case study Darmstadt

content.text: From the Ledigenheim to the boarding house: Building typology and social theory to the end of the Weimar Republic. From the welfare instrument to the radical avant-garde building with manifesto character: The transformation of the building type "Ledigenheim" reflects central ideas of modernism, which is in search of the "New Housing" of a "New Man" in a "New Time". - - The building task "Ledigenheim" appears from around 1850 as a reaction to very special economic and social constellations. These are precisely changing dramatically with the beginning of the 20th century - and thus also the design of the individual Ledigenheim buildings. Initially built from industry to accommodate workers, the development proceeds through experiments in the context of the housing reform movement, the garden city movement or expressionism to genuine program buildings of "classical modernism". Since their main protagonists are the large-scale, nomadic, from place, material ballast, family and national bonding, and "free" people as "timely" adjusted, the building type of "classical modernism" is unheard in the Bredigen district, and the subject of architecture, given to them as a raffoding, as a raffodist, as abubist, as abist, as abist, as abist.
content.title_en: From the Ledigenheim to the Boardinghouse : Building typology and social theory to the end of the Weimar Republic

content.text: Light and transparency: the factory building and the new construction in the architectural magazines of modernism. In the first half of the 20th century, innovative factory buildings were created, which were intensively discussed in the contemporary trade press, as incunabula of modernism. In the interplay of architecture and engineering in the development of glass facades, factory construction became the pioneer of modern architecture. - In the discussion about architectural modernity today, the central role of factory construction is often overlooked. After the founding of the German Werkbund in 1907, however, architects saw the opportunity to develop a new architectural language beyond traditional currents, thus making the question of the relationship between architect and engineer a point of dispute in the relevant debates. Adolf Benehne stated in 1913 that industrial construction was "an almost popular matter today", which attracted more attention to the public than church construction or theatre architecture. After the First World War, new techniques and materials made bold steel structures possible and the complete dissolution of the facade. As a culmination of this development, the daylight factories were created with a glass façade that was pre-hanged by a new generation of industrial architects.
content.title_en: Light and transparency : the factory construction and the new construction in the architectural magazines of the modern age

content.text: Child and Nature: the importance of nature for psychological development. Standard work on the psychological significance of the non-human environment. Human beings are bound to the state of nature as part of nature in the biological-material sense. This is no longer a question in view of the ecological situation. This book now deals with the psychological side of this fundamental ecological context and how it affects the development of children. To this end, theoretical assumptions - especially psychoanalysis and environmental psychology - are developed and empirical findings and observations are evaluated against this background. In this context, it is discussed how the external nature (animals, plants, landscapes) influences the inner nature of man and how a corresponding deficiency ("inhospitable cities", environmental destruction) affects.
content.title_en: Child and Nature: the importance of nature for mental development

content.text: The interpretation of the social and built environment is also interpreted in terms of the urban-planning problems of the city of Essen. The study on urban-planning problems of Essen focuses on the mutual significance of two social-mpirical investigation methods: the perception of urban-planning developments and conflicts via a differentiated text analysis of the regional daily newspaper and the application of qualitative interviews to detect specific identifications of urban dwellers of Altenessen. The newspaper analysis sees itself as a search grid, with which social-spatial problem areas, which signal a change in the relationship between people and the usual (spatial) world of life, can be made visible. The result of this newspaper evaluation revealed Altenessen as a potentially identity-prone district. Therefore, through targeted biographical interviews, the state of individual inhabitants in everyday life under changed structural and social environmental conditions was opened up. The interview evaluation brings to light conclusive evidence, which above all the individual handling of contradictions between the actual urban environment and the urban-planning reality of the urban-planning process of urbanization is interpreted as a concept of a concept of spatial-planning.
content.title_en: The perception of social and built environment : problems of urban development

content.text: The surveyed state: Cartography and the mapping of north-western German territories in the 18th century. In the history of cartography, the 17th century has been considered the "age of the Atlantians", while the 19th century is considered an epoch of official surveying. Christian Fieseler's study is devoted to the development of cartography in the 18th century and pursues its appropriation process through the early modern state: if the production of topographical maps was initially a private economic activity, it became a primary task. The mapping projects of European states and the development of scientific cartography in Germany form the background for four case studies on the north-west of the German Empire: the Principality of Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel, the Electorate of Hanover, the Duchy of Oldenburg and the Prince-Bishopric of Osnabrück are investigated. In a comparative analysis, the author shows what efforts the authorities in these four territories undertook to fully map the respective state. Christian Fieseler makes the phenomenon of "transfer of innovation and practices" visible between the administration and the administration.
content.title_en: The State in the Presence : Cartography and Mapping of North-West German Territories in the 18th Century

content.text: National myth or historical mourning? : the dispute over a central "Holocaust memorial" for the Berlin Republic. 25 June 1999: The German Bundestag decides with a large majority to establish a "Monument for the murdered Jews of Europe" in Berlin. The first was a lengthy controversy, which is to be reckoned with the most important self-conciliation debates of the emerging "Berlin Republic". On the basis of the journalistic statements, the main lines of conflict of the monument dispute are analyzed in this book. A second level of investigation is the artistic drafts, which plastically illustrate the difficulties of the project. From a culturally theoretical, historical didactic and memory-ethical perspective, the questions are also more general: How does historical memory change due to the growing time gap with National Socialism? What can mourning about the murdered of the Nazi rule still mean today?
content.title_en: National myth or historical grief? : the dispute over a central "Holocaust memorial" for the Berlin Republic

content.text: Islam Image and Identity : Subjectivization of German Moroccans between discourse and disposition. From the attacks of September 11, 2001 to the Sarrazin debate: The fact that German Muslims are currently confronted with a negative image is evident. However, how do these negative stereotypes affect the everyday life and identity structures of the affected people? Using the example of German-Moroccan interview partners, Maike Didero demonstrates that divergent reactions to the German Islam image can be explained by different translocal positionings. Her study presents an innovative concept for the analysis of narrative identities as a performative practice based on the subject theories of Laclau/Mouffe, Butler and Bourdieu.
content.title_en: Islam Image and Identity : Subjectivization of German-Moroccans between Discourse and Disposition

content.text: Environment, nature and morality: a critique of Hans Jonas, Vittorio Hösle and Georg Picht. The philosophers Jonas, Hösle and Picht have recognized that the moral questions of environmental issues affect all areas of human action. They see the environmental problem as a sign that the rule of modern reason violates a metaphysical principle of being and therefore advocates a concept of absolute reason in the tradition of Heidegger's philosophy of being, which can provide orientation in technological civilization. However, the problems of justification of an ontological ethics are theologically answered, and the intrinsic conflicts of objectives of collective action cannot be taken into account. The analysis of the evaluation problems shows that ecological, economic-technical and contemplative relations between man and nature are important in determining morally desirable action: "nature" is not required as an ontological principle.
content.title_en: Environment, nature and morality: a critique of Hans Jonas, Vittorio Hösle and Georg Picht

content.text: The power of memory : the emergence and transformation of local writing culture in late medieval Augsburg. The study opens a new look at the process of the creation of local writing culture in a European city of the late Middle Ages. The history of Augsburg's extensive tradition shows how several generations of urban authorities increasingly depended on writing in the course of growing emancipation and expressed their own needs for archiving. The writing process was a complex process that covered important areas of life and parts of urban society in different times and intensity. Less than previously assumed, this was about pragmatic effectivation of government action. The driving force of writing in the late Middle Ages was a growing need for control and verifiability.
content.title_en: The Power of Memory : Origin and Change of Local Writing Culture in Late Middle Ages Augsburg

content.text: Social structure analyses with lifestyles: a study on the theoretical and methodological reorientation of lifestyle research. Lifestyles as an analysis tool - The lifestyle concept has been discussed for two decades as an alternative to classical concepts of social structure analysis. However, the previous yield of lifestyle research is rather meager. The main problems of research practice are: the lack of comparability of lifestyle typologies; their theoretical poverty; the questionable reality content of individual lifestyle types; the survey effort of lifestyle variables. The study claims to solve these problems by developing a theoretically justified and empirically efficient analytical instrument. In three primary surveys, the developed typology is used to analyse individual party preferences, resident segregation, integration in urban scenes, holiday destination selection and the composition of social networks. This enables the answer to the overarching question of work: Which performance capabilities do lifestyles have compared to classical analysis concepts?
content.title_en: Social structure analyses with lifestyles : a study on the theoretical and methodological reorientation of lifestyle research

content.text: Iron in 19th century architecture. Iron was the first building material to change from a artisanal to an industrial building material at the beginning of the 19th century. This development involved countless innovations in the fields of calculation, processing and application. Christian Schädlich's work examines iron as a building material based on the architectural problems and its approaches to solving them. The analysis of production development follows the explanation of all the exemplary supporting and supporting structures. This is the basis for the analysis of the construction tasks existing in the 19th century in the second part of the work. The text is illustrated by hundreds of schema sketches by the author, as well as by large-format historical and current illustrations.
content.title_en: Iron in 19th century architecture

content.text: Football in Europe: a comparative study of the training systems and the professional image of the football coach in professional football in selected EU countries. The coach in the highly paid professional football of today's Europe is often the focus of the event. He makes decisions which either lead to victory or defeat, which has serious sporting and financial implications. But what is hidden behind the person of the football coach is the present study: on the one hand, the trainer training systems of Germany, England and Greece are presented and analysed, on the other hand, the coach himself. The person is represented as well as his attitude regarding the training of trainers and the Europeanization of training. Finally, the main characteristics of the professional practice such as employment situation and dismissal/unemployment are examined. This country-like study moves against the background of an accelerated professionalization and commercialization in the European top football and tries to present the dimensions of the training and professional image of the football coach with their special social backgrounds.
content.title_en: Football in Europe: a comparative study of the training systems and professional profile of professional football coach in selected EU countries

content.text: The grip on the churches: ideological and historical handling of war-destroyed church buildings in the GDR. Churches destroyed in the Second World War were neglected in the GDR for ideological reasons until collapse, often even blown up. Surprisingly, however, they were rebuilt just as much by both denominations as by the socialist state. - But who and what decided on reconstruction or demolition? In what form did the churches be rebuilt? What constraints did the socialist state subject them to? What do they convey about the SED, its church policy and the prescribed understanding of history, but also about the situation of the confessions in the GDR? This is illustrated by the examples of East Berlin, Potsdam, Magdeburg, Leipzig and Dresden
content.title_en: The grip on churches : ideological and conservationist handling of war-destroyed church buildings in the GDR

content.text: Product group analysis with POS scanning data: key data analysis methods for the consumer goods industry. Scanning data has been an important information basis for trade management and industrial sales management for some time. However, in company practice, especially in small and medium-sized enterprises, the methods for analysis of scanning data and the associated problems of scanning data research are largely unknown. Consequently, the information potential of scanning data in German business practice is not sufficient, practically not used at all in the middle class. From the point of view of small and medium-sized enterprises, therefore, a competitive disadvantage is often created compared to large companies, which partly have their own analysis methods or can buy cost-intensive data evaluations from market research institutes. This scenario illustrates the delay in the use of scanning data in the Federal Republic of Germany. In the present publication, the current state of use of scanning data for scanning data is described in the USA, on the other hand, the analysis of scanning data is one of the usual methods of obtaining market data.
content.title_en: Product group analysis with POS scanning data : key data-based analysis methods for the consumer goods industry

content.text: Political geography as spatial conflict research : Concepts for the analysis of the political and social organization of the space based on Anglo-American research approaches. Based on urban development policy projects in Vancouver, Canada, and the expansion of the port in Hamburg, the attempt is made to combine geographical spatial concepts and conflicts with political perspectives.
content.title_en: Political geography as spatial conflict research : concepts for the analysis of the political and social organization of space based on Anglo-American research approaches

content.text: Aspects of systems for separate urine collection and treatment - selected techniques and potential implementation in an urban context. To investigate the potential of separate collection and treatment of urine in an urban context, quantities and nutrient concentrations of substrate from public urinals were measured. A nutrient recovery and a reduction of micropollutants in the form of pharmaceutical residues were realized, among other things, by rectification and evaporation in a pilot scale. Transport and effort were discussed in relation to the magnitude of the overall system. Collectable amounts and concentration of public urinals were measured, to evaluate the potential of a system for separate urine collection and treatment in an urban context. The collected substance was produced among others by evaluation for nutrient recovery and reduction of micropollutants as pharmaceutical residues.
content.title_en: Aspects of systems for separate urine collection and treatment - selected techniques and potential implementation in an urban context

content.text: Destructive characterization of micromechanical structures for production-related applications. Monitoring of production steps in microsystem technology is an important point in increasing yield and reducing production costs. This includes characterization of all system components in early production steps and sorting out defective components. A particular challenge is the mechanical components of the microsystems, for whose characterization non-electrical measurement parameters are required and thus a use of the test methods used in microelectronics is not possible. The present work presents basic investigations of micromechanical structures, whose results can be used for a non-destructive structural characterization in early production steps. For this purpose, the deformation behaviour and self-vibration of micromechanical beams, plates and membranes are determined numerically by the finite element method and experimentally investigated by means of white light interferometry and laser doppler vibrometry. Building on the determined properties, the possible methods of production are also evaluated for the possible defects.
content.title_en: Non-destructive characterisation of micromechanical structures for production-accompanying applications

content.text: Paul Ludwig Troost : (1878-1934). In the 1910s and 1920s Paul Ludwig Troost (1878-1934) was one of the most sought after interior designers in Germany in the field of conservative luxury interiors. In 1930, he was also entrusted with the conversion of the Munich party headquarters of the NSDAP in Hitler's big-bourgeois environment. Troost subsequently designed further facilities for the party leader and, above all, buildings whose strict reduction classicism, due to Hitler's will, became decisive for the official representational architecture of National Socialism. Troost's remarkable career, his cooperation with Hitler and his subsequent work in the "Third Reich" are presented and examined in detail for the first time in this book, his architectural oeuvre is made accessible in a catalogue.
content.title_en: Paul Ludwig Troost : (1878-1934)

content.text: Private small businesses in Vietnam: the framework conditions and obstacles to their development. The economic reforms initiated by the Vietnamese government in the mid-eighties have led to significant changes in the micro-level, in addition to fundamental macroeconomic stabilisation. Private economic activities of small and family businesses, whose number of enterprises has increased rapidly with increasing legitimation, dominate already in agriculture and in the service sector and are also gaining importance in the manufacturing sector. They pursue the protection of family income with a start-up of their businesses. However, the potential to develop into competitive, growing economic units is limited. The economic, legal and institutional environment that private small businesses are subject to in the establishment and management of their businesses and the resulting factors that affect their development are the central theme of this work. Problems of small businesses in northern Vietnam, which cannot look back on a market economy-oriented past like the South Vietnamese, are particularly taken into account. Finally, the areas in which small businesses have opportunities for successful business development are highlighted.
content.title_en: Private small businesses in Vietnam: framework conditions and barriers to their development

content.text: The right to copyright is referred to as the "Magna Charter of the Information Society". Digitalisation and dissemination of works via the Internet have required a reform of copyright law in order to continue to meet the interests of rightholders and users. In this work, the redesign of copyright rules is assessed taking into account European and constitutional requirements and a guideline for the design of an appropriate copyright policy in the digital field. The focus is on the question of how a balance between the rights of the users and the application and legal protection of technical protection measures can be achieved.
content.title_en: Equalisation of interests in the information society: the adaptation of copyright barriers in the digital sector

content.text: European steel policy between political objectives and economic constraints. Publisher's information: The European steel industry has been subject to profound structural change since the early sixties. The EU Commission and the governments of the Member States have since taken extensive economic policy measures to overcome the steel crises. This study of European steel policy takes into account both economic and institutional aspects. It also analyses the background to the U.S.-EU steel trade conflicts. Numerous interviews have been incorporated into the study and the results of the author's extensive studies abroad have increased the practical value of the study. Overall, based on national and supranational objectives, the study offers a comprehensive analysis of industrial and external trade policy measures; it illustrates the urgency of establishing a politically independent European competition authority. The work is therefore aimed, in addition to science, at representatives of companies and their associations as well as at politics.
content.title_en: European steel policy between policy objectives and economic constraints
