content.text: Simplification models for welding default calculation. The inhomogeneous heating of welding compounds results in deformations which need to be eliminated by cost-intensive after-treatment. The mechanism of the forming of heat elongations and self-stresses is explained in this work and the relevant temperature-dependent material parameters as well as the significantly affecting temperature field during welding are presented and illustrated. Subsequently, the procedure is discussed in the application of the currently available methods and models for welding default calculation. Starting with FE simulation, the maximum temperature model, the model of inherent elongations and the local global model is explained. Very detailed is the description of the analytical shrinkage force model. The verification of the software, the coupling algorithm and the study of the stability and sensitivity of the hybrid model is carried out on stump joints. The validation is done at elementary welding connections, followed by the delay calculation of a demonstrator with 8 and a complete deck section from the shipbuilding with 90 welds is carried out. The core of the work is sufficiently large-scalely the calculation of the new structure, the hybrid is sufficiently large-scalely investigated.
content.title_en: Simplified models for welding default calculation

content.text: The right to guarantee information from electronic databases. Information is becoming increasingly important as an economic asset in an information society. The types of contracts of the BGB have been developed at a time when trade in goods and services dominated the market. Information has gained a comparatively small place; the BGB differentiates between goods and rights alone. As the subject of economic transactions, information therefore raises a number of new questions. The work is undertaken to clarify questions concerning the legal classification of the BGB's contractual typology and the rights of guarantee in the event of a poor performance in the case of a particular case of the information retrieval from electronic databases. (Source: Text Verlagseinband / Verlag)
content.title_en: Right of guarantee for the retrieval of information from electronic databases

content.text: Implementation and enforcement of immission limits in air quality law : illustrated by the example of compliance with particle limits (PM10). This work takes up the discussion on compliance with immission limits for fine dust. It deals with the problems of the transposition of European guidelines into German law, in particular with the new Directive 2008/50/EC, and addresses the differences arising from the combination of technology and law. The issue is the liability of immission limits, the establishment of air pollution and action plans as well as the adoption of concrete plant and traffic-related measures. The discussion will then discuss whether third parties have and how they can assert their claims on compliance with immission limits. (Source: Text Verlagseinband / Verlag)
content.title_en: Implementation and enforcement of Immission Limits in Air Quality Law : illustrated by the example of compliance with Particulate Limits (PM10)

content.text: The basics of the spring-winding system must be more precisely manufactured and more robust. To meet these requirements, the entire product-forming process must be checked and each individual working step optimised. The present work therefore includes fundamental studies on the spring-winding process and the effects of spring-winding parameters and wind machine parameters on the resulting spring-spring geometry, for the production of higher load-bearing screw-pressure springs and for the influence of end and transition coils on the function and production of screw-pressure springs. The wire parameters specified in standards allow only insufficient statements about the forming behaviour of the wire and the consistency of these parameters over the wire-length. With the developed test methods Long spring and test equipment with sensor wheel, fluctuations in the forming behaviour are made visible. The consideration of the extensive examination results for the impact of the wind-machine assembly groups Haspel, directional apparatus, turning and drawing rollers, wire guide and the wind-winding tools on the geometry parameters of the wound screw-spring are made more stable. The high-level adjustment time for the variable-wind-tools can be used for the variable-weight adjustment of the variable-wind-s.
content.title_en: Accuracy and load-optimized screw pressure springs

content.text: The concept presented in this book fills a gap in the research status on the field of process-related real-time communication for reconfigurable production systems. Current real-time networks used in automation technology are characterized by high configuration costs, which occur during commissioning and after each reconfiguration. For the realization of "Plug and Produce"-capable applications it is necessary to reduce these costs as much as possible. To this end, the development of a procedure for the automatic configuration of current real-time networks used in automation technology is described in this book. Specifically, the real-time networks Profinet, Ethernet/IP, Ethernet Powerlink and Ethercat are considered. For these networks, the information required for commissioning is first examined. Based on this, the concept for automatic configuration is developed. Based on a test person study, the scope of the implementation of the automatic configuration can be reduced by the automatic configuration. The author Dr.-Ing. Lars Dürkop studied information system technology at the Technical University of Braunschweig and has been working as a scientific employee at the Institute for industrial information technology – the Rppe identification of the university - the technical parameter - the technical parameter - the technical parameter - the technical concept - the strate and the strate
content.title_en: Automatic configuration of real-time Ethernet

Gerold Weber: "Wells and watercrafts in France in the age of Louis XIV". With a typological overview of the French fountains from 1500 onwards. Wernersche Verlagsgesellschaft, Grüne Reihe vol. 8, Worms 1985. 356 pp., 126 plates with 285 black and white illustrations, born, 185,- DM
content.title_en: Fountains and watercraft in France in the age of Louis XIV : with a typographical overview of the French fountains from 1500

content.text: Alternative estimations for the production potential in the euro area. In modern monetary policy strategies, the concept of production potential plays an important role. It represents the sustainable production potential of an economy that can be realized without risks to price stability. However, for empirical application, production potential must be estimated, whereby the user can choose from a variety of alternative estimation methods. The present work complements the existing literature by discussing the theoretical foundation of new estimations of production potential and compares their empirical performance in the context of an application to the European currency area. The results show no clear superiority of a particular approach in terms of empirical performance. In addition, the alternative methods come to very different estimates of the level of production potential. This uncertainty greatly limits the applicability of production potential as a monetary policy indicator. Therefore, estimates of production potential should be interpreted with caution in the context of monetary policy strategies.
content.title_en: Alternative estimates of production potential in the euro area

content.text: Research organization in higher education institutes : the case of mechanical engineering. The strong third-party funding orientation of university research institutes in the field of engineering and their sophisticated orientation towards problems in business practice have reinforced the view that these research units mainly conduct application-related research without a basic reference and with little thematic coherence or without a comprehensive content bracket. This text contradicts the fact that universal research institutes are pursuing thematically cohesive programmes, which must be mediated between a number of organizational boundary conditions. These aspects were described in the example of 13 university research institutes from mechanical engineering. (PHF/uebern.)
content.title_en: Research organization in higher education institutions : the case of mechanical engineering

content.text: The legal and legal frameworks of a hierarchy of standards are examined in all the regulations with a medical reference to their legal effects. From the requirements of international and European law to laws and legal regulations to the law of standing, from the publications of the Federal Medical Association and the medical societies to the regulations of the contract medical law to the questions of medical ethics and the medical standard, the entire area of medical law is systematized in practice. The work deals with issues of liability and the ranking of the medical profession of the behavioral requirements. Starting from the legal theoretical bases and the constitutional framework of a standard hierarchy, all regulations with a medical reference are presented and examined on their legal effects. From the requirements of international and European law to laws and regulations to the law of standing, from the publications of the Federal Medical Association and medical societies to the regulations of the contract medical law to the questions of medical ethics and medical standards, the entire area of medical law is systematized in a practical manner.
content.title_en: Standard hierarchy in medical law

content.text: Art protection in occupied Germany: Restitution and cultural policy in the French and American occupation zone (1944-1953). The Allied art restitution programmes of the first post-war years have hardly been investigated. Following on from historical research on occupation policy, Emily Löffler traces the French and American programmes in her book: from 1944 until the transfer of cultural restitution into German hands at the beginning of the 1950s. She locates them in the context of Allied cultural and occupation policy and analyses how certain concepts of cultural heritage and patriarchal restitution shaped the field of tension between interallied cooperation and national self-interest. The book provides important impulses for the history of art history, for research on restitution and reparation and not least sees itself as a contribution to fundamental research for provenance research.
content.title_en: Art protection in occupied Germany : Restitution and cultural policy in the French and American occupation zone (1944-1953)

content.text: Brand effect of sponsorship: A time series analysis using the example of the Formula 1 commitment of an automobile manufacturer. Folding text: Sponsoring is one of the established instruments of brand communication. In view of the cost explosion in many areas, controlling sponsoring effectiveness is an urgent task. However, previous research work is often undifferentiated and time-related, so that no relationship between cause and effect can be established. Consequently, in practice – if at all – a general control of sponsorship effect is carried out. David Woisetschläger examines the brand effect of sponsorship over time and with the method of growth mixing modelling, which is used for the first time in the marketing context. This enables the individual adjustments in the structural model to be assessed with simultaneous segmentation according to (un)observable consumer heterogeneity. An extensive empirical study can be used to identify class-specific effects of sponsorship. Consequently, communication effects can be measured more precisely and more reliable statements about the effectiveness of the measures can be derived within the framework of a brand controlling.
content.title_en: Brand effect of sponsorship : A time series analysis using the example of the Formula 1 commitment of an automobile manufacturer

content.text: The decline of the entrepreneurial state: Privatization policy in the UK, France, Italy and Germany. Preliminary considerations -- International context -- Formation and development of the public economy -- Great Britain -- France -- Italy -- Germany -- Analysis and explanation of privatisation profiles -- Summary and outlook Florian Mayer uses the example of four OECD countries to shed light on the state's loss of function and functional change: the change in the division of labour between the state and the market and the change from the performance to the regulatory/guarantee state. The focus is on privatisation policy: Despite the general privatisation trend, differences between the OECD countries' state activity profiles can be identified. The author presents commonalities, differences and convergence processes in the privatisation policy of the four OECD countries France, Great Britain, Italy and Germany. Finally, he discusses the crucial question: Are the privatisations of duration or a wave of renationalisation to be expected?
content.title_en: The decline of the entrepreneurial state: Privatization policy in the UK, France, Italy and Germany

content.text: Investment and planning in retail trade: Influence of spatial planning systems and institutional investors on structural change in metropolitan retail trade. State of research -- Theoretical conceptual framework -- Case study Germany -- Case study United Kingdom -- Summary: Results, further research questions and urban policy desiderate -- Annexes -- Literature The book deals with the relationship between spatial planning and real estate cycles as factors influencing structural change in retail trade. The main thesis is that spatial planning is only limited in terms of the particularly critical type of operation of large-scale shopping centres. This thesis was reviewed by a comparative approach between two countries with different traditions and orientations of spatial planning: Great Britain and Germany and the two metropolises London and Berlin. As a surprising result, it was clear that urban governance remains a controlling influence. However, this is only related to locations, not to the change of the type of operation itself, and it also requires complementary control at a supra-local level.
content.title_en: Investment and planning in retail trade: influence of spatial planning systems and institutional investors on structural change in metropolitan retailing

content.text: The fight against international Islamist terrorism. International Islamist terrorism - features and dangers -- Normative foundations of the fight against terrorism by the Federal Republic of Germany -- Anti-terrorism - from the term to the instrument of analysis -- Measures of the Federal Republic of Germany to combat international Islamist terrorism -- Symmetries and asymmetries of the approach to combat -- Recommendations for optimising the approach to combat -- Final consideration Johannes Urban examines the strengths and weaknesses of the German approach to international Islamist terrorism. Using a "target strategy model" based on the instrument of the purpose-mean analysis, the Federal Republic's approach to combat terrorism is characterized and evaluated. The author determines which strategies should be used to achieve which goals - and which means were used. To what extent appropriate, the relationship between state measures to specific hazard characteristics of international Islamist terrorism, i.e. whether measures were symmetric or asymmetrical to those. Based on the need for action identified in this way - but on the basis of valid normative bases and principles - gives recommendations on how the German approach to combat it could be optimized in an operational and organisational way.
content.title_en: Combating International Islamist Terrorism

content.text: Integrated communication in multi-stage markets: Theoretical and empirical analysis using the example of the Swiss mobile communications industry. Numerous concepts in science and practice aim at networking and uniform alignment of the communication tools of companies. In this context, one-stage markets are usually assumed, i.e. the communication activities are primarily carried out from the provider to the target groups. However, many industries are dealing with multi-stage markets in which an intermediate switching of sales intermediaries endangers the realization of effective and efficient integrated communication. Sales intermediaries practice influential communication functions that can only influence, control and control the providers conditionally. Kristina Lasotta examines the emergence and reduction of possible conflicts as well as deficits of integrated communication in multi-stage markets. The basis of the empirical study is expert discussions in the Swiss mobile communications industry. The author derives from the findings gained recommendations for the management of the coordination and control of sales intermediaries. "Integrated communication in multi-stage markets ▪ addresses the identification of lecturers and students in the field of marketing and communication as well as managers in companies with communication and marketing responsibility. The multi-stageness of markets as a challenge for integrated communication in the framework of integrated communication The concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of communication in the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of communication in the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of communication in the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the communication in the concept of the concept of the communication in the concept of the concept of the concept of the communication in the concept of the concept of the concept of the communication in the communication in the concept of the communication in the communication.
content.title_en: Integrated communication in multi-stage markets: Theoretical and empirical analysis using the example of the Swiss mobile communications industry

content.text: The efficiency of interaction platforms: efficiency and effectiveness at the interface with the customer. Interaction platforms are considered to be the successful business model on the Internet at the interface between companies and customers. However, up to now, most operators have not managed to generate relevant revenue gains. Rather, moderation, care and technical support are associated with significant expenditures, which often do not match adequate revenues. Compared to the level of knowledge in assessing traditional economic assets, however, the systematic analysis and economic assessment of innovative information and communication systems are at a rudimentary stage. Michael Ney presents a detailed analysis of interaction platforms, with particular emphasis on customer bundling, customer retention and process rationalization effects. He also examines the extent to which current processes of economic efficiency can be transferred to interaction platforms. On this basis, he develops a holistic evaluation approach for innovative information and communication systems, which illustrates the interaction between organisation, technology and users. Basis of economicity consideration -- interaction platforms -- The assessment problem in interaction platforms -- Conception of a customer-based assessment of interaction platforms - Summary of interaction platforms.
content.title_en: Efficiency of interaction platforms : Efficiency and effectiveness at the interface with the customer

content.text: Late project breakdowns in R&D : A behavioral analysis. Basics -- Derivation of an explanatory model -- Derivation of relevant factors -- Derivation of possible countermeasures -- Critical assessment. Failing projects - especially in the context of research and development - are often abandoned much later than a rational, economic consideration would recommend. However, such late break-offs lead to high efficiency and efficiency losses for companies. As the classical-economic theory of this phenomenon cannot be satisfactorily explained, Eric Zayer uses the findings of behavioral escalation-of-commitment research to identify and structure the causes of late break-offs. Based on the findings, he then derives concrete and pragmatically feasible measures, which help controllers ensure timely termination of unsuccessful projects.
content.title_en: Late project terminations in R&D : A behavioral analysis

content.text: The role of the user in the buying center: The example of procurement and marketing of biotechnological consumption products. The analysis of the buying center, the mental summary of all stakeholders involved in purchasing decisions in organizations, is an important building block in B2B marketing for targeted derivation of marketing measures. In corresponding scientific studies, the buyer has been focused so far, while in marketing practice in many cases users of procurement objects are also considered to be of high importance. Ludger Rolfes analyses the behaviour of users in procurement decisions using the example of the biotechnology industry. Based on an empirical investigation, he shows that users exercise different roles in procurement decisions, which should be taken into account in the targeted derivation of marketing measures. The author provides information on the design of measures in marketing management of a provider of biotechnological consumption products and derives implications for marketing research. Approaches for the analysis of organisational procurement behaviour - explanations on the behaviour of users in the procurement process - A synopsis of empirical research on the behaviour of users in the marketing process - An empirical analysis of the consumption-management of user-representation-Instruction of the procurement-Instruction of the procurement-Instruction of the procurement-Instruction of the procurement-Instruction of the procurement-Instruction of the procurement-Instruction of the procurement-Ins
content.title_en: The role of the user in the buying centre : The example of procurement and marketing of biotechnological consumables

content.text: Six Sigma Performance Measurement System : Process controlling as a tool of modern corporate management. Basics and terminology delimitation of different quality approaches -- Six Sigma in use as a company-wide strategy -- Total Six Sigma Key Data System -- Pilot Application -- Final remark. Given the increasing dynamics of today's markets, companies are forced to introduce different directions combining strategies. Six Sigma as a modern, customer-oriented quality management strategy offers a decisive promising approach that combines generic competitive strategies cost leadership and differentiation. Serkan Tavasli designs a method for developing, evaluating, and aggregating key data in the context of a process identification system with the help of Six Sigma Strategy. To this end, he first defines Six Sigma, assigns the strategy to common approaches and sets a delimitation to prevailing quality management strategies. Based on this, he develops a framework concept for the introduction of Six Sigma.
content.title_en: Six Sigma Performance Measurement System : Process controlling as an instrument of modern corporate management

content.text: Recommendations in tourism: An analysis of influential recommendation providers of tourist destinations. Chris Horbel analyses the determinants of the submission of recommendations in tourism and represents factors of the influence of recommendations on purchase decisions. Dr. Chris Horbel is a research associate at Prof. Dr. Herbert Woratschek at the Chair of Service Management at the University of Bayreuth. Tourism is an extremely competitive industry. Therefore, one of the most important tasks in the marketing of tourist destinations is the constant recruitment of new customers. Although recommendations are considered particularly effective, they are rarely successfully integrated into marketing because there are no indications of how recommendations can be initiated.Chris Horbel analyses the determinants of the submission of recommendations and represents factors of the influence of recommendations on purchase decisions. Based on an empirical study, she identifies various customer segments that have different preferences regarding the characteristics of influential recommendation providers. Furthermore, the author shows which conditions must be fulfilled in order to communicate recommendations. Finally, she directs reference points for tourism managers to identify appropriate opinion recommendations in order to identify the relevant opinion providers.
content.title_en: Recommendations in tourism : An analysis of influential recommendation providers of tourist destinations

content.text: Business analysis on operational data. Basics -- Transactional system -- Data Warehouse and Data Mart -- Main storage-based system -- Operational business intelligence: prototyping -- Summary and outlook. An important strategy for increasing competitiveness is for companies to obtain information from operational data. Existing systems are optimized for operational or dispositive data processing. However, the incompatibility of current business data with historical business analysis means that information acquisition processes are cost- and time-intensive. Pascal Schmidt-Volkmar examines whether the distinction between operational and dispositive data processing can be resolved. He develops the concept of a main storage-based system that supports both system types. Using a prototype, he demonstrates the practical suitability for large data stocks. The concept meets the requirements of Operational Business Intelligence and provides impulses for the design of future data warehouse architectures.
content.title_en: Business analysis on operational data

content.text: Project organization and financing of renovation measures in housing: development of a decision-making model for clients. The main task of many companies and actors in the housing industry is to revitalise their residential properties in the coming decades. One of the key tasks in the run-up to renovation measures is the selection of the project organisation and financing form for the implementation of construction performance. Michael Willwerth develops a decision-making model that allows the identification of suitable project organisation and financing forms for renovation measures in housing. In practical tests with housing companies, he applies his model to two renewal measures and develops concrete recommendations for action. The application of the model allows housing companies and potential clients to identify, according to systematic and comprehensible criteria, the project organisation and financing forms for their renewal measures, which are most advantageous in economic, ecological, social and aesthetic terms. Basics -- Project organisation forms for renewal measures in housing -- Financing forms for renewal measures in housing -- Development of a decision-making model for the selection of project organization and financing form -- Practical tests -- Benefits and limits -- Conclusion.
content.title_en: Project organisation and financing of renovation measures in housing : development of a decision-making model for contracting entities

content.text: Start-up networks in the scientific and university fields: Challenges for economic development. Research subject and research questions -- Research design -- Theoretical preliminary considerations -- Empirical -- Theoretical model formation -- Synthesis -- Resume and research desiderata. In Germany there are thousands of public economic promotion programmes and a huge number of economic promotion promoters. However, it is to be asked whether this immense selection is useful for the companies to be promoted and start-ups. Alexander Knuth examines this question in the context of business start-ups from the scientific and university fields by means of interviews, surveys, expert workshops and process analyses. He shows that entrepreneurs need intensive dialogues and continuous support for their start-up preparations, because they hardly even see the range of funding opportunities themselves. Moreover, cooperation between the funding providers is set high barriers. Therefore, for optimal support of the start-up projects, coordination of funding offers is required. The author explains under which circumstances a central or network coordination is most effective and efficient and how the cooperation of the funding providers can be actively supported by the policy makers, but also actively supported.
content.title_en: Start-up networks in the field of science and higher education: challenges for business promotion

content.text: Road user charges in cities: acceptance and mobility behaviour. Road user charges are considered a promising tool for reducing traffic and environmental pollution in cities. A significant implementation has so far failed due to low acceptance. However, this increases significantly in cities that have introduced road user charges. Tina Gehlert analyses the behaviour and acceptance data of an extensive field trial in Copenhagen and examines the question whether the increased acceptance is due to the decrease in car use as a reaction to the charges. Their results show that acceptance is highly dynamic and therefore influencing, but the reduction in car use cannot be confirmed as a cause of the positive acceptance change. The presentation of the psychological foundations and practical examples of European cities' pricing systems give new impetus to the discussion about innovative pricing instruments in the transport sector in Europe and Germany.
content.title_en: Road charging in cities : acceptance and mobility behaviour

content.text: Customer loyalty through recommendation : An experimental study of the effect of positive customer recommendations on the binding of the recommender. Customer recommendations are considered one of the most effective marketing instruments. However, only the effects of a recommendation on the recipient of the message have been investigated so far. However, the effect of the submission of a recommendation on the recommender is not what the effect of the recommendation on the recommender has. Based on behavioural scientific theories, Ina Garnefeld derives hypotheses on customer loyalty through recommendation and empirically checks them by means of two experimental studies. Based on the experiments carried out, it demonstrates the influence of the submission of a positive customer recommendation on the engagement and behavioural customer loyalty of the recommender. Customer recommendations therefore not only represent an effective instrument for the acquisition of new customers, but can also serve the customer loyalty. Conceptual foundations -- Development of the investigation model - Empirical-experimental investigation -- Final examination.
content.title_en: Customer loyalty through recommendation : An experimental study of the effect of positive customer recommendations on the binding of the recommender

content.text: Performance Measurement in Nonprofit Organizations. Introduction -- Starting position for Performance Measurement in Nonprofit Organizations -- Idea and development stages of Performance Measurement -- Stand of Performance Measurement in Nonprofit Organizations from an empirical point of view -- Performance Measurement from a theoretical point of view -- Summary and outlook. Many private Nonprofit organizations are now more under pressure than ever to use their resources efficiently and effectively. Furthermore, a public-oriented presentation of performance capacity is necessary. In this context, Performance Measurement is becoming important as a reporting and control tool for private Nonprofit organizations. Dorothea Greiling uses a descriptive, empirical and theoretical perspective to address performance measurement in private Nonprofit organizations and compiles an overview. It presents the results of two primary surveys on the state of Performance Measurement and the operationalization of success in voluntary institutions of the Health and Social Sector. In addition, the author discusses the possibilities and limitations of performance measurement and develops an overview for the nonprofit organization as well as the nonprofit performance reporting.
content.title_en: Performance Measurement in Nonprofit Organizations

content.text: Customer-oriented institutions as carriers of innovation-relevant customer knowledge: Sales and trade as potential integrators in product innovation. Although the importance of customer orientation as a success factor of product innovation is obvious, knowledge of customer needs in corporate practice is often insufficiently managed. This applies in particular to the knowledge of employees at the interface to the customer, which could provide the basis for new solutions and innovative ideas in the early phase of the innovation process. Verena Rath first assesses the "customer-oriented institutions" with regard to their awareness of the potential relevance of innovation activities. It shows that sales and trade are highly customer-intensive, but for example, due to predominantly sales and sales-oriented control, are only sensitized to a small extent for innovation activities. It presents, among other things, on the basis of an empirical study how these areas act as "customer-knowledge integrator" and thus support market- and customer-oriented product development.
content.title_en: Customer-oriented institutions as carriers of innovation-relevant customer knowledge : Sales and trade as potential integrators in product innovations

content.text: Rational herd behaviour and its impact on investment decisions: An analysis of herd behaviour caused by information and payment externalities with regard to investment decisions. Financial crises with their appearances of stock market bubbles and bank collapses cause mass phenomena that are expressed by herd behaviour. However, there is no compelling methodical approach to research on mass phenomena, which can be done in various ways. The decision-making behaviour of individual actors leading to herd behaviour is at the heart of Bingyu Zhu's investigation. By classifying the different causes, the mechanisms of herd behaviour are depicted and then proposed measures to remove this inefficient behaviour. It is evident that rational herd behaviour can be understood as an answer of individuals to uncertainty and information asymmetry in the decision-making environment. By analysing the interaction of information and payment externality, the author notes that a manager will pay less attention to his private information than to an information externality and a course of investigation of the framework of the herd-relationality-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-relationship-be-be-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-beh-
content.title_en: Rational herd behaviour and its impact on investment decisions: An analysis of herd behaviour caused by information and payment externalities in relation to investment decisions

content.text: Innovation management in biotechnology: Sustainability is a guiding principle of a development-accompanying evaluation. The topic of sustainability with its three pillars of ecology, economy and social affairs is becoming increasingly important in the development of new production processes and products. Biotechnology is seen by many experts as key technology and biotechnological innovations are regarded as promoters and promoters of social change in the way of dealing with the environment. Pascal Zuber focuses on the management of the early phases of biotechnological developments in terms of economic sustainability. He develops an economic evaluation model with which biotechnological development processes can be evaluated and approaches can be given to managing the innovation process. For the economic value of biotechnological innovations, especially non-monetary elements of the environment such as legal framework conditions or social acceptance are important. Biotechnological product and process development in competition -- Biotechnology: potential, application and development -- Methodical foundations of the evaluation concept -- Evaluation concept for assessing economic sustainability -- Case study: Pyruvat production -- Outlook.
content.title_en: Innovation management in biotechnology: sustainability as a guiding principle of a development-accompanying evaluation

content.text: Mobile qualified electronic signatures: Analysis of barriers and design proposals for introduction. Technical and legal bases -- Diffusion and adoption theory -- The market for qualified signatures -- Applications for qualified signatures -- Business models for qualified signatures -- Strategies for achieving critical mass -- Mobile qualified signatures -- Evaluation of economic relevance -- Summary. The legislator established a legal framework with the signature law more than 10 years ago that regulates the use, requirements and legal consequences of electronic signatures. Nevertheless, electronic signatures have not yet been able to prevail on the market. Heiko Roßnagel examines the causes of the lack of market success with the help of diffusion and adoption theory. As a central obstacle, he identifies the low number of applications and missing strategies for achieving critical mass and low-success business models of certification services providers. The author presents mobile qualified electronic signatures as an alternative and analyses their technical and legal feasibility. New applications are presented and alternative business models and implementation strategies discussed. By means of an economic analysis, he finally shows under which conditions mobile qualified electronic signatures can be justified in mobile mobile operators.
content.title_en: Mobile qualified electronic signatures : Analysis of barriers and suggestions for introduction

content.text: Network infrastructure management: concepts for the electricity industry. The basics and challenges of the grid business in the electricity industry -- concepts for grid infrastructure management in the electricity industry -- grid infrastructure management framework -- result summary and outlook. The electricity industry is undergoing a fundamental change through global liberalisation efforts. The main features are the separation of the grid business from the integrated value chain of the established power supply companies, the so-called "unbundling", and the introduction of regulatory efficiency requirements for grid usage charges, the so-called "incentive regulation". For performance management in the natural monopoly area of the grid business, this means a significant increase in requirements. Andreas Stender develops a concept for the management of an independent electricity network business in the context of incentive regulation. His network performance cockpit (NPC) enables an integrated overall consideration of the essential performance areas from the perspective of asset management. From the perspective of asset owners, the NPC in particular can illustrate the business-specific restrictions of the grid business as well as the long-term maintenance of the supply quality of the asset management system.
content.title_en: Network infrastructure management : concepts for the electricity industry

content.text: The diffusion of complex products and systems: a system-dynamic approach. Due to developments in information and communication technology in recent years, interactions and network effects in products are becoming increasingly important. Complex products and systems are among the products requiring explanation, through which additional benefits must be communicated individually with the customer. Sabine Schmidt examines the market penetration of complex products and systems, essential factors affecting the diffusion process and the interaction of consumer behaviour and diffusion. She analyses various diffusion models that consider interactions and interactions of products and develops the consumer-relevant characteristics of complex products and systems. The model developed by her on this basis improves the understanding of the interaction of these cost-intensive products, which have an increased purchasing risk due to the high product complexity. In addition, a meaningful survey was conducted. Diffusion theory -- Complex products and systems -- Research method: System-dynamic approach -- Structure of the diffusion model for COPS -- Analysis of model behaviour - Strategic control of the diffusion process -- Summary and outlook.
content.title_en: Diffusion of complex products and systems : A system dynamic approach

content.text: Model breaks in business models: A reference framework for innovative strategy concepts. Challenges for companies: Deriving requirements for the framework to be developed -- The business model: Positioning as a design tool and basis of the framework -- Instruments of the pattern break: Development of the central elements of the framework -- Summary and outlook. Patterns are action-driven basic assumptions that shape and influence entrepreneurial activities. Through the heads of management, they find their way into the business models of companies and determine the fate of companies and entire industries. But what exactly effect do patterns and how can constructively be dealt with with with? Tobias Umbeck uses nine case examples from the aviation industry to investigate how patterns can be systematically analysed, evaluated and meaningfully broken in his own business model. A framework is created that can be used to sustainably strengthen the overall system of enterprise and to promote the innovative power of all employees. In addition to the creation of new "tools" for practitioners, a gap in current research is closed by the scientific examination of patterns and strategies.
content.title_en: Model breaks in business models : A reference framework for innovative strategy concepts

content.text: Diversity and Profession : A bigraphical-narrative study in the context of educational sociology. Diversity can be considered one of the most dazzling terms for describing today's heterogeneous societies. But what relevance does this phenomenon have for elementary education? Although early childhood education is now given a special place, the current results of the PISA and OECD studies point to a great correlation between social origin and educational level. Against this background, Anne Rosken analyses the importance and impact of increasing social heterogeneity for elementary education. Using selected case studies, the first study is based on the consideration of biographical aspects of professional treatment of diversity among educators. The focus is on the educational sociological perspective, whereby the author integrates essential organizational aspects into the considerations.
content.title_en: Diversity and Profession : A biographical-narrative study in the context of educational sociology

content.text: Life between land and city: Migration, translocality and vulnerability in South Africa. Poverty and vulnerability characterize the lives of many people in Africa. To ensure their existence, migrations between land and city and the social networks that result from them play a much greater role than previously assumed by research. The book shows this by using South Africa's example. The emergence, inner dynamics and developmental relevance of informal land-city interdependencies are investigated and illustrated by a bilocal case study. Malte Steinbrink opens up a translocal perspective that is suitable for significantly advancing the current discussion about the relationship between migration and development in Africa.
content.title_en: Living between country and city : Migration, translocality and vulnerability in South Africa

content.text: Separation and interconnection: Sociological investigations on the theory of memory. Memory is a neglected category of sociological theory formation. This finding is first of all astonishing when one looks at the virulence of the topic in current discussions about social change processes through new media. The aim and task of this work is to show that from system and network theory preliminary work, which are connected with the names Luhmann, Latour and White, a heuristic of sociological memory analyses can be developed which can remedy this deficit. Memory is a neglected category of sociological theory formation. This finding is first of all astonishing when one looks at the virulence of the topic in current discussions about social change processes through new media. The aim and task of this work is to show that from system and network theory preliminary work, which are connected with the names Luhmann, Latour and White, a heuristic can develop sociological memory analyses that can remedy this deficiency.
content.title_en: Separation and joining : Sociological studies on memory theory

content.text: The Federal States' fiscal capacity to act: determinants, institutional deficits and reform options. The book has a double thrust: on the one hand, it explains the differences in the level of deficits in the German Länder, on the other hand, reform options for a more effective limitation of deficits are identified based on the empirically established causal factors. The difference between structurally forced debt and re-election-oriented debt is leading. The empirical results show that the re-election-oriented debt prevails, in particular the deficits are higher the wider the power is distributed in a country between different government parties.
content.title_en: The fiscal capacity of the Länder: determinants, institutional deficits and reform options

content.text: Disinvestment management: Success factors in the negotiation phase of a sell-off. The basics of the investigation -- Conceptualization and model development -- Methodology and approach of the empirical investigation -- Results of the empirical investigation -- Summary and implications. Disinvestments represent an important strategic tool for many companies to proactively shape the company portfolio. However, many of the investing companies fail to achieve the desired success, as they fail to overcome the buyer's information problem. The result is delayed negotiations and the achievement of lower sales proceeds. Based on the New Institution Economics, Timo Defren identifies key success factors to overcome the information problem in the negotiation phase of a sell-off. He examines the success effect of these factors against the background of moderate variables and considers the determinants of success factors. Based on data from a survey of 251 companies, the author shows that five of the theoretically derived success factors have a significant positive influence on the disinvestment success. In particular, the information quality in the due diligence and credibility of communication activities is measured with great success.
content.title_en: Disinvestment management : success factors in the negotiation phase of a sell-off

content.text: DSL versus Cable: Information externalities as determinants of path dependence and change costs in the adoption of broadband technologies. The lack of broadband penetration on the German market for information and communication technologies is the subject of the current discussion on the competitiveness of Germany. In this context, the question arises why the TV cable could not prevail as an equivalent infrastructure alternative to DSL despite excellent starting conditions. Against the background of path dependence and network effects, Thomas Bach analyses the information and purchase behaviour of users on the network market of fast internet access using a sophisticated empirical survey. The study is characterized by a clever combination of modern methods, including conjoint analysis, purchasing decision simulation and logistic regression, and offers interesting and innovative approaches for future market research efforts. The author succeeds in demonstrating the existence of herd effects and measuring change costs in the adoption of broadband connections, which thus provide quantifiable evidence for a lock-in and path dependency on the German broadband market.
content.title_en: DSL versus Cable: Information externalities as determinants of path dependence and change costs in broadband technology adoption

content.text: Financial reporting and forecasting errors of financial analysts. The main target groups of the annual report include, in addition to private investors and institutional investors, financial analysts. Although capital market-oriented companies in the annual report – if this is to fulfil certain information requirements – must publish a legally prescribed level of information, the quality and quantity of the information given in the annual reports vary. Tatjana Oberdörster analyses, by means of multiple regressions, for which sub-reports of the Group's management report and the Group's annex a significant correlation between the quality of these sub-reports and the EPS forecast quality can be determined. The result is that the quality of the EPS forecasts of financial analysts is significantly influenced by the content quality of certain parts of the Group's management report and the Group's annex. Above all, high-quality reporting in the sub-reports "additional report" and "capital flow accounting" results in financial analysts being able to forecast the economic development of companies. External accounting as a decision-making tool for reporting – the capital market analysis.
content.title_en: Financial reporting and forecast errors of financial analysts

content.text: Optimal nonlinear prices for two-sided markets. Nonlinear pricing -- Price setting on two-sided markets -- Analysis approach for a decision-making support system for price optimization on two-sided trade fair markets -- Models for price optimization for a trade fair event -- Measurement of the willingness to pay by exhibitors and visitors -- Calculation of optimal prices -- Summary and implications. Suppliers on two-sided markets face two challenges in terms of price setting for their products. On the one hand, they have to take into account the reciprocal dependence of demand, i.e. they have to simultaneously optimize the prices of both market sides. On the other hand, they can benefit from a nonlinear pricing system such as two-sided pricing with a fixed and variable price component. This form of price differentiation allows the decreasing willingness to pay per unit to be taken into account when demand volumes increase and consumer rents are cut off. Frauke Hagemeister develops a decision-support system for price optimization on two-sided markets. Taking into account segment-specific payment readiness by exhibitors and visitors, the user determines the opportunity to buy the optimal price for an increase event.
content.title_en: Optimal nonlinear prices for two-sided markets

content.text: Multi-sided secure ad hoc networking of vehicles. In the medium term, vehicles will be equipped with the ability to join in so-called vehicle ad hoc networks (VANETs) to exchange messages with each other and with other networks. The main objectives are to increase traffic safety and to efficiently use existing road capacity. However, insufficient security of the messages can have devastating consequences, e.g. provoked accidents. Against this background, Klaus Plößl designs a multi-sided secure VANET security infrastructure, which is designed to prevent attacks. After an introduction to the topic, he first analyzes and evaluates existing approaches comprehensively based on criteria specifically tailored to the requirements of VANET. In addition to the protection interests of all stakeholders, the focus is on efficiency in terms of required transmission and computing capacity as well as the protection of the privacy of users and economic aspects. Building on this, he develops a security infrastructure that meets all the requirements better than previous approaches.
content.title_en: Multi-sided secure ad hoc networking of vehicles

content.text: Horizontal composite structures in the German hospital market: potentials, processes and practice. The financial viability and permanent reform of healthcare directly affect a basic need of the population. Hospitals, which account for the largest proportion of health expenditures with about 26%, are required to increase their operational excellence and adapt to the constantly changing institutional conditions with the aim of reducing costs. Benjamin I. Person examines to what extent hospitals in various types of composites can meet these requirements. The author takes an advanced theoretical perspective, which combines transaction cost economics with the strategic approach of dynamic skills. He carries out a comprehensive survey of 1,740 German hospitals, which is representative of the German hospital sector with 607 responding institutions. Based on the data obtained, he provides detailed insights into the collaborative practice of German hospitals. Location determination for the German hospital landscape -- Horizontal composite structures to overcome the challenges in the hospital market -- composite structures in German hospital practice -- Resumé, limitation and research outlook.
content.title_en: Horizontal composite structures in the German hospital market: potentials, processes and practice

content.text: Climate change and resilience management: Interdisciplinary approach to decision-making. Climate change as a challenge to corporate governance -- Causes and impacts of climate change under system-theoretical structured consideration -- Theoretical basis for the context-relevant concepts of resilience, climate change adaptation and business-economic research -- Conceptualization of resilience management under empirical exploration of relevance and handling of climate change effects -- Summary and conclusion. Global warming is today presenting companies with a wide range of ecological and socio-economic issues. In addition to the mitigation of global warming, adaptation to the effects of climate change, such as ecological discontinuities or changing consumer behaviour is increasingly the focus. For corporate management, the challenge is to make organisations resistant to these effects. Elmar Günther for the first time introduces the concepts of resilience, vulnerability and adaptive capacity together with current business research. He provides a comprehensive assessment of the causes and effects of climate change in the socio-economic and ecological system.
content.title_en: Climate change and resilience management : Interdisciplinary approach

content.text: The relevance of gastronomy as a brand communication tool. Events play an increasingly important role in brand communication. Catering has also been used as an event platform for the introduction of beverage brands for several years. However, there are so far few theoretical and empirical publications available for the potential communication effect of gastronomy as a permanent event. Markus Zeller considers gastronomy as an extended profiling tool for brand-name companies in addition to its sales function and deals with the communication effect of the catering presence. Based on an classification into identity-based brand management and in the context of other experience-oriented communication forms, he develops an impact model that depicts the psychographic processes and determinants of catering communication. The investigation hypotheses are examined using empirical studies for the premium beer brand Beck-Es over a period of ten years. Catering as an alternative form of communication -- theoretical basic design -- development of a reference framework for the analysis of the relevance of gastronomy as an instrument of brand communication -- case study: Design of the communication form of gastronomy as an example of the Beck's brand -- conclusion and outlook.
content.title_en: The relevance of gastronomy as an instrument of brand communication

content.text: Conceptualization of the current income of networks of close ones. Relationships of close ones can be distinguished by a double nature of legal diversity in economic unity. This makes it difficult to integrate close ones into existing tax regimes. The increasing networking of companies and the greater importance of intangible assets as well as more diverse human forms of life create new problem areas in the taxation of close ones. Manuel Teschke analyses the two fundamental possibilities of taxation of networks of closer ones on the one hand by placing on the individual parts of the network (concept of self-employment), on the other hand by looking at the network as a whole (concept of unity). He develops both initially incompatible approaches in a first step and combines them on the other. The author develops both proposals for a more appropriate design of the external comparison and the formal profit distribution and shows design possibilities. Basis of the investigation -- Derivation of a requirement profile for concepts of taxation of the current income of networks of closer ones -- Development of the framework concepts of self-relation and unity - Development of possible reform approaches - Summary of key results and outlook.
content.title_en: Concept of taxation of the current yield of networks of close

content.text: Management of complex IT architectures: Empirical analysis using the example of the international financial industry. In science and practice, the need for holistic and long-term management of enterprise IT is increasingly recognised at the level of macro architecture. In recent years, IT architecture management (or enterprise architecture management) has developed its own discipline for this. However, the implementation of a corresponding function is considered one of the biggest challenges of IT management. Christian Schmidt is dedicated in his work to a comprehensive scientific analysis of this still largely undeveloped topic area. He develops a theoretical reference framework for this. Based on several empirical studies, the author then describes and analyses the diverse practice of architecture management. From this he identifies the most important success factors and derives concrete recommendations for action. Introduction -- Conceptual basics -- Management of IT macro architecture -- Practice of architecture management: Results of an expert survey -- Case studies -- Effects and success factors: a quantitative analysis -- Conclusions for practice -- Summary and outlook.
content.title_en: Management of complex IT architectures : Empirical analysis using the example of the international financial industry

content.text: Synergies in case law and accounting: Treatment of synergy potentials in corporate and commercial law. In business and corporate law, the synergy phenomenon is considered a central motive for corporate acquisitions and mergers. Synergies have also experienced an enormous increase in significance in accounting in the recent past. However, in addition to goodwill accounting, combination additional values remain a largely neglected accounting material. Florian Franke examines under what conditions synergistic earnings expectations influence decision and stock exchange values and to what extent consideration of uncertain composite advantages in determining corporate tax rulings is justified. Consider whether and to what extent acquired or unremunerated synergies are reflected in the financial and earnings situation of an undertaking under applicable and future commercial law (balance sheet law modernisation law). The author works out differences in the accounting treatment of similar synergy potentials and appreciates them against the background of the system of commercial law of accounting and alternative accounting arrangements. Problem status - terming of the synergical assessment - Synergicization of the management of the management of the management of the management of the company - Synergicization of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the management of the company.
content.title_en: Synergies in case law and accounting : Treatment of synergy potentials in corporate and commercial law

content.text: The amalgame Stadt : Orte. Netze. Milieus. The social, cultural and economic transformation from a Fordist industrial society to a post-industrial knowledge society poses new challenges to the management of urban connections through urban planning. Oliver Frey works out the model of an "amalgamous city" and names the specific conditions of urbanity as the hallmarks of a "creative city". It is shown how the superimpositions of mixed structures in the sense of a heterogeneity of social groups and through multi-layered uses of the places represent a resource for urban civil society. The study was awarded the Rudolf-Wurzer Prize for Spatial Planning 2008 by the City of Vienna and the Technical University of Vienna. The book is addressed to lecturers and students of spatial social sciences, spatial planning, geography and architecture and contains valuable information for the practice of urban development.
content.title_en: The amalgam game city : places. nets. milieu

content.text: Civil Peace Service : Exemplary impact analyses. The Civil Peace Service (ZFD) is a new institution for civil conflict management. Financed by the German government, development and peace organizations send personnel to conflict areas to support local actors in conflict transformation. This book examines the effects of the ZFD on two case studies in Serbia and Palestine and Israel, appropriate methods for impact analysis and consequences for the impact orientation of the ZFD. It highlights the peace-political potential of the ZFD and systematically shows possibilities and limits of social science impact analysis in this field of policy.
content.title_en: Civil peace service: exemplary impact analyses

content.text: Asset Pricing: To evaluate unsafe cash flows with time-variable discount rates. Basics of asset pricing -- Factor models -- Predictability of stock yields -- Asset valuation models -- Empirical analysis and further development -- Final view. Asset pricing is a long-established research branch in economics and aims to determine the fair value of future unsafe cash flows. An important issue is which discount rates should be used to assess unsafe cash flows. Michael Vorfahrt presents the basics of asset pricing and presents static factor models such as the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) and the Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT). As the risk-free interest rate, the risk premium of the market and the beta factor are time-variable, the author goes into this phenomenon of discount rates. To evaluate unsafe cash flows, he draws on valuation models and subtracts the essential research findings such as the time-variability of an empirical review. He identifies among the static models that can be used to explain the more dynamic models.
content.title_en: Asset Pricing : To assess unsafe cash flows with time-variable discount rates

content.text: Configuration of international production networks taking into account uncertainty. Relevant basics of central research directions -- Reference framework for configuration of international production networks -- Previous statements on the inspection of uncertainty -- Empirical investigation of the inspection of uncertainty -- Consideration of uncertainty in configuration -- Summary. If a configuration of decentralized production networks takes place in an international context, the number of business environments to be considered increases the uncertainty that is always inherent in such long-term issues. Christian Neuner derives from four central research directions the basic understanding of such a configuration. Using an empirical case study of four companies from different industries, the author gains new insights on how uncertainty can be taken into account in the configuration process. Finally, he presents an improved reference framework.
content.title_en: Configuration of international production networks taking into account uncertainty

content.text: Key events in media coverage. The theory of key events is a research area of media science that deals with the career of topics in media coverage. Elisabeth Rauchenzauner examines the short- and long-term impact of key events on journalistic coverage, the importance of news factors for key events, the importance of key images, concepts and figures, as well as the role of journalists as gatekeepers in this context. The theory of key events is a research area of media science that deals with the career of topics in media coverage. Elisabeth Rauchenzauner examines the short- and long-term impact of key events on journalistic coverage, the importance of news factors for key events, the importance of key images, concepts and figures, and the role of journalists as gatekeepers in this context. Dr. Elisabeth Rauchenzauner holds a PhD in communication science/department Journalism at the University of Salzburg. She works as a journalist in Salzburg.
content.title_en: Key events in media coverage

content.text: Integrated environmental cost management: a reference framework and a concept for environmentally sustainable corporate management. Within the framework of business administration and accounting, many environmental-oriented approaches have already been developed, but these relate to "foreign" disciplines only vaguely. Heinz Karl Prammer spans a reference framework from ecology, business economics, ethics and science to describe companies as ecological-economic subsystems. He develops the concept "Integrated environmental cost management", whose purpose is to create sustainability-oriented benefits for and for companies. INTRODUCTION -- EMPLOYMENT-COPULATION AND ECOLOGIC SUSTAINABILITY – ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND INTERDISCIPLINARY PERSPECTIVES FOR THE ENVIRONMENTAL COST MANAGEMENT -- INTEGRATED ENVIRONMENTAL COST MANAGEMENT – THE INSTRUMENT FOR ANALYSIS, EVALUATION AND EVALUATION OF THE TOTAL PERSPECTIVES FOR THE ENVIRONMENTAL COST COST MANAGEMENT
content.title_en: Integrated environmental cost management : Reference framework and concept for environmentally sustainable corporate management

content.text: Prototyping to support social interaction processes. Social interaction processes in start-up teams -- Prototyping -- Support social interaction processes through prototyping -- Empirical methodology -- Empirical results -- Conclusions and outlook. The establishment of growth-oriented companies is based on the collaboration of several actors. Founders face the challenge of building efficient interaction processes both within a start-up team and with their environment. Using an empirical study, Bernhard Doll shows how prototyping as an iterative development and learning process can influence the quality of social interaction processes in start-up teams, such as communication, coordination and cohesion, in a sustainable manner, so that they can achieve success faster.
content.title_en: Prototyping to support social interaction processes

content.text: Evaluation and improvement of the energy efficiency of municipal existing buildings: development of a holistic process for municipal practice. Measures for energy saving and CO2 reduction are important global challenges both in view of the scarce budgets of public households and to ensure future energy supply. Antje Junghans develops a holistic process model of the "Facility Efficiency Evaluation (FEE)", which enables a simple and fast energy assessment of buildings in the municipal stock using the example of heating energy. The author illustrates the life cycle costs of measures for energy saving and shows the alternatives to be easily identified. A practical test also shows the functionality of the model. Fundamentals of energy efficiency assessment -- description and evaluation of existing methods -- development of a holistic process model -- model application using the example of municipal existing buildings -- summary and outlook.
content.title_en: Evaluation and increase of energy efficiency of municipal existing buildings : Development of a holistic procedure for municipal practice

content.text: Using virtual worlds for customer integration into new product development: An exploratory study using the example of the automotive industry. Customer integration into new product development is a key factor for the economic success of innovations. Nevertheless, the potentials seem to be not exhausted, especially in the technology-driven automotive industry. Julia Daecke examines the concept of interactive value creation between companies and customers. She examines what the novel phenomenon of internet-based 3D worlds can achieve in this context and what organizational conditions are conducive to it. Interviews with managers of German automobile manufacturers and industry-related institutions serve as an empirical basis for the exploratory research design. Basics -- Empirical investigation -- The benefits of virtual worlds for customer integration -- Organization of virtual customer integration -- Conclusions and outlook.
content.title_en: Use of virtual worlds for customer integration into new product development : An exploratory study using the example of the automotive industry

content.text: Automatic generation and optimization of cycle schedules in rail networks. The computer-based production of timetables is an important element in the strategic roadmap for rail transport. Jens Opitz provides a significant contribution to the method building of cycle planning. The focus is on the development and evaluation of procedures and algorithms for solving practical problems. He shows how cycle schedules can be generated automatically for both rail-bound passenger traffic and freight transport, optimized and, if necessary, evaluated by the user. Introduction -- Introduction to the problem -- Thematic basics -- Areas of study – Real traffic examples -- Automatic generation of cycle schedules -- Theoretical basics -- Practical implementation -- Maximising clocked system paths -- Maximum current with dynamic capacity allocation -- Optimization of cycle schedules -- Optimization methods -- Traffic conversion -- Modulo-Network-Simplex-Process -- Summary and Outlook -- Summary.
content.title_en: Automatic generation and optimisation of timetables in rail networks

content.text: The European city in transformation: Urban planning and urban development policy in post-socialist Warsaw. The aim of the book is to analyse post-socialist urban planning and urban development policy in Eastern Europe. Using the example of the city of Warsaw, we will show which forms of urban governance shape the transformation phase and to what extent, after the phase of socialism, Eastern European cities approach the ideal model of the European city. Florian Koch presents the characteristics of the European city and sets them in relation to the current urban governance debate. The empirical study shows a duality of Warsaw's urban development policy between formal structures and informal processes and agreements. By comparing with other Eastern European cities, the characteristics of post-socialist urban policy and Warsaw peculiarities are identified. Introduction: Post-socialist transformation, urban development policy and the European city -- The model of the European city in transformation -- Governance and urban development policy -- The socialist city and its transformation -- Urban development and transformation in Warsaw -- Urban development policy in Warsaw -- Post-socialist urban development policy: Uncomplete transformation or its own form of urban governance?
content.title_en: The European City in Transformation : Urban Planning and Urban Development Policy in post-socialist Warsaw

content.text: Renewable energy technology. The authors describe the most important forms of technical use of renewable energy sources in practice. They represent their potentials, taking into account global energy problems and the thermodynamic limits of energy conversion processes, and discuss their contribution to a sustainable energy system. The book deals with photovoltaics, solar and geothermal energy, biomass, wind and hydro power and thus takes into account both systems for electricity and heat supply. In the individual chapters, the functioning of the central components and their connection to systems is presented, based on the natural and engineering principles. Concrete planning and design examples combine the theoretical principles with an action-oriented teaching. The integration of renewable energy systems into existing systems for electricity, heat and transport is each dedicated to a separate chapter. Context -- Energy efficiency -- Renewable energy sources -- Photovoltaic -- Solar thermal -- Biomass -- Wind power plants -- Hydropower plants -- Electrical energy systems -- Mobile#x00E4;t - Thermodynamic rain.
content.title_en: Renewable energy technology
