content.title_en: Removal obligations in IFRS capital market-oriented accounting

content.text: Intangible Impairment : Qualitative Impairment Test for intangible assets. Intangible Assets -- Accounting for intangible assets according to IFRS -- Intangible Assets according to IFRS in empirical research -- Adjustments in risk management for the purpose of qualitative impairment testing -- Summary and outlook. The mapping of goodwill and other intangible assets in IFRS financial statements places high demands on the final holder. Thus, impairment symptoms must be reliably identified in the context of impairment testing. However, the results of a comprehensive study of the reporting of over 250 German companies on impairments of intangible assets presented by Arnt Wöhrmann indicate deficits. The author therefore examines whether there is an adjustment requirement in risk management. To this end, he analyses risk management from an operational, regulatory and empirical perspective.
content.title_en: Intangible Impairment : Qualitative Impairment Test for intangible assets

content.text: In the catch of economics?: A critical look at media companies' coverage in the German daily press. Economics and media represent a explosive link for communication research. In addition to their social task, media companies and any other business enterprise also focus on economic criteria. Reports now media about media companies, it is obvious that economic self-interests influence their journalistic presentation in the form of competitive ideas. Finally, economic information that penetrates the media to the public has an influence on the image and positioning of the market. At the same time, the respective economic situation exerts a more or less strong economic pressure on the publisher level. This too could be reflected in the reporting on the subject on the basis of strategic considerations. So, is journalism already in the catch of economics? If so, this would mean a dangerous restriction of journalistic autonomy and the journalistic claim. With a lead word by Prof. Dr. Romy Fröhlich Nicola Pointner, Professor of the Chair of Dr. Romy Fröhl, Institute for Communication Research, Munich Media Research.
content.title_en: In the catch of economics? : A critical look at the media company coverage in the German daily press

content.text: Multilocal living : spatial patterns of multilocal housing arrangements of shuttles and persons in a long-distance relationship. The book empirically examines the multilocal living and living of persons with a second residence (shuttles) used for work and of persons in a partnership with separate households over long distances (remote relationships) in the context of occupational mobility requirements and social change. The results of the work are based on a standardized survey of randomly selected people in four German cities and in-depth qualitative interviews. Special features of multilocal living and living forms are examined in relation to social structural characteristics, living conditions and housing needs by means of comparative group analyses.
content.title_en: Multilocal living : spatial-temporal patterns of multilocal accommodation arrangements of shuttles and persons in a long-distance relationship

content.text: The International Governance of the State-Islamic and State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Is of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Is of the State-Issues of the State-Is of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Is of the State-Issues of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Issues of the State-Is of the State-Issues of the State-Issues of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is of the State-Is
content.title_en: International governance of self-determination and state formation: self-determination, conflict management, recognition and succession of states in recent international law practice

content.text: The right of proof before international courts and arbitration courts in intergovernmental disputes: The Law of Evidence before International Courts and Arbitral Tribunals in Inter-State Disputes. Against the background of an increasing number of intergovernmental proceedings, in which there are increasingly also factual issues, the dissertation examines the principles of factual determination and assessment before international courts and arbitration courts. It provides a systematic and critical consideration of the existing international law of proof and makes proposals for its further development. The work takes into account in particular the circumstances that international jurisdiction does not constitute a coherent, self-contained system.
content.title_en: The right of proof before international courts and arbitration courts in intergovernmental disputes : The Law of Evidence before International Courts and Arbitral Tribunals in Inter-State Disputes

content.text: MRP for material planning for circular processes: Optimization of protection strategies against demand and supply risks. The processing of old products has achieved an important role as a profitable recycling strategy. However, traditional planning concepts such as the MRP are not equipped for material planning in circular processes. Christian Gotzel expands the classic MRP and develops heuristics for material disposition in production systems with reprocessing. In this regard, the case of external product return from the market as well as the occurrence of internal return flows from losses of production are taken into account. Essentially, the safeguarding of recycling-specific risks by appropriate determination of safety stocks is important. As a result, easy-to-use heuristics are available, the solution quality of which is documented with the help of numerical investigations. Introduction -- Material planning for conventional and cycle-guided production -- Material planning for external product cycles -- Material planning for internal product cycles -- Final consideration.
content.title_en: MRP on material planning for circular processes : Optimisation of hedge strategies against demand and supply risks

content.text: Bond yields and minimum capital requirements for banks. Model theoretical analysis of investment behaviour of companies and banks -- Empirical analysis of the US bond market -- Summary and outlook. Regulatory capital requirements for banks often do not represent a correct assessment of the actual economic default risk of claims to be subordinated with own chapters. This discrepancy between economic and regulatory capital underlay raises the question, especially after Basel I, whether banks systematically invest in securities requiring a lower capital underlay. After a short model theoretical analysis of the question, three datasets with different statistical methods are analysed to see whether a significant influence of regulatory capital requirements on bond yields can be demonstrated.
content.title_en: Bond yields and minimum capital requirements for banks

content.text: Algorithms for vessel recognition for coronarangiography with synchrotron radiation. Basics -- Preprocessing -- Image contents -- Vascular recognition as a problem of structural recognition -- Vascular recognition in non-invasive coronarangiograms -- Vascular recognition in selective TPI images -- Conclusion and outlook. Synchrotron radiation is a versatile tool for cardiological imaging. It enables high-resolution images of the heart and quantification of its blood supply. The special features are investigated using experiments at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF). Using the application scenarios Coronar screening and blood flow measurement, Jörg Mielebacher analyses the properties of the most important image contents, i.e. blood vessels, heart interiors and heart muscles. As the image of the heart and its blood vessels is created by subtraction of two partial images, he analyses recording errors and shows proven solutions for image preprocessing and evaluation in vascular recognition.
content.title_en: Algorithms for vessel detection for coronary angiography with synchrotron radiation

content.text: Employee motivation in outsourcing with special consideration of facility management. Companies store billions of units of enterprise external third parties annually. Isabelle Wrase follows the hypothesis that in successful outsourcing, the receiving company can better motivate the employees taken over and thus benefit from their knowledge. Here, she includes resource-oriented and motivational psychological approaches as well as an empirical review based on a survey of affected employees. As a consequence of this, the receiving company should conduct an employee takeover primarily in the entire team in order to protect itself from a loss of knowledge in the long term. Summary -- Introductory considerations -- State of the literature on the benefit of outsourcing -- To theoretically justify outsourcing -- Employee motivation in the transition to the company using the example of a facility management provider: methodology and analysis -- Results and final considerations.
content.title_en: Employee motivation in outsourcing with special consideration of facility management

content.text: Flexibility in long-term contracts: An economic analysis of the contractual post-negotiation design for PPP projects. Compared to other forms of procurement, long-term contracts with fixed-price characteristics are usually much less flexible. In order to react to changes in the environment during the contract period, post-negotiations are usually required. Jirka Gehrt examines contractual regulations in private partnership projects which aim to obtain appropriate flexibility from the client's point of view. Based on theoretical considerations and interviews with experts, he evaluates contract rules used in practice and develops optimization proposals. Basics -- Essential concepts and focus of investigation -- Basic economic findings on post-negotiation -- Contract post-negotiation design for PPP projects -- Performance adjustments on public-manual requirements -- Private financing: post-negotiation design and impact on the assessment of individual instruments -- Optimizations of the operator, for example, refinancing -- Conclusion -- Summary of significant results -- Recommendations for action and implications.
content.title_en: Flexibility in long-term contracts : An economic analysis of the contractual post-negotiation design of PPP projects

content.text: A continent – a nation? : Prolegomena to form a supranational demo within the framework of the EU. Dr. Ondrej Kalina is a lecturer at the Chair of Political Science I of the University of Passau. The fact that the European Union itself would find it difficult to meet the minimum democratic standards for admission is now a popularly ventilated bonmot. Above all, it refers to a democratic deficit of the EU, which, if looked at more closely, turns out to be a European democracy dilemma: ‘Democratic governance' is only possible in a community that understands itself as such. Only then are minorities willing to recognise majority decisions as binding for them, and only then can social (re-)distribution measures be universally accepted. The study develops holistic strategies using an original concept, such as and with which results that dilemma can be broken through a specific European ‘nation-building'.
content.title_en: A continent – a nation? : Prolegomena to form a supranational demo in the framework of the EU

content.text: Activists of normal biography: On the biographical dimension of precarious work. If one follows studies on precarization, unsafe employees complain about the lack of possibility of life planning and strive for normal biography. At the same time, it is considered as a truism that the individuals have long since left normal biography and live discontinuous patchwork biographies (want to). Daniela Schiek combines these two strands of discussion theoretically and empirically, using biographical case analyses, she examines the current relevance that normal biography acquires through precarious employment situations. As a result, this does not appear as any biographical option, but as a hinge between individual and working society: as life - the only one who knows individuals.
content.title_en: Activists of normal biography : On the biographical dimension of precarious work

content.text: Process dynamics of implementing innovations: An empirical analysis of dynamic skills and their impact in hospitals. The ability to implement innovations has developed into a measure of long-term success in hospitals in view of changing competitive conditions. However, the high failure rate of innovation projects raises the question of why hospitals differ in their innovative capacity. Erk P. Piening analyses from the perspective of the Dynamic Capability approach how specific process dynamics influence the course and success of innovation projects in hospitals. In the context of a case study, he examines the implementation of a process innovation in nine hospitals and identifies processual explanatory patterns for existing differences.
content.title_en: Process dynamics of the implementation of innovations: An empirical analysis of dynamic skills and their impact in hospitals

content.text: Theoretical foundation and empirical analysis using the example of franchise networks. Network relationships are not of a static nature, but develop over time. Following on from the conceptual and theoretical development of the development phenomenon in network relationships, Tobias Heußler shows how this development looks like in franchise networks. In an investigation of more than 50 franchise networks, the author identifies typical development processes for the relationship constellation between franchisees and franchisees. The results of the investigation provide franchisors with valuable information for partner management. A multi-level analysis is used to derive concrete implications for network management.
content.title_en: Time development of network relationships : Theoretical foundation and empirical analysis using the example of franchise networks

content.text: Front End Decision Making : The emergence of highly new innovation projects in companies. The initiative is the trigger for an innovation project. However, the individual decision to take the initiative is not observable and therefore difficult to control. Despite the high importance of this early phase of the innovation process, it has so far received relatively little attention. Dietfried Globocnik examines different theoretical reference points on their explanatory contributions to the emergence of initiatives, derives basic conditions and develops a model of how the decision to take the initiative. Supported by an innovative empirical study, he explains which personality characteristics constitute a "initiator" and which working environment promotes the proactive adoption of the initiative.
content.title_en: Front End Decision Making : The emergence of highly new innovation projects in companies

content.text: Trust as an input/output variable in electronic negotiations : An empirical investigation of confidence-enhancing measures. Numerous management activities are carried out media-based, but this makes it difficult to build confidence. Katrin Stiglbauer develops possibilities of confidence-building, which she empirically derives by realistic negotiation simulation and systematic input/output-view. The author shows that trust-barriers can be overcome by early perception control as well as by concrete confidence-enhancing measures.
content.title_en: Trust as an input/output variable in electronic negotiations : An empirical study of confidence-building measures

content.text: The quality of supply situations in the distribution of management consulting services : An empirical study. With the change in the consulting industry, the way in which the client procures consulting services has changed. Professional management of supply situations is becoming increasingly important: from the supplier's perspective, these become marketing tools. The quality of the supply situation influences the client's decision. Michaela Skobranek analyses supply situations from the supplier's and demander's perspective and empirically examines the factors that influence the client's quality assessment. As a result, a quality model for supply situations is available.
content.title_en: The quality of supply situations in the distribution of management consulting services : An empirical study

content.text: Strategic success factor Information technology : Analysis of the value contribution of information technology to productivity increase and product differentiation. Information technology is one of the most important capital goods in many companies. However, a paradigm shift is currently emerging and IT managers are increasingly obliged to justify the expenditure. Dietmar Moch analyses the value contribution of information technology to corporate success. The results provide important insights on how companies can significantly increase their performance by using selected information technologies in terms of corporate strategy. The author shows how product differentiation strategies can be measured and controlled using hedonic models, using the example of the PC market.
content.title_en: Strategic success factor Information technology : Analysis of the value contribution of information technology to productivity increase and product differentiation

content.text: Implementation status of the Balanced Scorecard : Case study-based analysis in German companies. The Balanced Scorecard (BSC) has received high attention in business research and business practice over the past 15 years. Nevertheless, empirical studies show that in most companies in the German-speaking area the BSC is not used as a strategic management system in the sense of the authors Kaplan/Norton. Philip Matlachowsky uses a multi-case study to analyse the BSC applications in six companies of different industries and sizes. He shows that the BSC's implementation status is based on different development patterns, which can also include the development of the used BSC type. Based on a cognitive psychological, structuring and consistency theory-inspired perspective, he interprets the development patterns as adaptation processes within the company's operating order. Based on these findings, he shows implications for science and practice. Introduction -- Conceptual basis -- Literature on the implementation status of the Balanced Scorecard -- Methodical conception of the case study - Results of the case study - Final discussion - Results analysis.
content.title_en: Implementation status of the Balanced Scorecard : Case study-based analysis in German companies

content.text: Automated negotiations in multi-agent systems: Design of an argument-based mechanism for only imperfectly descriptable negotiation objects. Due to the growing importance of electronic markets, the need for automation of negotiations exists. Multi-agent systems (MAS) play a key role. Ricardo Büttner examines automated negotiations and designs an argument-based negotiation mechanism for only imperfectly descriptible negotiation objects. He derives this methodically from an organizational-theoretical reference framework (structure, process organization, micro and macro perspective) and designs it. Finally, the author evaluates the designed mechanism by means of simulation.
content.title_en: Automated negotiations in multi-agent systems : Design of argument-based mechanism for only imperfectly descriptable negotiation items

content.text: Cross-border mergers of capital companies in the EU: Treatment of silent reserves and existing losses. Mergers cause the legal loss of a tax entity. The question whether this circumstance can be used as a trigger for tax effects is of paramount importance, especially for the taxation of cross-border mergers. Lucia Helena Bambynek works out principles for an economically meaningful and constitutional and European-compliant taxation of mergers, using a formal model theory analysis of cross-border mergers between two capital companies.
content.title_en: Cross-border mergers of EU corporations : Treatment of silent reserves and existing losses

content.text: Sustainable brand differentiation of Commodities : Special features and starting points within the context of identity-based brand management. Commodities often appear as keywords when it comes to difficult-to-differentiable services. Despite the high spread of the term, however, there is little clarity about the possibilities and starting points of their brand differentiation. Tim Bohmann develops a detailed understanding of Commodities as part of identity-based brand management, on the basis of which he derives six commodity-specific brand differentiation approaches. Based on an empirical study on the German petrol station market, he shows that these approaches also allow providers of Commodities to differentiate their services within the framework of brand management.
content.title_en: Sustainable brand differentiation of Commodities : Special features and approaches in the context of identity-based brand management

content.text: The performance of public companies using the example of housing companies in Germany. Privatisation of public housing ownership has developed a particular dynamic in recent years due to the involvement of international financial investors. Privatization has so far been carried out without an assessment of the performance of public housing companies, as comparable empirical studies on the performance of public and private housing companies are missing at national and international level. Mathias Hain uses an extensive data set to investigate performance differences between public and private housing companies in Germany. Using a univariate and multivariate analysis, he shows that public housing companies show performance disadvantages in terms of profitability and productivity compared to private housing companies. The results of the work provide recommendations for the performance of housing companies for value-oriented property management.
content.title_en: The performance of public companies using the example of housing companies in Germany

content.text: Information from option prices : An empirical analysis of the US dollar/euro exchange rate. Basics of option price theory -- Extraction of risk-neutral probability density function -- Application areas of risk-neutral probability density functions -- Empirical studies -- Summary and conclusions. Market expectations play a central role in the explanation of exchange rates in macroeconomics. Individual structural relationships such as the validity of the uncovered interest rate parity, whose validity is clearly refuted in Empirical, are assumed. Nicole van de Locht uses the risk-neutral density function to investigate whether a peso problem can explain the empirically observed deviation from the uncovered interest rate parity in the US dollar/euro exchange rate. Furthermore, the author analyses various statistical characteristics of the risk-neutral density function, such as predictability compared to previously widely used forecast models.
content.title_en: Information from option prices : An empirical analysis of the US dollar/euro exchange rate

content.text: The morphology of cooperation as a basis for the concept of two-level cooperation. Cooperation between companies has become a matter of course today. This development leads to numerous concepts and explanations that only partially meet the diversity of such forms of organisation. A general theory of cooperation is still lacking. Heiko Baum takes up this topic and develops a general model of cooperation as well as a morphology based on it. Using this morphology, he describes the new concept of one two-level cooperation and explains its internal structures. The novelty of this form of cooperation and initial evaluation approaches are highlighted and discussed.
content.title_en: Morphology of cooperation as a basis for the concept of two-level cooperation

content.text: Combined registration and segmentation. Segmentation and image registration are two central areas of modern medical image processing. Konstantin Ens deals with the possibilities of combining registration and segmentation approaches. He develops a theoretical framework for such a combination of methods and classifys the procedures. The author explains further new possibilities to improve registration and segmentation and then makes a comparison of the procedures.
content.title_en: Combined registration and segmentation

content.text: Modern sourcing in the automotive industry. Outsourcing is one of the most important organizational concepts of the present day. In the automotive industry, too, Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is increasingly using outsourcing to meet the challenges of the dynamic and demanding market and competitive environment. Based on case studies on external assignments at the entire vehicle level, Kathrin Schneider is developing a practice-based method that enables the assessment of the feasibility and internal consistency of outsourcing projects.
content.title_en: Modern sourcing in the automotive industry

content.text: The Property Rights Equity Concept : Proposal for capital delimitation in the context of international accounting. Vera Sophie Schiemer presents a new proposal for the delimitation of equity: the Property Rights Equity Concept. This is characterized by a cross-legal and interdisciplinary foundation. With the help of the Property Rights Theory, the risk was identified as a central determinante in the demarcation question and developed on the basis of this a statement system for capital demarcation. The applicability of the concept is demonstrated by the analysis of various financing forms, whereby the arc of classical common shares and GmbH shares spans via convertible bonds to derivatives such as options or forwards.
content.title_en: The Property Rights Equity Concept : Proposal for the recognition of equity in the context of international accounting

content.text: Sustainability in health care: How health insurance companies successfully combine marketing and prevention. In dealing with scarce resources, sustainability becomes a significant success factor for economic action and social development. Legal health insurance companies are also exposed to a pressure of legitimization and justification. Viviane Scherenberg examines in this book possible target divergences of the statutory health insurance companies between the actual purpose of the company (according to SGB V) and the preservation of existence in the market, which can lead to a sustainability dilemma due to the current competitive pressure. Different perspectives of sustainability on social, health and economic level are considered and explained by means of a full survey, including bonus programs. Furthermore, different possibilities of a goal harmonisation are shown, which form the basis for "sustainability marketing" and "sustainable marketing". A balancing of the target divergences is not only responsible for long-term marketing and prevention successes, but also contributes to an increased emotional connection of the (potential) customers to the cashier, to a public responsibility and thus to a positive increase of the health insurance company's health insurance companies.
content.title_en: Sustainability in health care : How health insurance companies successfully combine marketing and prevention

content.text: Democratic School Development: Potentials and Limits of an Action Strategy Against Right-wing Extremism. Extreme right-wing tendencies among young people raise the question of the possibilities for action of the institution school. In her ethnographic case study, Gabi Elverich reconstructs an implementation process of democratic school development at an East German school. She examines potentials, limits and challenges of this action strategy and thus links right-wing extremism, school and organizational research. The theoretically sound evaluation study provides insights into areas of tension and contradictions in which political education moves as a cross-cutting task of school. The author works out that the concept of democratic school development requires theoretically conceptual sharpening and provides empirically justified impulses for the further development of school-right-wing extremism prevention in research and practice. Gabi Elverich is a study consultant at a Berlin-based school and a member of the research network women and right-wing extremism.
content.title_en: Democratic School Development: Potential and Limits of an Action Strategy Against Right-wing Extremism

content.text: Interim Management : Analysis of an atypical form of employment for managers. Interim Management, a temporary deployment of managers in companies, is increasingly being used as a result of the flexibilisation of industrial relations. Irma Rybnikova analyses the extent to which this market-oriented design of management positions represents an efficient arrangement. Based on case studies in companies and a quantitative survey of German interim managers, the author explores the opportunities, but also the limits of this practice.
content.title_en: Interim management : analysis of an atypical form of employment for managers

content.text: Automation of management decisions : framework, modeling and prototype. Managers must make an ever increasing number of important and comprehensive decisions. Many of these so-called management decisions are to be made to achieve the maximum economic effect with as little latency as possible in the tight working hours. Jonas Rommelspacher examines whether managers can be relieved by the automation of selected decisions. He develops the characteristics of management decisions and develops a concept that can automate selected management decisions with the help of hierarchically organized decision-making programs.
content.title_en: Automation of leadership decisions : Framework, modeling and prototype

content.text: The natural scientist as an entrepreneur : founding types and their motivation in the university environment. With the help of 35 interviews Enrico Sass forms different types of founders and non-founders: from the professor who placed his company on the stock exchange to the internationally renowned scientist who created more than two biotechnology companies. The reader is given an answer to the question, which type-specific span can be constructed from basic researcher to the independent entrepreneur. The work also illustrates fundamental factors influencing the explanation of the motivation of the foundation.
content.title_en: The natural scientist as an entrepreneur : founder types and their motivation in the university environment

content.text: The influence of culture on the strategy process : An empirical study. The strategy process is considered by its underlying logic as a very targeted and efficient management tool for the development of corporate strategies. Management research has so far neglected the question whether the strategy process in other cultural circles is also different. Werner Frese checks whether the culture of a country influences the persons involved in the strategy process and thus differentiates the strategy processes in their efficiency. With an empirical study of companies in 11 countries, he provides proof that strategy processes are carried out differently depending on the cultural values of the process participants.
content.title_en: The influence of culture on the strategy process : An empirical study

content.text: The Risk Map is used to classify and prioritize evaluated corporate risks. Christian Brünger examines how the risk threshold used in the Risk Map as a classification limit can be determined on the basis of decision-making theoretical criteria. The author shows for the first time that the traditional prioritization method used to date creates a "blind spot" in the Risk Map, in which important risks are not identified.
content.title_en: Benefits-consistent risk prioritization : Risk map in the context of rational decisions

content.text: Integration and flexibility of the organization through information technology. There is still a gap in business theory and practice between the organization and the IT system design. Christian Horstmann establishes a connection between the integration and flexibility of the organization system and that of the IT system on the basis of a system theoretical approach. Based on this, he derives recommendations for action that can serve as a guide for all strategic IT and organizational decisions. This makes it possible to align the enterprise optimally in the field of tension between today and future requirements.
content.title_en: Integration and flexibility of the organisation through information technology

content.text: A decentralized information and collaboration architecture for cross-company product development. Companies are looking for new opportunities in collaborative product development (CPD) to support cross-organisational knowledge processing through new IT and more efficient data exchange processes. Patrick Stiefel is investigating how loosely coupled, dynamic network structures that support ad hoc cooperation are suitable for use in the CPD. He believes that hierarchical client/server architectures are too inflexible to support future generation collaboration networks; the initial hypothesis is that the architecture approaches of peer-to-peer computing are more suitable for this. The author is attempting to combine methods of product data management in the early stages of product development with decentralized IT technologies. The aim is to develop an approach for future loosely coupled collaboration platforms taking into account important IT key technologies such as service-oriented architecture (SOA) or model-driven software development (MDSD).
content.title_en: A decentralized information and collaboration architecture for cross-company product development

content.text: Technological competence and success of young companies: An analysis of the factors influencing the company. In the context of increasing competitive dynamics, technological competence is becoming an increasingly important resource for companies. Often, however, managers and founders of technology-oriented companies lack awareness of the need to adapt their technologies regularly to changing market conditions. Franka Birke represents the importance of different dimensions of technological competence for the long-term success of young companies and shows that they have a different influence on individual levels of success of young companies.
content.title_en: Technological competence and success of young companies: An analysis of the factors influencing the company

content.text: Payment preparedness measurement for industrial hybrids Performance bundles : Methodology and empirical validation. Against the background of increasing competitive pressure and increasing customer requirements, companies in industrial goods markets are increasingly offering tangible and services in an integrated form as hybrid power bundles. However, successful marketing requires the exact knowledge of the price a customer is willing to pay for the maximum performance. Against this background, Markus Karger develops a new method for payment preparedness measurement based on the capital value method and the decision analysis, which takes into account the special characteristics of such offers. The validity of this method is examined using a two-stage empirical analysis.
content.title_en: Payment preparedness measurement for industrial hybrid power bundles : methodology and empirical validation

content.text: Online communication behaviour of multipliers : Personality-specific analysis and increase of innovation input via user-generated content. The oral advertising represents a major driver of the diffusion success of products. Michael Möller examines the personality-specific delivery of online customer articulations and thus the relationship between personality structure and its influence on opinion leadership in the online environment. The results of two surveys with over 17,000 participants, offer an economically useful use, since the attention of a previously neglected group of people can strongly favour both diffusion and the development process of new products. Scientific research benefits by putting the motivation construct "Stress after social recognition" in a detailed and systematic way in relation to the topic of online communication behavior and multiplier effect for the first time.
content.title_en: Online communication behavior of multipliers : Personal analysis and increase of innovation input via user generated content

content.text: Coexisting intellectual property right regimes : the case of open and closed source software. Software. Cultural and legal factors are investigated on open source software (OSS) and the coexistence of OSS with closed source software (CSS) is theoretically founded. A focus is on OSS and CSS-based business models: Strategic aspects and market balances with OSS and CSS companies are examined and analysed on this basis economic policy measures. Finally, the focus is on start-ups in the IT sector. The work deepens the understanding of OSS and CSS as an economic phenomenon. It is shown that coexistence is beneficial, and e.g. a unilateral state promotion of OSS companies by subsidies or procurement policy must be rejected.
content.title_en: Coexisting intellectual property right regimes : the case of open and closed source software

content.text: Migration, language and cultural capital. Good knowledge in the respective national language is repeatedly negotiated in integration policy as a fundamental prerequisite for the successful positioning of immigrants. Yvonne Henkelmann shows by the example of migrant academics in Germany and Canada that on the one hand, national language knowledge is not a sufficient condition for a labour market positioning corresponding to the training and the so-called educational foreigners are confronted with far more obstacles in their professional establishment. On the other hand, knowledge in other languages than the official can help to exploit or enhance both educational titles as well as professional and biographical knowledge on the labour market in a timely manner.
content.title_en: Migration, language and cultural capital

content.text: Information requirements and information tools of the company's emission management : An analysis within the framework of the European trade in greenhouse gas emission certificates. The handling of the new limitation of CO2 emissions changes the previous decision calculation in companies, the development of a company-specific operational emission management becomes necessary. Christiane Romeo systematizes the emission management-specific information requirements and analyses in detail possible traditional information tools from the company's accounting as well as the environmental data acquisition and analysis on their usability for the company's emission management.
content.title_en: Information requirements and information tools for operational emission management: An analysis in the context of the European greenhouse gas emission allowance trading

content.text: Determinants of the market entry sequence of imitative Internet start-ups : An empirical study of the speed of enterprise formation and its influence on the company's success. A long-lasting debate in the management science literature revolves around the connection between the market entry sequence and the resulting company success. Following on from this, Stefan Gutberlet examines the factors that lead to the early or late entry into the market by means of an example of imitation business start-ups in the Internet economy. Based on a self-developed research model, he examines the hypotheses made using an online survey of business founders and derives theoretical and practical implications.
content.title_en: Determinants of the market entry order of imitative Internet start-ups : An empirical study of the speed of enterprise formation and its influence on the company's success

content.text: Motiv analysis of user innovations in online communities. Online communities (OCs) and social networks have become an important tool for companies to understand user needs and offer innovative potential for new product development. Lars Janzik analyses the motivation of members of an innovative OC from the consumer goods sector and distinguishes groups of motifs in dependence on phases of membership. The multi-level empirical process combines qualitative (netnography) with quantitative methods (PLS) and the results help companies to discover OCs as an instrument of customer integration and product development.
content.title_en: Motiv analysis of user innovations in online communities

content.text: Changes from telecommunications to unified communications: Changes for companies through internet-based innovation. Despite technological changes, the market for telecommunications systems for companies is stable and is characterised by only a few providers. The current integration of voice communication into the internet-based communication concept "Unified Communication" leads to fundamental changes in the business model of this industry. Ralf Lehmann analyses the changes in the provider market and presents the current technological and social developments in connection with the Internet. He develops a model for optimizing the organizational development of affected companies.
content.title_en: Change from telecommunications to unified communications: change processes for companies through internet-based innovation

content.text: The rapid technological change and the increasing competition pose challenges for companies. A continuing trend is the outsourcing of activities that are not core competencies to suppliers and service providers. Wolfgang Irlinger takes the supplier evaluation as a crucial aspect of supplier management. Based on the existing theory, he develops a causal model that is derived from the objectives of supplier management. Based on extensive data, the specification and estimation of this causal model is carried out using the partial-lesst-squares method. The hypothesis can be confirmed for the most part by the estimation of the model.
content.title_en: Supply assessment causal models

content.text: "Political Assessment" as a form of action of international institutions: the example of the OECD's fight against corruption. Main description: Gefion Schuler works on public access to the law of international organisations using the OECD's anti-corruption reporting procedure. In the first part, she examines the phenomenon of corruption and examines the OECD's reporting process from a governance and legal perspective. In the second part, the author discusses the basis for a legal dogmatic version of the OECD report procedure. She describes a concept of international public violence and discusses forms of action as appropriate legal theoretical constructs for the formulation of governance activities. In the third part, Schuler conceives the OECD reporting process from a public-law perspective as a form of action "Policy Assessment".
content.title_en: "Policy Assessment" as a form of action of international institutions: the example of the OECD's fight against corruption

content.text: Limits of the useability of data from electronic toll collection for preventive and repressive purposes. Main description: Patrick Gasch makes a systematic contribution to better determine the often unclear limits of state information trading in the areas of law enforcement, security and the fight against crime in the future. -- The design of the electronic toll system leads to a seizure of numerous data, on the one hand, and on the other hand it enables the security authorities to determine the location of persons at any time in other ways (IMSI-Catcher, radio cell query). The author deals in depth with the resulting problems, in particular with the interfaces for data storage, and identifies practical solutions. -- The focus of the work is on answering the question of the extent to which it is compatible with the freedom of self-conducting when data is to be used in a criminal procedure that is incurred by a device to which the citizen concerned was legally obliged to use.
content.title_en: Limits on the usability of electronic toll collection data for preventive and repressive purposes

content.text: Main description: "No plan identification can guarantee protection against terrorist acts", says the OVG Münster in 1984 (Urt. v. 23.3.1984, 11a NE 38/81). Quite differently the BVerwG in 2007: "The potential dangers for the neighbourhood (...) by terrorist attacks are important urban development effects" (Urt. v. 25.1.2007, 4 C 1/06). On the basis of this contrast Richard Hopkins is devoted to the question to which extent the building planning law can contribute to the defense against terrorist threats. He concludes against the background of urban planning, sociological, risk, disaster and spatial regulation considerations that the building planning law adequately handles the spatial reference of terrorist threats and its instruments assume an interface function between law on civil and urban planning.
content.title_en: Fighting terrorist threats and risks through building planning law

content.text: Data protection and search engines: new impulses for data protection on the Internet. Main description: Search engines are now indispensable for finding information on the World Wide Web. In their intermediary role between users and information providers, they are heavily involved in the flow of information on the World Wide Web. -- Data protection issues are raised when search engines bundle personal data in their hit lists and bring it to the light of the web public. -- Even more conflict-prone is the logging of search engine users' requests because collected search queries may provide deep insights into the interests, inclinations and wishes of the respective user and thus enable the compilation of sensitive personality profiles. These profiles have a high economic value for the internet advertising industry because they can be used for the placement of individually adapted advertisements. -- Robert Elixmann examines these two conflict areas based on German and American data protection law. He shows that against the display of personal content in search hits there are no legal concerns, but that often the logging practice of user behavior by large search engines violates German data protection laws.
content.title_en: Data protection and search engines: new impetus for data protection on the Internet

content.text: Stochastic optimization : Inventory optimization in multi-stage warehouse networks. The determination of optimal order strategies in storage has long been employed by scientists and practitioners. Konrad Schade presents methods of stochastic linear integer optimization, which can be used to determine robust order points for a multi-stage warehouse network. The author shows how the expected total costs can be minimized over the entire warehouse network.
content.title_en: Stochastic optimization : Inventory optimization in multi-stage warehouse networks

content.text: Basic concepts of green genetic engineering: scientific theory and natural philosophy. Discussions about modern technologies such as green genetic engineering often suffer from the fact that used terms are not explicitly made. They are introduced into a reasoning in different meanings without explicitly making a change of meaning explicit. This leads to the fact that evaluative conclusions are actually based on misconceptions and not really follow the reasoning. In the present work, basis of argumentation is created by presenting conceptual presuppositions, analysing and criticising them. For important basic concepts of green genetic engineering – breeding, living beings, natural goals, plants, species, genes – a reliable and understandable explication is given. Thus, an appropriate analysis tool is provided and own reasoning can be built context-oriented. Thus, the present volume provides a clarifying contribution to the moral and social discussion about green genetic engineering. Introduction -- Science theory basics -- Concept analysis -- Expressions in context and the evaluation of an argument -- literature.
content.title_en: Basic concepts of green genetic engineering : Theoretical and natural philosophy

content.text: Network management: An analysis of the design of inter-organisational performance exchange relationships. Cooperation in networks enables companies to explore new possibilities and exploit synergies. However, the failure rates are high, as the main focus is often on selecting suitable partners and contract design, but the management challenges are underestimated in the operational phase of networks. Christoph Bogenstahl derives the necessary management skills. The statements are based on the results of a systematic meta-analysis of 68 empirical studies and a data development analysis based on this, which is based on this, efficiency analysis of the management of networks in the healthcare sector. Development of a theoretically sound model of network management -- meta-analysis for network management -- efficiency measurement using data development analysis (DEA) -- empirical analysis of network management.
content.title_en: Network management: An analysis of the design of inter-organisational performance exchange relationships

content.text: Risk measurement with coherent, spectral and convex risk measures : conception, decision-making theoretical implications and financial applications. In response to the weaknesses of the value-at-risk concept, axiomatic risk measurement approaches were proposed as alternatives in the literature. Mario Brandtner characterizes the underlying risk understandings of these approaches and presents techniques for their implementation when defining concrete risk measures. He also shows that these original risk measures designed for regulatory purposes are inherently a restrictive tendency to marginal solutions when used to identify optimal decisions.
content.title_en: Risk measurement with coherent, spectral and convex risk measures : conception, decision-making theoretical implications and financial applications

content.text: Freedom of belief: analysis of a fundamental right. Freedom of belief is one of the least studied fundamental rights of the German constitution. Patrick Hoffmann is therefore dedicated to the concreteization of its content and its fields of action. He illuminates conceptual blurs and offers new solutions that, against the backdrop of the increasing social conflict situations in the area of freedom of conviction, are intended to help increase the conflict-absorption, normative regulatory power of the constitution. -- The results of the study underline the independence of the world view alongside religious freedom and highlight its importance as an overall view that is gained through reflection of its own subjectivity. Differentiated areas of protection for forms of ideological action will in future offer practical possibilities for appropriate distinctions and open up evaluation standards for the critical reflection of unequal treatment.
content.title_en: Freedom of belief: analysis of a fundamental right

content.text: Economic efficiency of RFID systems in logistics: Ex-ante quantification of the economic effects of ubiquitous information processing. ubiquitous information acquisition in the form of radio frequency identification (RFID) reduces the gap between the physical world and its computerized image and holds high but often difficult to quantify optimization potentials for companies. Daniel Gille analyses existing solutions of IT and RFID economics analysis and identifies limitations with regard to a complete modeling. Taking into account the results of a specially conducted empirical survey, he constructs an analytical forecast and evaluation model for RFID-supported logistics processes and derives design options for investments in RFID systems. Information systems and productivity -- elements of RFID economics analysis -- suitability of existing approaches of economic efficiency analysis -- model for forecasting and evaluation RFID-induced process optimization -- relevance and generalizability of results -- summary and outlook.
content.title_en: Efficiency of RFID systems in logistics : Ex-ante quantification of the economic effects of ubiquitous information processing

content.text: Process planning in semiconductor and electronic production: hybrid optimization processes and decomposition techniques. Optimization of process planning problems in semiconductor and electronic production is becoming increasingly important, resulting from higher demands of new technologies for production, increasing product diversity and flexibility, and increasing cost pressure on production. Andreas Klemmt provides an overview of these methods and creates a new hybrid optimization approach, which consists in the coupling of an event-discrete simulation system with a solver for mixed-in-all optimization problems. The practical application of the process is achieved by the development of decomposition techniques, which allow the process planning problems to be specifically disassembled into efficiently solvable partial problems. The author discusses these techniques for typical problems of the semiconductor industry. Process analysis Semiconductor industry -- Modelling and optimization of process planning problems -- Coupling simulation-based and exact processes -- Decomposition approaches for practical problems -- Implementation aspects.
content.title_en: Process planning in semiconductor and electronic production : Hybrid optimization processes and decomposition techniques

content.text: Performance and scaling of virtualized SAP-ERP systems. Virtualization plays an increasingly important role in the operation of SAP-ERP systems. However, the influence of virtualization on performance and scaling is often in the dark and only emerges in the event of problems. André Bögelsack uses the benchmark "Zachmanntest" to show how easy and effective SAP-ERP systems can be be be marked and the influences of virtualization can be named. Due to a large-scale analysis, the influences can be presented in detail in many load phases. The author also shows how to react to such influences and to ensure the performance of the SAP-ERP system.
content.title_en: Performance and scaling of virtualized SAP-ERP systems

content.text: Netguidance for Young People: Opportunities and Limits of Internet Skill Promotion and its Mediation. Eveline Hipeli examines suitable measures to provide young people with Internet literacy. The author analyses which socialisation institutions can be used as intermediaries and where their opportunities and limitations lie. Besides age, gender and school type, creative and critical Internet use as an influence factor for the attitudes of young people towards network guidance measures and intermediaries was investigated. Because the creative and critical use of the Internet presupposes different knowledge than a purely consumer-oriented use. Growing up and living in a digital media world -- Netguidance -- The young Internet user -- Media literacy as a key qualification -- The process of media socialization -- The Use and Gratifications approach -- The media ecological approach -- Opportunities and limits of socialisation bodies in the promotion of Internet literacy -- Research on Internet use and Internet literacy Young people -- Concreteization based on reference studies in Europe -- Written questioning in the canton of Zurich -- Results discussion.
content.title_en: Network guidance for young people: opportunities and limits of Internet literacy promotion and its placement

content.text: Supply Chain Coordination through supply contracts with rolling volume flexibility : A simulation study using the example of supply chains of the German automotive industry. Supply Chain Management -- Bullwhip effect -- Supply Contracts - Supply contracts with rolling volume flexibility -- Procurement network -- Supply Chain Simulation -- Automotive industry. Investigations on the coordination of industrial supply chains, which are based on the strategic design of flexi-bility in the supply chain, have so far received little attention. Jörg Wilke investigates supply contracts with rolling volume flexibility (RHF) in their function as a coordi-di-na-tion tool in industrial procurement networks using the example of the automotive industry. To this end, he develops a system dynamics simulation model, which reproduces the Bullwhip effect in a multi-stage rolling planning process of an automotive supply chain and takes into account other typical process characteristics of the procurement network.
content.title_en: Supply Chain Coordination through supply contracts with rolling quantities flexibility : A simulation study using the example of supply chains of the German automotive industry

content.text: Cross-border title recognition in the European Union: the effects of recognition, declaration of enforceability and enforceability of foreign decisions and Community titles. Main description: If civil judgments are enforced abroad, the question arises as to what effects they have. Max Peiffer addresses this classic problem of international civil procedural law on the basis of a comparison of German, English and French law. Both for the recognition of foreign judgments and their declaration of enforceability he develops his own model of effect. It is evident that both types of title import – contrary to a widespread thesis – are based on the same mechanism of action. This mechanism is also suitable – as the author proves – to explain the effects of the new Community-wide valid titles of European law (including EuTitleVO, EuMahnVO, EuBagatellVO). Max Peiffer not only provides a theoretical contribution, but also answers various individual questions of recognition and enforcement of foreign titles.
content.title_en: Cross-border Titles in the European Union: the effects of recognition, declaration of enforceability and enforceability of foreign decisions and Community titles

content.text: Co-creation of values in service management : An empirical analysis of the influence of other people at sports events. Theoretical foundations of value creation -- Scientific framework theories -- Qualitative and quantitative investigations -- Implications for service management. Many services are used in an environment in which other customers are present and have an influence on subjective sense of value. Existing measurement approaches for the determination of service quality focus on characteristics of the offer. The actual process of value formation during the use of performance and the underlying context remain unnoticed. Christian Durschholz contributes to closing this gap. He empirically examines the influence of other people on the perceived value of a service using the example of a sports event and gives recommendations for the management of services.
content.title_en: Co-creation of values in service management: An empirical analysis of the influence of other people at sporting events

content.text: The internal organisation of seaports as a problem of European competition law. Main description: Sarah Dwertmann deals with the problem of access to the market for port services. In order to open up this market, the European Commission had presented two drafts for a market access directive in 2001 and 2004. After both draft directives had failed during the legislative process, the question of the fundamental necessity of such a directive arose. The focus of the work is therefore on the question whether a sustainable market opening in the area of port services can also be achieved through European competition law. The investigation shows that the antitrust "essential facilities" doctrine can be derived from access rights to port facilities. However, for reasons of legal certainty and legal clarity, the adoption of secondary legislation should be sought in the medium term.
content.title_en: The internal organisation of seaports as a problem of European competition law

content.text: The Baltic Sea Region Building: the role of universities in the process of regionalisation in the north-east of the European Union. Cooperation in the Baltic Sea Region -- Overview of the higher education systems of the countries studied -- Empirical analysis of university networking in the Baltic Sea Region -- The educational influence of regional political institutions -- Networks as key actors in regional cooperation Since the adoption of the Baltic Sea Strategy in 2009 by the European Council, the Baltic Sea Region has received special attention within the European Union. Stefan Ewert develops an index that can be used to review the thesis of the regional-building approach, according to which universities play a central role in the process of regionalisation in the Baltic Sea Region.
content.title_en: Region Building in the Baltic Sea Region : on the role of universities in the process of regionalisation in the North-East of the European Union

content.text: Preventive self-defense in international law: a systematic investigation of the current peace-keeping acquis from a dogmatic and practical point of view. Main description: Does international law allow states to strike for a violent first strike as "preventing self-defense"? If so, under what conditions? The author would like to give an international legal answer to these also politically explosive questions. This happens in successive logical individual steps: First, existing conceptual confusions are eliminated, the subject of investigation is precisely defined and the current discussion status is presented. Then, with the help of previously derived theoretical framework conditions, the international treaty and customary law of the last 200 years is evaluated. Attention is paid to the methods, which are hardly discussed, but which are predetermined by international law, such as the legal linguistic comparison of all five authoritative language versions of Art. 51 SVN. The overall analysis shows that preventive self-defense is legal if an attack is imminent or the probability of an attack is evident at any time.
content.title_en: Preventive self-defense in international law: a systematic identification of the current peace-keeping acquis from a dogmatic and practical point of view

content.text: The protection of privacy and the right to informational self-determination: using the example of personal data traffic in WWW under German public law. Main description: Recent incidents of data espionage by Apple, Google and Co. show that the time and location-independent use of the Internet for the user is accompanied by an increased risk of data misuse and the threat of privacy. Ruth Weidner-Braun is dedicated to the central question whether and in what way in connection with personal data traffic in WWW an effective protection of the constitutionally guaranteed personality right can be achieved. The contribution to legal certainty of the existing national and international legal regulations and whether the intended strengthening of the data protection guaranteed special rights of the user with the recent amendment of the Federal Data Protection Act has succeeded in the scope of the Federal Data Protection Act, especially for the areas of e-commerce, e-government and Internet use in the workplace, are further focus issues. An analysis on the responsibility of providers, measures to counter the risks and the proportionality of state control on the Internet, finally round off the comprehensive investigation in terms of ensuring freedom and security for the use of the Internet.
content.title_en: The protection of privacy and the right to informational self-determination: on the example of personal data traffic in WWW under German public law

content.text: Identities and stereotypes in cross-border interdependence spaces : The example of the Greater Region. Based on qualitative interviews with actors in the cross-border interdependence region, Antje Schönwald investigates identities and stereotypes as well as their effects on actions beyond traditional spatial concepts. The author analyses the origin and consequence of categorization in cross-border cooperation and the relationship between self- and foreign representation. In addition, she identifies large-regional identities. Cross-border interdependence spaces on the West German border -- identity and stereotype -- Empirical investigation -- Recommendations for action.
content.title_en: Identities and stereotypes in cross-border interdependence areas : The example of the Greater Region

content.text: Social City - Politique de la Ville - Political Logic : (Re-)Production of cultural differentiations in urban politics related to urban areas in Germany and France. Introduction: Urban policies related to urban areas and "cultural differentiations": An analysis of political logics -- Social City and politique de la ville: Developments and research status on "cultural differentiations" -- The discourse theory of Ernesto LACLAU and Chantal MOUFFE -- Reformulation of questions and methodological approaches -- On the (re-)production of "cultural differentiations": of breaks and transnational discourses. . In France and Germany, in the 1970s and 1990s, the Politique de la Ville and the Social City of Quartiers established politiques-related funding programmes. In both countries, many quarters are promoted, which are described as such with high migrant participation. While in the social city migrants have become a central target group, in the 1970s and 1990s, they are not explicitly covered at national level – due to the French idea of equality. Florian Daniel Weber examines the regionalities – regional differentiations are currently present on a national basis.
content.title_en: Social City - Politique de la Ville - Political Logic : (Re-)Production of Cultural Differentiations in Urban Policy in Germany and France

content.text: Changing school: Openness as a challenge in the governance of educational innovations. ?Why is it sometimes so difficult to anchor educational innovations in the school system? Marianne Ullmann deals with the often asked question from the perspective of educational governance and the actor-network theory. In this context, she shows that both the planning and the evaluation of innovation projects need methods that aim less at an event control than at an openness to the unexpected. The author contributes to the (further) development of a "good governance" in relation to school reform projects Why is it sometimes so difficult to anchor educational innovations in the school system? Marianne Ullmann deals with the often asked question from the perspective of educational governance and the actor-network theory. In doing so, she shows that both the planning and the evaluation of innovation projects need methods that aim less at event control than at openness to the unexpected.
content.title_en: Changing schools: Openness as a challenge in the governance of educational innovations

content.text: Main description: David Bruch deals with the difficult relationship between fundamental freedom on the one hand and the need to protect the environment as a natural basis of life on the other. Taking into account the fact that environmental burdens affect the environment as a prerequisite for exercising freedom or sometimes even eliminate it, the author explores to what extent the protection areas of fundamental rights such as professional freedom under Art. 12 para. 1 GG or the freedom of ownership under Art. 14 GG are opened for private environmental burdens. Bruch concludes that harmful or even fatal environmental pollution and environmental pollution, which constitute an instrumentalization of foreign property, are not protected by the protection areas of special freedom rights, i.e. that there is an environmental liability of the fundamental legal protection areas.
content.title_en: Environmental liability of the areas of fundamental rights

content.text: Secondary maritime climate protection: the example of ocean fertilization. Main description: Kerstin Güssow deals with climate engineering as a measure of secondary climate protection and analyses international standards for their applicability and suitability for assessing this method using the example of ocean fertilization. The first part outlines the scientific background of ocean fertilization. It is evident that neither the success of ocean fertilization as a method for long-term sequestration of CO2 on the seabed is assured, nor possible negative side effects can be eliminated or, vice versa, confirmed as unacceptable. The second part focuses on existing law and recent developments concerning ocean fertilization. The method is in legal terms in the conflict area between maritime international law, the law of biodiversity and climate protection law. However, the different areas of international law do not cover the issue of ocean fertilization in the final analysis. Instead, the scientific uncertainty associated with this technological method remains contradictory. As a connecting link between the affected areas of international law and the law of ocean fertilization, the third part of the work is based on the principle of nature, the rules of prevention and the rules of law allow for the use of the rules of law to be based on the principles of law.
content.title_en: Secondary maritime climate protection: the example of ocean fertilization

content.text: The extraterritorial application of anti-fraud rules in US capital markets law. Main description: The extraterritorial application of US federal securities fraud rules, the anti-fraud rules Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5, has been discussed for years. It is in the conflict of interests of states, plaintiffs and defendants. With the decision Morrison v. National Australia Bank Ltd. in 2010, the US Supreme Court first took on this issue. Johannes Richter discusses the foundations of extraterritorial legal application in the US, the development of jurisprudence and legislation before and after this decision, as well as criticisms, problems and suggestions for solutions. It is clear that the US Supreme Court has succeeded in excluding the particularly problematic issues from the scope of anti-fraud rules, but has not achieved any final clarity overall.
content.title_en: The extraterritorial application of anti-fraud rules in US capital markets law

content.text: Landscape in the changing world? : Contemporary landscape concepts in science, planning and everyday life. Since the mid-1990s, landscape has been increasingly the topic of spatial sciences; at the same time, the term has gained in importance in political and programmatic documents. Dorothea Hokema examines less physical space than the landscape concept. The starting point of the study is the view that landscape is a social construction that is different – depending on culture, socialization or interests. From this social constructivist perspective, commonalities and differences of landscape understandings in spatial sciences, planning practice and everyday language are analyzed. Contradictions and similarities within and between the discourses are determined, they are classified in both idea-historical and current social contexts. As a result, a model of the contemporary landscape concept is developed that allows to accurately show its ambivalences. The content · The idea history of the landscape concept · The landscape concept of spatial sciences, planning practice and everyday language · Discussion The target groups · Dozierende und Studieren der Geographie, Raumplanung, Landschaftsplanungplanung und Landschaftarchitekturarchitektur Berlin The TUothspektung Berlin is a German author.
content.title_en: Landscape in the Change? : Contemporary Landscape Concepts in Science, Planning and Everyday Life

content.text: Farewell to the concept of termination of the offence in criminal law. Usually, the final conclusion of a criminal offence is called termination, which differs from the completion of the offence. Although the term termination of the offence is only enshrined in §§ 2 and 78a StGB, it also acquires its meaning for the interpretation of the individual offences, for the theory of participation, intent and competition. -- The author assumes that the meaning of termination of the offence results only from the telelogical consideration of the relevant criminal law standards in the respective legal area. However, the previous doctrine of termination has largely overlooked this context of reasoning. A detailed legal-area-specific investigation shows that the concept of termination of the offence in the respective legal area is either superfluous or leads to unnecessarily complicated law interpretation.
content.title_en: Farewell to the concept of ending the offence in criminal law

content.text: Legal protection against legal injustice in civil proceedings which are no longer capable of being dealt with by the courts: an evaluation of the standards of the German and Swiss civil procedural right of retrial. The work is conceived as a legal evaluation, aimed at determining the effectiveness of the legal protection against legal injustice provided by the ZPO by means of extraordinary appeals in civil proceedings which are not (more) eligible for legal redress, and thus falls into the field of impact research. After a re-examination of the problem of "protection of the law against the judge" and the legislative implementation errors in the introduction of the hearing hearing proceedings, the study deals with the erosion of the law of § 339 StGB, which is to be held by the BGH, to be a legal norm with only symbolic function, which led to the factual elimination of the restitution action of § 580 No. 5 ZPO in cases of legal denial.
content.title_en: Legal protection against legal injustice in civil proceedings which are no longer eligible for legal assistance: an evaluation of standards of German and Swiss civil procedural retrial law which also compares law

content.text: Proper and effective : the principle of efficiency as a means of concreteizing general civil clauses. For decision-making with the economic analysis of the law and its efficiency principle, as the BGH also recognized, decisions in the scope of general clauses seem particularly suitable. Because here the requirements of the legislator are sparsely recognized, the role of the judge strongly and the consequences consideration. -- However, a comparison of the solutions reveals a conflict of objectives between the conventional and the new approach, confirming the methodological considerations: Applying the collective measure of efficiency prevents the function of the general clauses to take account of the individual case. The categorical principle of efficiency also contradicts the necessary consideration with other principles. The method-appropriate concretization of general clauses is therefore blocked for the efficiency principle beyond a supplement.
content.title_en: Good faith and efficiency: the efficiency principle as a means of concretising general civil clauses

content.text: The rise and fall of the European carbon economy: The crisis of the EU's emissions trading from the state and economic theory perspective. The statement that global climate policy is in a deep crisis sounds almost like a throbbing phrase. Only too much has become accustomed to media and scientific observers to accuse the parties of the Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Kyoto Protocol of short-term power-policy considerations of inaction, particular behaviour or even the cynicism of an après nous la déluge. If one asks the media and scientific observers or also the political protagonists of the global climate policy for an actor who could be able to take the lead with good example and to guide the international community into a decarbonized future, then the principle of hope is not infrequently directed to the European Union (EU). Martin Bitter examines the crisis of the European emissions trading system by looking at the contradictions of market-based climate policy and placing them in the power field of European regulation. The topic of the social policy on the problem-of-the-use of the environment.
content.title_en: Rise and fall of the European carbon economy: the crisis of EU emissions trading from a state and economic theoretical perspective
