content.text: The implementation of European directives in Germany and the UK, using the distance selling directive as an example. The "Remote Sales Directive" 97/7/EC intervenes deeply in contractual relations between consumers and entrepreneurs and thus in a core area of national civil law in order to create a common market in distance selling. Its transformation into national law in Germany and the UK and thus in two completely different legal traditions shows the advantages and disadvantages of the respective implementation methods. -- Thus, the regulations of the directive became part of the German Federal Code of Civil Law through the dynamic implementation history and employed the courts up to the ECJ, while the Consumer Protection (Distance Selling) Regulations 2000 in the British common law largely remain a foreign body. In addition, the deficits of national implementation also open the view of deficits of the directive itself, which could be partially corrected in the successor Directive 2011/83/EU.
content.title_en: The implementation of European directives in Germany and the UK using the example of the Distance Selling Directive

content.text: Trading with electricity from renewable energies: a combination of forecasts. In the context of the energy transition, the strong increase in electricity generation from renewable energies in Germany leads to a fundamental change in the electricity market. In the trade with electricity from renewable energies, the forecast used for marketing is very important. In the event of a strong deviation from the actual electricity generated, high costs can arise. Dietmar Richard Graeber presents in his book the basic principles of trading with electricity from renewable energies and forecasting methods of electricity generation from renewable energies. A combination method developed by the author for such forecasts enables a significant reduction in the costs of trading with electricity from renewable energies. The content: framework conditions for trading with electricity from renewable energies, methods for forecasting electricity from renewable energies and methods for combining such forecasts. The target groups: lecturers and students in the field of energy management, operations research, econometrics, energy meteorology, practitioners in the field of renewable energies, electricity trading, grid operation. The author Dr. Dietmar Richard Graeber is a consultant for special tasks in the field of energy market of a transmission network operator and is responsible for the foundations of trading with renewable energies at the University.
content.title_en: Trading in electricity from renewable energy : combination of forecasts

content.text: The appropriate profit premium of disposal companies in public contracts at cost. Up to now, no solid solution has been established in the case law on the question of how high a reasonable profit premium of disposal companies can be in public contracts at cost, although this topic has been the subject of numerous court judgments and is still the subject of this issue. The main responsibility for this is the tension between the price-law regulations and the municipal tax regulations. Timo Hövelborn analyses this open legal question from an economic perspective. Based on the objective of public price law, the author derives as a fundamental principle that a profit premium is appropriate in terms of price law if it leads to a market-standard interest rate on the capital capital employed. On this basis, he develops an approach to determine a reasonable profit premium and quantifies this empirically. The content ·Legal framework of public contract management ·Overview of the case law on the legality of the profit premium ·Price-legally reasonable profit The target groups ·Doctoral and students of the economic sciences with the emphasis on economic law and economic policy ·Applicator of the PR 30/53: public contract management and contractor as well as well as a user of the KAG's executive executive executive.
content.title_en: Adequate profit premium on public procurement by disposal companies at cost

content.text: The study examines the extent and relevance of federal variations in integration policies in the Swiss cantons. The study contributes to the development of the young research branch of quantitative migration research in three ways. First, it refines existing typologies of integration regimes by presenting a differentiated analysis of specific policy components underlying these regimes. Second, comprehensive regression analyses of the determinants of cantonal integration policies illustrate the stability and path dependence of these policies. Third, the findings of Bayesian multilevel analyses show the importance of cantonal integration policies for immigrant integration, especially for social and structural integration in school and labour market
content.title_en: Cantonal integration policy in comparison : an investigation of determinants and effects of subnational policy diversity

content.text: Borders and orders in Central Asia: transactions and attitudes between Afghanistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Central Asia is a space of state fragility that awakens associations such as drug trafficking and instability. Social orders and the boundaries that define them have frequently changed in this region.What functions do borders have there today in the face of parallel processes of the State and Nation Building? How do borders affect the perceptions of the border population? And above all: What drives cross-border relations and what inhibits them? State and Nation BuildingThe author examines these questions along the young state border between Tajikistan and Uzbekistan as well as at border sections of both states to Afghanistan – once the dividing line of geopolitical regions. Although the authoritarian regimes in Tajikistan and, more importantly, in Uzbekistan, are building their state building projects in delimiting supposedly destabilizing influences of the neighbours.
content.title_en: Borders and orders in Central Asia : transactions and attitudes between Afghanistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan

content.text: The cognitive dimension of lobbyism: a framing analysis of European technology policy. In the EU, lobbyists not only communicate their particular interests to political decision-makers, but also ask for interests to justify their projects. From a constructive perspective, policy-making is like a competition for the interpretation of a social issue. The actors are dependent on each other for the subjective perception of problems and for the justification of policy projects. The cognitive framework of the political discourse can be described as a policy framework. A framing approach shows that lobbyists' influence opportunities also depend on the necessity to justify policy projects at the EU level. Using the example of EU technology policy, it becomes clear that the Commission can achieve the interpretation sovereignty with the help of policy-frames, but that it is always dependent on the interdependent communication process of intermediation of interests in the respective policy field.
content.title_en: The cognitive dimension of lobbyism: a framing analysis of European technology policy

content.text: Security policy between the state and the market: the protection of critical infrastructures. Attacks on vital infrastructures such as IT, energy supply or transport cause consequential damage to the entire society. However, as a result of the privatisation of these "critical infrastructures", the state lacks direct control possibilities; security policy depends on the participation of private operators. Germany relies heavily on voluntary cooperation with the private sector. The author analyses this policy and the underlying premise. It shows that German politics is based on unrealistic assumptions about the functioning of markets that can endanger the fulfilment of the constitutional protection order "Infrastructure security"
content.title_en: Security policy between the State and the market: protection of critical infrastructures

content.text: Lifestyle segmentation based on content-based analysis of digital images : --. Market segmentation is one of the most discussed topics in marketing. A hardly used data basis is the content-based analysis of digital images. Digital images are becoming increasingly important in today's society and are becoming increasingly public. Thus, numerous new data is generated for market research which can provide new insights. Against this background, Ines Daniel pursues the question whether photographs reflect the activities, opinions and interests of their owners. In addition, she examines whether and how probanden-based photographs can expand the data collection and evaluation. The developed concept for photography-supported lifestyle segmentation has been validated by means of two empirical investigations. The content market segmentation Content-based analysis of digital images Fundamentals and concept of lifestyle segmentation Validation of lifestyle segmentation as well as recommendations for action The target groups Dozierde and students of business administration, business information technology and business engineering with the focus on market research and innovation management as well as image processing Specialists and managers in market research institutes and corporate consulting The author Dr. Ines Daniel completed his doctorate at Prof. Baier at the Marketing Center for Business Management of the Business of Lifestyle.
content.title_en: Lifestyle segmentation based on content-based analysis of digital images : --

content.text: Smart financial sanctions of the EU: a policy-scientific and bank-practical analysis of selected measures. The paradigm shift in UN sanctions policy after the end of the Cold War and the 9/11 attacks led to the decree "smarter-, including personal sanctions of the EU against terrorist financing. The study examines the fundamentals of ideology-political and implementation effectiveness of selected measures from a political, legal and banking perspective. It offers a scientific interdisciplinarity that is not so common and a consistently structured analysis framework "from Kant to the account". It is established that the regime lacks effectiveness due to legal deficits and associated legal uncertainty and compliance risks for banks when implementing measures. The study shows practical approaches to reform the EU financial sanctions regime as an instrument of the "Economic Statecraft" and offers valuable suggestions for researchers, policy makers and bank practitioners.
content.title_en: Smart financial sanctions of the EU: a policy-scientific and banking practice analysis of selected measures

content.text: The use of 3D printing technology in mathematics teaching: Theoretical basics and exemplar applications for analysis. Frederik Dilling examines the possibilities of 3D printing technology for mathematics teaching in upper secondary school. To this end, this is classified into didactic research as well as into the current curricular specifications for mathematics.The author discusses the following four concrete applications developed at the University of Siegen in the light of a material didactic background: functions of one and two variable, tangents at functional graphs and the main set of differential and integral calculus.The content Functionality of 3D printing technology Material use in conceptual processes Use of digital technologies to support learning processes Action-oriented learning with models of functional graphs Visual justification of the main set based on an integraph The target groups Dozende der Mathematikdidaktik Students and teachers for the field of mathematics The author Frederik Dilling is working as a scientific employee in the department for didactics of mathematics at the university.
content.title_en: The use of 3D printing technology in mathematics teaching : Theoretical principles and exemplary applications for analysis

content.text: The company's research on the pulse-separated charge of a four-cylinder petrol engine was conducted by the company's research team at the University of Stuttgart. Flushing charge change at the single-flooded loader concept -- Two-stage discharge lift and offset discharge phase -- CFD investigations on the cracker evaluation -- Modelling of a mass and friction-laden, vibration-laden wastegate. Adalbert Wolany investigates various aspects of the pulse-separated charge and presents new methods for this purpose. The author develops suitable discharge times for the flushing charge change at the single-flooded exhaust turbocharger and optimizes the charge change through partial flute separation in the nominal power range with regard to consumption. He presents a new method for assessing the current of exhaust gas coils in the CFD simulation, which examines the entire usable energy content of the fluid at the burster discharge.
content.title_en: Studies on pulse-separated charging on a four-cylinder petrol engine

content.text: The Elbe flood in 2002 has led to a rapid legal development at the national and European level. The author systematically and comprehensively examines the new possibilities for the recovery of public flood prevention in Germany. He takes into account the flood protection law (2005) in particular, the "Federalism Reform I-2006", the EC High Water Directive (2007) and the recast of the Water Budget Act (2009).The basis of the investigation is the measures required from the actual point of view to ensure an "optimal flood prevention" and the legal framework for this existing national constitutional and international law. Against this background, an analysis of the simple legal system is carried out. It is to be calculated to what extent the precautionary concept, which is considered desirable, can be implemented at present and how identified deficits should be corrected. The work is therefore particularly valuable for legal practice.
content.title_en: Public flood prevention against the background of actual and legal basic requirements

content.text: Legal problems of the design of the public service broadcasting mission in the online field. The work deals with the legal problems arising from the design of the online activities of public service broadcasting from an annex service to an original contract area. The regulatory framework for public service telemedia offers is highly differentiated and unclear. The legislator has established detailed regulations with one of the previous radio law regulations. The work deals with these content, time and procedural requirements (three-stage test) on the telemedia offers and shows their possibilities and limits, also in relation to commercial activities and taking into account cooperation with third parties. Finally, it carries out the regulatory framework of an evaluation. This gives a practical insight into the complexity of the integration of online services into the commission of the broadcasting institutions according to the 12th RÄStV
content.title_en: Legal problems of the design of the public service broadcasting mission in the online sector

content.text: Anonymity for user-generated content? : constitutional and simple-legal analysis of the information requirements for journalistic-editorial offers and other telemedia in §§ 5 TMG, 55 RStV. The work provides interpretative determinants for essential border concepts of information law such as for profit, journalistic-editorial or personal-familiar or that of the information and communication service. These characteristics decide in §§ 5 TMG, 55 RStV on the obligation of telemedia providers to reveal their identity. Under pressure they are affected by the increasing dissolution of communication roles in view of the phenomenon user-generated content. The original state of its work – anonymity or pseudo-nymality – enjoys fundamental legal protection, as the study shows. The goals pursued with the digital "obligation for the imprint of information" are thus the subject of a constitutional weighing process that is initially open to results. With its legal analysis, the work provides a basis on which the discussion already conducted by the state and by the company side about anonymous user contributions on the Internet can be continued meaningfully.
content.title_en: Anonymity for user-generated content? : constitutional and simple-legal analysis of information requirements for journalistic-editorial offers and other telemedia in §§ 5 TMG, 55 RStV

content.text: The work examines for the first time the various legal issues that arise in connection with the management of bottlenecks in national electricity supply networks and at the border points. A thorough analysis of the legal framework for congestion management (e.g., VO 714/2009, §§ 13, 14 EnWG, §§ 11, 12 EEG) will be used to identify and systematize the conditions and legal consequences of short-term (e.g., countertrading, redispatch) and long-term (e.g. explicit and implicit auctions, market coupling) instruments of congestion management. The work will address in detail the numerous individual issues that arise in connection with congestion management, e.g. capacity calculation and capacity allocation, secondary trading, revenue utilization, market delimitation, selection of measures of short-term congestion management, remuneration, liability and compensation, cooperation of network operators, supervision and efficiency control.
content.title_en: congestion management in German and European electricity supply

content.text: The concept and concept of integration in the Residence Act. "Integration of foreigners" has been a highly topical but highly controversial issue for many politicians and social scientists for years. So far, lawyers have hardly dealt with the topic. "Integration" has become a central concept of the Aliens Law since the entry into force of the Residence Act on 1 January 2005. It depends on its interpretation, for example, whether foreigners living in Germany may be allowed to stay or take up employment. The author tries to determine, analyse and evaluate the concept of integration and the integration policy concept of the Residence Act by applying legal interpretation methods and using relevant sociological theories.
content.title_en: Concept and concept of integration in the Residence Act

content.text: The principle of effectiveness: an investigation into the case law of the European Court of Justice. Since 1976, the European Court of Justice has ruled that, while Member States are allowed to rely on their national law when implementing Union law, it is not possible to make enforcement of Union law impossible or excessively difficult (Effectiveness Principle). Up to now, what is meant by this practically highly important standard statement was not clarified. This gap fills the author. It shows that a subjective and objective expression of the principle of effectiveness must be distinguished. Against this background, the case law is analysed and systematised. The author works out among other things those criteria on which the expression of the principle of effectiveness of the ECJ relies and how strictly it is used. Overall, despite the strong criticism in literature, the case law of the Court is regarded as largely positive.
content.title_en: The principle of effectiveness: an investigation into the case law of the European Court of Justice

content.text: The Federal Environmental Protection Legislation. The work deals in detail with the scope of the Federal Environmental Protection Legislation, which has not yet been clarified in the final analysis. It also contributes to the discussion on the advantages and disadvantages of introducing a uniform title of competence for environmental protection legislation. After an interpretation of the concepts of environment and environmental protection, the detailed remarks on the "environmental protection-specific" and on the essential "environmental protection-relevant" competences follow. The result of the inventory is then measured by the challenges and tasks of modern environmental protection legislation. This part shows that the changes in Art. 72 ff. GG, which were carried out in the course of federal reform, were not far enough in terms of environmental protection legislation, but rather the introduction of a uniform environmental protection competence of the Federal Environmental Protection Act would be appropriate.
content.title_en: The federal legislative competences in environmental protection

content.text: The purpose of the assignment is to provide for the calculation of third party behaviour in the field of security law. General accounting principles have not developed to this day. Different accounting criteria, which are aligned with the individual case, are applied. The author proposes a reconception of the purpose of the assignment, which separates individual cases-dependent imputability considerations from the assignment decision and allows the introduction of a uniform assignment criterion. Based on current case-designs – including the risk-reduction responsibility for riots at football league games and at Facebook parties, for counter-violence in the assembly law and for terrorist attacks on endangered objects – the reconception is examined to its adequacy and practical suitability. The author also examines the extent to which the calculation concept developed for the purpose admission can be transferred to similar accounting questions outside the police and order law, for example in the case of private persons for the purpose of public service, for indirect access to fundamental rights and for indirect prosecution.
content.title_en: Purpose : a contribution to the imputation of third party behaviour in public law

content.text: The European Investigation Order in Criminal Matters: Implementation Requirements for the German Legislator. Regulatory Content and Uniform Purpose of the RL EEA -- The European Investigation Order: from Legal Assistance to Mutual Recognition -- The EEA - a compromise instrument -- Requirements for the Transposition Legislator -- Questions of Evaluability of Evidence obtained through an EEA -- The new position of the accused rights Andrea Leonhardt examines the implementation requirements of the Directive on European Investigation Order in Criminal Matters (RL EEA) to the German Legislator.The author explains in particular after a comparison with the European Arrest Warrant and the European Evidence Order why she advocates a uniform inter-state and European investigation cooperation.The content Regulatory Content and Uniform Purpose of the RL EEA The European Investigation Order: from Legal Assistance to Mutual Recognition The EEA - a compromise instrument< Requirements for the Transposition Legislator Evaluability Questions of Evidence gained through an EEA The new position of the accused rights The target groups Dozierden and students of the legal sciences Speakers, Judges, State and Rechtsanwälte, Investigungsbehörstellein The author of the English law at the L.
content.title_en: The European Investigation Order in Criminal Matters: Implementation Requirements for the German Legislator

content.text: The Mediatisation of Climate Policy: A comparative input-output analysis for the adoption of media logic by politics. Jörg Hassler shows by means of the example of climate policy that parties and political groups take on the content-related criteria of success that they can use profitably for themselves. Using an input-output analysis and a comparison of media and political offline and online communication channels, he examines the adoption of media logic by politics. The contrast between media logic and political logic makes a theoretical contribution to the systematization of the approach to mediatization. The results show firstly that media logic and political logic are not significantly different offline and online. Secondly, the politics in the representation of climate policy are only partly oriented towards media logic. Third, parties and political groups on their websites hardly take media logic more than in their offline channels. The content dimensions of media logic influence on political logic The representation of climate change through media and politics International and national climate policy is based on the media logic.
content.title_en: Mediatisation of climate policy: A comparative input-output analysis for the adoption of media logic by politics

content.text: The contribution of the lecture recording in the teaching business: compatibility of study, tasks of existence and everyday roles. Lasse Wirz develops an e-learning system for recording university courses and investigates both implications for students, faculties and universities, and requirements that must be placed on the process of system development and the ongoing operation of the lecture recording. The content developments in the areas of e-learning and blended learning Theses about the stakeholder "Students-related effects of authentication students and mobile availability Lecture recording and flexibility Quantitative usage behaviour - evaluation of the recording of usage data with the system SADLIT The target groups Dozierde, student and researcher from the fields of business information technology, in particular e-learning and lecture recording, as well as the social science research Practicers from the field of e-learning and human resource development in companies, university policy makers Author Lasse Wirz is the founder and manager of the business enterprise.
content.title_en: The contribution of lecture recording in the teaching establishment : compatibility of studies, tasks of existence and everyday roles

content.text: What is the Online Voice of the German Parliament: The 2013 Election in the Web 2.0. Based on the 2013 Election in the Bundestag, Kay Hinz investigates how candidates and citizens communicate with each other in the online election campaign on facebook and Twitter and what this is influenced by. The aim is to find out what candidates are guided by their communicative actions. With findings of over 600 candidates, this study provides for the first time structured data on their campaign activities for a Bundestag election on the Web 2.0. How they inform, network with them, mobilize and encourage them to participate is most likely to be characterized by individual characteristics of the candidates. Influences of factors of the party and the overall election system play a subordinate role for communication behaviour. The content Actors and objectives of political online communication Functions of the online election campaign Meaning of personnel, organizational and demand-oriented factors Results: What influences the fulfilment of functions? Conclusion: Personelle Becharakterakterika als Stimmen der Online Communication The target groups Dozierdeen und Studieren der Politiknkommunik, Kommunikierung und der Politiksberatärberater, Campaigner, Sozialierunger Kopenschafter Kopenschaft der Stadt- Kaufen- Behörung und Behörung und Behmen
content.title_en: Candidates and their supporters in the online election campaign : The 2013 Bundestag election in Web 2.0

content.text: The concept of control of the performance of complex services. Stefan Gegg presents in this work a completely new controlling concept for the recording, measurement and evaluation of complex services. Based on a detailed analysis of the components performance and complexity, a groundbreaking further development of performance controlling is presented here and extended to the first controlling concept based entirely on cybernetics. This concept enables for the first time the adequate recording, measurement and evaluation of complex services without loss of information and quality. The content • Development and definition of a definition of operational performance • Presentation of a general basic model for the identification of complex services • The subject approach: Effects of complexity requirements on the necessary characteristics of the performance subject • Requirements for the generation of information on complex services • Presentation of the underlying controlling concept for a performance controlling for complex services • Conceptual design of controlling instruments for complex services The target groups • Dozierende, Studierenden und Praktiker aus der Bereichen Controlling und Management The author Stefan F. Gegg is currently Chairman of the board of the Flup AG (Berlin). After his studies in Freiburg, Vienna and Tübingen he completed a thesis on the concept of control of complex services. His focus on the definition of the concept of control and operational performance.
content.title_en: Performance controlling for complex performance

content.text: The SCM's Design Platform for Supply Chain Management: Design Recommendations for the Cooperative Coordination of Supply Chain. Based on SCM reference models of the automotive, consumer goods and logistics industry, Ronald Poppe systematically develops an SCM cooperation platform as a holistic and practical design model for the cooperative coordination of supply chain. The author outlines the feasibility and benefits of a descriptive case study of the pharmaceutical industry. Furthermore, the derived design recommendations for the combined use of structural, technical and informational coordination instruments are concretely defined together with other practical cases.The conceptual framework for an SCM cooperation platform Identifying design recommendations based on SCM reference models Analysis of SCM cooperation platforms for the pharmaceutical supply chain The target groups Dozierende und Studierende der Betriebswirtschaftslehre, (Wirtschafts-)Informatik und (Wirtschafts-)Ingenieurwissenschaften Subjects and executives from the fields of Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Purchasing, IT and Corporate Development The author Dr. Ronald Poppe has been a Ph.D.
content.title_en: Cooperation platforms for supply chain management : Design recommendations for the cooperative coordination of supply chain

content.text: The adequacy of the remuneration for the transfer of property rights as a problem of legally shaped corporate valuation: value-finding between business foundation and norm-oriented concreteization. Decision-oriented corporate valuation -- Objective corporate valuation according to IDW S1 -- Adequacy of severance payments and exchange relationships -- Adequacy of corporate acquisitions according to WpÜG. Christina Große-Frericks examines the adequacy of charges such as severance payments and exchange relationships in the conflicting field of corporate value and market price orientation for different legal events of corporate valuation. The assessment of the adequacy of these compensation services becomes a complex question, since the value-finding in the intersection of business economics and law has to be carried out and the claims of the required business management funding and the relevant norm-oriented concreteization must be satisfied. It is shown that a fundamental valuation is indispensable, however, the present calculation and structures need to be further developed and supplemented in the context of the business management management advisory. The content decision-oriented corporate valuation according to IDW S1 Adequacy of compensation and conversion relationships of business management management in the business management advisory areas.
content.title_en: The appropriateness of the remuneration for the transfer of ownership rights as a problem of legal corporate valuation: value finding between business foundation and normatively appropriate concreteisation

content.text: Municipal institutions and public services: Studies on municipal efficiency and satisfaction of citizens. Annette Illy develops evaluation standards for measuring decentralisation at the municipal level and uses modern econometric methods to investigate the influence of community types and community size on municipal efficiency and citizens' satisfaction. This is particularly relevant in the context of municipal area reforms since the 1990s, which have led to the emergence of ever larger municipalities and community associations. Furthermore, municipal associations are increasingly being dissolved and converted into unit municipalities.The analyses do not reveal clear advantages or disadvantages of decentralisation at the municipal level; rather, the political decision-making processes have to balance the goals and standards for the reforms.The content of municipal services in Germany Decentralisation at the municipal level Efficiency analysis of municipal services Satisfaction and connectivity with the municipality The target groups Dozierde and students in the field of economics, in particular financial sciences and institutional economics Practitioners in the field of regional and local politics The author Dr. Annette Illy received his doctorate at Prof. Dr. Heinz P. Galler at the Chair of Econometrics at the Martin-Lutherenberg-University in the municipal level.
content.title_en: Local institutions and public services: studies on the efficiency and satisfaction of citizens

content.text: Acceptance and use of mobile applications. Mobile applications -- Mobile recruiting -- Acceptance and use of mobile applications -- Use motivations, user experience and satisfaction -- Causal analysis and structural equation modelling. Susanne Niklas analyses key factors influencing the inital acceptance and further use of mobile applications. Using the example of mobile job portals, the author examines application characteristics as well as individual objectives and usage motivations, which influence the further use of mobile applications. Mobile applications enjoy a high acceptance of the download, but are often only used once and then forgotten.The results of causal analysis offer links for sustainable application development and marketing, in order to counteract the frequently occurring problem of one-time use.The content Mobile applications Mobile recruiting Acceptance and use of mobile applications Usage motivations, user experience and satisfaction Kausal analysis and structural equation modelling The target groups of Professor Stefan University of Applied Sciences and Media Informatics were taught at the University of Applied Sciences and Humanities.
content.title_en: Acceptance and use of mobile applications

content.text: The investment environment for new power plants -- investment assessment procedures -- model for real option analysis -- Optimal investment strategy. Matthias Hundt develops a real option model based on mixed-major linear programming, which is bi-directionally coupled with a fundamental electricity market model. This approach allows the value of the investment option to be adequately quantified, taking into account technical restrictions of the power plant operation. As investments in new thermal power plants in Germany are also needed in the future to provide sufficient secured power plant performance, the planning and decision-making process must be set up to a degree of uncertainty that has never been observed before. Therefore, the assessment of investments should explicitly consider uncertain factors on the project value and action flexibility of the investor or plant operator. The content of investment environment for new power plants Investment assessment processes Model for real option analysis Optimal investment strategy The target groups Dozierende and students of the economic and engineering sciences in the field of energy and electricity industry in the company's energy supply industry.
content.title_en: Investment planning under uncertain influence : Thermal power plants as real options

content.text: "Service Design" in tourist destinations: Guest-oriented product development with service design. In the future, a stronger focus on process and product tasks will be demanded from tourist destinations of the new generation. Due to its complexity, the development of tourist products requires an instrument that enables the development of customer-oriented products. A young way of thinking that could fulfil this high expectation attitude is the customer-focused and iterative approach of service design. In this work twelve instruments from service design are presented, which are particularly suitable for the development of tourist products. Based on the findings, all Austrian destinations (full survey) were asked whether these products develop for their destination and whether the methods and instruments from service design are used. The content Tourist destinations and destination management Strategic and operational product development of services Service Design as a multi-disciplinary competence platform Product development in Austria's destinations The target groups Dozierende und Studierendern in der Bereichen Tourismus, Service Management, Service Design Praktern im Bereich Tourismus, Tourismusorganisationen resp. Destinationmanagement Organisationen (DMO), Tourism Consulting The author Janosch Untersteiner istre Management of the Business School of Business Management in Innsbruck.
content.title_en: "Service Design" in tourist destinations : Guest-oriented product development with service design

content.text: Intertemporal criminal law, using the example of official permits in the context of illegal immigration employment. The core of the work is the official approval often required in criminal laws in their temporal context. The consequences for criminality are examined when there are changes in laws or administrative decisions between conduct and criminal decision. The study focuses on the temporal context of administrative permits that are often subject of criminal offenses. It examines the consequences for criminal liability in cases where changes are made to laws or administrative decisions between the conduct of the offense and the criminal court decision.
content.title_en: Intertemporal criminal law, using the example of official permits in the context of illegal immigration

content.text: The project is based on the research of the architectural and architectural contexts. Christine Neubert investigates the social relevance of the built environment. With her ethnographic study, she closes a research gap, because the influence of architecture on the infinite flow of everyday social practice is as natural as little empirically investigated. Using the example of different work contexts, the author investigates the effectiveness of architecture, its resistance and its respective specific material qualities. At the subject level, the study thus contributes to the development of the interrelationship between professional work and architecture and at the conceptual level of the architectural and materiality theory expansion of existing architectural sociology and practice theory research on the materiality of the social. The content of the project The state of current sociological architecture research Architecture in everyday life On the structure and practice of architectural experience Differentiation of architectural experience and materiality The target groups of the architecture and the architects The author is working on the project of the University of Dresden.
content.title_en: Built everyday life : architectural experience in working environments

content.text: The fight against racism and xenophobia in labour law. Christoph Fröb examines the undetermined concepts of racism and xenophobia in the law on the constitution of the company. The author examines the concepts of racism and xenophobia in the way of interpretation and questions their normation in historical, systematic, teleological and legitimological terms. The author points out in this connection many repressive and preventive instruments of labour law to combat racism and xenophobia. Particularly the fight against racism and xenophobia in the law on the company constitution, the law on dismissal, the law on the company constitution and the law on collective agreements and the labour law of the public service are in the focus. The content The concepts of racism and xenophobia (in particular the labour law) The concepts of racism and xenophobia in the law on labour law, the law on the labour law, the law on the works councils, the trade unions and the personnel responsible The author Dr. Christoph Fröb is a lawyer at the law office of the district court of Leipzig.
content.title_en: Combating racism and xenophobia in labour law

content.text: The methodology and guidelines for the construction of laser-based lightweight structures. Introduction -- State of the art -- Methodical approach -- Basic manufacturing restrictions of LAM for TiAl6V4 -- Design catalog for LAM lightweight structures made of TiAl6V4 -- Development of a methodology for component design -- Methodological application on a demonstrator -- Summary and outlook. Laser-based manufacturing offers great potential due to its high geometric design freedom, especially for lightweight construction applications in aviation. Against this background, the design guidelines for the process-oriented component design and their transfer to a methodology for the construction of lightweight structures manufactured by laser-based manufacturing. The approach is developed and demonstrated using two components from the aviation industry. The content State of the art Methodical approach Basic manufacturing restrictions of LAM for TiAl6V4 Design catalog for LAM lightweight construction structures from TiAl6V4 The method is developed and demonstrated using a methodology for component design at a demonstration centre.
content.title_en: Methodology and guidelines for the design of laser-produced lightweight structures

content.text: Cloud-Federations: SLA-based VM-Scheduling-Procedures. Andreas Kohne provides a comprehensive insight into the basics of cloud computing, cloud-feduling and SLA-based VM-Scheduling. Furthermore, FederatedCloudSim presents a flexible and expandable simulation framework for investigating various Federation scenarios. The framework then examines various scheduling strategies and their impact on the SLA compliance and finances of the cloud service providers.The content Basics on the topics of cloud computing, SLAs and VM Scheduling Presentation, structure, functions and workflow of the simulation framework FederatedCloudSim Presentation and detailed analysis of different VM-Scheduling-Proceduling-Procedulatives The target groups lecturers and students of IT specialists The author Andreas Kohne has intensively discussed the field of cloud computing in recent years and has specialized in the field of SLA-based cloud environments. He works with a large IT department in Dortmund.
content.title_en: Cloud Federations : SLA-based VM Scheduling Procedures

content.text: The following topics are presented in German: - Imbiometric Analysis and Efficiency Assessment of Concurrent Sourcing and Concurrent Exploitation. Holger de Bie und Maximilian Rimbach are dedicated to the question of how to describe and explain plural governance decisions ("Make-and-Buy") from a management and organizational theoretical perspective. Based on a bibliometric analysis of literature and a notation for value creation activities, the authors develop a systematic approach to the forms and characteristics of plural governance. Subsequently, the theoretical determinants and empirical findings are worked out before derivating a decision model for plural governance decisions with an evaluation of the efficiency of different designs of plural governance. The content · Relevance and systematics of plural governance · Theoretical explanatory approaches and empirical findings · Efficiency evaluation and implications for science and practice The target groups · Lecturers and students of economic sciences with the focus on corporate management and strategic management · The topic of the business executives and executives of the company.
content.title_en: Plural Governance : A management and organizational theoretical analysis and efficiency evaluation of Concurrent Sourcing and Concurrent Exploitation

content.text: - Use of Tablet App: An investigation of counting learners at the beginning of the second school year. Daniel Walter shows the potential of digital media and examines how primary school children use tablet applications and their physical equivalents. He assesses the usage methods identified in clinical interviews in terms of overcoming counting solutions. The author shows that digital media potentials are not always used intuitively and adequately by learners, but can only be exploited by appropriate tasks and impulses. Furthermore, he identifies ways of using both physical and virtual materials to facilitate learning, but also negatively estimating how to use them. The content of mathematics learning with digital media in primary school Counting arithmetic in initial mathematical instruction Detachment of counting arithmetic design of empirical investigation Use methods in the use of tablet applications Comparison of usage methods in the use of tablet applications and their physical equivalents The target groups of mathematics didactics teachers and teachers and their exponents The author Daniel Walter Ph.D. as a knowledgeable employee of Prof. Christoph Selm's Researcher at the University of Dortmund.
content.title_en: How to use tablet apps: An investigation of counting learners at the beginning of the second year

content.text: Experimental investigation of a dual fuel fuel combustion process for heavy commercial vehicle engines. Andre Tänzler shows basic thermodynamic relationships and the operating limits of the dual fuel combustion process. He investigates the potential for reducing greenhouse gas emissions using high natural gas components. The conflict between the reduced CO2 emissions and the increased methane emissions plays a decisive role in the overall consideration of the greenhouse potential. For further emission reduction, the author develops an alternative piston material with reduced fire lift height, whereby he develops different diesel injection patterns for generating a homogeneous diesel combustion on lean background mixture of natural gas and air as decisive parameters.The content Operating limits of the dual fuel combustion process Analysis of possible knock events Potential of a steel piston for reducing emissions Homogeneous combustion of diesel fuel for better mixture detection The target groups Dozierde and students of automotive technology Development engineers in the field of thermodynamics and combustion process development The author Andre Tänzler was a scientific employee at the Institute for Combustion Combustion Combustion of Diesel Fuels- Currently working on the development of the dual fuel combustion process.
content.title_en: Experimental investigation of a dual fuel combustion process for heavy duty commercial vehicle engines

content.text: Identification and analysis of software clusters: An empirical study based on the effects of cluster effects. Markus Eckrich examines whether cluster effects in the software industry help companies to become more innovative and productive. The author uses these two effects to identify and analyse software clusters and selects as indicators the patent density and labour productivity. In addition to the scientific relevance, the book also offers interesting aspects for software companies (site strategy) and the policy (economic promotion). The content · Industrial clusters and their mode of action · & nbsp; Description and delimitation of the software industry in Germany · Methods for the identification of industrial clusters · Measurement of innovative power and productivity in the software industry · Software clusters in Germany measured by innovation power and productivity The target groups Dozierende und Studierende der Wirtschaftsgeographie oder Wirtschaftsinformatik Manager von industriellen Clustern, Führungser in Softwareunternehmen, Entscheider im Politik im Wirtschafts/Clusterförderung. The author Markus Eckrich was a research associate at the department of business computer science at the Technical University Darmstadt. Industrial clusters and their impact -- Description and definition of the software industry in Germany - Software methods for the field of innovation power and productivity - Software.
content.title_en: Identification and analysis of software clusters : An empirical study based on the effects of cluster effects

content.text: Strategic customer analysis in medium-sized family-owned companies: An analysis in the automotive supply industry. Henny Lena Holzhauser analyses the reasons why medium-sized family-owned companies do not use strategic management concepts, which occasions can lead to an application and which special features need to be taken into account in the development of concepts. The focus is on the core of success: the customer. In the context of past successes and the living through corporate crises, the author develops a model of strategic customer analysis, which is integrated into the way of decision-making medium-sized family-owned companies. The model is intended to guide all those companies that have to deal with significant economic dependencies of customers and highly limited management resources. In contrast to similarly structured sectors, the automotive supply industry provides the appropriate practical framework. The content • Strategic customer analysis • Path dependence in medium-sized family-owned companies • Business crises and path break-offs • Developments in the automotive supply industry The target groups • Docierende und Studieren der Wirtschaftswissenschaften with a focus on M ittelstand, family-owned company • Executives in the automotive supply industry and similar sectors, business consultant The author is a strategic business manager in the field of the company Lena.
content.title_en: Strategic customer analysis in medium-sized family companies : An analysis in the automotive supply industry

content.text: The complexity of internal services: Conceptualization, measurement and integration into an impact model. The focus of the work is on approaches to the analysis of internal processes, which are increasingly characterized by a high degree of complexity. In addition to the evaluation of the complexity of internal customer contact, the evaluation of its determinants and consequences in different organizations takes place. The author shows both cost and benefit effects of the complexity of internal services and illustrates, taking into account non-linear effects, the central role of these in companies in terms of high internal service quality. Based on the empirical results, recommendations for professional complexity management are given.The content of research state on the complexity of internal services Development of a measurement and impact model of the complexity of internal services Empirical view of the complexity of internal services taking into account non-linear effects Recommendations on the control of the complexity of internal services The target groups Dozierende and students of the business administration teaching with the focus on marketing and management practitioners from the fields of strategic marketing, personal marketing and corporate management The author Dr. Corina Braun is a wis p>se employee at the University of Applied Sciences.
content.title_en: Complexity of internal services: conceptualisation, measurement and integration into an impact model

content.text: The methodology for factory system modelling in the context of energy and resource efficiency. Hendrik Hopf develops a methodology for factory system modelling in the context of energy and resource efficiency (FSMER), which is a planning-supporting tool for sustainable factory planning. The methodology consists of a metamodel, four factory system concepts, a reference model and a procedure model. The aim is to map the factory holistically, methodically and model-based, with a focus on the target sizes energy and resource efficiency in early conceptual planning phases, explain effective relationships and demonstrate potential for efficiency. Complex relationships of a factory and the impact of planning decisions can thus be presented and evaluated in a simplified and graphically oriented form. The content •Modelling of systems •Energy/resource efficient factory •Fabriksystemkonzepte •Reference model of the factory system •Evaluation of the methodology The target groups •Doctors, students and scientists of the fields of business planning, mechanical engineering, industrial engineering •Practicals in the field of factory planning, energy management, production management, factory management, factory management and management.
content.title_en: Methodology for modeling the factory system in the context of energy and resource efficiency

content.text: Housing and Housing Management in Russia: The situation and perspectives compared with Germany. This book provides an overview of the current housing real estate market in Russia. The main market participants are examined and a comparative analysis is carried out with Germany on construction costs, construction planning, construction quality, housing financing and housing real estate prices. This study serves as a basis for understanding the Russian housing real estate market and thus provides a basic knowledge for a general market understanding and possible investment projects. The content Housing markets Housing financing opportunities Construction and construction quality Construction costs calculation for housing projects Investment strategies to improve the housing situation in Russia The target groups Dozierdeen and students of the business economy, construction industry, architecture and political sciences with focus on Eastern Europe Real estate economists, project tax collectors, architects, engineers, project developers, construction contractors as well as construction lawyers and consultants with focus on risk management, asset management, investor consulting The author Dr.-Ing. Elena Herzog completed a construction engineering degree at the Rostower State Building University (Russia) and a quality engineer master's degree at the Bergische University Wuppertal. She completed her doctorate at Univ. Prof. Dr.-Ing. Wolftriche University of Wolftrich University of Russia.
content.title_en: Housing and housing in Russia : The situation and prospects compared with Germany

content.text: What makes coaching effective: Focus on the factors that affect coaching processes. Marc Lindart provides insights into the mechanisms of the effect of coaching processes, on the basis of which knowledge-based and effectiveness-oriented decisions can be made for high-quality coaching. Based on a systematic overview, the example of the hypnosystemic approach is examined using a qualitative study, which is important when coaching is to be effective. Questions are addressed such as: What makes coaching effective? How are active factors implemented in practice? What is important for successful coaching? The content Terminological clarification of the coaching concept Theoretical background to factors of action in coaching Systematic overview of the state of research The hypnosystemic approach in consulting and coaching Empirical survey, results and design recommendations The target groups researchers, lecturers and students of educational, psychology, sociology and business management Coaches Berufsmittelberberater MitarbeitsdeutschäfterInnen Organisationsbeschäftnis- Beschäftung im Beschäftsspracheitung.

content.text: The following are the topics of the German law on climate change: the conservation of Natura 2000 sites under the conditions of climate change. The law on natural and climate protection, adaptation of climate impacts -- adaptation of permanent decisions by means of general administrative law -- coordination of adaptation needs and possibilities in the administrative procedure. Moritz Gies examines the adaptation to the consequences of climate change required by Natura 2000 law and shows that these can be implemented not only through management measures but also through increased protection to preserve the conservation objectives. The author advocates the use of the funds of the general administrative law for the pre- and post-caution adaptation of permanent decisions in a targeted manner. By linking the principles of adaptation to the legal requirements of European nature protection law and the flexible instruments of administrative procedural law, the necessary adaptability can be established. content.text: Ingo Heinrich examines the maintenance of a non-scheduled maintenance and describes the methodical development of a mathematical model to bring the degree of damage to a fleet of railway vehicles into a valid correlation with existing operational resources. This correlation is transferred to a malicious index and presented in a predictive model in its temporal course. The forecast also takes into account the possibility of iterative adaptation, for example the future damage behaviour depending on a changed vehicle number or a change in employee hours in the maintenance plants. This gives railway transport companies more scope for action to pursue their strategic and economic goals. The content forecast models Resource limits in railway operations Method of determining a harmful index Ingo Heinrich has worked in a predictable manner with the planning of a predictable harmful index The target groups teaching staff and students with the focus on maintenance planning, logistics, transport, fleet management Engineers and managers from the areas of maintenance development and planning The author Dr.-Ing. Ingo Heinrich has worked in a predictable manner with the planning of a railway fleet-resource index.

content.text: A media history of the screen: Analysis of the dispositive visual perception construction. Lucia Sehnbruch deals with the history of the screen from the Middle Ages to the Modern Age. She explains that in the long history of the screen a visual perception or knowledge order has been generated and becomes, which decisively characterizes our perception and visual culture. In doing so, she develops a novel reading of the cultural significance of the important perception medium. The author explores the development and development history of the screen as a technique of vision and visualisation and offers new approaches for an extended understanding of the subject-technology relationship. The content Middle Ages: Early form of the screen Renaissance: Classical form of the screen Modern age: optical camera obscura Modern: Photo camera with lens Expansion of the screen medium in the Modern Age The target groups Teaching and Students of Media History and Media Studies, Technology and Science History, Media Sociology, Cultural History and Cultural Studies Interested in Media Theory The author Lucia Sehnbruch conducts research on media theory and technology history. She teaches media science, media socialization, media literacy, educational science, and educational science of modernism.
content.title_en: A media history of the screen : Analysis of the dispositive visual perception construction

content.text: University buildings in the field of education policy and urban development. Eva Lingg presents various design logics that meet in the new university building. She presents how they can be integrated into planning processes and finally become visible in materialisation. The author identifies decisive factors and moments in such planning processes and presents design guidelines for the future planning of educational buildings, which are intended to find an architectural equivalent of new teaching and learning concepts, contemporary work forms and extended forms of cooperation between research and teaching or the different departments. This often also requires new locations that offer space for university development as well as new radiance to the institutions. The content · Architecture as a translation process · Planning history FHS St. Gallen, the University Campus Vienna and the Toni Area Zurich · The design logics of the involved actors · Social Spatial view of planning processes The target groups · Dozierende und Studieren der Pädagogik und Soziologie · &n bsp; Architects, urban planners and social space researchers The author Eva Lingg is an architect and works as a research assistant at the Competence Centre Social Spaces of the FHS.
content.title_en: Higher education buildings in the field of education policy and urban development

content.text: Technically supported living in urban districts: potential, acceptance and use of an assistance system for older people. Living and living in old age -- State of research: Age(s) and technology -- Experience with assisted living technology in everyday life -- Practical examples of assistance systems. Lynn Schelish considers the acceptance and use of an assistance system for older people in everyday use over a period of several years and examines possibilities of support that arise for independent living in urban environments. The proposed assistance system is mostly received by users, although the various functions are assumed differently. The author shows that however, the described assistance techniques can only prevent progression in old age in individual cases. However, in combination with district-related social structures, effects can be expected that meet the desire of independent living in a self-determined environment in terms of health restrictions. The content of living and living in old age The state of research: Age(s) and technology Experience with assisted living technology in everyday life Practice examples of assistance systems The target groups Dozende and students from the fields of urban economics, urban science, urban science and technology research.
content.title_en: Technically supported living in the city quarter : potentials, acceptance and use of an assistance system for the elderly

content.text: The sectional speed monitoring and its constitutional evaluation. Sectional speed monitoring (section control) -- State protection -- Defence rights of traffic participants -- Constitutional justification -- Legislative competence for a legal basis (de lege ferenda) -- Design dimensions and proposals. content.text: The last-willed arbitration procedure - possibilities of design. In addition to the material influence of the will or inheritance contract, the deceased can also influence the estate in a procedural manner by taking an arbitration order into the final decision. This prevents the parties from making a dispute over succession to the state courts. In contrast to a state court proceedings, the arbitration procedure offers numerous advantages to all parties involved. Philipp Dawirs sheds light on the limits in which the deceased may determine a procedural order tailored to his interests, which supplements §§ 1025 ff. ZPO. If the last-willed disposition of the property results in a procedure, the deceased knows, based on the order of an appropriate arbitration procedure, his interests are safeguarded even after death. -- Meaningful is the adoption of an individual arbitration clause or the reference to an existing arbitration order always if the legal requirements of the deceased do not meet the design requirements or not correspond to his ideas. It turns out that there are certain procedural approaches, in which a deviation from the legal provisions of §25.
content.title_en: The last arbitration procedure - design options

content.text: The resolution of the BGH: a necessary change of system in accordance with the ECHR and German criminal and criminal procedure law?. With the resolution of the enforcement, the Grand Criminal Senate of the BGH revolutionized the reaction to the violations of the Convention and the rule of law in investigative and criminal proceedings in 2008. The practice of taking into account an over-long period of proceedings in the area of criminal measurement was replaced by the granting of an enforcement penalty. -- Stefan Biehl deals with the necessity for this change of jurisdiction and proves that the solution found does not fit into the criminal sanctions system of the StGB nor constitutes a uniform system which can be reconciled with the ECHR's compensation idea. Furthermore, the author shows why the resolution of the enforcement has become obsolete with the new law on legal protection in the case of excessive judicial proceedings and criminal investigation proceedings.
content.title_en: The resolution of the BGH: a necessary change of system in accordance with the ECHR and German criminal and criminal procedure law?

content.text: The right to media re-start: the "inability to forget the Internet" as a challenge to the general right of personality. The Internet forgets nothing – on its own – and once it is published on the Internet, the information that is identified by the data subject remains permanently available. Search engines lead everyone who enters the name of the person concerned to them. Because of this "inability to forget the Internet", they also do not fall prey to the natural forgetting of the people. Rather, the person concerned must fear that they will possibly pursue digital shadows for life as long as they are long and will burden all new social contacts. The further development of his own personality is so significantly impeded: to implement a personality draft that deviates from the published information can be hopeless. This risk also makes it advisable to avoid unconventional behaviour when developing his own personality. - Martin Diesterhöft shows why this Internet-specific threat is adequately only achieved by the recognition of a further expression of the general right of personality, a right to media re-start, can be met with the same media-like fear of a new beginning.
content.title_en: The right to a new beginning in the media: "to forget the inability of the Internet" as a challenge for the general right to personality

content.text: The medically unindicated intervention to increase cognitive performance from a legal point of view. Part One: Basics: Introduction -- The phenomenon of "enhancement" -- Pharmacological cognitive enhancement -- Concepts and legal aspects -- Part Two: Legal framework of pharmacological cognitive enhancement: The simple legal situation of de lege lata -- Constitutional framework of a regulation of cognitive enhancement de lege feranda -- Criteria for medical decision-making in the context of enhancement -- Results. The book provides a comprehensive legal overview of cognitive enhancement. This includes medically unindicated measures to improve cognitive performance in people who are considered healthy. The basic part of the work is the clarification and development of terms as well as medical aspects and legal matters. The second part deals with the simple and constitutional issues associated with cognitive enhancement. One focus is on the question of the importance of medical indication for medical action. Moreover, cognitive intervention is analysed in a limited way, the cognitive dimension is interpreted as being of a more general nature.
content.title_en: The medically not indicated intervention to increase cognitive performance from a legal point of view

content.text: The author uses the rules of the European tax law to determine the scope of national legislators' design when introducing new indirect taxes. In order to determine their regulatory content, the author conducts a critical analysis of the ECJ's case law on the block clauses of the VAT system (Article 401 of Directive 2006/112/EC), the excise system (Article 1 of Directive 2008/118/EC) and the company tax directive (Articles 5 and 6 of Directive 2008/7/EC).While previous representations have often focused on the representation of the case law, the work goes beyond this by dogmatically positioning the rules and comparing them with a separate analysis. The author identifies guidelines on the compatibility of national indirect taxes with the tax directive law, which are collected in addition to existing regulations such as VAT and special excise duties. The work is directed towards the legislator in its design of new tax regulations as well as to the legal seeker, who intends to have national payment obligations checked for their conformity with Union law.Dr. Marion Hombach is a referee in the Federal Ministry of Finance; the work gives the author's personal view.
content.title_en: Block clauses in European tax law

content.text: The analysis of the criteria used in the analysis of the TKG 2012 and the conditions of the FTTx networks, taking into account technical and economic considerations, has been based on the following criteria: The analysis of § 28 TKG compared to the KeL scale. Although the dogmatic approach to material regulation law, which has been advanced by the case law, has now reached an almost inconceivable degree of detail, interdisciplinary research on the regulation of tariffs has remained rare. In the context of the telecommunications law ex ante wholesale pricing regulation, the BNetzA is responsible for finding a balance between the divergent interests of market participants when setting prices. The requested fees are measured on the basis of the cost of efficient performance provision and the prohibition of misuse of § 28 TKG. The combination of these initially incommensurable standards represents a fundamental innovation to the TKG 1996 and has also been maintained in the TKG 2012.
content.title_en: Substantive standards of telecommunications ex ante wholesale pricing control : an analysis of § 28 TKG in comparison to the KeL scale

content.text: Cache me if you can : constitutional aspects of copyright classification of search engines. The study asks, based on the simple-legal evaluation of copyright usage by search engines, whether the importance of search engines for public communication requires a change in copyright.The work provides a constitutional analysis and develops criteria for the consideration of the opposing ownership interests of the authors and the interests of the public in a functioning search on the net. In this context, it takes up the criteria of the Fair Use doctrine. With the constitutional analysis, the work complements the case law and the engaged discussion about copyright usage actions.
content.title_en: Cache me if you can : constitutional aspects of copyright classification of search engines

content.text: The tax account for foreign company losses in Germany : an investigation under the constitutional aspect of consistency. German tax law contains a large number of provisions which exclude the consideration of foreign company losses. While the ECJ has taken a position on the European law compliance of some loss compensation restrictions, so far no clarifications of decisions of the BVerfG are missing, although the requirements of the Basic Law may go beyond that of supranational law. In particular, valuable insights on cross-border loss transfer can be gained through the requirement of consistency. Building on a comprehensive investigation of the constitutional basis of the consistency law, an analysis of the individual loss compensation prohibitions for outbound investment and their compatibility with the system-based principles of income, corporation and business tax follows.
content.title_en: Tax treatment of foreign losses in the domestic sector: a constitutional inquiry

content.text: The work provides a comprehensive overview of the regulations of the innovation-related service and financing law of the statutory health insurance company.
content.title_en: Lack of funding for medical innovation? : legal framework for financing new methods of investigation and treatment and innovative medicines

content.text: The court process in media coverage: the power of media-driven public opinion and the role of process participants in today's media society. The conflict between court proceedings and media coverage consists of a mutually influencing cycle among the actors of the process and media public sphere, which is particularly topical against the background of increased media attention, especially against prominent criminal proceedings. Due to the complexity of the influence cycle, not least due to the diversity of the participants, the conflict field must be considered multi-perspective. The work therefore links aspects of communication and media impact research, psychology and legal science. The starting point is the opinion-forming process and the media effect, in order to illustrate the mechanisms of media society and at the same time to provide a look at the "legal edge of the plate", while the second part examines the changing role of the process participants in terms of compatibility with the normed rights and obligations.
content.title_en: The court process in media coverage: the power of media-driven public opinion and the role of the parties involved in the media society today

content.text: The birth of the first grandchild: To adapt generational relationships. Veronika Salzburger examines changes in generational relationships after the birth of the first (grandchild) child. The mechanisms that can lead to a change in the solidarity dimensions in the transition to parenthood or grandparents are theoretically explained and then empirically examined using data from the family panel (pairfam). First, the value-of-child approach is integrated into the theory of social production function (TSPF). Subsequently, the exchange and bond theory is linked to the model of generational solidarity. By means of difference score models, it is shown that the generational transition leads to an intensification of contact and emotional proximity as well as a reduction of conflict frequency between generations. Furthermore, five relationship types were identified by cluster analyses, whereby birth partly contributes to a changed type-addiction relationship over time. The content · Influence factors on intergenerational relationships · Methodological and analysis strategy: Dimensional analysis of solidarity dimensions, generational relationship type of the family-type of the family-type of the children.
content.title_en: The birth of the first grandchild : To adapt generations' relationships

content.text: The concept of activity analysis in the field of data development analysis: From self-evaluation to cross evaluation. Andreas Dellnitz shows in this work the way to economies of scale of enterprise and activity changes and gives the reader an answer to the question "How efficiency and productivity behave in the case of activity changes". In the classic case of self-evaluation, he demonstrates, using German three-segment theatres, that both efficiency and productivity can be improved hypothetically by means of an interactive algorithm. In the case of cross evaluation, however, improvements can result in a conflict of objectives between efficiency and productivity – the respective companies are then in a so-called productivity gap. Service innovations have a high potential to surprise customers and inspire experiences and thus to take account of the corporate strategic goal of customer enthusiasm. content.text: Internet-specific conflict law? : applicable law in the sale of virtual objects. To find out whether the applicable conflict law in internet-related conduct fails, the legal questions arising from the sale of a virtual object are first worked out and qualified as contractual, cession, company and copyright issues. Subsequently, the relevant conflict law and applicable law are determined.Then it is worked out in which cases a legal question or the underlying life law of the liege ferenda can be the subject of an Internet-specific conflict law, i.e. how the connection subject of an Internet-specific conflict law is to be delimited. Subsequently, the possible connection points are examined, as well as the legal limits of an internal-specific standard. By comparing the current legal situation with such a conflict law, it can be determined whether and to what extent an Internet-specific conflict law is actually superior to the current IPR.
content.title_en: Internet-specific conflict of laws? : applicable law in the sale of virtual objects

content.text: The project manager is working on the identification of synergies between IT requirements in Scrum. Fabian Sobiech is researching an improvement in the planning of agile iterations. He shows how useful values for user stories can be determined in the context of agile software development with heterogeneous customers. He also develops a solution to illustrate synergy potentials between requirements that arise and can be used in the common consideration of several requirements. The author's goals are to avoid duplication of similar functions and subsequent interface adjustments, but to keep the processing of requirements comprehensible for customers. Building on this, he describes valid and optimal iterations in a mathematical model. The project managers can thus be relieved of the use of IT requirements by means of a partially automated process during the iteration planning process. Studies show that an algorithmic approach saves both time and increases the usage values of IT practitioners and practitioners in the field of IT applications in the field of business administration.

content.text: The work deals with the still largely unexplored legal issues of the recovery of ships and wrecks on the high seas, including four legal systems.The first part deals with the recovery of ships outside contractual agreements. To this end, the existing regulations of national and international law are examined and gaps in regulation are identified.The handling of the selected legal systems with the open questions and their procedures in determining applicable law are the focus. Against the background of increasing treasure-search activities in the oceans, the second part deals with the recovery of wrecks and in particular objects of archaeological and commercial value. Here too, the national and international legislation and its regulatory gaps are examined and, finally, a proposal for a solution to the harmonisation of cultural protection and commercial interests is presented.
content.title_en: Ship and wreckage on the high seas : a comparative study of German, French, English and US law

content.text: On the part of education: On the recursive form of educational theory. This raises the question of how an explicitly educational theoretic problematization of education is distinguished from the conventional educational theoretic problematization of education. The reason for this break-up is a surprise that in terms of the interlinking of education and education, the educational theory is also used primarily in individual and subjecttheoretical frameworks of education theory, rather than in terms of social theoretic framing of education theory as educational theory.
