content.text: Identity-oriented brand management in tourism: Development of an internal brand management model for destinations. Based on theoretical and empirical analyses, Isabelle Thilo develops an internal brand management model for destinations. In the course of her research, she analyses the factors of influence of the relevant target variables as well as the question how the demand for identification of internal target groups, e.g. from hotel industry and gastronomy, can be realized with the brand and the implementation in brand-compliant behavior in practice. To this end, she illustrates the relevance of the cooperation with the stakeholders and shows approaches for the implementation of the premises of identity-oriented brand management in destination management. Because increasing competitive pressure as well as the objective to profile itself by means of a strong brand also determine the tourism industry and the modes of action of its actors. The content • Models of internal brand management • Identity-oriented brand management in destinations • Approaches for destination management The target groups • Students and teachers of tourism management and marketing • Professionals and managers in destination marketing organisations and in the tourism industry The author Isabelle Thilo is a long-standing lecturer and consultant in marketing and marketing.
content.title_en: Identity-oriented brand management in tourism : Development of an internal brand management model for destinations

content.text: Network design for truck complete cargo traffic, taking into account economic and social aspects. The author shows using a mathematical model and a heuristic solution procedure that in the construction of complete cargo traffic, it can already be possible to reduce the number of overnight stays for the driver by setting up less additional company locations for a cargo exchange. This can increase the attractiveness of the driver's career image and thus one of the most important challenges for the German transport and logistics industry. Coalition formation processes in multi-level systems -- The transferability of coalition formation theories to the municipal level in Germany -- Black-Green in German cities: Prerequisites, coalition negotiations and coalition agreements. Development of a measurement and impact model of quality of dual communication -- cross-industry empirical examination of the model -- Recommendations for controlling employee brand behaviour and professional design of dual communication. Matthias Holzer develops a quality construct that comprehensively analyzes the effects of external communication on employee behaviour towards the brand for which they work. To this end, he introduces the concept of dual communication, which not only describes the primary effect of external communication on market participants, but also on employees and is therefore of particular importance for service companies with a high degree of customer interaction. The author validates the newly developed construct in three companies of different sectors. content.text: The Urban Bus Network: Technology Assessment for Cost-efficient Operation of Emission-Free Bus Systems. Alexander W. content.text: The developmental tool for the developmental engineer in the wind tunnel -- Studies on the transmission behaviour of the wind tunnel beam -- Studies on the DrivAer phase tail model in different experimental environments. Daniel Stoll uses experimental and corresponding numerical methods to investigate the side wind sensitivity of vehicles and the influence of the wind tunnel environment on the determined instationary forces and moments. He presents an approach to describe the wind tunnel beam with methods of linear time-invariant system theory. This enables him to demonstrate that the flow field in a wind tunnel with an open measuring track has a dynamic behaviour which is superimposed on the behaviour of the vehicle under side wind stimulation. With the presented validated simulation model and the numerical simulation environment without interference effects, it is possible for the first time to determine the aerodynamic transmission behaviour of a vehicle in a wind tunnel. The work thus makes a decisive contribution to the future development of the instationary aerodynamic vehicle properties.
content.title_en: A contribution to the study of aerodynamic properties of vehicles under a mean lateral wind

Internet communication and its importance -- The fundamental character of fundamental rights -- The social media of the Web 2.0 -- A digital understanding of freedom of communication -- Limits of digital freedom of communication. The Internet and thus the new media help the freedom of communication to a completely new dimension of its realization. Michael Bock shows that they can be applied to the digital media according to their underlying principles, but their strengthening by the new media goes along with significant unresolved social and legal challenges. He then goes on to investigate how to deal with these digital challenges. He examines the extent to which a digital understanding of freedom of communication needs to be applied, and what further measures to protect the understate of state protection obligations are to be demanded. Lenard Wengenroth investigates the criminality of a new virtual protest form. So-called virtual sit-ins aim to overload a server system by mass data requests, so that websites stored there are temporarily not accessible. -- More recently, politically motivated page blockades have caused attention. This raises the question of to what extent virtual sit-ins are protected by freedom of opinion and assembly and what consequences result from this, especially for the interpretation of § 303b StGB. -- Since today's server performance usually requires several thousand participants to generate a disruptive data volume, complex causality and imputation questions arise. -- The author develops an independent approach based on the characteristic of equivalence in order to justify a co-criminality of the protesters in the sense of a functional rule. -- The constitutional investigation has revealed that, however, virtual lawless acts as a rule of law are not a valid rule of law.
content.title_en: On the criminality of virtual sit-ins : at the same time a contribution to the (co)perpetratorship with minimal contributions

content.text: The special law of family societies : finding of a real type of company law and selected legal consequences. In family companies there is the need to preserve the assets embodied in the company for the family. The current severance right of departing partners does not take this into account. The author presents an alternative and appropriate severance method.
content.title_en: The special law of family companies : Findings of a real type of company and selected legal consequences

content.text: Market sounding according to the new market abuse law: legal certainty through regulation or regulation through legal uncertainty?. Confidential investor approach to preparing capital market transactions before their public disclosure is very important for issuers and banks. Market sounding can be used to estimate and take into account the demand of the capital market early on. Disclosure of confidential details of a planned transaction also involves the risk of insider violations.The Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) contains for the first time a European regulation of market soundings. Art. 11 MAR allows the disclosure of inside information for the purpose of market soundings, if certain obligations are fulfilled.This first monographal treatise on Art. 11 MAR examines whether the scheme is appropriate to achieve the intended promotion of market sounding and the avoidance of market abuse.The work is subject to legal dogmatic analysis and covers legal practical shortcomings of the regime based on qualitative expert interviews.
content.title_en: Market sounding under the new market abuse law: legal certainty through regulation or regulation through legal uncertainty?

content.text: Violence in computer games: Facets of pleasure. Grand Theft Auto, Battlefield, Counter-Strike – Violence in computer games is always controversially discussed.But what emotional experiences can be gained from the playful use of virtual violence?Through participating observations in online games and at LAN parties as well as through interview, magazine and video analyses, Christoph Bareuther works out how millions of people can experience something as enjoyable, which shocks others. Without using valuable clichés, the ethnographic study thus makes a decisive contribution to a debate on the intersection of popular culture, politics and the public.
content.title_en: Violence in computer games : Facets of pleasure

content.text: BSE, avian flu & Co. : »Food scandals« and consumer behaviour. An empirical study. BSE, avian flu or chamois meat - these keywords are an integral part of mass media coverage. But what significance do such events have for people in everyday life? How do they deal with permanent scandalization? What scandals are causing irritations in them at all?These questions form the basis for an empirical-sociological investigation of the everyday handling of food scandals. Contrary to other studies, this study does not assume a general concern and perception of danger, but rather works out different subjective experiences, interpretations, reactions and justifications based on qualitative interviews and reconstructs them in a typology of individual coping patterns.
content.title_en: BSE, avian influenza & Co. : »Food scandals« and consumer behaviour. An empirical study

content.text: Making Sex Revisited : Deconstruction of gender from a biological-medical perspective. Gender is made socially. The fact that this also applies to biological sex - a postulate of queer-feminist theories - can be proven for the first time by using biological theories.The natural philosophical and biological-medical gender theories of different periods of time (Antique, Beginning Modernism, Present) are presented and associated with social gender systems. Heinz-Jürgen Voß performs the competing positions in a differentiated manner and shows that many genders are conceivable in biological theories with process-oriented approaches - instead of just two or three.
content.title_en: Making Sex Revisited : Deconstruction of sex from a biological-medical perspective

content.text: Digital Realism: Between computer animation and live action. The new image aesthetics in feature films. Digital doppelganger and animated Hollywood stars, journeys through nerve pathways and skin pores, impossible camera perspectives and image spaces that continue indefinitely - in current feature films filmed parts of images and computer animations are often indistinguishably merged. A new category of »hybrid motion pictures« has emerged, which has produced a picture aesthetic beyond the effect cinema. Their staging strategies undermine our vision of realistic representations - they influence our perceptions sustainably and shape our view of the world. The book combines the presentation of the technical requirements of these new image worlds with an in-depth examination of their aesthetic implications. It thus closes a gap in the scientific examination of the digitization of image production.
content.title_en: Digital Realism : Between Computer Animation and Live Action. The New Image Aesthetics in Feature Films

content.text: Media (sub)culture : Stories - Discourses - Designs. The scientific analysis of the media society is often normative. Accordingly predictable and unsatisfactory are its findings and interpretations. Christoph Jacket's study seeks ways out of this impasse by presenting innovative readings of the three prominent strands of critical theory (Frankfurt School and Successor), cultural studies and sociocultural constructivism. From them, a separate media culture observation grid with the levels Main and Sub is prepared. The yields of this new method are shown in the final focus of the central actors in media and pop culture, the stars.
content.title_en: Media culture : Stories - Discourses - Designs

content.text: Provocative communication: Strategies for the political handling of transnational terrorism. The military fight against terrorism over the last one and a half decades is now considered counterproductive - has the »War on Terror« actually strengthened the jihadist movements and is it the reason for their growing number of followers? Sebastian Lange's communication and organizational theory analyses investigate the escalation mechanisms in the relationship between transnational terrorism and the state counter-terrorism. The study shows that the identity conflict between modern societies and fundamentalist world view can only be defoliated if security-political overreactions are avoided.
content.title_en: Provocative communication: Strategies for the political handling of transnational terrorism

content.text: Liquid Democracy in Germany : on the future of digital political decision-making after the fall of the Pirate Party. The rocket-like rise of the Pirate Party followed its equally rapid decline. Is the experiment of political will-building - »Liquid Democracy« - also failed? On the original path of Grounded Theory Anja Adler approaches the recent German political history in order to deal with the ambitious proposal for the development of a new operating system for politics. Through numerous interviews with the actors of internet-supported advisory and decision-making procedures, she draws a vivid and well-suited portrait of both the concrete procedures and the attitudes and visions of democracy developers.
content.title_en: Liquid Democracy in Germany : on the future of digital political decision-making after the fall of the Pirate Party

content.text: Radio as a listening-game space : Media reflection - Disturption - Artistic intervention. Artistic-playing and media-reflexive-operating interventions in the radiophone are as old as the media dispositive radio itself. The radio history audio pieces discussed in this book are characterized by an intensive examination of the possibility space between (especially technical) dispositive and radiophonic forms of representation and staging. Together they have an aesthetic of the disturbance that operates on different levels.At the centre of Bettina Wodianka's study is an interdisciplinary analysis that focuses on the close connection between design processes and production technology.The audio plays of broadcasting history discussed in this book explore opportunities between (particularly technical) dispositive and radio-phonic forms of performance and staging.
content.title_en: Radio as a listening-game-space : Media reflection - Disturbation - Artistic intervention

content.text: The West German Länder and the emergence of the Federal Republic: to the discussion of the Frankfurt documents of July 1948. With the "Frankfurt documents" the West-Allied military governors commissioned the prime ministers of their occupation zones in July 1948 to prepare a constitution for the West State. The author places the contribution of the Länder to the emergence of the Federal Republic at the centre of their investigation and asks about the motives and interests behind the decisions. In addition to the aspect of the constitution, she deals with the problem of the occupation statute and the border reform. Her study shows what important achievements the Federal Ministers achieved in 1948: Despite special national interests, tactical considerations and personal vanities as well as domestic and foreign policy constraints, the heads of countries made decisions that have proved their sustainability to this day.
content.title_en: The West German Länder and the emergence of the Federal Republic : to the conflict over the Frankfurt documents of July 1948

content.text: Genealogy of Ethics Policy : National Ethics Committees as new government technology : the example of France. National Ethics Committees are considered an adequate solution to ethical problems of life science - and increasingly nanotechnological - developments. But when, how and in what context did these ethics policies prevail? And what against? Sabine Könninger investigates these questions by using the example of France and shows how a government technology established itself, in which criticism of research goals and purposes is undesirable. The study offers a critical research contribution to ethical institutions and discourses in the field of science and technology studies. Extensive, it opens up the debates on science and technology in France to a German-speaking audience. How do national ethics commites establishment themselves as a solution to medical and technological conflicts? A provocative study on the genealogy of ethics policies.
content.title_en: Genealogy of Ethics Policy : National Ethics Committees as New Government Technology : the Example of France

content.text: A contribution to the study of vehicle pollution in experiment and simulation. Iwo Spruß provides an overview of the interaction of a vehicle with a wet roadway and the resulting vehicle pollution. He shows that an understanding of these processes is necessary in order to contribute to road safety by avoiding vehicle pollution in addition to the classic, aerodynamic optimization parameters in the vehicle development process. The findings from the presented investigations on a basic body as well as on a full-vehicle geometry serve the author as the basis for the further development and validation of a tool for numerical flow simulation. Thus, the possibility arises to make early statements about vehicle pollution in an earlier phase of the vehicle development process. The content of state of the art, self- and external pollution Numerical simulation methodology Drop size distribution at the extent of a free-standing wheel Rinsal motion on a generic test stand and a vehicle The target groups Dozierende and students of the field of vehicle technology Praktiker from the industry in the areas of aerodynamics and dirt-free keeping The author Iwo Spruß is currently employed as a development engineer at a well-known auto-diction manufacturer of a variety of aerodynamics in the field of testing.
content.title_en: A contribution to the study of vehicle pollution in experiment and simulation

content.text: The aesthetics of immersion: space-experience between world and image. Las Vegas, Washington and White City. The aesthetics of immersion are an aesthetic of immersion, of calculated disintegration of distance. The spaces in which this study is going on make border blurrings between image and world the object of immediate physical experience. They are such a significant part of contemporary life world because they experience collective reality fantasies in a 'real, effective place' (Foucault). Such a place is the 'new' Las Vegas. In its recent metamorphosis from neon to theme architecture, it has not lost its avant-garde status, but has once again become the pioneer of cultural developments in the material retranslation of digital image-painting.
content.title_en: Aesthetics of Immersion : Space-Experience between the world and the image. Las Vegas, Washington and the White City

content.text: Technology transfer contracts and the prohibition of restrictive agreements: the exploitation of intellectual property rights in the tension between legal certainty and economicization in the era of the 'more economic approach' in European antitrust law. The exploitation of intellectual property rights has always been exposed to the tension between intellectual property rights and antitrust law. Antitrust law aims to remove barriers to entry and to keep markets open. Immaterial property law grants exclusion rights. The legal areas therefore seem to contradict each other at first glance. However, not every technology transfer agreement constitutes a restrictive agreement per se. In the age of the 'more economic approach', however, in the context of the assessment whether a technology transfer agreement has a restrictive effect on competition, economic aspects must be taken into account more closely. This assessment is complex and primarily responsible for the addressees of the cartel ban to make the company their own. However, the resulting legal uncertainty on the addressee side must not prevent innovation competition!
content.title_en: Technology transfer contracts and the prohibition of restrictive agreements: the exploitation of intellectual property rights in the tension between legal certainty and economicisation in the era of the more economic approach in European antitrust law

content.text: Tariff regulation without membership : 'Pre-binding' to collective agreement after 'blitz exit' and 'blitz change'?. The tariff Senate of the Federal Labour Court sanctioned 'blitz exit' and 'blitz change' with a surprising legal consequence: tariff regulation without membership after 'secret' collective flight of the employer. Christina Heinz arranges the case law: Does the static tariff regulation without membership of the employer legitimate itself in the employer's association? Is it compatible with the established principles of collective bargaining law and constitutional law? How can the transparency of the exit or exchange required by the Federal Labour Court for the union be justified dogmatically? And finally: Does the Federal Labour Court still move within the limits of judicial law development?
content.title_en: Collective bargaining without membership : 'pre-binding' to collective agreement after 'blitz-out' and 'blitz-out'?

content.text: Forms of cooperation in public antitrust enforcement in European, German and English law: with special consideration of the European settlement procedure in accordance with Regulation No 622/2008. In the context of various forms of cooperation in public antitrust enforcement proceedings at European, German and English level, the author examines and compares commitment procedures, bonus schemes and younger settlement procedures. The investigation examines whether the procedures are conducive to or prevent more effective enforcement, e.g. because the relevant procedures are implemented and used inflexibly by the respective authority. The examination also takes into account the view of affected companies and the private antitrust enforcement often in a tension relationship with these procedures. The result is that the European Commission, the BKartA and the OFT have similar procedures but could sometimes use them more effectively. The legal comparison also shows which aspects of the systems should be reformed in a meaningful way in order to achieve more harmonisation and strengthen the individual procedures.
content.title_en: Forms of cooperation in public enforcement of antitrust law in European, German and English law: taking into account the European settlement procedure under Regulation No 622/2008

content.text: The European Union must take account of the concerns of agriculture and the environment in the context of the European Union's environmental policy: at the same time, it contributes to the reform of the CAP, cross compliance and climate protection.The European Union must take account of the concerns of agriculture and the environment in the context of the European Treaties.The guiding principle of environmentally sound agriculture offers the possibility of combining the partially conflicting target provisions with the aim of optimum effectiveness.The author traces the historical development of European agri-environmental law and examines how far the current agri-environmental law is in line with this guiding principle.The focus of his study is on linking agricultural support legislation with environmental protection requirements (so-called cross compliance) and climate protection as a new legislative task. Based on the results, the author develops his own proposals for a future design of the common agricultural policy.
content.title_en: Framework conditions for environmentally sound agriculture in European law: at the same time contributing to the reform of the CAP, cross compliance and climate protection

content.text: The Council of Europe's contribution to the fight against terrorism and its influence on the European Union. The Council of Europe makes an important contribution to the fight against terrorism, which has so far been a shadowy phenomenon in science. Therefore, the author examines not only the overall strategy but also the individual measures of the Council of Europe with particular regard to its human rights dimension. The increased anti-terrorism struggle of the EU since 2001 has enabled the degree of mutual influence of the two organisations in this field to be examined in a comparative manner. Whether the strategy is comparable to the extent to which human rights are protected in the fight against terrorism and what lies behind the conventions, framework decisions and terrorist lists is comprehensively analysed.
content.title_en: The Council of Europe's contribution to the fight against terrorism and its influence on the European Union

content.text: Social networks in labour law. Social networks are no longer to be thought out of everyday life. This does not mean that effects on the working world are not present and employers face new legal problems. This work deals with the labour and data protection issues that arise when using social networks.The author examines, among other things, the question of the legal admissibility of a candidate search in social networks relevant for practice. He further analyses whether and to what extent activities in social networks can constitute a reason for dismissal. He also deals in detail with the case law so far on this topic. Furthermore, the author addresses the question of who is entitled to the user account of a social network when the employment relationship is terminated. Finally, it is shown that employers can reduce the existing legal risks in connection with social networks by introducing a social network policy.
content.title_en: Social networks in labour law

content.text: Berlin mixed up: occidental, multicultural, cosmopolitan? : The political construction of an immigration city. For decades, political, media and social science debates on »integration« or »multiculture« have been based on Berlin's districts such as Kreuzberg and Neukölln. Mostly they are based on unquestioned historical concepts of nation, culture or integration, as well as on discursive constructs of a »own« and a »foreigner«.This book examines such discourse patterns, among other things, by means of interviews with high-ranking Berlin politicians and functionaries. It shows how Berlin's urban development and multi-societal border drawn towards immigrants interact with each other and traces their historical lines.
content.title_en: Berlin mixed up: occidental, multicultural, cosmopolitan? : The political construction of an immigration city

content.text: Sustainability reporting in Western, Central and Eastern Europe: a country comparison. This work deals for the first time with sustainability reporting of companies from 13 Western, Central and Eastern European countries. The work can be divided into two parts: To describe the status quo and to detect differences in sustainability reporting, a content analysis was carried out in the first part of each part with the 50 largest companies from Central and Eastern Europe and Western Europe.In the second part, internal factors were identified with the help of expert interviews, which have an influence on the sustainability reporting of companies.In a survey, it was checked whether the internal factors between companies that report and companies that do not report differ. Furthermore, it was analysed whether these differ from the regional ones.
content.title_en: Sustainability reporting in Western, Central and Eastern Europe : a country comparison

content.text: Customer integration and customer relationships: Conception, impact mechanisms and management implications. Julia Meik examines customer integration as a central component of customer relationship management in the service sector. The study addresses two aspects of customer integration: productivity and customer loyalty to the company. The author analyses the success-relevant consequences of the customer's active involvement as well as the relationship between customer integration and relationship duration. The study enables the derivation of implications for customer relationship management and personnel management in the service sector. The content Conception of a framework of research on the impact of customer integration on customer loyalty strength from a customer perspective and on the binding object of customer relationship from a company perspective Methodological foundations and empirical results on the determinants and consequences of customer integration Implications for scientific research and the practice of customer relationship management The target groups Dozierende and students of business administration with the focus on marketing and service management specialist and executives from the areas of marketing and CRM The author Dr. Julia Meik received his doctorate at Prof. Dr. Christian Brock at the Otto Group Chair of Service Marketing and Distance Trading in the University of Business.
content.title_en: Customer integration and customer relationships : Conception, impact mechanisms and management implications

content.text: Is it true that the teaching staff are not only the teachers who are involved in the teaching process, but also the teachers who are involved in the teaching process? : how teachers justify the distribution of their support efforts. 'Just treat you: everyone is equal, everyone is different!' Thus, a teacher could sum up their task. The main objective of this study is to better understand how Swiss primary teachers interpret and legitimize their partly contradictory functions towards children with different learning requirements from a point of view of justice. Theoretical modelling and empirical examination of the corresponding interpretation patterns are the main focus here. In theory, funding is understood as a distribution problem or a finite resource in school classes. Building on a questionnaire survey in two cantons, a sample of teachers was also asked in terms of extreme group comparison using problem-centered interviews. Among other things, the results indicate that funding efforts are distributed unequally between three performance groups, with the weakest third of the pupils over all the time periods in the school year and almost all activities being considered the most important of the tasks in terms of the primary school.
content.title_en: Is differentiated teaching just? : how teachers justify the distribution of their support efforts

content.text: Fractal security: A critique of municipal crime prevention. Across all social areas, the concept of prevention has a high degree of acceptance.The need for security is particularly evident in municipal crime prevention and is concretely expressed there in the form of a conglomerate of discursive truth production and local everyday practices.Following Michel Foucault and Algirdas Julien Greimas, Verena Schreiber encourages us to think speculatively about our relationship to prevention and explores the contexts that make crime prevention a promise of freedom that is no longer in question from any perspective.
content.title_en: Fractal collaterals : A critique of municipal crime prevention

content.text: Criminal responsibility without freedom of will. Is there "criminal responsibility in a determined world?" Many brain researchers deny this and plead for a pure criminal law. But since antiquity there have been philosophers who "compatibilists who plead for a reconciliation of determinism and responsibility and try to prove that we are responsible for our decisions and our actions in a fully determined world. On the other hand, the "incompatibilists" deny that moral responsibility and determinism are compatible with each other. This criminal law philosophical work evaluates the extensive philosophical literature for the dispute and makes it connectible for a legal discussion. The investigation thus also puts brain research into its limits: There is no brain compatible law. But there is a right that justified ethical principles and principles are taken into account and compatible with the thesis of determinism.
content.title_en: Criminal responsibility without freedom of choice

content.text: New Harmony: the experiment and its memory. The present cityscape of New Harmony and Indiana is remarkable for a remote, not even 900 inhabitants. Especially the visitor centre designed by Richard Meier, the Roofless Church and the Harmonist Labyrinth, is omnipresent. The memory of the first settlers, the Harmony Society and Robert Owens Society Experiment (1814-1827), is guided by the question of the legacy of the two so-called "intentional communities" which examines this local study on a versatile source base New Harmony's demographic, economic, political and cultural development. New Harmony's success story as a small town can not be explained solely by the known urban growth factors. New Harmony received unique opportunities for development in the United States due to the presence of two ideas historically rooted in Europe, then formed communities that have become more than 200 years old. At first glory, New Harmony approaches to the city's existence.
content.title_en: New Harmony : the experiment and its legacy

content.text: The participation of the university's students in mobile web surveys: An empirical study. Characterization and significance of mobile web surveys -- The state of research on the factors influencing participation in mobile web surveys -- Theoretical reference points for explaining participation in mobile web surveys -- Empirical investigation of participation in mobile web surveys. Marie Schulte identifies key factors influencing participation in mobile web surveys as part of a mixed methodology study. The expected pleasure in a survey and social influences are particularly important drivers. Inhibiting the willingness to participate primarily affects the expected effort of participation. Furthermore, it is clear that the strength of individual impact relationships, among other things, depends on the age and gender of the smartphone users and on the time pressure felt in the survey situation. The findings gained can be used to derive target group-specific implications for a participation-promoting response to potential volunteers. The content of characterization and importance of mobile web surveys The state of marketing surveys on the participation of mobile research in the business survey.
content.title_en: The willingness to participate in mobile web surveys : An empirical study

content.text: Migration to Germany and return to Kosovo: deportation and voluntary departure – four qualitative analyses. The authors investigate how people whose asylum application was rejected in Germany experience deportation and "voluntary departure" in Kosovo. In four qualitative studies they focus on the question of the subjective significance of this experience, address the special situation of children and explain how life continues after return. They show that migration and its state regulation by deportation and "voluntary departure" are not only politically explosive topics, but also critical life events for those affected. The content Narrations of deportation and voluntary departure Agency and subjective theories on return Challenges and resources after return The importance of children during migration The target groups Dozierdeen and students of psychology, migration research, political sciences, sociology and social work Practitioners of social work and migration counselling The authors Verena Biskup, Maria Jaschick, Kathrin Sautter and Lucia Thumm have currently completed the study of the rehabilitation of children and their diagnosis in the context of the rehabilitation of the refugee.
content.title_en: Migration to Germany and return to Kosovo: deportation and voluntary departure – four qualitative analyses

content.text: Control of the diesel engine: oxygen-based concepts for motors with variable charge change control. Oxygen sensor and physical model formation of the gas system -- Control design -- Results of decentralized design variants. Daniel Schwarz considers the oxygen mass share as a qualitative description of the intake air of a diesel engine. He shows the advantages compared to the AGR rate as a description size in transient phases of the engine. The author presents physical model approaches for the gas system of the diesel engine, which use the information of the measured oxygen mass share. This includes a mean model, which determines the gas state in the cylinder when using internal exhaust gas return by means of a variable charge change control. In addition, he explains a control-oriented model of the low-pressure exhaust gas return route and examines the regulation of the oxygen mass share in the intake range. The author applies nonlinear control algorithms and compares these with each other. He discusses the use of observers for the estimation of disturbance variables and implements and validates the developed methods both in simulation and at an engine test bench.
content.title_en: Control of the diesel engine : Oxygen-based concepts for motors with variable charge change control

content.text: The research on the internal coordination of procurement -- Qualitative analysis on the shape, influencing factors and effect of internal coordination -- Theory-guided interpretation of qualitative findings -- Quantitative analysis by means of surveying strategic buyers -- Contributions to knowledge and recommendations for action. Procurement is an important and complex task in companies, whereby a division of work into the functions of procurement and logistics is a widespread phenomenon. This is useful at the operational level, but at the strategic level it involves the risk of suboptimal decisions. Tobias Breitling focuses on this problem in a comprehensive study. By means of qualitative analysis he examines the shape and influence factors of coordination between the areas as well as the effect on procurement success. Furthermore, he uses quantitative analysis to examine the theoretically guided interpretation of qualitative findings on the basis of a survey of 130 strategic buyers and gives recommendations for corporate practice. The content of research on internal coordination of procurement is a research report on the form, influence factors and effect of internal coordination.
content.title_en: Coordination of Purchasing and Logistics : Interfunctional coordination of strategic procurement decisions

content.text: The logic and problem of anti-corruption: Germany and Italy in comparison. Corruption is mostly associated with undemocratic states. However, the phenomenon can also occur in consolidated Western democracies, where corrupt behaviours are opposed to the democratic fundamental consensus due to the prevailing self-understanding of a modern political culture. Against this background, the author characterizes corruption and anti-corruption and presents a demarcation between different levels, sectors and ranges. She examines the extent to which anti-corruption is functionally chosen and shows how it can be coordinated with the characteristics and premises of Western democracies in order to minimize corruption in the long term.The content of corruption and anti-corruption in Western democracies and their relationship: Development of two interdependent typologies of phenomena Case studies: Germany (CDU donation, Cologne garbage scandal, Siemens-Enel affair), Italy (Tangentopoli scandal, Global Service scandal, Enel-Siemens affair) The target groups Dozierdeologie und der Beträgerung der Politik, University of Management, University of Management, University of Management, University of Management, and of Management.
content.title_en: Logic and problem of anticorruption : Germany and Italy compared

content.text: The University of Berlin's Student and Student Integration System: The Academic and Social Integration Teaching Students in the University. Kathrin Petzold-Rudolph deals with the multi-layered relationships between the University as a socialisation authority and the development of students in the context of the increased relevance of academic education as well as the reform processes in the university sector and in teacher education over the last two decades. The author examines, among other things, the individual integration performance of students under the conditions of a teaching office study from a student perspective as well as the contribution of academic and social integration to the success of the study.The empirical findings point to significant differences in the perception and use of increasingly standardized study programmes.The content of universities in the German higher education system Students at universities – the perspective of university research Research on student integration The teaching office study at German universities University and student integration performance – results of the study The target groups of students in the German educational system Students at universities, university research and pedagogy The author Petzold-Rudolph is the research assistant of the University of Berlin University of Berlin University of Applied Sciences.
content.title_en: Success and university integration : Academic and social integration Teaching students in the university

content.text: The doctor's liability under criminal and civil law in the use of robot assisted surgery. The use of robot assisted surgery is accompanied by new risk and damage scenarios. The treating physician is confronted with liability-related uncertainties, which this work is intended to contribute to.Based on the well-known treatment error groups, the author analyses the effects of the use of robot assisted surgery on the criminal and civil liability regime based on fictitious scenarios. It is clear that the scope of the disclosure obligations as well as the scale of care-related treatment are significantly increased.The fact that the operating room is increasingly digitised poses a further challenge to the doctor who is obliged to maintain confidentiality. The cross-manufacturer networking of the individual technical components leads to a constant exchange of particularly sensitive patient data, which is to ensure access to these data by means of appropriate security systems.
content.title_en: The doctor's liability under criminal and civil law in the use of robot assisted surgery

content.text: Multidimensional concepts for controlling support in small and medium-sized enterprises. 1 Introduction -- 2 Characteristics of small and medium-sized enterprises -- 3 Characteristics of controlling in medium-sized enterprises -- 4 Tasks of controlling in medium-sized enterprises -- 5 Multidimensional concepts -- 6 Improvement of information provision for controlling support in SMEs with multi-dimensional concepts -- 7 Aptitude of multi-dimensional concepts for controlling support in SMEs -- 8 Conception of an exemplary data warehouse for SMEs -- 9 Realization of the exemplary solution -- 10 Conclusion. In small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) the controlling has considerable deficits. Modern data warehouse and OLAP concepts that allow the development of information systems tailored to the respective needs of a company for data analysis, offer great potential for controlling support due to their methods and tools. Tatjana Tegel examines the question of how these concepts can be used in the solution of controlling tasks in SMEs still examines the specificities, situation and objectives of controlling in SMEs, provides an overview of characteristics, architecture and components of multi-dimensional concepts and explains the approach to improving the availability of the information supply in the case of the existing business.
content.title_en: Multidimensional concepts for controlling support in small and medium-sized enterprises

content.text: A reference data model for campus management systems in German-speaking universities. Against the background of linguistic and structural diversity in German-speaking universities and the requirement for universities in the EU to implement the Bologna decisions, Marco Carolla is concerned with the question whether the structure of the database of campus management systems is standardizable. He constructs a reference data model for the – both technically and organizationally heavy – sub-area "Teaching and evaluates it on the basis of a sample of 10 of the 60 large German-speaking universities. The content Discourse area Study modelling Basic concepts, approach and approach The Ontology UFO Modelling method Reference data model Modelling The target groups Lecturers and students of business information technology, economics, computer science Practitioners in the fields of campus management (systems), administrative software, conceptual modelling, ontology development, database design, information system design The author Marco Carolla received his doctorate at the Faculty of Business Science at Bielefeld University. He is currently working in the IT department of a food company in Bielefeld. The Adrik Group of Editors.
content.title_en: A reference data model for campus management systems in German-speaking universities

content.text: The resurgence of partially issued insolvency claims according to § 255 para. 2 InsO. The work deals with the scope of the resurgence clause of § 255 para. 2 InsO. It examines to what extent creditors whose insolvency claims have been partially issued in an insolvency plan can participate in a insolvency proceedings newly opened before the plan is fulfilled. To this end, it is considered how payments are to be treated, which the debtor has already provided to these creditors before the opening of the subsequent insolvency proceedings in fulfilment of the insolvency plan. The work shows which different distribution models between old and new creditors have already been applied in the subsequent insolvency proceedings for the resurgence of claims and analyses the mode of action of today's § 255 para. 2 InsO. Furthermore, the treatment of whether and with what consequences the payments made by the debtor before the opening of the subsequent insolvency proceedings can be challenged by the insolvency administrator and whether the resurgence effect also covers interest.
content.title_en: The revival of partially issued insolvency claims according to § 255 para. 2 InsO

content.text: Post-socialist reform of the government system: Armenia, Croatia, Russia and Ukraine compared. Powerful presidents are generally seen as an obstacle to the consolidation of democracy. However, the conditions for reducing presidential competences have not yet been systematically and empirically investigated by policy-scientific research. In the context of this work institutional policy reforms in four post-socialist countries (Armenia, Croatia, Russia, Ukraine) are analysed and compared to common features and differences. While historical-empirical case studies show that institutional policy reforms primarily serve the realization of presidential utility calculus, the study also shows that both formal reform hurdles and vetoers such as constitutional courts and external actors play a significant role in the reform processes.
content.title_en: Post-socialist government system reform : Armenia, Croatia, Russia and Ukraine compared

content.text: The concept of social techniques -- Outlook: Conveniencedispositive in digital culture The present book presents the results of an ethnographic study on forms of cooperation in medium-sized enterprises and develops the theoretical concept of social techniques from this. The study shows that current collaborations are shaped by designed conductive action. The concept of social techniques describes this form as a technical direction of the social and distinguishes between simple and reflexive social techniques. It is a proposal for the understanding of the current, technological realities of life, whose analytical potential is finally demonstrated by current phenomena of digital culture. The reflections are based on the thesis that convenience is currently becoming the design imperative of the organization of social relations. The content analysis and results: Design and organization of cooperation in companies The concept of social outlook: Conveniencedispositive in the digital culture of the target groups.
content.title_en: Social techniques : design and organisation of cooperation in enterprises

content.text: The frequency conversion of the frequency frequency is thus illustrated by the chip-integrated fluster resonators from lithium niobate. Abstract: Laser light sources are no longer to be thought away in a variety of optical technologies. The reason for this is the good focusability and defined wavelength, which is defined by energy transitions in the laser medium. However, this is also a limitation, since laser light is not available in any wavelength range or the emission wavelength of lasers can usually only be adjusted over a small range. This limitation can be achieved with nonlinear optical frequency converters e.g. from lithium niobate (LiNbO3, LN). The high intensity for the nonlinear optical frequency conversion can be achieved in resonators. A more compact design is the fluster gallery resonators (FGR) to integrate the frequency frequency frequency frequency control with the frequency control unit is of great interest here.

content.text: Political excuses: Theory and empiricism of linguistic action. Concept of apology – multi-perspective considerations -- Apologies as speech and from a political science point of view -- Definition and typology of excuses -- Analysis and function of political excuses. Karina Smübbe investigates a previously hardly researched area of political communication: political excuse. She asks what it means when a politician apologizes and works out the functions of excuses. To this end, the author develops a theory of political excuses and a typology, in order to be able to analyse statements by federal politicians. The empirical analysis is based on a broad data set of Bundestag, party congresses and public discourses. Among other things, it shows that political excuses always have a power-political function and are strategically used to achieve content-related goals. The content concept of excuse – multi-perspective considerations Apologies as speech and from a political science point of view definition and typology of excuses alysis and function of political excuses The target groups dominating and students of political communication, political science, linguistics and communication politicians in the field of politics and of politics.
content.title_en: Political excuses : Theory and Empiricalism of Language Action

content.text: The production work and purchase practice of Personica objects: The auratic effect of pre-owned second-hand trade. Maria Elena Wiegelmann shows that the pre-owned property is a psychological object characteristic with economic and cultural relevance and practical usability through its auratic effect. This is made possible by a modeling using the example of second-hand trade of objects that are highly important for the owner on a personal level, such as automobiles, real estate, musical instruments, horses, jewellery, weapons. Pre-owned owners of such personica objects, associated life events and residues influence as an intermediate in their sales promotion and prospective buyers in their purchasing practice. The content of modelled overall process, theory sketch and vocabulary as a study result of scientific research on the subject of cultural psychology and applied relevance in the fields of market value, sustainability and trade The target group of dominating and students of psychology with the focus on consumer, market and sales psychology as well as second-hand dealers and second-hand dealers of the University of Münster has a doctorate in the field of secondary psychology.
content.title_en: Production work and sales practice for Personica objects : The auratic effect of pre-owned second-hand trade

The author not only examines conventional thermal management measures and preconditioning, but also equips the thermal management with a predictive component. Furthermore, he develops an emergency function that makes the driving target reachable even if it is outside the current residual range. To analyse the energy balance, a characteristic number is derived, which can be used to determine the optimal average speed for maximum range. The content State of the technology Modelling and validation Optimization of energy and thermomanagement Predictive thermomanagement The target groups Dozierende and students of the KFZ technology with the focus on battery-electric vehicles and thermomanagement engineers in the application area Battery-electric vehicles, thermal management and predictive thermo management The author Markus Auer has been awarded a PhD in the Institute for Internal Compression and Power Management (IVK) at the University of Stuttgart.

content.text: Performance incentives in transport logistics: Development and simulation from the perspective of the principal agent theory. Marcus Müller describes and explains conflicts of objectives between construction management and construction equipment leader and sets up a model that can make predictions of the effect of incentive systems. From the theory and application domain, the author derives requirements to answer the question of the design of incentive systems with the aim of increasing transport performance. His study confirms the experimental or empirical findings on the effect of incentive systems and shows that these also apply to transport logistics systems in civil engineering. From the findings of the simulation, the author derives recommendations for the design of compensation models. The content of transport logistics in earth construction The principal agent theory as a reference framework design and simulation of the incentive system The target groups lecturers and students in the fields of construction business teaching, BWL, business information technology Practitioner of the field of construction management The author Dr. Marcus Müller received his doctorate at Univ.-Prof. Dr. Stefan Kirn at the Chair of Business Informatics 2 of the University of Hohenheim and headed research projects with the focus on incentive logistics.
content.title_en: Performance incentives in transport logistics : Development and simulation from the perspective of the principal agent theory

content.text: Resilience of complex regional systems: Brunsbüttel between lock-in and learning processes. Barbara Weig builds a bridge between theory and empiricism in this book, first critically discussing the concept of evolutionary economic geography and extending it to a conceptual approach to the analysis of regional resilience. In the second part of the book, the author examines in the case study Brunsbüttel which system behavior and which system characteristics are conducive to the development of regional resilience. In times of change and uncertainty, a characteristic of complex regional systems is of particular importance: the ability to develop resilience. Resilience means being able to react flexibly to surprises, be adaptable and develop further endogenous. This applies in particular to regional economic systems.The content Evolutionary economic geography The Brunsbüttel region – a complex system in the transformation Regional resilience Brunsbüttel's The target groups Dozierende and student of economic and social geography, regional economics and spatial sciences.
content.title_en: Resilience of complex regional systems : Brunsbüttel between lock-in and learning processes

content.text: Business model development in the field of multinational companies: case study on electric mobility in the automotive industry. Dynamically integrative approach of business model development in the field of multinational companies -- elements of the business model core and its properties -- process for identifying the business model core -- electric mobility as a system innovation from the perspective of MNU in the automotive industry and the need to adapt business models. In this work, the author develops an integrative approach to the development and internationalization of business models in multinational companies (MNU). Furthermore, he designs the business model core as a central tool for the international scaling of business models. The conceptual development of the integrative approach and the business model core are based on a deep case study in the context of electric mobility. The case study shows how the stress field of MNU characterising the field of tension between local adaptation and global integration affects the development of new business models. The content of dynamic integrative approach of business model development in the field of multinational companies is based on elements of the business model core and its properties Process of determining the business model core of electric mobility as a system innovation from the perspective of MNU in the automotive industry and the need of business business model development in the field of business business business model business models.
content.title_en: Business model development in the field of tension between multinational companies : case study on electromobility in the automotive industry

content.text: The success of advertising on the Internet: effectiveness and efficiency of online video ads. The new technologies on the Internet allow brands and companies to advertise with the help of video ads. But what success can be expected from this? Whether the hype around the Internet is justified as an advertising medium and the use of online video ads is worthwhile, the author Rosa Kriesche examines with reference to the results of international online branding campaigns and an empirical study from the automotive trade. Her book provides a comprehensive overview of effectiveness and efficiency in internet advertising and compares the results with those of classic advertising.
content.title_en: Internet advertising success : effectiveness and efficiency of online video ads

content.text: The presentation of Sub-Saharan Africa in the German school book: Societal Studies, Geography, History and Politics of Secondary Education (Gundesschule) in North Rhine-Westphalia. School books have a great significance for the organization of the teaching within the school. The subject of Sub-Saharan Africa plays a rather minor role both in the local society and in school books. This experience was made by the author who fled Eritrea in the 1980/90s as a learner at a Wuppertal school as a whole. In the course of his studies of social education he noted that this problem is also only marginally addressed in the university context. Outside the school, Sub-Saharan Africa is also presented in general media coverage as a crisis and disaster region, in which the proportion of European and western countries plays a largely subordinate role in this situation and initiatives from Sub-Saharan Africa are hardly mentioned in the resolution of problems.
content.title_en: The presentation of Sub-Saharan Africa in the German textbook : Societal Studies, Geography, History and Politics of Secondary Education I (total school) in North Rhine-Westphalia

content.text: Optimization of automatic storage crane systems on container terminals. Planning problems at the container terminal -- The RMG system as a potential bottleneck -- RMG optimization of a storage block -- Procedure for integrated transport optimization -- Comparison of optimization approaches. Ulf Speer develops two optimization methods for the sequence planning of different automatic storage crane systems and compares them quantitatively using a simulation model. content.text: Climate change and gender: on the political ecology of adaptation in Mexico. The study aims at a deeper analytical understanding of the complex constitutional conditions and the intersectional significance of gender for dealing with climate change. How does gender become important for the adaptability of dealing with climate change? What role do other structural inequalities, symbolic representations and identities play in this regard?Based on social-ecological research approaches and feminist approaches, a theoretical-conceptional analysis framework is developed and a qualitative empirical case study is carried out in Mexico.With its results, the study not only provides a thoughtful and innovative contribution to social-scientific adaptation and vulnerability research, but also provides fruitful impulses for inequality research in social-ecological contexts as well as for critical feminist theory formation.

content.text: The 'linear model of innovation' in West Germany: a history of the hierarchy of basic and applied research after 1945. The 'linear model of innovation' is one of the most widely mentioned and at the same time controversial descriptions of research and development (R & D). The analysis of the scientific-political interdiscourse between politics, science and economy in the West German scientific landscape after 1945 shows how a profound hierarchization of basic and applied research emerged between economically shaped expectations of usefulness and humanistically coloured ideals. The 'pure', 'free' basic research was granted a privileged position in rhetorical, ideological, institutional and legal approaches towards application areas.
content.title_en: The 'linear model of innovation' in West Germany: a history of the hierarchy formation of basic and application research after 1945

content.text: The social construction of the city: A theory on the sociology of cities. The book focuses on the meaningful construction of cities. It aims to capture the construction principles and meanings with which urban reality is produced. For this purpose, interdisciplinary research on the logic of cities is linked to the sociology of knowledge and psychological theory of construction. From around 350 interviews, general principles on the social construction of the city are elaborated. A core result is the ‘social sense space of urban reality', which discusses the relationalities of the construction principles to each other, and thus establishes a theory on the sociology of cities. Using individual cities, the book shows how specific sense assignments differentiate the relational field of urban realities. The author shows that city becomes not only a perceived object of everyday life via the properties of size, density and heterogeneity, but above all in its qualitative effects. The book thus provides as basic findings for the urban sociology and theory formation as well as for the practice-oriented urban planning and development. The management theory on the construction of urban knowledge/multitudes of the city-oriented urban planning.
content.title_en: The social construction of the city: a theory on the sociology of cities

content.text: Creativity and Innovation: Application and further development of the Innovator DNA in coaching. Based on a study that identifies five discoverer qualities of innovative entrepreneurs, Nora-Corina Jacob develops a creative coaching for executives, which is based on current research results and practical exercises and results in a process model for the promotion of creative skills. The author provides a deep understanding of creative processes and contributes to current psychological creativity research. To this end, she provides a comprehensive insight into theoretical and practical foundations of the complex of creativity and develops theory-led and, based on individual case studies, a discovery model of creativity. The creativity model and the discussion of the work aim to provide impulses for future initiatives for creativity promotion as well as creativity research. The content Strategies of Creative Persons Theory Construction of Individual Studies Creative Coaching Further Development of the Innovator DNA Model Discussion of a possible general factor of creativity The target groups of the University of Munich University of Applied Sciences (in the field of humanities) know (in the field of humanities) and innovation.
content.title_en: Creativity and innovation : Application and further development of the innovator DNA in coaching

content.text: Corruption susceptibility of companies: significance and impact of structural factors. Jörg Neubauer develops a model that identifies structural factors influencing the vulnerability of small and medium-sized enterprises in Germany and quantifies their strength. In addition, he examines whether personal misconduct of the individual or existing structures in companies favours corruption more strongly. Using a structural equation model, he shows that procurement complexity and control and prevention instruments are in particular two drivers for corruption susceptibility in companies. Finally, the author gives recommendations for the compliance management of companies. The content Corruption as a structural challenge of compliance management corruption in Germany The principle agent theory in the context of economic corruption Influencing factors in the vulnerability of corruption Personal factors influencing factors and their predictive value The target groups Dozierdeen der Fachbereiche Supply Chain Management, Purchasing, Procurement and Corporate Ethics as well as vocational education Praktiker in the areas of compliance and supply chain management as well as economic examiner and business consultant The author Jörg Neubauer is a scientific employee at Otto-Friedrich-Universität Bamberg and the coordinator of the Bavarian university schools of work.
content.title_en: Corporate susceptibility to corruption: importance and impact of structural factors

content.text: In this book, Katharina Große develops a theoretically based user typology for e-participation in Germany. The author describes the five types of participation: designers, optimizers, players, world improvers and those who are trying to achieve this. For each of these types, she derives specific requirements and translates them into concrete design recommendations. This creates the basis for politicians, administrative staff and software developers to make e-participation more user-friendly and reduce barriers to participation. The content typology of e-participation Theoretical development of the list of characteristics Validation based on empirical studies Usage requirements and design recommendations The target groups Scientists, lecturers and students of political and administrative sciences, in particular participation and open governance research, sociology and fields of information system research The focus of the research is on the topic of open-label research at the University of Baden-Württemberg.
content.title_en: User-centered e-participation : typology, requirements and design recommendations

content.text: In the field of intellectual property management, Christian Stauf examines how companies can best protect and exploit innovations. He develops a holistic approach to this, which understands the choice of the protection instrument as a core element and integrates the entire spectrum of legal and factual instruments into the calculation. He highlights the product design as an essential building block and analyses the usefulness of the protection options in question. The aim is to convey the necessity and potential of a holistic intellectual property management to decision-makers, while building a bridge between the economic and legal aspects of the subject. The content • Intangible resources and innovation • Protection of innovations at the company level • Aim and design of intellectual property management • Selection and combination of protection instruments • Protection of external product design • Multiple protection and cumulation of intellectual property rights The target groups • Interdisciplinary researchers and students of business and legal sciences • Professionals and executives in technology companies, decision makers in the fields of product development and innovation protection The author Dr. Christian Stauf has a PhD in business administration and administration.
content.title_en: Holistic Intellectual Property Management in the Company

content.text: Between Like Button and Party Book: the role of the Internet in the political participation of young people. Anna Soßdorf examines the political offline and online activities of young people in order to check the crisis diagnosis of a politically almost uninvolved youth. She focuses on the question of how participation in the Internet is low-threshold for young people. Another focus of her work is the motives and factors of influence associated with the political participation of young people in and outside the Internet.The study presents diverse findings on the political participation of young people and shows problems, opportunities and necessary prerequisites in terms of sustainable integration of young people in political offline and online worlds.The content The ideal of political likes, share and tweets Political participation and the role of the Internet Political participation, media use and socialisation research <results: like="" and="why="participate="young="political?"The target groups Dozierde und Studieren der Politik- und Medienwissenschaft, Politikwissenschaft und Jugendischeforschung Industrierein Beitworteintagung in den Bereichen.
content.title_en: Between Like Button and Party Book : the Role of the Internet in the Political Participation of Young People

content.text: Long-term perspectives of the health economy: A CGE analysis of demographic and technological growth effects. Christoph Heible evaluates the health-economy effects of medical-technological progress and demographic change on the basis of model-based and scenario-based analyses. The author proves, among other things, that medical-technical progress does not necessarily result in growth-driven effects, but rather that the form in which technical progress materialises is decisive.From the total number of simulation results, a catalogue of technological and demographic scenarios is derived, which describes a differentiated picture of the potential effects for the growth prospects of the health economy.The content of the overall economic effects of medical-technical innovations Growth perspectives of the health economy and its sectors Impact of demographic ageing on the health economy until 2060 The target groups Dozierende and students of the economic and social sciences with the focus on the health economy, economic, health and social policy Practitioners in the fields of health economics and economy and its sectors Impacts of demographic ageing on the health economy until 2060 The target groups of the university's doctoral and social sciences are the effects of the medical economy and the university's doctoral thesis.
content.title_en: Long-term prospects of the health economy: A CGE analysis of demographic and technological growth effects

content.text: Epistemological beliefs of educators: the importance for pedagogical action in day-care facilities. In this study, Magdalena Plöger-Werner examines the specific epistemological beliefs of educators (based on natural sciences and early pedagogicals) and their beliefs regarding children's learning and shows the connection to the nature science-related and cross-sectoral design of learning situations in day-care facilities.The results show that epistemological and learning-related beliefs are important for pedagogical action.This influence is indirect, especially for the natural sciences, and conveys the information on learning-related beliefs.The content Orientation quality: beliefs of pedagogical staff Educational process quality Interview study on the approach to the beliefs of early pedagogical professionals Identification of latent classes of convictions Influence of epistemological beliefs and teaching learning convictions on pedagogical action The target groups Dozierdeans and students of psychology with a focus on early education and professionalization research The faculty of the University of Applied Sciences and Humanities is a specialist in the Department of Diagnostics and Diagnostics.
content.title_en: Epistemological beliefs of educators: the importance for educational activities in day care centres

content.text: Experience combines: The potential of older migrants in the field of migration and integration engagement. Udo Dengel examines the (migration) biographical and quasi-professional experience of older migrants who are located in the field of migration and integration engagement in Germany. Based on biographical and in part guide-based interviews, he investigates how this knowledge of experience is expressed in support of other migrants modified in new integration strategies. The results reflect typical attitudes, actions and functions of support for committed migrants, which take place across ethnic-cultural boundaries in a newly interpreted framework of activity between distance to ‘thirds' and personal proximity to help seekers. The content of research question in the context of empirically based theory formation Social theoretical perspectives Social theoretic framework Working in the field – Empirical results The target groups of sociology, social workers and social workers The empirical framework of the university's research is based on the research question of the empirical research community.
content.title_en: Experience combines : the potential of older migrants in the field of migration and integration engagement

content.text: Color preferences in gooseless bees and bumblebees : Analysis taking into account individual color parameters. Jessica Bossems develops a completely new method for testing spontaneous colour preferences of bees and successfully tests them in the open air at gooseless bees in Brazil and under laboratory conditions at bumblebees in Germany. Bees are among the most important pollinators of flower plants, whereby the detection of their flowers often runs via visual signals such as flower size, shape and colour. The author's behavioural biological colour selection experiments with gooseless bees and bumblebees show that bees prefer certain colors over others and react differently to the color attributes of predominant wavelength, color purity and color intensity. Flower plants use these color preferences to attract specific pollinators and prevent others from visiting flowers.The content Definition and properties of colours Color vision in humans & bees Meaning of colour vision during flower visits The target groups Doziers and students of biology with the emphasis on zoology, sensory physiology, ecology The author Jessica Bossems works on the visual view of bees of the senses of the flower.
content.title_en: Color preferences in spineless bees and bumblebees : Analysis taking into account individual color parameters

content.text: The importance of authenticity to explain the effects of counterfeiting on brand transfers. Companies are under pressure to develop growth strategies for increasing sales and profits. Based on a comprehensive empirical study, Anna-Christina Dietert demonstrates positive effects of authentically designed brand transfers on the brand's main brand. Due to the tendency to market saturation and the change in customer needs, companies can use the brand transfer strategy to dynamize the brand. Consequently, it is of great importance to know the success factors in such a project. At the same time, the search for authentic offers becomes increasingly important among the customers. Practical recommendations for action complete the work. The content of brand dynamization in the field of tension between growth and authenticity assurance Development of a theoretically based construct of brand authenticity Re-effect effects in the brand transfer strategy Empirical investigation in the example of automotive brands Target groups Dozierde und Studieren der Wirtschaftswissenschaften mit den Schwerpunktung zwischen Markenmanagement und Markenführung innovativegenrate, Bereich Beihrungsmanagement von Marken-Authentreifaktion.
content.title_en: Guaranteeing the success of brands through authenticity : The importance of authenticity to explain the effects of reciprocity in brand transfers

content.text: Global Staffing: Occupation of Executive Positions of German Companies in Brazil. Current Research Status -- International Positions as Interface Thematic of Coordination Research and International (Personal) Management -- Development of a Reference Framework for the Occupation of Executive Positions in Foreign Companies with Special Consideration of Coordinative Goals -- Identification and Analysis of International Positions of German Companies in Brazil over Time. Eva-Maria Lang identifies theoretically based influences on the coordination-related occupation of executive positions in foreign companies. By means of an empirical-qualitative investigation of Brazilian subsidiaries of German companies, the assumed impact relationships of reality are compared. Not least by considering changes in the course of time, remarkable insights into the placement practice of multinational companies are achieved. The content • Current Research Status • International Positions as Interface The topic of Coordination Research and International (Personal) Management • Development of a Reference Framework for the Occupation of Executive Positions in Foreign Companies with Special Consideration of Coordinative Targets • Identification and Analysis of the International Positions of German Companies in Brazil in Time Course The Research Unit • Dozende und Beseitung der Betriebungswirtschaftswirtschaftsbewirtschafts.
content.title_en: Global Staffing : Occupation of executive positions of German companies in Brazil
