content.text: Tribological behaviour of piston bolt bearing. Special measurement methods of engine components -- Tribological investigations of piston bolt bearing -- Recording of piston bolt movement and detection of miscrylation. By combining innovative measurement concepts in the field of distance and contact measurement and using detailed analysis methods, Maik Lazzara can represent a holistic understanding of the movement mechanisms and tribological behaviour of piston bolt bearing of an internal combustion engine. The author examines the relative movements of bearing components and their miscrylation states in different operating conditions of the engine and identifies a sensitive and complex interaction between load-related bearing contours, solid-body friction value and in particular lubricant filling and supply. The content Special measurement methods of engine components Tribological investigations of piston bolt bearing Recording of piston bolt movement and detection of miscrylation The target groups Dozierde and students of vehicle technology Engineers in the field of tribology and engine mechanics for combustion engines The author Maik Lazzara is responsible for the development of the product for series production and oil pumps.
content.title_en: Tribological behaviour of piston bolt bearing

content.text: Sample-based parallelization of sequential applications: Concept and implementation of a software transformation process. This work presents AutoPar, a novel process for transforming existing software, which determines sequential initial patterns and transforms them into parallel software architectures. The evaluation shows that AutoPar achieves the same performance as experienced developers. AutoPar only takes a few minutes instead of several days of intensive manual work. An empirical study with software developers also shows that AutoPar is significantly more likely to demonstrate parallelization potential in a shorter time than existing parallelization tools. The content Basics of pattern-based parallelization Concepts and solutions for model-based parallelization Implementation and evaluation of AutoPar The target groups lecturers and students of computer science and software engineering practitioners in the areas of software development and software project management The author Dr.-Ing. Korbinian Molitorisz is currently working as head of software development in a leading company in the chemical industry. In addition, he is engaged in the program committee of some scientific conferences on multicore software engineering. He is an active member of the international working group on software patterns.
content.title_en: Model-based parallelisation of sequential applications : Concept and implementation of a software transformation process

content.text: InnenStadtAktion - Kunst oder Politik? : artistic practice in the neoliberal city. Who owns the city? - This question is the core of the battles over the inner cities, which are increasingly becoming a contested terrain. »Security and cleanliness« are considered the top maxim of an attractive cityscape. What role does art play in this context? Where does it serve to enforce regulatory policies and what are critical artistic practices? The focus of this investigation is on the 'InnenStadtAktionen', with which artists, theorists and political initiatives intervened at the end of the nineties against »privatisation, exclusion and security delusion«.
content.title_en: InnerCityAction - Art or Politics? : Artistic Practice in the Neoliberal City

content.text: The Holocaust as a challenge for film: Forms of filmic handling of the Shoah since 1945: an impact typology. Films about the Holocaust continue to lead to controversial discussions, especially about the way they deal with the Shoah. Apart from a few exceptions, however, film-scientific literature on the topic of the Holocaust in film consists of contributions to individual films without an overarching question.The focus of this study is therefore a typology that analyses the effect of these films on the viewer - taking into account the special aesthetics and the specific perceptions offered by them.The films analysed - including, among others, »Night and Fog«, »Schindler's List«, »Life is beautiful«, »Zug des Lebens« and »Birkenau and Rosenfeld« - simultaneously represent a break-up of the filmic examination with the Shoah since 1945.
content.title_en: The Holocaust as a challenge for film : Forms of cinematic handling of the Shoah since 1945 : an impact typology

content.text: Expanded Museum : Cultural memory and virtual realities. With the entry of digital media into the museum, a new mix of real space and virtual space is emerging. At the same time, under these conditions, the museum's own media heritage is clearly emerging. This advancing "automation of the museum", in which it is increasingly becoming the medium of presentation, leads to the museum itself being virtualized and thus decoupled from the real space or "available" to it. The volume presents numerous international pilot projects of the use of digital media in museums. It becomes clear how museums, using participatory and interactive strategies as places of memory and social memory, expand into virtual space.
content.title_en: Expanded Museum : Cultural memory and virtual realities

content.text: The project manager's task is to determine whether general planning is advantageous or not. The nature and complexity of the project, including the temporal and technical possibilities of the persons involved in the project, are important criteria for this. Sometimes the organization of planning competence is presented as a "question of faith", not a rational decision. It is at the centre of a problem area, to which questions such as - does general planning make a general planning unnecessary a project management? - Does the basic performance catalogue of the HOAI 2013 already give the builder the safety of a general planning? - What has it with the security of the builder when involving a general planner concretely on itself? Fundamentals and individual aspects of the planning model are compiled and derived from theses which are subjected to a critical evaluation. The content Basics: Terms, project participants and their organizational forms - aspects of the planner's operation forms of individual and general planning - preparation of the modeling - basics of the planning model of the Brandenburg-Führungsbildungsmodell - Universitätsmittels.
content.title_en: Individual or general planners - the optimal form of planning : decision model for the organization of construction project planning teams

content.text: Revenue management approach for acceptance control of customer-specific regeneration orders of complex capital goods. Felix Herde develops a control system for the acceptance and planning of uncertain and heterogeneous orders in the context of the regeneration of complex capital goods. This enables the inflexible capacities of the regeneration network and the limited stock levels to be used efficiently. In addition, the author develops mathematical decision models, which allow the bid prices of capacities and storage parts to be determined on the one hand. On the other hand, the models serve the control algorithms of the simultaneous acceptance and planning decision. The optimization approach demonstrates a high quality of solution and ensures that the demanding customer requirements are met. The content Customer-specific regeneration of complex capital goods Decision models for acceptance and planning decisions on regeneration orders Bid price-based acceptance controls with utilization of planning flexibility The target groups Dozierende and students of the business administration teaching and business engineering with the focus on production industry and operations research Practitioners from the areas of revenue management and capacity management at the University of Hanover know about the project manager of the University of Hanover.
content.title_en: Revenue management approach for acceptance control of customer-specific regeneration orders of complex capital goods

content.text: The continuous development of the modular modular construction kit means that structures and essential core processes can be modified with their escalation and decision-making methods. The author's inductively developed methodology is based on a detailed analysis of the control processes in relation to the product development process. The author uses the practical reflection of the concept to validate the methodology. Finally, it provides a scientific evaluation, resulting in an classification into the method systematics and an evaluation of the applicability. The content Integrated product development and systems engineering Complexity management in the automotive industry Theory and practice of modular product development Development and application of the methodology for controlling a modular construction kit The target groups of lecturers and students in the fields of mechanical engineering, business research, life cycle engineering, engineering, construction and vehicle engineering Practitioner in automotive engineering, in corporate research and management The author Charlotte-Angel has a Ph.D.
content.title_en: Methodology for controlling modular product kits

content.text: Functional thinking in the transition from functional theory to analysis: development of a test instrument and empirical findings from the gymnasial upper level. From functional theory to analysis -- mathematical performance tests -- test development and empirical findings. The book presents the development and use of a rapid-scaled test instrument in the field of functional thinking for the introduction phase of the gymnasial upper level. Starting from a broad theoretical foundation, Marcel Klinger researches the abilities of the pupils in the field of function theory and earlier analysis. It is evident that learners do not network different content areas to a desirable extent, but also that significant gender-specific inequalities exist in terms of test performance in favour of male subjects. The content From functional theory to analysis Mathematical performance tests Test development and empirical findings The target groups Dozierde and students of mathematics didactics, education sciences and education science, and education subjects, and teaching staff, and further education in mathematics The author Marcel Klinger conducts research and teaches as academic advice at the faculty of mathematics of the university.
content.title_en: Functional thinking in the transition from functional theory to analysis : development of a test instrument and empirical findings from the gymnasial upper level

content.text: Potential evaluation of generative manufacturing processes for lightweight components. Introduction -- Definition of central terms -- State of science and technology -- Methodology of potential evaluation -- Validation and results of potential evaluation -- Application examples -- Final consideration. Potential evaluation of generative manufacturing processes for lightweight components This dissertation describes a methodology for the potential and overall economic evaluation of generative manufacturing processes of products in the pre-design phase. Three potential areas of lightweight construction, function and time are evaluated quantitatively. The content of the thesis is the assessment of the optimized component weight and lightweight potential. The examination includes the component groups of secondary structural elements and hydraulic components from aviation as well as the production processes Selective laser melting, CNC milling and fine casting. The content · Introduction · Definition of central terms · State of science and technology · Methodology of potential evaluation · Validation and results of potential evaluation · Application examples · Final examination The author Tobias Schmidt studied laser cutting, CNC milling and fine casting at the Technical University of Dresden. Since 2011 he has been working as a business consultant at The Boston Consulting Group (BCG) at the University of Hamburg.
content.title_en: Potential evaluation of generative manufacturing processes for lightweight components

content.text: Since the beginning of the year, the University of Berlin has been working on the development of the social networking system. Martina Braasch has been working on the influence of social online networks on the management of stress and the preservation of social support empirically in a qualitative-explorative research design. Based on Stevan Hobfoll's resource conservation theory, the Facebook online network is looking at its potential to provide its users with resources that can have a positive – but also negative – impact on their stress experiences and the management of stressors.The Facebook coping typology provides insights into functional and dysfunctional behaviors in Facebook and enables them to reflect on their own usage behaviour and adapt to resource-optimized use.The content of social networks on the Internet Stress, stress management and social support Qualitative study on stress management and resources in Facebook Empirical typing of a Facebook coping typology The target groups Dozierende and student in the field of education, psychology, social sciences, education and health research are teaching staff as well as teaching staff in the field of psychology.
content.title_en: Stress management and social support in Facebook : The impact of social online networks on the perception and management of stress

content.text: The spatial identity and culture: Forms and usage potentials in the city of Hagen. Definition of the subject: Identification, space Culture -- Empirie spatial identification -- Theoretical positions in the current urban sociological discussion -- Historical aspects Hagen identity and culture -- Typology of the population -- Approach points for the valorization and increase of the identification of city and inhabitants Jasper Böing presents a typology of spatial identification in the city of Hagen's example, which contains various forms of expression and pays special attention to the mode of non-identification.In the context of urban planning and marketing, but also from a city sociological perspective, identification with the city is considered an important resource. However, the support and promotion of these endogenous potentials presupposes their knowledge. Therefore, the author relates sociological findings to urban measures initiated by the city of the population and discloses approaches for informed and targeted evaluation measures and strategies.
content.title_en: Spatial identity and culture: Forms and potential uses of the city of Hagen

content.text: Sustainability and Consumer Confusion at the Point of Sale: An investigation into the purchase of sustainable products in food retailing. Anja Buerke examines how the purchase of sustainable products in food retailing can be promoted, as organic and fair trade foods still represent a niche in the market despite increasing sales. She looks at determinants and effects of Consumer Confusion at the point of sale when buying sustainable products and shows to what extent the products themselves and the design of the sales site can lead to consumer confusion. content.text: Optimization of the Goniometrics of the X-ray diffraction imagery. Florian Bachmann develops methods for user-supported and (partial) automated polfigur measurement with all-purpose diffractometers. For any area detectors, wavelengths and single or multi-phase sample bodies, he formulates the generation of measurement diagrams as a quantity decomposition problem, which minimizes the number of measurements, but maximizes the coverage of scanning polspheres. To this end, he explains the diffraction geometry and proposes a design specification for corresponding measuring grids. The processing of recorded X-ray diffraction images to polfigures is derived from the kinematic diffraction model and discusses an adapted method for the estimation of orientation density. Finally, the author explains methods for the automation of the measurement sequence for the estimation of required parameters from an initial measurement and discusses the resulting optimization of goniometrics based on examples of the operating groups of the TU.
content.title_en: Optimization of goniometrics for the determination of texture from X-ray diffraction images

content.text: The G8 reform in Germany: Impact on student performance and educational inequality. Christoph Homuth presents the most comprehensive evaluation study to date on the effects of the G8 reform in order to make reliable statements about the results of one of the most controversial educational reforms. He shows that, unlike often feared by the media-present critics, the G8 does not pose a real risk to the performance of the German Gymnasium students. On the contrary, it even shows a performance advantage of the G8 over the G9. However, less the changed learning conditions than rather different educational decisions are responsible for this. These lead to the fact that today more and more powerful pupils switch to the Gymnasium, while more efficient pupils leave the Gymnasium faster. content.title_en: The G8 reform in Germany: impact on school performance and educational inequality

content.text: Media Selection in Everyday Life: The Role of Habits in the Selection Process. Anna Schnauber deals with the question of how habits influence the media classification selection at the sitative level. Based on a quantitative diary study combined with a survey, the author shows that habits influence both whether a media genre is used and how the selection process is designed: They lead to a more likely - and thus more frequent - use and make the selection process cognitively efficient. Matching situative factors such as hints such as location or desired gratings can increase their influence, media classification habits are basically general in nature, thus determining the selection process in various situations. content.text: Distinction: Cultural policy, artist-in-residence programmes and the practice of art. All important factors which influence the economy and the throughput time of processes in the offices are presented, discussed, concreteized and the connections presented in an overall model. content.text: Reusable systems for packaging: Problems and design approaches in the consumer goods industry. For decades, multi-use packaging has been used in the distribution of consumer goods. This reduces the cost of packaging and conserves natural resources, but often also leads to additional expenditure on a logistical and administrative level. Karlheinz Mevissen investigates how reusable packaging can be used efficiently and - especially - how it can be fed into reuse. The author develops a simulation system with which different design options for redistributing reusable packaging can be compared and assessed in terms of resource consumption (costs). The performance of the simulator is illustrated by various scenarios of possible use of reusable packaging.
content.title_en: Reusable systems for packaging: Problems and design approaches in the consumer goods industry

content.text: Information processing in customer service : possible applications and design. Customer service as an important external interface of the company is not yet adequately supported by information processing. Based on the individual phases of the customer service process, the author shows possibilities for this with the help of practical examples. This is followed by considerations on how an integrated customer service system could be designed in order to avoid a coexistence of different modules.
content.title_en: Information processing in customer service : possible applications and design

content.text: Electronic service markets: Models and mechanisms of electronic commerce. Today, the Internet is no longer used only for the dissemination of online information, but also as a medium for the processing of business processes. Support for such trade transactions in their various facets is now summarized under the term "electronic commerce". This book is particularly devoted to the question of how a software platform should be designed, which efficiently supports requirements of demanders and suppliers, e.g. commercial software components. Here, the software design derives directly from the microeconomic market definition. In particular, questions of transaction cost reduction and the innovativeness of market software lead to the model of an electronic service market. Existing implementation procedures for cooperation in distributed systems are evaluated in terms of their compatibility with this service market. Where they only partially meet the idea of the service market, the author develops new procedures whose integration is demonstrated in the subsequent software technical realization.
content.title_en: Electronic service markets : Electronic Commerce models and mechanisms

content.text: Sustainability-related credit risks: Empirical analysis of the impact of sustainability and credit risk, with particular consideration of climate change. Sustainability indicators, risks and rating -- Climate change and climate risks -- Credit decision at commercial banks -- Credit risk analysis and credit default forecast. Sustainability has become increasingly important in the financial sector in recent years. Christian Barthruff shows that many banks in the German-speaking world conduct a sustainability audit in corporate credit business. An empirical analysis is used to quantify the sustainability risks of companies and analyse their influence on credit risk. It is shown that sustainable companies have better credit ratings and lower risk premiums for credit default insurance than less sustainable companies during the observation period, both on a day-to-day basis and over time. The investigations show that sustainability ratings are generally suitable as an indicator for determining credit risk. The content of sustainability-related risk figures, risks and rating climate risks Credit decision at business banks Credit risk analysis and credit loss forecast The target groups of lecturers and students of business management are responsible for sustainability management in the business sector.
content.title_en: Sustainability-induced credit risks : Empirical analysis of the impact of sustainability and credit risks, with particular attention to climate change

content.text: The European Union's Revenues: Between Supranational Autonomy and Intergovernmental Control. Forms of Revenue as a Cause and Expression of European Dependency or Autonomous Freedom of Action -- The European Financing System in Four Historical Periods -- The Results of the Study: European Revenue Autonomy under National Control The study provides a political-scientific systematization of the revenue instruments created at European level since the 1950s. The focus is on the way in which the common institutions were granted financial leeway during the course of integration development: Did the Montanunion, as the first European tax to be applied, have greater independence from the will of the Member States? Would the own resources system in its original conception have actually increased European autonomy? To what extent do the financing structures provide an image of the EU's state of development and what developmental lines have emerged over the decades? These and other aspects are also addressed by the analysis of the European financing system.
content.title_en: The European Union's revenue: Between supranational autonomy and intergovernmental control

content.text: Stereotypes and the perception of media effects. Katharina Sommer asks how the activation of stereotypes can influence the assessment of media effects on third parties: stereotyping is usually carried out unconsciously and is a daily process in social situations. The author combines the question of the factors affecting the perception of media effects with the process of stereotyping to different groups of people. In this way, she shows that the assessment of media effects can be situationally different depending on which stereotypes have been activated. The content • Measurement of activation and application of stereotypes • Media effects and the role of stereotypes • Suggestions for future research The target groups • Lecturers and students of communication science and psychology The author Katharina Sommer works as a senior assistant at the University of Zurich in the field of media psychology and media impact at the Institute of Public Studies and Media Research (IPMZ) Measuring the activation and application of stereotypes -- Media effects and the role of stereotypes -- Suggestions for future research
content.title_en: Stereotypes and the perception of media effects

content.text: How does robotics come to the social? Epistemical practices of social robotics. Numerous research projects are working on the fact that robots leave factory halls and become part of everyday worlds such as hospitals, kindergartens and private homes. Designers face a non-trivial challenge: they have to translate the ambivalences and contingencies of everyday interaction into the discreet language of machines. How they meet this challenge, what patterns and solutions they use and what implications they place for the use of social robots is the subject of the book. In search of the answer to what makes robots social, Andreas Bischof visited research laboratories and conferences in Europe and North America and researched ethnographically. Among the main results of this study is the typology of research objectives in social robotics, an epistemological genealogy of the robot's idea in everyday worlds, the reconstruction of the references to 'real' everyday worlds in social robotics development and the analysis of three genres of the epistemically employed by robots and engineers.
content.title_en: How does robotics come to the social? Epistemic practices of social robotics.

content.text: Self-regulation in virtual studies : Volitional regulation, learning time and learning strategies in online seminars. The independent design and management of essential parts of the study program bring numerous advantages for students. Especially many challenges are in the virtual learning environments in which students are dependent on efficient regulation of their actions due to the low social and organizational involvement. Above all, the achievement of the learning goals in asynchronous online seminars requires a strong self-regulatory competence. This book deals with the learning processes in virtual learning environments from the perspective of self-regulation. The focus of the empirical study is on the role of the conflictal competences and their influence on the occurrence of subjective action regulation problems, the learning time and the use of cognitive learning strategies. The results show that volitional competences contribute statistically significantly to favorable learning behaviour in web-based environments. The findings derive important starting points for the optimization of the didactic design of virtual teaching.
content.title_en: Self-regulation in virtual studies : Volitional regulation, learning time and learning strategies in online seminars

content.text: On 04.08.2009 the "Law on the Prosecution of Serious State-Risking Violence" (GVVG) came into force and implemented three new criminal offences in the field of terrorism criminal law, the §§ 89a, 89b and 91 StGB. The declared aim of these norms is to "fight" the continuing threats of international terrorism even with the help of the criminal sanctions system already well in advance of planned attacks. The criminal offences lead the criminal law into the border area of police law of defence of danger and raise fundamental questions regarding the constitutional limits of such a "prevention law".The work focuses on whether a wide pre-deposit of criminality is still covered by the constitution and whether the material criminal law constitutes the correct point of approach against the threat of international terrorism.
content.title_en: Anti-Semitism Law against the Law or the Necessary Measures to Combat Terrorism? : on the constitutionality of §§ 89a, 89b and 91 StGB

content.text: Word-setting effects in the understanding of sentences. How are sentences that differ from the basic word position, and how can the integration of the respectively dislocated constituent succeed? From linguistic assumptions for the identification and representation of non-canonical word sequences, hypotheses are derived from psycholinguistic research. Sandra Muckel examines the predictions of these hypotheses in psycholinguistic experiments with regard to the work of syntactic, verb-specific and prosodic information. She shows that the parser uses the place of integration (the verb or track) that he can first identify in front of the sentence-final verb in its basic position. On this basis and taking into account evidence from English, the author formulates a hypothesis on opportunistic integration, according to which the parser uses the place of integration (the verb or track) that he can then identify. Afterwards, she investigates which alternative information allows the identification of a basic position in German.
content.title_en: Word-setting effects in the sense of sentence

content.text: Basic right to state protection: a comparison of the basic law for the Federal Republic of Germany and the constitution of the United States of America. According to the Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany, the state must not only refrain from direct interference with fundamental rights. It is also obliged to defend and promote fundamental rights. Other continental-European constitutional regulations also have fundamental protection obligations. In contrast, the United States Constitution takes a special role, according to the usual conception. Against this background, the author examines the figure of fundamental legal protection from a constitutionally comparable perspective. It is evident that there is no clear explanation for the differences in the understanding of fundamental rights. Rather, various historical-sociological causes and normative-dogmatic reasons can be identified, which in their cooperation have prevented the formation of fundamental legal protection obligations under the Constitution of the United States of America in a lasting way.
content.title_en: Basic right to state protection : a comparison of the Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany and the Constitution of the United States of America

content.text: Remind on the Internet: The online discourse about the process and the process against the concentration camp supervisor John Demjanjuk. Based on this, it is empirically explained to what extent mediated memories form part of online communication, which changes are associated with them and which constants can be determined in comparison with other memory media. Theoretically, concepts of memory studies, practice research, discourse theory and mediatization research are linked to this. The method is used to triangulate the procedure of the Grounded Theory with the knowledge-sociological and social-emiotic discourse analysis. The content Remind on the World Wide Web Remind on the online discourse Mediatization of memory processes The public memory of the Holocaust The target groups Dozierde and students of the media and communication sciences, the sociology of knowledge and the cultural sciences, and the focus on memory and memory processes The TUI's research staff at the Institute know the media as a practitioner.
content.title_en: Remind on the Internet : The online discourse about John Demjanjuk

content.text: Control as a pedagogical problem: empirical reconstructions of interaction in school inspection interviews. Maike Lambrecht uses a pedagogical theory repertoire to address current questions of social design and thus contributes to the determination of the relationship between education and society. The basis for this is a practice-theoretical twist of the educational concept, which allows to empirically reconstruct political-administrative control practices as pedagogical practices. The current New School System Control appears less as "economized" or "evidence-based", but rather as pedagogical staging practice. content.text: The partially non-profit (natural) person: On the legal systematic recording of individual commitment to the common good. The central concern of the treatise is to examine the relationship between individuals and their actions to the public good mission. Starting with the classification of public utility as a special instrument of public welfare promotion, then essential features of a public utility sphere are defined. It includes activities that are carried out voluntarily, free of charge and with qualified public welfare reference. Advantage of a legally clear recording of the activities of natural persons in the public utility sphere would be in particular that such a status as a partial non-profit (natural) person could be taken up with various intensity depending on the life phase and related funding instruments such as additional pension points for the committed persons could be linked to it.The content The charitable status as an instrument of public welfare promotion The dogma of the limitation of the public utility status on body bodies Characteristic features of an activity-related public utility sphere of activity can be found in the scope of the law of the individual.
content.title_en: The partially non-profit (natural) person : To the legal system of individual commitment to the common good

content.text: The use of shadow IT in companies: A method for managing intransparent information technology. Stephan Zimmermann shows that intransparent information technologies, which introduce departments and end users independently and past the IT department, represent a major challenge for companies. Problems and opportunities of this shadow IT can be controlled by means of survey tools and an IT division between IT department and department. The author presents a method in the IT governance and enterprise architecture context, which creates transparency to maintain productivity, flexibility and innovation promises of the department IT and to reduce emerging risks and inefficiencies. With the resulting IT service governance, a controlled IT remains in the department. The content Definition of shadow IT Classification of shadow IT manifestations Description of shadow IT features and measures Design of the method for dealing with shadow IT The target groups Dozierende und Studieren der Betriebswirtschaftslehre with the focus on business information CIOs, IT director, IT officer, IT officer, IT officer, and business administration officer.
content.title_en: The use of shadow IT in enterprises: a method for managing intransparent information technology

content.text: New life from the laboratory: bioscientific and ethical aspects of synthetic biology. Leona Litterst systematically combines the question of whether synthetic biology can be used to produce "new life", with the ethical dimension of whether it should be produced and which rules apply. To this end, she presents five research approaches of synthetic biology in detail, highlighting their claim to "create new life", and evaluating risk potentials in ethical-anthroporelational terms. She examines central ethical and systematic aspects of responsibility, the concepts of play, life, naturalness and artificiality, and the moral status of research objects of synthetic biology. It becomes clear that the possibility of producing "new life" is not only a question of technical implementation, but also of how we want to deal with "new life" and the potential opportunities and risks of synthetic biology in the future. The content of bioscientific foundations of synthetic biology Responsibility in synthetic biology is not only a question of the technical implementation, but also of how we want to deal with "new life" and the potential risks of synthetic biology in the future.
content.title_en: New life from the laboratory : Bioscientific and ethical aspects of synthetic biology

content.text: The structure colours in the focal point of bionics: between art and natural sciences. Sigrid Zobl describes a low-tec-high-yield form method for synthetic and organic surfaces, which is fast, inexpensive, with little material effort and without elaborate equipment to replicate structural colours and possibly their functions. The 22 organic samples formed in the context of this work come from the group of flora and fauna. The author shows that CD-R positive prints not only provide a direct application area as an artistic stylistic medium, but that the positive epoxy resin prints can also serve to create a database for biomimetic surfaces. Furthermore, the prints provide new insights for basic research. content.text: The Multurative Analysis of Offshore IT Development Projects: Risk Management by System Dynamic Models of Global Virtual Teams. Global Software Development with Virtual Teams -- Decision Support, Risk Management and Simulation -- System Dynamics Model for Global Software Development of a Virtual Team -- Simulation Results and Analysis of Interference Factors. Eike Mönkemeier provides a thorough quantitative analysis of the relationships and cost drivers of globally distributed software development to support decision-making in outsourcing and the assessment of the factors of work and work performance. The author treats the software creation as a general process as well as the specificities of global virtual teams. He introduces the Dynamics methodology system and presents the study model. The results illustrate the complex network of effects of international cooperation and show what needs to be considered apart from the cost analysis. The author analyses four basic determinants individually as well as in interaction: the linguistic, geographical, temporal and especially cultural distance between the project participants. content.text: Lost in Transformation?: Space-related ties in the transformation of urban renewal measures. Karen Sievers examines the role of spatial ties - 'Heimat' - in the context of urban conversion in East Germany. Using the examples of urban renewal and opencast mining, she investigates the questions of what this current programme of urban development promotion could 'learn' from these, what criteria a 'cautious urban conversion' would have to be measured and how 'theory and practice' of urban conversion deal with this challenge. As a result, it is also evident that the starting point of these program measures - i.e. the urban-spatial structure of the city - is of importance as a place of spatial connections. This relevance is hardly reflected in the publicistic and practical 'editing' of the program. The content of spatial ties in historical perspectives and current contexts of everyday life and planning intervention is home and participation Lost in transformation?
content.title_en: Lost in Transformation? : Spatial Bonds in the Change of Urban Renewal Measures

content.text: From the Set to the Concept: Philosophical-logical Perspectives on the Discovery, Testing and Grounding of Mathematics Education. Michael Meyer examines the questions which options teachers or school book authors have in order to discover, examine and/or justify mathematical sentences, which characterizes the process of forming a mathematical concept and which content or structural connections exist between concepts and sentences. He presents two mutually building theoretical approaches by combining mathematical didactic, philosophical and sociological theories. His analysis results result in concrete learning environments, whose empirical use and subsequent theoretical reconstruction explain conditions and (realisable) possibilities of mathematics learning. The content of discovery, testing and reasoning Philosophical-logical analysis of school books Realizations of discovery with latent proof ideas of concept formation as language play Conceptual formation through discovery and reasons The target groups Dozierende und Studieren der Mathematik und der Didaktik Lehrpersonne des Faches Mathematik Der Autor Prof. Dr. Michael Meyer ist Einführer eines Berichtungs am Forschungs und Mathematik am Universitätsührungen.

Further research focuses on the impact of gender, company size or population density on the level of income. The work is the first comprehensive study on the wage effects of spatial mobility in Germany. content.text: Success in social work: In the field of micropolitical conflicts of interest. Effectiveness and efficiency of social work -- Integration aid for disabled people -- Triangular social relations -- Economization of social work -- Transformation of welfare production. This paper examines and analyses the macro- and micro-political processes, interests, strategy and power options of the actors involved in the complex discussion of success and effectiveness in social work. The qualitative approach is provided by the current developments in integration aid for disabled people in the light of the UN Convention on the Law of Disability. The starting point for further analyses is the hypothesis that the actors involved in the service process are not only guided by technical arguments in the specific definition of successful and effective work, but rather by individual, political, economic and professional interests play an important role. This has far-reaching consequences for the understanding of social work as a profession and not least for the "customers" of social service provision. The content Effectiveness and efficiency of social work Integration aid for disabled people Social-related triangular relations Economicization of social work Transformation of welfare production Target groups Dozende und Pädagogische in der Behörung der Studierenden

content.text: The Democratic Party of the Party Leaders: Parties in Germany and Great Britain in comparison. Hui Ding addresses the classic political science topic of inner-party democracy and asks to what extent and under what conditions the selection of party leaders can be democratized. In the context of an institutionalist research approach, major parties in Germany and Great Britain are compared. It is evident that the selection processes are becoming increasingly inclusive, so that for example, simple party members are often entitled to vote. At the same time, however, the gatekeeping power of the leadership elites has been strengthened by increasing the initiation, nomination and voting barriers. The content An institutionalistic approach of inner-party democracy The party leader selection in historical comparison 1949–2009 The learning mechanism of inner-party democratization The target groups lecturers and students of political science Journalists and others interested in time history and political parties The author Hui Ding is an assistant professor of political science at Sun Yat-Sen University (Guangzhou, V. R. China).
content.title_en: The democratization of party leaders: parties in Germany and Great Britain compared

content.text: The professional behaviour of the training staff in error situations: An empirical study in the hotel and hospitality industry. Professionalism of the company training staff -- Errors in the workplace as a source of vocational learning -- Professional error competence of trainers -- Error climate and individual handling of the trainees with errors. In the vocational and business education sector little is known about the professional competence of occupational trainers, although these are considered to be of great importance for the teaching-learning process in the workplace. This also applies to the competence of training staff, to deal with errors of trainees in an effective way. Alexander Baumgartner addresses this research deficit and analyses the knowledge about errors in work situations, the strategies of action in error situations as well as the perspectives on the benefits of errors (professional error competence). Moreover, the error climate in the training business and the individual handling of the trainees with errors are highlighted by the training staff. In terms of content, the author takes into account the training area of the business management staff business knowledge.
content.title_en: Professional action of training persons in error situations : An empirical study in the hotel and catering industry

content.text: Methodical problems in measuring crime fear and victimisation experiences. This publication deals with the methods of recording crime fear. In addition to process-produced burden figures of police crime statistics (PKS), survey data on the results of (victim) surveys are the second important source of information on crime. However, when using survey data, a variety of problems and sources of error can affect the quality of data to the point of unusability. Marcel Noack shows the various sources of error in the survey data collection and their effects and offers alternatives. The content · Measurement of crime fear · Fear of crime in Europe · Reliability of global crime fear · Model for explaining crime fear · Problems in estimating crime rates The target groups · Docents and students of criminology and sociology · Crime Sociologists The author Marcel Noack works at the Institute of Sociology at the University of Duisburg-Essen. Measuring crime fear - Crime fear in Europe - Reliability of global crime fear - Estimating crime fear - Estimating crime rates - Estimating crime rates.
content.title_en: Methodological problems in measuring fear of crime and victimisation

content.text: An institutional economic analysis of capitalisation processes in the context of a decentralisation of tax legislation competences using the example of real estate tax in Germany. "The property tax is the subject of long-term reform discussions. Whether it also capitalizes in real estate prices has been insufficiently investigated for the German real estate market, whereas capitalisation research is far-reaching for the US real estate market. A regression analysis is carried out for the real estate markets Bremen and Lower Saxony in each case to check whether public services and property tax burdens capitalise on real estate values. Furthermore, the governance concept and the New Institution Economics serve as extended analysis tools of the capitalization process with regard to dynamics of actors and institutions as well as to reform effects." (Verlagsinformation)
content.title_en: An institutional economic analysis of capitalisation processes in the context of decentralisation of tax legislation competences using the example of real estate tax in Germany

content.text: Data processing in the employment context: the scope of the opening clause according to Art. 88 GDPR. The EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) has raised high waves. Not only the Internet giants are therefore under enormous pressure to act. Many employers and business parties also have to do a lot by concluding company agreements or obtaining consent. The question arises which European regulations apply to national regulations for the processing of employee data. The legislator will also face the same problem: the long-awaited employee data protection law is again on the agenda. However, the GDPR does not contain any differentiated regulations in this respect, but rather plays back the regulatory competence in Art. 88 GDPR to the Member States. They can then provide for more specific regulations for the processing of personal employee data. What this means exactly and whether stricter regulations against those of the GDPR are permissible for the protection of employees is shown in this work.
content.title_en: Data processing in the employment context : the scope of the opening clause according to Art. 88 GDPR

content.text: The development and evaluation of a test instrument for the investigation of previous knowledge and preconceptions in cosmology. Cosmology describes the development of the universe as a whole. Cosmological discoveries in theory and practice have therefore decisively shaped our modern scientific world view. The conveyance of a modern world view through teaching is a frequent desire in the scientific education discussion. Nevertheless, research and development needs continue to exist. Cosmological topics are often found in the media and are at the same time further away from everyday life, so that here, especially scientifically incorrect ideas can develop, which can lead to problems in teaching. The aim of this scientific work is to contribute to this research area and the prerequisites for existing prior knowledge and preconceptions in cosmology with which students come into the classroom to study and then compare with those of other countries. This is done by qualitative content analysis of an open questionnaire. On this basis, a multiple-choice questionnaire is finally developed, applied and evaluated. ...
content.title_en: Development and evaluation of a test instrument for the investigation of previous knowledge and preconceptions in cosmology

content.text: Legal network research: modelling, quantification and visualization of relational data in law. Networks are everywhere. Lawyers use them on their way to work (infrastructure networks), for the search for advice (contact networks) and for legal research (information networks). They construct them (citizens networks), supervise them (financial networks) and fight them (crime networks). From this perspective, there is nothing that cannot be modeled as a network: as a set of units, combined with a lot of relationships between these units. Corinna Coupette examines how legal phenomena can be represented as networks, and explores what can be learned by quantitative and visual analysis of these networks for law. In doing so, she introduces legal network research into German legal discourse. Based on a specially compiled data set of decisions of the Federal Constitutional Court, she develops tools for modelling, quantification and visualization of law.
content.title_en: Legal network research : modelling, quantification and visualization of relational data in law

content.text: Optimization methodology for volume transmission holograms with LED illumination. This work presents an optimization method that allows the adaptation of volume transmission holograms to the spectral properties and the beam characteristics of LEDs. This methodology includes a design process for the calculation of optimized hologram information as well as a simulation approach for the realistic visualization of the reconstructed image. Both in the calculation and in the simulation, LED parameters such as wavelength, divergence angle and wave front shape are taken into account. The description and experimental determination of an LED-specific wave front is a particular challenge and is discussed in this work accordingly. In order to check the design process and the simulation, the calculated holograms are exposed to a photopolymer. The necessary exposure process is implemented in the context of the laboratory work and the exposure parameters in the design and simulation are taken into account. In addition, the specifically coordinated steps of design via exposure to the simulation results a holistic methodology for the optimization and verification of holograms is shown by the analysis of the sample and the results of the sample.
content.title_en: Optimization methodology for volume transmission holograms with LED lighting

The emergence and dynamics of such relationships are described from the perspective of teenagers and the resultant prevention measures, such as the development and implementation of teaching units for pupils from grades 7 to 10, are presented. In the context of a social psychological qualitative analysis of expert interviews from different areas of youth assistance and police and school social work, key points of sustainable prevention work are formulated.

content.text: The prevention and intervention strategies against right-wing extremism are compared with the emergence of the state programmes. Right-wing extremism is a multifaceted phenomenon that manifests itself both at the level of attitudes and action and represents a continuous challenge for the liberal democratic basic order and the political culture of the Federal Republic. Against this background, a state response pattern has been established since the beginning of the 1990s, which brings preventive and intervening measures together in coordinated strategies or programmes. At the time of the writing of the dissertation (end of 2016), a clear majority of the federal states (twelve in number) implemented such a strategy in the form of a country programme. The analysis follows the development configurations, conditions and mechanisms of the respective programmes and asks how these affect the settlement strategies. Here, theoretical references of the policy field analysis, the actor-centred institutionalism and governance research are used to reconstruct the process of program development in particular and to understand the emergence of the divergent programmes. The work relies on a broad data base consisting of the state's own participation in the field of analysis, the field of law and the discussion of the discussion of the report.
content.title_en: Prevention and intervention strategies against right-wing extremism: the emergence of national programmes in comparison

content.text: In the course of this work, aromats such as naphthalene and anthracene were converted into so-called endoperoxides with oxygen of the singulart, a reactive form of ordinary oxygen. The systems used here were modified with functional groups that are linked to the aromatic via an oxygen bridge. The resulting endoperoxides are usually particularly unstable and could be isolated and comprehensively investigated in this work. In this context, the reaction behaviour was examined. It was shown that the aromats react differently quickly with oxygen of the singulart according to their functional groups. content.text: Tannins for sustainable and functional carbon materials: Synthesis strategies and possible applications. In times of a rapidly changing and versatile energy market, carbon materials must be suitable for various requirements. This requires flexible synthesisable carbon materials preferably from cheap and sustainable carbon sources. However, it is not easy to identify precursor compounds that are suitable for different production processes and whose carbon products can be adjusted to specific properties, such as structure, nitrogen content, surface and pore sizes. In this context, natural polyphenols, such as excess tannins from wine production, can open up a new world of highly functional and versatile carbon materials with high yields. The main objective of this present thesis was to create new functional, adjustable and scalable nanostructured carbon materials from tannins (especially tannic acid) for different electrochemical purposes.
content.title_en: Tannins for sustainable and functional carbon materials : Synthesis strategies and possible applications

content.text: Tannins for sustainable and functional carbon materials: Synthesis strategies and possible applications. In times of a rapidly changing and versatile energy market, carbon materials must be suitable for various requirements. This requires flexible synthesisable carbon materials preferably from cheap and sustainable carbon sources. However, it is not easy to identify precursor compounds that are suitable for different production processes and whose carbon products can be adjusted to specific properties, such as structure, nitrogen content, surface and pore sizes. In this context, natural polyphenols, such as excess tannins from wine production, can open up a new world of highly functional and versatile carbon materials with high yields. The main objective of this present thesis was to create new functional, adjustable and scalable nanostructured carbon materials from tannins (especially tannic acid) for different electrochemical purposes.
content.title_en: Tannins for sustainable and functional carbon materials : Synthesis strategies and possible applications

content.text: The current market 2.0 in the light of European and German (competition) law: to classify the replacement of green and grey electricity. The work is dedicated to the detailed analysis of the so-called electricity market "2.0" . Specifically, the author examines whether the joint marketing of conventionally generated electricity and (sponsored) renewable electricity on the German-Austrian replacement market is in line with applicable law (competition) law. In the first step, a detailed and critical presentation of the competitive conditions, existing structural deficits and the relevant markets in the production sector is carried out. Then, the normative bases of the competition assessment of the market structure are systematically presented, with detailed presentation of the relevant administrative and judicial practice. Subsequently, the market is subjected to a detailed analysis based on the normative guidelines. Finally, alternative design options for the marketing of green electricity and grey electricity are shown in comparison with the current system.
content.title_en: The electricity market 2.0 in the light of European and German (competition) law : to classify the replacement of green and grey electricity

content.text: The regulation of the opinion power of Internet intermediaries. Internet intermediaries such as Facebook, Google and Co. are Internet services that primarily transmit third-party information to their users. Although they themselves do not provide their own content and do not select external content editorially, they can exert an influence on public opinion formation through algorithmic sorting and deletions or also through user exclusions. The work analyses whether this kind of influence de leg lata is regulated by media law regulations of the Broadcasting State Treaty and the Telemedia Act or by economic law regulations of cartel and competition law. Furthermore, taking into account the national and unional basic legal control requirements de legferenda, a regulatory concept for controlling the opinion power of service providers is developed. The analysis is also carried out taking into account the US-American legal requirements for Internet intermediaries as contrast foil.
content.title_en: Regulation of the opinion of Internet intermediaries

content.text: The ability to move and the availability of copyright licenses: an investigation of the disparity between legal framework and increasing economic and social relevance of intellectual property licensing. The investigation is dedicated to the question whether the legal framework governing the licensing of creative content, currently in force, meets the increased economic and social relevance of the licensing of cultural goods in terms of the availability of intellectual property rights and the ability to move. In addition to the dogmatic examination of the relevant legal regulatory complexes, the discussion calls for a practical compensation of the interests of all parties involved in the licensing chain, taking into account economic value-added optimization. Subsequently, the degree of availability and the ability to move copyright licenses in the regulatory complexes of insolvency, succession protection and further portability, which are existing according to current legal conditions, is examined.
content.title_en: The ability to move and the safety of copyright licences: an investigation of the disparity between the legal framework and the increasing economic and social relevance of licensing intellectual property

content.text: § 31 BGB in the case of double mandate: the liability of the assigning company for breach of duty of its seconded organ administrator. The work deals with the liability of the assigning company for violations of duty of its seconded organ administrator in the receiving company. The focus is on the assignment standard § 31 BGB. In a first step, the examination is made whether liability according to § 31 BGB also applies to liability standards which are not (also) addressed to the assigning company – namely the internal liability standards § 93, 116 AktG. This is to be denied, since § 31 BGB always presupposes a duty position of the company. In a second step, the examination is then made of when the double mandater acts in his activities in accordance with § 31 BGB "in the interpretation of the assignments for the assigning company. Finally, the liability standards to be assigned to the assigning company are examined in particular taking into account the situation of double mandate.
content.title_en: § 31 BGB in the case of double mandate: the liability of the assigning company for breach of duty of its seconded organ administrator

content.text: Repeals and amendments to investment protection agreements: an investigation into the scope of survival Clauses in BITs. Bilateral investment protection agreements (BITs) are international contracts for the protection of foreign investors and regularly have so-called continuation clauses (also survival or sunset clauses) which strengthen investor protection in time by making unilateral terminations effective only after waiting for a 10-, 15- or even 20-year period. However, continuation clauses leave open whether they also cover the case of mutually agreed terminations. This question is at the heart of the investigation and includes fundamental problems of the current international contract law: How is the relationship between the freedom of the contracting states and the individual protection created by a contract? Does investors have a particularly solid individual protection through the continuation clauses? What alternative ways are available to a BIT to remove or modify a BIT?
content.title_en: Repeals and amendments to investment protection agreements: an inquiry into the scope of Survival Clauses in BITs

content.text: Anti-extremism and defence-based democracy: criticism of the political self-image of the Federal Republic of Germany. This work is based on the premise that there is an understanding of democracy in the political self-image of the Federal Republic of Germany, according to which democracy is equally distinct from and is resistant to various extremisms. Defendability is accompanied by restrictions on popular sovereignty. The author reconstructs how this understanding prevailed against other forms of democracy, and works out approaches to deconstruction of anti-extremist, defence-based democracy. Using a hegemony analysis, he examines key texts since 1945. He also shows how institutions of political control and parts of science (totalitarianism research and extremism research) support this self-image. The author problems the increasing definition of constitutional protection over the borders of democracy and the insufficient justification and validation of extremism theory approaches.
content.title_en: Anti-extremism and defenceful democracy : Criticism of the political self-image of the Federal Republic of Germany

content.text: Investigation of defect reactions in silicon by means of charge carrier-life-long spectroscopy. In this work, the basics of temperature and injection-dependent life-span spectropy (T-IDLS) are explained, which is an extremely sensitive method of material characterization of semiconductors. These are then applied to specifically-contaminated model materials (silicon wafers) contaminated with iron, copper and nickel. It is shown that T-IDLS not only allows the parameterization of defects generated by contamination (energy location in the band gap, ratio of capture cross-sections) to be determined. In particular, chemical reactions of the individual defects in the model materials can be demonstrated (by changing the defect concentration) and also according to the laws of thermodynamics and kinetics. Finally, the results are applied to the simulation of the influence of the different defects on the efficiency of Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell (PERC) solar cells.
content.title_en: Investigation of defect reactions in silicon by means of charge carrier-life-long spectroscopy

content.text: Entrepreneurial self-presentation on the Internet: interactive online reporting of DAX companies. Alena Voelzkow describes in this book how DAX companies' business reports have changed in recent decades under the social guiding principle of sustainability and provides empirical results on the influence of digital media on corporate reporting. In her media sociological analysis, she examines what distinguishes online reports from classic business and sustainability reports on paper and what benefits the Internet provides reporting companies. The author shows to what extent companies use the new media in their communication behaviour for personalisation of their reporting and for dialogue offers and whether they better meet the different interests of stakeholders in reporting. The content The Annual Report as "comprehensive" Business presentation The change in corporate reporting in Germany The online reporting of DAX companies Inclusion and dialogue in online reporting of DAX companies The target groups Dozierde und Studierenden der BWL as well as media and communication sciences, sociology and design specialist and executives in the areas of corporate communication as well as corporate and integrated reporting The German Media Association has supervised them (involved in the field of business management)

content.text: Blackbox Parliamentary Control Board of the Bundestag : Deficiencies and optimization strategies in the control of the intelligence services. Andreas Friedel locates the causes of the functional weaknesses of the parliamentary control bodies (PKGr) of the German Bundestag, which is responsible for the control of the intelligence services of the Federal Government (BND, BfV and MAD). For this purpose, he systematically evaluates the structural framework conditions and the individual characteristics of the MPs in the PKGr during the period 1999 and 2016. Based on these findings and identified changes in the control strategy as well as formal and informal measures for the optimization of control, the author formulates recommendations for political practice. The content • Making use of theoretical approaches from the accountability, agency and parliamentarism research • Genesis, actors and special features of the control of the intelligence services • Locating the causes of limited effectiveness of the PKGr • Parliamentary handling of control deficits • Formulating optimization recommendations The target groups • Docents and students of political and administrative science • Practitioners from the parliament and security authorities The author Andreas Friedel currently teaches and doctorates at the Chair of the University of Comparative Science of University of Regensburg (at present)

content.text: The Aesthetics of Media Landscape Structures: Theoretical Reflections and Empirical Findings. Simone Ines Linke describes the stereotype and strongly aestheticized construction of media landscapes and addresses the social implications of them. The author draws on geographical, philosophical and sociological perspectives and shows that media landscape structures are sometimes remarkably worked out and selected. Moreover, they are clearly different from existing landscape structures. Since media representations also assume a socializing function, these images can lead to an acceptance problem in relation to, for example, new energy landscapes. content.text: One question of trust: to media policy in print and online media in the run-up to the 2005 Bundestag election. Trust has become a key concept of the political system and political communication. The aim of the work is to find indicators of media-media confidence in political actors, especially top politicians, and to compare the communication of trust in print and online news contributions. This is done by analysing the content of the policy coverage of the topic complex "Confidentiality Question/New Elections" between May and July 2005. By analysing factors and deriving a regression model, it is demonstrated that media-media-media confidence in political actors is a multidimensional construct, which is determined by a number of reasons. These confidence dimensions include on the one hand classical credibility features such as competence and trustworthiness of the main actors, on the other hand features for low political confidence such as skepticism and cynicism, which mediate an article. As a reason for this trust, however, the evaluation of a major act, the extent of staging and symbolic action as well as the content of a statement of confidence can be identified. In the result, however, the conclusions of a print- media are already drawn back to a major act.

content.text: Seeing globality: for the visual construction of "world". Space photographs, CO2 infographics and world maps - they not only illustrate data, facts and contexts, but also create specific ideas about a world that is common to all people. Sebastian W. Hoggenmüller explores how they can achieve this, what ideas the world has in detail and what can be learned from those visual media of representation about concepts of globality and the structure of world society by means of a newly developed method of interpretative image analysis. His book opens up ways to see things that remain hidden from everyday vision. content.text: Insufficiently capable of producing difference in the teaching of inclusive school classes. What happens in inclusive teaching? How do teachers differentiate there? And what does this mean for the production of difference and inequality? The present poststructural ethnography reconstructs a central teaching differentiation of teachers. These regulate pupils along the difference sufficient ability vs. insufficient ability: Who can meet the requirements (assuming) is regulated to behave accordingly. Whoever cannot do so may deviate. Thus, it is established everyday who is unable/sufficiently capable of teaching. With the perspective of the Disability Studies it is clear: Universal expectations of ability also apply in "inclusive" teaching. They are the cause of the construction of insufficiently capable students and the basis for enabling them to legitimately deviate participation. At the same time, this permanent practice creates school obstruction.
content.title_en: Insufficient/sufficient : to produce difference in the teaching of inclusive school classes

content.text: Social inequality in flexibilised vocational training: extended skills requirements and milieu-specific adaptations in training associations. This is because, compared to traditional vocational training, teaching organisations place substantially higher demands on the self-organisation and flexibility of the learners. A sovereign approach to these requirements requires specific requirements and resources which are unequally distributed in social structure. Nevertheless, teaching organisations also offer the opportunity to reduce social inequality. The condition for this is that teaching organisations do not require the key competences, which are fundamental to the professional life, such as flexibility and self-organisation, as well as systematically imparting skills in training. In addition, framework conditions must be created, thanks to which the challenges of the combined training can be met even for students from less privileged background environments.
content.title_en: Social inequality in flexibilised vocational training: extended skills requirements and milieu-specific adaptations in training associations

content.text:
Utopia and politics : Potentials of creative policy-making.

The current real-political action is characterized by an unaltered state quo and a constant continuation of the status quo. While society is developing more and more rapidly technologically and economically, there is a lack of innovations in the political field. At the same time, political utopias as media of time criticism and alternative solutions for social misconduct are not given much attention in the political and political scientific debate. Ina-Maria Maahs, however, shows that utopian thinking as a way of thinking in possibilities exists today and offers hitherto unused potential for creative policy-making, which is innovative, sustainable and common-interest oriented.
content.title_en: Utopia and politics : potentials of creative policy-making

content.text:
The palm oil boom in Indonesia: the political economy of a competitive resource.

What do hand cream, frozen pizza and detergents have in common? Right: they contain palm oil - like half of all supermarket products. But what triggered the breathtaking palm oil boom with its devastating social and ecological consequences in the producing countries? Alina Brad examines the political and economic drivers that enabled Indonesia to become the world's leading palm oil producer. Starting from the historical and political economic conditions, it decodes the complex network of interests and conflicts over land control and valorization in the Indonesian palm oil sector.
content.title_en: The Palm Oil Boom in Indonesia: the Political Economy of a Repetitive Resource

content.text:
Protest tweets: a media linguistic investigation of street protests.

When people protest on the streets today, digital media is always involved. Whether for mobilization or coordination, for preparation or follow-up: protests are determined by the linguistic interactions and media practices of the participants. Mark Dang-Anh is dedicated to the situational protest communication in digital media with a focus on interactions in the microblogging service Twitter. Using two case studies of protests against right-wing marches, he analyses the multi-layered relations between language, media and social practice of protesting.
The work underlying the book was awarded the "Award of the University of Siegen for the promotion of young scientists, awarded by the Dirlmeier Foundation" in 2019.
content.title_en: Tweet protest: a media linguistic investigation of street protests

content.text:
About projections: World maps and world views: from reconstruction to deconstruction, from convention to alternative.

»About projections« gives insights into world maps, their modes of representation and the associated world views. The projection is presented on the one hand as an ideal projection in the sense of a world view, which describes prevailing images of ideas, values, principles of order, thinking or explanatory models of the world. On the other hand, the geometric projection underlying world maps is focused on: each world map faces the difficulty of depicting the sphere surface in a two-dimensional plane.
In a reconstruction, different paradigmatic world views are shown by world maps. In a deconstruction, conventional world maps are contrasted. The wide variety of possible world maps shows that world maps do not represent a status quo, but merely a subjective interpretation of the world at a given time, which remains subject to constant upheavals.
content.title_en: About projections: World maps and world views : from reconstruction to deconstruction, from convention to alternative

content.text: Behavioural economics and normativity: the limits of the information model in private law and its alternatives. Behavioural economics based regulation, from 'nudging' to 'debiasing', has long since reached Germany and Europe. However, the implications of behavioural economics for normative setting are not always as clear as they may appear at first glance: at empirical level, there is uncertainty about the actual degree of rationality of market actors; at a normative level, uncertainty about which legal policy objectives should be pursued with the help of the new techniques.Philipp Hacker takes on these challenges, theoretically explains the relevance of behavioural economics for private law and makes itself strong for their use in increasing fairness in market contexts, especially in consumer and capital markets law. On this basis, the information model, the central European regulatory paradigm, is experiencing a new concept. People make mistakes, for example in purchase or investment decisions. Novel strategies of regulation seek to the rule on the impossible.
content.title_en: Behavioural economics and normativity: the limits of the information model in private law and its alternatives

content.text:
Anarchist clockmakers in Switzerland: microhistoric global history at the beginning of the anarchist movement in the 19th century.

Why did watchmakers in the Valley of Saint-Imier in Switzerland become anarchist? Explanations are provided by the perspective of 'modern globalization': Like the world economy, anarchism emerged from global communication, transport, finance and migration flows of the second half of the 19th century - but as an alternative to nationalism and capitalism.
With the investigation of Florian Eitel, a historical study of the influential anarchist Jura Federation was dedicated for the first time in 40 years. Previously, nameless members of this organization are out of the shadow of well-known revolutionaries such as Mikhail Alexandrovich Bakunin and Pjotr Alexeyevich Kropotkin. The microhistoric global history analyses how a globally active political movement emerged and worked.

Anarchical clockmakers as alternative globalizers: a book about the atmosphere to establish a new world order.
content.title_en: Anarchist watchmakers in Switzerland : microhistoric global history at the beginning of the anarchist movement in the 19th century

content.text: Linguistic interpretation of visual contents via deep learning. The main part of this work is to develop deep learning (DL) models for the linguistic interpretation of visual content. This part is structured into two research problems: interactive segmentation and captioning of regions and selective texture labeling. To solve the first task, a new hybrid DL architecture was presented, where the user can click on any region of an image that is to be automatically segmented and described in language. The new model changes the boundary box indications of the standard object localization process with the output of an interactive, deep learning-based segmentation module. In this way, a better result for the captioning is achieved and object segmentation is also improved. In the second part of the new developments, a reciprocal correlation between DL-based texture representation on the one hand and its linguistic description is produced by a new, special construction of neural networks. This novel, hybrid CNN-RNN model enables a so-called texture-end description ...
content.title_en: Linguistic interpretation of visual contents via Deep Learning
