content.text: Work-Parts Order Processing in the Transport Chain: Inter-company Systems in the Sea and Air Freight. Katrin Coleman deals with the potential and challenges of different order processing systems in the transport chain. The focus is on the cross-company, system-side integration, i.e. how IS technologies are used by the actors in the transport chain in order processing, which can be improved in the application of process efficiency and why advantageous IS technologies only slowly prevail. To this end, the work-part-time processing of transport orders is examined by means of expert interviews and a simulation study. Implications for research and practice arise from the perspectives of sea and air cargo as well as from the internal and cross-company insights of the application-oriented empirical analysis. The content Status quo and development trends of order processing systems Asynchronous order processing in the Sea Freight Synchronous order processing in the air cargo target groups Dozierende and students of the economic sciences with focus on logistics, supply chain management, business management and executives in the areas of logistics, supply management, business management and business management of the University of Darmstadt.

content.text: The Left: Interpretation patterns of the regional elite in Thuringian electoral strongholds compared to the CDU: a qualitative study. Recapitulating the question was the following: Are there interpretation patterns or resulting approaches of the politicians, which can explain the success of the party? Do those differ between the different levels (Landtag, mayor), strongholds or the party? It was based on the assumption that the attitudes of the politicians, how one exercises politics or how questions of content are evaluated, influence the success of the respective persons and thus on the party. Not only the structure of the party with its basic program shapes the political interpretation culture, but especially at the municipal and state level the interpretation patterns of the individual successful politicians are decisive. In this regard, the interpretation patterns of the left respondents were tried to distinguish from those of the CDU politicians and to illustrate this by the formation of types.
content.title_en: The Left: Interpretation patterns of the regional elite in Thuringian electoral strongholds compared to the CDU: a qualitative study

content.text: The electrolysis principle was investigated for the determination of low moisture levels and the use of ionic liquids as a novel sensor coating. Humidity, whether material or gas humidity, is an important measure in the quality assessment of plastics, agricultural products, energy sources, pharmaceuticals, industrial and medically used gases. Therefore, there is an interest in continuously improving moisture metering in terms of precision, repeatability, traceability and stability. A proven measurement principle for this task was developed by Keidel in 1959 and is based on the absorption and electrolysis of water vapour. The simple structure of this principle consists of a sensor element, a DC voltage source, a digital multimeter and a controlled gas flow over the sensor. According to the Faraday law of electrolysis, the charge quantity with the electrolysed water mass was correlated with the measurement principle. However, in today's time it is necessary to validate the sensors because by targeted miniaturization less active area is available and thus Faraday's law is not fully applicable. In this work, coulometric sensors with a planarized water mass was examined in terms of the liquid coating.
content.title_en: Investigation of the electrolysis principle for the determination of low moisture levels and the use of ionic liquids as a novel sensor coating

content.text: Studies on the use of polyelectrolytes and polymediators in organic electrosynthesis. In connection with the separation problem resulting from the use of lead salts and mediators, the applicability of soluble polyelectrolytes and polymediators was investigated. Based on the TEMPO-mediated conversion of alcohols into carbonyl compounds as a model reaction, it was demonstrated that polymethacrylates can efficiently fulfil their purpose. Alcohol oxidation is also highly efficient in the preparative scale, whereby the polymer-based approach allows the separation of mediator and lead salt in a single membrane filtration step.
content.title_en: Studies on the use of polyelectrolytes and polymediators in organic electrosynthesis

content.text: NMR spectroscopic studies of solutions of polar substances in ionic liquids. The core of the work are interactions in ionic liquids with and without the addition of solvents. Among other things, aprotic ionic liquids with the ethyl-3-methyl-imidazoleium ([C2mim]+) cation were investigated, in which two different configurations were found for the arrangement of the molecules. Furthermore, it was shown that a method developed by Wendt and Farrar for the determination of quadrupole coupling constants also applies to the examined Ils and solvents in the liquid phase. Through these, the stokes-einsteins could be re-established for methanol in [C2mim][NTf2].
content.title_en: NMR spectroscopic investigations of solutions of polar substances in ionic liquids

content.text: The shift-off planning decision under provisional conditions: an epistemological investigation using the example of the NABEG regime. The federal planning, which is to be carried out in accordance with NABEG, must compile its decision bases under difficult conditions. In its epistemologically precarious environment, the guarantee of corridor permeability and the production of planning proportionality compete with each other. The work reconstructs a federal planning by the Federal Network Agency from the decision on the assessments made to the basis of the investigation. The example is set in relation to several epistemological approaches, which can be identified as requirements for the successful justification of a decision. The author worked as a scientific assistant in the area of spatial planning and environmental law (TU Dortmund, Faculty of Spatial Planning) from 2015-2018 and is currently in the service of a transmission network operator.
content.title_en: The shifting planning decision under provisional conditions : an epistemological investigation using the example of the NABEG regime

content.text: The bill of lading is also valid for the public utility company. In the context of the energy transition, the decentral electricity supply has become more and more important. Meanwhile, the bill of lading companies are also increasingly supplying their tenants with electricity. Tenants can be supplied with electricity using so-called tenant electricity models by housing companies. Electricity costs as part of the maintenance costs can be a significant burden. Therefore, both tenants and housing companies are interested in keeping their electricity infrastructure as customer facilities in accordance with § 3 No. 24a EnWG. The bill of lading company is mainly aimed at housing companies that are active in the free-financed and publicly funded housing. In order to offer tenants a favourable electricity price, this definition is defined by a variety of undetermined legal concepts, which makes it highly controversial in the literature and case law. The author deals with the definition of the customer's facility in a practical manner and illustrates a number of examples from the younger case-law, as well as the number of the number of customers.
content.title_en: The customer's facilities (electricity) with a particular focus on housing aspects

content.text: Legal regulation of product life : a contribution to sustainable product design. The purpose of this work is the lifetime of products as the regulatory object of the German and European legislators. Product life is an essential factor in limiting the negative environmental effects of products. Under this premise, the work shows possibilities for extending the lifetime of products by legal regulation, in order to allow consumers to consume products more sustainably. The study first addresses the impact of the current law on product life, both in civil law and in public law of product regulation. Building on the current law, it then develops strategies for the national and European legislator to promote the longevity of products by regulating.
content.title_en: Legal regulation of product life: a contribution to sustainable product design

content.text: The influence of the production conditions on the mechanical stability of asymmetric BSCF membranes for oxygen delivery. Oxygen – O2 is used for process intensiveization in many industrial sectors. In combustion processes, its use, for example, enables fuel savings, the reduction of CO2 and NO2 emissions and a highly efficient separation of CO2. Commercial O2 production processes are energy-intensive, e.g. a complex transport to the end customer is necessary. Mixed conductive ceramic MIEC membranes (Mixed Ionic Electronic Conductor) allow for an energy-efficient generation of pure O2 on site. The high investment costs represent a market entry barrier that could be lowered by reducing the membrane thickness or an increase in the O2 permeation. However, the low mechanical strength and reliability of the BSCF tube membranes (BSCF – Ba0.5Sr0.5Co0.8Fe0.2O3-δ) must be improved significantly in the context of an optimized production process.

content.text: The influence of the production conditions on the mechanical stability of asymmetric BSCF membranes for oxygen delivery. Oxygen – O2 is used for process intensiveization in many industrial sectors. In combustion processes, its use, for example, enables fuel savings, the reduction of CO2 and NO2 emissions and a highly efficient separation of CO2. Commercial O2 production processes are energy-intensive, e.g. a complex transport to the end customer is necessary. Mixed conductive ceramic MIEC membranes (Mixed Ionic Electronic Conductor) allow for an energy-efficient generation of pure O2 on site. The high investment costs represent a market entry barrier that could be lowered by reducing the membrane thickness or an increase in the O2 permeation. However, the low mechanical strength and reliability of the BSCF tube membranes (BSCF – Ba0.5Sr0.5Co0.8Fe0.2O3-δ) must be improved significantly in the context of an optimized production process.
content.title_en: Influence of the production conditions on the mechanical stability of asymmetrical BSCF membranes for oxygen delivery

content.text: The enhanced delivery of biologically active substances by tailor-made polymers. Polymer-based nanocarrier systems are considered as promising technology of modern nanomedicine, as their application creates new perspectives in the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of a wide range of diseases. Due to their high flexibility in their chemical composition, polymers can be individually adapted to the respective substance to be mediated and thus reliably and purposefully transported to the desired place of action. In order to exploit the full potential of this technology, a fundamental understanding of the chemical composition and structure-property relationship of the polymer at the molecular and cellular level is necessary. In this dissertation, new multi-component polymers were presented, which fulfil all the requirements for the transport of nucleic acids as well as for relevant pharmaceutical active substances. New insights into the polymer-mediated gene transport of plasmid DNA and siRNA were used in the process of poly(2-dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate (PDMAEMA) and poly(ethyleneimin) regarding the influence of amino-optimization are used.
content.title_en: The enhanced delivery of biologically active substances by tailor-made polymers

content.text: Emotional Infection in Technology-based Service Interactions: The Effect of Smileys on the Emotions of Customers. Katja Lohmann develops impact models that consider the influence of Smileys on the emotions of customers in the new service channels of computer-mediated communication and self-service technologies against the background of the process of emotional infection. content.text: New order of education: the management logic of regionalization in the German education system. Regionalization is one of the educational policy flagship projects in Germany. A systematic literature overview was compiled, then a structured evaluation of the respective study results and a combination of the findings contained therein by means of qualitative comparison. Evidence of moral concepts in relation to therapy forsaktion and therapy deprivation, aggressive analgesia, intentional killing (on request), medical aid for self-killing, sedation at the end of life and disclosure of diagnosis and/or prognosis at the end of life were examined. The clientele of the respective studies were active or were treated in East Asia, India, Israel, or the rest of the Middle East, in Puerto Rico or in the rest of the United States or Latin America. The systematic literature overview consists mostly on a quantitative evaluation of medical statements. The detailed structured results of work were used to make it easier to describe the subject.

content.text: The European regulation of audiovisual media services: coherence of the material scope of the AVMD Directive for hybrid online services against the background of media convergence.Audiovisual media services – European regulatory concept – Media regulation – delimitation problems – material scope – case law on videos on press websites – Regulatory alternatives for hybrid online mobile image services – opinion-forming relevance The European AVMD Directive, which also determines German media regulation, has been in a reform process since 2016.In particular, the material scope of the Directive does not meet the requirement of a legally secure distinction between services requiring regulation and services requiring non-regulation. content.text: Smart private video surveillance: the admissibility of intelligent video surveillance by non-public authorities in public spaces according to § 6b BDSG. The book deals with the question of the permissible use of so-called intelligent video surveillance systems by private individuals in public spaces on the scale of §6b BDSG a.F. . The author deals with the system-compliant interpretation based on the Basic Law, the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, the ECHR and the DSRL 95/46/EC as well as the case law of the respective constitutional jurisdictions. It shows that in a set of complex value decisions in view of the affected right to informational self-determination and the fundamental legal prohibitions of discrimination, differentiated individual cases must be taken along a set of criteria. The result developed on § 6b BDSG a. F. also exists before § 4 BDSG n. F. and the EU GDPR.
content.title_en: Smart private video surveillance : the admissibility of intelligent video surveillance by non-public authorities in public spaces according to § 6b BDSG

content.text: As the ongoing discussion on the introduction of measles vaccination is showing, there is almost always a conflict between the rights and interests of individuals and those of the entire population in questions of infection protection law. This work therefore deals with the question whether German infection protection law has succeeded in resolving this conflict. To this end, it is examined first which objectives the state can use in the field of health care to justify fundamental rights interventions, and then to examine the constitutionality of central infection protection standards based on this. In this context, the question is examined in particular whether and under which framework conditions the introduction of vaccination obligations is legally possible, as well as whether the general clauses contained in the infection protection law are constitutional in their current design.
content.title_en: Infection protection in the liberal rule of law

content.text: About the claim of illustrators in literary book illustration: A discursive and practice-based study. The term illustration seems to have a mismatch between scientific reception and practical subject matter. Traditionally, the term illustration refers to an image that visually repeats a pre-textual content and doubles it in a picture. Traditional illustration thus calls a secondary image, explicitly dependent on another content, which could also be omitted without the content being lost. Today, this traditional illustration concept is used among other things in the research fields of art history, image science and literature. From the perceptives of practice, the traditional illustration concept contains a fundamental problem. He tries to describe with a static definition an extremely lively visual phenomenon of our time. Professional career planners, the so-called illustrators, today create works that are no longer descriptive with the traditional illustration concept. More still, the traditional illustration concept blindly makes them more difficult to describe these developments, which therefore cast a pre-image on the contemporary discourse.
content.title_en: About the claim of illustrators in literary book illustrations : A discursive and practice-based study

content.text: Data power in antitrust abuse control. The ever-increasing relevance of online platforms has led to data being of outstanding importance for competition. In the age of big data, data enables a quality and innovation competition. At the same time, potentials that threaten competition are associated with a data power. This raises numerous new legal questions regarding the treatment of a data power in antitrust abuse control.The work examines the impact of a data power on antitrust abuse control by referring to the prominent procedure of the Federal Cartel Office against Facebook. In this process, it is examined whether and in which form data protection aspects can and should be taken into account when applying abuse control.The work provides an overview of the antitrust risks of a data power and leads to a clarification of the relationship between antitrust law and data protection law.
content.title_en: Data power in antitrust abuse control

content.text: Access of the largest seagoing vessels to the port of Hamburg? : an investigation into the adaptation of the Elbe's navigation channels, taking into account § 12 para. 4 WaStrG. Can Hamburg demand an expansion of the Elbe on a legal basis compared with the federal government? In 1921/1922 the German Reich committed itself to the acquisition of expansion measures for the accessibility of the port of Hamburg for "the largest seagoing vessels". The present work proves that this obligation to refer to § 12 para. 4 WaStrG today meets the Federal Republic of Germany, thereby correspondingly a subjective public law of Hamburg based on the norm of protection. The scope of this synallagmatic relationship is the prioritization of the port of Hamburg in the planning of water road development needs of the federal government. In order to better take account of the subjective position of Hamburg as a legal entity, it is proposed to evaluate the role of the Hansestadt in the planning process of establishing plans by participating in a water construction company which can be transferred to the project management.
content.title_en: Access of the largest seagoing vessels to the port of Hamburg? : an investigation into the navigational channel adaptations of the Elbe, with special consideration of § 12 para. 4 WaStrG

content.text: Uninformative information: Information transfer as misleading leitmetapher of the information society. The misleading technological metaphor of information transmission implies paradoxically uninformative information: Information can be transmitted just as little as a flu can be sweated out. This is opposed to an information concept associated with knowledge and understanding: Informative becomes something not because of something transmitted, but in relation to interests and skills of interpretive beings. Jakob Krebs shows: Only a relational specific concept of informationivity allows an extensive analysis of our epistemic self-understanding in the information society. This conceptual reconstruction is not only relevant to science, but also important for all practices of communication, learning and teaching.
content.title_en: Uninformative information: information transfer as misleading information society leaders

content.text: From passive land use planning to active soil policy: the effectiveness of soil policy instruments using food-discounters. The "Galmiz Problem" of spatial planning -- State of Soil Policy Research -- Theoretical Assumptions on the Effect of Soil Policy -- Food-Discounter as an Investigation Unit -- Screening of the Institutional Soil Regime -- Findings on the Mechanism of Impact of Active Soil Policy -- Conclusions on Effectiveness of Soil Policy Andreas Hengstermann uses the example of food-discounters to investigate the effectiveness of active soil policy in comparison to traditional, passive soil policy planning and shows which approach contributes more to managing spatial development. The content ■ The "Galmiz Problem" of spatial planning is based on the current change in the Swiss planning system and is transferred into an empirically investigated research design. The choice of discounter-discounts as an active soil policy indicator enables comparable and meaningful conclusions to the effectiveness of soil policy strategies of public planning operators.

content.text: The electric drive system is designed to increase the reliability of electric drives by using the example of electromechanical power steering. Requirements for a fault-tolerant electromechanically supported steering system -- Conception of a fault-tolerant electric drive -- Validation of a new EPS drive architecture -- Comfort-optimized operation after errors Nick Trmummel addresses current challenges in the field of electric steering drives, such as the substitution of hydraulics, the realization and protection of (partial) automated driving states as well as the high integration of mechatronic systems, and addresses three aspects to increase their reliability. Driving experiments, a study of a subject and analytical methods enable the author to define a permissible degradation of electric drives. From the requirement analysis, he derives a fault-tolerant drive architecture and verifies it by means of test and simulation-based fault analysis. The third aspect of his investigations is the examination with suitable operating strategies for fault-laden drives.
content.title_en: Increasing reliability of electric drives using the example of electromechanical power steering

content.text: The European identity and media effects in the European debate are largely overlooked by the European Union's policy of European identity and its policy of European identity. The European Union (EU) is a political and economic union of 28 Member States with more than 500 million inhabitants whose legal existence and further integration depend on whether their citizens have a sense of collective European identity. The literature on this topic suggests that the media play a crucial role in ensuring that people get a sense of collective identification. Accordingly, the main objective of this thesis is to analyse the direct media impact on the European identity of people. The main empirical question of the study is: What impact do the media have on European identity? This work deals with this relevant question by analysing the theoretically sound relationship between the European identity and the different effects of the media in different contexts. The study is based on the social identity theory (SIT) and the results of the results of social psychologists who think of European identity in a concept that reflects the subjective allocation of an individual to a collective and its affective and over-emphasis of this collective. The results of the study show that the EU's positive identity is also reflected in different ways of being informed by the European identity.
content.title_en: European identity and media effects : a quantitative comparative analysis

content.text: Robot journalism. Starting with Rudolf Augstein's word, "say what is," the author examines whether the legal standards change when an algorithm says what is, and not directly a human being. The work is aimed at communication and legal scientists, but also at journalists and software companies who program journalism bots. In addition to problem solving for robot journalism, such as liability, imputation, transparency, and whether and to what extent it is sufficient for copyright protection of computer-generated texts to "plant a copyright seed" – a software whose output – a journalistic text – cannot be absolutely foreseen by humans, the author also addresses fundamental questions of (media) constitutional law. This includes the introduction of the principle of diversity of opinion as an independent constitutional principle, which stands alongside (media) fundamental rights with an independent guarantee content ("media diversity law").
content.title_en: Robot journalism

content.text: Digital market power. The growing influence of the 21st century internet platforms in economic, social and political terms has triggered a discussion on the appropriate regulation of these corporations. At the heart of this debate is antitrust law – the legal area created for controlling dominant companies. The definition of the concept of dominant position, which is fundamental to antitrust law, is faced with numerous challenges in the application of law to internet platforms, from the unremunerability of services to the multi-facetedness of business models. The present work disassembles the concept of dominant position in its parts and shows how the methodology needs to be adapted to the digital economy. This is done with the understanding of the legal economy and the legal systems of Germany, the European Union and the USA.
content.title_en: Digital market power

content.text: The use of copyright protected works. The present study deals with the phenomenon of mutual expression and the challenges of copyright law. The approaches examined show how copyright should meet these challenges in the future and thus in particular its economic function.The main focus is on the extensive interpretation of existing legal provisions of Swiss copyright law such as the parody barrier and the citation barrier. On the other hand, possible solutions are outlined and assessed de lege ferenda. A barrier for creative works is in the foreground. The author shows how the law should meet these challenges in the future.

content.text: Understanding support in literature teaching: theoretical and empirical foundation of a literary didactic task orientation. Regulatory ideas and tasks -- Tasks and understanding support -- Study on the effect of tasks with support Michael Steinmetz explains theoretically and empirically the thesis that literary text understanding in German teaching should be modelled more by tasks with support. Using an empirical study (two-group plan with repeat of measurement), the author shows that tasks with support favour the understanding and learning experience of the learners more than open tasks. Thus, a task-oriented literature teaching should – according to the author's plea – understand support as a core component of literature-related learning and teaching.The content Regulative ideas and tasks Tasks and understanding support Study on the effect of tasks with support The target groups Dozierende und Studierende der Fachbereiche Lehramt Deutsch (aller Schulständer), Literaturdidaktik, Germanik Forschende, Deutschlehrer und -lehrinnen Der Autor Dr. phil. habil. Michael Steinmetz ist Vertragsprofes für Deutschen Sprache und ihrenden Kulturen Giertik, Lehrebniskompetenz, Lehrheiten, Die Diesprachetik der Literaturstuellierungen, Die Weinschaftenheiten.
content.title_en: Understanding support in literature lessons : theoretical and empirical foundation of a literary didactic task orientation

content.text: In the context of the entrepreneurial challenge: a process model for risk optimization in the founding context. Success and failure are essential components of a functioning founding landscape. An understanding of the management process of challenges as well as entrepreneurial failures in the founding process is therefore necessary. For this reason, Alexander Goebel develops the process model for dealing with entrepreneurial challenges, which can be used as a procedure for evaluating individual, organizational and social opportunities and dangers. With the possibility of targeted reduction of obstacles as well as the promotion of resources and action schemes, it also provides valuable impulses for the design of a sustainable founding ecosystem. The content challenges in the founding process Failure of business start-ups: Consequences and coping The process model for dealing with entrepreneurial challenges Implications for research and practice The target groups lecturers and students of the departments Psychology, Business Sciences and Entrepreneurship Founders, Investors, Consultants, Policymakers etc. The author Dr. Alexander Goebel studied psychology and business sciences at the Friedrich Schiller University Jena and is a PhD in the Chair of Business, Business and Organizational Psychology.
content.title_en: Entrepreneurial challenges: a process model for risk optimization in the context of start-up

content.text: The costs of flight noise: price reductions of real estate and health costs in the surroundings of Vienna Airport. Birgit Schmidt deals in this book with the monetary consequences that an airport – here Vienna Airport – imposes on its environment. The focus is on price reductions for residential real estate, health costs and willingness to pay for the prevention of flight noise.The economic procedures used for this purpose are explained in detail and the author shows in a comparison how these external costs are differently taxed from the point of view of the population and from the point of view of the polluter.The content of the willingness to pay for the prevention of flight noise events Impact of flight noise on prices of residential real estates Flight noise induced health costs Costs of an infrastructure project External costs of aircraft operations The target groups Dozierde and students of the departments Infrastructure Economics, Finance Sciences and Spatial Planning Real estate experts, brokers and professionals in financing institutions and financial authorities The author Birgit Schmidt was a long-standing bank employee and carried out self-responsible activities in the field of property assessment. She completed her doctorate at the Department of Finance and Infrastructure Policy (IFIP) at the Institute for Spatial Planning at Vienna, Vienna, Austria.
content.title_en: The cost of air noise: price reductions of real estate and health costs in the vicinity of Vienna Airport

content.text: Liability for gas supply disruptions: A comparative analysis of German and Ukrainian law taking into account Russian law. Actors in the German gas supply system and liability bases for gas supply disruptions -- The reform of the Ukrainian gas sector from 2015 -- Relationship between contractual and non-contractual liability in Ukrainian law Natalia Ishyna deals with liability for gas supply disruptions, in particular for supply bottlenecks and for the supply of defective gas quality. This is done by comparing the legal status of these German and Ukrainian standards regulating the research subject matter with regard to Russian law. In a first step, the various solutions to the settlement of the liability issue in Germany and Ukraine are presented in detail to affected end customers in country reports. The author for the first time clearly structured the current legal status in the area of Ukrainian law for the German reader. In a second step, the determined results of the legal application are compared and based on their effects are assessed.
content.title_en: Liability for gas supply disruptions : A comparative analysis of German and Ukrainian law taking into account Russian law

content.text: The mentoring system Race Trainer: Concept for semi-automatic driver training. Analysis of cooperative FAS -- Concept for mentoring systems -- Planning adaptation in longitudinal and cross-planning -- Intervention dominance in cooperative driving dynamics control -- Implementation in the research vehicle Race Trainer Samuel Schacher is concerned with the development of a driver assistance system (FAS), which is intended to teach driving on race tracks through active interventions in steering and drivetrain. The close interaction between driver and FAS presents its design with new challenges. To solve this, a holistic concept for the development of cooperative FAS was developed, which the vehicle is considered a virtual mentor for humans. For this purpose, design possibilities for cooperative FAS are developed, new approaches are presented, such as the consideration of different types of cooperation and a concrete implementation are shown. Furthermore, contradictory requirements for the control engineering design are studied by the introduction of a situationally adaptable concept for "Mentorensysteme" research technology.

content.text: Analysis of the relationships between the beam force method and optical and hydraulic diagnostic methods of diesel injectors. Structure of the measuring systems used -- Requirements for the comparability of the presented measurement techniques -- Beam power as an extension to the hydraulic and optical analysis Hans Römisch for the first time completely analyses the transferability of beam force measurements to images in the Mie-Streulicht and Schlieren-Messungen as well as to hydraulic quantity and rate measurements. He defines prerequisites for the hydraulic connection of the injector and its control. In addition to establishing new evaluation routines, the author can show that the use of conventional impeller elements leads to a larger measurement error than previously assumed. This is avoided by a novel geometry of the impeller elements. The content Structure of the used measurement systems Prerequisites for the comparability of the presented measurement techniques Beam power as an extension to the hydraulic and optical analysis The target groups Dozierde and students of the automotive technology, in particular the departments of combustion engines and injection diagnostics Engineers in the execution of injection analyses with OEMs and suppliers The author Hans Römisch has currently worked at the Chair for vehicle drives of the University of Stuttgart as an application

content.text: The U-efficient resource management for continuous scenario fulfillment by UAV fleets. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) are autonomously flying and flexible mobile robots that offer many possibilities due to their great flexibility and expandability. Especially in the field of disaster management, they are becoming increasingly important, as the tasks for education in the area and for the creation of a communication infrastructure can be dealt with unbound and quickly by them. The research focus of this work lies in the challenge of resource management in such a scenario. While the priority of UAV deployment clearly consists in supporting the disaster control without interruption, must also be addressed the management of limited resources, such as electrical energy. We present a corresponding system design of a resource management and strategies to improve the performance and thus increase the energy efficiency of the overall system. The implementation and thorough investigation of such a complex system of subsystems is associated with high financial costs, great test risk and a long development period. For this reason, tri-extended and executable configuration of the UAV's environment and operational simulation is presented in the context of the UAV's continuous configuration.
content.title_en: Energy-efficient resource management for continuous scenario fulfillment by UAV fleets

content.text: Evergreening: Requirements for patentability in German, European and Indian patent law. Evergreening is understood as such patenting strategies in terms of pharmaceutical inventions, with which drug manufacturers effectively extend patent protection for a starting substance by developing derivatives. These are often variations of already patented medicinal products that are only filed at the end of the initial invention. In return for the obligation under the TRIPS Convention to introduce the protection of substance inventions, the Indian legislator has opted for a regulation that excludes further developments with low innovation value from patent protection. The work compares the interpretation of patentability requirements based on the PatG, the EPC and the Indian Patents Act, takes a position on the discussion on TRIPS compatibility of Indian regulations and analyses the reasons for choosing the respective regulatory context for price controls in the health sector.
content.title_en: Evergreening : Requirements for patentability in German, European and Indian patent law

content.text: Studies on the influence of rectangular z-pins on the mechanical properties of hot-curing fiber-reinforced plastics under quasi-static and vibrating loads. Classic fiber composite plastics are susceptible to the formation of cracks between the fibre layers, for example due to shock-like loads. The insertion of z-pins into the material is a proven method of counteracting the low interlaminar crack toughness of these materials. The dissertation's content is the examination of the influence of rectangular z-pins on the microstructure as well as the mechanical properties of hot-curing CFK-laminates under quasi-static and vibrating loads and the comparison of the results obtained with circular z-pins.
content.title_en: Investigations on the influence of rectangular z-pins on the mechanical properties of hot-curing fiber-reinforced plastics under quasi-static and vibrating loads

content.text: Static and dynamic analysis of multi-component sensors for forces and moments. The measurement of forces and moments is widely used in mechanical measurement technology. However, this typically only determines the amount of a force or moment vector in a given direction. However, since forces and moments are vectorial quantities, such measurement represents a significant reduction in the size to be measured. Multi-component sensors that can detect forces or moments spatially are common in various areas, but many questions are open when calibrating these sensors, especially when implementing calibration. In this work, a current procedure is to be optimized for the static calibration of multi-component sensors and a procedure available for dynamic calibration is to be developed. To this end, for the first time, classical mechanical calibration processes are extended by optical measuring systems based on the principle of near range photogrammetry. In the dynamic case, further information about the measurement sequence is to be collected which improve the results of calibration. In the static case, the improvement aims at reducing measurement uncertainty in the calibration device and determining the deformation of the sensor is to be made possible for the first time by means of photogrammetrically measuring the reference vectors with six degrees of freedom.
content.title_en: Static and dynamic analysis of multi-component sensors for forces and moments

content.text: From monomer to glycopolymer: application as biofunctionalities on surfaces and as transport molecules. Glycopolymers are synthetic and naturally occurring polymers that carry a glyco-unit in the side chain of the polymer. Glycans are responsible for many biological processes due to the Glykan-protein interaction. The involvement of the Glycans in these biological processes enables the imitating and analyzing of the interactions by suitable model compounds, e.g. glycopolymers. This system of Glykan-protein interaction is to be investigated and studied by the Glycopolymers to demonstrate the specific and selective binding of the proteins to the glycopolymers. The proteins that are capable of selectively binding carbon hydrate structures are called lectins. In this dissertation various glycopolymers were synthesized. Various glycopolymers should be considered for an efficient and cost-effective synthesis route. Various glycopolymers were produced by functionalized monomers with different sugars, such as mannosis, lactose, galactose or N-aceyl.
content.title_en: From monomer to glycopolymer : application as biofunctionalities on surfaces and as transport molecules

content.text: Development of new starch derivatives for use as water-based filmformers in paints and varnishes. In recent decades, the coating industry has also been re-thinking about environmentally friendly paints and varnishes. However, new solutions are not usually based on biopolymers and in an even smaller proportion on water-based coating systems made of renewable raw materials. This is the starting point of this work, in which it was examined whether the biopolymer starch has the potential to be water-based filmformers for paints and varnishes. In this respect, the following criteria must be met, based on established synthetic market products: The aqueous dispersion must have at least a 30% solid content, can be processed at room temperature and viscosities between 10^2-10^3 mPa·s. The final coating must form a closed film and possess very good adhesion strengths to a specific surface, in this work glass. As a basis for modifying the starch a combination of molecular degradation and chemical functionalization was selected. As it was not known what influence the starch type, the chosen degradation reaction as well as various substitutes could be investigated on the structural properties.
content.title_en: Development of new starch derivatives for use as water-based filmformers in paints and varnishes

content.text: Combination of fluorescence microscopy and scanning force microscopy to investigate physiological processes in living cells: characterization and application of a novel local micromanipulation technique. Within this thesis, a novel micromanipulation technique for local fluid release on the complex gland tissue of the P. americana cockroach was characterized and used for the targeted manipulation of individual cells in a cell complex (tissue). This micromanipulation technique is the nanofluidic scanning force microscopy (FluidFM = fluidic force microscopy) known since 2009, using very small microcanal scanning force peaks or micro/nanopipettes with an opening between 300 nm and 2 μm, which allows very small volumes to be delivered in the picoliter to femtoliter range (10-12 L – 10-15 L) and precisely to the location. The aim of this work was to analyse cellular processes, such as cell-cell communication or signal transmission, using a high-level of fluorescence microscology and a high-level of cell microscopy.
content.title_en: Combination of fluorescence microscopy and scanning force microscopy to investigate physiological processes in living cells : characterization and application of a novel local micromanipulation technique

content.text: Hexanuclear cluster compounds of the metals zirconium and hafnium: new, optimized synthesis pathways at low temperatures. This paper examines the formation of M6 cluster compounds of the metals Zr and Hf with a combination of DSC and XRD (cluster harvesting). The exchange of the oxidant against PbCl2 enables the synthesis of the cluster compounds already at 490 °C in large quantities using ampoules from low-cost stainless steel. By subsequent extraction in MeCN a number of known and unknown compounds could be isolated. Furthermore, the use of Lewis acid ILs at Hf leads to the formation of a nine-core cluster, which represents a new cluster type.
content.title_en: Hexanuclear cluster compounds of metals zirconium and hafnium : new, optimized synthesis pathways at low temperatures

content.text: The Global Conflict and Conflicts in the Land: The Protests against Industrial Mines and Agricultural Industrial Projects in Senegal. Louisa Prause compares protests against large-scale land acquisitions for the development of industrial mines and agricultural industrial projects. It shows similarities and differences between conflicts over land in these two sectors and identifies the central mechanisms through which the purpose of land's appropriation affects protests, using two cases in Senegal. This book provides new insights into factors of influence on conflicts over the appropriation of land and links to political practices regarding challenges of cross-sectoral alliances. content.text: Customer engagement through barrier-free online communication: potential and added value of the expanded market orientation strategy. In order to achieve the implementation, the language and the communication media must be designed in such a way that they can be usable and understandable for all potential customers. This is called barrier-free communication. Easy access and the comprehensibility of texts and media are not given much attention in the companies so far. content.text: Relational framework: The use of a relational perspective on migration in adult education research. »All that is is relationship, and everything that is not is also relationship.« With this apodictic sharpening, philosopher Julius Jakob Schaaf outlined fifty years ago what is becoming increasingly evident today as a relational turn in epistemology of knowledge. The present study acknowledges Schaaf's sophisticated philosophical design and unfolds his program: away from classical-Abendish thought of substance and identity towards an epistemology of relationality. Building on this, the author develops the method of relational framework. This no longer claims that an object can be defined and thus released from its context. Instead, it makes its relationships visible and emphasizes plurality, contingency and difference. Empirical research can benefit from such scientific theoretical reflection. The example of migration research in adult education illustrates how a relational perspective intervenes in the process of cognition – against limiting attributions, in favor of covert development possibilities.
content.title_en: Relational frame : Using a relational perspective on migration in adult education research

The stability of the extract was demonstrated in a batch and a continuous mode. Therefore, it was possible to apply the technique for the separation of sensitive feedstocks.
content.title_en: Development of a surfactant-based in situ extraction from authentic feedstocks

content.text: The "News Point for the Orient" in the context of global interdependence (1914-1921) : Structures - Actors - Discourses. The political interest in Germany in Islam originated in the First World War, when the Empire, together with the Ottoman Empire, sought to "revolution" the Islamic world against the Entente powers. A central organization in the field of jihadization and war propaganda was the "News Point for the Orient" founded in 1914. With the re-contextualization of this institution, including pre-war and colonial history, and the agency of individual actors, Samuel Krug succeeded in liberating the history of the News Point for the Orient from the narrative of failure as a war and propaganda instrument and revealing an exciting history of global networks and discourses.
content.title_en: The "News Point for the Orient" in the context of global interdependence (1914-1921) : Structures - Actors - Discourses

content.text: The European International Family Law grants the parties freedom of choice. However, there is a risk that they may choose a right which contradicts their own interests. Therefore, the question arises whether party autonomy is a mere formal principle or a material core. On the basis of a material understanding of freedom of choice, the Rome III Regulation, the Goods Law Regulations and the Hague Maintenance Protocol are examined whether they meet the requirements for the protection of the freedom of decision of weaker parties. The investigation ranges from generalized protection instruments such as the limitation of choice through form rules to flexible effectiveness controls in individual cases. At the same time, the materialization of party autonomy serves as an example of the materialization of conflict law and the law in general. Parties in European International Family Law are required to decide freely which law they use, even though they are a danger that this could be against the best interests. So and what the freedom of the profession?
content.title_en: Materialisation of choice of law in international family law: the importance of the protection of the weaker in European conflict of laws

content.text: The Reformation in Brandenburg is considered as a model example of a supremely initiated and controlled princely reformation in a north-eastern German territorial state. Therefore, for a long time the actions and motives of the state rule have united the attention of the Brandenburg Reformation history research. Felix Engel expands this rather narrow horizon by incorporating the perspective "from below" into his consideration and systematically exploring which means and paths were open to the urban actors to different phases of the Reformation process in order to actively influence the transformation of their communal church systems. Therefore, both the structural and ideal preconditions as well as the Reformation processes are taken into account. Afterwards, continuitys and fractures as well as the scope for action of the protagonists involved are analyzed in central areas of the urban church system.
content.title_en: City and Reformation in the Mark Brandenburg

content.text: The prohibition of preconceptional sex choice: an empirical and constitutional analysis. The desire for the determination of the sex of one's own children is not a new phenomenon, but deeply rooted in the history of humanity. The Embryo Protection Act fails to recognise this gender desire of potential parents. The artificial fertilization of an egg with gender-selected sperm is basically punishable. Exceptions to this are narrowly limited. Whether this can be justified constitutionally the present work examines. In this context, the ethical and social policy arguments against the sex choice are first translated into constitutional categories. The accepted arguments are then analyzed in the light of fundamental legal dogma and also supplemented by a study carried out specifically.
content.title_en: The prohibition of preconceptional sex choice: an empirical and constitutional analysis

This work explains the development, implementation and evaluation of methods to address deficiencies in hydrological numerical modelling of local drainage measures in dust-influenced meso-scale catchments. The need arises among other things from the demand for analysis of the effectiveness of adaptation measures to reduce flooding on regional scale. Fixed deficiencies in current numerical models include (1) a required flexible spatial-time resolution, (2) a physical-based parametrization, (3) hydrological methods to model backflow effects and (4) approaches to generating hydrological drainage measures the development, implementation and evaluation of methods to overcome limits in the hydrological modelling of local noise measurement.

content.text: Party communication in the age of social media: an empirical study of Facebook use by the circle associations of the German parties. What about the presence of the local party associations on the social web? Do parties also benefit social media in the training field of democracy? The investigation answers these questions on the basis of a comprehensive dataset, which is fed from survey and mass data (Big Data). By developing and examining a complex explanation model, central use reasons are identified. The results indicate that most circle associations are present on the social web. In addition to Facebook, WhatsApp, Twitter and YouTube are mainly used. A central use motive results from the desire to meet the expectations of their own members. Furthermore, social media at the circle level seem to be used for campaign purposes and due to a general mistrust in the reporting of the classical mass media. It is striking that in particular the municipal basis of the AfD seems to be extremely successful in the use of the new media.
content.title_en: Party communication in the age of social media: an empirical study of the use of Facebook by the circle associations of the German parties

content.text: Performative figures queer masculinity: a media history of film and cinema in Germany until 1945. Kaiserreich/Germany – film and cinema, gender and sexuality -- Weimar Republic/Germany – film and cinema, gender and sexuality -- National Socialism/Germany – film and cinema, gender and sexuality. The work on media culture is a German cinema and film history from the 1890s to 1945 with a focus on queer masculinity. With media-scientific approaches, the study shows how the ‘new medium' film is constituted by performative re-perceptions of spectacular elements from the entertainment and knowledge cultures of the 19th century. In this, bodies, desires and identities are constantly remodeled through differences. Male queerness therefore does not mean representation of male homosexuality. Rather, it is dynamic result of complex media processes, in combination with affect and (self-)knowledge on and before the screen.
content.title_en: Performative figures queer masculinity : a media story of film and cinema in Germany until 1945

content.text: The function of the collective agreement. The function of the collective agreement is one of the most dazzling terms of collective agreement law. It is often and gladly endeavoured to justify the extension of the regulatory effect of the collective agreement beyond the member's area. However, even after its legal standardization in § 1 AEntG and § 4a para. 1 TVG, this function of the collective agreement remains controversial and unclear in its legal content. Daniel Holler therefore accepts the question of this function of the collective agreement. In his legal dogmatic investigation, the function is legally analyzed, structured and inserted into the existing private law system. He not only proves that the function of the collective agreement is severely limited, but also establishes relations to current practical legal problems.
content.title_en: The order function of the collective agreement

content.text: Intersubjectivity, social exclusion and the problem of the border: The dialectic of the individual and society. Intersubjective encounter is the nucleus for social meaningfulness in culture and society. In modern times, however, a break of this emotional coupling between people develops – through social exclusion, discrimination and reification. Using an inter- and transdisciplinary approach, in which a theory of emotions is at the centre, Steffen's forms of social exclusion are examined as a break in the interpersonal and asks how a change in intersubjective forms of encounter is possible. He calls for a new culture of "in-relationship-treating" with the aim of a social transformation towards social justice. To this end, he combines numerous scientific discourses in the concept of the border, which deal with interpersonal interactions and their effects on psyche and culture.
content.title_en: Intersubjectivity, social exclusion and the problem of the border : The dialectics of the individual and society

content.text: The consideration of non-competitive interests in merger control: Considerations on the need for reform of the ministerial permit under § 42 GWB. The ministerial permit under § 42 GWB has always been a controversial legislative instrument with which the company can approve a merger despite competitive concerns, provided that "overall economic advantages" or "superior interests of the general public outweigh the identified disadvantages. The investigation is extensively conducted by the ministerial permit procedure. One focus is on the innovations made in the context of the 9th GWB novelle. The question is examined whether the institute needs a comprehensive reform of the ministerial permit or whether point-by-point changes are more targeted. To this end, proposals for amendments from politics and science are examined. The work shows that despite existing dangers there is still a need for the exception of non-competitive interests in merger control and the rule represents a necessary corrective of pure competition.
content.title_en: The consideration of non-competitive interests in merger control : considerations on the need for reform of the ministerial permit under § 42 GWB

content.text: Traditional progress: the Stuttgart Court Theatre, the electric modern and the big city (1851-1912). The study on the Stuttgart Court Theatre is thinking theatre and city together during electrification around 1900. What influence did theatre technology have on the growing city? How was the theatre influenced by urbanization? The study examines new spatial-material networks as well as collective urban imaginations that began to arise in the planning of a new theatre building in Stuttgart from 1902 and which were negotiated about theatre architecture and technology in the tension between tradition and modernity. The study brings together perspectives of theatre, technology, urban and cultural history. 1. Introduction -- 2. The old court theatre in the provincial residence city (until 1902) -- 3. The new court theatre and the Greater City of Stuttgart (1902–1912) -- 4. Final consideration -- Annex -- List of abbreviations -- Sources and literature -- Proofs of illustration -- Register.
content.title_en: Traditional progress: the Stuttgart Hoftheater, the electric modern and the big city (1851-1912)

content.text: Differential equations as a central component of theoretical physics: harmonic oscillator, wave equation and corteweg-de-Vries equation. Eva Maria Hickmann focuses on a didactically and mathematically precise representation of differential equations as a central component of physics for the description of states and movements. The author presents the relevant solution methods based on the harmonic oscillator, wave equation and the corteweg-de-Vries equation. Here, great emphasis is placed on the completeness of the intermediate steps, so that this work is also understandable for students and teachers in self-study.The content Mathematical basics Common differential equations Partial differential equations Nonlinear differential equations The target groups Dozierende und Lehramtstuferende der Physics Lehrende der Physik The author Eva Maria Hickmann is currently working as a referendarin at the study seminar for the teaching office for Gymnasial Basics - non-discipline differential equations.
content.title_en: Differential equations as a central component of theoretical physics : harmonic oscillator, wave equation and corteweg de Vries equation

content.text: Lifecycle costs of roads: implementation forms, modular calculations, optimization potentials. Obstacles to lifecycle-oriented road construction projects -- Optimization potentials compared to conventional road construction projects -- Lifecycle costs calculation. Clemens Müller deals with the lifecycle costs of federal, state and district roads. As a result of the study, the author identifies essential obstacles to the implementation of lifecycle-oriented contract forms and develops a model for the calculation of lifecycle costs. Furthermore, the volume presents optimization potentials by means of a lifecycle-oriented realization compared to conventional realization.The content Obstacles to lifecycle-oriented road construction projects Optimization potentials compared to conventional road construction projects Lifecycle cost calculation The target groups Dozierende und Studierende der Wirtschaftswissenschaften Praktiken aus den Bereichen Straßenbau und der Public Verwaltung The author Clemens Müller is an economic engineer and mainly concerned with the work preparation, calculation and realization of construction projects in non-European countries.
content.title_en: Lifecycle costs of roads : implementation forms, modular calculation, optimization potential

content.text: The teaching kitchen as a specialized area of school career orientation : an examination in theory and practice. The dissertation looks at the equipment, function, utilization and the didactic potential of Cooking classrooms at middle schools in Saxony. The author focuses specifically on options to focus classroom activities with a view to vocational orientation at school. The dissertation examines the equipment, function, use and didactic potential of the teaching kitchen at Saxon secondary schools. The author pays particular attention to the possibilities of re-occupying the teaching kitchen thematically and using it for vocational orientation in schools.
content.title_en: The teaching kitchen as a school-oriented vocational area : an examination in theory and practice

content.text: The learning diagnosis of the learning diagnosis of functional illiteracy: acceptance and strategies of action. The dissertation discourses the use of learning level diagnostics for literacy and basic education work. As those affected find it especially hard to deal with text-based testing procedures, tests for determining learning needs should be designed in such a way as to avoid fear and resistance. The author examines the current state of learning level diagnostics from the view point of students and analyses their action strategies. A more intimate understanding for the problems of adult functional illiterate in test situations may attribute to a better utilisation of the potential of learning level diagnostics. The dissertation discusses the use of learning diagnosis of the learning diagnosis of the problem of problem-related illiterate in test situations.
content.title_en: Learning level diagnostics in functional illiteracy : acceptance and strategies

content.text: These are the two regions within a country really independent islands? Do economic relations and effects really have a homogeneous, unique size across an enterprise? These two assumptions are often imploded in empirical economic and social research. In his doctoral thesis, Norbert Schanne discusses how statistical methods can deviate from this unrealistic model structure through consulting spatial patterns in both observable variables and presumed relations. Opportunities to improve our understanding of the economy as well as prospects in the application of methods are to be considered in terms of the regional structure.
content.title_en: Spatial dependence and heterogeneousity in empirical analyses of regional labour market dynamics

content.text: The survey of the learning system is a mandatory introduction into the learning field concept: the requirement for vocational teachers to measure practical competences instead of testing experienced knowledge. This publication introduces an empirically underpinned model, which takes up questions of how to capture and measure practical competences against the background of the development of professional identity across the entire enterprise generation process. The development theory tools allow not only a visualisation of individual development processes, but also a permit a didactic offensive in the sensitivisation of teaching support for the student. The survey of the learning system does not reveal the question of the learning system. The survey of the learning system is based on the question of the learning system.
content.title_en: Acquisition of competence and identity in electrotechnical work : establishment and testing of a model of indicators for empirical examination of the acquisition of professional competence

content.text: The question of the consideration of losses in the context of taxation is not only at the centre of the tax law, but also in an exemplary way concerns the more general question of the rules of tax distribution justice and its pre- and overformification by higher-ranking law. The legislator, who seeks to grasp this area of regulation, moves within a system of various, partly competing, regulatory principles. Christian Thiemann works out the foundations and contents of simple tax law and identifies the constitutional and Union-law conditions of a design that the legislator must observe in its shaping. He not only wants to contribute to the foundations of a tax-law dogma, but also to the concrete questions that arise in connection with the design of tax loss consideration, give concrete answers. What are the framework conditions for the legislator when it comes to regulating tax loss? Christian Thiemann sets out the formation and content of law law and constitution.
content.title_en: Tax losses : constitutional and Union law requirements for legislative design

content.text: If a reproducible medicine is used to perform an incident involving the exchange of germ cells or embryos, the actual and legal effects are not only drastic. In addition to the question of whether and how the doctor can clarify the incident, the affected parties are particularly confronted with the consequences of the defect and the consequences of the liability. Moritz L. Jäschke shows that the current legal situation is incomplete both in the field of prevention and in view of the legal consequences of such an incident. He attempts to resolve this situation by means of detailed regulatory proposals. Moritz L. Jäschke throws light on the duty of care guidelines for professionals working in reproductive medicine. He investigates the far-reaching legal implications of cases where or embryos are mixed up, bringing his differences to reform.
content.title_en: Interchanged germ cells and embryos : Analysis of reproductive medical incidents : context of standards, legal consequences, regulatory requirements

content.text: System risk management: through banking supervision, banking company and bank executive board. Destabilization of the financial system can have unpredictable and globally devastating effects. The law must, in spite of predictive uncertainties, intervene stabilisingly. In European banking supervision law, patterns of system risk management have developed and consolidated into a new regulatory regime. In its scope, the banking supervisor can rely on a precautionary principle and cooperate with banks in a state-private responsibility community. Bank company law, which is shaped down to the very detail by prudential law, can hardly be regarded as a mere civil law. Tim Engel therefore examines the translation of prudential paradigms into the corporate regulatory system and shows how system risk prevention can also become the responsibility of the bank executive.
content.title_en: Systemic risk provision : by bank supervision, bank company and bank executive

content.text: The work examines damage to security and its ability to replace it. The work is divided into two parts. First, the compensation of damage to security is determined by means of §§ 249 ff. BGB. On the one hand, criteria are developed to determine the equivalence and equivalence of two credit guarantees. On the other hand, it is shown that damage to security can only be compensated in money only to a limited extent. Finally, a mechanism is developed which coordinates the damage management in multi-person constellations. The second part of the work focuses on individual security institutions: namely the basic and furniture Pfandrechte, the security transfer, the retention of title and the respective forms of renewal. The results are transferred from the general first part with adaptation to the respective specificities.
content.title_en: The damaged security: an investigation into the harmful aspects of reciprocity of credit collateral

content.text: Quis custodiet ipsos custodes : Development, quality and enforcement of the duties of the Supervisory Board. The Supervisory Board of the Aktiengesellschaft is not a mere supervisory body, but advises and accompanies the Management Board closely. If the Supervisory Board violates its obligations, its members will later be liable for damages. However, can the Company protect itself in advance if its Supervisory Board is about to make a mistake? The work examines whether and by whom the Supervisory Board is supervised. It shows that the Aktiengesellschaft has a claim for compliance with its Supervisory Board members, which the Management Board can enforce before any damage occurs. By comprehensive historical analysis, the work solves a problem that has been over a hundred years old on the basis of applicable law. The practical part describes on the basis of the results of the work, how supervisory boards can gain legal certainty outside of a compensation process if they look out for claims that would be subject to the "ARAG/Garmenbeck" principles of the BGH.
content.title_en: Quis custodiet ipsos custodes : Development, quality and enforcement of the Supervisory Board's duties

content.text: The work examines the tension-laden relationship between European State aid law and the promotion of renewable energies in Germany. In the light of the ruling of the European Court of Justice on the EEG 2012 (Rs. C-405/16 P), the scope of the concept of aid is presented and critically assessed in relation to the German support system for renewable energies. Furthermore, the often criticised influence of the EU Commission on the state aid law on Member State policy is analysed. In the course of this study, the Commission's so-called policy of guidelines is examined more closely and, inter alia, is classified against the background of the European materiality limit. Furthermore, the basic conception of European State aid law as a legal matter is also elaborated in the area of tension between negative and positive integration.
content.title_en: European State aid law and the promotion of renewable energy: practice and limits on State aid control in Member States

content.text: Sociology of self-optimization. More productive work, more efficient work! More fitter, even more beautiful! Self-optimization is the focus of current social requirements and individual sense worlds of capitalist societies. But what exactly does self-optimization mean? Is it a new phenomenon? What individual and social preconditions and consequences does it have? Along these three questions Anja Röcke develops a definition of concepts as clear as they are fundamental, discusses the history of self-optimization and determines the factors that make self-optimization as a central and ambivalent phenomenon of late modern society.
content.title_en: Sociology of self-optimization

content.text: Refugee protest and trade unions : Negotiations of representation in the German labour and migration regime. Since 2012, there has been a new generation of self-organized refugee protest in Germany with a central demand: the right to work and trade union organization. The interactions of refugees with trade unions range from occupation of the trade union premises to joint demonstrations. A first success came in 2015 with the right to membership in the service union ver.di. Oskar Ilya Fischer's ethnographic investigation asks about the interaction rules of these meetings from 2013 to 2016, which are framed by negotiations of representation in the German labour and migration regime.
content.title_en: Refugee protest and trade unions : Negotiations of representation in the German labour and migration regime

content.text: The program was developed and evaluated positively by the RefueL programme to promote the resilience of teachers' students in the run-up to the practical semester. The program was used to complement the professional and didactic vocational preparation of teachers during their studies with a range of courses to provide them with a training for mental and social resistance. The developed program consists of five modules on the topics of resilience in the teaching context, social relationships, welfare, goals and solving problems and regulating emotions. These modules contain a wide range of practical exercises for the promotion of resilience and are implemented in the face-to-face setting. For the evaluation, a longitudinal control group design was chosen. Hierarchic regressions were calculated. The program proved to be effective at four different evaluation levels. The course participants contributed to the study results in the course of the course of the course, while controlling the initial values.
content.title_en: Fit for the classroom : Conception and evaluation of a resilience support programme for teacher students

content.text: Micro-Utopias of architecture: the utopian moment of minimal architectural techniques. After the utopia became increasingly discredited with the entry into the "postmodern" from 1968 onwards, the present cultural discourses show its return. The low and turning point of this development is marked by the collapse of the communist regime in 1989/91. Sandra Meireis makes the central hypothesis for the architectural field that a return of utopia can be observed in the form of plural micro-utopias - microtopoi of architecture. Moreover, she shows that utopia as a historical philosophical model is subject to social changes and thus reflects the late modern tendency of cultural partiality.
content.title_en: Micro-Utopias of Architecture : the utopian moment of minimal architectural techniques

content.text: Poverty and environmental protection: potentials and barriers in the urban area of West Africa. Elisabeth Huber analyses the possibilities of environmentally-friendly action by the poorer urban sections of West Africa. In this context, she analyses the practices of waste and wastewater disposal in Bamako (Mali) and Ouagadougou (Burkina Faso) under the relevant economic, social and cultural conditions. In addition to discussing poverty on the basis of monetary aspects, lack of opportunities for realisation and family and neighbourly solidarity strategies, she raises the question of the connection between environmental awareness, pollution, environmental protection, living and living conditions, infrastructure and the »right to the city«.
content.title_en: Poverty and environmental protection: potentials and barriers in the urban area of West Africa

content.text: In 2000, three young men founded the Internet portal »Indernet« - a German-speaking area of »Inders of the second generation« for »Indians of the second generation«. Building on material collected over 17 years, Urmila Goel presents three mosaics of this virtual space in her ethnography: It describes how the different parts of the portal (article, forum, guestbook, etc.) were used and traces the development steps of the community portal from its foundation to its move to Web 2.0. In doing so, it analyses racially critically how the »Indernet« became a space of national ethno-cultural (multiple) belonging and what exclusions were involved.
content.title_en: The Indiannet: a racialist-critical Internet ethnography
