content.text: The evidence in the minimum wage sanction procedure: the applicability in the context of the control and enforcement of the minimum wage by financial control of undeclared work of evidence collected to prove offences and irregularities in the minimum wage penalty procedure. The work examines in a pioneering work to what extent evidence collected by customs authorities in the context of the control and enforcement of the statutory minimum wage may be used to prove offences and irregularities. It concludes that the current practice of testing and sanctioning not only violates simple legal standards but also constitutional law: employers must not simply be "checked in in blue". Persons affected are to be instructed about their existing right of refusal to provide information. If you have to produce or submit documents, you have to apply a prohibition of proof of criminal or criminal liability for their protection. By considering these and numerous other potential violations of law by the control authorities, interested employers should be given arguments to prevent them from using illegal tests for the purposes of defence.
content.title_en: Proof in the minimum wage sanction procedure: the applicability of the control and enforcement of the minimum wage by financial control of undeclared work to prove offences and irregularities in the minimum wage penalty procedure

content.text: Peer-to-Peer-Lending: contractual and supervisory requirements. Real peer-to-peer-Lending is a financial innovation in which investors directly and anonymously grant loans via internet platforms to consumers and companies. Due to regulatory uncertainties, genuine peer-to-peer-Lending is not offered in Germany. In the work, the contractual and regulatory requirements for those involved in peer-to-peer-Lending are examined as well as possibilities for regulation. The focus of the regulatory part is the banking regulatory permission obligation to take up and award loans via the platforms. Here, it is shown in particular that consumers and companies could take up loans of up to 100,000 euros per year without requiring a banking regulatory permission. / "Peer-to-Peer-Lending and from Great.
content.title_en: Peer-to-peer lending : contractual and prudential requirements

content.text: Prison visit projects in Germany: a criminal investigation. In numerous prisons in Germany, so-called prison visit projects for vulnerable or criminal youths and adolescents are offered. However, the visit to a detention centre and conversations with prisoners are intended to show the consequences of (further) criminality first-hand and lead to changes in attitudes and behaviour among participants. However, a criminal preventive effect of such programs is not proven. Against the background of US-American projects such as "Scared Straight!", which promised high success rates, but which could not be confirmed in the context of impact assessments, the author presents the findings gained in the context of her empirical investigation of German projects. Due to many other, already recognized as effective measures of special prevention and behavioural change, she concludes that the implementation of the projects is to be discouraged without further impact research.
content.title_en: Prison Visit Projects in Germany : a Criminal Investigation

content.text: The criminal investigation of the organ transplant scandal includes the detailed presentation of the views of the court and the case law as well as concerns against the criminal release of the accused physician. The behaviour of the offender is examined and the possibility of an indirect perpetrator is assumed. Subsequently, an attempt is made to establish a causal relationship between the change in the allocation order and the occurrence of death or bodily injury of displaced patients. Furthermore, it is explained that the protection purpose of the distribution rules can be associated with the rescue of all patients on a waiting list and that the manipulating transplant surgeon has acted with dolus eventualis in the redistribution of the organ allocation process. The work provides a detailed overview of all critical issues of medical criminal law.
content.title_en: The criminality of manipulations in organ allocation after the murder and assault crimes

content.text: Subjective perception and evaluation of road-induced greed and wave movements in virtual driving experiments. State of the art -- Modelling and implementation of the virtual driving experiment -- Investigation of coupled greed and wave movement. The driving simulator is a crucial development tool to gain knowledge of system and vehicle behaviour in early stages of the development process. Using the subjective evaluation in virtual driving experiments, Minh-Tri Nguyen tests individual systems and evaluates them at the overall vehicle level. The author realizes experiments of human perception in driving simulator. Based on this, he develops an approach to improve driving comfort. Specifically, these are the coupled greed and wave movement of the vehicle, which is caused by road impermeability at higher speeds. The content of the state of the art Modelling and implementation of the virtual driving experiment Investigation of the coupled greed and wave movement The target groups of driving dynamics and vehicle simulation engineers in the research and development of the automotive industry and their suppliers at the University of Stuttgart are currently working autonomously on the field of driving engineers at the University of Stuttgart.

content.text: Discipline and performance in the everyday life of a second primary school class: an ethnographic study. What happens in a primary school inclusion class when the first graded class work is transferred? What happens when discipline and performance enter the everyday life of secondary students as implicit cultural codes of performance assessment? Annette Hess describes the observations of a teaching participation in the school year 2015/2016 and analyses them in a subjective theoretical perspective. Empirical examples show the subjective and situational factors that determine the degree of difficulty of class work and the grade. The study provides insights into processes in which the pupils begin to produce the hierarchical system of grades in the reality of their social relations. Situation descriptions shed light on the difficult paradoxical situation of teachers between inclusion and ranking performance assessment.A genealogy of today's school performance assessment following supervision and punishment research (Foucault 1976) shifts their cultural historical roots into a disciplinary system of early European citizenship.
content.title_en: Discipline and performance in the everyday life of a second primary school class : an ethnographic study

content.text: The present work deals with the development and effect of synchronous disturbances in electric drive systems. Parasitic synchronous impedances form together with counterclock impedances of the drive system parasitic resonance oscillation circuits, which are stimulated by the switching actions of the inverters used in the drive system to swing. One of the two main areas is the development of an analytical calculation method to determine the existing parasitic synchronous paths and their resonance frequencies. The second main focus is on the possibility of active damping of synchronous disturbances. To this end, an algorithm analyses each switching flange in the inverter on its effect in the synchronous system. Subsequently, this can be shifted in such a way that the switching flank is able to achieve the best possible damping in the synchronous system. Introducting the necessary foundations for the conversion technique as well as the training and stimulation of resonance oscillation circuits is explained by the example of a RLC series oscillation cycle, which is already used for the highly reduced DC mode. The literature research provides a detailed overview of current methods of the reduction of synchronous disturbances.
content.title_en: Active damping of synchronous disturbances in electrical drive systems

content.text: The age of interdependence: global thinking and international politics in the long 1970s. From the late 1960s onwards, contemporaries discussed closely global interdependence in world politics and the world economy. More than a decade before the start of the globalization debate, they declared their present "the age of interdependence". Martin Deuerlein, for the US and the Soviet Union, is investigating for the first time comprehensively such globalist contemporary diagnoses in the social sciences and their interactions with international politics. The author shows how the 19th century-established understanding of interdependence as a interlinkage between national units from the 1960s was questioned. The increase in world trade and financial flows, "global problems" such as hunger and environmental pollution, and the new significance of multinational companies and other transnational actors led observers to doubt on previous assumptions. Against the background of the East-West and North-South conflicts, global interdependence has been increasingly threatening and seemed to require new political approaches. However, what a world order adapted to the changing context was to be, was fiercely controversial - nothing that has lost its relevance until today.
content.title_en: The Age of Interdependence : Global Thinking and International Politics in the Long 1970s

The above ground biomass (Above Ground Biomass = AGB) is an essential variable for the estimation of carbon stocks in the forest. Quantification of carbon stocks is a central factor in forest management and policy decisions in times of climate change. A scientifically precise and therefore credible estimation of the above ground biomass is one of the essential prerequisites in the correct implementation of the commitments made by the Vertrasg parties to the climate convention UN-FCCC to reduce carbon emissions. Aboveground biomass (AGB) is related to the carbon content of the forest and forest carbon is a core variable for contemporary management and policy decisions. content.title_en: Quantifying the uncertainty caused by sampling, modelling, and field measurements in the estimation of AGB with information of the national forest inventory in Durango, Mexico

content.text: The role of campaigns in law enforcement: the example of sanfei campaigns in Chinese immigration law. Campaigns are an established means of enforcing political and legal objectives in the People's Republic of China. Since the beginning of reform and opening policy, the country has developed economically rapidly, which is a reason both for the constant development of the local legal system and for the attractiveness of China for foreign workers. This book examines the role of campaigns in the context of Chinese immigration law, which was fundamentally reformed in 2012. It is a question of why the revision of the law on the administration of entry and exit was accompanied by the increased implementation of campaigns against illegal immigration and illegal employment of foreigners. To this end, this book examines both the internal structure of the campaigns and the embedding of the current immigration law in the context of Chinese administrative law.
content.title_en: The role of campaigning in law enforcement: the example of sanfei campaigning in Chinese immigration law

content.text: The municipal minimum funding claim in federal and state constitutional law. The law of municipal minimum funding is practically controversial and dogmatically unexplained. The work structures the various aspects of this highly relevant matter for municipal households and systematically examines the constitutional content: Is the much quoted core and marginal area dogmatics helpful here? Does the minimum funding claim stand under funding retention? What is the concrete content of such a claim – in vertical and horizontal terms? All questions relevant for legislation, jurisprudence and legal advice are discussed knowledgeably and in comprehensible language for federal and state constitutional law and concrete solutions proposed.
content.title_en: The municipal minimum requirement in constitutional law of the federal and state governments

content.text: Personal predictive policy: criminal science research on the automation of criminal prognosis. Preventing crimes before they happen? This tempting narrative is no longer just science fiction. Computer-based systems with the aim of predicting criminal behaviour are used worldwide. The author critically illuminates this use with legal-interdisciplinary access. It comes to the conclusion that the technology brings with it an erosion of constitutional guarantees and carries considerable risks for the rule of law and society. In particular, the crime control threatens to go into a self-imposed thoughtlessness – in the form of Arendt. The work concludes with a proposal for minimum requirements, which the technology should be guided by in the future.
content.title_en: Personal Predictive Policies : Criminal Science Study on the Automation of Crime Forecasts

content.text: Intersexuality in sport: media and medical body policies. Gender is linked to a specific idea of physical performance. In sport, for example, this is shown by the fact that separation into two sexes is considered to be a necessary practice in order to enable fair competition. But what does such separation mean for intersexual people who are physically evading the two-sex order? From a sociological, sexual and medical perspective, Dennis Krämer works out the existing notions of intersexuality as contemporary body policies and reflects their discursive consolidations taking into account social conditions.
content.title_en: Intersexuality in sport : medial and medical body policies

For this purpose, the facts and research on the phenomenon 'Transgenerational transmission of traumas' are first elaborated and the origin, reasons and consequences are presented. In order to locate the topic appropriately in the Protestant context, the role of the Protestant Church in the Second World War is summarized and the reference to the problem is established. Afterwards, the whole connection from a practical-theological point of view in the context of today's church life is considered and recommendations are presented, how a constructive approach to the limitations of the problem can be shaped.
content.title_en: Transgenerational transmitted traumas : a practical-theological examination

content.text: The legalisation of the prohibition of official corruption abroad pursuant to § 335a StGB: an analysis of international and constitutional law. The work examines the compatibility of the foreign corruption punishable by § 335a StGB with the law of nations and constitution. The conflict between international contractual obligation and the majority of unwritten international law limits – in particular the principle of non-interference – is examined. The following determination of the protected legal property of § 335a StGB is the starting point for the answer to the controversial question, to what extent a criminality of bribery and bribery of each official worldwide finds a constitutional justification. High court case law on offences that have a comparable protection direction (e.g. § 89a StGB – preparation of a serious state-threatening violence) provides valuable conclusions for this investigation.
content.title_en: The legitimacy of the prohibition of official corruption abroad pursuant to § 335a StGB : an international and constitutional analysis

content.text: Virtual secondary insolvency proceedings in European insolvency law: shadow existence or an important step towards a European culture of restructuring?. The EUInsVO, also the flagship of European insolvency legislation, has been able to address the Union legislator's efforts to establish a European "renovation culture". The investigation is concerned with the possibility of issuing an assurance under Art. 36 EUInsVO, which is newly introduced in the course of this development. The standard provides a legal basis for the implementation of virtual secondary insolvency proceedings in Europe. The idea is to avoid secondary proceedings by promising creditors to make a meaningful contribution to the resolution of cross-border insolvency cases, in spite of the many criticisms expressed.
content.title_en: Virtual secondary insolvency proceedings in European insolvency law : a shadow or an important step towards a European restructuring culture?

content.text: Regulatory principle Efficiency: Standards and limits of efficiency-oriented regulation in the telecommunications and energy sectors. Telecommunications and energy networks are the lifelines of modern companies and forward-looking economies. As these networks are natural monopolies, they must be regulated by the state. This regulation is now legally detailed, but nevertheless confronts fundamental questions: How are the interests of network operators and network users to be weighed? How far can a regulatory authority intervene in the rights of the network operator? How much must the network expansion be promoted and made possible? How independent can a regulatory authority be? This work represents how the guiding principle of efficiency can be transferred from economics to law and how it offers clear answers to these current regulatory questions here, especially in the context of recourse to constitutional law.
content.title_en: Regulatory principle Efficiency : Standards and limits of efficiency-oriented regulation in the telecommunications and energy sectors

content.text: Protection and responsibility in the digital and global working world: the position of people in the occupational safety system on the road to (un)dependence 4.0. The digital and global working world combines elements of dependency and independence. The establishment of an appropriate balance between protection and freedom is becoming more important as a protection purpose. This encourages an understanding that is not to be reduced to a "right of protection" and goes beyond this, to understand this as "right of protection and responsibility", with institutions to be determined according to effectiveness. This challenge is the thesis. It focuses on health protection, analyses the shift of dependencies and freedoms and, using the example of self-hazard, takes a cross-legal approach with a focus on the occupational safety law.
content.title_en: Protection and responsibility in the digital and global world of work: the position of people in the occupational safety system on the way to (un)dependence 4.0

content.text: Involvement as a school transformation process: possibilities and limits of the indicators-based presentation of common learning at the municipal and individual levels of school. The implementation of the idea of inclusion confronts the entire education system with new challenges. In accordance with federal responsibilities, in addition to the country, circles and school leaders are also obliged to help shape development. Currently, there is little systematic information on the state of inclusive education in the school system at the municipal level, as well as on educational participation and the educational success of children and young people with special educational needs. This also depends on a broad uncertainty about the basis for assessing the quality of inclusive schools available. In the context of the work, the possibilities and limits of the development of common learning in the school area are examined, the development of common learning in the school area is based on indicators and conclusions for inclusive school organisation and planning at a small-scale level are derived. The aim is to provide both decision-makers from politics and administration as well as actors in the educational institutions with approaches to organizational and systemic development of inclusive education data-based and to provide the basis for the observation in the school-based context of the school-based observation.
content.title_en: Inclusion as a school transformation process: possibilities and limits of indicators-based presentation of common learning at municipal and individual school level

content.text: The digital acquisition of an e-book: a contract typological study on the interface between the granting of rights of use and the provision of an intangible object. The download of digital content has established itself as a form of reference and raises questions in contract, competition and copyright. The legal relationship between the provider and the customer during the digital acquisition is examined in detail using the e-book. The focus is on the typological assignment of the contract. For this purpose, the subject matter of the contract and the interaction of the legal areas are elaborated. This builds on the follow-up question about the contractual design possibilities. Using selected GTC clauses and technical protection measures, the admissibility of restrictions is examined. In particular, the discussion about the resale of used e-books is addressed to a solution.
content.title_en: The digital acquisition of an e-book: a typological study on the interface between the granting of rights of use and the provision of an intangible object

content.text: The legally required handling of findings requiring clarification in epidemiological studies. In epidemiological studies, so-called random findings are increasingly occurring. The present medical law dissertation therefore examines the question of which treatment of these findings is legally required. The focus is on whether or under which conditions an epidemiological researcher is entitled or even obliged to notify the subject of any conspicuous, i.e. pathological or at least needing clarification. In this regard, the contractual obligations arising from the treatment or subject contract are examined. At the same time, the work also examines data protection, occupational and criminal aspects that arise in this context.
content.title_en: The legally required handling of the findings in epidemiological studies that need clarification

content.text: Religious codes in the popular culture: clothing of the Black Metal scene. In the fashion world and pop culture, religious symbols are surprisingly often encountered, whether they are crosses on t-shirts, Buddha figures on handbags, or the Indian goddess Kali on bathing suits: religion on popular clothing seems to be "in fashion." But what do such symbols still have to do with religion? The study designs a religious science approach to this reception of religious symbols in popular cultural clothing, explains the complex connections between religion and popular culture, and tests this proposed approach to an investigation into clothing in the Swiss black metal scene. In fashion and pop culture, one encounters religious symbols surprisingly often, be it crosses on T-shirts, reflections of Buddha on handbags or the colourful goddess Kali on swimsuits. ‘Religion' on cloting seems to be 'in vogue'. content.text: The English-language work offers a legal analysis of internal and external differentiation in European Union law. content.text: Liability and insurance in the operation of wind turbines. As an integral part of the energy transition, wind turbines have become widely distributed both on the mainland and at sea and are continuously integrated into the social environment and into nature. As a result, the effects on their environment of their operation differ fundamentally from those of conventional, mostly isolated power plants. In this work, the liability risks arising from the operation of wind turbines are comprehensively processed and examined for their liability and insurance relevance, taking into account liability-related questions arising from international private law relating to offshore wind turbines and property rights relating to external land and land installed wind turbines. / »Liability and Insurance for the Operation of Wind Turbines« -- Unlike conventional power plants, wind turbines have become integrated into resident and natural spaces. content.text: Control of abuse in the telecommunications and energy sectors between regulation and municipal action. Responsibilities of monopoly and the objective of functioning competition in the network sectors require in particular an effective control of the abuse of market power – especially at the level of network infrastructure. At the same time, increasingly comprehensive expansion requirements are placed on the networks and, in addition to companies and the federal government, the municipalities are also relevant actors in the field of broadband expansion and energy concessional allocation in the area of network infrastructure. content.text: The first phase of the study was to use a single carbon fibre with pulsed laser deposition (PLD) and a quality-connected CO2 laser to completely coat the zinc oxide (ZnO) thin layers to produce photoanodes for textile, flexible and air-permeable dye solar cells (DSSCs). The first phase of the study examined the growth behaviour of the thin layers first on rigid substrates, as well as the influence of the substrate temperature, oxygen pressure and all parameters caused by the coating of fibers. In particular, the separation behaviour at room temperature was investigated, where it was obtained to produce less crystalline, thicker, zinc-containing layers, and a model for the explanation was developed. The second phase of the study was to determine the efficiency of the ZnO low-frequency substrates and the efficiency of the distilled glass was first characterized by the presence of a distilled glass.
content.title_en: Production of crystalline ZnO thin layers by means of PLD on flexible substrate materials

content.text: Approaches for visually supported comparison analysis of connectome data. Comparison of connectomes is an essential step in identifying changes in nervous systems. Analysis of connectome and its comparison requires a wide range of methods. The platform-independent and generic framework neuroVIISAS provides flexible solutions to functional and comparative issues. In the context of this work, a methodology is described to compare different connectome with a wide range of analytical and visual methods. The developed comparison system is described and applied to two questions.
content.title_en: Approaches for visually supported comparison analysis of data from the connectome

content.text: Product development for the use of Rapid Manufacturing in the development of hydraulic clamping bushings. In the work a hydraulic clamping bushing with the additive manufacturing process FDM was produced. The use of the high-performance ABS-P430 plastic allows the printed bushing to be used directly as a connection between shaft and hub for the transmission of forces and moments. Thus, this production belongs to the area of Rapid Manufacturing. The aim of this work is to implement the existing concept of hydraulic clamping bushing with an additive manufacturing process and thus check the functioning of manufactured components.
content.title_en: Product development for the use of rapid manufacturing in the development of hydraulic clamping bushings

content.text: Modelling and generation of user interfaces for interactive software systems using patterns. The dissertation includes the design of a development environment for user interfaces that combines model and pattern-based UI development into an integrated development and generation approach. The basics of model and pattern-based development are presented and existing implementations are analyzed. The results of the investigations are incorporated into the design of the combined development environment, which is described in detail. The work includes a case study that illustrates the practical significance of the theoretical statements.
content.title_en: Modelling and generation of user interfaces for interactive software systems using patterns

content.text: Digital estate: the ability to transition and the way digital data is processed, taking into account the rights of third parties. The inheritance of data has recently gained great attention. In the example of Facebook accounts, the dissertation develops a general concept for dealing with data after death. It is explained that data is generally transferred to the heirs. However, the highest personality of portal information and in particular the rights of communication partners require further examination. Therefore, the work links hereditary issues with those of data protection, copyright, telecommunications and general contract law. It is explained that data does not pass by itself as a result, but depends on the transition of the storage medium or the contract under criminal law.
content.title_en: Digital discount: the ability and manner of digital data to be transferred, taking into account the rights of third parties

However, an assessment of individual exposure to urban pollution is still neglected, as current methods are based on stationary measurements or modelling. However, empirical methods have not been developed until the last few years to understand the awareness and motivation of exposed persons, but the assessment of the individual exposure is not only essential for short-term adaptation measures, but also for long-term studies of environmental health effects.

The aim of this work is primarily to answer the question whether the multifunctional plants in the North Sea AWZ are feasible in the current legal situation. In case of a positive answer, help for the practical implementation of such projects should be provided to the operators – in the sense of a guide or a compilation of the legal requirements for such plants. Improvement proposals for the current law are also developed.

content.text: Automated driving and criminal responsibility for negligence. The use of automated vehicles in road traffic raises numerous questions for criminal law, which this work is intended to help clarify. In this regard, the legal situation and the handling of accidents of automated vehicles in the USA are compared. The investigation examines whether a responsibility for intelligent systems – in a sense as "the first thing" – seems possible. In terms of the driver, holder and manufacturer of the vehicles, the criminal liability for negligently committed bodily injury and killing offences is considered by reference to case groups and fictitious scenarios. In this regard, the focus is on ways of limiting due diligence obligations by "allowed risks". In addition, it is discussed who is the responsible driver when the system takes over the driving task. The work concludes with considerations on the decriminalisation of traffic negligence.
content.title_en: Automated driving and criminal liability for negligence

content.text: The fight against computer crime in Europe: standards, institutions and cooperations. The study is dedicated to an interdisciplinary research field of high relevance and relevance in the field of international law, European law, criminology and security policy: the fight against computer crime. According to the author, computer crime must be understood as a dynamic and hybrid crime field. In addition to the Directive 2013/40/EU on attacks on information systems, the measures to combat child pornography, cybergrooming, cyber laundering, the propaganda of terror on the Internet and fraud related to virtual currencies are also examined. In addition, the author calls for a clear division of competence in the fight against cyberterror.
content.title_en: The fight against computer crime in Europe: standards, institutions and cooperation

content.text: This study examines the relevance of biographical work as part of the development of identity and highlights practices against the background of media biographical experiences. Biographicality and visual competence are reflected as educational goals of media education. Using the documentary method, interviews and photographs of the interviewed young people were interpreted, whereby the communication contexts of social media were systematically integrated. This resulted in the typology of ‘visual biographical work', which reveals milieuspecifically different forms of photo-related communication and biographical work as part of identity development and examines the excess of the background of media media literacy.
content.title_en: Visual biography work : Smartphone photography in adolescence from a media pedagogical perspective

content.text: Liability for autonomous systems: Distribution of the risks of self-learning and networked algorithms in contract and criminal law. The work deals with the contractual and criminal liability issues for artificial intelligence de lege lata and de lege ferenda. Autonomous systems bring the classical legal dogmas to their limits due to their risks (autonomy, networking and intra-sparence). The work therefore represents a modern regulatory-rights dogmatic approach in order to holistically define the spheres of responsibility of the parties (contract partners, manufacturers, users and third parties) in the applicable material law and the burden of presentation and proof. The work links in future law to a co-regulated "stage building of liability" (including the draft regulation), thus promoting innovation in technical law.
content.title_en: Liability for autonomous systems : Distribution of the risks of self-learning and networked algorithms in contract and criminal law

content.text: Legal Tech applications : legal analysis and development of the term algorithmic legal service. The author shows that a product-related licensing instrument must be introduced for the provision of out-of-court legal services, which should be used in addition to the existing personal licensing rights of the legal service and collection service. To this end, the existing regulations for all functional legal tech categories (also known as smart contracts) are comprehensively presented on the basis of selected offers and the resulting regulatory challenges are formulated. As a result, neither the deregulation of the legal profession nor the UWG can guarantee the quality of (legal) services provided by software.
content.title_en: Legal Tech Applications : Legal Analysis and Development of the Concept of Algorithmic Legal Service

content.text: Access to data under European antitrust law. By using new technologies in the context of digitalisation, more and more data are generated that are concentrated in a few companies. Data monopolies arise, which can have a lasting impact on competition. A company dependent on data may be prevented from participating in the competition without access to data. How can European antitrust law react to such data accumulations? Does the prohibition of misuse of Article 102 TFEU mean that access to data for competitors – similar to intangible property rights – is subject to a compulsory licence? Stefan A. Schmidt analyses the market conditions where negative concentration trends can be met with access to data and when such access should be refused due to the competitive situation or other negative effects, e.g. data protection issues in the context of digital resources and the art. 102 TFtective of the data access rules of the 10th GWB-Novelle. Stefan A. Schmidt investigates when companies can demand access to competitors.
content.title_en: Access to data under European antitrust law

content.text: Confident stability: the deceptive calm of trust in the process of social interdependence. Niklas Luhmann has made a significant contribution to the understanding of trust. However, his system functionalism places too much emphasis on the situational moment of risk of having to 'progress' trust there where it cannot be decided in an informed manner. In contrast, Julian Valentin Möhring points out the equal aspect of routine: trust is formed and stabilized through existing relationships of familiarity. The fact that these themselves are the product of a once-received trust leads the author to a relational-process sociological approach that follows Norbert Elias' concept of interlinking. Trust is never consolidated but develops and changes. The present study pursues the stabilization of trust in long-term civilization processes. It examines subjective, institutional and historical-societal aspects and thus also detects alienating, repressive confidence constellations that must escape the functionalist theory that is about expectation certainty.
content.title_en: Confident stability: the deceptive calm of trust in the process of social interdependence

content.text: The transparency of data protection law: the limits of individual data protection based on covert data processing on the Internet. The everyday use of information technology has long been no longer only provided the user with the information he wants. With the constant use of devices – such as computers, smartphones and tablets – the user himself becomes a valuable source of information. In order to establish a balance of arms between the responsible and the affected parties, the data protection law knows the principle of transparency. The work focuses on data processing, which is not openly recognizable and for which the corresponding information of the affected parties is mandatory in order to meet the protection objectives of data protection law. The work here is bi-partite and first collects the essential legal foundations. These are then compared using practical examples, which are also analysed in depth technically. Finally, by resorting to these preliminary work, problems and improvement potentials of the transparency requirement and its actual and legislative implementation are demonstrated.
content.title_en: The data protection transparency requirement : the limits of individual data protection based on covert data processing on the Internet

content.text: The preventive restructuring framework: European requirements and scope for implementation for the EU Member States. Depending on the design, the preventive restructuring framework will have a significant impact on the existing German law on restructuring and insolvency. The work analyses the mandatory implementation by the German legislator by 17 July 2022 at the latest, and analyses the requirements of the Directive (EU) 2019/1023 of 20 June 2019 on the creation of this legal framework, presents the remaining scope for implementation, shows inconsistencies and provides incentives for implementation into German law. The work thus provides guidance for further discussion of the implementation of this legal framework and is highly revealing for a later interpretation of German law based on the EU directive.
content.title_en: The preventive restructuring framework: European targets and scope for implementation for EU Member States

content.text: The industrial dispute in national and European law: an investigation into the influence of European law on freedom of industrial action derived from Article 9(3) of the Basic Law, using the example of the collective bargaining requirement. National law still only recognises the collective bargaining dispute. The collective bargaining requirement is derived from the concept of freedom of industrial action as an annex to a collective bargaining autonomy enshrined in Article 9(3) of the Basic Law. There are dogmatic concerns against this. Furthermore, the work questions to what extent the collective bargaining requirement is compatible with supranational legal sources (Article 6(4) ESC, Article 11 ECHR and Article 28 ECRC). The result is a question of a re-examined labour law in the face of a European economic and labour market which largely detracts from collective bargaining power with its new employment leaders (digitalisation, platform economics, crowdworking).
content.title_en: The industrial dispute in national and European law: an investigation into the influence of European law on freedom of action derived from Article 9(3) of the Basic Law, using the example of collective bargaining requirements

content.text: Igor-Stravinskij's theatre of the future: the choreo drama "Le Sacre du printemps" in the mirror of the 'Theater Reform around 1900'. Igor-Stravinskij's Sacre du printemps is considered a milestone in the history of music and dance. Nevertheless, science has so far overlooked a key aspect of understanding the work: the ‘Theater Reform around 1900'. Leila Zickgraf shows for the first time that Stravinskij realized his very own ‘Theater of the future' with the Sacre – together with choreographer Vaclav Nižinskij and inspired by Georg Fuchs and Edward Gordon Craig. Through the rhythms of his composition, he put dancers and audiences into a physically experienced rush, thus integrating the audience into the stage scene. Ballets Russes anticipated a mechanistic aesthetic at that was not to be seen in music, dance and theatre until the 1920s. With his interdisciplinary orientation between dance, cultural, theatre and music science, and his comprehensive, but also Russian-speaking, the study of the sources – the central research still shows how little important aspects of the book play.
content.title_en: Igor-Stravinsky's theatre of the future: the choreo drama "Le Sacre du printemps" in the mirror of the 'Theatre reform around 1900'

content.text: Digital Transformation in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises : Strategy, Management Control, and Network Involvement. The book highlights the digital transformation in SMEs. It supports scientists, entrepreneurs and policy makers alike by enabling a structured, logical discussion. The book consists of three parts. Part I develops a framework for a strategy in digital transformation along the four categories of technology use, changes in value creation, organisational aspects and financial aspects. Part II identifies components of a digital transformation control system that includes cultural, planning, administrative and performance-based controls. Part III identifies 11 generic types of innovation networks.
content.title_en: Digital Transformation in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises : Strategy, Management Control, and Network Involvement

content.text: Lars Hagen shows application scenarios how "Connected Car-to-Cloud and especially connectivity can be used in software development and in series use for motor control. The author pays attention to topics that go beyond data collection and include both up- and download data on the vehicle. The external computing power on a cloud is taken into account as well as the limited data rate of the vehicle bus and mobile communications. The content Application fields for car-to-Cloud in the field of motor control Application examples and diagnosis for car-to-cloud in the motor control system software The target groups Teaching staff and students in the field of vehicle and engine technology Engineers and natural scientists in vehicle and engine technology The author Lars Hagen received his doctorate at the Institute of Vehicle Technology Stuttgart (IFS) at the University of Stuttgart at the Chair of Vehicle Drives.
content.title_en: New possibilities for the engine control unit software through car-to-cloud networking

content.text: Personality-based personalization in mobile commerce: A behavioral analysis using the example of supermarket apps. 1. Introduction -- 2. Conceptual foundations of personality-based personalization -- 3. Study 1: Personality and app interface preferences -- 4. Study 2: Effect of personality-based personalization -- 5. Final consideration. Using intelligent algorithms, the digital footprint of a user can increasingly predict psychographic features – especially the personality. This information provides new starting points for marketing, especially for the personalization of apps. Personality information is used primarily in computer science research to optimize recommender systems. The present work, however, takes a behavioral perspective and examines how personalization is perceived and evaluated on the basis of the personality of users. Based on the results of two studies in the context of supermarket apps, the author makes recommendations for a successful implementation of personality-based personalization. The author Stefanie Arz received his doctorate from Prof. Dr. Andreas Mann at the marketing department of the University of Kassel.
content.title_en: Personalized Personalization in Mobile Commerce : A Behavioural Analysis using the Example of Supermarket Apps

content.text: Stochastic performance analysis of storage systems: analytical models for single-games optimized for travel time. Introduction -- Basics of performance analysis of automated storage systems -- State of research -- Stationary analysis of storage processes using Markov chains -- Modelling using closed queue networks -- Use of models for performance analysis of storage systems -- Conclusion and outlook. This monograph presents new approaches for efficient stochastic performance analysis of large storage systems for single-games optimized for travel time, which forms the basis for the demand-oriented design of the marginal flow rate. After an introduction to the methodological principles and the state of research for stochastic performance analysis of automated storage systems, various methods are developed that fully reflect the optimization potential of travel-related import and outsource strategies. In an extensive experimental study, the efficiency and accuracy of the procedures as well as the significantly stab-through effect of travel-time-optimizing strategies are demonstrated by the University of Applied Sciences and Management.
content.title_en: Stochastic performance analysis of storage systems : analytical models for single-games optimized for travel

content.text: The commenting of status messages in social networks from a criminal perspective. Social networks offer dimensions of information exchange through the possibility of rapid dissemination of messages and linking users, which cannot be implemented in this effective form of networking in real life. Often, they no longer only discuss, but are exposed, insulted, charged with criminal offences or right-wing extremist propaganda. In social networks, a large audience finds itself. Numerous people can perceive, comment and support the acts. The subject of the work are the dogmatic problems of criminal law, which arise when commenting on status messages with illegal content in social networks and whether they meet the specific features of the media. The question of possible criminality in commenting on status messages in social networks is no longer a theoretical problem, but a problem already arrived in the courtrooms. Likes, sharing, commenting; all this is now part of everyday communication and is even acquired several times a day in different contexts.
content.title_en: Commenting on status messages in social networks from a criminal perspective

content.text: The appropriation of images: a copyright study from appropriation art to memes. Under the term appropriation, various forms of the acquisition of copyrighted works are investigated. Already in the 1970s, artists of appropriation art used copies for their works of art. With the digitalisation and the culture of participation on the Internet, the techniques of appropriation art have become democratized and as memes and gifs of mass communication. These forms of image use – in appropriation art and in digital – are evaluated by copyright. Here, a focus of the work is on whether the current copyright of the social reality of digital communication still adequately reflect and how legal freedom for appropriation can be created.
content.title_en: The appropriation of images: a copyrighted view from the appropriation of art to Memes

content.text: Constitution: the Darwinian evolution of a societyally exile the humanity. The volume discusses the role and importance of constitutions in modern societies. From an interdisciplinary perspective, it is shown how constitutions could develop despite great diversity within society and how they help to create a common moral system. The emergence of modern societies organized members are genetically independent individuals. This diversity makes the role of constitutions particularly complex. The work sheds light on how constitutionalism contributes to the establishment of a unified moral system.
content.title_en: Constitution : the Darwinian evolution of a socio-economic structure

content.text: Marie Luise Gothein's history of gardening: the image of the garden as a text. Marie Luise Gothein wrote a classic in 1914 with her 'History of Gardening Art', which has been translated and re-published to this day, but never brought into focus as a basic work. This work examines the author's intellectual and aesthetic concepts in terms of their depiction of gardening art. What premises does the cultural scientist follow in fixing the ever changing space art work Gardening into text and image' What role does the reform garden movement, which was in full swing at the time of publication, play?' The analysis of Gothein's garden descriptions, for example, the Villa d'Este, shows how fundamentally the historical writing is influenced by the challenges of time: in the sense of Ecocriticism, the volumes reflect the engagement of man with his environment.
content.title_en: Marie Luise Gotheins History of Garden Art : the image of the garden as text

content.text: Educational knowledge in the teacher's profession : reconstructive findings from school practice. What do teachers from school practice understand as the concept of pedagogical knowledge and how do they conceptualise this? The knowledge of teachers in everyday school life and the associated understanding of professionalization are central topics in teacher education. In this book, pedagogical knowledge of teachers of different school forms is reconstructed based on an interview and observation study and is worked out in terms of conceptual insights for teacher education. In addition, differences and similarities between the understanding of pedagogical knowledge and the respective actions in school everyday life are made visible. Starting from a presentation of different forms of knowledge, pedagogical knowledge and pedagogical action is discussed in the context of social approaches (Mead and Giddens). It is the main aim of this volume to expand the discourse on the pedagogical knowledge of teachers in the context of social transformation processes.
content.title_en: Educational knowledge in the teacher's profession : reconstructive findings from school practice

content.text: System accreditation at universities: requirements, measures and effects from the perspective of university actors. The empirical study examines dynamic change processes from the perspective of university managers and quality management managers, which occur in the introduction of system accreditation. Challenges, action practices and strategies of change actors as well as effects of system accreditation are identified and theoretical and practical implications for the design of university development processes are shown.
content.title_en: System accreditation at universities: requirements, measures and effects from the perspective of higher education actors

content.text: Development and evaluation of a measurement and evaluation process for determining a sand dunes deformation under wind and wave influence.A major engineering challenge is to enable the structures of coastal protection to meet future challenges such as climate change, as in connection with the rise of sea level these must be resized.The dissertation presents the development of a method for measuring a coastal structure at a high-speed and spatial resolution during a storm flood.The generated data should contribute to significant insights about the dune dynamics and the behaviour of dunes in breakthrough situations.
content.title_en: Development and evaluation of a measurement and evaluation process for determining a sand dunes deformation under wind and wave influence

content.text: Long-term climate variability of the Baltic Sea region. This work examines the impact of the Atlantic multidecade oscillation (AMO) on the North European climate and follows the AMO signal in the Baltic Sea region. Observation data are limited to about 150 years. Due to the AMO frequency of 50 to 90 years, it is impossible to make statements about the effect of the AMO. Therefore, numerical models are used in this work: With a combination of a global and regional climate model, the period from 950 to 1800 is analyzed. This work shows that the AMO plays an important role in the Baltic Sea region. With a frequency of 50 - 90 years, effects of the AMO are affected to evaluate, show if you have a population of 150 days.
content.title_en: Long-term climate variability of the Baltic Sea region

When social elites negotiate behind closed doors, a lack of transparency is often criticised. Christina Viehmann puts this controversial and multi-layered debate on a theoretical basis by modeling public and media-media-media-media-media-media-media-mediated communication processes in negotiation-based decision-making processes of function elites. The result is a model that points out diverse, above all indirect and subtly acting mechanisms from the media public to the social decision-makers. content.title_en: Corset and power resource: the media public in negotiations of social decision-makers

content.text: Design of digitalized service ecosystems: Conceptualization of decision-making structures and derivation of design instructions. Design of digitalized service ecosystems as a challenge -- Conceptualization and theoretical foundation of digitized service ecosystems -- Design instructions for digitized service ecosystems based on empirical evidence and conceptual deepening -- Transfer of knowledge into an application model -- Summary and outlook. Companies are increasingly developing digital service innovations in cross-industry ecosystems together with other companies. Tim Senn presents in this book the theoretical backgrounds and dynamics of collaboration between actors in digitalized ecosystems. The concept validated by case studies allows a structured view of such systems and distinguishes between central actors who actively orchestrate the ecosystem and peripheral actors who participate in value creation. The insights from the case studies show options for management and give concrete design instructions. Tim Senn is a strategy and marketing consultant and researched as an external doctoral student at the University of Hohenheim on the transformation of companies, digital business models and cooperation between companies in the design of complex ecosystems.
content.title_en: Design of digitised service ecosystems : Conceptualisation of decision-making structures and derivation of design instructions

content.text: Man and his grammar: a historical corpus study in anthropological intent. What importance does knowledge of grammar have for the relationship of man to the world and to himself? And what does grammar need anyway, if grammatical ambiguity is usually unnoticed anyway and rarely represents a problem of understanding? Simon Kasper provides an empirically and theoretically based comprehensive answer to these questions. Based on a historical corpus study of parallel texts, he documents the successful human handling of ambiguity and subsequently provides an anthropological draft for understanding, which takes into account both the physical existence of man (embodiment) and the grammaticality of his language. In doing so, he not only includes basic assumptions of cognitive linguistics and philosophical anthropology, but also brings together quantitative (frequency) and qualitative (meaning) approaches of language theory.
content.title_en: Man and his grammar: a historical corpus study in anthropological intent

content.text: The definition of financial statements using textual and financial data is also a key factor in the overall assessment of the financial statements. The confidence in the accuracy of published annual accounts is also a key factor in the functioning of the capital markets. Celebrities of financial statements continue to shake the confidence of market participants in the credibility of the published information and thus lead to an inefficient allocation of resources. Reliable, automated fraud detection systems based on publicly available data can help to allocate audit resources more efficiently and strengthen the resilience of capital markets by protecting market participants more strongly from balance sheet fraud. In this study, the focus is on the development of a fraud detection model, which extracts typical patterns of fraudulent manipulation from textual and numerical components of annual accounts and combines them in a comprehensive detection model. The study is based on a comprehensive methodological approach, which addresses important issues and issues in the process of drafting, expanding and testing models. The analysis of the textual components of annual accounts is carried out on a multiword phrase to better understand the results of a comprehensive recognition of the indicators and of good practice.
content.title_en: The detection of fraudulent financial statements using textual and financial data

content.text: The study of the effects of anthropogenic influences on abundance and composition of Vibrio coastal communities. The study examined the effects of invasive species on the Baltic Sea and aquaculture on the Chinese island of Hainan. While N. melanostom was identified as a possible novel reservoir for Vibrio communities, aquacultures could change Vibrio communities in Abundance and composition in these communities. This showed that anthropogenic factors potentially influence Vibrio coastal communities. <ger> This work studies the interaction between anthropogenic factors and the abundance and composition of coastal Vibrio communities. The role of invasive species were studied using Neogobius melanostom as an example for the Baltic Sea and the impact of aquatures were observed on the shark.
content.title_en: Vibration in anthropogenic coastal ecosystems

content.text: Development of a virtual power plant based on a flexible biogas plant and a photovoltaic system. The main objective of this study is to develop integrated power generation through virtual power plant (VK) to respond to load demand or deliver electricity market products. The results show that multi-agent based system (MAS) and Smart Grid architecture model (SGAM) allow the integration of intermittent renewable energies (photovoltaics) and flexible power plants (biogas, battery) into a VK. The developed VK can respond quickly to changing requirements (legal, economic, technical) without compromising the stability of the system. <ger> The aim of this project is to develop an integrated power plant through Virtual Power Plant (VPP) in order to respond to demand by considering a corresponding power market product. The results show that the deployment of Multi-Agent based system (MAS) and Smart Grid measurement of the control system (AM).
content.title_en: Development of a virtual power plant based on a flexible biogas plant and a photovoltaic system

content.text: Challenges in software development in the Scrum process: to the necessity of the atypical contractual design of the BGB contract types in practice. The BGB contract types in the form standardized in the BGB do not adequately represent the legal requirements of software projects in the Scrum process. This work examines the possibilities to which extent by contract design nevertheless interested regulations can be achieved for both parties. Starting with an overview of agile software development, the suitability of the standardised BGB contract types for software projects in the Scrum process is examined. In the main part of the work, practical regulation options by contract design are presented for those regulatory objects, which are insufficiently or not represented by the BGB contract types standardized in the BGB.
content.title_en: Challenges in software development in the Scrum process : the necessity of the atypical contractual design of the BGB contract types in practice

content.text: Profiling under the GDPR: Digital personality profiles in the conflict between corporate interest and personal rights. With the term "Profiling", the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) records data processing in different economic sectors that affect the evaluation of personality aspects. The legal definition raises questions: Is profiling to be treated differently from "normal" processing under data protection law? What personal rights risks are threatening and how can these be economically mitigated? Can profiles be marketed in compliance with data protection? Under the umbrella of a "profile formation perspective" the author shows in cross-sectoral comparison basic rights acceptable and at the same time practical framework conditions for individual employee, customer and insured profile formations.
content.title_en: Profile formation under the GDPR : Digital personality profiles in the conflict between corporate interest and personal rights

content.text: Error correction of memory errors with low-density parity check codes. The error correction in coding theory deals with the detection and correction of errors during transmission and also backup of messages. Here the message is encoded by additional information into a code word. These coding methods have different claims, such as the maximum number of errors to be corrected and the speed of correction. A common coding method is the BCH code, in which industrially for up to four error corrected codes are used. A disadvantage of these codes is the technical throughput time for the calculation of the error points with increasing code length. The dissertation introduces a new coding procedure, in which a long code is generated by special arrangement of smaller code lengths of a BCH code. This arrangement is done via another special code, an LDPC code, which is designed for faster error detection. For this a new design procedure is presented, which provides a code ...

content.text: The survey, the subject of the survey, the survey, the study: the care of the nursing staff in Rhineland-Palatinate. The aim of this study is to trace the situation of the nursing staff from the perspective of the nursing staff in Rhineland-Palatinate. The central question is how the nursing staff perceive their everyday work and the working conditions in nursing care. The focus is on the study of the perceived workloads, the self-assessed burnout risk, the handling strategies used and the work satisfaction. An online survey among members of the Rhineland-Palatinate State Care Chamber (n=830) from 2017 serves as a basis for an online survey of the members of the Rhineland-Palatinate State Care Chamber (n=830) from the year 2017. Overall, the nursing staff are exposed to special burdens arising from the multiple factors that result from the study's management of the nursing staff. For example, an on-line survey of the employees' health care department and the increasing number of working hours under constant pressure. In addition to the problems and risks, the work performed by the nursing staff can also be used to determine the risks of the management of the patient.
content.title_en: Working conditions and workloads in care : An empirical study in Rhineland-Palatinate

content.text: The additive manufacturing of a hypereutectic aluminium-silicon alloy for the production of mirror substrates is an easy process. This work describes the production of a hypereutectic aluminium-silicon alloy by selective laser melting and the use of this process for the production of metal optics. This approach enables metallic mirrors for space applications with a high reduction in mass. Aluminium with 40 % silicon has a thermal expansion coefficient adapted to the polishing layer of chemical nickel-phosphorium. This is used to realize athermal metal optics in a temperature range of -185 °C to 100 °C. This adaptation is demonstrated for the additive material. Process parameters for the processing of AlSi40 powder by selective laser melting are fundamentally developed. By optimising a production of structures with sizes below 0.5 mm is possible. The resulting porosity remains below a value of 0.1 %. Studies on the mechanical and thermal behaviour of the generated material are shown by the applicability as substrate material for metal optics. A design approach is not used negatively by the design of the conventional methods.
content.title_en: Additive manufacturing of hypereutectic aluminium-silicon alloy for the manufacture of mirror substrates

content.text: The avant-garde of computerization: hacking cultures of the Federal Republic and the GDR. Hackers and Haecksen are part of the avant-garde of computerization. Since the late 1970s, they have formed self-interested computer users in the Federal Republic and the GDR with relevant knowledge. They playfully adapted the medium, created contact spaces and thus actively contributed to the process of computerization. Through their border crossings, they showed opportunities and risks of digitization. Julia Gül Erdogan investigates the emergence of hacking cultures in East and West Germany. She analyses how their partly subversive practices challenged power structures in politics, economy and society. At the same time, the work illustrates common ground and differences between the early sub- and counter-cultural computer use in the two German sub-states.

content.text: Identity management in ICT systems: Theoretical justification of a mediation agent for negotiating personal identities. The subject of personal data protection pursuant to Article 4(1) GDPR is extended to the protection of context-specific personal identities. Given the simultaneous realization of cultural, economic and social identity, for example, a mirror image protection from the offline context is required for the online context. This requires the play-theoretical negotiation capability of images of personal identities, so that self data protection can be effectively exercised with a mediation agent. Accordingly, an iterative "identity management by design" should become a technical design requirement in order to meet the principle of a negotiable personal identity in the online context.
content.title_en: Identity management in ICT systems: Theoretical justification of a mediation agent for negotiating personal identities

content.text: The enforcement of consumer rights : a comparative analysis of consumer law enforcement in France, the Netherlands and Germany. The enforcement of consumer rights is considered to be deficient. In order to bring consumer law into practice, Germany, France and the Netherlands traditionally pursue different approaches. European measures also have an increasing intensity in the national enforcement structures. The work presents the different forms of consumer law enforcement in Germany, France and the Netherlands. In this context, individual, collective and regulatory legal instruments and their importance in the legal system are examined in greater detail. Based on a comparative analysis, a separate approach to the enforcement of consumer rights is presented. The enforcement of consumer rights is also considered as deficient. Germany, France and the Netherlands have traditionally taken different approaches to ensuring that consumers are legally enforced effectively.
content.title_en: The enforcement of consumer rights: a comparative analysis of consumer law enforcement in France, the Netherlands and Germany

content.text: Collective agreements in the EU company transfer law: the maintenance of working conditions agreed in collective agreements in accordance with the EU company transfer directive 2001/23/EC. Company transfers are widely used in business life. To what extent the purchaser of a company applies collective agreements depends on factors such as the wage fixing or the interpretation of reference clauses. The assessment of the legal situation often encounters difficulties. After the ECJ has dealt with the complex of issues on several occasions, the time has come for a legal location determination. The power imbalance in the employment relationship is predicated on collective contract law. Building on this finding, fundamental issues such as the classification of reference clauses, the applicability of the EU fundamental rights charter to favourable national law, the social deficit of the EU fundamental agreements and the prohibition of abuse are dealt with.
content.title_en: Collective agreements in the EU company transfer law: the maintenance of working conditions agreed in collective agreements in accordance with the EU company transfer Directive 2001/23/EC

content.text: The interaction of the bundled lines of the high and maximum voltage networks of different frequency and nominal voltage. The present work is dedicated to the analysis of interactions in the bundling of lines of the high and maximum voltage networks of different frequency and nominal voltage and investigations on the possible dangers for operation. An influence model for the consideration of interactions due to capacitive and inductive coupling between interconnected lines is proposed. The model depends on several parameters which can disrupt the operation of networks. When performing repair work of the bundled lines the dangerous contact voltage must be taken into account, since the inadmissible limit values can be reached. In view of this, the method of mathematical modelling of the expected contact voltages is developed in the work with consideration of the person's physical resistance. The implementation of the influence model and the developed method for calculating contact voltages is carried out with the aim of validating the obtained results in a field test. The comparison of the measurement and calculation results shows that the developed mathematical network models with bundled lines are functionally applied to the determination of the actual contact voltages.
content.title_en: Interactions of bundled lines of high and high voltage networks of different frequency and nominal voltage

content.text: The use of the classic tools for the industrial application of artificial intelligence techniques in relation to image processing was well-established. In addition to a detailed research on the state of the art, important indications for the practical use of machine learning were collected. As already existing data sets were used, the first step of the image processing chain - image recording - was omitted. For segmentation, a method based on the clustering was examined and compared with conventional methods. The next step was to detect outliers using clustering. Subsequently, the possibilities of unsupervised learning for the characteristic selection and dimension reduction were examined. Furthermore, large numbers of objects were not included in the survey. In the context of the new data processing, the new data were not included in the survey.
content.title_en: Possibility of supporting the use of unsupervised machine learning methods along the image processing chain

content.text: Molybdenum pincer complexes: synthesis and application in catalytic distillation of hydrogenation. This work describes the synthesis of new molybdenum pincer complexes and their application as catalysts for homogenous catalytic hydrogenation of unsaturated organic compounds. content.text: From civil engineers and social workers: Studies (subject) elections in the context of social milieu and gender. This open access book explores theoretically and empirically how studies (subject) elections in the context of social milieu and social gender arise and uses the habitu concept according to Pierre Bourdieu and the subsequent method of habitus hermeneutics. The path to a university and a specific subject of study is still fundamentally influenced by the social origin as well as the social gender. However, the interaction of these two dimensions in studies of education and gender research is often only insufficiently considered. It is shown that the decision whether and why a study is taken is primarily determined by the social milieu – ‘women' and ‘men' of a social milieu are more than separated here. Within this milieu-specific framework, the social gender shapes the further scope of the study choice. The author Lena Loge is working as a scientific employee at the Darmstadt University and coordinates the nationwide professional and study orientation project ‘Militum-Essenschaft-Bürcheinheit-Berichtung.
content.title_en: By civil engineers and social workers : Studies (subject) elections in the context of social environment and gender

content.text: The Open Access publication describes the opportunities and limitations of the transparency of public procurement for the various actors from the administration, politics, business, science, media and non-governmental organisations in Germany based on a comprehensive analysis of the international research results relating to the opening of public administrative and purchasing data as well as an empirical survey. The author: Britta Reuter has been working for more than 20 years in information and communication technology. content.text: God's Word and Princely Power: 17th century silver altars between Munich and Stockholm. "The silver altars designed for European residences in Frederiksborg (1606), Munich (1607), Husum (1620), Rügenwalde (1637), Stockholm (1651) and Gottorf (1666) have the highest artistic quality and contentual claim within the art of the 17th century. In their complex iconography, the altars made of ebony and silver adapt to their site. They show as artifacts the increasing polarization of Protestant and Catholic potentates in religious politics. Particularly important is the representation of the legal belief as educational structure. Each of the silver altars was subordinated to state political functions, by visualizing political and confessional continuity and identity. Counter-reformation or Protestant forces and legitimizing self-presentation are embodied as the corresponding creedness as a sign of the inherent responsibility of the landlor towards the territory"-----

content.text: A process-based model for the economic-technical mapping of wastewater companies: exemplary application for a rural region with population decline. The model was used for: 1) determining the relevant fee driver, 2) determining future cost and fee development, and 3) quantifying counter-acting measures and determining their potential to reduce marked increases in fees.
content.title_en: A process-based model for economic and technical mapping of wastewater companies: exemplary application for a rural region with population decline

content.text: Water as a common: potentials and problems of commoning in water management conflicts. Water conflicts are difficult to follow, especially in times of climate change, overuse of resources and social distortions. Johannes Euler is looking for the economic and social causes of water conflicts as well as ways to counteract these causes and at the same time to deal constructively with existing conflicts. content.text: The importance of the market power in European merger control: damage theories, remedies, safeguards. Data are the core of internet-based business models. Since the takeover of WhatsApp by Facebook, European antitrust law has been faced with the question of how to deal with mergers, especially with the participation of well-known Internet giants ("FANG"). In what circumstances can market power be relied on as a criterion of refusal to own and access data? What competitive effects of data-based market power are to be feared in horizontal, vertical and conglomerate mergers? How can any commitments in this form of market power remedy? In doing so, the work looks at technical developments such as artificial intelligence as how to deal with merriers, especially those involving the well-known Internet players ("FAcitive da disease") and what is the significance of the market power?
content.title_en: Data-based market power in European merger control : claims theories, remedies, hedging mechanisms

content.text: Tax loss use in the retroactive period : § 2 para. 4 UmwStG: Legitimate fight against abuse or unconstitutional restructuring hindrance?. The taxpayer's freedom of design is in a tension relationship with an effective fight against abuse by the legislator. This is particularly pronounced in the field of tax loss use. The constitutional anchoring of loss use is increasingly being viewed from the perspective. Using the example of § 2 para. 4 UmwStG, the work examines the constitutional limits of loss compensation restrictions. The close link to § 8c KStG is worked out and the regulation is examined against the background of the European abuse concept. The results obtained are the result of a proposal for a new version of § 2 para. 4 UmwStG, which takes into account national and European requirements.
content.title_en: Tax loss use in the retroactive period : § 2 para. 4 UmwStG: Legitimate fight against abuse or unconstitutional restructuring obstacles?
