content.text: The deception of the accused. Misguided investigation methods and interrogation patterns have always been part of the repertoire of law enforcement authorities and are still not to be considered out of the investigation proceedings. The StPO takes its position in the use of these methods of investigation insofar as they establish a prohibition of deception for the interrogation in § 136a, paragraph 1, sentence 1, and orders in § 136, paragraph 2 that the interrogation should give the accused the opportunity to remove suspicions and to present excusing circumstances. Tobias Müller concludes that, contrary to the ruling opinion, the interrogation serves exclusively to grant legal hearing to the removal of a suspicion, which is why nothing must happen in the interrogation, which runs counter to this discharge function. Statements made contrary to this prohibition may not be used regularly. Outside the interrogation, the accused is partially protected from misconducts by the self-conducting freedom of charge.
content.title_en: The Deception of the Indictment

content.text: Integration of inorganic fillers into polysulfon membranes and effects on gas transport properties. In this work, the production and characterization of mixed matrix membranes (MMM) for gas separation is discussed. Various fillers were used to produce polysulfon MMMs in conjunction with the membrane material. Three active and two passive fillers were used as fillers. The active fillers had pores openings that are capable of separating gases depending on the molecule size. This results in a higher ideal separation factor for certain gas pairs than in polysulfon itself. Due to the permanent channels formed by the pores in the active fillers, the gas transport (permeability) is faster than in polysulfon. The active fillers were the Zeolith SAPO-34 and 2 batches of a Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework (ZIF)-8. The two batches ZIF-8 differed in their specific surface, which should specifically include this influence in gas transport studies.
content.title_en: Integration of inorganic fillers into polysulfon membranes and effects on gas transport properties

content.text: Legal enforcement by technology: Basics and legal conditions by the example of the use of filter technologies in copyright law. Automated systems for filtering legally infringing content on the Internet are known in particular for the protection of copyright. However, since the adoption of the DSM Directive, the topic has gained a further dimension. The use of automated systems is now made legally obvious. This eliminates the factual freedom which is considered in the legal system to be a violation of law. This raises new questions which Sophie Beaucamp pursues from a constitutional perspective, a welfare perspective and from a legal theoretical perspective. The central role of the users is the role that will be decisive for the future viability of the use of such systems. Here, the author outlines protective mechanisms that the right-understood individual perceives in his or her subject quality while the potential of the technology is exploited. Due to the use of automated systems to enforce the law, the actual freedom to commit a crime, quasi-implied in the legal system, is eliminated.
content.title_en: Enforcement by technology: Basics and legal conditions based on the example of the use of filter technologies in copyright

content.text: The search for evidence in criminal proceedings involves increasingly frequent access to data stored electronically. In the context of searches, the investigators are allowed to inspect storage media or information technology systems on the basis of § 110 para. 3 StPO. The interventions in the privacy of the data subject are massive; in part they meet the fundamental rights holders without their knowledge. Christian Rühs examines these fundamental rights and pleads for the application of the basic IT law as a central legal protection measure for the transparency of information technology systems. Based on this, he examines the standard of § 110 para. 3 StPO as the legal basis for this review and examines it in the light of the relevant case law of the Federal Constitutional Court for its constitutionality and any need for reform.
content.title_en: Inspection of information technology systems : § 110 para. 3 StPO in the light of the IT fundamental right

content.text: The law imposes a much stricter control of content than is the case with individual agreements. Only a few of these are not included in the terms of the contract. However, the practice is still characterised by individual decisions and one can still hold that: "Jurisdiction does not control where it may, but where it may" (Roth, 1990). This is particularly evident in the field of modern types of contract in copyright and IT law. Wenzel Steinmetz uses practical contractual arrangements to compile the case law and literature that have been given, examines the constitutional and Union law bases of content control and develops a market-based and competitive approach to determining the non-controlling area. Why are general terms and conditions monitored more closely by the courts than individual agreements?

content.text: Control by Prevention : A Critical Analysis of the Burnout Prevention according to Michel Foucault. In view of the global crisis of mental health, it is essential to consider burnout prevention as a government problem and part of a prevention dispositive. Starting from the perspective of governmentality, Jozef Zelinka shows how the prevention of mental disorders is used to secure the neoliberal performance society: subjects are pushed to self-management by continuous risk pressure and risk calculation. The critical dispositive analysis makes these discursive, everyday practice and above all material manifestations of prevention visible.
content.title_en: Governing by Preventing : A Critical Analysis of the Burnout Prevention According to Michel Foucault

content.text: Transnational mining and local politics : political influence in the context of industrial gold mining in Argentina. Mining, social conflicts and environmental disasters - since the 1990s Latin America has been experiencing a historical commodity boom. What role do the operators of mines play in mining regions? How do they create acceptance among the local population? And what political impact does this have? Alexandra Bechtum analyses the actions of transnational mining companies in Argentina and critically questions the social and infrastructure policies that mining companies implement in mining regions of industrial gold mines.
content.title_en: Transnational Mining and Local Policy: Political Influence in the Context of Industrial Gold Mining in Argentina

content.text: Analysis of segmented electrical machines in a motor vehicle drive train. For the integration of electric drives in a motor vehicle drive train with specific construction space, segmented electrical machines are investigated in the present work. Segmented electrical machines are characterized by the fact that the rotor is not completely covered by the stator and thus not cylindrical construction spaces can be used better. After an analytical analysis, assumptions made by FEM calculations are checked, recognized effects at the segment boundaries are examined more closely and the calculated results are finally validated by measurement. The author Sebastian Hermann Franz Schulte was engaged in the preparation of his dissertation in the research department of Volkswagen AG and has mainly dealt with magnetic circuit calculations for electrical machines. Currently, he is involved in the development of electrical drives. Introduction -- Basics and preliminary work -- Investigation of a segmented PSM with varying segment number -- Investigation of the edge effects of a segmented PSM -- Measurement Technical Validation and Interpretation of Calculations -- Summary and Outlook.
content.title_en: Analysis of segmented electrical machines in a motor vehicle drivetrain

content.text: Performance-Based Consultation: a Performance Measurement & Management Conception and empirical analysis of impact relationships. Against the background of digitalization and increasing competition from the Far East, companies are increasingly questioning their traditional business models. The shift towards primarily commercialised value creation is concerned with the design of cross-company networks. For some years, procurement market research has proposed incentive-based contracts as a solution mechanism. Performance-Based Contracting (PBC) represents an approach in which customers no longer buy investment goods such as machines and systems but pay for their use. The performance core is then no longer the physical product, but the overall result associated with its use. It is surprising, however, that research on performance management and performance measurement (PMM) from controlling is hardly taken up – and this is despite the fact that the definition, measurement, monitoring and control of performance has been recognized by PBC research in purchasing as one of the key implementation problems. The present work addresses this precisely deficit in which PBC and control-based development is examined by PBC in the context of an empirical analysis of performance analysis and PBBBB.
content.title_en: Performance Based Contracting : a performance measurement & management concept and empirical analysis of relationships

content.text: The anti-Semitism's transformational features: the position of anti-Semitism in research on racism, ethnicity and nationalism. Anti-Semitism is an equally long-lasting and changeable phenomenon of exclusion. Oliver Marusczyk develops a process-oriented theory of anti-Semitic border pulls in order to make the (dis)continuations and changeables of anti-Semitism tangible. To this end, he combines the cultural sociological boundary pull paradigm with the intersectional research and thus contributes to the re-enhancing of anti-Semitism research and sociological inequality research.
content.title_en: The changing nature of anti-Semitism: the position of anti-Semitism in research on racism, ethnicity and nationalism

content.text: Pedestrian areas and pedestrian traffic in city centres in the Federal Republic of Germany. Since 1972, the number of pedestrian areas has more than tripled, their size has increased considerably, their functions have expanded - and yet the discussion about pedestrian areas is still controversial. In the meantime, many centers of German and foreign cities have been marked by their pedestrian areas. The attractiveness of pedestrian areas is based on their functions and their urban design character, on the other hand, on their "urban life", the diverse activities of their visitors. While most studies focus on problems of retail, traffic technology or urban development, in this study pedestrian traffic is chosen as the starting point for a better assessment and planning of pedestrian areas in the wider sense, i.e. the number and behaviour of passers-by and the activities of the city centre visit. The focus of the presentation of pedestrian areas is on the normative-conceptional aspects of city-centre development and pedestrian traffic in the wider sense as a mirror of the functioning of pedestrian areas. The work is conducted by administrative experts, sociologists and administrators, and associations that are involved in a multi-faceted discussion of pedestrian areas and passers' behaviour, and in research, but also in urban and in urban and in the field.
content.title_en: Pedestrian areas and pedestrian traffic in urban centres in the Federal Republic of Germany

content.text: Solidarity as a practice: the negotiation of diversity in the World Social Forum. How is solidarity possible in increasingly diverse societies? Nikola's sound investigates this question at the level of individual practices. Using the example of the World Social Forum 2016 in Montreal, he analyses the laborious, situational practices necessary in transnational activism – especially between indigenous and non-indigenous activists – in order to establish solidarity against the background of a violent colonial history and unequal power relations. Here, it becomes clear to what extent negotiations and a productive handling of conflicts have a central importance for the emergence of solidarity relations.
content.title_en: Solidarity as a practice : the negotiation of diversity in the World Social Forum

content.text: Siloah - source of life: a cultural history of the Jerusalem city source. The Jerusalem city source is known in tradition and present under the name Siloah, even though its water comes from the Gihon source. An underground channel, the so-called Hezekiah tunnel, leads the water of the source to this day under the southeast hill. For almost two millennia this western outlet of the tunnel was considered the Siloah source or the Siloah Jerusalem. The actual source, the Gihon, however, was forgotten for over a millennium. Today, the water systems of the South East Hill are among the archaeological sites most intensively explored worldwide. The present work deals with the cultural memories of the Siloah. It develops a cultural history of the Jerusalem city source from its beginnings to the present on the basis of a diverse selection of different text and image media.
content.title_en: Siloah - Source of Life : a cultural history of the Jerusalem City Source

content.text: Established Provisionals : Leipzig and the Long Summer of Migration. Using the example of Leipzig, Philipp Schäfer shows that the ubiquitous nature of the Provisional in the long summer of migration in 2015 was not the result of a sudden crisis, but of long-standing debates on issues relating to the handling of refugees on the ground. Based on numerous interviews, observations and political documents, his sociological investigation shows how the local government institutionalized the provisional nature of migration and thus allowed refugees to stay spatially, temporally and morally at a distance.
content.title_en: Established Provisionals : Leipzig and the Long Summer of Migration

content.text: Introduction -- Theoretical introduction to the research field -- Empirical access to the research field -- Results of the study -- Bibliography. School absentism as the illegitimate absence of education and school has long been seen as a primarily urban problem. Against the background of an increasing periphericisation of rural educational landscapes with corresponding problems, the question arises whether school absentism is spreading in these regions and how it is handled. In a triangulative multi-level study, this research committee was examined from the perspective of teachers and other experts. Author Marcus Schmalfuß is a trained special educator and currently works as an academic assistant at the Institute for Promotional Pedagogy of the Faculty of Education of the University of Leipzig. His work focuses on consulting, multi-professional cooperation and school absentism as well as on diagnostic questions.
content.title_en: School Absentism against the background of regional disparities

content.text: The characteristic of the electrochemical deposition of chromium from chromium(III) electrolytes for decorative applications. Decorative chromium layers are omnipresent in everyday life, as they give component surfaces an appealing appearance and at the same time provide protection against corrosion and abrasion. Electrochemical deposition methods, which have been known and well understood for decades, are based on hexavalent chromium compounds. An increasingly stringent chemical legislation limits the use of these substances and makes long-term substitution necessary in industrial processes. Electrolytes based on trivalent chromium compounds have proved to be an alternative and increasingly push to the market. Chromium(III)-based electrolyte systems, however, are not yet an equivalent replacement and show weaknesses in terms of separation rates and optical appearance of chromium layers. This work is intended to provide contributions to the understanding of the separation process and the layer formation from chromium(III) electrolytes, in order to derive measures for optimization based on this, thus the separation process was characterized by in-situ microgravity, measurement of surface-oriented pH values of the deposition of the layer.
content.title_en: Characterization of electrochemical deposition of chromium from chromium(III) electrolytes for decorative applications

content.text: Metal organic compounds of the s-block metals and dibenzosuberenan-based ligands: preparative and theoretical studies. A comprehensive analytically explaining understanding of the non-covalent interactions between cations and electron-rich π systems requires further research. They are essential for biomolecular structures, protein folding and protein-ligand detection processes. Recent theoretical studies of the interaction of simple cations with the curved π surface of the corannulen and Summanens showed that the contribution to interaction energy is in no case more than 50% electrostatic. The influence of dispersive interaction increases with the size of the cation. In this dissertation, based on an extensive literature overview, a ligand system is presented which in NMR experiments provides a flexible behavior in relation to the s-block metal ions selected as counterions. The NMR spectrums demonstrate the purity of the substances obtained and show specific, well-separate signals for the different compounds that allow for further studies to be scalable.
content.title_en: Metal organic compounds of the s-block metals and dibenzosuberenan-based ligands : preparatory and theoretical investigations

content.text: YouTube vs. GEMA: Music and Copyright in Digital Capitalism. »This video is unfortunately not available in your country.« With this sentence, the video platform YouTube fueled the years of debate with the German collecting society GEMA. In numerous online discussions, it was about the appropriate remuneration for music streaming – the GEMA-Bashing followed. Music and copyright were and are a conflict-packed topic. With digitalization, a process that changed the way of producing, consuming, distributing and exploiting music and other creative goods began. This discord undermined previous business models of the music industry and shocked fundamental assumptions in the understanding of copyright. Philip Stade focuses on the special online discourse YouTube vs. GEMA and opens up interdisciplinary and historical perspectives in the sense of cultural studies on the fields of music industry, copyright and capitalism in the digital transformation. In this context, the focus is on hegemonic strategies and the central role of social media. Even if the social and economic upheavals of digital transformation are not yet complete, Stade works out precisely how to understand the relationship between digital capitalism and its exclusive.

content.text: The conformist revolt : the mythology of right-wing populism. Right-wing populism is not a misguided protest against neoliberalism and post-democracy, but a form of conformist revolt. Its core are racist and conspirationist myths: The one's own is overwhelmed by the stranger, because globalist elites have destroyed sovereignty and community. Leo Roepert analyses how these myths try to process the crisis tendencies of the present without having to perceive their social causes. It becomes clear that the right-wing populist struggle against "globalism" and "alienation" aims to restore an order that has always been there.
content.title_en: The Conformist Revolt : The Mythology of Right-wing Populism

content.text: Distribution questions: Perception and knowledge of wealth in the Federal Republic (1960-1990). When and how did social actors from politics, media and science in the Federal Republic of Germany deal with wealth and its social distribution? What role did the (non-)perception of wealth, which, in addition to the growing social inequality, is one of the defining experiences of our present day, play in the enforcement of democracy and market economy? Anne Kurr asks from a historical perspective about the economic cycles of knowledge production to wealth between 1960 and 1990. Wealth – according to her thesis – was negotiated only as a marginal issue in distribution debates, but the discussion about it was politicized in the long 1960s. Whoever was considered rich and concentrated wealth in a few hands remained controversial. The scandalization of a concentration of wealth declined in the 1970s due to the powerfulness of market liberal concepts and only gained a boost after the "reunification" of the economy.
content.title_en: Distribution questions : Perception and knowledge of wealth in the Federal Republic (1960-1990)

content.text: The lost colonial empires: failed utopias in America. "In a broad panorama from the North to the South tip of America, Simon Karsten's zwolf presents little known stories of failed conquests of the so-called New World and describes the multiplicity and serious encounters of indigenous cultures with the newcomers from Europe. This book follows the coast line of the American double continent from the icy Baffin Island west of Gronland over the grune valley of St. Lorenz, the swamp landscapes of Florida and the jungle of Guyana to the Magellanstrasse deep in the South. It pays the story of Monks, Freemen, Courtiers, Missionaries, Renowned Seaherds and Simple Men and Women who traveled to America as servants, farmers, punitives or craftsmen. They all met there, peacefully or violently, on the indigenous cultures of America: small groups of men and women who lived as Jagers and Collectors, farming villagers, spiritual customsmen, female warriors, and leaders of the great colonial and female leaders, and they all made a decisive statement of their own success despite the history of the colonial and the history of the lost colonial empires.
content.title_en: Falling Colonial Empires : Failed Utopias in America

content.text: Hydroelectric projections: an emotional history of hydroelectric power in industrial films. Today, more than ever before, the expansion of renewable energies has been achieved. However, massive investments in the construction of hydroelectric power plants caused conflicts: the vision of the inexhaustible, clean electricity faced concerns about the destruction of nature and landscape as well as the criticism of the lack of participation of the affected population. The historian Fabian Zimmer examines these public debates of the 1950s, starting with industrial films and other PR materials of three exemplary hydroelectric companies: Bayerischer Wasserkraftwerke AG in Germany, Vattenfall in Sweden and Electricité de France in France. The author analyses how the companies used films to manage the public's emotions about hydropower expansion. He works out the narratives and justification strategies of the company PR, integrates them into the broader contexts of debate and thus can show how the 1950s transformed the way in which emotions were dealt with in public debates about energy infrastructures.
content.title_en: Hydroelectric projections: an emotional history of hydropower in industrial film

In addition, a potato starch with an average molecular mass, which is a waste product of the potato processing industry, was used. The starch flow agents were synthesized by chemical modification in a two-stage process. In the first step, the molecular weight of wheat and potato starch was reduced by acid hydrolytic degradation. For the short-chain manioc strength, a degradation of the molecular mass was not necessary. content.text: In the twilight: Studies on the pre- and early history of critical theory. Klappentext: With Max Horkheimer's essay "Traditional and critical theory" written in exile in 1937, critical theory finds its meaning in the post-war Germany, and as a Frankfurt school it becomes an intellectual institution and moral authority. However, Christian Voller shows the origins of critical theory in the catastrophe of the First World War. Social democracy's approval of war credits in patriotic Taumel 1914, the suppression of workers' and soldiers' councils after the end of the war and the rapid Bolshevisation of the revolution in Russia are a shock. Everything is again under review. In Heidelberg's university milieu of the early 1920s, disappointed revolutionaries meet with desperate New Cantians. Together, they turn to Karl Marx's work to undergo a critical reconstruction. Here, too, the productive divide of the new philosophy emerges: it is the theory of social revolution in the sign of its continued failure.
content.title_en: At dusk : Studies on the prehistory and early history of critical theory

content.text: The Paris Agreement on Climate Change: the effectiveness of international climate protection agreements. In 2016, the states concluded a new international agreement with the Paris Agreement on Climate Change to address one of the biggest challenges of the 21st century: climate change. Based on the scientific background and the development of the international climate protection regime, Thorsten Bischof presents a comprehensive legal study of the Paris Agreement. He then examines whether and under what conditions, on the basis of an international treaty in general and the Paris Agreement in particular, it can actually succeed in addressing climate change in time. The author combines legal scientific findings with those of international relations in order to assess the potential of the Paris Agreement.
content.title_en: The Paris Agreement on Climate Change: on the Effectiveness of International Climate Change Agreements

content.text: - The "Hordenung der Disktionenkultur" in social networks such as Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and Twitter has arrived in the general public some time ago and still offers a lot of reason for discussion. The preliminary highlight in the debate about an effective handling of so-called hate crime is the network enforcement law, which provides for the first concrete complaint procedure for social networks - and threatens to violate with a high fine. This work investigates the question whether the network enforcement law is the right instrument to effectively counter hate crime in social networks. The author explains first of all why the civil use of authors of illegal content and the prosecution often reaches its limits and for this reason is inconvenient to the use of the social networks. The work results that the network enforcement law and its amendment are an important step in the right direction, however, remains as before legislative action requirements. The author Sandra Niggemann is currently a legal officer at the board of appeal in Berlin and has completed a course of investigation under the German Federal Office of Public Information and Public Relations.
content.title_en: Hate crime in social networks: A legal classification in accordance with the network enforcement law

content.text: A network of debts: debt relationships and court use in late medieval Basel. Everyday life in a late medieval city like Basel was characterised by debt: small loans and Borg purchases kept the economy in motion, pension purchases made long-term investments possible. Debt relationships connected people from the city, from the surrounding countryside and also from a wider distance in very different constellations. The school's court proved to be an important institution for negotiating outstanding debts of all kinds. Here, creditors could obtain payment promises, threaten seizures and accuse debts. Benjamin Hitz examines the emergence of debts in their social context and describes the influence of factors such as gender, origin and assets of the parties involved as well as the use of the court by various groups of persons. Qualitative approaches, which are based on microstoria and historical practices, combine with quantitative network analyses to form an overall picture of Basel's debt economy, which enabled many to participate in the urban economy, but could also bring them into existential difficulties.
content.title_en: A network of debt: debt relationships and court use in late medieval Basel

content.text: Resisting resource : typology and use of historical farmhouses. An updated view of farmhouses reveals this as a resisting resource - come-over but impressive, full of history(s), but not always appreciated, supposedly no longer contemporary and yet characteristic of a region. Ines Lüder shows in this context heterogeneous practices of use and the struggle for interpretational sovereignty. She develops a state description and typological reordering using the specialist halls and barg houses of the Steinburg Elbe Marchen. In this context, she contextualizes the ambiguous buildings with their interdependencies as part of the transformation of rural spaces and examines them for their potential for future development in terms of building culture.

content.text: Building renewals and demographic changes in line buildings of the 1950/60s: the example of Hanover. Line buildings of the 1950/60s were built according to the model of the "divided and relaxed city", are located close to the city from today's point of view and offer compact, usually low-cost housing. Line buildings are attributed great development potential, however, a "double ageing" of residents and building stock, the concentration of socially disadvantaged households and sales of housing stocks to international housing providers can lead to upheavals and, if necessary, downward spirals. What contributes to whether there is a modernization or a devaluation? What possibilities exist to further develop this large housing stock of the post-war period? As small-scale quantitative studies on constructional and demographic changes have so far been lacking, an analysis of the type of building specific for line buildings of the 1950/60s was carried out using the example of the city of Hanover.
content.title_en: Constructional renewals and demographic changes in line buildings of the 1950/60s: the example of Hanover

Sponsorship terminations lead to positive, neutral or negative effects in the target group under various conditions. Felix Salzer develops an impact model in this book on a theoretical-conceptual basis in order to present all relevant factors of influence, perception dimensions and brand-related effects in connection with a sponsorship termination. The results of the quantitative study in combination with theoretical-conceptional findings enable the derivation of recommendations for action for corporate practice. content.text: The possibilities of IT-based planning and forecasting in crisis situations are the topics of the planning process. Our market environment today is subject to a variety of different endogenous and exogenous factors. In addition to disruptive factors such as globalization and digitalization, global crises also cause increasing complexity, dynamics and uncertainty in the corporate environment, which has led to the deterministic planning models of the past no longer being sufficient and obsolete. Against this background, the author examines how planning and forecasting must be designed to meet the requirements of crisis prevention, early detection and management in a corporate environment characterized by extreme uncertainty. In doing so, the author Klaus Quirin has successfully completed the master's degree program in accounting, auditing and finance at the HTW Saar. In the context of his award he has been engaged in a critical analysis of his individual suitability for a changing process of corporate planning.

content.text: Urban form, urban warning and time : from global regulations to local heterogeneousities. A key factor for the thermal behaviour and education of urban heat islands of cities is the urban structure, the spatial-time, two- and three-dimensional arrangement of the material components of cities (urban form). This dissertation examines the spatial development of 194 cities and operationalizes time as an essential dimension that characterises urban form. Worldwide, the urban form of cities is characterized by homogenisation, regardless of its size and location. The temperature development of cities with different background climates is subject to local regulations. The increases – and in some cases also decreases – of inner-city surface temperatures are diverse, spatially clustered and influenced by the environment of cities. Different changes in urban form can result in similar trends in surface temperatures.

content.text: Reflection and Subversion: Society's self-observation in Twitter and the mass media. The former function reserved to the mass media to reflect society and to make these social self-descriptions known throughout society can now also be fulfilled by social media platforms, when users describe society there and these contributions are widely disseminated. At the same time, the social descriptions spread in social media differ enormously from those of conventional mass media – not least because of the technical infrastructures of the platforms. From the perspective of social system theory, commonalities and differences between these two forms of social self-reflection are elaborated using the example of Twitter. The fundamental rights in their effect as a protection obligation therefore play a prominent role in environmental law. -- The environmental protection content of the Basic Law is examined from the ground up: The presentation covers the historical development of environmental protection obligations in the BVerfG's case law, their reasoning, their protection area, their preconditions and effects. For the practice of particular interest is the involvement in the enforcement of the State to Environmental Protection, both in the legislative and executive courts. content.text: Data-financed apps as subject-matter of data protection law. Apps and software products that are made available to a user free of charge can be summarised under the term data-financed offers. The disclosure and processing of personal user data replace the monetary consideration. The work examines the extent to which the applicable requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation respond adequately to these phenomena. A special focus is on the various data processing processes of data-financed offers and their intervention intensity. Especially from a commercial disclosure of the data to third parties, there are data-related implementation difficulties with regard to the transparency of the processing and the voluntary consent of the user. Based on this analysis, the work provides suggestions which instruments of data protection law should be reformed traditionally to reduce these difficulties. »Data-Funded Apps as an Object of Data Protection Law«: Data-based apps are made available to users free of charge. Data disclosure and data processing substitute consideration, which raises questions about the protection of the processing of the processing of the processing.
content.title_en: Data-financed apps as subject-matter of data protection law

content.text: For controlling shock current events in case of faults in submodules of modular multipoint converters. The short circuit of an MMC submodule leads to shock currents and explosions of semiconductors, which can be mitigated by additional circuits. In addition to high-speed fuses, the RL transformer is suitable for shock current reduction. For explosion protection of semiconductor modules, active additional circuits are used, whose assessment is improved by the explosion integral XI. The connection of RL transformer and secondary circuit thyristor combines explosion protection for semiconductor modules with the reduction of shock current in the intermediate circuit.
content.title_en: For controlling shock current events in case of faults in submodules of modular multipoint converters

content.text: Molecular detection of cellulose and cellulose fragments by cellulosic binding modules & interaction studies between the cytoplasmic domains of Integrin-β1/β3 and the focal adhesion protein Paxillin. Proteins play an essential role in a variety of processes. To understand these functions, it is necessary to clarify their structure and their binding behaviour with other molecules such as proteins, peptides, carbohydrates or small molecules. In the first part of this work, the wild type and the point mutant N126W of a carbohydrate-binding protein from the heat-stable bacterium C. thermocellum were investigated, which is part of a complex that can detect, bind and degrade carbohydrates such as cellulose. In addition, this protein was produced with E.coli bacteria and purified by metal chelate and size-extraction chromatography. Proteins were identified by means of a nuclear spinresonance spectroscopy (NMR) and a protein-replacements were found to be easily intertwined with both compounds.
content.title_en: Molecular detection of cellulose and cellulose fragments by cellulose binding modules & interaction studies between cytoplasmic domains of integrin β1/β3 and focal adhesion protein paxillin

content.text: This is a claim of already paid compensation for the Executive Board: Admissibility and design of "clawback" regulations in executive board contracts. Clawback regulations are intended to enable the recovery of already paid variable compensation for members of listed companies in the event of negative developments. The work is concerned with whether and to what extent Clawbacks are integrated into the existing system of management board remuneration. The historical, economic and legal basis of the board remuneration is comprehensively examined. An analysis of the business reports of the DAX and MDAX companies shows that the concrete design of Clawback clubs is often subject to uncertainties despite their increasing importance for the German stock companies. The author goes into this issue in depth and shows that Clawbacks can be agreed on effectively both terms and shares when viewed more closely. On the basis of the explicit investigations, a design proposal is finally submitted.
content.title_en: Recovery of already paid compensation for the Executive Board : Admissibility and design of "clawback" regulations in management board contracts

content.text: Data sciences and society: the genesis of a transversal knowledge field. Data sciences are concerned with the analysis of large, complex data volumes and thus attract high media and political attention in the context of digitalization. Philippe Saner examines the emergence of this transversal knowledge field around big data with a field-theoretical approach. He explains that this is a cross-field network of expertise, structured by different interests, strategies and power relations. The data sciences thus open up a permeable space, which opens up lucrative possibilities for actors from established fields such as science, economics, higher education and politics.
content.title_en: Data Science and Society: the genesis of a transversal field of knowledge

content.text: The logistics performance of countries as a location factor of foreign direct investment. 1 Introduction -- 2 Foreign direct investment -- 3 Logistic performance of countries -- 4 Conceptual reference framework and hypothesis development on the influence of LPC on foreign direct investment -- 5 Research design of the empirical study -- 6 Results of the empirical study - The influence of LPC on foreign direct investment -- 7 Final consideration of the results. This book examines the influence of the logistical performance of countries (LPC) on foreign direct investment or the international location decision of multinational companies. This complements the classical explanations on the location factors of foreign direct investment with a logistical perspective and combines the two disciplines of international management and logistics research, which are largely independently worked on so far. The study aims to identify those areas of LPC which lead to an improvement of locationatractivity and the competitiveness of economies. For this purpose, a theoretical reference framework is first developed in which the LPC is conceptualized with its determinants and hypotheses on their influence on foreign direct investment. This theoretical approach is dynamically validated in the context of the business administration of the DFD.
content.title_en: The logistical performance of countries as a location factor for foreign direct investment

content.text: The unsafe channels: negative and queer security in cryptology and computer science. Contemporary IT security operates in a bid logic between security precautions and attack scenarios. This paranoid structured form of negative security can be traced from the origin of IT security in modern cryptography, computer viruses and worms, ransomware and backdoors to the AIDS discourse of the 1980s. But security in and with digitally networked media can also be thought differently: Marie-Luise Shnayien proposes the use of a reparative, queer security term, whose practices are not located at the level of technical, but nevertheless do not get along without an accurate knowledge of it.

content.text: The typical multi-electron beam evaporation system for the production of binary and ternary systems for thermosensors was then used to achieve a good improvement in the efficiency of the multi-electron beam evaporation system. In this work, a system of three parallel and individually controllable e-ray evaporators was designed, constructed and optimized based on the world's first commercial three-fold e-ray evaporation unit (e-ray). In this way, a single, binary and ternary thermoelectric system with freely selectable stoichiometry was developed. Special value was placed on the reproducible and homogeneous coating of 10cm standard substrates to enable later use in the production of sensors. In order to optimize the rate determination and implementation of an automated real-time control of the rates, a two-fold e-ray evaporation system was put into operation and optimized in one intermediate step. For the qualification, binary BiSb coatings were produced using thermally evaporated samples, a standard pre-treatment process was further characterized.
content.title_en: Construction and optimization of a triple electron-jet evaporation system for the production of binary and ternary systems for thermosensors

content.text: Information streams in digital cultures: theory formation, history and logistical capitalism. We are surrounded by a multitude of information streams that seem to us to be natural. To describe these digital cultures, media-scientific works develop theories in the flow of a world. Their diagnoses often succumb to a technical fetish and neglect social structures. Mathias Denecke presents a systematic critique of this theory formation. To this end, he traces the history of the talk of flowing information in the development of digital computers and discusses how the term for contemporary descriptions can be made productive.
content.title_en: Information streams in digital cultures : theory, history and logistical capitalism

content.text: Islamic violence in Western Europe: Development and empirical review of a model of explanation of radicalisation and crime. This open access book deals with the question of how and why people want to commit serious Islamist violence in Western Europe, for example in the form of terrorist attacks or violent hate crime. The model of explanation developed in the book approaches the answer to this question in two steps: firstly, it explains how and why people are prepared to kill in the name of an ideology. However, most people who radicalize towards such a willingness to violence do not commit violence. Secondly, it explains the conditions under which this ideologically based violence is culminated in a concrete act of violence in Western Europe. The model of explanation developed is then empirically reviewed. The focus is on the theoretically formulated conditions of the act. These assumptions are based on the example of realized or planned Islamic violence crimes in Western Europe between 2000-2013. Author Marco-Thejesh Lohmann is currently working in the field of Islamism prevention in Germany. He works towards the prevention of the early act of radical violence.
content.title_en: Islamic violence in Western Europe : Development and empirical review of a model of explanation of radicalisation and crime

content.text: The first is the "Moti di Pietà" (the "Moti di Pietà") which was founded in the 15th and 16th centuries, and was based on a Christian economic ethics, especially on the ideas of charity and common good. Inspired by this ethics, hundreds of urban pawnshops were founded in the 15th century in Italy. These "Mountains of Mercy" (Monti di Pietà) gave cheap loans to craftsmen, day laborers and small traders, and offered money and banking services. Tanja Skambraks also examines the history of these pawnshops and their economic ethical foundations in the 15th and 16th centuries. It uses a variety of Latin and Italian sources such as tracts and legal opinions, but also numerous administrative writings such as accounting books and statutes. In addition, there are prospects in the German-speaking area. The study covers the long-term duration of small loans for working poor and deals with the idea of a moral economy with a high relevance for the present.
content.title_en: Caritatative credit : the Monti di Pietà, Franciscan economic ethics and urban social policy in Italy (15th and 16th centuries)

content.text: The conformist revolt : the mythology of right-wing populism. Right-wing populism is not a misguided protest against neoliberalism and post-democracy, but a form of conformist revolt. Its core are racist and conspirationist myths: the alien overcomes his own because globalist elites would have destroyed sovereignty and community. Leo Roepert analyses how these myths attempt to process the crisis tendencies of the present without having to perceive their social causes. It becomes clear that the right-wing populist struggle against "globalism" and "alienation" aims to restore an order that has always been there.
content.title_en: The Conformist Revolt : The Mythology of Right-wing Populism

content.text: Transparency through committees?: parliamentary committees of inquiry in response to corruption scandals in Germany (1873-1973/74). The term "transparency" was only used in the 1970s. Nevertheless, Sandra Zimmermann shows on the basis of six case studies that transparency has been discussed since the German Empire. It was conceived in particular as an anti-corruption remedy and thus called for in connection with corruption scandals. Parliamentary committees of inquiry or commissions, which were often used to clarify such scandals, played an important role in this process. In them transparency was demanded and discussed. The committees should investigate the scandal through transparent investigations, clean Parliament and calm the population.
content.title_en: Transparency through committees? : Parliamentary committees of inquiry in response to corruption scandals in Germany (1873-1973/74)

content.text: "In front of the judge's chair of contemporaries and public meetings": the case of the Prussian state servant and late enlighter Hans von Held. Hans von Held (1764-1842), an official and writer working in the eastern parts of the Hohenzollern monarchy, was notorious as a writer of various revelations and pamphlets. Due to his journalistic activity he suffered criminal transfer, fort and impeachment. Using the example of Held, the study sheds light on the tension between the state and public in Prussia around 1800, the struggle for political influence, the press campaigns of radical writers against the administrative elite, but also the beginnings of state public relations, censorship practice and the pursuit of political journalists of the time.
content.title_en: "In front of the judge's chair of contemporaries and public meynung": the case of Prussian state servant and late reconnaissance Hans von Held

content.text: From popularists and false players: the populism accusation in Germany. For more than 40 years, the accusation of populism has been a popular means of democratic exchange of hits by political opponents. Based on the empirical analysis of his work in the German Bundestag, Jan-Holm Sussieck investigates the question of who formulates and analyses his content and context towards whom. The assumption that outside parties such as the AfD would be stigmatized in this form does not stand up. At the same time, the understanding of populism represented in current political science covers, according to the knowledge, only a small part of what is negotiated under it. In order to be analytically justifiable in its use in political practice, the author proposes to take sociologically the many everyday populism accusations within the political mainstream, especially the many everyday ones.
content.title_en: By folk and fakers : the populism accusation in Germany

content.text: Riskful thinking : the function of human-machine analogy in media science. Media science often operates with equally over-stretched and long-lasting analogies. Seduced by the coupling potential of analogies, it thus gives away parts of its genuine theoretical potential and sometimes risks fatal follow-up costs. Melina Kirchartz reveals the still underestimated constitutive role of prominent analogies such as the one between man and machine for the genesis of theories. The view on the theoretical structure of media science itself promotes a argumentative strategic phenomenon that must be brought to the attention of the humanities discourses.
content.title_en: Riskful thinking : on the function of human-machine analogy in media science

content.text: The relevance of digitalisation in day care centres: Perspectives of pedagogical specialists and (professional) school teachers in the context of a qualitative interview study. Klappentext: With a high dynamic of development, digitalization is currently changing the living world of many people. Children also grow up with digital media and devices and see them as natural components of their life through an omnipresence. With a view to growing up in digital life worlds, this study explores the relevance of the topic of digitalisation in the pedagogical work in day care centres and in the school education of future educators. At the same time, the focus is on where empirical vacancies currently exist within this topic. The author Jaqueline Veenker has studied teaching at Leuphana University at vocational schools with the focus on social education. Subsequently, she was immatrikiert as a doctoral fellow at Vechta University - a research topic of relevance.
content.title_en: The relevance of digitalisation in day care centres : Perspectives of pedagogical professionals and (professional) technical school teachers in the context of a qualitative interview study

content.text: Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysed carbofunctionalizations of novel C,N diacyliminium ions. This work is about functionalizations of C,N-diacyliminium ions under Brønsted and Lewis acid conditions. In this way, access to Friedel-Crafts products with indol derivatives, to α-Aminonitrilen and Mukaiyama-Mannich products with silylene olethers is possible in very good yields. The latter reaction could be transferred into an enantiosselective variant. For this purpose chiral scandium complexes served as catalysts. The resulting α-amineoketon was isolated with an yield of 88% and an enantiomer ratio of 5:95.
content.title_en: Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysed carbofunctionalizations of novel C,N diacyliminium ions

content.text: The Conversos : Christian opponents and defenders of the Iberian New Christians in the years before 1492. The 15th century is the age of the last mass conversions to Christianity on the Iberian Peninsula. Under strong pressure and partly with force the previously large Jewish population was urged to be baptized. Nevertheless, large parts of the Christian majority did not accept the new converts as equal and doubted their legal faith. Against this discrimination repeatedly clergymen and scholars turned with sermons, letters and memorandums. The present study describes for the first time the essential contents of their theology, their special interpretation of the Bible and its roots in the law and tradition of the Latin Church.
content.title_en: The Conversos : Christian opponents and defenders of the Iberian New Christians in the years before 1492

content.text: Synthesis of small molecules for skin cancer treatment with plasma and non-plasma application. This thesis deals with the modification and production of small molecules for use in skin cancer with possible plasma application. Initially, N-glycosylated oxindole and N-glycosylated isatine were synthesized with electronal substituents. Furthermore, synthesis modules were synthesized in regio- and chemoselective palladium-catalyzed clutch reactions with various boronic acids and alkines, which were then converted into heterocycles by Brønsted-acid-mediated cycloisomerisation or alkin-carbonyl-metathesis.
content.title_en: Synthesis of small molecules for skin cancer treatment with plasma and non-plasma application

content.text: Prevention of reading and spelling disorders in the classroom : systematic learning of writing from the beginning. Children with language or attention problems have an increased risk of reading and spelling disorders. Systematic teaching in reading and writing avoids disorders from the outset. The book shows for class 1 what optimised teaching in writing language acquisition can look like and how reading and writing techniques as well as communicative reading and writing can be promoted from the beginning. For classes 2 to 4 the focus is on the learning field spelling. The scientifically sound, practical teaching concept for learning writing language follows the guiding principle "prevention instead of intervention": even weak students can learn to read and write successfully! The 3rd edition has been updated and brought up to date with regard to specialist information and literature. Additional material is available for download.

content.text: Virtual Autobiographies : Construction and staging in weblogs and social media. The progressive mediality of everyday life is one of the great characteristics of the 21st century. The concept of virtuality blurs media boundaries and thus also influences literature. Ricarda Julia Vodermair examines autobiographical aspects in the context of weblogs and social networks and shows how digitalization modifies forms of representation and content and transforms self-construction into virtual self-presentation. Her literary and media-scientific perspective opens up an extended understanding of what virtuality as an aesthetic, structural, social and subject-constituent phenomenon currently constitutes and means
content.title_en: Virtual Autobiographies : Construction and staging in Weblogs and Social Media

content.text: Hereditary regions: Acquisitions and uses of regional heritage in the Wendland and in the Lausitz region in comparison. Cultural heritage plays a central role in border regions not only in the context of home-building, but also in energy-industrial transformation processes: e.g. in the Wendland as a former "zone border area" and in the Lausitz as a neighbour to Poland since the end of the Second World War. Jenny Hagemann examines its underlying historical developments and current areas of action in her interdisciplinary study by combining historical comparison, discourse analysis and qualitative interviews. It provides new insights for heritage studies and regional history alike and offers for the first time proposals for the conceptualization of "regional heritage".
content.title_en: Heredity: Acquisitions and uses of regional heritage in the Wendland and Lusatia in comparison

content.text: Hybrid Deep Learning techniques for interference suppression and high-resolution angle estimation for automotive radar applications. Two fundamental challenges for the automotive radar concern robustness against interference in the same frequency band, as well as the improvement of angular resolution for precise location of objects and persons. In this research work, new approaches of modern signal processing for automotive radar sensors based on deep learning (DL) are being investigated to exceed the performance and robustness of conventional methods for interference suppression and angular estimation. For the training of data-based DL procedures special data sets are required, which are generated by novel hybrid methods. Subsequently, both the effectiveness of these hybrid methods and the robustness of trained models against model deviations and non-idealities are demonstrated. In the example of interference suppression, the advantages of DL in automotive radar signal processing are shown. Successful validation of the concepts is performed by measurements of interferences in the 77 GHz frequency band. Furthermore, it is shown that the presented methods can be used effectively to realize precise localization of the vehicle radar signal processing.
content.title_en: Hybrid Deep Learning Methods for Interference Suppression and High-resolution Angle Estimate for Automotive Radar Applications

content.text: The topic of language teaching changes as well: media and online discourses create a new basis for authentic language action in teaching. Up to now, however, there has been no systematic, discursing linguistic examination of language patterns and strategies in an online discourse relevant to foreign language teaching. This work is based on empirical analyses: the study provides new insights into the interactive constitution of identity and relationship management based on an online discourse on the topic of meat alternative nutrition. Methodically, the work follows central research lines of style analysis and sociolinguistics as well as the socially oriented discourse analysis according to Foucault. The book thus draws attention to the language use in social action as well as to the group-specific peculiarities and differences in specific media environments and shows didactic potential for German as a foreign language subject.

content.text: An information system for predicting the influence of spontaneous volunteers at operating sites in natural disasters. Past natural disasters show that disaster management is no longer possible without consideration of the civilian population. So-called spontaneous workers organize and coordinate themselves and their help in doing so. Their influx of deployment sites has, however, led to massive overloads of deployment sites, which has hindered official disaster personnel on site in coping with their work through this additional challenge. The problems that have arisen from the influx of deployment sites were mainly due to the unpredictable nature of spontaneous workers and the lack of disaster management tools to plan and prepare such scenarios. Using a design science research approach, the dissertation aims to design, develop and evaluate an information system, which should predict the flow of spontaneous workers at deployment sites.
content.title_en: An information system for predicting the influence of spontaneous volunteers at operating sites in natural disasters

content.text: Synthesis of hexanuclear niobium and tantalum cluster complex compounds with iodido and alcoholato liganden. The cumulative dissertation, based on eight publications, contains a total of 20 hexanuclear niobium and tantalum cluster complex compounds with iodido and alcoholato liganden. It describes the synthesis and structure as well as chemical and physical properties. Particularly noteworthy are compounds of the main structural types (M6X8) and (M6X12) with isopropanolato ligandens, 13-CBE cluster complexes and a homonuclear double cluster system.
content.title_en: Synthesis of hexanuclear niobium and tantalum cluster complexes with iodido and alcoholato ligandens

The work takes on the potential of the algorithmic decision-making process and highlights the limits of the use of algorithmic systems in the context of labour law decision-making processes. The work also focuses on the obligation program in relation to the AI use which is merely preliminary to decision-making. The work, based on § 26 para. 1 BDSG, is based on the strict requirements of a definition of exclusivity.
content.title_en: The reservation of human decisions in employment relations: the use of "Artificial Intelligence" in labour law decision-making processes

content.text: The linguistic dimension of socialism: Dominance and group constructions in political speeches on the International Women's Day by Erich Honecker and Hugo Chávez. What linguistic mechanisms can be observed in socialist discourse for the construction of ‘We and the others'? The volume examines linguistically established socialist principles and values in a comparative study on speeches on International Women's Day by Erich Honecker (DDR) and Hugo Chávez (Venezuela). From a political-olinguistic perspective and with discursinguistic methods, aspects of group and dominance construction are elaborated in the speeches. The results show that demarcation mechanisms and hierarchies can be interpreted in a comparative way by analysing the nomination and predictive strategies of the groups that are identified and used as persuasive means in political discourse.
content.title_en: The linguistic dimension of socialism: Dominance and group constructions in political speeches on International Women's Day by Erich Honecker and Hugo Chávez

The project was initially based on dual-double radar data and was then used to analyse the uncertainties of the extrapolation of wind speed and atmospheric stability. The project has demonstrated the potential of obachated forecasting and the ability to predict the future of the turbine.

In the context of the challenge of nosocomial infections in hospitals, the influence of various waste containers on the ambient air was shown. The aim of the research was to investigate the possible influence of the design of three different waste containers (open (O), closed (C), with tread mechanism (HF) ) on the microbial contamination of the ambient air in a hospital of maximum supply. content.text: The role of common-interest actors in supporting common residential projects in Berlin. Community housing projects are increasingly popular in Germany. Despite their overall little quantitative importance, they are attributed a high degree of social relevance. At the same time, a scientific and political discourse on the common-interest orientation in housing is taking place, in which joint residential projects are increasingly being brought to the fore. Here, actors who support common residential projects in different ways are being examined. In this work, the role of these actors is being examined in the case study Berlin. This question is being addressed by means of an stakeholder research and the analysis of five experts interviewed with selected actors. To this end, their perspective on common-interest housing projects, their common-goods understanding, their working methods and their cooperation with other actors is being examined in greater detail. The results show that the actors are part of a well-connected landscape of actors, which is strongly influenced by ideal beliefs and personal relationships. Despite their similar perspective on the challenges and needs of common-purpose housing projects, the actors choose different priorities in terms of their working methods, their target groups and their strategic orientation. The current challenges due to the political and economic frameworks lead to a limited role of the common-use of the common-based residential projects.
content.title_en: The role of public-interest actors in supporting joint housing projects in Berlin

content.text: Text- and data-mining: the requirements of digital research methods to an innovation- and science-friendly copyright. More and more digital methods such as text- and data-mining are used to find knowledge, which offers the possibility to recognize patterns in large data sets and at the same time is the basis of machine learning. The work considers this method from a copyright perspective, taking into account the importance and control effect of copyright barriers, the special interest situation in science law and interdisciplinary findings. The comprehensive analysis structures the complex legal material, identifies shortcomings and proposes concrete solutions. One focus is on the long-term accessibility of the generated research data Digital methods search as text and data mining are used more and more frequently to gather knowledge, thereby offering the ability to reflect patterns in large data sets as well as being the basis of machine learning.
content.title_en: Text and data mining: the requirements of digital research methods for innovation and science-friendly copyright

content.text: Corona and Neighborhood: qualitative analysis of Corona and Neighbourhood in two Berlin districts. The present work examines the impact of the Corona pandemic on the use of its own neighbourhood. Individual mobility behaviour is used as a mediator to spatially understand these changes in relation to the Berlin urban area. In a mixed method approach, a qualitative study with standardized preliminary survey was carried out for the two Berlin districts Treptow-Köpenick and Mitte from late summer to autumn 2020. The starting point of the work is the assumption that initial and contact restrictions, closures of shops and event venues and other measures of pandemic containment such as social distancing during the Corona crisis had a significant influence on the places that Berlin had visited since March 2020. The survey shows that changes in mobility behaviour were especially carried out in voluntary activities, while necessary activities were not affected to the same extent. The choice of means of transport is also affected by this change: While the ÖPNV still registered a loss of use, the car-based approach to the question of adaptation to the city's free-range approach to the city's leisure activities is also more responsive to the issue of the more attractive.
content.title_en: Corona and Neighborhood : qualitative study of Corona and Neighborhood in two Berlin districts

content.title_en: Material aspects of building and craft traditions : spatial programs - building material - natural environment : a Himalayan case study

content.text: The aim of this work was to improve the understanding of the dynamic flow effect by using a wind tunnel to develop a dynamic flow of the wind turbine. The dynamic flow of the wind turbine was then developed by a scaled model wind turbine. Comparisons with IMs showed large deviations from the experiment and a modification was suggested. This experimental work extended the understanding of the dynamic flow effect for pitch steps and represented the relevance of the effect for gusts. The dynamic flow of the turbine was suggested.
content.title_en: Wind tunnel experiments with a model turbine : dynamic flow investigation

content.text: AI-based product development: automated knowledge extraction from existing product generations. Producers are now facing the challenge of bringing innovative products to the market at the most affordable price in an ever shorter time due to the strong global competitive pressure. This creates enormous time and cost pressure, especially for product development, but the so-called time-to-market is crucial for market success. By reusing existing product models and the knowledge contained therein, this development time can be significantly reduced. However, due to their implicit nature, this knowledge base is often not used systematically. However, the increasing use of digital tools and the associated growing data base results in the possibility of extracting, formalizing and making use of this (implicite) knowledge through data-driven approaches. The aim of this dissertation is to develop a method for automated extraction of implicit knowledge in the form of features and patterns from existing product models using machine learning methods. Using learned patterns, for a given design state, the following state of follow-up can be identified in a similar way to the existing model, and the initial knowledge-based assessment of the existing model can be made of the following.
content.title_en: AI-supported production-oriented product development : automated knowledge extraction from existing product generations

content.text: Information streams in digital cultures: theory formation, history and logistical capitalism. We are surrounded by a multitude of information streams that seem to us to be natural. To describe these digital cultures, media-scientific works develop theories in the flow of a world. Their diagnoses often succumb to a technical fetish and neglect social structures. Mathias Denecke presents a systematic critique of this theory formation. To this end, he traces the history of the talk of flowing information in the development of digital computers and discusses how the term for contemporary descriptions can be made productive.
content.title_en: Information streams in digital cultures : theory, history and logistical capitalism

content.text: The role of environmental NGOs in the implementation and enforcement of the Paris Climate Change Convention. The 2015 Paris Convention on Global Climate Change has increased the expectation that states will be held accountable for their contractual obligations. However, the formal accountability mechanisms are weak. Beyond the pure peer review, additional ways of accountability towards non-state actors emerge. Non-governmental organisations promoting environmental protection are involved as transnationally networked actors in the implementation and enforcement of climate change law. The work examines the procedural rules and practices of non-state participation in international climate governance. In this context, barriers and restrictions that prevent effective civil society participation and control are revealed. Numerous proposals and options are presented on how to strengthen the procedural position of NGOs in climate governance. The further development of procedural law contributes to increasing transparency and democratisation of the international climate bureaucracy.
content.title_en: The role of environmental NGOs in implementing and enforcing the Paris Convention on Climate Change

content.text: The analysis and development of a software architecture for intelligent optical inspection. Automatic optical inspection is the most important tool of quality control in modern electronic production. By automated image capture and the execution of pre-defined image processing steps, these systems have largely displaced manual optical inspection. Despite the large degree of automation, human experts are indispensable at many steps of the test and thus potential sources of error. In recent years, numerous approaches have been investigated which individual aspects of optical quality assurance by the application of methods of artificial intelligence significantly improve. For the change of optical inspection towards a reliable and fully autonomous inspection, in this work a model with five phases is presented, which depicts the development steps in this way. The new model differs from previous approaches by a holistic view of quality control and consideration of all process steps. To carry out the implementation of this model, this work shows a new architectural pattern, which can train and execute solutions based on artificial intelligence. By its high flexibility, the new architecture can be applied to a different amount of systems and many different applications of artificial intelligence through the implementation of this field of optical inspection is defined by the scope of this analysis.
content.title_en: Analysis and development of a software architecture for intelligent optical inspection

content.text: Digital assistance systems for collaborative work in unique production. The production of complex unique products (e.g. ships, aircraft or even structures) requires the work-sharing interaction of many different actors. If a fault occurs in a partial process, it affects parallel or downstream work processes and delays the overall process. The digital assistance system for collaborative work presented in this work provides a situation-specific information provision for workers and enables them to create informative fault messages with a few clicks. Players in relevant construction areas are automatically notified and construction managers have the possibility to manage, prioritize and destroy the faults clearly. The system greatly increases transparency in the overall process context and makes an important contribution to the reduction in the lead time. Table of Contents: Introduction -- Basics -- Problem setting and solution -- Collaborative work processes in single-scale production -- Digital assistance systems for collaborative work -- Evaluation of the overall system -- Final consideration -- Literature index -- Appendix.
content.title_en: Digital assistance systems for collaborative work in unique production

content.text: Bentho-pelagic transport of methanetrophs at methane gas seep sites : parameterization, identification, and contribution to the pelagic methane sink. This thesis expands the general understanding of gas bubble-driven transport processes, as the controlling parameters could be defined and the transported methanetrophic bacteria could be identified. In addition, the studies show the special importance of bentho-pelagic transport processes in Seep areas and their positive influence on the pelagic methane sink. <ger> The presented work contributions to the overall understanding of the bubble-mediated transport process, by defining the parameters controlling the transport efficiency and identifying the methanetrophic bacteria transported into the water column via the gas bubbles. Further, it highlights the importance of bentho-pelagic transport the drugtrophic drugstore transport into the water column.
content.title_en: Bentho-pelagic transport of methanetrophs at methane gas seep sites : parameterization, identification, and contribution to the pelagic methane sink
