content.text: What are we working on? : E-commerce platforms understand ethnographically. Platforms are often referred to in social discourse as the defining feature of digital capitalism of our present day. However, it rarely allows insights into this capitalism, which cannot only be regarded as reports of employees. Dennis Eckhardt brings together in this ethnography conversational notes and practices of employees of platform economics. He shows that digital economicization does not make people superfluous contrary to common assumptions. On the contrary, we ourselves are those who create new value-added models with enthusiasm by digitizing our needs and thus opening up new markets in the form of e-commerce markets. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/40.0/deed.de
content.title_en: What are we working on? : Understanding e-commerce platforms ethnographically

content.text: Vitality effects : Knowledge and affect in the media culture of cell biology. How do images create knowledge? What role does aesthetics play in scientific imaging? What changes in the evidence power of the image through digital image production? Bettina Papenburg uses cell-biological research and teaching films to investigate the imaging methods of computer-aided microscopy. From a perspective of media and film-scientific as well as art and science history, she investigates how digital images in natural science research act as media of knowledge. It shows that the professionally trained perception, oriented towards knowledge gain, and affective participation in the films do not behave contrary to each other, but enrich and expand each other. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/40/
content.title_en: Vitality effects : Knowledge and affect in the media culture of cell biology

content.text: Personalized classification of driving style through machine learning. One way to increase the safety of vehicles is to use driver assistance systems. These are often subject to low user acceptance, as the individual needs of drivers are underestimated. In order to increase the level of use of these systems and thus fully exploit their potential, this dissertation presents a personalized driving style classification. As an initialization for personalization, a rule-based classification algorithm is first implemented. Thus, the driving style is classified into three classes using driving dynamics. The chosen approach provides a robust classification based on a small amount of parameters to be adjusted, so that a high practical usability is given. For the implementation of personalization, methods from the field of machine learning are used in this work. Thus, a neural network is used, which is initially initialized on the basis of the rule-based classification. Personalization is based on individual driver vehicle interactions, which are used in an incremental transfer learning. The potentials of the presented methodology are shown in a proband study of the real improvement32.
content.title_en: Personalised classification of driving style through machine learning

content.text: The dynamics of research and society: simulations of scientific processes. How are science and society intertwined and what impact do social processes have on the development of scientific theories? This book describes a framework for the overarching consideration of science. Starting from scientific theory, sociological and socio-scientific perspectives are combined in a computer simulation. A simulation environment developed specifically in Prolog forms the basis for concrete simulation experiments and thus shows cross-relationships between different levels of observation with corresponding factors of influence on scientific processes. For example, the impact plagiarism has on theory formation or the extent to which publication processes or the distribution of research budgets influence. If one considers current trends, such as the increasing number of publications and the increasing importance of third-party funding in research, the social relevance of these topics becomes clear. Accordingly, the framework presented in this book offers not only a bridge between different levels of observation, but also the potential for a tool for controlling scientific processes and framework conditions.
content.title_en: The dynamics of research and society: simulations of scientific processes

content.text: The aim of the thesis is to quantify the influence of higher order increment statistics on wind turbines in the atmosphere. As a main tool for generating wind fields with appropriate statistics, an improved stochastic turbulent wind model based on continuous time processes, called Continuous Time Random Walks (CTRWs), is developed and used as input for computer-based flow simulations. After comparing various inflow methods with respect to the flow pattern in an open channel, it can be shown in rotor simulations that an increased Kurtosis of the increase distribution of the wind field leads to greater fatigue loads both in the rotor leaf segment and in the entire rotor.
content.title_en: Analysis of the effect of intermittent wind on wind turbines by means of CFD

content.text: Optimised charging of electric vehicles as a Markow decision-making process using machine learning algorithms. Electromobility with sometimes high charging power is a challenge for the safe operation of the electrical distribution networks in the future. To reduce overloads in the low voltage, control algorithms are therefore needed to control the charging power of the vehicles. However, the problem arises that the low voltage networks are usually not monitored by measurement and thus input data for control algorithms are missing. In the work, the combination of two machine learning algorithms is investigated. The control of the charging power of electric vehicles is defined as the Markow decision-making process, which is solved by the enhanced learning. An artificial neural network is used for the provision of the input data, which evaluates the condition of a low voltage network. By the interaction of both algorithms, the grid overloads triggered by the charge of electric vehicles can be reduced.
content.title_en: Optimized charging of electric vehicles as Markow decision-making process using machine learning algorithms

content.text: A systematic approach for controlling electrodeposition based on studies of an acidic copper electrolyte. Known academic findings in electrochemistry, such as the Butler-Volmer kinetics, and their changes, allow, among other things, a more accurate insight into the mechanism of metal deposition. Due to a lack of link these academic findings were given little or no attention in industrial process monitoring. Instead, the Hull-cell deposition is used as an indirect approach for the analysis of deposition behaviour. By developing a method that uses the edge element method as the basis for simulation, the kinetic parameters - the exchange current density j0 and the transfer coefficient α - are obtained from experimental Hull cell deposition (reverse determination). This approach is validated by using cyclical voltammetric data of an acid copper electrolyte used in simulation and comparing the simulated Hull cell curves with experimental curves. In addition, the influence of additive is obtained on the structurally kinetic properties, using this approach to lose the physical properties.
content.title_en: A systematic approach for controlling electrodeposition based on studies of an acidic copper electrolyte

content.text: State housing provision. The housing sector has been facing state and society with particular challenges for a long time, especially in the large cities and conurbations. The lack of housing development on the housing market raises the question of state responsibility for adequate housing provision for the population, after the state had largely adopted its own active housing policy at the turn of the millennium, led by economic considerations. Pia Lange, through a (constitutional) legal analysis, explains that the social state is subject to a guarantee responsibility for housing provision for the population under the Basic Law, which, however, cannot be specified as a specific obligation to act. The state has a wide range of instruments available to fulfil its responsibility, which are categorized and systematised against the background of its historical development. Thus, public housing law is configured as its own legal field. Germany's basic law does not contain any fundamental social rights and thus no right to housing. Yet as Pia Lange demonstrates in this study, the social law of the rule of law regarding the law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law law

content.text: The private in the security society: controversial liberties in the USA 1963-1977. The concept of privacy strongly shapes the political culture of the USA and remains at the same time weakly contoured. This study sharpens the concept analytically by distinguishing between privacy/sphere of politics, privacy/public and privacy/governmentality."Privacy" has a long tradition as a bourgeois concept in the USA. In the 1960s and 1970s, the concept fundamentally changed when the Supreme Court recognized a "right to privacy" in family planning, the argument "Privacy" restricted the use of listening technology and the "Privacy Act" regulated the protection of data in the federal government. How did it come about? What was the relationship between these disparate fields? The author argues that claims on "privacy" arose in a condensing "security society" (Michel Foucault). He examined the importance of social and national security, of population and crime debates in the context of Great Society, civil rights movement, Vietnam, the use of the state-laws, and the use of the state-laws, as well as was negotiated.
content.title_en: The private in the security society : controversial liberties in the USA 1963-1977

content.text: In the long 1960s, Russian heritage conservation and preservation of monuments were involved in the Russian heritage organization. In the wake of the major reforms of the late 1950s and early 1960s, which resulted in the demolition of historical architecture, the conservationists tried to determine the fates of monuments in their region – first in their own direction and later within the framework of the voluntary organisation for the protection of historical and cultural monuments. But what did their social commitment in the context of Soviet cultural policy look like in concrete terms? And how did the appropriation of the pre-revolutionary cultural heritage in a place that gained fame as a bastion of old-Russian piety and a germ cell of the Soviet forced labour camp system (Gulag)?
content.title_en: Participation in the dictatorship : Russian heritage protection and preservation of monuments in the long 1960s

content.text: State cyberconflicts: Proxy strategies of autocracies and democracies in comparison. What role do non-state actors, so-called "Proxys", play in state cyberconflicts? And how is the (de-)escalation management different in regime-specific terms? Kerstin Zettl-Sabath compares the state cyber proxy strategies of China, Russia, the USA and Israel with a comprehensive data set for the years 2000-2019. Depending on the political system, there are clear deviations: Autocracies use proxys as "buffers" against democracies in order not to be charged for their actions. For democracies, reports of private IT companies can communicate "acting knowledge" and reduce pressure on action due to political responsibility assignments.
content.title_en: State cyberconflicts: Proxy strategies of autocracies and democracies compared

content.text: The study of the subject-specific quality of an educational video and the form of embedding in learning processes are also open. Furthermore, it is unclear whether there are groups of people who can benefit from explanatory videos in particular. The aim of the work is therefore to develop a theory-based category catalogue for the design of educational videos as learning-effective as possible, to design two explanatory videos of different didactic quality on a topic from the electricity theory and to empirically examine the learning-effectiveness of these two videos. The survey with N = 146 teacher students of the subject-matter teaching shows that there are great learning gains over all treatment groups. The results of this study show that the quality and also the embedding format in this survey do not have a direct influence on the learning increase. The survey with N = 146 teacher students of the subject-matter teaching shows that there is a great amount of learning gains in the study group.
content.title_en: The learning effectiveness of explanatory videos in physics: an examination depending on their didactic quality and their embedding format

content.text: Talking with data: Practices, expertise and visualization modes in data journalism. Data journalists use digital data, which they process, visualize and publish in a journalistic manner. Rahel Estermann develops on a practical and field level which expertise, materialities, cultures and social processes intertwine in data journalism. Data visualizations are shown as common vocabulary, which enables us to speak with the data in two ways: on the one hand, to produce insights, on the other hand, to present insights using data. Thus, the processes of renegotiating epistemological and professional cultures in a data-infected society become visible.
content.title_en: Talking with data: Practices, expertise and visualization modes in data journalism

content.text: The convictions of teachers for teaching and learning of subject content and subject methods and their relationship to teaching-related actions are an important objective of scientific education. An effective approach to promoting these competences is the explicit thematicization of related knowledge. However, in teaching, it seems that the subject-related and only rarely subject-related knowledge is explicitly addressed. Based on the assumption that this difference is partly due to the beliefs of teachers, a questionnaire was used to identify the beliefs of teaching and learning of subject content and subject methods of N = 175 teachers. In addition, a partial sample of n = 16 teachers was called upon to plan an hour for the development of subject-related skills and to investigate the implementation of explicit subject-related analysis in content analysis. The results show that the gradient differences in the target-specific beliefs of teachers are not relevant to the topic. Thus, for example, these often are the conviction that explicit topic-setting of knowledge is effective for both objectives, but that the content-related content is not used as an explicit topic.
content.title_en: Convictions of teachers in teaching and learning of subject content and methods and their relationship to teaching-related action

content.text: Promotion of digital skills in vocational teacher training: A design-based research study at the Justus Liebig University in Gießen. The lack of digital competence of (vocational) teachers, teacher students and pupils results in a "digital vicious circle". The author develops, tests and evaluates in his dissertation a concept for an online seminar within the vocational teacher training at the Justus Liebig University in Gießen. The central component of the seminar is the self-production of explanatory videos, which promotes digital competences in a low-screw way and contributes to sensitization for the topic of digitisation in the field of action school. The author derives general conditions of success and recommendations for the digitalisation-related professionalization of prospective vocational teachers from the results of the practical study in the context of the study location in Gießen.
content.title_en: Promotion of digital skills in vocational teaching : A design-based research study at Justus Liebig University in Giessen

content.text: Subjective rights to research data : de lege lata and de lege ferenda. Are researchers entitled to research data? Friederike Knoke makes a change of perspective and instead of accessing scientific products, investigates the legal position of scientists who generated them in the context of their research activities. To what extent do property, ownership, copyright, patent law, performance protection, secrecy and data protection law confer powers on research data and to what extent should this happen? Answering these questions not only affects the relationship between exclusivity and availability of research data, but also the scope and legitimacy of intellectual property rights and the legal collection of data and information. The author opens up the need for protection of researchers through an empirical investigation and develops a concept for powers to research data de lege ferenda.
content.title_en: Subjective rights to research data : de lege lata and de lege ferenda

content.text: Neuroscience in Critique : Positioning in the Economized Science System. Neuroscience research has been and is the subject of diverse criticism. In addition to implicit philosophical and socio-theoretical basic assumptions, methodological approaches are also problematized. Eileen Wengemuth offers a comprehensible summary, systematically classifys the various criticisms and examines the question of what neuroscientists themselves criticize about the subject and how they position themselves on different criticisms. Furthermore, it explains how in-depth discussions within neuroscience are mediated by the framework conditions of economized science as well as by different scientific understandings.
content.title_en: Neuroscience in Criticism : Positioning in the Economized Science System

content.text: Work and health in late modern age : occupational prevention in the conflict between individualization and top-down structure. More and more! In this performance-oriented dictum work-related health risks are omnipresent. Socially, their prevention is focused in the company prevention, which is traditionally oriented towards accident prevention and male industrial work. In contrast to this, the demand for more flexibility and commitment from late modern service societies stands. Marie Jelenko examines how the management of increased requirements and the associated health risk is discharged on the shoulders of the individual.
content.title_en: Work and health in the late modern age : occupational prevention in the conflict between individualization and top-down structure

content.text: Zeiten in Deutschland 1879-1919 : Konzepte, Kodices, Konflikte. Klappentext: Why did the idea of a "Central European Time" (CET) emerge in the German Empire? Why did it come here in 1916 for the first time to the regulation of a "summer time"? What experiences were made with the "eight-hour day"? And to what extent did people at all oriented themselves to official specifications of abstract time? Caroline Rothauge deals with these and other questions on a broad source basis and taking into account transnational interactions and technical-material aspects. Her historical study shows that temporal negotiation processes in Germany between 1879 and 1919 were highly dynamic and conflicting. They did not result in a standardized form of time order, but rather - paradoxically - led to a further pluralization of times. Thus Rothauge's book offers a nuanced view of the German Empire, a 'long' 19th century and the '(high) moderne'.
content.title_en: Times in Germany 1879-1919 : Concepts, codes, conflicts

content.text: The development of a cognitive assistance system for the use of experience in quality management. Knowledge in an organization is now an important production factor and leads to decisive competitive advantages in the global market. Particularly valuable for companies is the experience knowledge that arises context-dependent and is retrieved due to situation.Quality management depends on this knowledge because of its competence requirements, because unstructured problems can often only be solved in an experience-guided manner. Moreover, the experience knowledge is the source of any creativity that is absolutely necessary in the problem-solving process.In the present work, a cognitive assistance system is developed that supports the human ability to remember cognitive events and situations.The developed system provides knowledge that is classified as relevant on the basis of a context situation. This leads to the provision of the situation-oriented experience knowledge and enables an effective problem-solving in the work process.
content.title_en: Development of a cognitive assistance system for the use of experience in quality management

content.text: The car, which is a more flexible counter-player, influences architecture from the modern era to the present. Erik Wegerhoff, an architectural historian, tells the story of this special relationship between movement and statics for the first time: he is dedicated to Le Corbusier's fascination with racing cars, the beauty of the straight line, Erich Mendelsohn's Mossehaus as a tranquilizer for Berlin traffic, a land without pedestrians, the struggle of the ADAC against the parking space need, a spa at the end of the road - and the ecologically conditioned braking movement of cars and architecture. As a side by side, the scenes of this relationship and the new view of famous and less known buildings create another, highly original architectural history of the 20th century - entertainingly written and richly illustrated
content.title_en: Automotive and Architecture : a Creative Conflict

content.text: "Transparency is needed in Bonn": the Flick affair and the implementation of a new political ideal, 1975-1987. The Flick affair has its fixed place in contemporary history. Transparency is one of the most popular keywords of today's political debates. Martin Mainka is looking for the historical roots of this phenomenon: in the wake of one of the largest political scandals in the Federal Republic of Germany – in the 1980s it was revealed that the Flick group had spent years on secret political donations – transparency gained in importance as part of new democratic concepts; representative democracy and established parties lost legitimacy and confidence. Expectations of politics changed; new political actors representing a different understanding of democracy entered the political stage. Against the background of increasing moralisation of public debate, a new harshness of party criticism and the accusation of corruption, transparency became the ideal and guiding concept of federal German politics – whether in the investigation committee of Flick or in the reforms of party financing and the rules of conduct for members of parliament.
content.title_en: "Transparency is needed in Bonn": the Flick affair and the implementation of a new policy ideal, 1975-1987

content.text: The mass housing construction was a response to the lack of housing in Yugoslavia caused by industrialization and urbanization and still shapes the post-Yugoslav urban fabric. The meaning of mass housing construction goes far beyond its materiality. Starting from the concept of the media arena, the book leads through the levels of discussion on construction site, housing, housing and image. The study tells a cultural history of mass housing construction in Yugoslavia along with discussions in the specialist public and popular culture – from the first architectural designs in the 1950s to the expansion of mass housing culture in the 1960s and the increasing criticism in the 1970s and 1980s to the destruction in the Yugoslavian wars in the 1990s and the fictional reinterpretations in the 2000s. At the same time, the volume discusses intra-Yugoslavian commonalities and asymmetries.
content.title_en: Hard currency concrete : a cultural history of mass housing construction in socialist Yugoslavia and its successor states

content.text: The introduction of standardized times in Germany: time-reforms between industrialization and national state formation. What time is it? This supposedly simple question caused a growing headache in the course of the 19th century. Industrialization made it necessary to standardize time: the old, sun-determined time periods no longer fit modern times. After initial unifications by railway times, the German Reich also devoted itself to synchronisation to the valid time regime until the present: in 1893, the MEZ introduced a single time for the first time in Germany, which should contribute to the formation of identity in the young nation state.In the following decades, the question of new state time regulations remained the subject of intense social debates. This was the first time that summertime was introduced during the First World War, as well as the transition to the 24-hour census. Just as German politicians and scientists fought around the time, which standards established themselves and the manifold compromises that had to be reached by the population, Felix Schmidt presented them in detail for the first time.
content.title_en: The introduction of standardized times in Germany : Time-reforms between industrialization and nation-state formation

A multi-theoretical, value-based evaluation approach differentiated success criteria and factors. It becomes clear that climate protection and energy transition represent an enormous overall societal design task?

content.text: Teaching staff and learners: an asymmetrical relationship: a reconstructive study of experiences and habituated orientations of teachers. The relationship between teacher and learner is characterized by a complex asymmetry. It is considered to be constitutive of the pedagogical relationship, but also a problem of action to be dealt with by the teacher. This reconstructive study examines the habituated handling of teachers with asymmetry in interaction with learners. It proposes a heuristic conception of the asymmetrical relationship structure in its multidimensionality and uses documentary methods of evaluated group discussions to examine the habituated orientations and conjunctive experiences of teachers with regard to the asymmetry formation. The results raise further questions about the examination of teachers with the asymmetry of the pedagogical relationship as well as metatheoretical questions on the conception of habituated orientations of teachers.
content.title_en: Teachers and learners: an asymmetric relationship : a reconstructive study of experiences and habituated orientations of teachers

content.text: Against Michelangelo: the pictorial parody in the northern and central Italian art of Cinquecento. The European art scene of the 16th century was dominated by the person and work of Michelangelo Buonarroti. The rapid artistic rise, the loud devotion and the rise of Michelangelo to the norm and unsurpassable authority in art, however, triggered criticism in the Cinquecento. One of the critical art techniques used at the time to delegitimate norms, degrade competitors and discredit works of art was the pictorial parody. The study is dedicated to the study of this particular technique of comision and devaluation by systematic and exemplary research into Michelangelo's "negative" reception in the northern and central Italian art of the time. The first comprehensive study on the pictorial and written critique of Michelangelo in northern and central Italy in the 16th century. A study of the theory, function and manifestations of image parody in the early modern era.
content.title_en: Against Michelangelo: the pictorial parody in the art of Cinquecento in northern and central Italy

content.text: In production planning, it is a daily challenge to find the best machine placement with regard to the company's target. In this process, it is important to decide which product is to be produced on which machine at what time. For application-oriented scenarios, a number of ancillary conditions as well as stochastic influences must be considered. In order to address a problem as relevant as possible for practice, the following intrinsic characteristics of realistic machine placement problems have been included: machine failures, uncertainty in process parameters, planned maintenance and fluctuations in production requirements. With the help of a developed software, the overall processing time is minimized in production. Using the example of a hybrid flow shop from practice, the combination of operations research, simulation experiments, predictions and company processes is evaluated. The author Christin Schumacher is a senior engineer at the Institute for Transport Logistics at the Technical University of Dortmund and has a M.Sc. in business mathematics. This dissertation serves to obtain the Dr.-Ing. of the Faculty of Computer Science at the Technical University of Dortmund.
content.title_en: Adaptable machine occupancy planning of a practice-oriented hybrid flow shop

content.text: Simulations: a means of understanding of the administration and its constitutional containment. The tools of knowledge used in administrative procedures typically rely on experience; they are based on actual observations from the past to draw conclusions from them. However, in some legal areas, they are limited to cognitive limits. Simulations can provide a remedy by creating fictitious substitute realities that are experimented with in order to then return the results to reality. content.text: Cognitive strategy of system regulation: a plea for the reflexive handling of systemic risks on financial markets and in the age of digitalization. System risks are as present in times of digital upheaval as never before. A growing influence of digital intermediaries on the financial market (such as platform companies and FinTechs) and digital business models is inherent in new challenges and systemic risk potentials that do not adequately reflect conventional descriptions of systemic risks. They require a new basic understanding of systemic risks, which largely detachs itself from the value of past crises. For the regulatory handling of them, only a cognitive strategy can be promising, which is committed to the continuous processing of market-immanent complexities and adapts to the dynamic development openness of financial markets. Digitalization offers itself new opportunities to optimize reflective supervisory mechanisms. Since the global financial crisis of 2007, systemic risks have become a core regulatory concern. In view of digitalization and structural weakness, it is possible to change its attitude.
content.title_en: Cognitive strategy of system regulation: a plea for the reflexive management of systemic risks in financial markets and in the age of digitalization

content.text: The sovereign distribution of scarce goods, using the example of renewable energy support: calls for tenders in the EEG as a distribution process. Since the EEG came into force, the basic objective has been to increase the share of renewable energy in electricity generation. With the introduction of tenders, a change from a legal definition to a competitive determination of the promotion of renewable energy was taken. Thus, no longer every applicant is granted a subsidy right when the conditions are met, but the extent of the expansion of renewable energy is precisely limited. This leads to a shortage situation, which forces the state to make a selection among the applicants. Even if such a procedure was new in the EEG, these criteria are known from partly completely different legal areas, in which the public authorities also conduct a tender or distribution. In this regard, the specific specialized law of renewable energy can be considered from a general perspective using the so-called distribution procedure.
content.title_en: The public distribution of scarce goods using the example of renewable energy support: calls for tenders in the EEG as a distribution process

content.text: The existence and regularity theory of the two-dimensional variational calculus with applications on the Plateauian problem for surfaces of prescribed medium curvature. This open access book deals with a theory of existence and regularity for a wide class of two-dimensional variational problems, which is used to solve marginal value problems of partial differential equations. In this context, known results are thoroughly investigated and comprehensively worked out. In part, a suitable adaptation of the prerequisites of some results is made. In particular, the theory is applied to the Plateauian problem for surfaces of prescribed medium curvature in R^3. The author Andreas Künnemann is a research associate at the Institute of Mathematics of the Brandenburg Technical University Cottbus-Senftenberg. His research interests are solveability and regularity questions of partial differential equations as well as the associated theories of functional analysis, variational calculus and function theory.

content.text: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent channel flow with condensation. This work presents direct numerical simulations of turbulent flow of humid air through a cooled vertical channel. The combination of humidity, temperature and mixing convection occurs in the ventilation of passenger spaces. In this application, unwanted condensation on cool surfaces such as windows and windshield poses a problem that affects the use of the vehicle in the short or long term. The interaction between buoyancy, convection and phase transitions equally affects the thermodynamics and fluid mechanics. For the conditions relevant for ventilation in automobiles, the flow of liquid water can be neglected. Therefore, the direct numerical simulation only considers the gas phase and model the influence of the phase transition only in terms of the damp air. Liquid water is either completely neglected or treated as condensate drops after the positive wall deformation. Using simulations with and without phase transition and with and without deformation, the influence of the different factors is examined separately from the free cooling effect of the condensation, the positive flow of the condensation results in the direct flow of the condensation.
content.title_en: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent channel flow with condensation

content.text: Voluntary engagement in child and youth mentoring: a series of social and organizational psychology studies. Mentoring in the children's and youth fields is an important tool for reducing social disadvantage and educational injustice. However, the willingness to engage as a mentor: in the implementation of this study is still largely unexplored. In this study, the commitment to child and youth mentoring is examined in a multi-perspective and multi-methodological manner in social and organizational psychology. It is evident that the mentoring relationship, perceived self-effectiveness and organizational appreciation are of central importance for promoting long-term engagement, while the fundamental commitment is influenced in particular by individual justice and responsibility perceptions.
content.title_en: Voluntary engagement in child and youth mentoring: a social and organizational psychological series of studies

content.text: Allegory, Symbol, Ding: German-language subject poetry from Goethe to Rilke. Starting from the terms ›Allegory‹, ›Symbol‹ and ›Ding‹, this volume is designed to be an ideal model that is supposed to be more just beyond the limits of the term ›Dinggedicht‹, and to be more complex in dealing with the significance of objects in poetry. The three large sections consist of a problem-historical and a practice-related part. In the light of the conceptually evolutionary theory of Stephen Toulmin, the problem-historical parts characterize the development of the terms ›Allegory‹, ›Symbol‹ and ›Ding‹ with a view to object-related significance from antiquity to around 1900 in essential aspects. In the practical parts, poems about objects are analyzed; the ideal-typical model initially mentioned is applied to poems, but under the principle prioritization of the discussed problem-historical aspects. In addition to German-language poems from Goethe to Rilke, which are predominantly in focus, the exemplar texts from other epochs and disciplines.
content.title_en: Allegory, Symbol, Ding : German-language subject poetry from Goethe to Rilke

content.text: The homeless are part of the city. They live among us and yet are hidden in asylums or prisons. Nadine Recktenwald looks into the historical spaces of the homeless. She examines their experiences with urban structures, social state measures and social inclusion and exclusion. An insightful social and urban history of the homeless in the Weimar Republic, in National Socialism and in the Federal Republic.
content.title_en: Rooms of the homeless : urban experiences between care and repression, 1924-1974

content.text: Music and movement in individual pedagogical work: video-based analyses of music- and movement-related coordination processes. How does physical - musical learning become reality? What coordination processes are visible when moving to music? This empirical work provides an insight into movement-related coordination processes for music using a videographed music-educational project with children. A multimodal interaction-analytical research approach was used. Through the theory-based, empirically identified structuring of coordination processes, beneficial factors for music-educational work in the context of "music and movement" could be determined. The findings can thus contribute significantly to the planning, implementation and reflection of music- and movement-related projects.
content.title_en: Music and movement in individual pedagogical work : video-based analyses of music and movement-related coordination processes

content.text: The high-volume of current industrial three-phase two-level grid inverters, and the associated low power density of the entire inverter, are mainly due to the necessary EMC filter. Current publications on the Flying Capacitor Multilevel Topology show the enormous potential of this topology in terms of compact EMC filters and associated high power density of the entire inverter. The result of this work shows how the Flying Capacitor Multilevel converter can look in combination with GaN switches for low-voltage industry applications. Based on the required components of such inverters, a Monte Carlo optimization is initially made. The results of this optimization show an area for the electrical parameters in which maximum power density and efficiency can be achieved for this converter can be achieved. Reliant on the results of a wide range of hardware prototypes, starting from the individual commutation cell to the three-phase converter, are presented. Studies on these prototypes show that there are also high-frequency revolving of the variable frequency of the control is still used.
content.title_en: Optimized multilevel GAN converters for low voltage applications

content.text: Photoinduced excited-state dynamics of small molecules measured in cellulo. The photophysical properties of molecular probes in solutions can provide insights into the excited state dynamics in cells. However, the cellular environment is complex. Modeling the dynamics of the excited states solely on the basis of the data recorded in solutions would therefore not be valid. Therefore, the work presented in this dissertation illustrates the need to understand light-induced processes of molecules that can be used as potential sensors, cellular dyes and photodrogens. A corresponding analysis of such systems could be demonstrated in a complex biological environment in the middle of time-resolved pump-probe spectroscopy. Within the framework of this work, it was shown that this approach represents a promising strategy for evaluating the performance of functional light-driven molecular components.
content.title_en: Photoinduced excited excited-state dynamics of small molecules measured in cellulo

content.text: The invisible living space: residential efficiency as a response to housing shortage, climate crisis and loneliness. Klappentext: Many people are looking for housing, but new construction does not solve the problem: it is expensive, consumes space and pollutes the climate. A solution promises the "invisible living space" - unused rooms of older people after the children's departure. Daniel Fuhrhop examines the potential of housing efficiency through social programs such as the mediation of sub-letters according to the model "living for help" or the relocation and conversion of such apartments in the context of housing mediation. His conclusion: Overall, 100,000 apartments can be created annually - without climate pollution and with the chance of proximity and neighbourhood.
content.title_en: The invisible living space : Housing efficiency as a response to housing shortages, climate crisis and loneliness

content.text: Digital diseconomy: Unproductiveness, inertia and excess in the digital environment. Parents' warning that they are watching what they share online is omnipresent. Data protectionists are alluding to this and are advocating a conscious and economical use of services and data. However, a digital diseconomy is opposed to these warnings and is seeking critical handling of digital contemporary culture not in asceticism, but in excess. Artworks, images and data are "too much," and are constantly coming up and repeating themselves. Sebastian Althoff analyses this unproductive mode of production of the digital with reference to approaches of governmentality, queer theory and theories by George Bataille and Roger Caillois and shows a practice that creates inertia rather than flow.
content.title_en: Digital de-economy: inproductiveness, inertia and excess in the digital environment

content.text: Lonely dying and undiscovered deaths in the city: about a hidden social problem. Klappentext: Lonely dying and a socially unaccompanied end of life are everyday, but often hidden social problems. In a multi-layered social science analysis Susanne Loke combines the findings of loneliness, death and inequality research in urban space to innovative results. She illustrates the ambivalences of a lonely and undiscovered death as the end point of a downward spiral of loneliness and social isolation or exclusion. Field research in a dying social space gives marginalized people the word that otherwise are not heard, and leaves readers partially knocked back.
content.title_en: Lonely dying and undiscovered deaths in the city: about a hidden social problem

content.text: The key as an object in the course of time. In the world of objects, the key is one of the most important and oldest objects of human use. The life and values of civilized cultures are co-determined by this object. In this work, the transformation of a universal product of today's world of things is put into focus. Increasingly, objects of the world of things are dematerialized. The relationship of the users to the objects loses power of action. The central object of the observations and research is the key as an artifact of the real world of things - in the course of time, in relation to the needs of the users and the decisive technologies. On the basis of structured data, measures for a user-oriented product design are to be shown. Often, the corresponding understanding for the user and its requirements are lacking, in order to be able to incorporate these as part of the product formation process. The object of this work is the analysis of the user generations in the context of technologies with a view to the development of a conceptual design basis. The research work is shown how the historical investigations, the findings of the studies and a practice-oriented design process can be used for the purposeful and the future.
content.title_en: The key as an object in the course of time

content.text: State and statehood in the digital age: political governance in change. Klappentext: What about the state in the "digital age"? The change of the state in the performance dimension and statehood in the governance dimension is the rule rather than an exception. For the 1990s, it was described as a transformation by the model change from the "intervening performance state" to the "cooperative guarantee state". In the face of "digitalisation" and other megatrends, the next profound transformation processes are evident. Samuel Greef illuminates the new mix of control forms and instruments as well as a hybrid performance achievement that shape the state's shape in different policy fields. His conclusion: Germany is today on the way to the "quota patchwork state".
content.title_en: State and Statehood in the Digital Age: Political Governance in Change

content.text: When used in the new generation of solar solar energy, the solar solar energy solar energy solar energy solar energy solar energy solar energy solar energy solar energy solar energy solar energy is a renewable energy form that is available to every country of the earth free of charge. Therefore, compared to nuclear energy, wind energy and blue energy, it is the most promising alternative to fossil energy. In this work, broadband materials for solar energy production are produced as light absorbers for applications for solar energy conversion, such as power generation, water vapour generation and hydrogen generation. First, black silicon (b-si) is used for photo-energy conversion (b-si) with a variety of micro-nanostructures by reactive ion etching (RIE).
content.title_en: Broadband solar energy harvesting enabled by micro and nanostructured materials

content.text: School management and digitalization: Conditions and challenges for the acting of school leaders. Increasing digitalization changes school - and thus also the daily work of school leaders. But how exactly do the resulting partly new conditions of action in the context of the digital look exactly? Ulrike Krein has accompanied school leaders in their everyday work and observed with the method of shadowing. Using a multi-perspective and context-sensitive approach, she thus discloses various research ideas and shows links to other research disciplines. From this, new possibilities are opened up for the practice and action of school leaders.
content.title_en: School management and digitalization: conditions and challenges for acting as school leaders

content.text: The work examines the data protection implications of the environment in highly automated vehicles. In order to be able to drive highly automated, the vehicle environment must be recorded and evaluated. To do this, numerous data of road users are required, such as passenger images or vehicle registration marks. It must be taken into account that the environment recording is not a "classical" video surveillance, but a camera technology that uses characteristics of the raw material and only partly stores raw images for further development. Currently, there is no clear legal situation regarding data protection aspects for this technology.Therefore, the focus of the work is on selected issues that arise from the regulatory framework of the General Data Protection Regulation. Among other things, the possible categories of personal data, the legality of processing and the provision of information obligations are examined in more detail.
content.title_en: Selected data protection issues in the field of environment acquisition for highly automated driving

content.text: Parliamentary police violence in the European context: a political cultural history. Parliaments were and are at risk. They can be prevented by obstruction and violence in the plenum, but also by outside unrest in their work. Not only since the "storm" on the US Capitol is evident: Parliament as a "holy place" needs special protection so that the elected representatives of the people can peacefully discuss and decide on effective solutions for the benefit of the whole.The study sees itself as a cultural history of the parliamentary police. The focus is on conflict and crisis situations in the history of parliamentarism. The author describes the emergence of parliamentary protection as a transnational learning and transfer process, in which various models of parliamentary culture and the self-understanding of the legislative organs can be identified.
content.title_en: Parliamentary police force in the European context: a political cultural history

content.text: The D-D-Method of Simulation is a comprehensive 1D/3D simulation method in which the exact temperature distribution on the piston is first calculated via a 0D/1D motor model and then implemented as an edge condition in a transient wall temperature model in order to be able to display the local instationary wall temperature vibrations during combustion in 3D CFD simulations.In the course of the validation using surface temperature measurements in combination with a developed analytical soot layer or material correction, the author shows that the new workflow as well as the selected heat transfer model can provide basically satisfactory results and can be used for future simulation-based combustion process development.The content of the D-D-D-Method of Conversion Basic studies on the D-D-Motor model of the D-D-Method of Conversion in the 3D CFD combustion simulation The target groups of the vehicle and engine technology departments Engineers with a focus on combustion engine development in the field of D-D-D-Method of Simulation at the D-D-D-Method of Simulation at the German University of Applied Technology.
content.title_en: Experimental and numerical investigations on the wall heat transfer in diesel engines

content.text: The following work examines the insertion and the carrying behaviour of combined pile walls of surface enclosures. This work examines the insertion of the mixture of the mixture and the mixture of the mixture of the mixture and the mixture of the mixture, the spatial load distribution and the consideration of the soil as resistance in the stability detection. A numerical replacement model is developed which reflects the interaction between the ram guide, the carrier and the soil and thus simulates the entire loading process. The spatial load behaviour is described with a vault factor between the carrier and the intermediate bores. For single floors, an approach of the frictional spring stiffness is presented and the earth pressure distribution as well as the consideration of the soil.
content.title_en: For the insertion and carrying behaviour of combined pile walls of shore frames

content.text: The Lockdown : political, philosophical, legal and ethical aspects. What considerations and emotions have influenced the decisions for lockdowns to contain the COVID-19 pandemic, which should have been more closely considered? The author searches for answers and deals with political, philosophical, legal and ethical arguments for and against a lockdown. In addition, she examines the influence of images and the human psyche - for example the urge to act against better knowledge - on the decision for the lockdown. Thus, the book creates an important basis for a sound and productive examination of this policy.
content.title_en: The Lockdown : Political, philosophical, legal and ethical aspects

content.text: The administrative framework is increasingly being used by algorithmic systems. Impact assessments for administrative algorithms can be a means to deal with risks and optimise the benefits. The data protection impact assessment according to Article 35 GDPR provides a first example of this. The planned EU AI Regulation does not provide for impact assessments, but it knows similar procedures with the risk management system and the conformity assessment. Jonathan Dollinger examines the extent to which these rules constitute a suitable legal framework for AI use in the administration. To this end, he compares this legal framework with the model regulations of the European Law Institute on impact assessments for administrative algorithms and selected foreign regulations. He then advocates administrative impact assessments, which provide for a further examination measure and more public participation in relation to the general regulations.
content.title_en: Impact assessments for administrative algorithms

content.text: The copyright of the architect in the case of subsequent modifications of works and the destruction of works. The copyright of the architect in his protected work of architecture is mostly in conflict with the subsequent change of interest of the owner in the building. The compensation of these interests has long been concerned with the case law and literature. Based on the decisions to rebuild the Stuttgart Central Station and the exchange of the multi-purpose room in the Dresden Cultural Palace, the various interests are thoroughly categorized and weighing parameters presented. In addition, the intervention in the author's personal rights of the architect in the case of complete destruction of works is illuminated. If the owner destroys the only work, the work that is to be expressed can no longer continue. The author is also in this case infringed in his copyright right and the conflicting interests must be brought into a balance. Recently, the Federal Court of Justice has proposed a solution to the conflicts in the contract law.
content.title_en: The copyright of the architect in the case of subsequent modifications and destruction of the work

content.text: Key points in the initiation of spatial concepts: a video-based process analysis of basic conceptual learning paths. The extended spatial understanding holds great potential for geographical education. The qualitative study examines how basic conceptual understanding can be initiated using the example of spatial concepts and which learning processes are carried out. For this purpose, learners of Sec. II work on a treatment for the gradual initiation of concepts. Based on video-supported, content-analytical learning paths analyses of variance-maximised cases, basic conceptual learning processes, including key points and learning obstacles in concept understanding are identified.
content.title_en: Key points in the initiation of spatial concepts: a video-based process analysis of basic conceptual learning paths

content.text: Risk and general life risk : to assess socially appropriate risks. What risks does the state resist and which risks it takes? According to a common argument, general life risks are acceptable. But what is meant by the term? Are the arguments behind it viable? Laura Lorena Wallenfels investigates these questions and provides insightful insights into the criteria of public risk assessment.
content.title_en: Risk and general life risk: to assess socially appropriate risks

content.text: Political theory of anarchism : the paradoxical pursuit of autonomy, self-determination and self-organization. The anarchist concept of politics seems contradictory: the rejection of politics is opposed to a reference to it. This paradox arises from a certain way of thinking that helps to weave networks between different currents, groups and discourses. Thus, the possibility of responding to contradictory social relations in order to transcend them opens up. This is shown in the mode of striving for autonomy, in controversy between individualism and collectivism and in theoretical concepts such as the social revolution. In this context Jonathan Eibisch makes clear that there is a contemporary political theory of anarchism - and how it can look like.
content.title_en: Political theory of anarchism : to the paradoxical pursuit of autonomy, self-determination and self-organization

content.text: The MMFE is a comprehensively-described concept of the MMFE and the simulation of the MMFE. The MMFE is a challenge in modern optical production of aspheres and freeforms. While the MMFE is able to eliminate form errors by appropriate local correction methods and also to achieve the specified surface roughness by means of corresponding smoothing processes, the MMFE limits the attainable optical qualities. In this work, therefore, the development mechanisms of MSFE are systematically investigated and described. The aim is to identify the development mechanisms of MSFE and to derive concrete prevention strategies for existing production processes of precision optics. The prediction of the grinding of emerging MSFE by means of simulation models is a further focus of the work. The first step in the process chain is to create aspheric geometries and freeforms due to the local curvature changes technically necessary. The MMFE is therefore developed as a reference for the geometry of precision optics of the production-technical standard.
content.title_en: Avoidance and simulation of the emergence of medium frequency errors in the grinding process for precision optics

content.text: The literary form of travel guides in the 19th and 20th centuries: investigations using the example of the Rhine. Folding text: Around the middle of the 19th century the new textual places of travel guides were created. Observations on the text-type characteristics as well as on the style and semantics of the new technical language are made. The basis for this are older travel guides texts. Because of the early tourism on the Rhine, the "Rheinreise" is particularly suitable for this. The text changes up to today's travel guides reflect the changes in travel life and travel culture, the travellers and their perception behaviour. It shows the importance of the textual places for the creation of clichés. The influence of the external framework of politics, sociology, economics and technology on the travel guides' contents proves the special dynamics of the textual places and their value for a cultural historical evaluation.
content.title_en: The literary form Guide in the 19th and 20th centuries : Studies on the example of the Rhine

content.text: Virtual Reality : Acceptance and impact of immersive product presentations using the example of experiential goods. Virtual Reality (VR) technology enables companies to present products that go far beyond traditional presentation methods. Although the integration of VR technology opens up many opportunities for companies, their use is also associated with risks. In particular, the lack of empirically secured insights into customer acceptance, the effects of use and cannibalization effects is an essential reason that still inhibits the dissemination of VR in customer communication. The book addresses these research gaps and identifies concrete opportunities and risks associated with the use of VR product presentations by means of user-centric, quantitative research design.
content.title_en: Virtual Reality : Acceptance and impact of immersive product presentations using the example of experiential goods

content.text: State and statehood in the digital age: political governance in change. Klappentext: What about the state in the "digital age"? The transformation of the state in the performance dimension and statehood in the control dimension is the rule rather than an exception. For the 1990s it was described with the model change from the "intervening performance state" to the "cooperative guarantee state". In the face of "digitalisation" and other megatrends, the next profound transformation processes are shown. Samuel Greef illuminates the new mix of control forms and instruments as well as a hybrid performance achievement, which shape the state's shape in different policy fields. His conclusion: Germany is today on the way to the "quota patchwork state".
content.title_en: State and Statehood in the Digital Age: Political Governance in Change

content.text: The influence of microbiological treatments on the phytoremediation potential of various tree species on metal-loaded soils of a former mining site. The rehabilitation of former mining areas is associated with challenges such as metal load on the soil and acid pit waters. Conventional remediation methods are expensive and destroy the soil structure. The more cost-effective remediation by plants (phytoremediation) has been investigated. The study evaluates the influence of soil treatments and microbiological inoculations on the growth and phytoremediation potential of various tree species in a former uranium mining area in Thuringia, Germany. On the test field Gesesswiese, birches, alders and pastures were planted with various rendzina and inoculation combinations. Rendzina influenced the metal content and growth, with Erlen showing the best growth. Furthermore, the erles showed the best extraction potential for the investigated metals (except cadmium and copper). On the test fields EPH and EPP, the microbial inoculations were not considered as inappropriate for eber biomass.
content.title_en: Influence of microbiological treatments on the phytoremediation potential of various tree species on metal-loaded soils of a former mining site

content.text: The aim of an inclusive physics lesson is to combine the inclusive pedagogical considerations with subject-specific considerations. The perspective of inclusive physics teaching is to be presented, among other things, via the guiding figures diversity and participation. The perspective of physics or physics teaching is constituted primarily in relation to the experiment or experiment-related actions. In an inclusive physics lesson, both perspectives are to be combined. To this end, the documentary method is used to analyse the diversity facets of the experiment in the sense of a `doing diversity' and the participation possibilities generated in the interactions in the sense of a `doing participatory' using teaching videographies. The reconstruction results show that the behavioural possibilities of the experimenting of the different modes of experimentation are brought forth in the context of the subject-related physics.
content.title_en: Experimentation practice in the spectrum of possibilities : A reconstructive analysis of experimenting practice in inclusive physics lessons

content.text: The concept of "reliability" is based on the concept of "reliability" and "reliability" of the system. The concept of "reliability" is based on the concept of "reliability" of the system. The concept of "reliability" is based on the concept of "reliability" of the system. The concept of "reliability" is based on the concept of "reliability" of the system. The concept of "reliability" of the system allows for improved concepts for the systems needed for vehicle movement. However, the removal of mechanical connections in automated systems reduces the possibilities of human intervention in dangerous situations. This implies safety-relevant availability requirements for the systems involved. This results in new degrees of freedom that must be taken into account when assessing potential system variants. In order to identify the optimal variants in compliance with all requirements, a two-stage modeling approach is introduced, the behavioural and logical system elements are combined. This allows a reduction of the number of the assessments of the analysis time to determine the possible results.
content.title_en: Model-based optimization of mechatronic systems for safety-relevant vehicle applications

content.text: Moments of datafiction: the mode of production of personal data in data economics. In digital economy, data is considered to be "the new oil". However, "personal data" is not just there, but must be produced. Markus Unternährer analyses how data-generating relationships are used to generate relationship-generating data. Using an ethnography of companies and an analysis of algorithmic recommendation systems, he reveals the various moments of datafiction, in which banal, digital behaviours are transformed into a valuable resource in themselves - and shows that datafiction changes between the value regimes of gift and commodity.
content.title_en: Moments of datafiction : on the mode of production of personal data in the data economy

content.text: From Curricular Innovation to Science Communication: Explorative Development and Evaluation of a Science Communication Strategy for Science Research Associations. In the context of an exploratory development, the present study developed a concept for science communication for a Research Training Group in which photochemical processes are being investigated and subsequently evaluated. The reason for this is the ever-increasing demand for science communication from politics. Furthermore, it is demanded that the communication of one's own research in the future become an integral part of scientific work. In order to prepare young scientists early on for this task, science communication is also being realized in research associations. For this reason, a preliminary study examined the requirements for a concept for science communication within a research association by evaluating the attitudes of doctoral students to science communication and their communication capabilities on the basis of a closed questionnaire.
content.title_en: From Curricular Innovation to Science Communication : Explorative Development and Evaluation of a Science Communication Strategy for Scientific Research Associations

content.text: The private and distributed person: Studies on personalization and privacy in times of digitalization. The "person" is not synonymous with "human", but a social way of existence for human and non-human beings. While the person of modernity is linked to the private, it is re-established with digitalization. Fabian Pittroff analyses this development in a series of studies that focus on comprehensive aspects: the social theory of the person, the history of the private, the crisis of democratic institutions, the avant-garde postprivacy movement, the digitization of friendship, the production of selfies and the predictions of data economics. Two modes of personalization are distinguished: while the private person is directed towards a centre, the distributed person exists decentralized.
content.title_en: The private and distributed person : Studies on personalization and privacy in times of digitalization

content.text: Digitalization in hospital: a knowledge-sociological study of the process and structural logics of a platform development for the monitoring of therapy in post-transplant care. The digitalization of the healthcare system and its most important sub-institution, the hospital, is the focus of professional, political and everyday practical debates. Maike Janssen develops an analytical connection between these discourses and the process and structural logics that interact in situations of digitalization. The focus is on those meanings that attribute and shape digital artifacts accordingly. Her empirically sound "hospital sociology of the digital" allows a resolution-strong access to the interplay of meaning, artifact and organization.
content.title_en: Digitization in hospital: a knowledge-sociological study of the process and structural logics of a platform development for the monitoring of therapy in post-transplant care

content.text: Social Bots: digital manipulation and constitutional law. Automated profiles (so-called social bots) manipulate public opinion formation in social networks. Paul Dürr deals with this conflict-prone topic from a constitutional perspective. He creates a normative framework to map the risks of digital manipulation for the democratic system and to develop suitable regulatory concepts.
content.title_en: Social Bots : Digital Manipulation and Constitutional Law

content.text: Stories in the digital space: historical learning in the "App into History". In the age of digitality, the question is less whether historical learning in the digital space is relevant, but rather how to model it. Alexandra Krebs develops a theoretical concept in her work and concreteises it in the digital learning platform "App into History". In this context, learners can carry out their own research projects in cooperation with archives and using digital tools. The focus is on principles of controversy, multiperspectivity and plurality, as well as project and archive work, which the author brings together with the potentials of digital space to create a re-constructive learning process. In addition, she examines these using the platform's "Bethel Module", which addresses current debates about eugenics, euthanasia and forced sterilisation in the NS time. It identifies in a mixed-method design and uses qualitative content analysis as well as machine learning algorithms to identify different types of app use as well as types of historical narratives. These not only provide insights about the use of the app, but also, in the future, digital design methods of the digital learning.
content.title_en: Stories in the digital space: historical learning in the "App in the history"

content.text: The study will examine the technical implementation of the kilogram in accordance with the new definition of the kilogram in 2019. The state of the art will be used to trace the history of the kilogram and present the most important milestones in weighing technology. Subsequently, various approaches will be presented to implement the kilogram in accordance with the new definition. The basics of high-precision mass determination, including the limits, problems and latest developments in the field of weighing technology, will be presented. Furthermore, the basics of absolute mass determination will be presented with a Planck scale based on the new definition of the kilogram. In the further course, the development of a Planck scale will be described as an extension of a commercial high-vacuum mass comparator. This will allow the determination of the kilogram in accordance with the new definition on the basis of mass comparators, which have been developed and tested with long experience. Furthermore, the mass comparators can be used to maintain the calibration chain after the old definition of the kilogram. In the context of this function of the system, the general function of the sample extension will be discussed.
content.title_en: Planck extension for a prototype vacuum mass comparator

content.text: The basic knowledge of artificial intelligence of (aspiring) teachers in the vocational field: model-based test development and validation. In the dissertation by Dr.in Schmidt, based on the increasing relevance of artificial intelligence (AI) in the context of digital transformation processes, a structural model for AI-related competence facets (approaching) teachers in the vocational field is developed. AI knowledge plays a central role in this, following professionalization research. In the course of the work, the question is examined how the basic knowledge (approaching) teachers can be theoretically modelled and empirically captured. The developed test instrument was extensively validated using a quantitative study design.
content.title_en: Basic knowledge on artificial intelligence of (aspiring) teachers in the vocational field : model-based test development and validation

content.text: Design and adjustment of weighing cells for vacuum mass comparators. Weighing cells based on flexible mechanisms are of crucial importance in mass metrology. The adjustment of mechanical properties determines the metrological performance of the instruments. This dissertation contributes to their further enhancement. The design and adjustment of flexible mechanisms for electromagnetically force-compensated weighing cells in vacuum mass comparators are treated. The most important component of these mechanisms are ultra-thin solid body joints, whose modelling, manufacturing and measurement are considered. The mechanical system is model-based in terms of mechanical properties stiffness, inclination sensitivity and corner load sensitivity and experimentally investigated from three load cell prototypes. The developed alignment method and its implementation in alignment facilities allow targeted alignment under vacuum conditions. They are designed to eliminate the mechanical uncertainties contributions of first order of the weighing cell and thus enable further reduction of measurement uncertainty for mass comparators.
content.title_en: Design and adjustment of weighing cells for vacuum mass comparators

content.text: The experimental analysis of the phase-to-phase transformations in Cu-Zn-Al alloys is also used for the first time to define the phase-to-phase conversions in the form of the phase-to-stage conversions. Therefore, a deep understanding of phase transformations is necessary for a targeted improvement of materials. In many alloy systems, such as Fe-C, heat treatments and associated solid-to-phase conversions have already been intensively investigated. However, in some binary alloy systems, such as Cu-Zn, this is only very limited and therefore little research is being done. However, when a third element, such as Al, is added, new possibilities of material optimization such as curing or using the form-to-form analysis are found to be rapidly present in the phase conversions.
content.title_en: Experimental investigation of rapid solid state phase transformations in Cu-Zn-Al alloys

content.text: Structural diversity of N-Mesityl-P,P-diphenylphosphinic amide in s-block metal chemistry. In this dissertation the coordination chemistry of N-mesityl-P,P-diphenylphosphinamide (HL) was investigated in the presence of the s-block metals M = Li, Mg, Ca, Sr and Ba. Using the Schlenk technique, 12 new N-mesityl-P,P-diphenylphosphinimidate complexes from THF, Toluen, 1,2-dimethyethane or Diethylether could be isolated. The characterization of the complexes was done by X-ray single crystal diffractometry of the crystalline components as well as 1H and 31P-NMR spectroscopy of the reaction solutions and solids were found for Nnuclear-combular-res. In addition, the Bacular-combular-resedation was found to be of the same magnitude in the sample.
content.title_en: Structural diversity of N-Mesityl-P,P-diphenylphosphinic amide in s-block metal chemistry
