content.title_en: The Dikes

content.text: Urban development and conversion: a study of the Flensburg case. In the Federal Republic of Germany, the extent of the military reduction has not yet been achieved as a result of the international disarmament process and the changed geopolitical and security situation. The task of military institutions has considerable social, economic and urban structural effects, such as urban development. Thus, the conversion of military areas in the professional world is described as one of the main urban planning tasks of the 1990s. Similarly, the present volume tries to provide a contribution to urban development research in a new, little-used field of tasks - conversion. The case example of the garrison city of Flensburg is the structure of military and urban development as well as the structural changes and opportunities associated with the troop dismantling and is subject to an evaluation. The study area has typical features of West German garrison cities, in which almost half of all Bundeswehrsolden are stationed, so that the model analysis allows conclusions to be drawn on other cities with similar problems. <d.>
content.title_en: Urban development and conversion : an investigation at the Flensburg case study

content.text: A three-dimensional, numerical suspended transport model with application to the German Bight. From the summary: In this work a numerical, three-dimensional suspended transport model is presented and applied to the area of the German Bight. The investigation of the current events in the German Bight in April 1991 and additional simulations could justify the existence of the Helgoland Schlick area. However, the material deposited there originates more from different sediments than directly from the water of the Weser and Elbe estuares or the watt ranges.
content.title_en: A three-dimensional, numerical suspended transport model with application to the German Bight

content.text: Historical half-timbered work : on the history of architecture in the 19th century in Germany, Great Britain (Old English Style), France, Austria, Switzerland and the USA. The text contains objects by architects Conrad Wilhelm Hase, Edwin Oppler, Christoph Hehl, Ferdinand Schorbach, Johannes Otzen, Wilhelm Lüer, Gotthilf Ludwig Möckel, Eduard Endler, Gustav Schönermark, Carl Schäfer, Hugo Hartung, Friedrich Ostendorf, Ludwig Dihm and August Dauber.
content.title_en: Historical half-timber : on the history of architecture in the 19th century in Germany, Great Britain (Old English Style), France, Austria, Switzerland and the USA

content.text: Ecological assessment of river landscapes: basis for renaturation and remediation. In Central Europe, the waters are often subject to intensive exploitation requirements, so that their landscape-shaping character is increasingly endangered and their function in the landscape budget is disturbed. In order to reliably assess the current state and the effects of anthropogenic interventions in river landscapes, the author presents an ecologically oriented assessment procedure here. It can serve as a basis for renaturation and remediation measures in the area of the northern German lowlands as well as in the central mountain region. The very detailed water survey sheet developed by the author on the basis of the Oker (Lower Saxony) provides the user with concrete help in assessing the protection value of river landscapes. (Source: www.buchhandel.de 12.10.2011)
content.title_en: Ecological assessment of river landscapes : basis for renaturation and restoration

content.text: Vegetation and population dynamics in N-loaded agricultural ecosystems after the transition to extensive use. Research areas lie in the area of falchwelliegn Querfurter Platte between Etzdorf and Bad Lauchstädt
content.title_en: Vegetation and population dynamics in N-loaded agricultural ecosystems after the transition to extensive use

content.text: The political governance of science is taken over by the German Federal Republic in the period of the Second World War. The institutionalization of research funding is a previously neglected field of research policy analysis. Based on a historical and international comparative description (Germany, England, France, USA) this book examines how funding systems as a mechanism for mediating between politics and science can contribute to increasing the governance of today's political systems compared to science. Structure: 1. Introduction. - 2. The cooperative state as a new paradigm in policy-based governance approaches. - 3. Hypotheses on political governance capacity in intermediary systems. - 4. The taxability of science. - 5. The evolution of research funding systems (5.1 Starting conditions: The scientific and political interest in government funding of research. - 5.2 The national-specific development patterns in the institutionalization of state research funding. - 5.4 National institutionalization patterns in the organization of research policy control of science before the Second World War.
content.title_en: Political governance of science: a contribution to the "cooperative state"

content.text: Technology assessment as group performance : the effectiveness of a newly developed moderation method. The aim of the present studies was to develop a moderation method which would achieve "typical" process losses of groups, as empirically verifiable and theoretically reconstructable, if not completely avoid, but help to reduce. The groups moderated in the context of a complex technology assessment should achieve higher-quality results than non-moderated parallel groups. The effectiveness of the method should be demonstrated on the basis of theoretically significant TA criteria. To this end, an extreme group comparison was carried out in the sense of basic research, in which 12 moderated 12 self-controlled groups were compared. Content: 1. Problem solving and decisions in groups 2. The moderation of problem solving processes in groups 3. Technology assessment (TA) as complex group problem 4. Method and criteria development for the chosen TA problem 5. Empirical studies on the effectiveness of the developed group moderation 6. Results of the group study - comparison of group performance: Examination of effectiveness - ANNEX: Materials of the pilot study - Materials of the group study. (TUB/ Übern.)
content.title_en: Technology assessment as a group performance : to the effectiveness of a newly developed moderation method

content.text: The body administered: the medicization of pregnant women in the early 19th century's birth houses. The author wants to illustrate the interplay of the systems involved in the medialization process of pregnant women - state, justice, church, science, traditional life world - in his dynasty. Thus, a living picture of everyday life is to be created in the 19th century unintentionally pregnant women, of their fears, hopes, their despair and also their resistance to an environment in which they could see little real opportunities for themselves.
content.title_en: The administered body: the medicization of pregnant women in the early 19th century birth houses

content.text: Women and men on computers: aspects of gender-specific technology appropriation. Klappentext: Sabine Collmer examines the ways of appropriation and access of women and men to the technical device computer. She refers to the concept of the social constructivity of the sexes and the everyday reproduction of the gender order. Within the symbolic order of bisexuality, computer technology takes a prominent position as a gender-differentiating factor. The results of her empirical study show that the gender system, which is based on asymmetry, also develops its effect when the computer is appropriated, because it takes place in a social space that assigns technical competence to boys and men, while women and girls do not. At the same time, factors such as age, educational level and previous knowledge of the computer influence the process of appropriation of computer knowledge. The author shows how this pre-structuring of social reality opens up or closes the scope for action for the female and male actors.
content.title_en: Women and men on computers: aspects of gender-specific technology acquisition

content.text: Sustainable Development as a new aspect of urban planning and urban development: Comparative study of the action processes in urban planning and urban development in the PRC and the Federal Republic of Germany using case studies. Case study Expo sites and Kronsberg residential quarters in the city of Hanover, pp. 209-272. Expo, Kronsberg, Sustainability, Agenda 21, sustainable development
content.title_en: Sustainable Development as a new aspect of urban planning and urban planning : Comparative study of the action processes in urban planning and urban planning in the PRC and the Federal Republic of Germany using case studies

content.text: G-algebras and Clifford theory. The dissertation deals with applications of G-algebra theory (in particular with regard to Clifford theory) in modular representation theory, that is, the characteristic of the body F is positive. The most important results are: a generalization of a lifting set for Idempotentes of The'venanz. With the help of this result it is proved that a classical result of Fong, which means that each projective module of a p-solvable group G is induced by a p'-half group, is also valid in a relative situation. Another chapter of the work deals with induction phrases. It is proved that each induction set for the character ring of G can be "lifted" to an induction set for the greenring. This result shows, for example, that the Artinian induction set is concerned with the conlonschen, as well as the brewer's induction set. This result generalizes the greening indelegacy sentence. Furthermore, the gregation is shown by the gregation-generalization.
content.title_en: G-algebras and Clifford theory

content.text: The body is heard: on the historical sociology of medical examination. Using the example of listening to the stethoscope, this book will analyse the historical foundations of diagnostic interpretation competence in modern medicine.
content.title_en: The rehearsed body : on the historical sociology of medical examination

content.text: Development of a virtual ergonomic work design system: with 13 tables. Publisher's info: The design of working conditions in industry, crafts, trade, services and administration is a challenge which industrial societies are increasingly facing. Increasing demands on the economy, flexibility, quality and innovation of work and work result characterize this development for years. Their fulfilment is an essential prerequisite for the continued success of highly developed economic systems. Socially equally important is the goal to make work human-friendly and thus to make a significant contribution to the health preservation of the working person. Successful occupational and health protection is increasingly preventively oriented, so that the health of the employees through the design of work and working conditions is maintained and demanded by prospective interventions. To design human-friendly working conditions suitable methods and tools for the implementation of knowledge of the work sciences are necessary. Basic importance in the design of work is given to ergonomics. A work system designed according to ergonomic criteria is a prerequisite for the human and economic use of human work force (Luczak 93, Bullinger 94). Eromically designed working systems are also used to improve the quality of work and to improve the performance of the work.
content.title_en: Development of a virtual ergonomics work design system : with 13 tables

content.text: The subject of the study is the establishment of a faculty information system (FABIAN) as an instrument of university controlling and its contribution to improving the quality of studies and teaching. The present work develops a design possibility on the basis of a conceptually supported discussion of the tasks and objectives of an information system as part of the faculty management system and shows ways of implementation. Structure: 1. Necessary of a faculty information system to support the coordination of decision-making processes in universities 2. Conception of university cotrolling and importance of a faculty information system as part of the faculty management system 3. Statements about the contribution of an information system to the coordination of decision-making processes in the faculty area 4. Design proposal of the structure and instruments of a faculty information system. (HoF/Text taken over)
content.title_en: Faculty Information System as an Instrument of University Controlling

content.text: Reet & Stroh as historical building material: [a material guide and guide]. Another meritorious volume (after "wall brick as ...", BA 12/97), whose aim is the promotion and possibly use of historical building materials that allow building in accordance with nature. Reet and straw are among the oldest building materials used by humans. History, extraction, use possibilities and the actual reed roof are the main topics. The experts and laymen who are interested in private or professional reed cover are also addressed beyond the northern German area. Recently, the reed roof is also taken into account (as an alternative) in roofing teaching. Those who want to learn more about it than the volume of Ina Anders (BA 7/98) intended for tourists, but do not want to take up with the standard work written for experts by W. Schattke (last ID 42/92; 4th edition 1996), which is well served with this interesting written work. (3) (Leo Prawitt)
content.title_en: Reet & Straw as historical building material : [a guide and guide]

content.text: Materialism : Origin and effect in the sciences of the 19th century. Materialism is one of the most influential world views in Western Europe today. It says that there is no other reality than matter, whereby thought and feeling are also traced back to movements of matter. Annette Wittkau-Horgby deals with the origin of materialistic world interpretation and its spread during the 19th century.
content.title_en: Materialism : Origin and effect in the sciences of the 19th century

content.text: The present work has the content of the late glacial and early holocene development of the western Baltic Sea region (Mecklenburger Bight to Arkona Basin) from the end of the Vistula ice-creaming to the Litorina Transgression. The basis for a consideration of the palaeogeographic conditions in this area are flat seismic and sedimentological data from the Mecklenburg Bay, the Arkona Basin and from the Darsser Thresshold between these two recent accumulation areas. It is possible to derive previously unknown details of the late glacial ice-degradation, the development of the Baltic Ice reservoir and the Ancylus Lake in the study area. In addition, new aspects of the course of the initial Litorina Transgression in the western Baltic Sea are emerging.
content.title_en: Sedimentation and paleogeographical development in the western Baltic Sea region (Mecklenburg bay to Arkona basin) from the end of the Vistula ice-cream to the Litorinatransgression

content.text: Modelling curved surfaces to support the Markscheiderische processing of storage caverns in the salt mountains. From the summary: This study has tested the usability of a newly available interpolation and display technology. So far contours of salt caverns in cut cracks and perspective views are created by linear interpolations of the echometrically determined measurement values. However, this does not correspond to the smooth-walled and curved course of the cavern wall and has effects on the calculation of the cavern volume and cavern convergence. A more plausible interpolation by parametrized curves and the surface modelling and rendered representation based on it have been tested by a so-called NURBS-based surface modelling. Through this test, a promising outlook on the equally plausible processing of complex geotechnical relationships is opened up.
content.title_en: Modelling curved surfaces to support the Markscheiderische processing of storage caverns in the salt mountains

content.text: Italian stucco-work between the Elbe and the Baltic Sea: stucco decoration of late baroque in northern Germany and Denmark. Stucco-work is one of the most important design tools of the Baroque period; it can be found in many North German mansions, castles and city palaces. Its execution was in the hands of Italian masters who settled in a region with their workshops for a long time. The stucco-worker Joseph Mogia demonstrably dominated the order market from Gottorf to Rostock from 1698 to 1739, as the first Tei proves this excellently black and white illustrated study; he was also active in Damp, Plön, Probsteierhagen, Steinhorst and Lübeck. After his death, other Italian workshops continued the tradition, whose room decorations are examined and assigned in the second part according to characteristic style elements. This volume begins a new series of "Bau + Kunst", in which art-historical research from Schleswig-Holstein is to be made accessible to a wide public. (I. Hanewald)
content.title_en: Italian stucco-teachers between the Elbe and the Baltic Sea : stucco decoration of the late baroque in northern Germany and Denmark

content.text: Incentives, out-of-company conditions and sickness: an action-theoretical concept and empirical evidence to explain the state of the sick of the workers. The focus of the work is on the formulation of an action-theoretical concept to explain the state of the sick of the workers and the presentation of empirical evidence in this regard.
content.title_en: Incentives, out-of-company conditions and sickness: a theoretical approach and empirical evidence to explain the state of the sick of workers

content.text: Traffic avoidance : Concepts of action for integrated urban and transport development planning. The increasing traffic loads in cities are becoming increasingly constrained by both urban development and traffic itself. Traffic avoidance complements the objectives of modern transport planning, shifting necessary traffic to more environmentally friendly transport modes and managing the remaining traffic more effectively, but primarily aims at a fundamental change in the awareness of transport, but also in the environmental and social fields, at reducing mobility constraints and at reducing travel distances. A traffic reversal in the sense of a general reorientation of the economic and social classification of transport requires a reduction of transport effort in all social areas. Traffic avoidance attempts to influence the causes of traffic development through urban and spatial planning measures. The study provides a comprehensive presentation of a urban and transport development planning that is understood in this way. In addition to the comprehensive breadth of the actions, measures and overall control options to be considered, the study offers a wealth of facts by means of point-by-point in-depth analysis.
content.title_en: Traffic prevention : Concepts for action for integrated urban and transport development planning

content.text: Authenticity as a political problem: a contribution to the history of the theory of the legitimacy of political order. The great revolutions of the 17th and 18th centuries establish a new legitimization of political rule. For the first time in the history of humanity we bind the legality of political orders to the approval of the subjects subjected. This is the paradigmatic expression of the philosophy of the social contract. The focus is on the freedom of politically socialized individuals, which must not only be protected against the state monopoly of violence, but also be examined for its internal consistency. Thomas Noetzel's book is the first German-language study of the connection between authenticity and politics. The author shows that with the new legitimacy of political orders a public discourse on the authenticity of individual freedom begins, in which the question of true/presence will is at the center. The fiction of a moral essence of man lets its authenticity become the problem of modern critique of domination and legitimization. Noetzel examines philosophical, political science, sociological approaches to authenticity research and arranges it into an interdisciplinary framework.
content.title_en: Authenticity as a political problem : a contribution to the history of the theory of the legitimacy of political order

content.text: The measurement of plasma properties in the limit range of strongly and weakly coupled plasmas is the subject of this work. New, time-resolved methods for measuring important inner plasma parameters such as electron density and temperature in the limit range of strongly and weakly coupled laser plasmas are the subject of this work. By measuring the absolute brilliance with the help of a novel reflection zone plate spectrographs, the high conversion efficiency of laser energy in X-ray radiation energy - with comparable values as in Synchrotrons - is detected for the first time with high spectral and spatial resolution. In further experiments electron density and temperature are correlated in different stages of plasma development with the help of coherent, ultrashort harmonic radiation of known frequency and with high time resolution. In this case, the characteristic of plasma is used that only radiation with frequency above the electron density-dependent plasma frequency can be transmitted by plasma.
content.title_en: Measurement of plasma properties at the limit of strongly and weakly coupled plasmas

content.text: Technology and judgement: to recast the concept of education. The present "social practice of technologization" marks a historical gap which also covers the criteria for assessment itself. Contrary to the cultural self-image still valid, technology is to be perceived as education and understood. This does not mean, however, that a seemingly hopelessly occurring technologization also gives the blessing of education. On the contrary: the "recasting of the concept of education" (Heydorn) becomes the central task of our epoch within the technologization. However, it contradicts a characteristic of bourgeois-Abendland civilization, in whose course education and technology - even in critical theory formations - became finally two cultures. In the consciousness of global social and ecological disasters, but also the eroding legitimization of prevailing civilization, the consequent self-criticism of education is demanded. In the horizon of this epochal change, Kant's determination of the power of judgement gains central importance for critical educational theory. From it is designed in this work the "reflected competence" as a concept of subjective education, while the demand for "interdisciplinarity" is objectively conceived as a critique.
content.title_en: Technology and judgement : to recast the concept of education

content.text: The development of a model of enterprise culture, taking into account ethnological findings and their application to innovation themes, is being studied. The diffuse construct of enterprise culture is being developed. Theses on fundamental relationships and meaning relationships are being derived. The importance of enterprise culture for innovation success is being analysed.
content.title_en: Enterprise culture: the development of an enterprise culture model taking into account ethnological findings and their application to innovation themes

content.text: From the building officer to the freelance architect: technical occupations in the construction sector (Prussia/Germany 1799 - 1931). In 1799 the building academy was founded in Berlin, where architects and engineers were trained for the state building sector. These understood themselves as elite within the technical professions. While the building officials dominated the public and parts of the private construction market, the construction master remained for a long time the primary expert for private construction. Through the construction schools the construction workers tried to professionalize themselves. For the late, collective appearance of freelance architects, less labour-partial needs than overfilling in the civil engineering service were the cause. The securing of fields of work and title questions (Construction Master's Decree 1931) were the main conflict areas of these competing professional groups.
content.title_en: From civil servants to freelance architects : technical occupations in the construction sector (Prussia/Germany 1799 - 1931)

content.text: Educational theories of interaction in the age of new technologies: Attempts to evaluate interactive computer teaching/learning programs. Klappentext: Interaction with the computer is still much too often discussed from a technological point of view. Pedagogical theories of interaction are necessary to check what is commonly and pre-accidentally linked to interactive computer teaching/learning programs. John Deweys and George Herbert Meads in particular, who are oriented to pragmatism, get up-to-date in the age of new technologies in this way. With their help, it can be opened up whether and to what extent computer teaching/learning programs can be called "interactive". The demands arising from interaction theories and computer didactic considerations are ultimately placed on programs from the fields of "interactive video", "hypermedia" as well as information and communication technology basic education.
content.title_en: Educational theories of interaction in the age of new technologies : attempt to evaluate interactive computer teaching/learning programmes

content.text: The transparency requirement in the law of the general terms and conditions. Publisher's information: In its spectacular judgments of 24 November 1988 and 17 January 1989, the BGH declared repayment settlement clauses and a value clause invalid solely because of their not sufficiently comprehensible content according to 9 para. 1 of the AGB Act. These decisions were largely unprepared by both the AGB users and the legal science and solved a controversial discussion on the location and scope of a transparency requirement in the law of the general terms and conditions as well as a flood of partly contradictory subsequent decisions. The present work attempts to "deconstrute" the transparency requirement, which is now a "magic formula", which is to determine its content, direction and scope as far as possible. In this regard, it particularly deals with individual criteria for establishing a sufficient GTC transparency, which are intended to ensure more legal certainty in dealing with the transparency requirement.
content.title_en: The transparency requirement in the law of the general terms and conditions

The administrative and economic history of the German colony Togo 1884-1914. Contributions to colonial and overseas history, Volume 51. Franz Steiner Verlag, Stuttgart 1991. 351 pages, 86,- DM
content.title_en: A "place in the sun"? : the administrative and economic history of the German colony Togo ; 1884 - 1914

content.text: Work and non-work in cities in northern Germany from the 14th to 16th centuries : Studies on the history of social time order. Klappentext: This study, which sees itself as a contribution to historical anthropology, deals with the rhythm of work in pre-industrial urban society, the formation of rational working hours since the late Middle Ages, and the discipline of the working person, the rationalization of his life in the sense of time. Work and non-work are to be investigated using the example of four selected cities in northern Germany: Lübeck, Hamburg, Lüneburg and Braunschweig.
content.title_en: Work and non-work in cities in northern Germany from the 14th to 16th century : Studies on the history of social time order

content.text: Warburg aus Briefen : Kommentare zu den Copierbüchern der Jahre 1905 - 1918. Michael Diers: "Warburg aus Briefen". Kommentare zu den Copierbüchern der Jahre 1905-1918. VCH, Acta Humaniora, Weinheim 1991. 251 pp., born, 84,- DM
content.title_en: Warburg from letters : Comments on the copy books of 1905 - 1918

content.text: Science and Theology : Theoretical aspects of science in the horizon of religious pedagogical considerations. This volume fundamentally reflects the relationship between science and theology from a religious pedagogical perspective. Using various empirical studies, the first question is examined how children, adolescents and adults relate to each other in their everyday theories of science and theology. Subsequently, theoretical considerations on the characteristic relation models of science and theology (model of conflict, independence, dialogue and integration) are discussed. The consequences resulting from empirical and scientific theoretical considerations are deepened in the context of the corresponding pedagogical and didactic discussion and developed in the context of the education and training of teachers for religion and adult education.
content.title_en: Science and Theology : Theoretical Perspectives in the Horizon of Religious Pedagogical Considerations

content.text: The theory of social systems, as is well known, sets the claim of a uniform social theory. The author uses this work to explain that system theory is both capable and necessary for microsociological elaboration.
content.title_en: Communication among present: Studies on interaction systems

content.text: Fuzzy-PPS systems: The potential for application and success of the theory of blurred quantities. PPS systems are usually used in poorly structured decision-making situations. The decision-making field components to be considered are generally not clearly identifiable. Based on a systematic fuzzyfiction of classical PPS systems, the conceptual application possibilities of the fuzzy set theory for the illustration of the indeterminates are disclosed and analyzed using (further) developed heuristic fuzzy approaches. The basis for this is provided by the MRP logic as well as the load-oriented order release (BOA). It is shown that the basic assumptions and structures of the fuzzy set theory inherent, generally possible "strategic" efficiency and efficiency potentials are largely conceptually feasible in fuzzy-PPS systems.
content.title_en: Fuzzy-PPS systems : potential applications and potential success of theory of blurred quantities

content.text: Sexy Bodies: a sociological journey through the sex body. In this introductory and manual, current sociological perspectives (action theory, phenomenological and discurstheoretical) as well as feminist perspectives on the body are reconstructed. The synthetic merging is primarily about a critical examination of yields, limits and shortening of the respective perspectives, in particular about the social theoretical deficit of current (social) constructivist analyses. Bourdieu and Kreckel are used to understand sex processes that influence the body's forms and physical experience of sex, also as processes shaped by the social disparity between social resources. A final chapter on the Argentine Tango brings the sociological analyses to 'dance'.
content.title_en: Sexy Bodies : a sociological journey through the sex body

content.text: The influence of phytoplankton aggregation on sedimentation : a model study. A model for phytoplankton aggregation will be presented in which the aggregation equations and sedimentation on a continuous range of phytoplankton sizes were dissolved and implemented in 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional models for biogeochemical cycles. The model is compared with other models. Furthermore, the model is used for simulations of the northern Atlantic and the Arabian Sea. Presentation and discussion of the results.
content.title_en: The influence of phytoplankton aggregation on sedimentation : a model study

content.text: Suburbia - Postsuburbia - Interurban: the younger housing development in the surrounding areas of the major cities of West Germany and the consequences for regional planning and control. Despite other expectations in the 1980s, the spatial expansion process in the urban regions is unbroken. At the same time, the possibility of housing ownership decreases as land prices rise. In the choice of location, the more affordable periphery and the intermediate axis spaces are increasingly preferred. This is the starting point for an analysis of the 90s housing development in the surrounding areas of the large cities. In parallel with the scientific discussion stand (Suburbia - Postsuburbia - Interurban) and a broad empirical basis for the regions Dortmund-Nordost, Munich-Nordost and Stuttgart are being worked out. The harsh trends in spatial development are taken into account as well as the actions of private households and municipalities. Building on these studies, a scientific conclusion will be drawn on spatial patterns, land prices and the interests of households and municipalities. This will include political and planning-related consequences for modernised planning and management, which will serve as an impulse for future discussion.
content.title_en: Suburbia - Postsuburbia - Interurban: the younger development of housing development in the surrounding area of the major cities of West Germany and the consequences for regional planning and control

content.text: International Joint Venture as a form of technology transfer organisation. I. Introduction - II. Conceptual examination of the joint venture and the concept of technology transfer - III. Key features of the joint venture - IV. Conceptual statements on the process of technology transfer - V. On the design and functioning of a joint venture - VI. The transaction cost approach: basics and operationalization - VII. The transaction cost approach: the international dimension - VIII. content.title_en: International joint venture as a form of technology transfer organisation

content.text: The Margarethenhöhe Essen : Architect and client in the context of the municipal policy Essen and the corporate policy Krupp between 1886 and 1914. The Essen settlement Margarethenhöhe has an undisputed significance as a prominent point in the development of the building of the factory to social housing. The position of the architect Margarethenhöhe, which has been raised over 90 years on the mystified phenomenon Margarethenhöhe, led the author to reveal the background of the development by deeper penetration into the conditions of the planning. With the examination of the framework conditions of municipal and company policy, the profiles of the builder Margarethe Krupp and the architect Georg Metzendorf sharpen. In five chapters the present work reveals the bundling of all interests which should lead to the realization of the settlement. By means of a comprehensive study of sources, the constraints and mechanisms of decisions are highlighted as well as the personal profiles of the decision-makers. With the merging of the municipal interests of the city Essen and the family situation of the Krupps, the research in the past is rather isolated consideration of individual phenomena, and it is demonstrated that only the interaction of all forces of the Margarethenhöhe could be made possible. The architect is represented in the city of Essen in terms of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of the city of Essen.
content.title_en: Margarethenhöhe Essen : Architect and client against the background of the municipal policy Essen and the company policy Krupp between 1886 and 1914

content.text: Women's promotion at universities: new instruments for controlling equality. Klappentext: Women are still disadvantaged at universities. Christine Färber looks for ways to design a university that offers women and men equal opportunities and perspectives. After examining the previous concepts for promoting women, she presents new instruments for controlling equality. In her assessment, the author concludes that a university reform offers opportunities to overcome the old institutional order of the university from a women's political perspective.
content.title_en: Promoting women at universities: new instruments for gender equality

content.text: From criminalisation to pedagogy? : to the attempt to reform the juvenile prison in Saxony [from 1947 - 1952]. The present work deals in the essence with its development in a historically attractive situation: the social and political changes in the Soviet occupation zone after the Second World War. Against the background of the massive social and economic hardships, the management of juvenile crime, which was particularly high in the Land of Saxony, posed a great challenge to the political leaders. Youth was needed for the construction of the new social order.
content.title_en: From criminalization to pedagogy? : to the attempt to reform the juvenile prison in Saxony [from 1947 to 1952]

content.text: Hydropower machines for mining in the Harz: early modern traces and their interpretation using the example of the Thurm Rosenhof pit and selected plants. Hydropower machines, art and sweepers, for centuries supplied the energy for the propulsion of water pumps and conveyors in the Oberharz mining. Around fifty years before the cessation of mining in Clausthal-Zellerfeld, the change first came with steam power and then with electricity. In the small part region of the Western Harz, a diverse machine world has developed, the differences and similarities of which are worked out and systematized. Proven machine technology from earlier times must not be forgotten.
content.title_en: Hydropower machines for mining in the Harz region : early modern traces and their interpretation using the example of the Thurm Rosenhof pit and selected plants

content.text: Architecture in the GDR. The text also contains plans for Rathenow, East Berlin, Stalinstadt and Eisenhüttenstadt, Hoyerswerda, Schwedt and Rostock.
content.title_en: Architecture in the GDR

content.text: Tests for model specification in nonlinear regression. As the basis of many statistical methods, the process of data generation is modelled, and then further estimation and testing methods are applied. This work deals with the question of how this specification for parametric models can be tested itself. In extension of existing methods, tests with solid core are introduced and their asymptotic properties are analyzed. It is shown that the determination of the critical values with several sampling methods is possible. Of these, a new Monte Carlo approximation is particularly important, as it can significantly reduce the complexity of the calculation. A conditional smallest quadrate estimate for nonlinear parametric models is defined and its essential asymptotic properties are derived. All versions of the tests and all new concepts were examined in simulation studies, the most important results of which are presented. The practical applicability of the test methods is explained in a data set for product selection, which is to be analyzed with multinomial logit models.
content.title_en: Model specification tests in nonlinear regression

content.text: The theory and fabrication of subwave length structures using the example of polarizing metal stripe grids. The dissertation deals with subwave length metal stripe grids (i.e. optical grids consisting of metallic and dielectric areas alternately and having periods in the range of approx. 100nm to 500nm) which can be used to influence the polarization state of visible light. The theoretical description of such grids (using the theory of the Effective Medium and rigorous diffraction theory), the production of grids using various methods of microstructure technology (electron beam lithography, ion beam etching) and the application of such grids are not considered separately. These individual topics are not dealt with separately from each other, but rather they are shown in relation and cross-linking, leading to a complex understanding of both this special grid type and the general problem of producing microoptical elements. As a result of experimental investigations at various grid configurations, the normal polarization effect as well as its reversal (the inverse polarization effect) was demonstrated, whereby a maximum polarization effect was achieved in 1000 times greater than the transmission.
content.title_en: Theory and fabrication of subwave length structures using the example of polarizing metal strip grids

content.text: A study of the excess decay of mixture mixture and mixture mixture of mixture mixture into the excess of mixture mixture. In a binary diffusion system, different diffusion coefficients on the sample side containing the slower diffusion component lead to a net mass excess. A model model was developed according to which the measurement of the excess of the particles and the decay induced 'bullet cross section' at 50 to 3500 micrometers of thick quader-shaped diffusion samples of the Au/Ag system was determined.
content.title_en: A study of diffusion-induced isotropic volume expansions in thin gold/silver samples

content.text: The history of the construction of the city of Luckenwalde: from 1918-1933. The book describes the construction policy and the architectural history in the Brandenburg city of Luckenwalde between the two world wars. The small city modernised its infrastructure to an unprecedented extent: the settlement building under Joseph Bischof and Willi Ludewig, administrative buildings and the city theatre of Paul Backes and Hans Graf, the Waldfriedhof by Richard Neutra, the Hutfabrik by Erich Mendelsohn and the town bath of Hans Hertlein mark the highlights. The author can present new research results on the predecessor designs of the Hutfabrik by Mendelsohn and, based on the good source situation, represent for the first time for a city in Germany the function of urban construction consulting and its influence on architecture and color. The building of the private house is covered with the comprehensive text. The basis of the text is an extensive catalogue, which is attached to CD-ROM. It is both a data collection on the text and an indispensable information basis for the work on the building maintenance of the object. The construction services of the Twenties in Luckenwalde are also systematically presented here with information on the city data on the subject.
content.title_en: The history of the construction of the city of Luckenwalde : from 1918-1933

content.text: The North Atlantic Oscillation : variability and interactions with the North Atlantic Ocean and Artic Sea Ice. The North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) is the dominant mode of atmospheric variability in the North Atlantic and describes changes in the strength of the westerly winds in mid latitudes. This study analyses the variability of the NAO during the winter season and its interaction with the North Atlantic and Arctic sea ice. Observation data and model simulations of the Atlantic Ocean, Arctic Sea ice and global coupled climate system are analysed.
content.title_en: The North Atlantic Oscillation : variability and interactions with the North Atlantic Ocean and Artic Sea Ice

content.text: God and Time: the anthropological principle of Stephen W. Hawkings and "Science Theology". This work seeks to examine the speech of "God and Time" in the light of the possibilities and limitations provided by the so-called "anthropic principle". Through its "anthropic concept" of S. W. Hawking's "anthropic principle", science theology wants to present as a new natural theology "the principles of science theology". It is an attempt to explain what quantum physics is the existence and phenomenon from which we understand the world, nature and universe and make theology. And it is a path of knowledge that is still unproven in view of classical theology and metaphysics, which exposes a wealth of extremely fundamental problems. As nature is natural, science theology looks at the world and the natural holistic and asserts a total conversion to nature itself from our mechanistic and deterministic world view, because nature and the world from the beginning is holistic and quantum mechanistic, and becomes. - Out of the modern and natural existence - can take up the concept of the biblical and the concept of the world.
content.title_en: God and Time: the Anthropological Principle of Stephen W. Hawkings and "Science Theology"

content.text: Environmentally committed corporate management and framework conditions for its implementation in South Korea. Economic activity regularly requires the consumption of natural resources, which can easily lead to a sustainable damage to nature if its regeneration capacity is exceeded. In South Korea this is a particular problem, because the industrialization process is progressing particularly rapidly. Moreover, the relatively low attention to environmental concerns in South Korea allows the taking over of burdensome processes from industrialised countries. In the present work, the question is to be considered to what extent the business administration in South Korea addresses the ecological problem and offers practical assistance. The starting point is the thesis that in business research comprehensive strategic concepts are lacking, which take into account the business policy environmental protection problem ...
content.title_en: Environmentally committed corporate management and framework conditions for its implementation in South Korea

content.text: Development of a test concept for parametrizable simulation models of mechanical, hydraulic and control systems. Classification Tree Method. - In the context of this thesis I define a general concept for the automatic testing of simulation models developed by Robert Bosch GmbH. The presented test concept falls into the class of black box or functional testing. We extend the classification tree method with a manually controlled automatic test case generation. A second extension consists in the generation of test scenarios and the processing of these with the help of a determinative finite automats, which regulates the simulation models.
content.title_en: Development of a test concept for parametrizable simulation models of mechanical, hydraulic and control systems

content.text: Evolutionary algorithms for the optimization of the process in maintenance stations. The railways are increasingly exposed to competition on the road and, through EU Directive 91/440, WG, also on the rail. Therefore, great efforts are needed to increase competitiveness and thus also productivity. Therefore, increasingly complex trains are being used, whose maintenance is becoming more and more complex, while their downtimes are being reduced for productivity reasons. This requires, on the one hand, the most secure advance planning and, on the other hand, quick and flexible response to unexpected events. In order to support the planners in their complex task, a system for the optimization of the process in maintenance stations is being developed. The aim of this work is to discuss and formalise the processes and optimization possibilities in maintenance stations. To this end, after an introduction to the planning problem at maintenance stations, a data model is being developed with which maintenance stations can be modelled.
content.title_en: Evolutionary algorithms for the optimization of the process in maintenance stations

content.text: The Hanseatic League and its beer: brewing and beer trade in the Hanseatic Republic. Klappentext: Based on eight case studies on selected Hanseatic cities, this book presents the brewing and beer trade of the Hanseatic League for the first time in detail. The production of hop beer, the export of sea beer, as well as the sales routes, quantities and conditions of beer trade. Furthermore, the importance of the brewery for the urban economy, the social position of brewers and the legal background of brewing are presented. By combining economic, social and constitutional questions, the author can prove that the peculiarities of the Hanseatic brewing industry are not due to the extensive export in the late Middle Ages. Rather, they go back to the phase of the town's founding, when all the basic owners were entitled to brewing law.
content.title_en: The Hanseatic League and its beer : brewing and beer trade in the Hanseatic transport area

content.text: Conception, optimization and theoretical foundation of a measuring system for gravitational experiments at Fallturm Bremen. Experimental verification of the equivalence principle, high-resolution position detector based on DC SQUIDs, theoretical foundation of the experiment.
content.title_en: Conception, optimization and theoretical foundation of a measuring system for gravitational experiments at Fallturm Bremen

content.text: The first is the description of the optical properties of semiconductors, especially SiC polytypes. In this work, parameter-free calculations of the linear and nonlinear optical properties of cubic and hexagonal semiconductors are performed. The underlying atomic and electronic structures of semiconductor materials are calculated from the initial using density functional theory in local density approximation (DFT-LDA) using a plane-wave pseudopotential method. The description of optical properties is based on the approximation of independent quasiparticles; multi-diverse effects are included in the GW-Aproximation. At the linear optical properties of the cubic group IV materials silicon, diamond and silicon carbide (SiC), general aspects of the description of optical properties are discussed, such as the influence of non-local contributions to the optical transition operator, the question of the eggchin variance and the influence of quasipartial corrections. Using different polytypes of the SiC, the influence of the atomic and electronic structures on the linear and non-local variables of the optical transition operator are compared.
content.title_en: For the ab initio description of the optical properties of semiconductors, in particular SiC polytypes

content.text: Coronatine analogues: molecular probes for plant signaling pathways. Coronatine is a phytotoxin of Pseudomonas syringae. Its toxicity is based on the structural similarity with important signaling agents of the plant defense response in pest infestation. By this analogy, coronatine acts as a mimic of jasmonic acid and 12-oxophytodianic acid in secondary metabolism of plants. By developing 6-azido and 6-ethyl-4-indanone carboxylic acid isoleucin methyl esters as structural coronate analogues, new biological highly active tools are available to investigate plant secondary metabolism.
content.title_en: Coronatine analogues : molecular probes for plant signaling pathways

content.title_en: The Theory of Representation of Representation Rings

content.text: Calorimetric determination of the catalytic activity of immobilised enzymes. The work shows the use of calorimetric methods to determine the catalytic activity of enzyme immobilisates. A flow calorimeter was used for the investigation of spherical immobilisates. A mathematical model was developed to calculate the kinetic parameters of the immobilised enzyme from the measured temperature difference. By means of studies on model immobilisates it was shown that the flow calorimeter in impulse mode is suitable for rapid screening of the activity. Using the enzyme immobilisation in Sol-Gel layers the use of the impulse method for the optimization of immobilisation regulations was shown. An IC calorimeter was used for the investigation of flat immobilisates. In order to obtain kinetic statements, the IC calorimeter was characterized in terms of sensitivity and dynamic behaviour.
content.title_en: Calorimetric determination of catalytic activity of immobilized enzymes

content.text: Segregated poverty in the city: Causes and social consequences of the spatial concentration of welfare recipients. The book analyses the causes of the expansion and consolidation of spatially concentrated poverty and its effect on the duration of poverty situations of residents based on the example cities of Bremen and Bielefeld.
content.title_en: Segregated poverty in the city: causes and social consequences of the spatial concentration of social assistance recipients

content.text: Stationary psychiatry in the context of the Federal Republic psychiatry reform : analyses and possibilities of design from a socio-scientific perspective. The author analyses the current discussion about stationary psychiatry against the background of the psychiatry reform in recent decades. The aim of the executions is to provide an equally theoretical and practical contribution to the design of a need-oriented and personal psychiatry.
content.title_en: Stationary psychiatry in the context of the Federal Republic psychiatry reform : analyses and possibilities of shaping from a socio-scientific perspective

content.text: Tensions in glass ceramics. In the enclosed work the stress distribution in the environment of an inclusion was investigated in an infinitely extended glass matrix. Two different methods were used: the mathematical model calculation using finite elements method (FEM) and the experimental determination by voltage-soptic analysis.
content.title_en: Tensions in glass ceramics

content.text: Microbial modification of the isotope signature of nitrogen in marine particular material. To investigate the effects of microbial processes on the nitrogen isotope signature of particular material, experiments were carried out with material of different composition (East Sea, Southeast Atlantic, algae culture) and analyses of in situ material of different sea areas. The nitrogen isotope signature of the particular material, dissolved inorganic nitrogen, carbon isotope signature of the particular material, concentrations of particulate organic nitrogen, particulate organic carbon and dissolved inorganic nitrogen, bacterial numbers and bacterial nitrogen quantity were analysed. It is generally shown that microbial reactions can have a different impact on the isotope signature of the particular material.
content.title_en: Microbial modification of the isotope signature of nitrogen in marine particular material

content.text: CIDNP investigations of photoinduced radical pair reactions with field cyclication in the magnetic field range 0 to 7 Tesla. The focus of the work is the investigation of photoinduced (by light stimulation) radical pair reactions with the method of chemically induced dynamic magnetic magnetic spin polarization (short: CIDNP). The CIDNP method is a magnetic resonance method, the observable of which is a non-thermally generated nuclear spin polarization, which is detected with NMR methods ...
content.title_en: CIDNP investigations of photoinduced radical pair reactions with field cyclication in the magnetic field range 0 to 7 Tesla

content.text: The interaction of sulphosuccinates with tanned collagen: a contribution to the basics of leather grease. In the work the influence of the use of ethoxylated sulphosuccinates on the softness of collagen substrates was investigated. Chromated skin powder and chrome-tanned leather (Wet-blue) serve as collagen substrates. Special attention was paid to the influence of the chain length of sulphosuccinates, the offer and application conditions on the insulation of the fibrils of collagen (as documented by REM image) and the C14-ethoxylated sulphosuccinate was most well-known. The results were based on the calculation of the fat cover of collagen structural elements, the critical mizelle formation concentration of sulphosuccinate solutions and the change of the isoelectric point of collagen, the deposition of the fat molecules and the occurrence of ionic and hydrophobic interactions were demonstrated. The results are a contribution to the theory of the fatification of collagen and the optimization of leather grease.
content.title_en: On the interaction of sulphosuccinates with tanned collagen : a contribution to the basics of leather grease

content.text: In this paper, the polymer analogue ketal splitting of cyclic poly-(keten-O,O-acetal) is presented, which should achieve the formation of a poly-(keton)/ poly-(enol). In particular, the reactions to poly-(2-methylen-4-phenyl-1,3-dioxolan) were investigated. The conversions with triphenylmethyl-tetrafluoroborate (tritylenetrafluoroborate), iodtrimethylsilane and hydrochloric acid led to the depolymerisation of the starting polymer. The conversions with LDA and silylation reagents led to the formation of poly-(silyleneol ethers). The products show an ununiform polymer structure (cyclization reaction as a side reaction) and are hydrolysis sensitive.
content.title_en: π-conjugated polymers by ketal splitting on cyclic poly-(keten-O,O-acetal)enes

content.text: Numerical investigations into the fracture and deformation behaviour of fractured mountain areas during tunnel construction. The Distinct Element Method (UDEC program of Itasca) was used to systematically investigate the fracture and deformation behaviour of fractured mountain areas during tunnel construction and the interactions between the mountains and tunnel construction. The numerical investigations showed the factors affecting the fracture and deformation behaviour and the main types of failure of fractured rock. A new "deactivation and reactivation process" was developed and successfully used. Based on the simulation of anchor and shotcrete fuses and the individual construction states in partial eruptions, a concept for assessing the stability of a cavity in cracked rock and for the dimensioning of the securing measures was presented.
content.title_en: Numerical investigations into the fracture and deformation behaviour of fractured mountain areas in tunnel construction

content.text: Computer-based image data analysis in environmental monitoring: for the use of knowledge-based classifications and change analyses with commercially available remote sensing software. The work examines to what extent the computer-based analysis of digital air and satellite image data can optimize existing processes in environmental monitoring. First, the state of research in the field of "Remote Sensing in Environmental Monitoring" is documented before the various pre-processing processes (mosaicing, atmospheric correction, etc.) of the data are explained. Subsequently, the state of research for classification methods and methods of change analyses is developed before the own partly newly developed methods/methods are applied; the traceability forms a focus here. The results lead to a practical guide. The critical examination of possible sources of error is intended to help the reader to assess the performance of the processes. An outlook on future application possibilities of remote sensing data in environmental monitoring is the conclusion; the focus is on ethical questions and the role of the Internet.
content.title_en: Computerized image data analysis in environmental monitoring: for the use of knowledge-based classifications and change analyses with commercially available remote sensing software

content.text: Knowledge transformations : semantic analyses of science and mediation texts. Scientific knowledge is changed during mediation, not simply transferred. This book analyses such knowledge transformations using the example of the ozone hole debate. This makes it clear that basic questions of expert lay communication arise, for example whether the mass media transfer of scientific knowledge creates new knowledge or merely "elegant nonsense for the people".
content.title_en: Knowledge transformations : semantic analyses of science and communication texts

content.text: Bahnhofstrassen : History and Meaning. Bahnhofsstraße as a place of self-presentation and self-insurance of urban elites is dedicated to this book. This is done by the example of six German cities between the mid-19th century and the present: Weimar, Gotha, Chemnitz, Frankfurt am Main, Hanover and Wiesbaden are the subject of consideration. As a city entrance and connection to the city centre, Bahnhofsstraße can look back on a long tradition as a space of public stagings of parades or festive events. But it also offered the appropriate architectural framework for political demonstrations of power. The author opens up interesting insights into this central aspect of urban and political history. The differentiated and vivid representation is of fundamental importance for the decoding of the relationship between space and ritual due to its historical, sociological, cultural, cultural and cultural historical and architectural references.
content.title_en: Bahnhofstrassen : History and meaning

Properties can be both technological and other. The work shows that good technological properties often only represent necessary conditions of use, while the other characteristics neglected in engineering sciences are often decisive factors of application. In the empirical part, the analysis of technological, economic, ecological and social factors by means of cross-sectional and case studies shows deficits, shows positive starting points, and confirms the outstanding technological properties. content.text: Research on the mechanical properties of the sand cast magnesium alloy AZ91. In this work the mechanical properties of the magnesium sand casting alloy AZ91 were investigated depending on the process parameters. It was shown that the application of filtration, grain fineness and heat treatment can adjust the level of the mechanical properties of the sand casting to that of the die casting. In this work the influence of the process parameters on the stress relaxation and damping properties was also investigated.
content.title_en: Research on the mechanical properties of the sand cast magnesium alloy AZ91

content.text: Data processing and lifetime measurements in 107In. In the first part of this work, the data recording system for the OSIRIS and GEMINI spectrometers at the University of Cologne's Institute of Nuclear Physics is described. For the implementation of the system on a PowerPC under the Lynx-OS operating system, the development of device drivers was necessary. In addition, all other programs - exclusively in client-server architecture - were developed. The graphical user interfaces form the interface for the user. They make all functions necessary for setting up and conducting experiments easily accessible.The results of an experiment at the g-spectrometer CFSP in Legnaro, Italy are presented in the second part of the work. In this experiment, the proven Cologne reaction chamber for measuring lifetimes -- the ball-plungen -- together with the Italian particle spectrometer ISIS was used for the first time to use the 2pa output channel for the 104Cd. The choice of coincidence conditions in the projections of the g-coincidence matrix was only partially evaluated by the three levels of the data.
content.title_en: Data processing and life span measurements in 107In

content.text: Validation of models in survival analysis. In this work new test methods for evaluating the quality of different statistical models are developed. In particular, the situation of randomly right-centered data is discussed. Two different problems are examined, on the one hand the verification of parametric models on the basis of a sample and on the other hand the validation of semiparametric models for the case of two samples. The assessment of model quality is carried out by means of certain distance functions for measuring the deviations of the reality represented by the data from the investigated model. Limit values for empirical estimators of these functional models are derived using the functional delta method and on the other hand, suitable asymptotic test methods are constructed using the Bootstrap method.
content.title_en: Validation of models in survival analysis

content.text: This is the class of schur ring in algebraic combinatorics: graphs, partial difference sets and cycletomic schemes. The theory of schur rings, introduced in 1933 by I. Schur, played a role over several decades only in the field of permutation groups. Since the fifties, similar concepts such as association schemes, cellular rings or coherent configurations for various problems in algebraic combinatorics and statistics have been developed independently. In this dissertation, questions from the fields (1) exchangeable graphs, (2) strictly regular graphs and partial differences are discussed and (3) cyclotomic schemes are discussed in the context of these concepts. The first part deals with graphs with commuting adjacency matrices. Results for exchangeable regular graphs are presented and the questioning for non-regular graphs is determined. The second part deals with the construction of partial differences by strictly regular Cayley graphs. For this purpose, a theoretical and computer-based method is discussed to a full order of regular elements is defined in order of regular numbers.
content.title_en: Applications of Schur rings in algebraic combinatorics : graphs, partial difference sets and cyclotomic schemes

content.text: Some results concerning arrangements of half spaces and relative loss bounds. In the first part of the work we deal with the problem of embedding a concept class into an arrangement of Euclidian semi-spaces. We specify lower barriers for the dimension and upper barriers for the margin of such arrangements. For some concept classes we explicitly specify embedding with optimal margin. We also discuss applications of our results in communication complexity. In the second part of the work we deal with the competitive analysis of learning algorithms. In particular we simplify the proof of a relative fault barrier of Vovk for on-line linear regression. We prove a new barrier for off-line linear regression and generalize the results for on-line linear regression to a problem in reinforcement learning.
content.title_en: Some results concerning arrangements of half spaces and relative loss bounds

content.text: A Bayesian approach to learning Hidden Markov model topology with applications to biological sequence analysis. Hidden Markov models (HMM) are successfully used in statistical modelling and pattern recognition in numerous application areas. There is a fundamental problem in the selection of the underlying architecture or topology, i.e. the number of states of the HMM and the transitions allowed between them. This applies especially if knowledge from the field of application is insufficient for a secured topology choice, or in the so-called black-box modeling. The importance of HMM topology arises from the fact that too large a number of states leads to unreliable parameter estimates and, on the other hand, a too small number of states does not allow to model relevant statistical properties of the data source. We have developed an algorithm that learns an HMM including topology and parameters from sequence data generated by an ergodic process. The Bayes\'s approach used for this allows control of the achieved generalization via a central apri parameter.
content.title_en: A Bayesian approach to learning Hidden Markov model topology with applications to biological sequence analysis

content.text: Technology ethics and its foundations : presented in an examination of the technology ethical approaches of Günter Ropolch and Walter Christoph Zimmerli. The subject of the discussion is the disclosure of the factual and potential ethical relation of technology. The fundamental principle for each ethics is a certain understanding of man and his reality. This fundamental positionality is to be noted against discourse and process ethical approaches as well as against utilitarian levelling fundamental theoretical questions. The present investigation from a Protestant perspective shows the relevance of technology ethics not only for technicians but also for human actions in general. - This discussion concerns the actual and potential ethical ramifications of technology. All ethical issues are based on a particular understanding of humanity and its reality.
content.title_en: Technology ethics and its foundations : presented in an examination of the ethical approaches of Günter Ropohl and Walter Christoph Zimmerli

content.text: A posteriori error estimators for mixed finite elements in linear elasticity. Based on the PEERS element or Stenberg's family of mixed finite elements, a posteriori error estimators are developed. Both a residual error estimators for the natural standard on the used rooms and error estimators are considered based on local auxiliary problems. For the latter, the stability of Stenberg's elements is first demonstrated in relation to this standard. The error estimators are reliable and efficient, and further care is taken to ensure that the estimates are robust with regard to the Lamè parameters.
content.title_en: A posteriori error estimater for mixed finite elements in linear elasticity

content.text: Radiation effects in instationary heating wire measurements on porous thermal insulation materials. The integral differential equation for describing the energy transport of coupled radiation/wire in a grey, absorbing and emitting medium limited by two coaxial cylindrical surfaces is solved numerically with the method of finite differences in order to theoretically analyse radiation effects in instationary heating wire measurements on porous thermal insulation materials. The influence of the emission coefficient of the sample medium, the emissivity of the heating wire, the measuring temperature, the heating power and the thermal contact resistance is investigated. Based on the calculation results, the effective thermal conductivity of porous thermal insulation materials is underdetermined if the emission coefficients of the sample medium are small. The lower limit of the permitted extinction range shifts to larger values with increasing measuring temperature. The thermal contact resistance means a distortion risk of measurement results, especially if the heating wire is strongly emitted and the sample surface reflects.
content.title_en: Radiation effects on instationary heating wire measurements of porous thermal insulation

Optimization of optical transmission functions corresponds to a viewing of the optical system in the function image. In a later step -- the structural design -- the determined transmission function can be transferred to the geometric description of an optical element. To optimize transmission functions we consider the application of so-called projection algorithms. These are iterative algorithms, in which projections are used to achieve so-called limits, in order to find a solution for the free parameters of the optimization problem, which meets the target requirements corresponding to the limits. In addition to an examination of the design of diffractive beam dividers, observations are carried out in the work to improve the convergence behavior of projection algorithms with the help of intensified projections. In addition, so-called multifunctional projection algorithms are developed for simultaneous optimization with respect to any number of system requirements and their use in the improvement of the tolerance properties of optical systems.
content.title_en: Projection algorithms in wave-optic transmission design

content.text: Antichrist-Polemic in the period of the Reformation and the battles of faith until the beginning of the 17th century : Argument, form and function. The antichrist-Prophecy plays a prominent role in the cultural history of the Middle Ages and the early modern era. The high efficiency and popularity of this image of enemy is evident especially in the period of the Reformation and the battles of faith, where the antichrist-Polemic since Luther's equation of the institution of the papacy with the antichrist developed a tremendous potential. This work examines the argumentation, form and function of the antichrist-Polemic of the various confessional camps of this period until the beginning of the 17th century. The focus is on content analysis, traditions and norms, the polemization and proof methods and the rhetorical strategies as well as their role in the struggle for confession to explain their enormous success. The investigation provides fundamental insights about the functioning of effective polemics.
content.title_en: Antichrist-Polemic in the period of the Reformation and the battles of faith until the beginning of the 17th century : Argument, form and function

content.text: Successful cooperation: Success factors of cooperative processes in regional development. Cooperation between individuals and institutions has proved to be one of the most important factors of successful regional development in recent years. Currently, several hundred co-operative processes are being carried out in Germany. Not all of them achieve the goals they set themselves and some fail to achieve avoidable errors. The present book deals with the factors relevant for success and failure. The basis is a comprehensive empirical study. Four case studies are being examined in depth, another 23 processes analysed. Sorted by W-questions What? Who? Why? The success factors on objectives, content framework conditions, organisation, actors, integration of politics, integration of administration, networking, process control, moderation, result orientation, external monitoring, marketing, benefit, motivation are being addressed. The work includes findings from other studies. The work provides moderators and responsible persons with information on what they need to consider when designing processes. The results are transferable to all processes with bottom-up proportions and not limited to field development.
content.title_en: Successful co-operation : Success factors of cooperative processes in regional development
