content.text: Geometry and trigonometrics of homogeneous 3-manifolds with 4-dimensional isometry group. In this dissertation, all the mono-contiguous homogeneous 3-manifolds (M,g) studied by a Riemann submersion over a homogeneous 2-manifoldness fibers. It is shown that each geodetic orbit is a 1-parameter group of isometry. By means of the Clairaut set, each geodetic can be assigned a slope size relative to the fiber. The Jacobi fields and the conjugated radius are explicitly calculated as a function of this slope size. It is shown that each geodetic under the submersion is projected onto a curve of constant geodetic curvature. In addition, the vertical offset of the geodetic is given, which is projected on closed curves. In addition, the radius of injectivity and the intersection of (M,g) is calculated. In addition, a sine set for triangles is derived (M,g). Finally, a complete description of the trigonometrics is given in the form of trigonometric relations.
content.title_en: Geometry and trigonometry of homogeneous 3-manifolds with 4-dimensional isometry group

content.text: Monte Carlo simulation of adsorption of amphiphilic molecules on solid surfaces. The work presents results of Monte Carlo simulations for adsorption and self-organisation of amphiphilic molecules on solid surfaces. The aim of the work is to investigate the relationship between molecular properties and thermodynamic conditions for the formation of adsorption of adsorption-based aggregates. The core grained grid model describes the adsorption of model surfactants on flat surfaces. Hydrophilic, hydrophobic and chemically heterogeneous model surfaces are considered. The results of the simulations are in line with experimental investigations and provide interpretation aids for the observed structures. For the use of surfactants in calcium fluorite flotation, it was shown that the effect of the co-collector surfactant is based on adsorption.
content.title_en: Monte Carlo simulation of adsorption of amphiphilic molecules on solid surfaces

content.text: Parallel space separation processes for optimization problems with applications on parameter identification tasks. The subject of this work are procedures for large free and restrected minimization problems. The approach is pursued to design procedures with an immanent parallel structure with the help of the space separation concept, which thus lead to coarsely parallelizable algorithms.
content.title_en: Parallel space separation procedures for optimization problems with applications on parameter identification tasks

content.text: Experimental deformation of jadeite. To investigate the rheology of the mixed crystal series Jadeit-Diopsid experimental investigations were carried out at the end of the Jadeite. Polycrystalline jadeite samples were synthesized from a glass in a stamp-cylinder apparatus. These samples were deformed in a modified Griggs apparatus at a closing pressure of 2.5 GPa at different temperatures and deformation rates in axial direction. Parameters for a flow law for transfer smells were derived. Deformation in the regime of transfer creep could be derived from an analysis of the microstructures. The microstructures produced were compared with those of natural, deformed omphacites. Application of the Flow Law allows an estimation of stress magnitudes in the eclogite layer in subduction zones. From experiments on natural samples the critical shear tension for mechanical twin formation in Jadeite was derived.
content.title_en: Experimental deformation of jadeite

content.text: Phase conjugation in Silenite crystals and BaTiO3 with ns pulse lasers. The work is concerned with the realization of phase conjugation in ns pulse with Silenite crystals and BaTi03. In addition to characterization of the crystals in the intensity range used, various methods for the realization of phase conjugation are described and analyzed. Already successfully applied in cw operation, such as phase conjugation with fibre-like Silenite crystals, are realized for the first time in the impulse range, structures already realized in the impulse range, such as the self-pumped phase conjugation in BaTi03, are characterized more precisely, and new structures for the four-wave mixing in Silenite crystals are developed and analyzed. The focus of the investigations is on the evaluation of the quality of phase conjugation arrangements. An interferometric method is used to this end, whose advantages are demonstrated compared to the international Pinhol method.
content.title_en: Phase conjugation in dillenite crystals and BaTiO3 with ns pulse lasers

content.text: Oxalamidine type ligands for the construction of mono-, bi- and tetranuclear complexes with redoxactive transition metals. Oxalamidines are special derivatives of oxalic acid, which can be used as multifunctional ligands in metal organo- and complex chemistry due to their four nitrogen donor atoms. Thus, they react in their protonated form with suitable metal precursors under the formation of mononuclear compounds, in which the metal centre coordinates to the 1.4-diazadia unit. A special feature is the possibility of coupled cation/anion coordination. After deprotonation of the oxalamides with suitable bases and conversion with metal compounds, a large number of binuclear oxalamideinate complexes can be represented. By the choice of suitable reaction conditions, tetranuclear complexes are also accessible, in which the oxalamideinate acts as a bridging ligand.
content.title_en: Oxalamidine type ligands for the construction of mono-, bi- and tetranuclear complexes with redoxactive transition metals

content.text: Symmetry of the quantum cohomology ring of Grassmann's varieties. I define an involution on the quantum cohomology ring, which is related to complex conjugation on its spectrum, and defines a kind of inversion. Together with the cyclic symmetry of the quantum cohomology ring discovered by Agnihotri and Woodward, these symmetries generate the zero space of the bilinear form, which is given as the sum of coefficients in the development of products with respect to the slipper base. I show that the equivalence classes of this relation are freely generated by Schubert classes, whose young diagrams are contained in a small rectangle. Furthermore, I prove a simple inductive formula for a modified product of Schubert classes, which closely correlates with the classical cup product of Schubert classes. As an application, I obtain a formula for the sum of Littlewood-Richardson numbers, which in the development of a product of Schur polynomials, a elementary formula for a variable number of numbers of the quantum numbers of the quantum numbers of the quantum numbers of the quantum numbers of the quantum numbers of the quantum numbers of the quantum.
content.title_en: Symmetries in quantum Schubert calculus

content.text: Polly two - a public key cryptosystem based on Polly Cracker. Fellows and Koblitz developed a general, combinatorial-algebraic public key cryptoprocess in 1993. Since then it was unclear whether certain instances of Polly Cracker existed. Especially the so-called linear algebra attacks of Boo Barkee et al. (1994) and Lenstra (1998) seemed to be strong means to compromise instances. Apart from Koblitz's suggestion "Graph Perfect Code", no methods were developed to apply the linear attacks. In my dissertation I analyze the linear algebra attacks and develop a new public key cryptoprocess "Polly Two", based on Polly Cracker. Through a detailed security analysis I show how to create Polly Two instances that are safe against the linear algebra attacks. Additionally I suggest concrete parameter strategies and pre-emptive approaches.
content.title_en: Polly two - a public key cryptosystem based on Polly Cracker

content.text: In this work, optimal experimental plans are determined to estimate the coefficients in the heteroskedastic polynomial regression model. First, based on D-optimality, a standardized maximin optimization criterion is derived, which is robust against misspecifications of the unknown parameters in the respective efficiency function. Two different methods are used for calculation: canonical moments and differential equations. There are explicit solutions in the class of experimental plans with minimal carrier. In this case, the carriers for different classes of efficiency functions result as zeros of the classical orthogonal polynomials. In many cases, the optimumity of these special experimental plans is demonstrated in the class of all experimental plans with finite carrier.
content.title_en: Classical orthogonal polynomials and their application in optimal experimental planning

content.text: Fuzzy-Logic Filter for the Global Atmospheric Watch Program : Development of database-based filter functions for identifying the air mass influences in the global station Zugspitze measurement series. The Global Atmospheric Watch measurement program of the World Meteorological Organization aims to continuously record the atmospheric background and its changes. For the European space, this observation is carried out at the Global Station Zugspitze, which, despite the situation, experiences temporary disturbances due to local effects. In the work, filter rules for the train tip measurement series are developed, which are a prerequisite for the representative description of the atmospheric background. The filters are based on a measurement series analysis and take into account air mass influences resulting from vertical transports from the base layer and stratospheric intrusions. As filter parameters, air chemical and meteorological measurement data, 3D reverse trajectories and emission inventories are used. The methodical implementation of the filter functions is carried out with the model presentation of the Fuzzy-Logic.
content.title_en: Fuzzy-Logic Filter for the Global Atmospheric Watch Program : Development of database-based filter functions for identifying air mass influences in the measurement series of the Global Station Zugspitze

content.text: Fuzzy Business Process Management. Modelling business processes has been at the heart of the analysis and design of the operational structures of companies and public administrations since the early 1990s. In contrast to the calculatoric-mathematical modeling, this form of (structural) enterprise modeling has developed to date little formal means for the systematic handling of blurring aspects, although a variety of flow-organizational issues are subject to immanent blurring of different kinds and a flexibilized practice of the processes is becoming increasingly important. With this work, the author pursues the goal of formally specifying, practical concepts for the illustration in the broadest sense of uncharmerical information aspects in the enterprise modeling with the focus of business process analysis. The aim of this work is to develop a synergistical connection of elements of the fuzzy-theory, the graphically-based concept of the graphical and the graphically-based simulation of a mathematically-based, the mathematically-based approach of a business process management.
content.title_en: Fuzzy business process management

content.text: Formal verification of digital systems with Petrinetzen. The work deals with the design and verification of digital systems. The aim is to model and formally verify digital systems with Petrinetzen on a functional level. In the first part of the work a petrinet-based hardware design methodology is proposed. Petrinetzen are used as a means of description for digital systems and as a tool for their simulation, validation, analysis and verification. The formal verification of a Petrinetzent model is realized with the method of property verification.
content.title_en: Formal verification of digital systems with Petrinetzen

content.text: Production and characterisation of lateral microstructured monofilms on silicon and glass chip surfaces for use in bio-chips. In this work, hydrophobic monofilms on silicon and glass surfaces were produced by combining surface chemical and microsystem technology methods and microstructured by producing hydrophilic OH binders. For the production of bio-chips, OH chemotopes were modified by further surface chemical reactions to monomolecular amino surfaces for protein binding and monomolecular surfaces with ethylene glycol links for DNA immobilization. In addition to the characterization of molecular monofilms by wetting behaviour, AFM, and scanning electron microscopy, fluorescence microscopic studies were the focus of the work on quantitative determination of binding group dens and biomolecules.
content.title_en: Production and characterisation of lateral microstructured monofilms on silicon and glass chip surfaces for use in biochips

content.text: Computers and ethics instead of computer ethics. The computer as a powerful example of changes in technical action within our technological culture is not only a further development of technology in the industrialized world, but offers new possibilities of action as a so-called universal tool (moor), "autonomous" (weizenbaum) or "non-trivial" (of Foerster) machine. These models of ethics can no longer be met with previously developed models of ethics. Without a reinterpretation of the concept of purpose-rational action, it becomes difficult to conduct a discussion about computers and ethics, which is permanently integrated into the current discussions of technology and media ethics.
content.title_en: Computers and ethics instead of computer ethics

content.text: Cultural landscape catalogues for urban spaces: open spaces : illustrated by examples from Hamburg. Klappentext: Kulturhistorische Werte find increasing attention in spatial planning. Up to now, however, no general evaluation system for cultural landscape elements exists. Extensive discussions are being held about previous proposals for recording and evaluation. Subsequently, the book describes a newly developed method for mapping and evaluation especially for undeveloped areas in urban spaces. From a geographical point of view, a new instrument for urban planning is proposed. With exemplary cadastral entries of selected Hamburg open spaces, the volume documents the practicality of the method. The basis for the work was a diploma thesis at the Institute of Geography of the University of Hamburg. It thus offers suggestions for further scientific discussion and future planning practice.
content.title_en: Cultural landscape catalogues for urban spaces: open spaces : illustrated by examples from Hamburg

content.text: Ulrich Hufeld, representing the Authority, establishes the representative act for the Authority in general administrative law. He poses the classic Quis iudicabit question ad personam. Under the premise that every decision of the Administration is based not only on standards but also on persons, he develops a democratic administrative person law. In his systematic investigation he deals with internal forms of participation, opens up the external and internal legal, but not completely determined representation of the hierarchically formed authorities - such as the ministries and the financial offices -, discusses the collegial representation and asks for the legal administrative officer.' The author tests the contribution to the system formation in the last chapter, which distinguishes the possible representation errors and integrates the error consequences into the general error theory for reasons of personal incompetence. (Source: Verlag).
content.title_en: The representation of the Authority

In the present work, two methods for the production of electro-optical wiring carriers were investigated. Particular attention was paid to the development of the so-called waveguide-in-copper technology. With this method, polymer waveguides are available for the first time to generate within a multilayer circuit board by using only typical production sequences of the circuit board technology. content.text: The author reconstructs some of the most influential time theories from natural sciences, philosophy and social sciences. He does this out of a constructiveist attitude to knowledge and develops a new and independent time concept that can meet the demands of an inter-actionist-constructivist pedagogy on the background of postmodern problems. The unravelling of the ideological roots of different time theories makes clear how mostly unquestionably assumed culturally prevailing time concepts can be thought differently through shifts of perspective, accents or aspect changes. Through this deconstruction of the objective and transcendental unity of time, this appears to be a pluralistic result of social construction and situational interaction. However, it is precisely because it is "remembered" of the time-situation and the possibility of time-taking that it is "remembered" of the time-situation.
content.title_en: Ways at the moment : a constructive interpretation of objective, subjective and intersubjective time

content.text: Traveling to the strange Pompeii: anti-classical antiquities perception of German Italian travellers 1750 - 1870. The discovery of Pompeii and Herkulaneum seemed to occur in a happy coincidence with the genesis of classicistic taste at the beginning of the 18th century. Instead of "noble simplicity and quietness", travellers saw a city of small, arabesque decorated buildings with windowless, often obscenely decorated rooms. Their reports struggle to balance with the classicist antiquities
content.title_en: Travels to the strange Pompeii : anti-classical antiquities perception of German Italian traveler 1750 - 1870

content.text: Multi-stage market segmentation for new customer acquisition: using the example of telecommunications. Contents: Differentiated sales management as a challenge for companies in business-to-business markets Methodical foundations of differentiated sales control Basics and approaches of market segmentation on business-to-business markets Further development of a multi-stage segmentation approach as a basis for differentiated sales control and empirical verification on the example of telecommunications In the context of increasing market saturation trends, especially in the telecommunications market, the acquisition of attractive business customers becomes a growing challenge for the companies. However, the instruments currently used in sales of this task are only partially met. Based on a multi-stage market segmentation approach, Oliver Kohrmann develops a method for the acquisition of new business customers, which takes into account both psychographic and economic customer characteristics. It refers both to the requirements of telecommunications providers and the value of individual customers explicitly in his considerations.
content.title_en: Multi-stage market segmentation for new customer acquisition : on the example of telecommunications

content.text: The "German settlement city" and the "model settlement of the German labor front" of Braunschweig-Mascherode, the origin - design - analysis. During the time of the "Third Reich" Braunschweig had the role of the central city within a huge center of the armaments industry. In a very special scope, housing had to be created for the settlement of soldiers and military members. As a general example for the construction in the National Socialism, the present book represents for the first time a city in its entirety extremely factually and with extensive pictorial material. In the then capital of the state of Braunschweig architecture, not only in settlement and housing, became a special instrument of political endeavours. Also representative party buildings, urban planning, barracks or bunker installations were part of a total construction activity, which is only understandable from the complete way of viewing. content.text: Knowledge management and knowledge controlling in learning organisations: a system-theoretical approach. Content:Learning organisations as knowledge-based systems Knowledge management Knowledge controlling We are living through a period of fundamental changes in economy and society. Knowledge has become the most important value-added factor for our companies, the management of the resource knowledge is the decisive success factor in global competition. Knowledge management has not lost any relevance to practice since the publication of this book. The fourth edition has not changed the fundamental character of the work, but some improvements have been made in the text and the underlying literature updated. The central research goal of this work is to design the learning organisation as a knowledge-based system and to design this management concept in a practical manner through a management system. After an introduction to the basics of system and learning theory necessary for understanding the work, the conception of the learning organisation as a knowledge-based system is carried out. Subsequently, a design framework of knowledge management and knowledge controlling is developed in learning organisations that are applicable in practice.
content.title_en: Knowledge management and knowledge controlling in learning organisations : a system-theoretical approach

content.text: The presence and spread of Borrelia burgdorferi in selected natural herd areas of Thuringia, with special consideration of the role of the main vector Ixodes ricinus L. 1758. In three natural herd areas of Lyme disease in the Thüringer Ilmtal, populations of the Ixodes ricinus L. 1758 were investigated with regard to host search activity and Borrelia prevalence. This showed a negative correlation between these two parameters in Adulti and Nymphs both seasonal and annual. Furthermore, the role of abundant host species (rott mouse, yellowneck mouse, deer) was included in the prevalence studies in order to contribute to the knowledge of the function of the natural herd system pathogen vector host.

Individual learning and development opportunities and thus social participation opportunities also mediate through a successful connection to institutions, e.g. to the educational aid. From life-historical narratives of young women, central aspects can be developed for the success of such follow-up processes. These refer on the one hand to the biographical dimension, as life-historical experiences influence the perception of development opportunities and learning options. They refer on the other to the gender-specific dimension and thus to typical conflict fields, which lead to the sheltering of girls and structure the care processes in the institutional context. Whether the girls reached by home education can develop an independent life plan or whether they more or less reproduce the life of their mothers or families of origin, is decisive of the support in their self-employment striving and the reinforcement in their claim to their own life. Home education then opens up to them the extended developmental spaces, to which they hoped so much with the abandonment of the family, if they can find their own self-reliability and can also discover their own self-consciousness, and thus maintain their own self-consciousness.
content.title_en: Self-employment and some happiness: influences of public education on the biographical perspectives of young women

In the context of the numerical simulations, equilibriums were simulated in a closed and an open system. In a closed system, a single-storage topology is obtained, which is not too large for a disturbance, which passes into the turbulences as the disturbance increases. The simulations of an open system were intended to model the so-called jets of fast outflows of matter along the rotation axis. It has been possible to describe a balance in which matter is collected at the equator level and then reflowed in the form of jets.

content.text: Theoretical electro-technology: an introduction. The classic of "theoretical electrical engineering" was completely reworked for this 16th edition. The authors have attached particular importance to maintaining the Küpfmüllerian style, which has made the book a bestseller. content.text: Aspects of k-k routing in meshes and OTIS networks. The performance of parallel computers communicating via a connection network is crucial for efficient data transport. A basic transport problem in such a computer is the k-k routing problem. In this work, aspects of this problem are examined in r-dimensional grids and OTIS-G networks. The first forgetful (oblivious) routing algorithm is presented, which solves the k-k routing problem in these networks in an asymptotic optimal runtime with constant buffer size. For OTIS-G networks, lower runtime barriers are specified for the problem investigated, which are based on the diameter and the bisection width of the networks. Furthermore, an algorithm is presented that solves the k-k sorting problem with a runtime close to the bite and diameter limit. Based on the OTIS-G networks, a new class of networks is introduced, the so-called Extended OTIS-G networks, which differ from the OTIS-G network's smaller diameter.
content.title_en: Aspects of k-k routing in meshes and OTIS networks

content.text: The interdyne interferometers for non-contact vibration analysis are the most common tools for the non-contact detection of mechanical vibrations. Both Speckle and Hologram interferometry for the analysis of surface vibrations as well as heterodyne interferometers (laser vibrometers) are the established measuring methods in this field. The use of homodyne interferometers (single frequency interferometers) for vibration analysis has until now required an optical surface of the measuring object. An advanced system based on a single frequency interferometer, which is distinguished by a high linearity and low measurement uncertainty, is the subject of this dissertation. In the dissertation the fields of application and requirements of non-contact vibration measurement systems are presented. The focus is on the use of the classical single frequency interferometry for vibration analysis under normal industrial conditions of rough and unprepared surfaces. The possibilities of the interdyne interferometer are analyzed in the context of the analysis of the interdyne interferometers.
content.title_en: Homodyne interferometer for contactless vibration analysis

content.text: The integrated state density of Schrödinger operators with random, inhomogeneous potentials. In this work two models of operators with random but inhomogeneous disturbances are considered: Schrödinger operators with random surface potentials and such with falling chance. The existence of the integrated (surface) state density defined in this way and its independence from the accidental realization of the potential are shown. For Schrödinger operators with random surface potentials it is shown that the surface state density thus defined is a distribution of order 1 at most, which can be represented here as the derivation of a signed measure. In the case of completely inhomogeneous disturbances, which are generated by potentials with falling chance, a strong law of large numbers for non-stationary random variables is generally proved, which replaces the ergodentheorems available only for stationary potentials and thus shows the existence of the integrated state density and its independence from marginal conditions.
content.title_en: For integrated state density of Schrödinger operators with random, inhomogeneous potentials

content.text: Structure studies of laser modified crystal areas in quartz. In this work, modified crystals were investigated by femtosecond lasers. The aim was to clarify the mechanism of the waveline. High-resolution X-ray topography and high-resolution X-ray diffractometry were combined. By means of finite element simulation, the deformation field and thus the distribution of local refractive indices were determined. The mechanism of the waveline in laser modified quartz crystals could be clarified in the present work. It is a compaction of the surrounding material around an expanded core that produces refractive number modifications by means of the elastoptic effect.
content.title_en: Structural investigations of laser modified crystal areas in quartz

content.text: The first SiC/HfB2-based micro hotplane for metal oxide gas sensors were used for the first time in this work. For the first time, silicon carbide (SiC) and Hafnium diboride (HfB2) were used as materials for a microheater. Due to the small modification of the production processes, the heater can be used in a way that allows both the automotive application range (12V-24V) and portable devices (1V-2V) for a variety of different measuring gases. It is the first microheater for gas sensors in the world to allow battery operation at only 1-2 V. The modular manufacturing approach allows the reduction of the development and production costs for the different application areas. From the market development in sensor technology, industrial requirements and alternative technologies competing with the metal oxide gas sensors, the sensor's requirement profile is based on a thick 10-bit material.
content.title_en: A new SiC/HfB 2 based micro hotplane for metal oxide gas sensors

content.text: Stabilization of He-Ne lasers for interference optical measurement technology. Interference optical length measurement technology is based on the use of coherent laser radiation whose wavelength represents the measure. Reproducibility and accuracy of the vacuum wave length determines the uncertainty of length measurement. This thesis describes the development and application of various methods for stabilizing the frequency of He-Ne lasers of wavelength at 633 nm. The stabilization characteristics are derived directly from the amplification curve or from external atomic transitions e.g. from molecular iodine. The methods that refer to the amplification curve are the most widely used methods. This includes the two-mode comparison method, which is the basis of stabilized laser systems for industrial applications and is examined in this work specifically using the reactive radiation of commercial lasers. However, the center frequency of the amplification curve is strongly determined by the gas composition and causes a great uncertainty of the laser frequency. For this reason, the frequencies of stabilized systems must be determined by frequency comparisons against a reference stabilized frequency stability of high frequency stability.
content.title_en: Stabilization of He-Ne lasers for interfering optical measurement

content.text: Patterns and mechanisms of plant community assembly in an industrially degraded ecosystem. 4207 Spatial and temporal patterns of colonization by higher plants were investigated at the Steudnitz site, which is located about 10 km north of Jena. The study area was exposed between 1957 and 1990 to the emissions of a nearby fertilizer plant, which led to significant impairments of the ecosystem. The study shows that the order of colonization is correlated with the salt tolerance of the settling plant species and with the propagation capacity of their diaspores. On a large scale, the spatial vegetation patterns are correlated with the level of soil nitrogen, while on a smaller scale, soil moisture exerts an influence. The occurrence of strategy types (grass/breeds and one-year/two-year/multi-year plants) corresponds largely and entirely to the predictions derived from the theory. In addition, the study includes an examination of the diasporenbank and an experiment which examines the reaction of the plant community to various fertilises/microbials.
content.title_en: Patterns and mechanisms of plant community assemblly in an industrially degraded ecosystem

content.text: The applicability of mathematics in empirical sciences requires a philosophical explanation. On the one hand, it is an explanation of why knowledge of abstract objects and of the reality of experience can seem to be completely independent of them, such as numbers, relevant to the sciences of concrete objects, and on the other hand an explanation of how we as concrete beings can know something about mathematical objects at all. Some philosophers want to solve these problems by simply denying the existence of mathematical objects. On the other hand, the author rejects such nominalistic approaches after a thorough assessment. It is evident that nominalism cannot satisfactorily explain how mathematics can only mirror its field of object and yet provide us with applicable knowledge. On the other hand, the mathematical realism, which assumes that there are actually abstract objects to which mathematical discourse refers to, can answer the problems. However, it must be discussed in detail about this position by means of a "beware" mathematical realism, which means that abstract mathematical objects are universals, which have realizations in the reality of experience. This can be explained both by the empirical situation and by the context of the empirical context of the mathematical objects.
content.title_en: Number and Reality : a philosophical study of the applicability of mathematics

content.text: Geo-information systems in municipal planning practice. The universal manual for GIS application in the entire field of municipal planning and spatial planning. GIS can do much more than allow GIS information systems and cadastral applications to be identified. GIS applications and procedures are currently being developed in the field of local planning, which can significantly facilitate the development of municipal programmes and plans in the design and participation and approval phases. This applies in particular to standard tasks (regional planning, urban transport planning, youth assistance planning, landscape planning...) but also to informal planning tasks, such as the design of landmines and sites for wind turbines or the study of the impact of large tourist projects. These GIS procedures provide the authors with practical experience. In this context, technical innovations (e.g. integration of the Internet into the planning process) are considered. The processes covered can usually be transferred to any powerful GIS.
content.title_en: Geo-information systems in municipal planning practice

content.text: Perception and aesthetic education : to the reconception of aesthetic education in the paradigm of self-organisation. The work brings together in an interdisciplinary manner various approaches from human science disciplines of the humanities and natural sciences. It opens the discussion about the subject of aesthetic education first to the concept of aesthetic experience and then introduces physical and neurobiological models to self-organization into a theory of synergetic self-organization of aesthetic experience. On the basis of this theory, a radical-constructivist concept of aesthetic perception and aesthetic behaviour is developed, which leads to a new understanding of aesthetic education in the sense of a comprehensive educational principle. This principle has consequences for the view of the educand as well as for the self-understanding of the educator: within the framework of such an educational principle, not only the promotion of aesthetic competence and aesthetic understanding appears as a central educational task, but also the understanding of the educational interaction and with it the ethos of educational action towards an aesthetic education attitude.
content.title_en: Perception and aesthetic education : to reconception of aesthetic education in the paradigm of self-organisation

In the first part it is exploited that if the spectral norm associated to a function is "small", then the function itself has a "high complexity" (e.g. it is not efficient by (technically limited) circuits over threshold functions of depth 2 calculable and it has high communication complexity. It is naturally presented functions (booleic praedicates of cryptographic functions), which have provably a small spectral norm. Here techniques from the algebra (e.g. complex matrices and norms) and from the number theory (e.g. exponential series) are used. In the second part related functions are considered to the diffie-Hellman function, s.g. P-Diffie-Hellman functions are used lower limits on the interpoly and the interpoly.

content.text: Organization on the wire : Consequences of the use of e-mail in companies. Email systems have been increasingly used in companies since the 1980s. Business economics are expected to increase efficiency and organizational improvements by using e-mail systems. In sociology, the use of communication techniques in organizations is analysed differently and its consequences are generally assessed negatively. Both disciplines have empirically investigated the use of e-mail systems in companies based on their approach in many studies. However, the collected data do not clearly demonstrate the assumptions underlying the studies or can they be linked to general statements without contradiction. The question remains, both scientifically and practically relevant, in what the connection between the use of e-mail systems and intended or feared changes in organizations exists in general. Since the empirical data were obtained on the basis of secured methods, new insights can only be gained on the basis of another theoretical model. With the help of the sociological system theory, the organizational functions performed by e-mail systems are precisely determined and the resulting consequences for the organization of companies are described and evaluated. This makes it clear which forms of use remain negative and which forms of organisation lead to the changes in the organisation and which forms of use are not positive or which are used in the company.
content.title_en: Organization on wire : Consequences of e-mail use in companies

content.text: Studies of laser-induced cavitation with nanosecond and femtosecond lasers. The optical breakthrough that is the focus of a strong laser pulse can tear liquids open. A bubble develops which is suitable as a well reproducible model for the research of cavitation mechanisms. In the main part of this work, the bubbles induced by femtosecond laser pulses are experimentally investigated. By self-focusing these laser pulses in the liquid, an elongated geometry is first embossed on the bubbles. Within a few microseconds, a complex dynamic is developed, which gives a systematic overview. In a second part, selected properties of the bubbles produced by nanosecond laser pulses are illuminated. Neutron measurements are used to investigate whether the hypothesis of a cavitation-induced nuclear fusion can be refuted or confirmed.
content.title_en: Studies on laser-induced cavitation with nanosecond and femtosecond lasers

content.text: Message électronique or e-mail? : Attitudes of French computer scientists to official substitutes for the technical language of the Internet and to language policy: a WWW survey. France looks back on a long linguistic tradition. In the second half of the 20th century, attention is focused on anglizisms and possibilities for their replacement by French expressions. This also applies to Internet terminology since 1999. Not only in France, English-speaking terms are replaced by French terms, but also in the French-speaking parts of Belgium and Switzerland. In all three countries, corresponding commissions develop proposals for the replacement of English-speaking Internet terms. This work is based on an WWW survey to what extent neologisms such as message électronique, page d'accueil, four-nisseur d'accès, which originate from the official French Internet terminology, computer scientists from France, Belgium and Switzerland are known, and what general position the respondents represent to linguistic policy measures.
content.title_en: Message électronique or e-mail? : Settings of French computer scientists to official substitutes for the technical language of the Internet and to language policy : a WWW survey

content.text: Alternative routes of polysaccharide acylation : synthesis, structural analysis, properties. Within the scope of the work, efficient and gentle ways of esterification of polysaccharides should be explored. In addition to synthesis, new methods for structural clarification had to be developed to analyse the unconventional derivatives.
content.title_en: Alternative routes of polysaccharide acylation : synthesis, structural analysis, properties

content.text: Forest status recording and monitoring with high-resolution satellite image data. Forestry is traditionally one of the most important areas of application of remote sensing. In contrast to the operational use of analog aerial images, the practical use of satellite remote sensing in central Europe remains behind the technical possibilities. It is important to close the gap between technology development and practical application (praxis-ready). The characteristics of modern sensors also arouse hopes that satellite image data will soon be used for information acquisition for large-scale planning levels (especially forest facility, 1 : 10 000). In this work, planning-relevant application possibilities and (present) limits of satellite remote sensing for forest purposes are highlighted. The focus is on the requirements of the user. Commercial software products, standard procedures and data of operational reception systems of high and medium resolution are used. To improve the use of further information, a further exploration and further planning-relevant systematization approach for forest-based object types is proposed.
content.title_en: Forest state recording and monitoring with high-resolution satellite image data

content.text: Istanbul and the water: on the history of water supply and sanitation from the mid-19th century to 1966. In this volume, Noyan Dinçkal tells the history of water supply and sanitation in Istanbul, spanning a period of more than a hundred years. The author takes into account the respective interests of the actors, creates the political and economic framework conditions, outlines the natural conditions, the technologies used and the cultural specifics of water use, and discusses the importance of modernisation motifs and contemporary hygiene concepts. The book contains informative image and map material as well as graphic graphics. Noyan Dinçkal, born 1969, is a research associate at the Institute of History of Darmstadt University of Technology.
content.title_en: Istanbul and the water : the history of water supply and sanitation from the mid-19th century to 1966

content.text: Ultrafast carrier dynamics investigated by a novel pump-and-probe-terahertz technique. In this work, a novel method is proposed, the so-called "pump-and-probe-THz" technique for the investigation of charge carrier dynamics in the semiconductor GaAs and the high-temperature superconductor YBa2Cu3O7-x (YBCO). Here THz radiation is emitted from the sample to be investigated. This is additionally influenced by a pump laser pulse and measured in a time-dissolved manner. It is shown that charge carrier-relaxation times in the GaAs can be determined in their dependence on the external electric field, the charge carrier density and the charge carrier capture in localized states within the energy gap. In the case of YBCO, the relaxation rate of the quasiparts and the recombination time of the cooperative pairs can be determined in the superconducting state and thus the influence of different scattering mechanisms depending on the temperature below TC.
content.title_en: Ultrafast carrier dynamics investigated by a novel pump-and-sample-terahertz technique

content.text: Knowledge management processes in face-to-face and virtual communities: characteristics, design principles and success factors. Can one meet the knowledge management challenges that the information and knowledge society poses to individuals and companies with a centuries-old concept promisingly? Communities are the key to knowledge management from the point of view of many experts. This book provides a comprehensive overview of community concepts from the perspective of knowledge management and their implementation using concrete examples. In particular, the question of meaningful design criteria for communities is investigated. In addition, characteristics of face-to-face communities are presented as well as the specificities of virtual communities. In order to achieve in organizations and companies a promotion of knowledge management by communities, success factors for virtual and face-to-face communities are worked out using case studies and linked with existing findings. On this basis, a guidance framework for the development of communities is created, which enables the transfer of concepts into practice.
content.title_en: Knowledge management processes in face-to-face and virtual communities : characteristics, design principles and success factors

content.text: The Church's crisis of historism in the late 19th century, the Church's upheavals in religious life and the increasing church building activity in the Empire, presented the sacred decoration around 1900 tasks for which there were no historical models for the solution. The change in style in the religious building, the liturgical reforms and the current biblical criticism followed in the late 19th century new conceptions of the pictorial representation of salvation history. With the unbeautiful naturalism of life-sized frescoes to the earthly everyday life of Jesus or the ornamentation of the youth style, the church painting "strapapaed" the vision habits of its church clients trained in the sacred art of the Middle Ages. For the Christian art criticism of late historicalism, however, their style breaks were "life signs" which announced the step of ecclesiastical art into the controversial modernism. For the first time here, the eyes of the client are already viewed with the interaction of sacred architecture and religious painting of historism.
content.title_en: The crisis of historicism in the German sacred decoration in the late 19th century

content.text: Michelangelo - the architectural drawings : design process and planning practice. Although Michelangelo began his career as an architect only at the age of 40, his name is linked to such famous buildings as the Medici Chapel and the Biblioteca Laurenziana in Florence or the Capitol, the Sforza Chapel, the Porta Pia and the Basilica of St. Peter in Rome. This book systematically examines for the first time a larger group of Michelangelo's architectural drawings. It is not Michelangelo's finished works, but his design and working methods that are at the centre of this work. It may seem surprising that the painter and sculptor had to learn the building business laboriously. The progress that the finished buildings show only in the result can be closely followed in the drawings. The combination of previously poorly observed indications and the comparison with the methods of the contemporaries results in a new, surprising overall picture of the architect Michelangelo. The comparison with the contemporaries also shows that he has been an "artist between the epochs" who tried to implement his highly innovative designs with regard to the architectural design and the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the concept of the architectural and the concept of the concept of the concept of architecture.
content.title_en: Michelangelo - the architectural drawings : design process and planning practice

content.text: Legal protection in the remuneration regulation of the telecommunications law: the third-party protection problem on the part of competitors of the dominant company. Legal protection in the TK compensation regulation is a controversial topic. This is not least due to the fact that this is of enormous economic importance for the competitors of Deutsche Telekom AG, since the tariff structure is an essential factor for the success of a company. At the same time, legal protection in the TK compensation regulation also raises legal problems. It is mainly the question whether and to what extent the remuneration regulation regulations of the current TKG have a third-party protective effect in favour of competitors. In particular, it is shown which changes arise for the existing third-party protection problem as a result of the upcoming amendment of the TKG.

Angiogenesis, the formation of new blood vessels by proliferating from an existing vessel network, is an important phenomenon which is based on various physiological and pathological conditions. The yolksack vessel system of fertilized and incubated chicken eggs is used as a { em in vivo} investigation model and the angiogenic growth by the automatic calculation of the length and diameter of the vessels and the mean distance between vessel branches is investigated. For this reason an interactive approach should be developed, which contains vessel detection and analysis methods. Various smoothing operators and segmentation methods were developed and tested at a selected sample to find the most suitable for this type of images. Analysis data such as the total vessel length, the mean vessel diameter and the mean distance between each two vessel branches are then calculated from the binarized images. To determine the local contrast parameters, the user interface was evaluated to eliminate the container divisional classification of the container.

content.text: Environmental management and environmental product policy: participation of corporate and social actors in ecological processes in companies and industries. "Environmental management and ecological product policy are the two key points of attack when it comes to improving the environmental performance of a company. The present work describes and systematically examines the way in which the instruments used so far have worked in both dimensions of environmental corporate policy, especially in terms of the participation of corporate and social actors in their design and implementation. Herbert Klemisch's innovative aspect of the work is now the approach to develop the field of tension between company and product-related environmental protection at the level of sectors (textile/clothing and wood/furniture) and to present solutions that combine participation and effectiveness. In both sectors, however, a dialogue between state, social and operational actors in the form of "round tables" has been established. The result is ecological stakeholder networks that have taken the first steps towards corresponding industry agreements. Above all, however, and this is the merit of the present treatment, are empirically well-founded, the concrete implementation conditions under which integrated environmental policy can be followed by a product-hard, the demanding product-based concept.

content.text: City - Building - History : Urban development and residential construction in Erfurt from the 12th to the 19th century. Using numerous examples as well as maps and plans, the structural development of the city, the parcels, the plot construction and the internal structure of the residential buildings are analyzed and systematized through the centuries.
content.title_en: City - Building - History : Urban development and residential construction in Erfurt from the 12th to the 19th century

content.text: Monadischer Raum : Continuum, Individual and Infinity in Leibniz's Theory of Space. Leibniz has developed the first comprehensive theory of relational space and developed it in various sciences. Metaphysics requires individual substances, physics a system of functional forces and mathematics a pure absolute space for the construction of spatial object by means of the conditions of location. For a consistent understanding of Leibniz's space theory, the distinction between two ontological dimensions, which is required by the continuum problem, must also be taken into account. The author analyses the dimension of phenomenal spatiality and that of individual monads separately, addresses their reciprocal relationship of reasoning and finally discloses the limits of theory.
content.title_en: Monadic space : continuum, individual and infinity in Leibniz's theory of space

content.text: Downsizing of engines: an effective concept for reducing fuel consumption. Reciprocating piston combustion engines continue to represent the most economical and reliable sources of propulsion for many applications. The main requirements are low fuel consumption and low pollutant emissions. An effective concept for both petrol and diesel engines for the implementation of the above mentioned objectives is the so-called downsizing. Here, high power and torque are generated from comparatively small lifting rooms. Downsizing requires particularly efficient fuel injection and charging systems and represents high demands on engine mechanics. Based on a description of the subprocesses of motor energy conversion and the causes of loss, the basic idea of downsizing as well as the mechanisms of action and essential concept building blocks are explained in detail. Another focus is the description of additional and novel technologies for increasing efficiency and defusing the special problems of highly charged combustion engines. Furthermore, overall concepts for petrol and diesel engines are explained in detail taking into account the vehicle classes and the applications. Another focus is the description of additional and novel technologies for increasing efficiency and defusing the special problems of high-charged combustion engines.
content.title_en: Downsizing of internal combustion engines: an effective approach to reducing fuel consumption

content.text: Content management in public administration. All online. This is the goal of large-scale e-government initiatives. The European Commission has set itself the goal of eEurope, as well as the Federal Government, with the aim of increasing the service quality of its administrations by making public services online-capable. Our state and local governments have also started with initiatives, but are lagging behind developments. It is evident that there is still a huge need for the online delivery of the service portfolio of public administration overall in terms of internal and external resources in Internet technologies, both for strategy and design/architecture as well as for development, introduction, operation and evaluation. There are strategic approaches needed to show how organisation and technology in the administrations have to interlock each other, so that online services can be quickly, cost-effectively and customer-oriented. For this purpose, the book develops a holistic, strategy-based approach. This consists of a content management architecture and a framework for the strategy-based content management in the public administration. The content management model is described in terms of the implementation model.

content.text: Scientific Realism : a study of the realism-antirealism debate in the newer theory of science. The debate about scientific realism has been a prominent part of the philosophy of science for several decades. The focus of the study is on whether the successful theories of modern natural science provide a at least approximate true description of a physical reality independent of us. In the present study, an attempt is made to develop a strategy to defend scientific realism, which can defy some of the common objections. The decisive role is to develop a realistic concept of observation for the natural sciences. Empirist and constructiveist counterpositions to scientific realism are critically examined.
content.title_en: Scientific Realism : a study of the realism-antirealism debate in the newer theory of science

content.text: From parental leave to parental leave: political learning in the reform process. Klappentext: Family and equalization policy reforms can be a response to needs that parents and especially women articulate. This basic assumption deals with this study to show that policy solutions are not only negotiated in the field of conflict between interests, but are also the subject of learning processes. It becomes clear that effective regulations are not necessarily taken into account and that political reforms can have a very long lead in time. On the other hand, political actors change their positions in the reform process quite, new regulations can also be enforced against political resistance. Thus, the analysis of the reform of parental leave by the red-green government simultaneously spans a policy-analytical arc and tries to answer a fundamental policy-theoretical question: Which room for manoeuvre do politicians have in the bequeathed political business?
content.title_en: From parental leave to parental leave: political learning in the reform process

content.text: Taboo of Unity? : the East-West Community of Protestant Christians and the German Division (1945 - 1969). The study deals with the interpretation and practice of ecclesiastical and national unity in the whole of Germany against the background of changing national and international conditions. The focus is on the phase of mental and political upheavals from the mid-1950s to the late 1960s. The author examines which old guiding principles continued to work and which new interpretation and meaning-building patterns were developed in the context of the German division in the field of nation retention and "nationalization". She investigates the possibilities and limits of practiced all-German church unity and analyses the East-West community of Protestant Christians as the subject and object of German politics.
content.title_en: Taboo of unity? : the East-West community of Protestant Christians and the German division (1945 - 1969)

content.text: The social security system in the restructuring of the health care system: development needs and options for health policy. The role of the statutory health insurance system in the health care system has changed considerably over the past two decades: in the 1980s it was still an executive body of social law, but today it is active in competitive performance and care management in the US and Switzerland. It is true that citizens today are confronted with a variety of tariffs and services in the choice of their health insurance system. This scenario is the result of a health policy that has been written into the reform programme as a design goal of the competitive self-regulation of the GKV system. The present book reconstructs the goals and fields of intervention of health policy in the context of a phase change: the cost-reduction policy of the 1970s and 1980s still refers exclusively to the financing system of the health sector. Today's policy also aims to open up economic reserves and the regulation structure of the association's power to reshape the internal structure of the regulation. content.text: The German military's foreign operations after 1990 became political options for action. How can the change of German security policy be explained in this central point? The present book investigates these questions. The author's thesis is that the central explanation can be found in a gradual change of "security-political culture". Political culture is understood here as an intersubjectively produced, reproduced and changed phenomenon primarily in discourses. The author can show in his discourse analysis from 1990 to 2002 that the "antimilitaristic consensus" existing until 1990 was replaced by a new security-political consensus. Two central interpretations of the legitimacy of foreign operations of the German armed forces were formed: (1) Alliance solidarity/multilateralism and the resulting action call "Never again special routes!" (2) a changed understanding of the German past/base count, which means a change of the action call of "Nie again war!" to "Nie again Auschwitz!" can be attributed to the "revolutionary" of the "revolutionary" of the cultural policy.

content.text: The numerical evaluation of American options requires the solution of a linear complementarity problem, the component of which is the black-scholes (in) equation. Finite differential discretization of this partial differential equation (PDE) can generate numerical dispersion. The resulting oscillations make it impossible to hedge the option. By means of appropriate transformations it is possible to avoid numerical dispersion. This work analyses the dispersion properties of known and new transformations of the black-scholes PDE. For dispersion-free transformations the problem is transferred to a time-dependent sequence of linear programs. Due to the premature exercise possibility, for each of these time steps a smoothing of the numerical solution is necessary by means of L-stable discretization methods. To keep the numerical effort low, various procedures are presented which reduce the number of necessary time steps. The Knack point is thus the qualitatively occurring timeline of the method.
content.title_en: Transformations to avoid numerical dispersion and methods for controlling the time step width for numerical option evaluation

content.text: The present work deals with the use of eye electron spectroscopy in the investigation of SiC layers and single crystals with particular attention to the effect of the ion beam on the SiC surface during sputtering. The eye electron spectroscopy is suitable for the determination of many properties of a SiC surface after firing with noble gas ions. The theoretical part includes a contribution to the application of the factor analysis in the analysis of eye spectra. Another topic of the theoretical part is sputter theory. Here a correction of Sigmund's formula for the calculation of sputter exploits is presented. In the experimental part of the work, statements about the deviations of surface composition after sputtering and the concentration of the installed noble gases are made. From the comparison between the experimentally measured and theoretically calculated and simulated values of the sputter exploits are made about the Siper-Effective surface bonding energy of 4 eV/Atom for the sputtering of the sputtering of the silicon.
content.title_en: Auger electron spectroscopy and low-energy ion firing of silicon carbide

content.text: The design concepts of the resonator internal mode forming allow the transversal mode properties of stable and unstable lasers to be improved and adapted to specific applications. However, the complexity of the resonator and its adjustment effort increases with increasing number of degrees of freedom. The present work deals with the investigation of experimental methods and possibilities for avoiding adjustment problems and for simplifying the construction concept for the resonator internal mode forming both in the free space and in the wave conductor laser. In the free space resonator this is made possible by the transition to the folded resonator geometry. The possibilities of the principle are demonstrated experimentally in an Nd:YAG laser. In the wave conductor area, the direct monolithic integration of phase elements in the wide strip laser is theoretically investigated and experimentally demonstrated by means of a colour-dominated polymer strip laser.
content.title_en: Investigation of experimental methods for in-conductor mode forming

content.text: Architecture and harmony: number, measure and proportion in Western architecture. The pursuit of harmony is a basic need of man. How does the principle of harmony manifest in architecture? How are the dimensions of the human body decisive for harmonious architectural design? This book explains from the basic idea of harmony various aspects of architecture, in order to allow its conception, historical meaning and present effect to be a living experience in front of the reader. The striving for harmonious design, which can be read in the history of architecture, ranges as an idea from "measured" building to the current discussion on the tasks and objectives of architecture.
content.title_en: Architecture and harmony : number, measure and proportion in Western architecture

content.text: The aim of this paper is to investigate the influence of microwave radiation on solid catalysts in the microwave assisted heterogeneous partial oxidation in the gas phase as well as the turnover and selectivity behaviour. Furthermore, microwave active catalysts were developed and tried to clarify the causes of the microwave activity of the catalysts.
content.title_en: Contribution to microwave assisted heterogeneous gas phase catalytics

content.text: Divine services on the Internet: perspectives of a dialogue between the Internet and the liturgy. The Internet is increasingly a place where certain forms of divine services are possible. In this context, it is not the classical transmissions of divine services on television or on radio. It is rather the services that are designed by means of the interactive possibilities of the network. Internet theory and theology enter into a correlational dialogue with each other, whereby the disciplines involved in the conversation approach the common object from their own point of view: the Internet communities. Interdisciplinary work is carried out throughout, not only at the levels of liturgy and technology, but also in view of the merging of various theological disciplines: biblical, historical, systematic, liturgical. Thus, divine services on the Internet are not a pastoral concession to changing media contexts, but are systematically and theologically derived from the core of the liturgy as a set of experienced sign actions of God to man.
content.title_en: Divine services on the Internet : Perspectives of a dialogue between the Internet and the liturgy

content.text: Asymptotic properties of solutions to wave equations with time-dependent dissipation. The dissertation will examine the asymptotic properties of solutions to the Cauchy problem for a wave equation with time-dependent attenuation $b=b(t)$ and the interplay between the behavior of the coefficient $b(t)ge0$ and resulting estimates of energy based on $L^q$, $qge2$. It turns out that between two scenarios, that of the non-effective and that of the effective attenuation, the main topics of the solution representation are constructed and, from this, for the first time, $L^p$--$L^q$ estimate for the solution and its derivatives is given. Likewise, the sharpness of the estimates is discussed and concreted in the form of a modified scattering theory or diffusion phenomenon.
content.title_en: Asymptotic properties of solutions to wave equations with time-dependent dissipation

content.text: Novel two-stage redox systems based on 4H imidazoles. In this work, the redox behavior of 4H imidazoles with oxalamidine substructure was investigated using electrochemical methods such as cyclovoltammetry and square wave techniques. Using two synthesized series of compounds, it was shown that the redox potential can be estimated with the help of the Hammett constants. Access to a new compound class - derived from the 4H imidazoles - the 1,3.2-diazaborolidins was created. They are structurally very interesting and show an extraordinary combination of properties, such as intense color, red fluorescence and redox activity with semichinone formation constants around 1014.
content.title_en: Novel two-stage redox systems based on 4H imidazoles

content.text: The nonlinear optical coefficients of third order of conjugated polymers and glass based on tellurium oxide were investigated. The nonlinear optical coefficients of third order of solutions and thin films of conjugated polymers and of tellurite glass were investigated by Z-scan and degenerate four-wave mixture. In all cases an instantaneous nonlinearity was observed. The measured amounts of the nonlinear refractive index of polymer films decrease with increasing film thickness, caused by two-photon absorption and better ordered polymer chains in thinner films. The nonlinear susceptibility of the third order of the new tellurite mixing glasses examined was up to fifty times that of quartz glass. content.title_en: Study of the nonlinear optical coefficients of third order conjugated polymers and glass based on tellurium oxide

content.text: The task of integrating heterogeneous spatial objects from fragmented spatial data sets, which can be found in numerous variants in practice, is analysed and solved in this work. Based on an analysis of the use cases of geometric integration, various process models for solving the integration problem are shown. The three main steps of geometric integration are the assignment problem of homologous spatial objects, the search for implicit geometrical relations and the determination and implementation of a transformation that transforms all source data sets into a homogeneous target data set. A simple model of a map is defined in which geometric integration is a transformation problem between the idealized true map, which is only partially given in practice, and multiple realizations of maps that are distorted by random and unknown systematic errors. In the statistical model, the connection between the true map and its realizations as vectorial spatial random process is understood and with the methods of geostatistics and classical estimation methods are examined with the basic modeling set of the basic modeling set of the statistical data sets is considered as a relative basis for the statistical data set of the population.
content.title_en: Integration of heterogeneous spatial objects from fragmented spatial data sets

content.text: A hydrodynamic 3D multi-component model of the heliosphere and its interaction with cosmic radiation. This work presents a new modelling experiment of the heliosphere and its interaction with cosmic radiation. It uses a three-dimensional hydrodynamic model, which no longer requires symmetry assumptions regarding the geometry of the problem. In the first part of the work the effects of activity cycles of the sun (11-year cycle, mound minimum, small scale disturbances) as well as changes in the density and direction of the local interstellar medium (LISM) on the heliosphere structure are investigated. Based on this three-dimensional model, the effects and transport of cosmic radiation in the heliosphere are then studied in the second part. For the first time realistic anisotropic diffusion stesors are used, which are self-consistently considered in the model.
content.title_en: A hydrodynamic 3D multi-component model of the heliosphere and its interaction with cosmic radiation

content.text: The three-dimensional structure of alliinase from garlic in various crystal forms. The garlic (Allium sativum) owes its pharmacological and culinary significance to the action of a single enzyme - the alliinase. This C-S-lyase splits the odourless cysteine derivative alliine in pyruvate, ammonium and sulphonic acid, whereby two sulfenic molecules non-enzymatically condensate to the likewise odorless allicin, from which the odorless garlic active substances spontaneously arise. The enzyme isolated from fresh tubers, vitamin B6-dependent, has been crystallized in four different crystal forms and the three-dimensional structure at high resolution (1,53 Å). The folding is very similar in two of the three domains to the family of pyridoxal phosphate-dependent enzymes of class I; the third (N-terminal) domain contains an EGF domain with novel disulfide connection. A chloride binding point in the N-terminal area leads to the formation of a substrate-species-function of the substrate-link.
content.title_en: The three-dimensional structure of alliinase from garlic in different crystal shapes

content.text: The control methods for the realization of decentralised three-phase current networks for 3 conductor systems using parallel voltage inverters. Decentralized power supply systems can be realized on the basis of the parallel switching of several equal voltage inverters. The expandability and flexibility of the supply system required for the increase of power demand requires besides modern power electronics good control and control methods for controlling the parallel switching. For a hardware-minimal and cost-effective construction of the system, the potential separation, both AC and DC side, the inverter and additional communication equipment is dispensed with in the present work. The regulation of the voltage and frequency depending on the active and blind current (characteristic method) ensures a uniform load distribution between the participating inverters. In the present work, on the basis of the transformation of the system sizes simplified replacement diagrams, which describe the overall system, are developed for the room vector and for the zero component. For a stable and safe operation of the parallel switching, the control systems are largely performed by means of the control systems using the variable frequency and the corresponding control systems.
content.title_en: Control procedure for the implementation of decentralised three-phase current networks for 3 conductor systems using parallel voltage inverters

content.text: On the media public sphere of third-party violence: legal aspects of media access to the jurisdiction in the constitutional state of the Basic Law. Christian von Coelln deals with the legal, in particular constitutional questions of media access to justice. In addition to general considerations on the importance of media publicity of third-party violence for democracy and the rule of law, he also deals with the participation of journalists in oral negotiations and the problem of image and sound recordings in court buildings.
content.title_en: The media public of third-party violence: legal aspects of media access to justice in the constitutional state of the Basic Law

content.text: Plant polyketide synthases of type III in Wachendorfia thyrsiflora (Haemodoraceae). Wachendorfia thyrsiflora (Haemodoraceae) contains a group of secondary natural substances, so-called phenylphenalenone, which are believed to be involved in the defence of pathogens. Type III polyketide synthases should be involved in the first steps of biosynthesis of these substances, the formation of linear diarylheptanoides. The work presented is concerned with the isolation of polyketide synthases from root cultures of Wachendorfia thyrsiflora and their characterization. Three enzymes were analyzed and examined with a view to their involvement in biosynthesis. One of the three enzymes is probably involved in biosynthesis, but is not able to form diaryheptanoides alone. The work contains besides the characterization of these proteins by enzyme assays, also indications of the nature of another enzyme needed.
content.title_en: Plant-type polyketid synthases III in Wachendorfia thyrsiflora (Haemodoraceae)

content.text: Interactive sustainability reporting of companies: Concept and analysis of the internet use of GF-500 companies with regard to sustainability reporting. Through internet-based sustainability communication, companies can reach a larger number of stakeholders and better recognise and satisfy their individual needs. However, this requires a systematic approach that focuses on the communication-theoretical and application-oriented framework conditions of an interactive sustainability reporting. The author shows with which criteria of an interactive sustainability reporting company can increase the credibility of its sustainability reports and thus their corporate reputation. The empirical study of how GF-500 companies use the possibilities of the Internet for their sustainability reporting allows conclusions for corporate practice.
content.title_en: Interactive sustainability reporting of companies : Concept and analysis of the internet use of GF-500 companies with regard to sustainability reporting

content.text: RaumLanguage : East-West differences in reporting on German unity; a social geography theory. Traditional concepts of space and borders are neither overcome nor relinquishable – even if the current human geography theory often says them dead. For in everyday practice they are common and functional. However, in order to achieve a deeper understanding of this practical meaning of spatial concepts, a systematic analysis of the everyday 'geographical making', the linguistic use of spatial concepts and their social integration is required. Based on the reporting on German unity, this book develops successive theoretical developments in the relationship between space, language and society. As a result, the everyday differentiation of West and East is not merely a 'German phenomenon'. It refers to the general problem that even when designing integrative concepts and cross-border programs, it cannot be dispensed with the concept of a deintegrative and limiting space.
content.title_en: RaumLanguage : East-West differences in reporting on German unity ; a social geography theory

content.text: Authentication in ad-hoc and sensor networks. In the near future, ad-hoc and sensor networks will become more and more part of our daily lives. However, they could become a danger if security aspects are not taken into account from the outset. Authentication is a core aspect for secure protocols and secure applications. Therefore, authentication in ad-hoc networks is treated as an overarching topic of this work. The security problems of ad-hoc and sensor networks differ significantly from those of conventional networks. Therefore, appropriate protocols must be designed. This work first provides an overview of different authentication methods and analyses their suitability for ad-hoc networks. This follows an analysis of the suitability of digital signatures. In addition, two new extremely efficient protocols for mutual authentication in such networks are presented, and ultimately an application of authentication, the component identification, is described.
content.title_en: Authentication in ad-hoc and sensor networks

content.text: Production of textured lithium disilicate glass ceramics by means of electrolytically induced germination. In this work, textured lithium disilicate glass ceramics were successfully produced by means of electrolytically induced germination. The formation of glass ceramics was systematically clarified and their properties characterized. Structural investigations such as XRD-texturgoniometrics and SEM were the focus of the study, which contributed to the understanding of the growth mechanisms and the formation of the textures of glass ceramics. The Lihtium disilicate fabric system was endowed with suitable additives to visualize structural units and crystals in the SEM. The test parameters were used to clarify the causes of electrolytically induced germination and crystallization and to determine crystal growth speeds. Furthermore, a method for optimising the texture of glass ceramics was developed and the anisotropic mechanical properties were demonstrated by means of micro-curity measurements.
content.title_en: Manufacture of textured lithium disilicate glass ceramics by electrolytically induced germination
