content.text: Scientific policy advice in the 1960s: the study group for system research, 1958 to 1975. Technology assessment has been established and institutionalized in the Federal Republic of Germany for years. It is understood as both a system analytically oriented scientific method and a science-based policy advice. An important basis for institutionalization as well as for the content orientation of the technology assessment in Germany was laid by the Heidelberg "Study Group for System Research" (SfS), which existed between 1958 and 1975 as an independent institution and which is a direct precursor of the Institute for Technology Assessment and System Analysis (ITAS) of the Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe. The aim of the study is to present the time of existence and operation of the study group, but not as a "pure", "close", internal institutional history, but as an investigation of the interactions between the study group and the relationship between science, research, politics and society, which in those years is changing in the Federal Republic of Germany.
content.title_en: Scientific policy advice in the 1960s: the study group on systems research, 1958 to 1975

content.text: In the case of bionically inspired monolithic joint elements with fluid mechanical drive. In many areas of technology, a specific yield of technical systems is an urgent requirement. Soft robotics is the state of current research. The yield of technical systems is ensured either by control or by structural and material properties. The advantage of the latter is the production and/or control simplicity of the system. Bionic approaches are becoming increasingly important for solving complex technical and technological problems also in applied mechanics. The biomechanics of limbs with monolithic extremities offers suggestions from several aspects for the design of technical yield structures. In the present work monolithic, elastomeric, fluid mechanically driven joint elements with a plane range are to be considered. The theoretical and experimental investigations are carried out to derive characteristic characteristics of such structures and, using bionic approaches, to accept the solution of pressure variants with the comparison of known solutions, to develop qualitatively new properties. The work is divided into four parts. In the first part, the analysis of the variable structures is considered in the case of the quantitatively improved structures.
content.title_en: Bionically inspired monolithic joint elements with fluid mechanical drive

content.text: In this work, novel bridge ligands with N-donor set and chelate binding spheres were synthesized and structurally enlightened. These ligands were implemented with various metal complex fragments, with the synthesis of well-defined, mononuclear Ruthenium(II)-bipyridyl complexes being the focus of the investigations. The resulting complex compounds were presented in a pure form and completely structurally enlightened. Extensive investigations of the photochemical and photophysical properties of these Ruthenium complexes led to the discovery of a particularly active compound in terms of their behaviour towards protons and metal ions. This complex is concerned with Ru(bpy*)2(5-(1H-imidazole-2yl)-2,2'-bipyridyl), which by slight changes in the chemical environment in solution has been subjected to significant changes in absorption behaviour and especially in emission behaviour. In this sense, this compound is discussed as a 'pH-dependent double switch' and as a 'metal detector'.
content.title_en: Metal complexes with novel bridge ligands

content.text: Development of a model for the assessment of detection ranges of infrared camera systems. Driver assistance systems are becoming increasingly important in the automotive industry for the comfort of the driver and the improvement of road safety. The most important size for the driver is the visual condition. Especially in limited visibility conditions due to darkness and/or fog, the risk of accidents increases disproportionately. Night vision systems provide the driver with additional information by using the medium and distant infrared spectral range. While at night and clear atmosphere information can be obtained from the driving environment beyond the illumination range of car spotlights by an infrared camera camera system, the range of infrared camera systems in dense fog is not yet known. - This work describes a model for determining the ranges of infrared camera systems, which is based on the model of standard vision range. An essential component of this model consists in a visual target suitable for infrared applications. Using this model, the camera ranges of camera systems of the medium and far infrared with dense fog were compared with the range of standard vision of less than 500 m.
content.title_en: Development of a model for the assessment of detection ranges of infrared camera systems

content.text: Non-aqueous capillary electrophoresis for the analysis of peptides. In this work various peptides were analyzed using non-aqueous capillary electrophoresis (NACE). Both basic, separate methodological questions were worked out and practical applications for the NACE analysis of peptides were developed. In the first part of this work the influence of non-aqueous solvents on the dissociation behaviour and the secondary structure of peptides were investigated, which determine the migration behaviour of peptides in the CE. In the second part of the work two application examples for the use of NACE for the analysis of peptides were developed, whereby the coupling with mass spectrometric and electrochemical detection was the main focus.
content.title_en: Non-aqueous capillary electrophoresis for the analysis of peptides

content.text: IT support for knowledge management in cooperations. Companies do not generally create complex goods and services alone, but work together with other companies. They often coordinate through non-market coordination forms such as internal and inter-company cooperations. At the same time, the importance of knowledge in the company and at the intersections of corporate cooperations increases. However, the established methods and tools for managing knowledge were mostly developed with the focus on integrated large companies. To address this deficit, the specific requirements for cross-company knowledge management tools are first identified and the existing tools are examined for their suitability for use in different forms of cooperation. On this basis, innovative changes and extensions of knowledge management tools are developed, which enable cross-company use.
content.title_en: IT support for knowledge management in cooperation

content.text: Continuous surface profiles for optical beam shaping. The aim of this work was to contribute to the question of which signal distributions can be realized with the help of refractive beam forming elements. It could be shown that beam forming is almost possible in the case of flat-top signal distributions with a limited diffraction, whereby a clear dependence between the lateral expansion of the signal distribution and the signal quality achievable at a given resolution was found. In the case of gray value signal distributions it was elaborated that the achievable resolution is the least in case of a local minimum in signal distribution, compared with other distributions. Regardless of the width, the achieved detail resolution is not sufficient for the generation of several plane with an intermediate minimum. For this reason, two-dimensional flat-top distributions with a convex edge with a slightly higher resolution can be realized than such with a concave edge. By lowering the contrast, a higher detail resolution is achievable at any output distribution.

content.text: Studies of permeation of encapsulated hydrophilic nutritive additives by differently structured food matrices. When bioactive substances are incorporated into food matrices containing water, their high level of preservation and bioavailability should be ensured. It is therefore desirable to design such matrices in such a way that, on the one hand, a high amount of material loss is avoided and, on the other hand, the enrichment with bioactive substances is facilitated, which have unpleasant taste or odour nuances (e.g. vitamins, plant extracts, trace elements, peptides). To this end, it is necessary to incorporate barrier systems with certain properties in food matrices. The aim of the work was to create basics for barriers in multidisperse food matrices, which were formed from dispersed aqueous phases in microfat particles of a multiple emulsion system of type W1/O/W2, whereby such microfat particles could also be embedded in a polysaccharide matrix.
content.title_en: Studies on permeation of encapsulated hydrophilic nutritive additives by different food matrices

content.text: The aim of this paper is to compare the problems of efficient regulation of liberalised service markets with network structures, in the light of the telecommunications and electricity markets, and to identify the institutional problems of efficient regulation of the telecommunications and electricity markets with network structures, in a comparative study of the telecommunications and electricity markets. The two market segments considered in this paper were opened up to competition in Germany within a few months. In terms of regulation of the sectors, completely different concepts with significantly different intervention intensity were pursued by the state. Initially, this paper presents the regulatory structures for telecommunications and electricity sectors separately, and then examines market developments in the two sectors for the first few years after liberalisation. On the basis of this comparative analysis, deficits and successful approaches of regulatory structures are formulated and conclusions drawn from future improvements in concepts are assessed from an efficiency point of view. In another part, the review presents the legal changes made in the original regulatory arrangements in the years following the opening of markets and their suitability for eliminating the deficit.
content.title_en: Regulation and competition in the telecommunications and electricity markets : a comparative analysis of regulatory structures and market developments in the German telecommunications and electricity sector

content.text: Exposure in migratory birds: orientation mechanism and their under-districting neurobiological background. The aim of the thesis is to analyse the neurobiological and physiological mechanisms underlying the magnetic compass orientation of nightmarish birds. Behavioral observations show that nightmarish mosquitoes (Sylvia borin) perform stereotype head movements (head scans) to perceive the reference direction of the Earth's magnetic field. An evaluation of neuronal activity in the brain by visualizing immediate-early genes leads to the identification of a teleencephalic region, called cluster N, which is specifically active in nightmarishers during the night, but not in standbirds neither during the day nor at night. Further data shows that cluster N may be information from the eye and thus an integration area for magnetic compass information based on a light-dependent system.
content.title_en: Orientation in migratory birds : orientation mechanisms and their underlying neurobiological background

content.text: Investigations of the interaction of the phosphoinositide-3 kinase γ with lipid membranes. PI-3 kinase γ is involved in a variety of cellular processes such as neutrophil migration, T cell proliferation, mast cell degranulation and cardiac myocytes contraction. In addition to lipid kinase activity, protein kinase activity and direct protein interactions of PI-3 kinase γ contribute to the control of these cell functions. Only for the lipid kinase function of the enzyme there is the need to bind to the cell membrane, the location of substrate localization. The membrane binding mechanism of PI-3 kinase γ, especially in the absence of the adaptor protein p101, is still unexplained. In principle, enzymes can bind protein and lipid interactions to cellular membranes. The aim of this work was to investigate a possible membrane binding of PI-3 kinase γ via lipid association.
content.title_en: Studies of the interaction of phosphoinositide-3 kinase γ with lipid membranes

content.text: Automation of service-oriented computing through semantic service descriptions. Service-oriented architectures will then develop their full potential if services are automatically integrated at runtime. The aim of this dissertation was to create a suitable semantic service description language. Their approach is to break the basis of the language into two parts: a lightweight part for the acquisition of domain knowledge and additional elements for the recording of the characteristics of services. This results in descriptions that place the achievable states of services in the center and can thus be efficiently compared.
content.title_en: Automation of service-oriented computing through semantic service descriptions

content.text: Quantitative analysis and evaluation of soil profiles by means of multivariate statistical methods and hate diagram technique. The subject of this work was the study and evaluation of soil profiles in the environment of point-shaped issuers. For decades, dusts with a highly alkaline effect were recorded in the soils of a phosphate fertilizer plant, while the soils of an ironworks were exposed to heavy metal dusts. Three soil profiles were sampled at each site both horizontally and equidistantly. In addition to pseudo-total contents of selected elements and soil properties, the binding conditions were examined by means of sequential extraction. The evaluation of the resulting data matrix for each site by means of multivariate statistical methods (cluster analysis, LDA, PCA, three-way PCA) and the hate diagram technique covered the relationships and differences both laterally between the profiles and vertically within the profiles. It could be shown that even without expert knowledge when sampling the characterisation of a soil and the description of the contamination diagram technique was not possible.
content.title_en: Quantitative analysis and evaluation of soil profile exposure using multivariate statistical methods and Hasse diagram technique

content.text: Competition federalism : reform of the German state according to the Australian model. Using the example of the federal state Australia, it is shown how a reform of the German state can lead to declining unemployment and increasing economic growth. The focus is on the financial constitution, the state financial compensation, the importance of the Federal Council, the legislative procedure and the powers for administration. A proposal is made to reform the relevant parts of the Basic Law. (Source: Verlag / Umbeschreibtext).
content.title_en: Competition Federalism : to reform the German state according to Australian model

content.text: The rationalization of the human being : Architecture and culture of the German employment offices 1890 - 1945. Employment mediation and encounter with unemployment are not only topics of today. The author shows in her study the origin and development of the construction type employment office. Where and why did the first of these institutions come into being? How did the concepts of social, social, cultural and aesthetic conditions of the time behave? - - With the new administrative type employment office - first realized in 1902 in Berlin - a new type of building, for which there were no models until then, was united. Christiane Mattiesson's art historical investigation of the numerous labor offices created is based on nationwide researched architectural plans, interior and exterior photographs, contemporary technical texts and press reports as well as entrances to existing buildings. The employment office architecture thus went beyond a purely architectural approach to the historical buildings, but above all as a specific framework for the spatial organization of people - men, women and young people, unskilled workers and civil servants of the institutions.
content.title_en: Rationalization of the human race : Architecture and culture of the German employment offices 1890 - 1945

content.text: Living in the GDR : Dresden-Prohlis: Housing policy and housing 1975 to 1981. Historically, housing in a typical GDR new building area is of interest from an everyday perspective. Even after the announcement of the housing programme in 1973, housing supply remained poor and the new housing, which, as in Prohlis and Gorbitz, were stamped out of the green meadow to thousands of people, were still highly sought after until the end of the 1980s. Today, given the massive empty housing situation in these new areas, living in the same area gained more symbolic character for the lives of the people in the GDR. On the other hand, the study provides further insights into the relationship between political rule and society in real socialism. The housing programme and housing policy on the basis of the unity of economic and social policy and against the background of the fulfilment of the main task formed essential components of the social policy concept. In this regard, it is now considered uncontested that society was politically constituted and regulated in almost all areas. On the other hand, opinions differ whether the above objectives were achieved and could be achieved without further delay by means of the above.
content.title_en: Housing in the GDR : Dresden-Prohlis: Housing policy and housing 1975 to 1981

content.text: Discrete optics in inhomogeneous waveguide arrays. The present work deals with the propagation of optical waves in inhomogeneous waveguide arrays. In the first part of the work, defect modes of defect waveguides and interfaces in waveguide arrays are theoretically and experimentally investigated. Furthermore, the reflection and transmission coefficients for bloke waves are calculated at such inhomogeneities. In the second part of the work it is shown that zener tunnels, an effect known from solid-body physics, can also be observed in waveguide arrays under the influence of a transversal calculus index gradient. The results presented represent the first direct detection of zener tunnels. In the third part of the work, bloche oscillations and zener tunnels are investigated in two-dimensional waveguide arrays.
content.title_en: Discrete optics in inhomogenous waveguide arrays

content.text: BETI site separation methods with fast edge element methods and applications. In numerical simulation, the treatment of coupled problems becomes increasingly important in view of fast product development. Area separation methods offer simple treatment and efficient numerical simulation for materials with different material parameters and for coupling different model equations. They also allow the coupling of different numerical methods and a simple parallelization of the simulation to reduce the computing times. In addition to the area separation method itself, the methods used to solve local partial problems are also important for a fast overall procedure. In the edge element method, the variation formulation of the partial differential equation is transformed by partial integration into a border integral equation. Advantages of the edge element method compared to the frequently used finite element method lie in the easier networking of the edge, in the treatment of external space problems and the explicit calculations of the complete chauchy data on the edge. A disadvantage of the standard edge element method is the at least square storage and computing effort. This can be reduced by the use of fast edge element methods, such as the complexity method ...

content.text: Rubber, quarantine, war : Dhauhandel in East Africa 1880 - 1914. In the mid-19th century hundreds of long-distance trading houses from Arabia and India reached the trading metropolis of Zanzibar, where trade with East African products took place. This pre-colonial trading system was endangered in its existence from 1890, as direct steamer connections to Europe were established, colonial trade restrictions and port closures took place and competition between European and Indian trading companies intensified. The present investigation of an African economy that existed alongside the colonial economy sheds a new light on the economic transformation processes in the early phase of European colonial rule and illustrates the peripherization of individual regions. At the same time, the reconstruction of the Dhauhandel provides decisive evidence that the Maji-Maji War took place in a region that had broken down coastal trade and had long since been pushed to the edge of the colonial economy.
content.title_en: Rubber, Quarantine, War : Dhauhandel in East Africa 1880 - 1914

content.text: The reduction of the obligation to pay damages in Europe: to the chances of including a general reduction clause in a European right of damage. Reduction clauses are meant to mean genuine breaks in the principle of total reparation, which reduce the compensation claim proportionately in the area of damage rights. Reduction clauses in German law, for example, are maximum damages or the rules on the division of damages in case of co-inflict. Instead of defining in the so-called special reduction clauses the conditions under which a reduction of the compensation claim is considered and, if necessary, to the extent to which the reduction is to be made, some legal systems in Europe have instead created or parallel a general reduction clause which puts it in the court's discretion whether and to what extent a reduction of the compensation claim should be made. This study aims to contribute to the necessary legal unification in Europe by examining the suitability of a general reduction clause for a European right of damage law and clarifying how the need for a reasonable limitation of the compensation obligation can best be taken into account in individual cases. This question is to be examined in the way of legal comparison, the German legal order, the German law, and the Dutch law.
content.title_en: The reduction of the obligation to pay damages in Europe: the opportunities for the inclusion of a general reduction clause in a European right to property

content.text: A new dynamic visualization system for the online and offline presentation of interactive 3D site models. This dissertation shows, using the newly developed 3DMapView software, ways to minimize deficits in the field of interactive real-time exploration of 3D site models. The work includes a practical part (software 3DMapView) and a scientific-theoretical text part. In the text section, presentation variants of three-dimensional digital site models as well as current visualization technologies are analyzed and evaluated, thereby also highlighting the motivation for the development of an individual software solution more differentiated. In addition, this work is intended to document the development steps of the 3DMapView software, introduce the user into the operation and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this solution approach, in order to finally assess the potential of individually developed software solutions in the interactive 3D visualization of terrain models.
content.title_en: A new dynamic visualization system for online and offline presentation of interactive 3D site models

content.text: Optimization of fast-acting electromagnetic drives. This dissertation is to be classified into the analysis and synthesis process for technical systems. In the context of a new concept for charge-change control, the electrohydraulic valve control (EHVS), electromagnetic valves with very short switching times are required. In this work, the control unit, the electro-magneto-mechanical energy converter, including the coupled mechanical components, is considered as a system which is to be optimized in terms of positioning accuracy of the gas-change valve. Due to the high dynamic requirements, the interactions of the components integrated in the system are crucial for the overall function. The development of a model that enables the simulation of the technical system is described. In order to be able to specifically consider interfaces, the implementation of the model takes place on a common simulation platform. The simulation model is used for the development and optimization of the technical system. To optimize, selected parameters that influence the dynamics are examined and quantified. Based on the simulation results, highly dynamic magnetic valves are developed and checked for their dynamics. Finally, a way is shown to optimize technical systems in the future.
content.title_en: Optimization of fast-acting electromagnetic drives

content.text: The conversion of random closed sets and applications in stability theory of stochastic optimization is examined in this dissertation. In this dissertation, the one-sided convergence in distribution for closed quantities and their application for stochastic optimization problems is examined. Starting from the convergence concepts of Kuratowski-Painleve, convergence is defined in distribution based on hit and miss topologies. Important tools such as the continuous mapping theorem and semi-stem generalizations are provided. A multitude of sufficient conditions for the convergence of epigraphs of sub-stantial functions are demonstrated. Here, it is shown how classes of stochastic processes can be compared to the quantity convergence approach. In addition to the sub-stantial modification of the scorohod-Raeum D, a new convergence criterion for the convergence of stochastic processes with sub-stantiated trajectories is demonstrated. In addition to the sub-stantiation of the distribution of the optimum values and the one-sided optimization of the variable quantities is also shown in the sample.
content.title_en: Convergence in distribution of random closed sets and applications in stability theory of stochastic optimization

content.text: In-city retail development through major projects: Impacts on traditional retail areas using the example of the shopping center "City Gallery" in Siegen. With the penetration of the high-performance property type Shopping Center into the inner city area, there is no doubt that positive impulses for its purchasing reputation are combined. However, developments - especially in traditional retail locations - can also occur, which are undesirable from a city development policy point of view. This includes primarily the loss of functionality of existing business areas.The dissertation examines such effects with the example of the city of Siegen, in which a large-scale shopping center was opened in autumn 1998. In addition to real estate economics topics, the impact of the center on the shopping behaviour of visitors and the reaction patterns of existing businesses in the Siegen city centre are examined in detail.
content.title_en: In-city retail development through major projects : Impact on traditional retail areas using the example of the shopping center "City Gallery" in Siegen

content.text: Towards efficient implementation of artificial neural networks in systems on chip. The lack of artificial neural networks effectively implemented on a chip calls for a new approach. The utilization of the physical effects that the semiconductor technologies used for realization offer us can be used for the space-saving implementation, for example. Neuronal networks as an integrated component of complex systems can only be embedded if the requirements for a compact realization are met. This includes above all a space-saving implementation of all components.This work deals with new approaches for the implementation of artificial neural networks in digital hardware. As these usually require much more chip area, but work for it with significantly higher bandwidth and data rates, there will always be a need for space-optimized realizations. In addition, a procedure for the implemetation of temporary dynamics of neural potentials with minimized resource utilization is presented with the aim of comparing the criteria and objectively evaluating the accuracy. As an example, a system for the localization of sound sources has been used. In addition, a method has been developed with which it is possible to compare the hardware realization of the neural networks with each other.
content.title_en: Towards efficient implementation of artificial neural networks in systems on chip

content.text: Smolyak's algorithm, save grid approximation and periodic function spaces with dominating mixed smoothness. The work is concerned with periodic function spaces with dominant mixed smoothness of the Besov, Triebel-Lizorkin and Sobolev types. Starting from the Fourier-analytical definition, various embeddings and equivalent characterizations are provided. In particular, characterization by differences plays an important role. However, the focus of the investigations is on the approximation of such functions by abstastoperators based on the Smolyak algorithm. We get sharp estimates for the error, measured in the Lp metric. From this we gain new upper limits for the problem of optimal reconstruction of such functions from a finite amount of functional values.

content.text: Theoretical and algorithmic methods for the calculation of vertices of irreducible modules of symmetrical groups. This work deals with the determination of vertices and sources of irreducible modules of finite symmetrical groups. Both theoretical and algorithmic methods for vertex calculation are developed and applied to different classes of irreducible modules of symmetrical groups. These include, for example, certain external potentiaries of the natural irreducible module in straight characteristics, the so-called completely decaying modules and the generalized Young modules. content.text: The Topoisomerase IIß-binding protein 1 : Investigations of regulation of the gene promoter and function of the protein. The Topoisomerase IIß-binding protein (TopBP1) is a human protein with eight BRCT (BRCA1 Carboxyterminus) motifs, which is associated with important cellular processes such as DNA damage response, DNA replication and apoptosis. The aim of this work was to identify regulatory elements in the TopBP1 promoter and to demonstrate a possible influence of expression by transcription factors. With these investigations, new indications of the function of TopBP1 in the regulation of the cell cycle were obtained. By computer analyses, two potential binding points of the transcription factor Egr-1 were identified in the promoter of TopBP1 and the binding to this in vitro and in vivo were detected. TopBP1 interactivated with a number of proteins involved in different functions in the cell. In this work, a knock-down experiment of help of RNA-Breduction was observed in the presence of a henoid DNA-induction.

content.text: Testimonies of the emergence of the Ruhr industrial cultural landscape: the Hanover-Hannibal-Königsgrube mine landscape in Bochum and Herne and its industrial cultural potential. The industrial heritage of the Ruhr region is a potential for the future of this old industrial space. Industrial culture is therefore one of the leading themes of the European Capital of Culture 2010. Industrial culture is more than the architectural heritage of the industrial age, it is the emergence of the industrial cultural landscape, the social and everyday history of the region and its mentalities. In its presentation, there is a lack of basic research, which is why the potentials of a sub-space were investigated: the Hanover-Hannibal-Königsgrube mine landscape in the border area of Bochum-Herner shows in the fourth decade after the closure of these three Kruppian mines a wealth of signifying evidence due to a low re-use pressure that was documented. Not the mines, but the emergence of the typical urban landscape and the mountain-männische everyday culture are the potential presentation themes of this space, which proved to be almost untapped by urban tourism.
content.title_en: Testimonies of the emergence of the Ruhr industrial cultural landscape: the Hanover-Hannibal-Königsgrube mine landscape in Bochum and Herne and their industrial cultural potentials

content.text: Applications for model transformations: Design and implementation of an application framework. Graphical model descriptions play a crucial role in designing and verifying systems. These model formalisms have varying degrees of abstraction and formality, making them more or less suitable for algorithmic processing. Metamodel model transformations are intended to enable the transfer of model instances of a metamodel to another, more formal metamodel, with the intention of making statements about the original model based on verification of the target model. The aim of this thesis is to provide a software-based basis for the definition of metamodels, the realization of model transformations and the processing of the resulting models. The results are the design and implementation of a Java-based framework that provides generic structures for any model type of customizable model environment. These environments can be linked to each other via rule-based conversion relationships and are expandable by any functional components. The implementation is done for the Eclipse platform using the Eclipse Framework and the Modeling Framework in IBM.
content.title_en: Applications for Model Transformations : Design and Implementation of an Application Framework

content.text: The measurement accuracy of the measurement measurement is improved by the use of a laserinterferometric tracking system for the accuracy increase in coordinate measurement technology. In the industry, products are developed in ever shorter development cycles, with increasingly tighter production tolerances and an increasingly complex functionality. This is the result of increasing demands on the production measurement technology. Against this background, the present dissertation describes the realization of a precision-enhancing procedure for coordinate measuring instruments. This additive method is based on the implementation of a high-precision laserinterferometric tracking system into a coordinate measuring instrument. For each measuring point in the room, a further length measurement in the interesting measuring direction is performed in addition to the coordinates of the coordinate measuring instrument. The mathematically optimized integration of this additional information leads to a reduction of measurement uncertainty. The development of the laserinterferometric tracking system is another focus of the present dissertation. This is a special execution of a laser tracker which proves to be a fixed reference measurement in space.
content.title_en: A contribution to the development of a laserinterferometric tracking system for the increase of accuracy in coordinate measurement technology

content.text: Development of microencapsulated probiotic preparations for use as an additive in meat products. Probiotics, microencapsulation, meat additives. - The aim of this study was to develop the technological and microbiological foundations for the use of microencapsulated probiotics in meat products. The four different probiotic strains Lactobacillus reuteri (S 24), Lactobacillus rhamnosus (S 25), Lactobacillus paracasei (S 26) and Lactobacillus gasseri (S 28) were investigated as possible as an additive in meat products. The influence of various spices and saline concentrations, as well as different microencapsulations and storage temperatures, were tested. In preliminary trials, the effect of twelve different spices and three salt concentrations on the growth of the four probiotic germs was investigated.
content.title_en: Development of microencapsulated probiotic preparations for use as an additive in meat products

content.text: Investigations of activated and induced chemical defense of marine macroalgae. In order to investigate the influence of mechanical wounding on D. dichotoma's chemical defense potential, metabolic profiling was performed. In doing so, extracts of intact D. dichotoma were compared with algae previously wounded with GC/MS and LC/MS-based methods. The metabolite profile was investigated using polar and nonpolar extraction agents, different derivative agents and at different intervals between wounding and extraction. However, it could not be demonstrated that the production and conversion of primary and secondary metabolites recorded with the described methods in D. dichotoma was influenced by mechanical wounding. Thus, the known anti-freeze terpenoid substances appear to be constitutive chemical defense metabolites. Furthermore, despite the large number of proteins and reactive compounds in the algae matrix, no clear changes in the protein pattern after mechanical wounding could be detected.
content.title_en: Investigations of activated and induced chemical defense of marine macroalgae

content.text: Neuronal networks as a model of Boolean functions. In this paper, the possibilities of Boolean functions are investigated by Neuronal networks and a new kind of Boolean Neuronal Networks (BNN) is developed. The basic element of Boolean Neuronal Networks is a novel Boolean Neuron (BN), which, unlike the classical neuron, operates directly with Boolean signals and uses Boolean operations only. For the training of BNN, a sequential algorithm has been developed which guarantees a fast convergence and thus requires a short training time. This training algorithm forms the basis of a new method for the architecture synthesis of BNN. The developed training also represents a special decomposition method of Boolean functions...
content.title_en: Neuronal networks as model Boolean functions

content.text: A functional biomimetic for nickel superoxide dismutase. Superoxide radical anions (O2.-) are produced as a by-product in natural energy production. O2.- cell best-contents are affected by their high reactivity and cause irreversible damage in the long term, which is considered a reason for age phenomena. Superoxide dismutases convert the O2.- into less dangerous hydrogen peroxide and oxygen. Thus, the SODs are an important part of the protective system in organisms. The aim of this work was the synthesis and characterization of a minimal biomimetic model of nickel superoxide dismutes (NiSOD). NiSOD has been found in heavy metal resistant bacteria as well as some cyanobacteria and consists of six homologous subunits. Each of these subunits has a nickel-containing activity centre, which is quite freely bound to the subunit. Due to its macrocyclic structure, the activity centre is called Nickel Hook. This consists of nine, partly highly preserved amino acids, of which only the first six amino acids surround the nickel ion.
content.title_en: A functional biomimetic for nickel superoxide dismutase

content.text: Fluorescent glasses and glass ceramics in the ZnO-Al2O3-SiO2-Sm2O3 system. The aim of this work was to investigate glasses and glass ceramics in the ZnO-Al2O3-SiO2-Sm2O3 system. The main focus was on changing the fluorescence behaviour of Sm3+ in the visual spectral range when the glass was transferred to glass ceramics. The crystallization behaviour of the ZnO-Al2O3-SiO2 basic glasses, the influence of the germ forming addition ZrO2 on the crystallization and the associated fluorescence changes of Sm3+ were systematically investigated. It was possible to gain basic knowledge about the influence of crystallization in the glasses on the fluorescence of Sm3+ in the ZnO-Al2O3-SiO2 system, to clarify the greater fluorescence of glass ceramics and to develop glass ceramics with greater fluorescence intensity.
content.title_en: Fluorescent glasses and glass ceramics in the ZnO-Al2O3-SiO2-Sm2O3 system

content.text: Everyday images of climate change: to the climate consciousness in Germany. If one considers the rising carbon dioxide emissions, it becomes clear: A fundamental change towards a sustainable society with an energy balance, which does not cause dangerous consequences for the natural climate system, is still pending. A transformation of energy systems does not depend solely on the technical possibilities, but also and above all on the willingness to change social lifestyles. But social change takes place in a contradictory context: constraints of action play a role as well as incentives, infrastructure, public discourse of competing interests, habits, preferences and lifestyles. Melanie Weber investigates the question of how climate change is perceived in the population and whether and how within the institutionally shaped patterns of action, the competing norms and everyday practices a climate consciousness develops.
content.title_en: Everyday images of climate change : on climate awareness in Germany

content.text: The first approach of the present study was to analyse systematic and genetic effects on the prevalence of common eye diseases in the single- and multi-coloured English Cocker Spaniel (ECS), to characterize similarities and differences in prevalence and the origin of primary cataract in these two separately bred color variants of the ECS and to develop a selection strategy against the primary cataract based on the obtained results. The second approach of the work consisted in clarifying the genetic basis of this disease in the ECS using molecular genetic methods. For the comparative study, another dog breed affected by the primary cataract, the rough-haired Kromfohrländer (KFL), was made available for the first-stage study of the ECS. The data for the population of male male male and female male male, was provided for the first-stage study of the BD.
content.title_en: Population and molecular genetic analysis of primary cataracts in English Cocker Spaniels and wire-haired Kromfohrlanders

content.text: Basic Law and Superstatehood : Conflict and Harmony in Germany's External Relations. The "association of states and the unity of the human race" can only be found in the acceptance of diversity under the present conditions of internationalization. Frank Schorkopf makes the German constitutional state and its right recapable from this problem perspective and from the contradictions of the internationalization of state relations. (Source: Klappentext des Verlags).
content.title_en: Basic Law and Superstatehood : Conflict and Harmony in Germany's External Relations

content.text: Barrier-free architecture : old and disabled-accessible planning and construction in the 21st century ; [Handbook and planning aid]. Publishing text: Building barrier-free means more than just setting up wide doors and low light switches. Accessibility enables independent and self-determined living, promotes mobility and integration in the coexistence of all age and groups of people. Approximately 50 current project examples, extensively presented in texts, photos, plans and drawings, convey a modern formal language, with the help of which modern habitats are created and designed for humans. Expert essays and an illustrated commentary on DIN 18025 complete this new manual. Includes among other things planning bases for barrier-free apartments (e.g. disabilities and their specific planning requirements, in the apartment area such as hallway, hallway, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom).
content.title_en: Barrier-free architecture : old and disabled-friendly planning and construction in the 21st century ; [Manual and planning aid]

content.text: Video interviewing child witnesses : on the practice of the law on witness protection. The author examines the practice of video interviewing child witnesses. The starting point of her empirical investigation is the question whether the law reform is not only well meant but can also be implemented in practice. Here she refers to the regulations of the law on witness protection created in 1998, to whose feasibility in the sense of an effective protection of victims intended by the legislator, in particular the avoidance of the so-called secondary victimization (dreamatisation), experts from Lower Saxony - prosecutor's office, police and courts - report on her first experiences. In five selected Lower Saxony district courts the author also carried out a comprehensive file analysis for the use of video interview and concludes that the video technology is as good as not used in the criminal proceedings.
content.title_en: Video interview of child witnesses : on the practice of the witness protection law

content.text: Migration - a topic of urban development policy?. From the summary: This dissertation deals with the question whether and to what extent urban development policy uses urban development concepts to address tasks and challenges arising from immigration and the presence of migrants in the city. To this end, key topics of migration are first identified, which have a connection to urban development. Along these topics, six selected urban development concepts are examined on their migration and integration-related statements. In summary, it can be seen that urban development policy has only recognized the importance of "migration" as a topic in a fragmentary way. Urban development concepts are only used with discretion to transport this topic into urban development policy.
content.title_en: Migration - a topic of urban development policy?

content.text: Mathematics and linguistic competence: preschool diagnostic possibilities for children with and without a migrant background. 'Without numbers, no world and without words, you only look at', the mother of a preschool child formulates the connection between mathematics and language. In this volume the focus is on this hitherto largely unexplored topic. Starting from the unequal educational participation of pupils with and without a migrant background, theoretical and empirical findings on early mathematical and (more)linguistic skills are presented and possibilities and limits of diagnostic methods are shown. The linguistic competences have a multifaceted impact on mathematical skills. Moreover, factors of perception and the family background are important for the mathematical competency. To collect these context variables, practical observation sheets were prepared and tested for various mathematically relevant development areas of the children, as well as a guide to the collection of the family background. Selected individual cases illustrate the theoretical explanations of this volume. <dt.>
content.title_en: Mathematics and linguistic competence : pre-school diagnostic options for children with and without a migrant background

content.text: Field-oriented control of the permanent excited synchronous machine without position encoders for the entire speed range to standstill. The present work deals with the energized, field-oriented control of the permanent excited synchronous machine with surface mounted magnets. Based on the basics for the energized control, a classification of the rotor angle determination methods available in the literature is performed. From the point of view of the requirements for application in cost-effective industrial drives, two methods were selected, which can cover the entire speed range. One of the methods is based on the integration of the induced voltage and is used for rotor angle determination in the upper speed range. At low speed and in standstill, a second estimation method is used, based on the embossing of a test signal. Both methods are combined in a single structure, so that a smoother transition between the two methods results in relation to speed. The focus of the work is the practical implementation of the determination methods by means of a commercially available converter, which is based on a low-cost 16-bit fixed point digital signal processor. For the characteristics of the rotor angle determination with the test signal, the need of the sample of the sample of the sample of the sample.
content.title_en: Field-oriented control of the permanent excited synchronous machine without position sensor for the entire speed range until standstill

content.text: The increasing demands on technical glass and the intended realization of new applications lead to the continuous development of their chemical compositions, resulting in the need to improve the control and control of the production process. This requires an optimisation of the glass production technology.To achieve this goal, experimental investigations were carried out in crucible melts to investigate the effects of electromagnetic flow influence. The electromagnetic flow influence is based on the targeted generation of larentz forces in the glass melt, which arise from the superposition of an electrical current density distribution with a magnetic field. For an evaluation of the potential of electromagnetic flow influence, the estimate of the size ratio of larentz force is suitable for the inner friction and buoyancy force. The experimental results with glass melts from the BaOB2O3SiO2 system and model fluids show that the electromagnetic generated force effects lead to the formation of different flow forms in relation to the physical properties. The demonstration of an electromagnetic flow influence2 was used to determine the average radiation fraction of the glass fraction in the process of distillation.
content.title_en: Effect of electromagnetically generated force effects on the flow in glass melts

content.text: Knowledge-intensive service providers in automotive development : Locational organization of engineering service providers under the influence of local institutional control systems of automotive manufacturers. The development of attractive new vehicle models is a key competitive factor for automotive manufacturers in globalized markets. Knowledge-intensive service providers today take on a considerable share of automotive development. The book shows how automotive manufacturers use engineering outsourcing, simultaneous engineering and the digitalization of the process chain to involve engineering service providers in how they organize their knowledge by building up different forms of proximity and pursue a cross-location work under the influence of asymmetric power relationships.
content.title_en: Knowledge-intensive service providers in automotive development : location organization of engineering service providers under the influence of local institutional control systems of automotive manufacturers

content.text: The immoral sex: the birth of negative andrology. Behind the gender debate is the conviction: in modern times, the man is staged as a rational alpha animal, the woman is considered to be his other: emotional and inferior. Christoph Kucklick deconstructs this myth with a system-theoretical close reading of canonical texts on the gender relationship from around 1800. He brings to light a completely different order of speech: the negative andrology in which the man appears as a deterrent product of modernization: as violent, immoral and driven. Even spruce deduction of marriage - previously read as a manifesto of machismo - can be understood as a new way of being able to civilize the "bad men".
content.title_en: The immoral sex : to the birth of negative andrology

content.text: Characterization and application of photorefractive dillenite crystals. New optical methods for characterizing photorefractive crystals are presented, which enable the determination of crystal parameters, crystal section or internal electrical shielding field in dillenites in a simple way. The application of photorefractive crystals for coherent beam profile formation in the so-called three-wave mixture is demonstrated. It is shown that in real-time hologram interferometry the crystals can be used in the so-called double two-wave-mix arrangement for measuring phase changes (also in video clock) with high phase resolution.
content.title_en: Characterization and use of photorefractive dillenite crystals

content.text: 3D reconstruction of CAD objects and moment-based 3D-Fitting. In the first part of the work a new idea and based on it a system architecture for the reconstruction of 3D CAD objects from their projections is presented. It is suitable to create a 3D-Feature model directly from scanned paper drawings without vectorization. In the second part two algorithms for the fitting of 3D objects by normalization are specified. The objects are to be given as a 3D-voxel quantity. The treated object classes are on the one hand quadratures regarding similarity transformations, on the other hand superellipsoids regarding affine transformations.
content.title_en: 3D reconstruction of CAD objects and moment-based 3D-Fitting

content.text: The use of laser radiation in surface technology is currently synonymous with excellent surface quality, the lowest thermal component influence, fine microstructure and minimal mixing during coating. At the same time, however, this also stands for extremely high layer costs. Comprehensive industrial use will only be achieved if the process efficiency is drastically increased. An innovative approach to increase efficiency pursues the targeted forms of the cross section of the caterpillar during coating. To this end, it is necessary to influence the force ratio in the melting bath by an externally applied force component. Electromagnetic forces allow the melting bath to be formed without contact and flexibly by the interaction of magnetic fields with electrical currents. The mechanisms are investigated and detailed in terms of influence factors, effect, process boundaries and technological usability. Under industrial production conditions, the three mechanisms are always overlaid with the potential difference between meltable and solid substrate material and an external difference in potential are considered.
content.title_en: Laser beam welding under the influence of magnetic and electrical fields

content.text: Correlation of the process parameters and the solid body physical structure as well as the macroscopic properties of electrolytically generated chromium systems. The work is concerned with galvanic chromium deposition from a process and material point of view. This refers to the separation from various hexavalent chromium electrolytes with and without the addition of ceramic nanoscale particles and the separation from trivalent chromium electrolytes. The theoretical procedural background of the individual systems is presented. However, the focus is also on experimental investigations. In their analysis, solid body physical and macroscopic properties, i.e. the user's interest, are distinguished. In detail, the aspects texture, grain size, hydrogen content, hardness, crack number, internal stresses and current yield are presented and interpreted in relation to the process parameters. The properties are not only recorded as individual but in correlation with each other. Known phenomena and relationships can be partially confirmed. Other correlations are presented from new perspectives, with regard to some aspects completely new findings can be presented.
content.title_en: Correlation of process parameters and solid body physics as well as macroscopic properties of electrolytically generated chromium systems

content.text: The new building for the new human being: the transformation and effect of the human image in the architecture of the 1920s in Germany. At the beginning of the 20th century, reform efforts of all kinds are developing in many areas of culture and society. The resulting mood of departure, which is even more intensified after the end of the First World War and the beginning of the Weimar Republic, is supported by the hope of an egalitarian age and a new society, which is to be formed from "new people". - - The search for the adequate housing of this new human being is a guiding theme in the thinking of numerous architects of the 1920s and the focal point of the discussion about the reform of various building tasks. Single and multi-family houses, collective residential high-rises, settlements and urban planning are conceived with a view to a new human being. Theoreticians and architects such as Adolf Behne, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe or Ludwig Hilberseimer refer to the findings of contemporary physicians, sociologists or psychologists in order to bring the new housing needs into experience and to predict the further social development of the modern individual. - the book architecture - the subject of the present is increasingly devoted to the new art of the subject of the new art of the new human being in 1920.
content.title_en: The new building for the new human being : the transformation and effect of the human image in the architecture of the 1920s in Germany

content.text: Positioning and active optics of the Hexapod telescope. The Hexapod telescope combines numerous innovative ideas in telescope construction, which were never tested by industrialists in an astronomical operation. Although the individual components of mechanics and optics are all of the highest precision, their interaction was not tested in the laboratory or in the sky. The present dissertation did this work and brought the telescope into the immediate vicinity of the astronomical operation. For the first time, the Hexapod telescope could be used to take and evaluate star photos.

content.text: Estimators in periodically observed autoregressive models. There is a linear autoregressive time series that we do not observe completely, but at periodically repeating times. Based on these observations, we construct estimators for the autoregression parameter and the innovation density of the fully observed time series. The estimator for innovation density uses a deconvolution estimate. A simpler variant has already been introduced in a so-called limited deconvolution problem for independent observations. Furthermore, we show the local asymptotic normality of the periodically observed time series. Efficient estimators for the autoregression parameter are characterized. We construct an efficient estimator under an additional structural assumption. To do this, we use the smallest quadrate estimate as a start estimate and improve it with the Newton-Rhapson method.
content.title_en: Estimators in periodically observed autoregressive models

content.text: Against the zeitgeist: the way to the VELKD as a Lutheran confessional church. The United Evangelical Lutheran Church of Germany (VELKD), the union of Lutheran regional churches within the Evangelical Church in Germany (EKD) emerged in 1948 from the so-called Lutheran Council. Thomas Martin Schneider examines the complex history of the VELKD on the basis of archive material that has been largely undeveloped so far. This is the first time that the Lutheran wing of the Confessing Church, the so-called Luther Council and its various predecessors, has been brought into focus, especially in the context of the efforts to achieve Lutheran unification that have been long since gone back to the 19th century.

content.text: The educational work on Nazi memorials between knowledge transfer, victims' memory and human rights education. Practice fields, concepts and methods in Bavaria. Klappentext: What can education really do about National Socialism in view of the often enormous claim between knowledge transfer and human rights education? The present study investigates this question and examines the special contribution of educational work to historical places of Nazi crimes for the formation of tradition about National Socialism. In Bavaria's example, a very vivid picture of the diversity of memorial-site educational offers is drawn. A historical overview gives an overview of the historical significance of the memorial site. The focus is on the educational efforts of the concentration camp memorials Dachau and Flossenbürg as well as other Nazi memorials in Bavaria: places of former concentration camp for foreign and forced labor camps, and places of Jewish life, which bear witness to exclusion, the deprivation of rights in the midst of German society and the deportation of Jewish citizens, finally historical places of political resistance and those that play a role in the establishment of Nazi-rule and the practice of central-style-relation-repedagogical-relation.
content.title_en: Educational and Commemorative Culture : Educational work on Nazi memorials between knowledge transfer, victims' memory and human rights education. Practice fields, concepts and methods in Bavaria

content.text: The Bundestag as the builder in Berlin: ideas, concepts, decisions on political architecture (1991-1998). Against the background of the building history of the Bonn parliament buildings and the Reichstag building, the present book examines the numerous ideas, concepts and decisions with which the commissions convened by the Bundestag's Council of Elders for the construction of the Bundestag occupied themselves during the period 1991-1998. The focus is on the question of how the Bundestag, in the eyes of an ever vigilant public, has taken its decisions in the area of tension between the claim for representation, expeditiousness, cost awareness, time pressure and historically burdened building substance. In addition to conceptual questions of the move and the balancing of Bonn and Berlin interests, the book describes the relevant construction decisions: from the urban competition and the construction of the new buildings, via the dome and the design of the Federal Eagle, to the color concept in the plenary hall. The decisions taken at that time by a small group of representatives today shape the external appearance of the German capital and thus an important part of the state self-presentation and the political architecture of the reunited Germany - the "Berlin Republic".
content.title_en: The Bundestag as a builder in Berlin : ideas, concepts, decisions on political architecture (1991-1998)

content.text: The study also examined the area-related lighting in office rooms. According to the current state of the art, using the site-dissolving luminance and colour measurement and psychometric evaluation of 20 subjects, questions about the desired lighting quality in the office room were addressed. The investigations at the reading and writing workstation and screen workstation determined the desired sizes of the defined work areas and the desired lighting level. The screen and the screen work were given special attention. In the course of the work, the development and realization of a contrast analyser was carried out, with which contrast reproduction in the workspace can be evaluated. For contrast assessment, a light density camera and an experimental structure were used. By using the contrast analyser on the screen, further observations on the veil density and reflex suppression were made possible. In the field of screen work, the quality of visual communication was evaluated by the location-dissolving luminance measurement on the face-representation of the work areas of the work.

content.text: Antibacterially active additives in nanodisperse distribution for permanent modification of polyamide 6. The aim of the research is to produce antibacterially effective additives that can be distributed nanoscalely in polyamide during the processing process and have a low agglomeration tendency. Furthermore, by choosing a suitable active substance carrier material, the immobilization of such additives in the polymer can be achieved with simultaneous high surface activity. Selected layer silicates with antimicrobial active substances are set up organophile and intercalated in the compounding process. The additives have a good compatibility with polyamide 6 and ensure optimal incorporation of the additives in the polymer matrix. The materials are suitable for the production of foils and filaments. Thermogravimetric analyses (TGA) selected additive samples provide statements on thermal stability, which allow their use in extrusion processes in the thermoplastic deformation of polyamides.

content.text: Biomechanical analysis of the levels Locomotion of Ancylometes Bogotensis (Keyserling, 1877) (Chelicerata, Arachnida, Lycosoidea). Spider legs are characterized by their arched configuration and are unique in the animal kingdom due to their hydraulic stretching mechanism&rsquo. Previously, spiders were considered to be stereotyped, velocity-independent step patterns and an essential role of the hydraulic mechanism in force generation. Global kinematics and single-leg floor reaction forces of the continuous and accelerated flat locomotion of the South American run spider Ancylometes bogotensis were investigated. In this process, three step patterns could be distinguished using discontinuous velocity dependencies of various kinematic parameters. The directions of the ground reaction forces vectors show that the hydraulic mechanism does not contribute significantly to the production of soil reaction forces either in continuous or accelerated locomotion.
content.title_en: Biomechanical analysis of the levels Locomotion of Ancylometes Bogotensis (Keyserling, 1877) (Chelicerata, Arachnida, Lycosoidea)

content.text: Cryogenic quality measurement of optical substrate materials for future gravitational wave detectors. This work deals with the reduction of the thermal noise of optical components for gravitational wave detectors. Thermal noise represents the process, which is limited in its sensitivity. By using low temperatures and materials with a high mechanical quality, the thermal noise can be reduced. The core point of the work is the construction of a novel measuring system for the experimental investigation of the temperature dependence of mechanical quality.

content.text: The Federal Tax Legislation in the field of financial constitution: Tax Autonomy of the Countries without Reform?. According to the current financial constitution, tax competition between the Länder in the field of state taxes is possible? This question, which is currently being addressed by the federalism debate, is the author. Starting from the competence title of Art. 105 sec. 2 GG, a detailed examination of the new Art. 72 sec. 2 GG takes place, which limits the federal legislative competence in the field of state taxes to a "necessary" measure. Anja Korte shows that the concrete application of Art. 72 sec. 2 GG to individual state taxes already gives the countries considerable freedom today. The federal government is largely limited to conflict prevention, preferably by a double taxation law. It should be noted that a state tax competition cannot currently take place without a federal release law and not without restrictions.
content.title_en: The Federal's competing tax legislation in the field of financial constitution: tax autonomy of countries without reform?

content.text: Space qualification of the transition radiology detector of the AMS-02 experiment and indirect search for dark matter. It is known that the universe consists of about 22% of dark matter and that its constituent particles must be stable at non-relativistic speeds, which only have a weak effect on the exchange. However, it remains uncertain what dark matter consists of and how it is distributed in our galaxy. Supersymmetric extensions of the standard model predict the existence of new particles whose lightest (LSP) is stable in case of preservation of R-parity. In supersymmetric extensions based on the theory of supergravitation (mSUGRA), the best motivated candidate for the LSP is the lightest of the four neutralinos, a neutral, weakly changing and heavy particle. The neutralino is characterized in particular by the fact that the rognostic relic density is compulsively beneficial to the observed value of the latter. Antiparties in the cosmic media are produced exclusively by the secondary models.
content.title_en: Space qualification of the transition radiation detector of the AMS-02 experiment and indirect search for dark matter

content.text: Tests on multiplicative structure in strictly stationary processes. In this paper, new test methods for the hypothesis of a constant coefficient of variation in the nonparametric regression model are presented. The test statistics are based on an empirical distance between the squared regression function and the variance function. Assuming the stochastic independence of the underlying process, the asymptotic normality of the test statistics is demonstrated under zero hypothesis and under fixed alternatives. Subsequently, the results are extended to the more general case of strictly stationary, absolutely regular processes, which include in particular financial time series such as the ARCH(1) model. Finally, the behaviour of the presented test procedure is examined in the context of a simulation study for finite sample circumferences. Both stochastic independent data and strictly stationary time series data are illustrated the test behaviour with the help of a boat-trap procedure.
content.title_en: Tests for multiplicative structure in strictly stationary processes

content.text: Optical method for two-dimensional measurement of angles and angular changes at large distances. In this dissertation, the development of a new measurement method and a new measuring device for two-dimensional measurement of angles and angular changes are presented on the basis of a concrete task from industrial production. Conventional methods already in use as well as alternative methods based on other physical principles are used and evaluated. A solution based on a so-called vignettizing field blind method is described in its principle structure and its functioning and the suitability for the task is examined. The theoretical foundations are initially presented purely geometrically-optically and in addition subjected to a light-technical examination with natural vignetation. The intensity distribution of the light spot in the image plane, the so-called V-SPOT, is determined by various influence variables analytically. Moreover, intensity and focus shift within the V-SPOT are investigated by means of effects such as geometrical-optical influences, beam characteristic of the object light surface as a function of the beam angle and light density distribution in relation to the field of the measurement.
content.title_en: Optical method for two-dimensional measurement of angles and angular changes at large measuring distances

content.text: Highly dynamic logical networks as an infrastructure of mobile agent systems. To plan their route through the Internet, mobile agents need up-to-date service information from their globally distributed infrastructure. Today's networks have become highly dynamic through the use of mobile devices, so the frequency and number of necessary update messages in global logical networks does not scale with the amount of services offered. This work focuses on the distribution, timeliness and scalability of service information in a global logical network, taking into account the time limits caused by mobile devices. The presented solution consists of an architecture of three infrastructure services whose reference implementation is the infrastructure service framework QuickLinkNet. This builds a transparent, two-layer logical network that serves as a service-oriented infrastructure for mobile agent systems, but can also be used for other distributed applications in highly dynamic networks.
content.title_en: Highly dynamic logical networks as infrastructure of mobile agent systems

content.text: Identity and difference : Meaning problems of the differential system theory. Niklas Luhmann's system theory claims to make a paradigm shift from an identity logic to a difference logic. Can sense actually be understood differently? The book deals with this question on the basis of two central explanatory deficits: On the one hand, in the communication processes between functional systems, meaning structures can be found that cannot be explained differently ("hybridization", explained in an objective-hermeneutic analysis of the "The President's Council on Bioethics"). On the other hand, an exegesis of the meaning concept shows that Luhmann uses identity concepts to explain the system/environment interaction.
content.title_en: Identity and difference : meaning problems of the differential system theory

content.text: The design of the electromagnets is to be attributed to the design of neutral electromagnet systems. In particular, the dimensioning of a fast-activated electromagnet drive is considered to be an optimization of a mechatronic system. By observing the properties of the mutually influencing subsystems electrical power pointer, magnetic circuit, mechanical load and loss/heating it is possible to design magnetic drives with switching times in the range of several hundred microseconds and magnetic forces in the range of 50 ... 150 N. Building on the method of optimizing magnetic circuits with network models according to static aspects, optimization models are derived, which are suitable for the design of high-dynamic drives. By using the software tool SESAM it is possible to design the magnetic circuit dimensioning and the subsequent control of the dynamic parameters by dynamic simulation of a complete switching cycle with respect to the properties of the power pointer with a single tool.
content.title_en: Design of fast switching (high dynamic) neutral electromagnet systems

content.text: To the beauty of the artist: August Endell's texts on art and aesthetics; 1896 to 1925. "Reine Formkunst ist mein Ziel. Fort mit jeder Association. Formkunst als Parallele der Musik." - Like a prophecy of abstract painting, the core sentence of the aesthetics of August Endell is read in 1897. Exactly this year he planned the photo studio Elvira, which was based on a foundational aesthetic structure by the sea-mongering ornaments and bizarre colority at one stroke among the one famous and notorious among the other. If one looks more closely at the written work of Endell, it quickly becomes apparent that the apparent arbitrariness of the individual design was based on a foundational aesthetic structure. With about 60 texts Endell expressed himself multifacetedly on art and aesthetics. - - Endell's thinking and creation was influenced by the lively exchange with the cultural avant-garde of his time: He had studied philosophy with the perceptual psychologist Theodor Lipps and converted to visual art after an encounter with Hermann Obrist. The philosophy of Friedrich Nietzsche and the environment of Äps left a legible trace in the aesthetic of Wolf.
content.title_en: To Beauty : August Endell's texts on art and aesthetics ; 1896 to 1925

content.text: The finite element method analysis for assessing the residual strength of corroded oil field casting and tubing. In order to ensure the operational reliability of drilling and storage drilling even after long-term use, careful examination and assessment of damage points is recommended. In particular, the stress of the selected pipe sections for further operation is to be investigated and the safety reserves to be proven. For a special evaluation of detected corrosion sites in underground completion, especially in feed pipes, numerical calculations must be applied. A calculation procedure based on the finite element method has been developed. Thus, extensive calculations for oil field pipes with corrosion hollows have been carried out. The successful application of FEM-PS for the strength and stability calculations of unsustained oil field pipes and the results of the calculation of the damaged pipes allowed the conclusion that even pipes with corrosion hollows can be modelled correctly, recalculated and evaluated.
content.title_en: The finite element method analysis for assessment the remaining strength of corroded oil field casting and tubing

content.text: One-dimensional stochastic differential equations with generalized drift regarding constant local Martingale. In this work, stochastic differential equations with generalized drift are considered, driven by a steady local Martingal. Conditions for the weak existence and clarity in the distribution of solutions of such equations are formulated and demonstrated. To this end, the characterization of the distribution of constant local Martingale by means of Markov core plays a central role. In addition, the existence of strong solutions and the pathwise ambiguity of solutions are considered. Finally, the results found are applied to equations with ordinary drift.
content.title_en: One-dimensional stochastic differential equations with generalized drift regarding constant local Martingale

content.text: Modelling of sequential metalloenzes based on magnesium. This dissertation deals with the modelling of quantum chemical models for the description of sequential enzymes in the selected examples Inositol monophosphatase and Yeast Enolase. Initially, a template model for IMP was developed, which showed that these metallocentric models are not in a position to describe metalloenzymes when metal ion actively participates in the catalytic cycle. Furthermore, an unusual coordination behaviour of magnesium was revealed. The usually observed octaedric coordination geometry of the Mg2+ ion is not only developed in the gas phase, but also in biological systems for the benefit of a trigonal bipyramidal (penta-coordinated) arrangement. By modifying a QM/MM strategy, a quantum chemical model for the description of sequential enzymes was successfully applied in the form of a hollow space strategy and uses a spheroidal section of the activity center, on which a structural grade OR-angled is implemented by the TSO.
content.title_en: Modelling of sequential magnesium-based metalloenzymes
