content.text: Reorganization of databases: triggers, procedures, and benefit identification. In the course of time, large database-based application systems often cause a sustained deterioration of system performance due to degenerations arising in physical storage structures (e.g. scattered free space, overflow areas, migrated tuples, no longer available data clustering or sorting). Degeneration can be done with database reorganisations. However, such maintenance work, even when performed online, is usually associated with limitations in normal database operation, ranging from temporary deterioration of system performance to limited availability of data during reorganization. These limitations increasingly conflict with growing availability requirements of database management systems (DBMS). One way to reduce negative effects is to carefully select and prioritize reorganisation measures. This can identify and preferably execute useful measures, and to place others behind or fail.
content.title_en: Reorganisation of databases: triggers, procedures, identification of benefits

content.text: Synthesis and characterization of heterooligonuclear functional units for photo-induced catalysis. In this work heterooligonuclear metal complexes - consisting of two photoactive Ru units, a collector ligand and a catalytic unit - were synthesized, structurally characterized and examined in their photocatalytic properties. The aim of the research was to control the reactivity of the catalytically active metal centers by directed photo-induced electron transfer, starting from the Ru units, via the collector ligand towards the catalysis center. The C-C cracking reactions necessary for the construction of the heterooligonuclear complex were tested on suitable model systems. The process of photocatalytic hydrogen and methane production was investigated by extensive variation of process parameters at a heterotrinuclear complex and other heterodinuclear model systems.
content.title_en: Synthesis and characterisation of heterooligonuclear function units for photo-induced catalysis

content.text: Dynamic fluorescence behaviour of rare earth ions in visual spectral lenses. Fluorescence behaviour of various rare earth ions (Eu3+, Eu2+, Sm3+, Sm2+, Dy3+, Tb3+) depending on the structure and composition of the host glass used and the doping concentration of the respective rare earth ion. The investigations were carried out on several types of glass of two glass systems: on the one hand fluoride phosphate glasses with different fluoride and phosphate contents (FP00, FP03, FP10, FP20 and P100), and on the other hand on two sodium borosilicate glasses (NBS1 and Duran®) with different alkaline-borate ratios, i.e. different optical basicity. The dynamic fluorescence behaviour of the ions used depends greatly on the locally predominant binding character of the lasstructure surrounding the dosed ions. Thus, fluoridic glasses with more ionic binding character produce a relatively long fluorescence binding content.
content.title_en: Dynamic fluorescence behaviour of rare earth ions in lenses in the visual spectral range

content.text: Synthesis and characterization of polyarylenvinylenes with benzo (1,2,5) thiadiazole structural elements in the main chain. The aim of the work was to synthesize alternating polyarylenvinylenes and to characterize their optical and electronic properties. Links between the primary structure of polymers and optical and electronic properties should be studied. By the incorporation of donor and acceptor structural elements into the polymer backbone, a specific influence on the electronic properties can be exercised. Polyarylenvinylenes were synthesized in the main chain benzo[1,2.5]thiadiazole as an acceptor building block alternating with electron-rich alkyl and alkoxysubstituted aromatics. In the investigations, the low molecular model compounds are included. For the synthesis of the polymers and model compounds, the Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons-Reaction (HWE-Reaction) and the Knoevenagel-Consation are suitable.
content.title_en: Synthesis and characterisation of polyarylenvinylenes with benzo (1,2,5) thiadiazole structural elements in the main chain

content.text: City and Forest : from the urban planning approach to the near-city forest presented by the example of the urban development Karlsruhe 1870 - 2000. Under design, structural-spatial and planning aspects, this work investigates the conceptual significance of urban development Karlsruhe in the past and in the real planning of near-city forests up to the present. The focus is on the question of how urban planning has dealt with forests close to the city in the past and how the results of this approach are presented.
content.title_en: City and forest: from the urban planning approach to the near-city forest illustrated by the example of the urban development Karlsruhe 1870 - 2000

content.text: Experimental mid-infrared spectroscopic extinction measurements of agglomerate dust grains in aerosol. At present, laboratory measurements of real dust particle compositions are not able to provide accurate strip profiles for a direct comparison, because the samples are surrounded by a medium (KBr), which affects electromagnetic polarization. I have developed a new method in this work, which can be used to measure extinction spectra without the electromagnetic influence of surrounding media. I have used the aerosol technique to record extinction spectra of amorphous, crystalline silicates, quartz and species with high condensation temperature in medium infrared, which can be compared directly with observed spectra. I investigated the differences to the data recorded with the KBr method by determining and comparing the location of the maximum of the band profiles. I also examined the dust grains electron microscopically to examine morphological influences (size, shape, agglomeration) on the measured profile.
content.title_en: Experimental mid-infrared spectroscopic extension measurements of agglomerate dust grains in aerosol

content.text: In addition, the Bift-based sensors are used to optimize the Bift-based and Bift-based sensors for the application of the Bift-based technologies. In the present work, heterostructures of aluminium-gallium nitride (AlGaN) and gallium nitride (GaN) are processed, characterized and optimized as pH sensors. In the early 70s, the concept of pH measurement by ion-sensitive field effect transistors (ISFETs) is based on silicon. The advantage of these components is the miniaturisation of the sensors. The present work is concerned with characterization and optimization of the pH sensors. In the process, the Bift-based sensitivity and the light-induced reduction of the Bift-based components are investigated in the context of the Bift-based applications.
content.title_en: GaN-based pH sensors : Sensitivity, drift and passivation technologies

content.text: Physiological and biochemical characterisation of stress and adaptation states in grasses under the influence of geo-biogenic interactions. For this work the geo-biogenic interactions of the two grass species Arrhenathelium elatius (Glatthafer) and Elytrigia repens (Quecke) were studied. The problem of the work was the spread dynamics of the two grass species at a site heavily polluted by years of emissions of a cement and phosphate fertilizer plant (Stoudnitz near Jena in Thuringia). The investigations were divided into three experimental sections: 1) investigations of the influence of geochemical and geohydrological factors on soil substrates from the site in comparison with a reference substrate, 2) investigations of the influence of inter- and intraspecific bio-bio-interactions of both grass species, 3) investigations of the influence of allopathic phyto-effectors on geo-biogenic interactions of both grass species.
content.title_en: Physiological and biochemical characterisation of stress and adaptation conditions in grasses under the influence of geo-biogenic interactions

content.text: Procedures for processing XML values in SQL requester genes. According to the current version of the SQL standard, a query result may contain any XQuery sequences as column values. This includes in particular XQuery sequences consisting of several sequence entries, whose nodes are enriched with type information. However, to the question of how such XQuery sequences (included in an SQL request result) can be adequately processed with the help of an application program, neither the SQL standard nor a RDBMS product provides a satisfactory answer. To close this gap, the sequence cursor-based processing process is introduced in the present work. The basic idea of this procedure (which allows an appropriate and convenient processing of the XQuery sequences contained in an SQL request result) is to use a new cursor type, the sequence cursors, to be used to determine whether the changes are to be made to the current result tuple. These sequence sections are then processed locally and the application program is then processed in the application section.
content.title_en: Procedure for processing XML values in SQL requester genes

content.text: The influence of autofrettage on the vibration resistance of internal pressure-loaded components made of spherical graphite casting. This scientific work deals with the fatigue resistance of autofrettated components made of spherical graphite casting EN-GJS under internal pressure-swelling stress. On component samples with a 90° bore trimming from EN-GJS-400-18, EN-GJS-500-7 and EN-GJS-600-3, the component scooping lines were determined in one-stage tests at the stress ratios R ~ 0 and R = 0.5 and the pressure resistance increase was determined by autofrettage. Furthermore, the complete cracking-swelling-square lines of the unautofretted and autofrettated component samples were calculated in order to evaluate the impact (omission level) of small vibration plays on the pressure resistance of these components.

content.text: Models of rotationally symmetric : collision-dominated debris discs. This work deals with models of size distribution and spatial distribution of the material in so-called circular debris discs with rotation symmetry. These discs, which are considered to be the remnants of planet formation, orbit main sequence stars and consist of objects from submicrometer-sized dust to possibly planetesimals of several hundred kilometers in diameter. Collision and the ejection of very small dust by stellar radiation pressure lead to a constant thinning out of otherwise undisturbed disks. As a tool for modelling, a numerical implementation of kinetic, statistical theory was used. On the other hand, analytical approximations were developed to verify and interpret the obtained results.
content.title_en: Models of rotationally symmetric : collision-dominated debris discs

content.text: A semantic concept for the mapping of low-level analysis data to high-level scene descriptions. Together with the growing need for security, an increasing amount of surveillance content is created. To enable a fast and reliable search in the recordings of hundreds or thousands of monitoring sensors installed in a single facility, indexing this content is indispensable in advance. To this end, the concept of Smart Indexing & Retrieval (SIR) allows for cost-effective search by generating high-level metadata. As it becomes increasingly difficult to generate these data manually with acceptable time and cost effort, the creation of this metadata must be done automatically on the basis of low-level analysis data. While previous approaches are highly domain-dependent, in this work a generic concept for the mapping of the results of low-level analysis data on semantic scene descriptions is presented. The constituent elements of this approach and the underlying terms are presented, and an introduction to their application is given. The main contribution of the presented approach is its generality and the early stage is performed on the step of the closing domain of the analysis of the small-level of the context of the context of the context.
content.title_en: A semantic concept for the mapping of low-level analysis data to high-level scene descriptions

content.text: Design and implementation of innovative architectures for learning content management systems (LCMS) for use in revenue-oriented education export. The aim of this work is to systematically analyse the requirements and explain various approaches to the realization of these requirements in the use of learning content management systems (LCMS) in revenue-oriented education export. After the systematic establishment of the requirements, different LCMSs are analyzed in relation to these requirements and selected for further consideration of one of the systems. content.text: The reduction of the obligation to pay damages in Europe: to the chances of including a general reduction clause in a European right of damage. Reduction clauses are meant to mean genuine breaks in the principle of total reparation, which reduce the compensation claim proportionately in the area of damage rights. Reduction clauses in German law, for example, are maximum damages or the rules on the division of damages in case of co-inflict. Instead of defining in the so-called special reduction clauses the conditions under which a reduction of the compensation claim is considered and, if necessary, to the extent to which the reduction is to be made, some legal systems in Europe have instead created or parallel a general reduction clause which puts it in the court's discretion whether and to what extent a reduction of the compensation claim should be made. This study aims to contribute to the necessary legal unification in Europe by examining the suitability of a general reduction clause for a European right of damage law and clarifying how the need for a reasonable limitation of the compensation obligation can best be taken into account in individual cases. This question is to be examined in the way of legal comparison, the German legal order, the German law, and the Dutch law.
content.title_en: The reduction of the obligation to pay damages in Europe: the opportunities for the inclusion of a general reduction clause in a European right to property

content.text: The European Union stresses the increasing importance of integrated rural development (ILE). Maximilian Ortner shows how forestry can successfully participate in this development. Forest model projects for drinking water forest, wood mobilisation, wood sales increase, energy forest, airport protection forest or environmental education are analysed as examples of active action in forest practice in the context of integrated rural development. The examples refer to the state forest, municipal forest, private forest owners and the Chamber of Agriculture. A checklist of the identified success factors provides information on the success factors with which the success chances of concrete projects can be quickly assessed.
content.title_en: Success factors for the participation of forest actors in integrated rural development: the example of LEADER+ programme of EU structural policy

content.text: Supersymmetry on a space-time lattice. An important component of common extension scenarios of the standar model of elementary particle physics is supersymmetry, which creates novel relationships between bosons and fermions. For this, quantum field theories have long been known to lead to astonishing consequences. The fact that no signatures of supersymmetric particles have been found in previous observations is explained by the fact that supersymmetry is broken on a very high energy scale. The dynamics of this phenomenon cannot be investigated with the otherwise very successful trouble-theoretical methods. As an alternative, the construction of grid-regulated supersymmetrical theories is offered. In addition to a rigorous definition of quantum heory, this approach also allows the numerical treatment of many questions. However, this approach is not free of problems. The dissertation focuses in depth on the supersymmetric wess-Zamino model and presents the problems encountered in the construction of the lattice theory. With the help of a special conjugation theory, the supersymmetry of the lattice theory can be constructed.
content.title_en: Supersymmetry on a space-time lattice

content.text: The current transition from an industrial to a knowledge society is accompanied by spatial and temporal flexibility of work, leisure, consumption and mobility. This profound social transformation is not only reflected in the individual everyday organization of the affected people, but also leads to a transformation of the rhythm of our cities, in which the causes and consequences of the dissolution of collective time structures are particularly evident. The social geography study shows the consequences of this development for cities and their inhabitants, using the example of the metropolis of Hamburg.
content.title_en: Delimited city: spatial fragmentation and temporal flexibility in the late modern age

content.text: The neoliberal city : discursive representations in the city marketing of German cities. Using Foucault's theory of governance and the theory of hegemony by Laclau and Mouffe, this book analyses the current upheavals in urban development, often referred to as "neoliberal". The empirical object of this book is urban marketing, which is used to trace hegemonic conflicts and discursive constitutional processes. To this end, a methodical approach is developed which integrates quantitative-lexicometric and statement-analytic methods and thus makes an important contribution to the discussion of methods currently taking place in discourse research.
content.title_en: The neoliberal city : discursive representations in the city marketing of German cities

content.text: The concept of a government information system. Business IT has been working on IT-based strategic management in companies for several decades. Management information systems provide control-relevant data for the respective decision makers. However, such IT-based strategic-oriented management has hardly been dealt with in politics and administration. Frank Finkler reviews the optimization needs of political control and designs an electronic government information system to improve management work in politics and administration. He develops a target concept that provides policy- and administrative-relevant information for effective management of policy measures. Based on two real-life solutions, the author checks the findings for their practical suitability. This is the government information system CONIFERE (country level) established in Saarland and the Intraplan B (Federal level) system used by the Federal Chancellery.
content.title_en: Design of a government information system

content.text: Seasonality and long-drive/short-drive differentials in gymnosperms: derived or originally?. Most gymnosperms are always green. Seasonality is generally considered a derived feature in this group. Studies in the angiosperms show that the drive differentiation here is closely correlated with seasonality and the leaves of a short-drived leaf replace the area of a single long-drived leaf. This simple correlation often does not exist with seasonal bald gymnosperms. In the gymnosperms, however, some evergreen taxa are drift differentials (e.g. Cedrus, Pinus, Sequoia). Moreover, both seasonal bald and evergreen taxodioid cupressaces show a reduction zone at the base of short-drive or short-drived shoots. Such structures therefore give reason to suspect that seasonality in gymnosperms was much more frequent than the present species spectrum suggests.
content.title_en: Seasonality and long-drive/short-drive differentiation in gymnosperms: derived or originally?

content.text: Synthesis and characterization of sulfur-containing platinum(II) complexes and their cytotoxic properties. In the course of this thesis, synthesis strategies of new and already known platinum(II) complexes were developed, which are to be investigated with regard to their cytotoxic properties. Here, sulfur- or selenium-containing amino acids, thioles, thioethers, phosphine and diamine ligands were used. The already known complexes are a metabolic product, which is produced by the administration of the cytostatic agent oxaliplatin. For this complex type a reproducible synthesis was developed and cytotoxicity was tested on different cell lines. The novel platinum(II) compounds are diamine-platin(II) complexes with lipoic acid derivatives as well as O,S-chelatligands and bisphosphine-dithiolate-platin(II) complexes.
content.title_en: Synthesis and characterisation of sulphurous platinum(II) complexes and their cytotoxic properties

content.text: Synthesis of novel ligands based on 5/6/5 heterocycles. The dissertation presented here focused on the reactions of the bisthiadiazole triazinium salts (5/6/5 heterocycles) with various sticky ng nucleophiles. Of particular interest were the reactions of 2-hydroxyphenylsubstituted 5/6/5 heterocycles, as their reactivity is known to differ from their analogues. The implementations of the 5/6/5 heterocycles with nitrogen nucleophiles were carefully investigated in terms of selectivity and product diversity. Some representatives investigated the complex properties of the new compounds.
content.title_en: Synthesis of novel ligands based on 5/6/5 heterocycles

content.text: The Jesus Movement : Backgrounds of its origin and spread ; a historical-exegetical investigation of the motives of Jesus' succession. How did the historical circumstances of the ancient society of Palestine in the first century favour or impair the Jesus Movement? What motives have led to people seeking help with Jesus or having joined his movement and followed him? Three main themes are highlighted in the horizon of these questions: illness and healing (Jesus as a healer and exorcist); economic factors (Jesus freed from poverty, debt, saturates the hungry); the power-political dimension (Jesus as a figure empowered by God, as a liberator of foreign domination, Jesus as an eschatological ruler).
content.title_en: The Jesus Movement : Backgrounds of its Origin and Spread ; a historical-exegetical investigation of the motives of the Jesus Succession

content.text: Oxidative dehydration of ethylenebenzene to styrene in the Mikorwellen field. The aim of this work is to contribute to a better understanding of the microwave assisted heterogeneous gas phase catalysts, using the example of oxidative dehydration of ethylenebenzene to styrene. This reaction was chosen because of its industrial importance. Styrene is one of the oldest and most important starting materials for the production of plastics, especially synthetic rubber and polystyrene, from which many everyday household articles such as clothes hangers or clothespins are produced, as well as housings for electronic devices or food-compatible packaging. Currently, styrene is almost exclusively produced by dehydration of ethylenebenzene at temperatures between 600 and 700ʿC in the presence of water vapour via potassium-promovated iron oxide catalysts. Water vapor supplies the heat and also suppresses the draining deactivation processes, such as the deposition of coke. This process is particularly energy-intensive and this at a time point in the energy hunger of the world, whether from oil, coal, and even more energy from the emission of this atom.
content.title_en: Oxidative dehydration of ethylenebenzene to styrene in the Mikor wave field

content.text: Contributions to heterocycle synthesis based on ring transformation reactions of [Delta]2-1,2-diacetins. A synthetic approach to the [Delta]2-1,2-diacetins compound class found in the 2002 working group is the basis for this work. It shows optimized synthesis and basic pathways of these four-member heterocycles. Numerous examples demonstrate that the [Delta]2-1,2-diacetins can be regioselectrically transformed to a wide spectrum of highly substituted heterocycles with independent follow-up chemistry. Synthesis and properties of 1,3,4-oxadiazins, 1,3,4-thiadiazines, 1,3,4-selenadiazines, 1,3,4-thiadiazoles, 1,3,4-selenadiazoles, 1,3,4-selenadiazoles and 1,4-dihydropyridazines are described. Together with quantum chemists, physicists and pharmacists, mechanistic details of the ring transformations were re-engineered by a structural-diameter-diameters of a particularity.

content.text: Multi-Frame Rate rendering. Multi-Frame Rate rendering is a parallel rendering technique that calculates interactive parts of a scene on a separate graphic map. The image of the rest of the scene is asynchronous on another graphic map. The resulting color and depth images of both representation processes are combined and displayed by means of optical overlay or digital composition. The results of a user study show that multi-Frame Rate rendering significantly accelerates interaction for large scenes.
content.title_en: Multi-frame rate rendering

content.text: Metaphors in geopolitical discourses: Space presentations in the debate about American missile defense. Jan Helmig was coordinator of the Research Training Group 'World Concepts and Global Structure Patterns' at the Faculty of Sociology at Bielefeld University. His research focuses on American defence programs and geopolitical approaches in international relations. The spatial turn in the social sciences is increasingly emphasising the importance of space for the analysis of social relations. Based on a constructive political geography, this book addresses a topic area that has experienced a considerable media response in recent times. The American missile defense programs were and are not only transatlantic security relations, but are repeatedly being used as evidence of American hegemony efforts. However, analyses approach the topic complex mostly from a classical point of view and primarily focus on military technology as well as (geo) strategic considerations. At this point, however, the use of spatial representational methods is always being used, especially taking into account central metaphors in the foreground of the work.
content.title_en: Metaphors in geopolitical discourses : Space presentations in the debate about the American missile defense

content.text: The source behaviour of alkali silicate gels with due regard to their composition. In the course of this work 48 gel samples were produced and examined for their source behaviour via various manufacturing methods. A repeatability of the measurements with other processors was tested and demonstrated. In the source experiments it is shown that high alkali contents in the gel samples produce high spring pressures at low solubility (due to small amounts of calcium in the sample). An influence of the sodium-potassium ratio (alkali ratio) on the source behaviour of the gel samples cannot be detected.
content.title_en: The spring behaviour of alkali silicate gels in accordance with their composition

content.text: Einstein's opponent : the public controversy surrounding relativity theory in the 1920s. In the 1920s, numerous popular writings were published that wanted to refute Einstein's relativity theory. Milena Wazeck shows to what extent the physicist and his theory were perceived as a fundamental threat by academics as well as non-academics. This threat was so strong that an international network against relativity theory formed, whose existence here is first documented by new source material.
content.title_en: Einstein's opponent : the public controversy over relativity theory in the 1920s

content.text: The forgotten space: the third dimension in the facade architecture of the early modern era. The spatial stability of facades was an essential component of early modern architecture. It determined the formal design, but also the scenography, iconography and use of structures and first made them related to their surroundings. From the 19th century onwards, it was to be forgotten, it should now be rediscovered. - The facade space was an important element of architectural design in Renaissance, Baroque and Classicism. However, it was already in the 19th century that open facades were transferred to glazing, latching or even walling for reasons of weather protection, security or the acquisition of space. However, the structure and proportional structure of the facades were thus disturbed as much as their relationship to the interior and their surroundings. Particularly eye-catching examples here are the Damasushof of the Vatican, the Petersdom or the Upper Belvedere in Vienna. Art history has never given due consideration to the third dimension of facades. - This study calls the facade space back to an early art historical category and systematically records it in the whole time of architecture.
content.title_en: The forgotten space: the third dimension in the facade architecture of the early modern era

content.text: Parental alignment syndrome - the loss of one's own child through separation and divorce : a study of the course of the break-up of contact with one's own child and the resulting effects on affected parents. Summary: A socially hardly perceived phenomenon is that some fathers and mothers lose contact with their children completely as a result of separation and divorce and can no longer participate in their lives. What is hardly conceivable for outsiders is an existential trauma for the affected parents. The present work gives a detailed introduction to the problem and deals with the study of the previously scientifically neglected side of the affected parent in the loss of contact due to separation and divorce. How does the break-up of contact occur? In what form does it affect the psychological and somatoform health of the parents? What effects does it have on the quality of life and satisfaction as well as on working and everyday life? The results of the study provide a comprehensive insight into the situation of affected parents and important suggestions for research and politics

Against the background of the changed technical and economic framework conditions, the author addresses the highly topical question of how the equal access of programme operators to the television cable network can be ensured. The aim of the study is to give an overview of the legal framework conditions in the relationship of programme organisers - network operators with special consideration of the voltage field of broadcasting and telecommunications law as well as of antitrust law. content.text: The compound imaging FT-IR and MALDI-TOF-MS: site-dissolving analysis of plant surfaces. Leaf waxes cover as an extreme boundary layer all surface plants and are already described for many species in terms of their morphology and composition. These waxes control the plant's water balance, act as a reaction barrier against pollutants or influence the attachment of parasites and pathogens, thereby significantly contributing to plant fitness. The aim of this work was to develop a surface analysis of combined imaging infrared spectroscopy (IR) and imaging MALDI mass spectrometry (MALDI-MS) for site-dissolving study of leaf surfaces. The combination of both analytical methods allows the examination of individual structures as well as complete substance classes, even with unknown sample composition. For this, a selective method of isolation of epicuticular growth had to be identified in the area of the leaf and a suitable sample carrier was developed. Using the developed surface analysis, the previously unknown, higher molecular ester in the epicutical monitoring of the plant surface was used for the first time to characterize the presence of the plant and the presence of the plant surface of the plant.
content.title_en: Combined Imaging FT-IR and MALDI-TOF-MS : site-dissolving analysis of plant surfaces

content.text: The subject of the "Barrier-free Internet for People with Intellectual Disabilities" has not yet been empirically investigated in the German-speaking world. The present study closes this gap by examining the legal guidelines for the creation of barrier-free Internet sites in Germany for their effectiveness for people with intellectual disabilities. In this context, the inclusion of the target group and the acceptance of these as experts are ensured by specially created research instruments, while simultaneously being usable. The research design is characterized by a methodological triangulation, which usefully links the various study objectives and different disciplines. The core of this study is an experimental test page study, which is combined with observation and survey and thus provides results suitable for everyday and practical use. The results are developed in detail with reference to the scientific and the corresponding regulations (BITV, WCAG 1.0 and WCAG 2.0). The results are discussed in relation to the technical guidelines.
content.title_en: Barrier-free Internet for people with mental disabilities: an experimental pilot study on technical requirements and participatory effects

content.text: Baby flap and anonymous birth: a critical inventory in the context of current reform proposals. From Aachen to Wuppertal, more than 80 baby flaps are intended to preserve unwanted children of abuse and death. In Hamburg alone, 22 children were deposited in it in the first five years. Many clinics also allow mothers to give birth unrecognized, with the mother and infant at least medically and psychologically in good care. Media and politics generally celebrate the rescue of every newborn child. Mostly, however, they conceal the background or do not question it. Around ten years after the introduction of the first modern baby flaps in Germany, their shadows are shown. Every third mother who gives her child falls into depression, many become sterile. Critics doubt that young parents use the offer in panic at all, since it requires rational action. The actual clientele could possibly be won over for at least a regular adoption procedure. And no one knows how the children will react, to whom knowledge about their true descent is denied for life. (Source: Text Verlagsinband / Verlag)
content.title_en: Baby flap and anonymous birth: a critical inventory in the context of current reform proposals

content.text: The new generation of monoenergetic ion beams with a laser accelerator is presented in a more reliable way for the development of the new particle arrays, the new generation of monoenergetic ion beams with a laser accelerator. The present work is concerned with the generation of monoenergetic proton and ion beams using laser-based particle accelerators. A method was developed which allows to combine the spatial charge effects on solid-body targets with a point-like particle source. This unique interaction geometry allowed for the first time to generate proton beams with an intrinsically narrow energy spectrum with a few micrometers large laser accelerators. The experimental structure was consistently improved over the past three years in terms of reproducibility and the maximum particle energies achieved. The resulting degree of reliability allowed the determination of the first energy scale laws especially for monoenergetic proton beams. In addition, the interaction geometry could be transferred to various target materials, which enabled the generation of monoenergetic carbon beams to produce the experimentally complex development of a fully-represented particle array of observations.
content.title_en: Generation of monoenergetic ion beams with a laser accelerator

content.text: Early protection of the title of the work. Jan Görden examines when the protection of the title of the work begins under the trademark law. In particular, he addresses the question whether and under what conditions this time can be preferred by means of a title protection notice, i.e. the public announcement of the first planned title of the work. (Source: Text Verlagseinband / Verlag)
content.title_en: Early works title protection

content.text: "Theme libraries" as a cross-sparing phenomenon? : a library typological experiment. What exactly is a "theme library"? The present work provides a first definitive answer to this question. Starting from the historical emergence of theme libraries, it illuminates the character of the library's existing profiles and configuration forms as well as tasks and target groups and makes a library typological location determination. Using cross-sparing application examples, the reader is taught an idea of the diversity and heterogeneity of the "theme library" type.
content.title_en: "Theme libraries" as a cross-sparing phenomenon? : a library typological experiment

content.text: Theater as a place of utopia : the aesthetics of event and presence. In the theatre studies, the talk is persistent about the utopian function of the arts, which usually goes hand in hand with the cultural-critical topos of the negation of any representational aesthetic. Despite extensive criticism of the avant-garde concept, post-dramatic theatre and its theory are also largely linearly related to the historical avant-garde. - Miriam Drewes questions these implicit historical philosophical patterns of thought, which are connected with the terms >>events<< and >>presence< and which, considered in the history of ideas, are constructed in analogy to the mystical experience of absoluteness. - In contrast, she pleads for an understanding of >>aesthetic experience< which is committed to an anti-mystic, contextual event-concept.
content.title_en: Theatre as a place of utopia : to the aesthetics of event and presence

content.text: How to surf to work: Crowdsourcing on Web 2.0. Who surfs the Internet nowadays is increasingly asked to join ?. Users can submit a rating here, post an idea, participate in a design competition or create a logo. In sum, these working users, often without knowing it, perform value-added activities of high economic importance. This phenomenon, described as ?crowdsourcing ?, is not yet predictable in its dynamics and importance. Nevertheless, this book offers an exemplary overview of various types of crowdsourcing as well as an analysis of the origin, characteristics and effects of the young phenomenon.
content.title_en: How surfing becomes work : Crowdsourcing in Web 2.0

content.text: Interfacial thermodynamics and kinetics of solid-liquid phase transformations. In the present work, melting processes were experimentally investigated and described as a numerical model. In the experiments it was shown that a melting mechanism, i.e. local melting and re-rigidation, is responsible for the change of structure and concentration distribution. This melting mechanism shows that melting processes can also have a great influence on the structure development in metallic alloys in addition to solidification. Therefore, it is necessary to correctly describe the kinetics of both solidification and melting in order to provide quantitative statements for simulations of the formation of the structure. In the second part of this work a phase conversion model was developed and implemented, which describes the thermodynamics and kinetics of solidification and melting and thus allows quantitative descriptions of the boundary concentrations and boundary velocities.
content.title_en: Interfacial thermodynamics and kinetics of solid-liquid phase conversions

content.text: Biotope network and drainage retention in the agricultural landscape: model analysis studies using the example of the Saxon Lösshügelland. Modern agricultural landscapes are increasingly intended to fulfil ecological functions such as the preservation of biological diversity or the protection of abiotic resources. These high requirements meet in many places landscapes characterized by a decade-long decline in mule and small biotopes as well as by multiple impairments of the natural budget. Since the 1980s, it is increasingly demanded that parts of the agricultural area for natural biotope structures and for the restoration of the multiple function of the agricultural landscape are made available. The flood events that have occurred more frequently in recent years have brought down the drainage retention in the agriculturally shaped catchment areas into the field of interest. Land-building measures such as the installation of hedges or field terrain provide the possibility to combine the objectives of flood protection with other conservation objectives (e.g. erosion protection, species and biotope protection). Due to the diversity of the factors involved and their interactions (e.g. the area area, width, however, are sought by means of the nature protection.
content.title_en: Biotope network and drainage retention in the agricultural landscape : model analysis studies using the example of the Saxon Lösshügelland

content.text: Socio-economic consequences of fertility: the consequences of childbirth for the welfare of couples. This paper deals with the socio-economic consequences of childbirth. While the course and causes of the changed birth level in Germany and the influence of socio-economic determinants on individual fertility behaviour have been intensively studied in recent years, the immediate socio-economic consequences of childbirth for the affected households have not been taken into account so far. The focus of the study is on an analysis of the incomes of specific households on a longitudinal basis.
content.title_en: Socio-economic consequences of fertility: the impact of childbirth on the prosperity of couples

content.text: After-negotiation of outsourcing contracts: efficiency and flexibility in complex performance relationships. Beatrix Alexandra Ertsey determines the characteristic framework conditions for outsourcing relationships. The results are incorporated into a formal model, which uses them to derive recommendations for the design of outsourcing contracts.
content.title_en: Renegotiation of outsourcing contracts : Efficiency and flexibility in complex performance relationships

content.text: Asset Securitization in the healthcare sector: Experience in the USA and other countries as a basis for a weighing of possible applications in Germany. Asset Securitization is also increasingly perceived as a financing alternative by companies in Germany. Asset-backed securities or asset-backed securities (ABS) can be used in particular by participants in the healthcare sector for financing purposes. Ulrich Franke examines for which participants in the healthcare sector the use of ABS would be useful and how such financing could be designed. He particularly addresses the difficulties of capital market access for non-profit companies and analyses the extent to which ABS can be used as a form of financing that is of a kind of equity. The detailed experience in the USA and other countries provides the basis for discussion of various approaches in Germany. The study provides a basis for the discussion of various approaches to financing and health systems and illustrates this on the basis of case studies. Ulrich Franke addresses the difficulties of capital market access for non-profit companies in Germany and analyses the extent to which ABS can be used as a form of equity financing.
content.title_en: Asset Securitization in the health care sector : Experience in the USA and other countries as a basis for a balance of application possibilities in Germany

content.text: Threat communication: a socio-theoretical study on security and insecurity. Realism and constructivism argue for supremacy over the topic of "security" in international relations, but both blind the observer. Werner Schirmer shows that every kind of security problem presupposes an observer and develops a communication-theoretical concept of security and uncertainty based on Luhmann's system theory. Realism and constructivism argue for supremacy over the topic of 'security' in international relations, but both blind the observer. Werner Schirmer shows that every kind of security problem presupposes an observer and develops a communication-theoretical concept of security and uncertainty based on Luhmann's system theory, which bears the name 'threat communication'. Dr. Werner Schirmer received his doctorate from Prof. Dr. Armin Nassehi at Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. He works as a lecturer and researcher at the Institute for Sociology of Uppsala University in Sweden.
content.title_en: Threat communication: a societal theoretic study on security and uncertainty

content.text: Internet Self-Service in Customer Relations : Design Elements, Process Architecture and Case Studies from the Financial Services Industry. Harald Salomann presents recommendations for the design of Internet Self-Services in Customer Relations from Financial Services. He derives requirements for the planning, conception and implementation in customer-oriented processes.
content.title_en: Internet Self-Service in Customer Relations : Design Elements, Process Architecture and Case Studies from the Financial Services Industry

content.text: Everyday images of climate change: on climate awareness in Germany. She is an environmental consultant at the VERBRAUCHER INITIATIVE e.V. (Federal Association) with headquarters in Berlin. If one considers the rising carbon dioxide emissions, it becomes clear: A fundamental change towards a sustainable society with an energy balance that does not cause dangerous consequences for the natural climate system is still outstanding. A transformation of energy systems depends not only on the technical possibilities, but also and above all on the willingness to change social lifestyles. However, social change takes place in a contradictory context: constraints of action play a role here as well as incentives, infrastructure, public discourse of competing interests, habits, preferences and lifestyles. Melanie Weber investigates the question of how climate change is perceived in the population and whether and how within the institutionally shaped actions, the competing norms and everyday practices of climate consciousness.
content.title_en: Everyday images of climate change : on climate awareness in Germany

content.text: The integration potential of the Internet for migrants. The developments in modern information technologies reinforce the processes of demarcation and interdependence, which can be subsumed under the term "globalization". This also affects social structural conditions in Germany, which are simultaneously influenced by the change to an immigration society. Migrants are confronted with a reception society in which the Internet is becoming increasingly important. Here, the question arises as to what role this medium can play for migrants in integrating them into the host country. Kathrin Kissau, using the example of Jewish immigrants from the former Soviet Union, shows that the Internet can facilitate and promote their integration and social participation. Through processes of information, communication and participation migrants can be integrated into the host society with the help of the Internet and build up a new social network for themselves. Kathrin Kissau shows that the Internet can play the role of an integration engine for migrants, which facilitates and promotes their integration and social participation. Dr. Kathrin Kissau is a research assistant at the Institute of Political Science at Münster University.
content.title_en: The Internet's potential for migrants to integrate

content.text: Protest and Commitment : Where is our protest culture headed?. In order to be able to make statements about changes in the social climate, we are looking at the example of a citizen's initiative against the construction of a forensic clinic, whether the participation in such a BI means sustainable effects for the participants, especially for democratisation. What do local BIs of the type presented here cause at the social level? Can the findings gained in the research of social movements be applied profitably for these BIs? The work is also open for methodologically interested readers.
content.title_en: Protest and Commitment : Where is our protest culture heading?

content.text: Mentoring in the field of conflict between human resources development and women's promotion: a policy of equalization in the context of professional fields. Mentoring is a much propagated term in the context of company personnel development as well as in gender policy. However, the associated expectations and practices are unclear in terms of content and their gender and personnel policy effects. Manuela Kaiser-Belz investigates in the context of gender research the question whether women are enabled to "play" in previously male-dominated professional fields by equalization policies or whether these measures do not in turn help to stabilise rules and patterns that lead to the widespread exclusion of women. She explains how mentoring can help women systematically to discover these rules and patterns and ultimately change them through the positioning of female actors. With a lead words by Prof. Dr. Dr. Peter Alheit Dr. Manuela Kaiser-Belz holds a doctorate at the Chair of General Education at Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and is coordinator of the Hessen-wide mentoring programme SciMento at Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main.
content.title_en: Mentoring in the field of conflict between human resources development and women's promotion: a policy of equality in the context of professional fields

content.text: Design and implementation of innovative architectures for learning content management systems (LCMS) for use in revenue-oriented education export. The aim of this work is to systematically analyse the requirements and explain various approaches to the realization of these requirements in the use of learning content management systems (LCMS) in revenue-oriented education export. After the systematic establishment of the requirements, different LCMSs are analyzed in relation to these requirements and selected for further consideration of one of the systems. Using this system, the realization of further requirements, such as automatic data exchange, integration of multimedia and various security requirements, which were also realized as prototype and are presented in the last part of the work, is presented.
content.title_en: Design and implementation of innovative architectures for learning content management systems (LCMS) for use in revenue-oriented education export

content.text: The main changes in private life in recent decades include the increase in the importance of nonmarital life. Within this form of life, important choices are made: while some partnerships continue to strengthen through the establishment of a family and marriage, other premarital couple relationships end up in separation. The present work examines the extent to which lifestyle characteristics can provide independent explanations, which can be explained by classically used methods of living and development of nonmarital life-groups.
content.title_en: Lifestyles and development paths of nonmarital communities: an empirical analysis with the socio-economic panel

content.text: Oxidative steps in phenylphenylenone biosynthesis in Anigozanthos präisesii and Wachendorfia thyrsiflory (Haemodoraceae). The paper deals with studies on oxidative steps in the biosynthesis of phenylphenalenone of two species of the plant family of Haemodoraceae. For this purpose feeding experiments were carried out using suitable 13C-labelled precursors in an 18O2 atmosphere. In this process, the detection of the sequence of the installation of oxygen functions in different positions of phenylphenalenone was provided. NMR and MS techniques were used as analytical methods.
content.title_en: Oxidative steps in phenylphenylalenone biosynthesis in Anigozanthos präisesii and Wachendorfia thyrsiflory (Haemodoraceae)

content.text: The present work deals with the development of an adaptive load control for electric steel works. Such large consumers pay not only for the electrical energy they have received but also for the performance they have provided. The agreed performance quota is monitored over a quarter-hourly power average. The operator's requirement is to use the power quota as far as possible, and to avoid any overrun in any case. The latter is automated by so-called load control systems, which may drop load at the end of the quarter-hour interval. Previous load control systems do not take into account the special characteristics and unusual distribution of the electrical loads in the electric steel works. Therefore, when operating such a conventional plant, an optimization potential arises, which is to be tapped into the load control strategy by better integration of the process engineering processes. The central idea of the work to solve this task is the forecast of the electric arc furnace, pan furnace and the base load of the steel plant, which is expected to be used for the current electrical energy demand in the current tariff-relevant quarter-hour intervals.
content.title_en: Predictive dynamic load control for an electric steel mill

content.text: Help between generations: a European comparison. Everyday assistance between generations is of great importance for individuals, families and society - and its relevance is even increasing with demographic ageing. The study examines the following questions for eleven European countries based on the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE): Who helps whom to what extent? In what circumstances are intergenerational assistance in the family carried out? What influence do the state, market and culture have on private support between parents and adult children? How can existing potentials be used efficiently?
content.title_en: Generational assistance: a European comparison

content.text: PICA : an information system for the Landesmedienstelle in Lower Saxony?. With a view to an increasing approximation of individual specialist landscapes and the increased networking of information systems, this work deals with the question whether an application of the library automation system PICA (Project for Integrated Catalogue Automation) at the Landesmedienstelle in Lower Saxony could represent an appropriate solution to the problem of insufficient information transfer via available audiovisual media. In order to clarify the information requirements and the information deficit, a broad space is deliberately given to the demolition of the historical development of the pictorial station and the historical development of the Landesmedienstelle in Lower Saxony.
content.title_en: PICA : an information system for the state media office in Lower Saxony?

content.text: Adaptation inline microscopic methods to the monitoring and characterization of biotechnological crystallization processes. In-situ video microscope (ISVM), crystal size distribution (KGV), crystal growth, crystal morphology, lysozyme, aspirin, paracetamol
content.title_en: Adaptation inline microscopic processes to the monitoring and characterization of biotechnological crystallization processes

content.text: The compound imaging FT-IR and MALDI-TOF-MS: site-dissolving analysis of plant surfaces. Leaf waxes cover as an extreme boundary layer all surface plants and are already described for many species in terms of their morphology and composition. These waxes control the plant's water balance, act as a reaction barrier against pollutants or influence the attachment of parasites and pathogens, thereby significantly contributing to plant fitness. The aim of this work was to develop a surface analysis of combined imaging infrared spectroscopy (IR) and imaging MALDI mass spectrometry (MALDI-MS) for site-dissolving study of leaf surfaces. The combination of both analytical methods allows the examination of individual structures as well as complete substance classes, even with unknown sample composition. For this, a selective method of isolation of epicuticular growth had to be identified in the area of the leaf and a suitable sample carrier was developed. Using the developed surface analysis, the previously unknown, higher molecular ester in the epicutical monitoring of the plant surface was used for the first time to characterize the presence of the plant and the presence of the plant surface of the plant.
content.title_en: Combined Imaging FT-IR and MALDI-TOF-MS : site-dissolving analysis of plant surfaces

content.text: The competence-oriented management of the tourist destination: identification and development of cooperative core competencies. Traditional tourist destinations are under strong competitive pressure. One way to strengthen the competitiveness of these destinations is to concentrate on core competencies. However, resource- and competence-oriented approaches of strategic management have only been transferred to destinations or regional inter-organisational value creation systems in a few works. Elisabeth Fischer examines how the cooperative core competencies of the tourist destination can be identified and developed. The aim is to make the management of the core competencies operational and to expand the current perspective of the strategic management of the destination. From the perspective of the resource, competence-based and relational view, she describes the competence-building factors, the processes and the regional factors responsible for the development of cooperative core competencies, as well as the management cycle for their development. In addition, the author develops an analysis framework for the identification of cooperative core competencies, whose operationalization is empirically reviewed in the context of a study.
content.title_en: The competence-oriented management of the tourist destination : Identification and development of cooperative core competencies

content.text: The present work deals with bio-geo-chemical interactions, especially with plant stress reactions of the grass species Arrhenatherum elatius (glatthafer) and Elymus repens (quecke) in the vicinity of a former phosphate fertilizer plant. The grasses studied responded to an increasing phosphate supply in the soil with a decrease in the percentage total phosphate intake. High plant-available phosphate surpluses in the soil inhibited the growth and physiological processes of the grasses examined. Depending on the stress intensity, Cu/Zn-SOD and Mn-SOD found themselves, the content of the free amino acid Prolin increased and the intake of the essential elements of zinc, manganese and iron for plant development was hampered by very high soil phosphate levels. Studies on Phytoremediation and remediation showed that the increase in nitrogen intake from the soil did not promise to affect the soil.
content.title_en: Investigations on the influence of phosphate exposure on stress reactions of grasses at the Steudnitz site

content.text: Form, System and Psyche : on the function of the psychic system and structural coupling in system theory. This study presents a proposal for a theoretical conception of psychic systems which allows us to understand both linguistic and non-linguistic psychic experience as the autopoietic process of an operational constitution of the psychic system. Such an understanding of psychic systems is based on a reading of Luhmann's system theory, which assigns a key function in the theoretical construction to the reception of Spencer Brown's "Laws of Form" and the concepts of the psychic system and structural coupling as a supplementary theori
content.title_en: Form, System and Psyche : for the function of the psychic system and structural coupling in the system theory

content.text: The virtual structure as an information environment for planning in the inventory: for the organization and structuring of a digital building documentation. Object-oriented building models are currently the subject of extensive research activities for the computer-internal management of building-related information. An approach discussed in this context is the realization of a virtual computer-internal building in the form of a variable composite of subject-specific object-oriented models. This form of organization of the computer-internal representation is, on the one hand, very suitable for a life-phase-wide continuation as digital building acts. Such building acts form an important information basis for the planning of maintenance, modernization, reconstruction or extension measures in later phases of life of the building. On the other hand, the decentralized organization form of the model network makes it difficult to find information, which is primarily due to the presence of multiple representations of individual real-world objects as well as the complexity of the model schemes involved in the network. The subject of this work is the development of a generic system core as a basis for a project-related configurable information environment, which can provide a manageable access to the model in the context of the existing project phases.
content.title_en: The virtual building as an information environment for planning in the inventory : for the organization and structuring of a digital building documentation

content.text: A computer-based model system for the generation of urban spatial structures: a computer-based generative approach to the generation of spatial urban structures as a methodological complement to today's planning practice in urban development. The work deals with the complex task of generating urban structures with a simulation model in the computer. For this purpose, a four-level model is introduced as a submodel level in order to work with general information, parcelling, buildings and optimization of the structure.
content.title_en: A computer-based model system for the generation of urban spatial structures: a computer-based generative approach to the generation of spatial urban structures as a methodological complement to today's urban planning practice

content.text: The legitimacy of the market regime: performance and justice orientations in new forms of corporate performance policy. The once much discussed "crisis of the performance society" has not been achieved. "performance" is more than ever a central norm for social inequality and the most important evaluation principle for labor. This is currently a fundamental change in the definition of performance. In the company market regime, human effort is always less (only) important, but what meets external criteria of utilization. But if this structural change in the form of the performance principle is subjectively covered at all, can the market regime claim legitimacy for itself? In consideration of the industrial and labor-sociological discussion as well as with three theoretical traditions following Weber, Marx and Foucault, the conceptual framework of analysis is outlined first. Subsequently, the subject perspective is empirically at the center. How is the change in the valuation and remuneration principles normatively evaluated? Does a new "performance subject" emerge from the "performance subject" and "performance-related" orientations?
content.title_en: The legitimacy of the market regime : performance and equity orientations in new forms of operational performance policy

content.text: The dissertation "Investigations for the industrial use of nanometer coordinate measurement technology" shows the possibilities for solving problems arising from the large-scale use of scanning force microscopy and the use of coordinate measurement technology principles. To this end, the state of the art of production and its quality assurance in the nanometer range and the associated guideline work are presented in detail. As an example of a metrological system, the nanometer coordinate measuring machine (NCMM) is presented in detail. --- Several approaches to solving thermal problems are discussed using this device. After a comprehensive analysis of temperature behaviour, constructive measures are taken to minimize temperature input and temperature expansion and to improve heat dissipation including active regulation. Furthermore, mathematical correction methods for temperature compensation of measurement data are evaluated. --- After a modification or addition of an existing optics, algorithms for automatic sample spike approximation are implemented in both vertical and lateral direction. For this purpose, the measurement filter is also characterized by an additional optics and the measurement function is shown in the analysis of the measuring system.
content.title_en: Investigations for the industrial use of nanometer coordinate measurement technology

content.text: Material science studies of CdTe-CdS heterosolar cells. The topic of this work is the production and characterization of CdTe-CdS heterosolar cells. In a separate laboratory line, solar cells with properties according to the industry standard are first produced. By selective modification of the process, solar cells with improved properties can be achieved while reducing the absorber thickness. The deposition of the CdTe layer is investigated in the temperature range between 270 and 470ʿC. 270ʿC shows a strongly oriented growth and the occurrence of hurcite phases. A new strategy for the production of particularly thin CdTe layers using low temperature deposition is derived. Measures for the recontact formation are investigated. In the NP etching, a tellur enrichment is generated, which is quantified for the first time by Rutherford scattering measurements. Cu-Au-Mo-recontacts are particularly suitable for use in thin solar cells.
content.title_en: Material science studies on CdTe-CdS heterosolar cells

content.text: Constitutional and administrative issues concerning accreditation of courses of study. For some years now, universities have had to undergo an accreditation procedure for their newly established courses. This was introduced as a system for quality assurance in the Bologna process and initially practiced without a legal basis. In legal literature, accreditation has so far received little attention. Kerstin Wilhelm tries to close this gap and illuminates the German accreditation system from both constitutional and administrative points of view. The main focus is on the legal nature of accreditation. As a result, the author considers this to be an illegal loan and calls for the conclusion of a state contract in order to legitimise the transfer of sovereign tasks from the countries to the mostly privately-organised accreditation agencies. Constitutional concerns are expressed by the author regarding an obligation to accreditation and complains about a violation of the academic self-administration law of the universities. Their legal protection in the event of a failed accreditation are discussed as well as antitrust aspects. (Source: Verlag / Internet)
content.title_en: Constitutional and administrative issues concerning accreditation of courses of study

content.text: Zone Heimat : Altstadt im modernen Städtebau. The art-historian Vinken analyses the historic centers of Cologne and Basel, tracing how the "old towns" are a creation of modernization rare than a historic development. "Altstadt" is commonly synonymous with the authentic and historical, the heart of the city. Contrary to this assumption, art historian and urban researcher Gerhard Vinken analyses Altstadt as a product of modern urban development. He exemplifies Cologne and Basel as how old cities are designed in the modernization process as a "Zone Heimat"

content.text: The project's design methods are used by the Euro-Hendrik Bartels to implement multiple execution modes in business practice: Deconstruction planning for nuclear power plants and experimental vehicle planning in automotive development projects. Jan-Hendrik Bartels transfers models and methods of resource-restricted project planning with multiple execution modes into business practice. He presents solutions that can achieve significant savings for real problem instances. Dr. Jan-Hendrik Bartels, who received his doctorate from Prof. Dr. Jürgen Zimmermann at the Institute of Economic Science at Clausthal Technical University. In theory, a large number of models and methods of resource-restricted project planning have been developed in recent decades. However, their transfer to practice with their specific problems often poses a major challenge for many companies. Jan-Hendrik Bartels takes up existing models and methods of resource-restricted project planning and transfers them to two applications - the reconstruction planning of nuclear power plants and the planning of experimental operators in automotive development projects - to the operational practice.

content.text: Synthesis, characterization and immobilization of fluorescent sensor dyes for pH and saccharide determination. In this work water-soluble pH-sensitive naphthalimide derivatives and those for selective detection of D-fructose were presented and spectroscopically presented. The dyes showed a significant increase in the intensity of the emission at analyte contact. The pH-sensitive naphthalimide chromophore was covalently immobilized to a PEG-based hydrogel after two synthesis routes. Based on fluorescence spectroscopy of the planar substrates at different pH values, the reversibility of the sensor reaction was demonstrated by timedrive measurements. The covalent connection of the pH-sensitive dye to the hydrogel matrix succeeded in maintaining the sensor properties completely.

content.text: Geoelectric monitoring of a thermal in situ groundwater and soil remediation. This work was developed as part of a pilot-scale soil and groundwater remediation at the industrial site Hydrierwerk Zeitz. Large-scale contamination of soil and groundwater was detected on the site of a former benzene production plant. Modern exploration techniques were used to explore and narrow down the main entry areas of the dominant pollutant benzene. Various types of groundwater, soil and soil air sampling and geophysical processes allowed an exact localisation of the pollutant source area and the pollutant path to develop from it. The aim of the pilot remediation carried out at the site was to eliminate the pollutant source in order to prevent further post-shipment into the pollutant pheasants. The pollutant source area of the pilot remediation treated here was limited to a cubatur of about 15 x 9 x 11 cubic metres. The main contaminant was the concentration of 98% benzene in the centre. Furthermore, one toluol, ethylbenzene and xylene was encountered in small quantities by the high-level remediation of the radioactivity of the radioactivity of the plant.
content.title_en: Geoelectric monitoring of thermal in situ groundwater and soil restoration

content.text: Computational analysis of alternative splicing in human and mice. In the first part transcript splicing points were investigated with the aim of distinguishing alternative and reference splicing points. The results show that both classes of splicing points can be distinguished by a splicing point score and increased occurrence of splicing factor binding motifs in the vicinity of splicing points. In addition, a positive correlation between the frequency of use of certain splicing points and the splicing point score in both comparison classes could be demonstrated. This dependence implies that the accuracy of the annotation of alternative splicing variants increases with the number of observed transcripts. In the second part, the splicing signal motif GYNNGY was investigated, which accounts for more than 40% of all overlapping donor splicing signals. By means of silico analyses and experimental validation, the plausibility of this subtle splicing pattern was confirmed. The comparison with other human splicing variants and with tandem donors in mouse transcripts showed that the incidence of the splicing points was characterized by the presence of the turbits.
content.title_en: Computational analysis of alternative splicing in human and mice

content.text: The present dissertation describes the systematic transfer of the biochemical principles of the reaction of the enzyme carboanhydrase (CA) to purely chemical questions. CAs catalyze the reversible hydration of carbon dioxide and have enormous significance in a wide variety of biochemical processes in each organism. Not least due to their evolutionary age CAs belong to the enzymes with the highest alternating numbers and acceleration factors. Using suitable models for experimental implementations and quantum chemical calculations, the reaction mechanisms of allen and the heteroalene carbodiimid, ketene, ketenimin and thioketes of biomimetic zinc complexes could be clarified. The calculations of this work show, among other things, that not cyanamide, but the isomer carbodiimid is the active substrate of the mechanism-based inhibition of CA. Keten, ketenimin and thioketen can also act as inhibitors for CA, since the intensive activation of the active metabolites of the carbon dioxide is clearly investigated.
content.title_en: Allenes and heteroallenes as substrates of zinc-mediated biomimetic addition reactions

content.text: Novel multi-functional ligands based on 4H imidazoles and their metal complexes. The aim of this work was to establish the class of 4H imidazoles 1 as multifunctional ligands for metal complexes. To achieve this, known 4H imidazoles were first tested in complexing reactions and easily accessible bis-4H imidazoles were investigated in relation to selective complexation. To synthesize novel functionalized 4H imidazoles, known synthesis pathways were optimized for the construction of 4H imidazoles and established for a larger number of eductes. Sterically sophisticated 4H imidazoles were synthesized to investigate the influence of the Ar2 residual on chromophore and complex formation properties. Based on functionally functionally modified educts, the possibility of building unsymmetric bis-4H imidazoles was subsequently tested. Functionalized 4H imidazoles pd(II) and bipy/terpy/ruII complexes were developed into a second class of metal-aluminium-based ligand complexes.
content.title_en: Novel multifunctional ligands based on 4H imidazoles and their metal complexes

content.text: Axiomatic digital geometry and the Jordan-Brouwer set. This text provides a possible answer to the question raised by T.Y. Here, the discrete geometries investigated by Albrecht Hübler in [10] are generalized, a general concept of a (n-1)-dimensional digital manifold in a discrete geometry of dimensions n is introduced and this manifoldness is transformed into a simplicitial complex. The result of the work is that every digital manifold among a good pair defines a simplicitial complex whose geometric realization meets the set of Jordan Brouwer. This is answered positively by Kong.
content.title_en: Axiomatic digital geometry and the set of Jordan Brouwer

content.text: In order to influence the diaphragm-reducing additives and active substances on autogenic shrinkage and other properties of cement stone. Since the early 1980s, additional agents (SRI) and active substances contained in them have been systematically investigated in the construction chemical industry, which can reduce the shrinkage of cement stone and concrete. In the present work, the mechanisms of the diaphragm-reducing additives (SRA) and the active substances contained in them have been systematically investigated in cement stone. It has been shown that the autogenous shrinkage of cement stone has been reduced by commercial shrinkage and active substances contained in it by up to 77% in the age of half a year. In relation to the respective reference samples without SRI, the proportion of gel pores in the cement stone has been increased and the proportions of capillary pores reduced. At the same time, the cement stones with shrinkage reducers or the active substances contained in them have been treated with a higher internal compensation moisture when stored in a preserved manner than in the respective reference samples without SRA. ...
content.title_en: To influence diaphragm reducing additives and active substances on autogenous shrinkage and other properties of cement stone

content.text: The synthesis and characterization of new trifluoroacetyl functionalized chromoreactands for the optical detection of aliphatic amines. In the context of this work, new trifluoroacetyl functionalized chromoreactands were produced, which are able to detect aliphatic amines and thereby generate an optical signal in the form of a color change. The trifluoroacetyl group has been able to produce both stylbenoid compounds and compounds with tolan base framework and respective terminal trifluoroacetyl groups via palladium catalysed coupling reactions. In the new chromoreactands, the trifluoroacetyl group serves as a receptor unit for amines. Due to the interaction of the trifluoroacetyl group with amines, hemiamines are formed in a reversible reaction and under the formation of a covalent binding. The resulting changes in electron delocalization in the conjugated systems result in a shift of the absorption and emission maxima of the sensor dyes in the short-wave spectrum of the chromo-relation and thus in the chromo-re-relation of the chromo-re-reactions.
content.title_en: Synthesis and characterization of new trifluoroacetyl functionalized chromoreactands for the optical detection of aliphatic amines
