content.text: Photocatalytic coating systems for highly transparent self-cleaning glass. The aim of this work was to produce self-cleaning layer systems with high transmission in the wavelength range from 380 to 800 nm on float glass using reactive DC sputtering. At first, extensive investigations were carried out on photocatalytically active titanium oxide layers. The influence of layer thickness, sputter pressure and partial pressure ratio as well as the effects of subsequent temperature control on the structure and properties of SiO2-TiO2 layer systems were investigated. Furthermore, the study of photocatalytically active interference systems based on TiO2 was carried out. To this end, SiO2-TiO2-SnO2 layer systems were separated and the influence of layer thicknesses of titanium oxide and tin oxide layer as well as the sputter pressure used for the separation and a subsequent temperature control step on the properties of the layer systems were investigated.
content.title_en: Photocatalytic layer systems for high-transparent self-cleaning glasses

content.text: From initial calculation of the interaction potentials of helium, neon and methane, as well as theoretical investigations of their thermophysical properties and those of water vapour. Thermophysical properties of the gases helium, neon, methane and water vapour were calculated over wide temperature ranges. For the determination of transport and relaxation properties, the kinetic gas theory was used, which was previously limited to linear molecules and was extended to nonlinear molecules for the calculations of methane and water vapour. The required interaction potentials were determined for helium, neon and methane with quantum chemical methods from initial and for water from the writing. The calculated values for thermophysical properties are very well in line with the best experimental data.
content.title_en: From initial calculation of the interaction potentials of helium, neon and methane as well as theoretical investigations of their thermophysical properties and those of water vapour

content.text: Synthesis of fluorinated natural material analogues, polyketide-like phenols and methylthiophenols by reactions of 1,3-bis(trimethylsilyloxy)-1,3-butadienes with dielectrophils. In this dissertation, the focus is on the expansion of the synthesis potential of 1,3-bis(silyleneol ethers) in cyclosizing reactions. In this thesis, 1,3-bis(silyleneolethers) in [3+3] cyclosizing reactions with different dielectrophiles to novel functionalized phenols were implemented. By variation of dielectrophils fluorinated, polyketide-like and methylthiophenols were presented in very good chemo- and regio-selectivity. A great focus has been placed on the clarification of the constitution of the preserved compounds with the help of 13C- and 2D-NMR.
content.title_en: Synthesis of fluorinated natural material analogues, polyketide-like phenols and methylthiophenols by reaction of 1,3-bis(trimethylsilyloxy)-1,3-butadienes with dielectrophils

content.text: The use of a novel peroxidase from the Basidiomyceten Agrocybe aegerita using the example of enantioselective sulfoxidation. The novel Agrocybe aegerita peroxidase (AaP) was successfully characterized and established as an enantioselective biocatalyst in the synthesis of optically active sulfoxides. The (R) enantiomer is produced in the high surplus (ee value > 99%). The high potential of the AaP for use in industrial biocatalysis was confirmed by the use of organic solvents, by the immobilization of the enzyme and the stability against its cosubstrate.
content.title_en: The use of a novel peroxidase from the Basidiomyceten Agrocybe aegerita using the example of enantioselective sulfoxidation

content.text: Microbial community metabolic concurrence involved in toluene degradation: effect of oxygen availability on catabolic gene expression of aerobic and anaerobic toluene degradation bacteria are permanently confronted with varying oxygen gradients in their natural environment, such as in aquifers, microbial mats and in the root space of plants, the rhizosphere. Pollutant-degrading microorganisms have also developed the ability to adapt to the constantly changing environmental conditions of contaminated sites with the help of adaptive mechanisms and the regulation of their catabolic genes. In this work, the relative expression of catabolic genes under oscillating oxygen concentrations of two pollutant-degrading bacteria, the aerobic toluene-abbauer, Pseudomonas putida mt-2 (which contains TOL Plasmid pWW0), and the anaerobic toluene-absorber were investigated by Taueroma and Tauera aroma.

content.text: The liability test is an effective tool for the application of the liability test. Alexandra Scholz examines the extent to which the distribution regimes of Germany, England and the USA prevent opportunistic distributions which damage the creditor. The results are used by the author to derive design recommendations for a liquidity-oriented solvency test and discuss supporting instruments. Dr. Alexandra Scholz obtained his doctorate at the Institute for Corporate Accounting and Taxation at the University of Münster. The liability test of German capital companies has traditionally been interwoven with special capital raising and maintenance regulations. In particular, however, the capital retention, which determines the amount available for distribution, has come under pressure both in the past years and in the last years. A possible liquidity-oriented solvency test is therefore increasingly at the center of the discussion. Alexandra Scholz investigates the extent to which the distribution regime of Germany, England and the USA has been subject to opportunistic distributions which damage the creditor. A possible liquidity-oriented solvency test is therefore increasingly used as a tool for the application of the liability test.
content.title_en: Capital conservation through solvency tests: an economic and experimental analysis

content.text: Active galaxy nuclei and their luminosity function depend on the cosmological description. The first part of the work discusses a Monte Carlo method based on extended-press-spechter formalism for the generation of the fusion histories of Halo's dark matter. This is used to investigate the influence of different cosmological descriptions on the fusion probabilities of galaxies. From this their effect on the luminosity function of active galaxy nuclei is derived. It can be seen that a change in the cosmology used essentially affects the temporal position and expansion of the luminosity function. A new model for the description of active galaxy nuclei is also presented, which is for the first time consistently capable of transporting gas from galactic scale to the accretion of the central black-diametered micro-diameter is achieved by a new model for active galaxy nuclei.

content.text: Process-based and spatially distributed modelling of soil nitrogen flows to estimate the effects of climate change on nitrogen availability and nitrate leaching in the Upper Danube basin: Development, validation and application of a component of the DANUBIA integrative decision-making support system. In the context of the Global Change, spatial and temporal information on nitrogen availability in the soil and nitrate leaching are crucial for the development of measures for the integrated management of (basic) water resources. As part of the GLOWA-Danube project, this work examines the reactions of soil nitrogen budgets to climate change in the Upper Danube basin. As a component of the DANUBIA integrative decision-making support system, the object-oriented and process-based soil nitrogen model SNT was developed on the basis of the CERES Maize 2.0 model. SNT is the most important processes (minerization/immobilisation, denitrification, nitrification, urea hydrolysis and nitrate deposition) and the dynamics of two mineral (nitrate and ammonium) as well as two organic (fresh biomass and humus) nitrogen reserves were determined in the soil by means of a multi-scale analysis of the parameter.
content.title_en: Process-based and spatially distributed modelling of soil nitrogen flows to assess the impact of climate change on nitrogen availability and nitrate leaching in the Upper Danube basin: Development, validation and application of a component of the DANUBIA integrative decision-making support system

content.text: The virtual product development is an answer to the question of a fast and cost-optimized product formation process. The vehicle lighting is developed and secured with virtual techniques. In addition to the legal standards for the distribution of light intensity, the appearance in the night situation must also be virtually evaluable. For the evaluation of the night appearance, the determination of the luminance distribution of luminaires for lighting purposes is necessary. For this purpose, the previously established simulation process is analysed and the existing methods for the suitability for the luminance determination are examined. This results in the necessity to develop new methods for the processing of light fields for virtual protection. The result of this work are two newly developed methods, the 4D full histogram and the 4D core density estimate. These methods enable the luminance estimation from simulated photons of the area light field. The histogram approach is based on an apriori discretization of the location direction space and evaluates the complete light field. The core density estimate is based on the k-negative development of the luminescent method.

content.text: Real-time investigations of ferroelectric phase transformations in K2SeO4 and SrTiO3 under the influence of an electric field. In ferroelectric functional materials, switching behaviour plays a decisive role in the use of the electrical field as storage media and is therefore a current topic of basic research. In the context of this work, potassium-selenate and strontium-titanate were investigated as model systems of ferroelectric crystals. The kinetics of the field-induced phase conversions could be observed with stroboscopy scattering methods on a millisecond time scale.
content.title_en: Real-time investigations of ferroelectric phase transformations in K2SeO4 and SrTiO3 under the influence of an electric field

content.text: Cohomology vanishing and exceptional sequences. The subject of this work is the study of the cohomology decline of invertable sheaves on toric varieties and their application to the construction of strictly exceptional consequences on toric and general rational surfaces. The work consists of three parts. In the first part a counter-example is given to a conjecture of A. King, which states that on each toric variety there exists a strictly exceptional sequence of invertable sheaves. In the second part the cohomology decline of invertable sheaves on toric varieties is generally examined from a combinatorial and arithmetical point of view. The third part deals with exceptional consequences of invertible sheaves on general rational surfaces.
content.title_en: Cohomology vanishing and exceptional sequences

content.text: Studies of C-F binding activations and fluoride effects in chiral-substituted metallocenes of the fourth group. The present work deals with the activation of CF and MF bindings within the metallocene chemistry of the fourth subgroup. A realization of the transition-free CF binding activation in non-activated CF bindings is described. In addition, a strong focus is on the examination of menthyl-substituted metallocene, wherein in this context the synthesis of novel chiral-substituted compounds is reported. These complexes are subjected to a comparison of their spectroscopic and structural data as well as their reaction behavior.
content.title_en: Investigations of C-F binding activations and fluoride effects in chiral-substituted metallocenes of the fourth group

content.text: Digital analysis of the accuracy and quality of the collection and presentation of old maps from Mecklenburg-Vorpommern : presented at the maps of Wiebeking (ca. 1786) and Schmettau (ca. 1788). Starting with the possibilities of digital data collection of analog cartographic works and their possible necessary digital restoration, methods for integrating old maps into geoinformation systems are presented. Within this core point, the qualitative aspect of metric accuracy is simultaneously addressed together with an appropriate representation. In addition to this quality criterion, the maps are illuminated from the perspective of topographic and cartographic properties.
content.title_en: Digital analysis of the accuracy and the quality of the collection and presentation of old maps from Mecklenburg-Vorpommern : shown at the maps of Wiebeking (ca. 1786) and Schmettau (ca. 1788)

content.text: Network Football : a power psychological analysis of the role of the Bundesliga in the sphere of influence of the mass media. The network football has four essential elements with a view to the Bundesliga. In addition to football as a starting point, the recipients as target persons, the mass media as a distribution channel and the economy as financial provider complete a social network of different wishes, influence and power structures. The empirically determined results prove that the mass media as a reality staging channel are able to influence the behavior of the surveyed football professionals at the micro level and at the macro level of the overall network.
content.title_en: Network Football : a power psychological analysis on the role of the Bundesliga in the field of influence of the mass media

content.text: Synthesis, structures and properties of new niobium clusters. The halogenidoligates of the solid-chemically obtained niobium clusters A4[Nb6Cl18] (A=K,Na,Rb) can be substituted in a variety of ways. In order to improve the solubility of niobium clusters in organic solvents, ligand substitution reactions were performed. In the context of this work, 30 new niobium clusters were synthesized. These were characterized with the help of single-crystal X-ray structure analysis and investigated using IR, Raman and UV/Vis spectroscopic methods.
content.title_en: Synthesis, structures and properties of new niobium clusters

content.text: Empirical impact analysis of direct transfers - using the example of agri-environmental measures and compensatory allowance for disadvantaged areas. In this paper, the individual effects of two agricultural policy programmes (agri-environmental measures, compensatory allowance for disadvantaged areas) are examined on the farm factor input (soil, labour, capital, stocking, livestock density, expenditure on crop protection and fertiliser per hectare), production (turnover) and the extra-farm labour force participation of the farm manager pair. The analysis is based on a non-representative sample of over 20,000 German bookkeeping holdings over the period 2000 to 2005. A semi-parametric matching approach (propensity score matching) and various parametric panel models are used for empirical analysis ...
content.title_en: Empirical impact analysis of direct transfers - using agri-environmental measures as an example and compensatory allowance for disadvantaged areas

content.text: Experimental planning in public spaces. Experimental planning is becoming increasingly important in view of the economic and ecological crisis as well as the social change. What can planning experiments in urban areas and the landscape do to find new solutions? Can architecture be used temporarily? And what role do solutions developed in processes play in the appropriation and use of open spaces? Even for the spatial-designing disciplines, previously practiced planning and design processes must be questioned and rethought.
content.title_en: Experimental planning in public space

content.text: A new piece of Paris: planning discourses, references and the formation of an urban image in the large urban project Paris Rive Gauche. The work deals with the discursive construction of urban images in large projects. Based on a sociological definition of the terms "space image" and "location image", the example of the large urban project Paris Rive Gauche examines how site-specific references form in a planning process, for which purposes they are used and how these references are used to create an image for a developing district in the planning process.
content.title_en: A new piece of Paris: Planning discourses, references and the formation of an urban image in the Paris Rive Gauche urban project

content.text: Urban districts on time: Quality of life in shrinking cities. The population of Germany is shrinking and aging. In an increasing number of municipalities, the erosion of the structural and social environment meets an older population, whose quality of life is particularly important for stability and continuity. Based on theoretical models of ecological gerontology and a broad data base from their own empirical surveys in Hoyerswerda and Wolfen, Andreas Peter analyses the multi-layered human-environment relationship in old age under the conditions of shrinking and urban conversion. Practical and transferable orientation options are derived for various local actors, which can help to minimize risks for the quality of life in old age. Furthermore, he discusses the challenges and perspectives for spatial-related age research as a result of demographic change and makes it clear that urban development concepts are to be limited to urban development, (communal)politics and housing economics.
content.title_en: Urban neighbourhoods on time : Quality of life in shrinking cities

content.text: Studies on oxidative stress in dogs with special consideration of liver diseases. Dog, liver, oxidative stress, dog liver, oxidative stress. - The present study aimed to investigate possible changes in lipid peroxidation (LPO) and oxidative stress in dogs with liver diseases compared to dogs with other soft tissue diseases and healthy dogs. Furthermore, the influence of anaesthesia on LPO and oxidative stress measurements was investigated in methodological preliminary tests.The results of the following experimental groups were included in the study: liver diseased dogs (n=29), dogs with cross-band crack (n=8), moth disease (n=9) and healthy control animals (n=32).
content.title_en: Studies on oxidative stress in dogs, with special attention to liver disorders

content.text: Flexibility and specificity in protein protein interactions using the example of complexing of Trypsin variants and the protease inhibitor Eglin C. Variants of bovine trypsin, developed to emulate the binding properties of inhibitors of factor Xa, a central enzyme of blood clotting, were investigated using NMR spectroscopy and DSC. Furthermore, complexes of these variants and macromolecular protease inhibitor Eglin C were produced. These protein complexes were then investigated using ITC and X-ray crystal structure analysis. The results obtained show, among other things, that the observed different binding affinities and the dehalpic and entropic contributions to the binding of Eglin C to the trypsin variants with structural changes in two loops in the ligandibular pockets of the trypsin variants are correlating. These data are consistent with previous studies on low-molekular inhibitors of the gerandiol enzyme enzyme.
content.title_en: Flexibility and specificity in protein-protein interactions, using the example of complexing of trypsin variants and the protease inhibitor Eglin C

content.text: Development, implementation and validation of a practical method for the determination of biogas and methane yields. This work has enabled a method to be developed based on the VDI 4630, which provides practical and reproducible results of biogas yields from solids. The investigations show that different methods (theoretical and practical) for the determination of biogas yields lead to results of different quality. Currently, no correlation can be assumed between the results of the tested theoretical models and the results of the practical determination.
content.title_en: Development, implementation and validation of a practical process for the determination of biogas and methane yields

content.text: The implementation of a business-based CAQ system is not yet proven by the example of integration of the CAQ system, but the implementation of the QMS and the application of the QMS system. The survey shows that only very few small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have been able to implement the QMS system because of their limited resources and the dominance of the production planning and control systems (PPS) and that the quality management tools are being used in an adequate manner. Therefore, the theoretical concept of an office-based software architecture for CAQ systems is developed, that it allows to use existing software products in the company and to combine them into a more efficient, flexible software solution based on the client server principle. By using different standard interfaces, integration with other business applications is made easier to use, the exchangeability and expandability of individual software components and finally to achieve independence from different software providers.
content.title_en: Office-based CAQ systems : using the example of integration of test planning, FMEA and complaint management

content.text: The rear light can be used for the purpose of adjusting the light signals to variable visual conditions. The rear signal image of motor vehicles transmits relevant information about their own driving behaviour to the following traffic. However, the perceptibility of the light signals with constant light intensity is influenced differently by varying visual conditions. In the context of this work it is shown that for optimal detection the signal light density must be regulated primarily depending on the adaptation light density in the road traffic space. To describe the different adaptation conditions numerous location-resolving luminance measurements from the driver's point of view were carried out in different daylight and weather conditions as well as geographical conditions. On the basis of this data collection, an important basic investigations were carried out which enabled an assignment of almost all the apparent light density distributions. This classification of the environmental conditions was at the same time the basis for the development of a plant for daylight simulation. The realistic reproduction of ambient light density and sunlight-like illumination strengths were currently presented in the field light tests.
content.title_en: Development of an intelligent rear light for adaptive adjustment of the light signals to variable visual conditions

content.text: Color image generation by means of computer generated holograms. The projection of monochromatic, two-dimensional images by means of computer generated holograms (CGH) is a known method which has several single-pointed advantages (shrink depth, adjustment tolerance, high efficiency, simplicity of construction). The aim of the work is to extend this type of projection to multi-coloured images while preserving the specific advantages. Three different approaches are theoretically investigated and experimentally realized. In the first approach, a combination of wavelength selective dielectric layer mirrors and reflective CGH develops a stacked element that allows independent influence of the three basic colors red, green and blue, whereby an almost identical source point of the color portions can be achieved and thus the depth of focus is completely preserved. In the second approach, which is characterized by great simplicity, the dispersion of the basic colors is used to generate a color image by means of an ordinary monochromatic CGH in an off-axis structure. In the third approach, the concept of CGH is arranged to several light angles, in a short distance of the multi-levels.
content.title_en: Color image production by computer generated holograms

content.text: New building blocks for molecular spintronics. In this work, the three general steps in the construction of new materials from functional building blocks are traced by examples. In detail, this is the linking of known functional elements and the identification of structural elements of new functions, the presentation of functional building blocks with links and the linking of the building blocks and the proof that the function is not lost. The synthesis of new building blocks is also in the focus, as is the extensive analysis of preserved compounds. Two new ligand scaffolds are described, which contain highly functional triphenylamine units. Furthermore, the connection on the basis of triaminobences, triaminoguanidine, mesal-like ligands and acetylsubstituted phyloglucin are examined and carefully characterized with regard to their magnetic properties. The obtained results could be successfully transferred to other material classes: The magnetic anomaly, as found in connections based on triamineobents, could be successfully integrated into carbazol compounds.
content.title_en: New building blocks for molecular spintronics

content.text: Focusing on ultrashort laser pulses. Motivated by the rapidly growing number of applications of micro-material processing with ultrashort laser pulses, the present work deals with the interaction of focused ultrashort laser pulses with silica glass, which was selected as an exemplary dielectric. The first is examined here the spatial-temporal distortions of aberrated laser pulses with additional consideration of an intensity-dependent refractive index. On the other hand, the electron plasma resulting from the focusing in the material is calculated and the interaction of the laser pulse with this. This is followed by the comparison of the electron density distributions with experimentally generated structures in silica glass. An important basis of the numerical simulations of the nonlinear interaction of focused laser pulses is the precise knowledge of the spatial-temporal distortion of the pulse fronts by the optical system used (real) in order to achieve this objectively improved measurement method, with the aim of achieving a higher rate of resolution in the first time.
content.title_en: Focusing ultrashort laser pulses

content.text: Molecular formula identification using high resolution mass spectrometry : algorithms and applications in metabolomics and proteomics. We investigate several theoretical and practical aspects of the identification of the sum formula of biomolecules using high-resolution mass spectrometry. Through the last advances in instrumentation, mass spectrometry (MS) has become one of the key technologies for the analysis of biomolecules in proteomics and metabolomics. It measures the masses of molecules in the sample with high accuracy, and is well suited for the measurement data acquisition in high throughput. One of the core tasks in MS-based proteomics and metabolomics is the identification of molecules in the sample. In the metabolites are subject to metabolites of structure enlightenment, starting with the sum formula of a molecule, i.e. the number of atoms of each element are identified. This is the decisive step in the identification of an unknown metabolite, since the determined formula can be reduced to a much smaller quantity of molecular structures, the number of molecular pre-processing methods.
content.title_en: Molecular formula identification using high resolution mass spectrometry : algorithms and applications in metabolomics and proteomics

content.text: Competence commitment: a way to integrate unemployed people into society. Empirical study on the acquisition and civil society. Dr. Rosine Schulz interrupted her professional activity for several years within an international economic group and received his doctorate on the current research topic at the Faculty of Philosophy of the University of Münster. The current debates on the future of the employment and civil society are synergetically related to each other in this book. Rosine Schulz pursues the goal of exploring the practical significance of the respective developed integration potentials with regard to the social group of unemployed. The results of this empirical study show that the competence commitment has parallels with the experiences of the employment work and can serve as a bridge function in the first labour market. The book is aimed at lecturers and students of the social sciences with the focus on work and educational sociology and to political scientists as well as representatives of labour market and social policy, third sector organisations and workers' associations, especially trade unions.
content.title_en: Skills commitment: a way to integrate unemployed people into society. Empirical study on the occupation and civil society

content.text: Mobility-related attitudes in transition from child to youth: cross-cutting age comparisons among 14 to 16-year-olds. The transition from child to youth includes many changes and new degrees of freedom in almost all areas of life. Many reasons are that important attitudes and values related to mobility are formed, especially in early adolescence, which are subsequently also taken over into (auto)mobility and where behaviour plays a decisive role. An accelerated and rapidly changing process of change is taking place at this age level. Based on parallel surveys in three classes, Thomas Bastian examines differential differences in the age groups of 14 to 16-year-olds. The findings gained contribute to identifying and caring for young people who deliberately anticipate the introduction to automobiles at risk, early on. The book addresses lecturers and students of transport sciences, development psychology and sociology as well as practitioners in these areas, especially police officers.
content.title_en: Mobility-related attitudes in transition from child to youth : cross-cutting age comparisons among 14 to 16-year-olds

content.text: Principles of regular loss write-downs: Objectification concepts of loss anticipation through off-plan depreciation according to GoB and IFRS. In relation to the individual principles of off-plan depreciation according to GoB and IFRS, there are significant differences in both conceptual and manifestations. In particular, there is no uniform interpretation of these special principles of anticipation of future losses in case law and literature. Marc Weindel systematically examines the different objectification concepts of loss anticipation through off-plan depreciation in active assets according to GoB and IFRS. Based on an analysis of the underlying loss concept, he works out that the deviating accentuation of general loss anticipation principles decisively determines the concrete design of the loss write-down principles. Depending on the nature of the income statement, he develops a concrete framework for unplanned depreciation of inventories held for sale and for further use, and acknowledges the assets components that exist in relation to loss objectivisation in both accounting systems.
content.title_en: Principles of regular loss write-downs : Objectification concepts of loss anticipation by non-scheduled write-downs according to GoB and IFRS

content.text: Novel synthesis and reaction of functionalised 3.5-diketoester and 2.4-diketosulfone : synthesis and structure elucidation of cyclopropyl and permethyl polyketides. 1,3,5-tricarbonyl compounds and 2,4-diketosulfone were represented by condensation of 1,3-bis(silyleneol ethers) with functionalized acid chlorides under mild conditions. The reaction of 1-methoxy-1,3-bis(silyloxy)-1,3-butadiene with 2-methoxyarylcarboxylic acid chlorides and 2-nitroarylcarboxylic acid chlorides resulted in 3,5-diketoesters, which were transferred to functionalised 2-hydroxychroman-4-one or chromone or 4-hydroxyquinolins. The first open chain symmetrical and unsymmetric cyclopropyl and permethyl oligoketides were presented and their conformations investigated.
content.title_en: Novel synthesis and reaction of functionalised 3.5-diketoester and 2.4-diketosulfone : synthesis and structure elucidation of cyclopropyl and permethyl polyketides

content.text: Design and analysis of beam forming systems of high numerical aperture. The production of tailor-made light is today the focus of many innovative applications. One possibility of flexible manipulation of light is laser beam forming. The aim is to transform the intensity profile of a laser beam into a desired profile. The focus of this work is the modelling and propagation of laser light in paraxial and non-paraxial beam forming systems as well as the optimization of these systems by means of a generalized projection algorithm. This algorithm is used to optimize pointwise, by means of asphere formula or polynomial parametrized beam forming surfaces. It is shown that during optimization consideration of bending, interference and aberrations is possible. The latter can be used not only for the purpose of the optimization, but also for the purpose of beam forming. Finally, it is shown that the aberrations of spherical catalog lenses are already sufficient for some beam forming applications. The effectiveness of the developed optimization algorithm is demonstrated both on paraaxial and non-paraxial beam forming examples with a numeric aptur from 0.6 to 0.6.
content.title_en: Design and analysis of beam forming systems of high numerical aperture

content.text: The dynamics of the laser-induced metal semiconductor phase transition of samarium sulfide (SmS). This work is dedicated to the experimental investigation of the metal semiconductor phase transition of samarium sulfide (SmS). Temperature and time-resolved experiments for characterizing the phase transition of mixed-valent SmS samples (M-SmS) are presented. The measurement of the dynamics of the laser-induced phase transition is performed by time-resolved ultrashort-term microscopy and by X-ray diffraction with subpicoseconds of time resolution. The electronic and structural processes, which follow an excitation of M-SmS with infrared femtosecond laser pulses, are interpreted physically on the basis of the results and model concepts obtained in this work.
content.title_en: The dynamics of the laser-induced metal-semiconductor phase transition of samarium sulfide (SmS)

content.text: Ion beam-enhanced etching for the 3D structuring of lithium niobate. The present work deals with the utilization of ion beam-enhanced etching (IBEE: Ion Beam Enhanced Etching) for the 3D structuring of lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Here the approach of increasing the wet chemical etching rate due to irradiation with energy-rich ions is pursued. This method is very promising for the realization of micro- and nanostructures with vertical structural walls and low roughness. The aim of this work was to form the basis for the realization of three-dimensional micro- and nanostructures (e.g. layer systems and photonic crystals) in LiNbO3 with high optical quality and to demonstrate on selected examples. Prerequisites for the success of the IBEE structuring technique is primarily the understanding of defect formation under ion radiation as well as the radiation-induced structural changes in the crystal and the associated change in chemical resistance. Here, defect formation in relation to ion radiation and radiation in the ion mass must be studied.
content.title_en: Ion beam reinforced etching for 3D structuring of lithium niobate

content.text: Pocket library: library services for smartphones; Innovation Award 2010. Mobile devices, such as the Apple iPhone, Google G1 and other smartphones, are becoming increasingly popular worldwide due to increased bandwidth and usability. They combine the functions of a computer, audio players, cameras and mobile phones. In connection with these new technologies, mobile use of the Internet is dramatically increasing and also poses the challenge to libraries to embed their services in virtual environments and to offer content and services to mobile users. Mobile technology can be used for various library services: mobile interfaces, localization services, multi-media guides and SMS notifications. While in Germany mobile services in libraries play an even minor role, US libraries already use a wide range of services. This work is intended to illustrate, after an introduction to the topic, using selected practical examples, which of the mobile services are already offered by libraries in the US and Germany. In addition, an email survey and various usability tests have been carried out and the services offered evaluated.
content.title_en: Pocket library : library services for smartphones ; Innovation Award 2010

content.text: Methods and tools for the performance measurement, analysis and evaluation of input/output units of computing systems. Studies show that the computing power of processors increases more than the input/output power of secondary storage. This leads to CPUs often not exhausting their computing potential as they wait for secondary storage data. To avoid these waiting times, the performance analysis and optimization of the memory is necessary. I/O benchmarks are software tools for performance analysis, whose problems are shown and solved in this work. An approach is developed that enables realistic, comparable and simple I/O benchmarking with the MPI-IO interface.
content.title_en: Procedures and tools for the measurement, analysis and evaluation of input/output units of computing systems

content.text: Compact antenna arrays in mobile communications: a quantitative analysis of radio coupler. However, in order to meet the ongoing demand for higher transmission rates and greater mobility, modern mobile communications systems increasingly use adaptive group antennas. However, if beam elements are closely combined to accommodate small portable devices (e.g. mobile phones), coupling effects of their radiation characteristics are affected. In order to describe these impairments in comparison to the usual viewing methods more clearly, the present work extends the known efficiency concept of an individual antenna to any antenna group by introducing orthogonal radiation freedom degrees. The effects of beam coupling are shown by examples. Adapt and decoupling networks can counteract beam coupling. For a broad class of ntennen groups a systematic design guideline is presented and confirmed by numerous examples, whereby Ohm's network losses and narrow bandwidths are shown as general main weaknesses of such networks. To investigate the influence of beam coupling on the transmission of radio spectrum a comprehensive spectrum of spectrum is discussed.
content.title_en: Compact antenna arrays in mobile communications : a quantitative analysis of radiator coupling

content.text: Design and production of a planar integrated micromass spectrometer with micro-channel plate detector. The work described describes the development of a micromass spectrometer in microsystem technology. All components of the mass spectrometer planar are manufactured on a 7 x 10 mm2 chip made of glass and silicon. This work focuses on the process development of the processes necessary for the production as well as the use of a mico-channel plate (MCP) in a self-calibrating bracket etched from silicon. This work describes the development of a micro-mass spectrometer with the methods of microsystem technologies. All components of the mass spectrometer are combined in a planar design of a 7 x 10 mm2 chip fabricated out of glass and silicon. This work focuses on the development of the MEMS factory and on the operation of a micro-channel-plate (MCPsilicon) in a silicon.

content.text: For diagnosis and integrated control of wood-destructive insects, with special consideration of the color beetles (Coleoptera, Cleridae) as their natural opponents in historical buildings. Paper-gluing and adhesive traps are suitable instruments for monitoring pests and beneficials in wood protection. Synanthropic color beetles are important predators of the rodent beetles. The color beetle larvae accepted replacement yield, but a mass increase of the clerides was not possible. In fumigation with sulfuryl difluoride, larvae of Korynetes caeruleus showed no higher resistance than that of Anobium punctatum. content.text: Concepts and operating strategies for the use of rapeseed oils in combustion engines for use in agricultural machinery. content.text: The analysis of fiscal consolidation and reform processes: determinants, consolidation profiles and reform strategies in the analysis. The consolidation of public finances is a constant challenge for governments. Economic crises burden households in regular cycles, and politicians are afraid of elemental punishment for tax increases and spending cuts. content.text: The dynamics of the laser-induced metal semiconductor phase transition of samarium sulfide (SmS). This work is dedicated to the experimental investigation of the metal semiconductor phase transition of samarium sulfide (SmS). Temperature and time-resolved experiments for characterizing the phase transition of mixed-valent SmS samples (M-SmS) are presented. The measurement of the dynamics of the laser-induced phase transition is performed by time-resolved ultrashort-term microscopy and by X-ray diffraction with subpicoseconds of time resolution. The electronic and structural processes, which follow an excitation of M-SmS with infrared femtosecond laser pulses, are interpreted physically on the basis of the results and model concepts obtained in this work.

content.text: The life of light generated charge carriers in silicon is an important quality criterion of silicon. It has a significant influence on the efficiency of a crystalline silicon solar cell. In the present work, the factors affecting the charge carrier life in crystalline silicon used for the production of solar cells are analysed in detail and compared with quasi-stationary photoconductivity (QSSPC) life-time measurements. A new time-resolved evaluation method of the MWPCD signal is developed and used for the characterization of silicon. With the help of this process, the interstitial iron content is determined and the influence of minority charge carriers is investigated.Another focus of this work is on the investigation and characterization of the silicon used for the production of solar cells. The interstitial iron content is determined locally and the influence of minority charge carriers is strongly analyzed in the silicon cell quality of the silicon cell.
content.title_en: Investigations on the charge carrier life in crystalline silicon for solar cells

content.text: European states in competition: on the transformation of gender regimes in the context of the EU. Since the outbreak of the economic crisis, questions about the changes in the relationship between politics and economy and/or the transformations of statehood have been on the agenda. The study provides a basic presentation of the prehistory of the current political-economic crisis. In critical discussions with materialistic and feminist theories on the change of statehood in the context of internationalization and Europeanization, the book presents a gender-sensitive analysis of the post-Fordist competition rule. Genetti's central thesis is that, due to contradictory effects on the existing gender regimes and regimes, gender-ambivalent competition rule is developed. This is a deeply contradictory process characterized by static and dynamic tendencies in the social structuring and political organisation of gender relations and by inconsistent gender policies on various political scales. This is shown by the author's example of gender policy in the EU's research and science field. (HoF/Text adopted)
content.title_en: European States in competition: on the transformation of gender systems in the context of the EU

content.text: Development of a biocatalytic method for the asymmetric production of alcohols. In this work, the development of a method for the biocatalytic reduction of prochiral ketones based on oxide reductases is described. The conversion to the corresponding alcohols was achieved with the alcohol dehydrogenase ADH 'A' from Rhodococcus ruber DSM 44541. Investigations on the thermodynamic equilibrium position of the system and on the retention methods of the enzyme could be successfully converted into a continuously operated reactor model. Furthermore, various online methods for a non-invasive and direct determination of the reaction composition could be found for the given system. This thesis presents the process development for the biocatalytic reduction of prochiral ketones based on oxidreductases. Conversion to the corresponding alcohols was catalyzed by an alcohol dehydrogenase ADH-'A' derived from Rhodococcus ruber M 445.
content.title_en: Development of a biocatalytic process for asymmetrical production of alcohols

content.text: The interferometric phase contrast method and its application for the production of diffractive optical elements. For the flexible and inexpensive production of analog microoptics, an interferometrical exposure concept was designed, which is called interferometric phase contrast method. The present work describes the interferometric phase contrast method analytically and mathematically. Two models are developed from the interferometric phase contrast, which can be calculated using Fourier filtering based phase contrast methods. Using one of these models, phase contrast imaging is derived by phase delay of the bent light. In the optimization of the interferometric exposure structure, a new type of halftone mask for analogue lithography is obtained. Four further halftone masks are derived from the physical effect principle of this new halftone mask, which all enable the favorable production of analogue microoptics.

content.text: Isolation of a biopolymer from genetically modified plants. A crucial aspect in the use of renewable raw materials for the production of complex molecules is the isolation of the valuable material from the corresponding matrix. In the course of the work, two methods for the isolation of cyanophycin from transgenic plant materials were established. The first method was used to optimise the individual parameters of the insulation. The system is based on a novel concept that exploits signal delay on internal circuits. This concept is called BOUNCE. The experiments carried out show that a prototype of the BOUNCE concept achieves a temporal resolution of 4.2 ps with an accuracy of +/-10 ps for multiple measurement. The theoretical resolution of the system is unlimited, since it does not depend on gate durations.

content.text: Ion beam-enhanced etching for the 3D structuring of lithium niobate. The present work deals with the utilization of ion beam-enhanced etching (IBEE: Ion Beam Enhanced Etching) for the 3D structuring of lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Here the approach of increasing the wet chemical etching rate due to irradiation with energy-rich ions is pursued. This method is very promising for the realization of micro- and nanostructures with vertical structural walls and low roughness. The aim of this work was to form the basis for the realization of three-dimensional micro- and nanostructures (e.g. layer systems and photonic crystals) in LiNbO3 with high optical quality and to demonstrate on selected examples. Prerequisites for the success of the IBEE structuring technique is primarily the understanding of defect formation under ion radiation as well as the radiation-induced structural changes in the crystal and the associated change in chemical resistance. Here, defect formation in relation to ion radiation and radiation in the ion mass must be studied.

content.text: Practical assessment model of environmental and climate protection aspects for the use of biogas in the German-Chinese comparison. Climate protection is the biggest environmental challenge. Climate researchers see numerous indications that climate change has already begun. One of these is that of the ten hottest years since the beginning of the global temperature records in the mid-19th century seven were accounted for the last decade. According to many scientists, this development is also highly likely to be due to human influence (IPCC-WG1 2007). Therefore, the emissions of greenhouse gases caused by humans - especially the carbon dioxide produced during combustion processes (CO2) - must be drastically reduced worldwide. The interaction of climate protection and increasingly scarce fossil raw materials has been causing a boom in renewable energies since the recent past. Biogas use in Germany has become one of the most important components of renewable energies in addition to wind and solar energy projects. In China, the situation of biogas use has become complicated but also increasingly important.
content.title_en: Practical assessment model of environmental and climate protection aspects for the use of biogas in the German-Chinese comparison

content.text: Accelerating the molecular dynamics program LAMMPS using graphics cards' processes and the Nvidia Cuda technology. This bachelor thesis discusses the possibilities and limits of extending the widespread molecular dynamics program LAMMPS (the Large Scale Atomic/Molecular Massive Parallel Simulator) in which simulations are accelerated by incorporating modern graphics cards - in the context of NVIDIA's Cuda technology. A separate implementation serves as the basis for discussion. The first chapters repeat selected aspects of molecular dynamics, lambps and Cuda technology for graphics card programming. Based on this, details of the aforementioned implementation are discussed, comparing different strategies for force calculation and showing methods to avoid frequent data transfer from and to graphics card. The following part of the work deals with speed tests and the influence of factors such as numerical accuracy and system size in typical molecular dynamics simulations, whereby the results are always compared with those of the original LAMMPS version that has no graphics card support. Finally, conclusions are presented from this work and similar projects.
content.title_en: Accelerating the molecular dynamics program LAMMPS using graphics cards' processors and the Nvidia Cuda technology

content.text: The digital library of Babel : about how to use knowledge resources on the Web 2.0. Do free access to knowledge actually lead to less education on the web? content.text: Prussian - German - Belgian : national experience and identity ; life at the German-Belgian border in the 19th century. The aim of this study is to trace and analyse national experience and identity at the German-Belgian border in the 19th century. The subjective view, experience and sense of the national in the circles Eupen and Malmedy - belonging to Prussia since 1815 and transferred to Belgium as a result of the First World War in 1920 - is of central importance. What is decisive is how the people at the border inhabitants could and should learn German being at the arbitrary border, which should be translated into everyday life and meaning of life, or denied it, compared with Belgian being. - How did that process of nationalization, which was shaped by the border inhabitants, and which should leave a "contemporary borderline" every day when entering the 20th century? - To show the importance of national experience and feeling for the region as reliably as possible, is the work among other things based on Egoik documents, the community's powerful associations and police records, the border country's history, the German-German-German-Belgian language, and its identity, the German-Belgian language.
content.title_en: Prussian - German - Belgian : national experience and identity ; life on the German-Belgian border in the 19th century

content.text: Ecological variability in coastal ocean: simulating biological-physical interactions with Lagrangian Individual-based models. This dissertation examines the effect of biological-physical interactions on two fundamental processes in coastal ecosystems using individual models. The dynamics of phytoplankton spring bloom were significantly controlled in two consecutive years on a coastal parallel transect in the German Bay either by the light climate in the water column or by the flow pattern. Hydrodynamics was also the main factor that determined the invasion of a non-native benthic invertebrate. In addition, planktic larvae of these benthic invertebrates can significantly influence their drifting due to vertical migration in vertically sheared tide currents despite limited swimming ability. The results of this work show that the interaction of biological and physical processes has a decisive influence on the growth and distribution of marine organisms in the coastal sea. <dt.>
content.title_en: Ecological variability in coastal ocean : simulating biological-physical interactions with Lagrangian Individual-based models

content.text: An effective binary processing model based on interaural phase differences. People have the ability to find sound sources blindly and to concentrate specifically on a speaker in a voice mix and thus understand its language. An important reason for this is the ability of the hearing system to compare signals from left and right ears. These interaural differences are, on the one hand, time and phase differences and, on the other, interaural level differences. In the standard model of Jeffress (1948), an internal cross-correlator with two opposite chains of delay elements is assumed. New neurophysiological but also psychoacoustic studies, however, speak against the existence of delay chains in mammals. In this work, an effective binaural model is developed based on instantaneous phase comparison instead of delay chains. An effective model is to be understood as a sequence of elementary signal processing steps, whereby the signal does not describe concrete realization, but quantifies the transmitted information.
content.title_en: An effective binary processing model based on interaural phase differences

content.text: The parametric transition of stationary and axisymmetric bodies to black holes. This dissertation deals with solutions of stationary and axial symmetrical bodies and their parametric transition to black holes. Numerical solutions of fluids in equilibrium are calculated with very high accuracy by assuming a strand quark matter-state equation. Various sequences of configurations are investigated for spheroidal and toroidal bodies to show the essential properties of this family of objects from strand matter-. Configurations with maximum mass and maximum rotational momentum were found near - but not at - the mass-shedding-limit. In addition, we show that stranded matter-rings allow a continuous transition to the extreme Kerr solution. Multipole moments were investigated and point to a universal behavior of bodies that approach parametrically the extreme Kerr solution. Then we show that in terms of stability, a test part that is shown on the surface of the ring is used to determine the total of the turbidity, and to formulate the universal behavior of a parametrically approaching of a turbidity in the sense of the parametrical equation.
content.title_en: Parametric transition of stationary and axisymmetric bodies to black holes

content.text: Micro- and nanostructuring of lithium niobate. The aim of this work was to develop and implement a suitable manufacturing process for the realization of micro- and nanooptical components in lithium niobate. To this end, the technique of reinforced etching after ion irradiation (IBEE) was used. This technique was based on the damage of the crystal structure by irradiation with high-energy ions and the subsequent wet chemical removal of the damaged areas in a etching bath. The production of photonic crystal membranes was carried out by combining vertical and lateral structuring, using a quartz glass mask. In these photonic crystal membranes, defect waveguides were produced and demonstrated in these waveguide properties. In a W7 fault waveguide the existence of a ministopband at a wavelength of 1562 nm was demonstrated by a multi-application of the IBEE technique with a multi-stage application of a rib waveguide with a particle-rectangular geometry. The position of this ministopband is in line with the position obtained from the simulation of light propagation of the lithium.
content.title_en: Micro- and nanostructuring of lithium niobate

content.text: The modular approach is used to extend the functional variability of such systems. A modular climbing robot is developed as part of a three-stage mechatronic design process that takes into account mechanical as well as electronic and informational aspects. The results of this design process are two motion modules, three grip modules, an energy module, adapted mechanical connectors for coupling the modules and the module internal and external electronics. By recombining these module types, different robot structures can be built up. The climbing capability on a round substrate of an example configuration is demonstrated. The developed modular system offers the potential for the future development of different climbing robots.

content.text: Hervey Bay - insights from numerical modelling into the hydrodynamics of an Australian subtropical bay. Hervey Bay, a bay in the immediate vicinity of the continental shelf edge of the central east coast of Australia, shows an inverse structure/layers due to the high evaporation rate (about 2 m/year) and low rainfall (less than 1 m/year). As the bay has a strong tidal signal (tide stroke > 3.5 m), the bay can be classified as well mixed vertically. In Hervey Bay there is an almost constant salt gradient of 0.5 psu, with a salt content of 35.5 psu in the open ocean and peak values of over 39.0 psu in the coastal area. The study also shows that the passat winds dominate the water exchange in the bay. Due to long-lasting droughts, the subtropical areas on the east coast of Australia show a change in the balance of precipitation and evaporation.
content.title_en: Hervey Bay - insights from numerical modeling into the hydrodynamics of an Australian subtropical bay

content.text: Storage effects : the relationship between the hydrological dynamic of small infield pools and plant functional groups. Sölle are valuable habitats. But their properties, which make them attractive for swamp and aquatic plants and the species properties, which allow the plants to exist in such dynamic habitats are mostly unknown. I determined the habitat quality from levels with a time series model or developed transfer functions for seams with lower level resolution. The results show a downward trend at minimum water level and an increase in the annual level fluctuation caused by increasing temperatures in the study area, implying a change in habitat quality due to climate change. I developed a new method for determining the species occurrence to habitat quality. The resulting PFGs are characteristic in their over-permanence, competition and adaptation strategies.
content.title_en: Storage effects: the relationship between the hydrological dynamic of small infield pools and plant functional groups

content.text: Environment, energy, and economic performance. The dissertation analyses the relationship between economic success, environmental regulation and energy market developments. It shows that the economic consequences of the recent climate policy of the European Union were low. Its design is placed in a political-economic context. In addition, the thesis shows the role of investments in environmentally friendly technologies and products. The work also provides insights into the economic consequences of energy market developments. It contains an analysis of the equity market effects of the European Emissions Trading System. It shows that the corporate value of European electricity producers depends on the price of pollution rights. Finally, the work underlines the economic relevance of energy markets. The oil market is identified as the most important energy market from the perspective of financial markets. Furthermore, the thesis proves the relevance of oil price shocks for unemployment in Germany. <dt.>
content.title_en: Environment, energy, and economic performance

content.text: The structure and properties of the Oxo-arsenates(III) of the rare-earth elements are presented in this work. The main focus is on the development of new synthesis strategies for the formation of compounds in which rare-earth elements and transition metals are linked to Oxo-arsenate(III) anions to complex networks. These ligands are particularly suitable for the construction of such aggregates because they are characterized by a large number of different coordination and interconnection modes and thus allow for a wide variety of variations in the structure of the solid bodies and thus in the arrangement of rare-earth and transition metal ions. By solid-body chemical conversion of the oxides of the rare-earth elements with transition metal oxides and chlorides and arsen oxides, SE5(AsO3)4Cl3 (SE = La, Pr, Nd), SE3(AsO3)(AsO5).
content.title_en: Structure and properties of transition metal containing oxo-arsenates(III) of rare-earth elements

content.text: The high-throughput version of the Comet Assay is a screening process. There is a high need to record the increasing number of genotoxic compounds in the environment and in the development of new substances. To this end, the frequently used Comet Assay as a high-throughput process has been developed. In this work, the study investigated the extent to which this new high-throughput method is suitable for screening for genetic toxicity of environmental samples and chemicals during drug development. For this purpose, a comparison to conventional Comet Assay was carried out in 4 sub-workes, an automatic evaluation was developed, the applicability of various cell types was verified and a study was conducted to verify the genetic toxicity of water samples. The results show that the developed high-throughput process is very suitable for screening a variety of compounds and thus represents a simplification of gene toxicity testing. <dt.>
content.title_en: Ability of the high throughput version of the Comet assay as a screening method

content.text: Relating generalized and specific modelling in population dynamical systems. In this paper, two new areas of population dynamics are investigated using a generalized modeling approach: stoichiometric and eco-epidemiological population models. The stoichiometric population models take into account that primary producers usually have a fluctuating nutrient content, but consumers need a finely balanced composition of nutrients. In eco-epidemiological models, however, the influence of diseases on the interaction of populations is investigated. In particular, we will deal with diseases in predatory populations and the influence on predator-beute dynamics. Bifurcations play a decisive role in the analysis methods used. Initially, an innovative method is presented with which bifurcations can be found in generalized models and presented three-dimensionally.
content.title_en: Relating generalized and specific modelling in population dynamic systems

content.text: Efficient coding of natural sounds. Methods for efficient encoding of natural sounds based on the concept of "sparing coding" are proposed, a main mechanism in neurosensory information processing. Improved audio quality, especially at low bit rates, was achieved in the audio coding process MPEG-2/4 AAC by replacing the modified discrete cosine transformation (MDCT) with a shifting invariant sparse signal model (Matching Pursuit). It was shown that the number of M>100 gamma-ton filters (2.4 filters per ERB) allows an almost perfect reconstruction of the signal space of natural sounds. Furthermore, it is shown how an effective coding of sparse coefficients can be achieved by means of significance trees. Using a data-dependent set of significance trees this coding concept can be used to overcome the state-of-the-art audio coder MPEG-2/4 for bitrates below 32 kbps, while additionally allowing for fine-tuned bitrate scalability.
content.title_en: Efficient coding of natural sounds

content.text: The synthesis and application of functionalized bisenoyl acetates: new tools to elucidate the wound occlusion reaction of the green algae Caulerpa taxifolia and to selectively mark esteras. The sesquiterpene caulerpenin is the main secondary intestine of the single-cell, marine macroalgae Caulerpa taxifolia. In this work an analogue to this compound was synthesized, which could be marked by copper-catalysed azid-alkin coupling fluorescently. This compound was used to demonstrate in vivo how caulerpenin is enzymatically deacetylated in case of wounding and that the resulting reaction product is able to connect proteins of the algae to a protein biopolymer. Through this reaction, the algae succeeds in sealing injuries within minutes with this biopolymer and to prevent the flow of the cell content. In addition, this process plays a role in the defense of alga against herbivores.
content.title_en: Synthesis and application of functionalized bisenoyl acetates : new tools for clarifying the wound closure reaction of the green algae Caulerpa taxifolia and selective marking of esterases

content.text: The molecular and functional analysis of volatile isoprenoids in arabidopsis. Evolutionary plants are very successful organisms. They have developed complex but efficient systems to cope with different stress factors. Plants react both to biotic stress (e.g. herbivores, pathogens) and to abiotic stress (e.g. light, temperature, nutrition, oxidative stress). In a changing environment volatile terpenes have an ecological significance for the fitness of plants. Based on the various ecotypes of arabidopsis thaliana, studies on changes in the fragrance composition of plants are possible. By knowing the genomic sequence and the availability of numerous mutants, arabidopsis thaliana is a good tool for investigating molecular mechanisms. By leaf fracture, the ecotype Col-0 mainly induces sesquiterpene (E, E)-?-farneses, while the ecotype WS is mainly (E, E)-β-farneses and monoterps are free.
content.title_en: Molecular and functional analysis of volatile isoprenoids in arabidopsis

content.text: Studies on the function of the proteins SHMT6 and SHMT7 in Arabidopsis thaliana. Serin-hydroxymethyltransferases (SHMT) are central enzymes of C1 metabolism. The present dissertation provides an insight into the importance of SHMT in the cell nucleus of plants. C1 compounds are required for methylation, e.g. of DNA. According to the previous data, SHMT can contribute to C1 metabolism. A knock-out in the nuclear SHMTs of Arabidopsis leads to a reduction of methylated DNA. Changes in the metabolite concentrations of various metabolic intermediates and a growth inhibition in the germination stage are the consequence.
content.title_en: Investigations into the function of the proteins SHMT6 and SHMT7 in Arabidopsis thaliana

content.text: Model-based risk analyses of a biogas plant investment as a basis for a holistic risk assessment and strategic risk management. In order to draw conclusions about a meaningful integration of a biogas plant into the strategic overall concept of an agricultural enterprise, interdependencies of the investment inputs are evaluated by means of sensitivity analysis. Based on this, the investment success and the associated probability of occurrence are assessed with the Monte Carlo simulation and the suitability of different operating forms for the biogas plant investment in view of the changes in the overall operating return risk complex are evaluated by portfolio analyses.
content.title_en: Model-based risk analyses of a biogas plant investment as a basis for holistic risk assessment and strategic risk management

content.text: Immunohistological examination of the KCa2.2 (SK2) potassium channel and the GABAA receptor subunits in the basal ganglia in the childling model for temporal lobe epilepsy. Epilepsy, basal ganglia, GABAA receptor. - Epilepsy is a common, chronic, neurological disease in humans, as well as in dogs and cats. Some epilepsy forms, such as temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), are considered to be difficult to treat, as 50-90% of the patients concerned show resistance to the antiepileptics available today. For the rational development of new pharmacotherapy for the treatment of complex focal seizures occurring in TLE, it is urgently necessary to extend the understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of TLE. In the continuation and modulation of epileptic seizures that occur in the limbic system, the regions of basal ganglia play an important role. In particular, the epileptic epilization of the disease is subject to a retinalization of the disease.
content.title_en: Immunohistological examination of the KCa2.2 (SK2) potassium channel and the GABAA receptor subunits in the basal ganglia in the childling model for temporal lobe epilepsy

content.text: The emergence of green politics: Cultural sociology of the West German environmental movement. Thirty years after its foundation, The Greens are an established political force. This situation seems to us to be a matter of course today, but in fact it is the result of an equally improbable and drastic change in political culture. This is largely due to the new left movement that is going on in the 1960s and is first prominent as a student movement. Andreas Pettenkofer shows how and why the "green" interpretation pattern in the protest movements of the old Federal Republic was gradually developed and how the founding of a new party became conceivable and feasible. He thus exemplarily demonstrates the possibilities offered by the study of social movements for the explanation of cultural change.
content.title_en: The emergence of green politics : Cultural sociology of the West German environmental movement

content.text: Atomic vapor depositions of metal insulator Metal capacitors: investigation, development and integration. Metal-isolator metal (MIM) capacitors are among the most important passive components in high frequency components and circuits for analog/mix signals. Regardless of the application, MIM capacitors require up to 50% of the chip surface. This significantly supports reducing the chip surface, which strongly determines the cost but also the functionality and performance of the chip. An increase in capacity per area (capacity density) is therefore the focus of further analog scaling of components. Because the capacity is a direct function of the dielectric constant of the insulator, replacing the currently used silicon oxide or silicon nitride with alternative dielectrics with higher dielectric constants is a promising approach. The present work is mainly on the preparation and characterization of such alternative dielectrics, such as HfO2, Sr-Ta-O and Ti-vision-based materials. The current work is directed towards the preparation and characterization of these alternative dielectrics, such as the use of alternative dielectric oxides, and the use of Ti-sight-based materials.
content.title_en: Atomic vapor depositions of metal insulator Metal capacitors : investigation, development and integration

content.text: Titanium catalyzed hydromining of alkenes and alkines in drug synthesis. In this work, titanium complexes were investigated and compared with their activity for the hydromining of alkenes. It was found that all the complexes investigated showed catalytic activity in the implementation of amino-2,2-diphenylpent-4-en. The main part of the work before us deals with the synthesis of 1-Benzyl isoquinolin derivatives with eletron-poor and electronically neutral A-ring. Furthermore, the electronic situation on the C-ring could be varied. The connection of the A- and C-ring was carried out by a Sonogashira reaction. The B-ring was built by an intramolecular hydromining. The 1-Benzyl 3,4-dihydroisoquinolin derivatives thus obtained were directly simplified to the 1-Benzyl-1,3,4,4-tetrahydroquinolin derivatives and a Bise-hydroquinoline derivative was significantly simplified by the addition of a single-benzyl-hydroquinoline-derivate.
content.title_en: Titanium-catalysed hydroamination of alkenes and alkines in active substance synthesis

After an acute brain infection phase, the virus is eliminated in resistant C57BL/6 mice, whereas an insufficient antiviral immune response in susceptible SJL/J mice causes viral persistence. Furthermore, the virus antigen leads to a hypersensitivity response from the backline response, which is predominantly related to the incidence of the disease of the disease.

Red wine polyphenols, resveratrol, vineatrol, anticancerogenic effect. - Cancer diseases are among the most common causes of death in the Western world. Several studies have shown a relationship between the lifestyle and the diet of humans and the development of tumour diseases. Several studies have shown that a diet rich in fruit and vegetables can reduce the occurrence of such diseases. Polyphenols, which are considered to be secondary plant ingredients and are found in various plants as colouring and flavoring substances, are attributed to these positive properties, which such a diet brings with it. trans-resveratrol, a polyphenol found in fruits such as raspberries, peanuts and grapes, has been studied several times in relation to its health-promoting and especially anticancerogenic effect. content.text: Contribution to the chemistry of 2H-1,4-Benzothiazines: Synthesis of new lactam structures and α-aminophosphonic acid esters. The focus of this work is the synthesis and derivatization of 2H-1,4-Benzothiazines. Due to the reactive C=N double bond, some addition reactions can be performed with these imines. By adding acid chlorides to benzothiazines and subsequent substitution reaction with different nucleophiles, α-functionalized carboxylic acidamides are presented, which are further converted into various lactams. In addition to mercaptocarbon acids, gamma-lactams are obtained. The presentation of isoquinolin carbonates can be realized by adding homophthalic acid anhydride to the imines. Finally, the synthesis of α-aminophosphonic acid esters is presented with the help of the MICHAELIS-ARBUZOV reaction. Special attention is paid to the stereoselection of the individual reactions.

content.text: The European Union's international transport of dangerous goods is increasingly developing, with the result that the risk of accidents involving dangerous goods transport is generally more serious than that of ordinary goods transport. The resulting, practically important liability issues for the damage caused by third parties, i.e. persons not involved in the transport law relationship between consignors, carriers and consignees, are the subject of this investigation. All five modes of transport are being dealt with: road transport, rail freight transport, inland waterway transport, maritime transport and air freight transport. The presentation focuses on existing international conventions (CRTD, HNS Convention, CRDNI draft, second Romans liability agreements, oil liability and fund agreements, Paris and Vienna Conventions), even though these are largely not yet in force and therefore are not applicable in practice. The liability arising from this is still subject to the national law applicable to the international law.
content.title_en: Liability for dangerous goods transport in Europe: non-contractual liability for dangerous goods transport on land, water and aircraft

content.text: Visual information presentation in smart environments. The aim of the dissertation is to adapt information visualization in smart meeting rooms taking into account a heterogeneous and dynamically changing device ensemble. To this end, a classification for such adaptation mechanisms has been developed, which refers either to the information presentation or the process of creating visual representations, which differs between a spatial and a temporal adaptation or between a global or local image adaptation. For each of the classes a solution strategy was designed and implemented.
content.title_en: Visual information presentation in smart environments

content.text: Between all chairs: cultural self-attribution in the process of accultation of young settlers. The focus of this dissertation is on cultural self-attribution as "Germans" and as "Russians" of young resettlements who have emigrated from Russia to Germany. It examines the extent to which changes in these cultural self-attribution depend on perceived attitudes and behaviours of native German towards migrants and whether such changes are reflected in the social interactions and psychosocial adaptation of young people. For this purpose theoretical approaches of developmental and social psychology as well as accultation research are used. The longitudinal results show that the young people describe themselves as German and Russian on average, whereby self-attribution as German remained stable and self-attribution as Russian decreased. Young resettled immigrants then saw themselves more strongly as "Germans" when they perceived positive attitudes of the local population to contact them. The more the young people described themselves as "Germans", the more positive attitudes and the more frequent actual contacts with locals, the more frequent German language use and the higher self-efficence expectations they reported.
content.title_en: Between all chairs : cultural self-attribution in the acculturation process of young settlers

content.text: Non-proportional reinsurance models with risk preferences. This work considers non-proportional reinsurance contracts with their coverage limits priority and ceiling from the perspective of a first insurer. A reason for different requirements for reinsurance contracts is the risk preference of the first insurer. Decision principles that can represent risk preferences of a decision maker are, for example, the CVaR principle as well as hybrid decision principles based on the CVaR. These are applied in this work to the profit function of a first insurer, which includes the first and reinsurance business. Subsequently, statements about the coverage protection of a first insurer are made depending on its risk attitude. The work is divided into 8 chapters. Chapters 1 to 3 represent the basis of the work. Chapter 1 provides an overview of the reinsurance business with its types and forms. Chapter 2 contains the decision-theoretic foundations, such as the principles and criteria for decisions under risk and uncertainty, but also the definition of risk attitudes, but also the consistency of the theory of the case.
content.title_en: Non-proportional reinsurance models with risk preferences
