content.text: Mechanistic investigations of terpenesynthases from Medicago troncatula. Plants have developed various strategies during evolution to respond to biotic and abiotic stress factors. For example, Medicago troncatula, a clover related to Lucerne, reacts to the infestation by herbivores with the release of a large range of volatile compounds, whose main component is sesquiterpene. The formation of terpene is mediated by so-called terpene synthases, which catalyze the conversion of the prenyl diphosphates present in all plants to a large number of different carbon scaffolds. As this is the first step of the biosynthesis pathway in which the generation of terpene can be significantly controlled, terpene synthases are generally called the key enzymes of terpene biosynthesis. content.text: A synthetic approach to designing automotive on-board networks, taking into account dynamic loading processes. Motor vehicle on-board networks are responsible for the reliable functioning of all electrical and electronic systems. Therefore, the development and design of on-board networks must be carried out with the utmost care. Large-scale dynamic electrical consumers, which are resulting from the increasing electrification of mechanical and hydraulic components, have received little attention. These consumers can cause disturbances in on-board networks that may impair the functions of electrical and electronic systems. In this work, a new approach to designing on-board networks is shown, taking into account dynamic loading processes, which allows on-board networks to be adapted to these new requirements at an early stage of development. It will be addressed in terms of the characteristics of on-board networks themselves and the characteristics of the measures for stabilising on-board networks.
content.title_en: A synthetic approach to designing vehicle on-board networks, taking into account dynamic load processes

content.text: Multi-criterial evaluation of technologies for the provision of electricity and heat. The present paper deals with the question of how decisions regarding future energy supply can be supported in an effective, transparent and comprehensible way against the background of partly conflicting objectives. The relevance of the question is explained first against the background of important framework conditions for decisions in the energy sector. Subsequently, the most important technology paths, which already contribute to energy supply today or represent potential future options, are shown. It is clear that none of the many options alone can meet the requirements for an economic, environmentally friendly and reliable energy supply. Rather, their strengths and weaknesses must be carefully balanced against each other against the background of the specific framework conditions. This is the result of the need for multi-criterial decision support in order to be able to evaluate energy technologies in a comparative way, taking into account several objectives ...
content.title_en: Multi-criteria evaluation of technologies for the provision of electricity and heat

The present case study aims to reveal potentials for optimisation and further development as well as expansion of dual study programmes and to propose action. Optimization proposals will also be based on empirical results on models and cooperations between universities, students, the participating companies and vocational schools as well as other training institutions and chambers. The author addresses comprehensive aspects of dual studies in Thuringia. The dual study programme can be regarded as a variant of dual vocational education and a little-known path in medium-sized professional positions, as well as university development and qualification research hardly deal with this educational path. The work is understood as a case study on the status and development perspectives of dual studies in Thuringia, described and examined at study programmes of the universities of applied sciences in Erfurt and Schmalkalden. The core of the work are empirical studies on the respective experiences and expectations of the dual study programme.

content.text: Spatiotemporally explicit incidence analysis of plant functional groups in metacommunities. This paper examines the role of metacommunity mechanisms for the diversity of plant communities in a dynamic urban landscape. In this context, the relative importance of propagation limitation, abiotic stress and competition is determined on the basis of functional features, as well as the importance of ecological differences among species. While stress was not important, propagation and competition effects were demonstrated and associated with functional characteristics. Nevertheless, the observed functional diversity did not differ significantly from the expectations of a zero model. Thus, the results support the neutral metacommunity paradigm, which ignores functional differences among species. The result thus underlines that, even if species differ in their ecological characteristics, in addition to species characteristics and local factors, stochastic variables must be considered, if necessary, to understand the formation of plant communities. <dt.>

content.text: Aggregation and fragmentation dynamics of inertial particles in fluid flows. This paper numerically examines the dynamics of inertial particles that aggregate through collisions and then fragment under certain conditions. Our main aim is to better understand natural phenomena such as the formation of drops in clouds and marine aggregates. Our main focus is to investigate the long-term behavior of particle size distributions. First, we describe a model for aggregation and fragmentation of spherical drops in a turbulent flow. We also analyze systems with more complex aggregate structure where the structure can be approximated with a fractal dimension. We show that the distribution of fragments after breaking is crucial for the shape of the size distribution of the aggregates. Finally, we show how our approach is integrated into the established models from literature. < dt.>
content.title_en: Aggregation and fragmentation dynamics of inertial particles in fluid flows

content.text: Service replication in wireless mobile ad hoc networks. The present work deals with the management of services in mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs). MANETs are wireless network associations of mobile units that manage themselves decentralised without a higher-level organization. The network topology of a MANET changes dynamically with the movement of autonomous participants. Sensor networks, personal area networks and satellite networks are typical examples of such MANETs. With the increasing importance of wireless networking of mobile devices, MANETs have developed into an important research area in recent years. In disaster management, in civilian rescue cases or in military scenarios, their infrastructureless self-organisation MANETs can make the only possible means of communication. The mobile nodes of a MANET cooperate to ensure essential network services such as routing and data transport jointly. Resources such as the bandwidth between nodes, the computing power of mobile devices and their battery performance are typically highly limited and also changing. Therefore, sharing the available resources is a necessity for the efficient functioning of a MANET. Service-oriented architectures (SOA) are a shared paradigm.
content.title_en: Service replication in wireless mobile ad hoc networks

content.text: Asymmetries in the new economic geography: models, simulation methods and economic policy discussion. The New Economic Geography (NEG) explains agglomerations from a microeconomic total model. To simplify, various symmetry assumptions are made. Thus, it is assumed that the regions considered have the same size, the expenditure shares for different product groups are identical and the transport costs for all industrial products are the same.A consequence of these assumptions is that, although it can be explained under what conditions agglomeration formation occurs, not where this happens. In this work, three standard models of the NEG are extended by different asymmetries and the change of the results compared to the respective base model is presented. In addition to the theory, the methods of simulation are discussed, which can be transferred fundamentally to other models. Building on this, an asymmetric model variant is applied to the economic development of Germany. Thus, the absence of a land-wide upturn in the new countries, the strong migration movements into the old countries and the permanent wage-rate cases can be explained in a total model.

content.text: In the modular representation theory, finite groups are realized by matrices over bodies with positive characteristics. The corresponding characters are distributed among so-called blocks. Many information about a block are encoded in its defect group. Often, for example, one can derive the number of characters in a block from its defect group. In this work, such information is examined for special defect groups. Here, it is always assumed that the underlying body has the characteristic 2. Important assumptions, such as Alperin's weight presumption for these special cases, are proved. In another part of the work, new methods for detecting Brauer's k(B) presumption for general blocks are presented. These are among others able to show that Brauer's k(B) presumption for 2-blocks is fulfilled by the defect less than 4.

content.text: Service-based infrastructure for pervasive teaching and learning arrangements. This dissertation analyses the infrastructure challenges for pervasive universities. It assesses the suitability of today's communication models as an infrastructural basis and motivates the use of service-oriented architectures (SOA). It also presents well-known interoperability approaches and evaluates them in terms of their suitability for interoperability in pervasive environments. A systematic interoperability approach is then presented. Strategies for their integration into this approach are developed for the classified SOA implementations.

content.text: The information processing of auditors when examining estimated values: A behavioral and empirical analysis. The information behavior of auditors is becoming increasingly important. Jochen Schwind examines the connection between expertise and decision performance in different structured tasks as well as determinants of successful problem solving. He shows that experts derive better audit opinions than novices in both well-structured and poorly structured areas of tasks. As factors of successful problem solving, task-specific examination experience and attendance of continuing education events are particularly evident.

content.text: In the course of the increase in the regular retirement age to 67, more individualised forms of transition to retirement – such as the (real) part-time retirement and the partial pensions available under pension insurance – are being given more attention in recent years. Although there has been a constant debate over moving transitions into retirement for decades, impact analyses based on empirical data are, however, rare for Germany. The present work starts here and analyses the importance of moving transitions for the current institutionalised forms of transitions. In addition to the derivation of further effects of moving transitions based on human capital theory and rotational considerations, the data from the Socioeconomic Panel investigates the importance of moving transitions for the employability-maintaining health and (further)education. In addition to common multivariate procedures, matching approaches are used. It shows that although the trend towards active participation is less likely to be reflected by the increase in the number of employees.
content.title_en: Moving transitions to retirement: impact on labour market participation and the human capital of older people in Germany

content.text: Ab-initio studies on the adsorption and desorption mechanism of CO on a titanium dioxide surface are presented in the paper. A Ti9O18 cluster is being presented in the context of the embedded cluster sewing. In addition to the electronic basic state, the electronically excited states relevant for photodesorption are being investigated. Based on 1D studies, 2D potential surfaces are calculated taking into account further degrees of freedom of the CO adsorbate. Based on the potential surfaces, quantum dynamic wave packet simulations for laser-induced photodesorption are being presented in the form of a photodesorption co-ordinate Z and the polar angle theta. Based on a systematic analysis of wave packet dynamics, this dissertation presents the underlying photodesorption mechanism of the CO molecules from the TiO2(110) surface area.
content.title_en: Ab-initio studies of the adsorption and desorption mechanism of CO on a titanium dioxide surface

content.text: Photoelectron diffraction on transition metal oxides. In this work simulations are performed using the Multi-Scatter Cluster Model (MSCM). It is shown that the simple approach of the forward scatter model is not sufficient to determine the structure of 3d transition metal monoxide films due to strong interferences. The structure of ultra-thin films from two experiments (MnO/Ag(001), 0.5-20ML) is determined by R-factor analysis. Simulated X-ray photoelectron diffraction spectra (XPD spectra) are compared to different structural models from experimentally measured spectra. All films have a tetragonal distortion, which depends on the growth mechanism (temperature and duration of tempering). content.text: Laser finishing of metallic materials. Laser finishing of metallic materials summarizes the individual processes of the dissipating micromaterial processing of metals with laser pulses of ns duration. In this process, beam propagation is included for the first time in the considerations. content.text: Micropolitics in the district: Resident participation in the urban conversion process. Urban conversion is a current focus of federal German urban development policy, which has so far been analysed in a very limited way, just like the citizens' participation required on all sides. Against the background of the programmes 'Stadtumbau Ost' and 'Stadtumbau West' Miriam Fritsche analyses local citizen participation processes in two metropolitan districts: Marzahn-Nord (Berlin) and Tenever (Bremen). In order to identify factors that promote participation and inhibit participation, she assigns the local forms of participation to the context of local participation cultures. It is clear that the understanding of participation by central actors as well as the micropolitical internal structure of local residents' bodies decisively influence the dominant forms of participation, its range and intensity. The book addresses lecturers and students of urban geography, urban sociology, local politics, spatial planning and related disciplines as well as actors from the practice of politics and (communal) administration. Dr. Miriam Fritsche is a political scientist and PhD student at the University of Gefragschafts-Institut for Berlin.
content.title_en: Micropolitics in the district : Resident participation in the urban conversion process

content.text: Conception of a system for the collection and use of quantitative data on information security incidents. An orientation towards economic principles is increasingly required for the management of information security and thus a consideration of the costs and benefits of security measures. Thomas Nowey designs the concept of a platform for the collection and use of quantitative data on information security incidents. content.text: Everyday theories on the causes and consequences of global climate change: the collection and analysis of student ideas from a geographical didactic perspective. Klappentext: What ideas do students have about the causes and consequences of global climate change? How do they construct their own everyday theory on this complex human-environment problem based on media information, teaching and various everyday ideas? What typical learning problems can result from this and what didactic consequences can be derived for the teaching design? The present volume deals with these questions from the perspective of geography didactics and education for sustainable development in a comprehensive empirical study, in which both the natural and the socio-economic dimensions of global climate change are considered. The everyday theories of the students are captured and analyzed as concept maps. In this way, typical concepts and thinking figures can be worked out about the causes and consequences of global climate change, which can lead to significant learning problems in the teaching. It is clear that overcoming these learning problems is only possible if science-faring student ideas are understood as a valuable learning resource and are appropriately considered in the teaching context of the teaching of the teaching anthropological guidelines.
content.title_en: Everyday theories on the causes and consequences of global climate change : Survey and analysis of student ideas from a geographical didactic perspective

content.text: Library services for literary administration: a comparative analysis of the range of scientific libraries with special consideration of the user perspective. Literature management is an integral part of scientific work. In order to facilitate and effectivate this activity, a wide range of electronic literature management systems now exist. The use becomes more attractive given the growing possibilities for functions as well as available and reusable bibliographic data. At the same time, an increasing need for support among users is evident. Scientific libraries are increasingly acting as service providers. The present work provides a function-oriented, classificatory systematization of the service spectrum as well as an empirical study of 109 library websites from a user's perspective, a discussion contribution to the overview, the assessment and the improvement of the current library service practice for literary administration.
content.title_en: Library services for literature management: a comparative analysis of the supply of scientific libraries, with particular reference to the user perspective

content.text: Crystal orientations in glass-ceramics determined using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). he present cumulative dissertation consists of seven publications published in the journals Crystal Growth & Design and CrystEngComm. The focus of this work is the investigation of crystal orientations in glasskermike using Electron Backscatter diffraction (EBSD). This method enables the local resolution of crystal orientations in the electron microscope (REM) and is described in more detail in the introduction. The investigation of surface crystallization showed that previous models about the formation of oriented layers were wrong or incomplete in this way and enabled a more correct description of the resulting oriented layers and their formation. The examination of glass ceramics produced by electrochemically induced germ formation also led to new findings such as the detection of differently oriented crystals in the otherwise extremely homogenous oriented dendtites. Furthermore, it was found that the orientation of glass ceramics produced by electrochemical induced germ formation was not homogenous but rather the determination of the crystal crystal crystal.
content.title_en: Crystal orientations in glass-ceramics determined using electric backscatter diffraction (EBSD)

content.text: Numerical simulation of dynamic stable for heavy airfoils using adaptive mesh techniques. In this work we perform numerical simulations of currents via lowering wing profiles using a high-resolution spectral element method. A very detailed spatial and temporal description of the flow is achieved. The results we have obtained are validated with previously published experimental and numerical investigations. Resistance, neutral and thrust sequences are successfully simulated. In addition, we have observed two previously unknown modes. We consider that the Strouhal number is the only characterization parameter of lowering wing profile sequences. Our results show that the amplitude and frequency of lowering are also to be considered. Finally, we have examined the frequency regimes in lowering wing profiles. We have found that the frequency regimes determine the subsequent cycle. < dt.>
content.title_en: Numerical simulation of dynamic stable for heavy airfoils using adaptive mesh techniques

content.text: Nickel superoxide dismutases of heavy metal resistant streptomycetes. Nickel is on the one hand vitally integrated as a cofactor in bacterial enzymes. On the other hand, nickel is already partially toxic to cells in low concentrations. A finely adjusted regulation of the absorption or storage of this metal is therefore necessary. Several enzymes are known to contain nickel, including the nickel superoxide dismutase detected first in streptomycetes. Nickel is used to regulate the expression of these proteins often as a co-regulator. Among other things, nickel induces the synthesis of the nickel-containing urease, FeNi-hydrogenase and NiSOD, while it inhibits the iron absorption and FeSOD. To use nickel, cells must develop sensitive mechanisms that bind the heavy metal, transport it and release it to target proteins. In addition to the explanation of regulation and Homoeostasis, the enzyme function also raises the question of the role of niSOD in the resistance to heavy metals. Heavy metals cause the formation of the subtute metabolites are also isolated to the hyperdioxides.
content.title_en: Nickel superoxide dismutases of heavy metal resistant streptomycetes

content.text: The German Civil Protection Law is constantly criticised. The criticism points are presented in the work by order of perspectives and are subject to an assessment. The author explains why the Federal Civil Protection Law requires a comprehensive reconception including the amendment of constitutional standards. For the Thuringian Civil Protection Law the author also presents the criticism points. It develops its own approaches for which only minor changes to the current law are necessary. A proposal is the creation of the Office of the State Disaster Protection Officer. The third focus of the investigation concerns the tasks of the municipalities in Thuringian Fire and Civil Protection Law. Based on a presentation of the predicted and proven climate changes, existing and possible deficits in the field of hazard prevention are named. As an option of the municipalities to maintain and restore the capacity to cope with the problems of climate change, the German Civil Protection Law does not apply to the public authority's floods. The German Civil Protection Act (GG) contains a statement of the public authority's obligation to cooperate in this field.
content.title_en: Civil Protection and Climate Change in Thuringia : ThürBKG and ThürKGG as instruments for dealing with the consequences of climate change

content.text: Further development of a model based on the LIQUAC and LIFAC methods for the calculation of salt solubility in solvent mixtures. The present research describes the further development of a model for the description of thermodynamic properties in electrolyte systems based on the LIQUAC and LIFAC methods. This model was called the LIQUAC* or LIFAC* model. In addition to the revision of the model, the model-specific parameters were adapted or calculated. In addition, the basic thermodynamic assumptions of underlying models, such as the Debye-Hückel theory, are presented in detail. Furthermore, the calculation methods of different thermodynamic properties of electrolyte systems are given and the results of the new model are shown in comparison with experimental data of the Dortmund database. In addition, a comparison of the calculated accuracy of the new model with the older LIQUAC and LIFAC models was made.
content.title_en: Further development of a model based on the LIQUAC and LIFAC methods for the calculation of salt solubility in solvent mixtures

content.text: Investigations of signatures of planetary waves in the ionosphere. Subject of investigation are periodic variations of electron density in the ionosphere, which are called signatures of planetary waves (PWTO). They have periods between 2 and 30 days and a horizontal extension that can exceed 10,000km. Due to their similarity to planetary waves (PW) of the lower and middle atmosphere, a connection with these is assumed. The present work deals with the investigation of the possible coupling between the lower atmosphere and ionosphere by PW. To describe the ionospheric PWTO, maps of the total electron content (TEC) of the ionosphere are used, which cover the northern hemisphere from 50ʿN to the pole cap and are produced operationally in DLR with an hourly resolution. The calculation of relative differences to the current 27-day median ($\Delta TEC_{rel}$) is used as a bandpass filter to minimize variations of the wavelet method.
content.title_en: Investigations on signatures of planetary waves in the ionosphere

content.text: Sol-Gel induced conductivity modulation of networks from carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and their causes. This work deals with a new method for the production of a highly conductive layer from a CNT/Sol-Gel compound. To this end, thin CNT networks are applied initially to an electrically non-conductive substrate and then penetrated with the Sol-Gel in the dipping process. In addition to dispersed CNT networks, this method is also used for dispersant-free. Subsequently thermal processing of the coatings allows the modification of the electrical properties of the compound due to thermally induced compression mechanisms of the Sol-Gel. Due to the possibility of equivalent processing of Sol-Gel free CNT networks, it is also possible to study the influence of the Sol-Gel on the CNT networks. In the course of this study, the unexpectedly increased electrical conductivity of the CNT/Sol-Gel composites (in comparison to the Sol-Gel free equivalent) was evaluated by the CNT-Gel's experimental properties.
content.title_en: Sol-gel induced conductivity modulation of networks of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and their causes

content.text: Kelvinsonden microscopy on organic thin-film semiconductors: Influence of layer processing on electrical, optical and morphological properties of organic solar cells. In this work, a comprehensive study of the influence of manufacturing-related differences on the electrical and optical properties of organic BHJ solar cells was conducted. The results of the electrical and optical characterization were compared with the force microscopic analyses of the semiconductor layers and investigated for possible connections. The investigations were carried out on organic semiconductor mixing layers, produced on the basis of the polymer-fuller-gematic P3HT and PCBM. In addition to the variation of the materials used (among other things different dopings and molecular weights of the polymer), differences in the solar cells were considered by selecting the solvent used, heat treatment after the production and the mixing ratio of the individual components.
content.title_en: Kelvinsonden microscopy on organic thin-film semiconductors : Influence of layer processing on electrical, optical and morphological properties of organic solar cells

The calculations for the sample ship under investigation show that this is successful for the design aspect rudders based on operational profiles will be present. content.title_en: Development of a design process for ship rudders based on statistical operating profiles

content.text: Dynamic "green" process design in microreactors with the help of research-accompanying eco-balances. In this work, the simplified life cycle assessment is presented as an instrument for identifying environmental potentials of the investigated process at the research and development stage of chemical process development and for developing optimization proposals. The ecological assessment is made difficult by data uncertainties and data gaps as well as by the numerous experiments carried out. Therefore, for a reliable statement of the environmental potential of a process, a simple and easy-to-use methodology is essential, which takes into account the uncertainties occurring at the same time. The simplified life cycle assessment presented is demonstrated by three case examples. These examples are process developments from the field of microprocess engineering, which are intended to contribute to an intensification of industrially relevant chemical processes compared to the use of conventional reactors. In addition to the use of microstructured process units, additional reactive media, e.g. ionic liquids, or alternative possibilities of energy input, e.g. by microwave radiation or ultrasound, are used for process intensification.
content.title_en: Dynamic "green" process design in microreactors with the help of the research-accompanying eco-balance

content.text: Economic, social and spatial consequences of seasonal labour migration in the region of origin: the example of the Konin region (Poland). This work is based on research in the years 2007-2009. It looks at seasonal labour migration from the Polish region of Konin, where labour migration has a long tradition for economic reasons, as well as in similarly structured areas of Poland, dating back to the 19th century. It is considered seasonal migration abroad with the economic, social and spatial effects from the perspective of the individual and its immediate surroundings, but also the society and the territory of the migrants.
content.title_en: Economic, social and spatial consequences of seasonal labour migration in the region of origin : the example of the Konin region (Poland)

content.text: The design of electromagnetic actuators, taking Hysteresis into account. Electromagnets are drive elements that are used for a wide variety of tasks in automation technology and automotive construction. Current requirements for high dynamics and energy efficiency often move at the limits of the physical possibilities. Especially in order to ensure a reliable and robust model-based design in these boundary areas, it is necessary to consider all relevant physical effects. Electromagnetic hysteresis is an effect that has a strong impact on the behaviour of a drive, but has not been generally considered in the design. In the context of this work, it was attempted to close this gap for early design phases. For this purpose, hysteresis models known in literature for the representation of pure material characteristics were compared and the most suitable choice was made. Due to their accuracy and computational efficiency, the Jiles-Atherton model is well suited for extensive simulation calculations. Various methods for identifying and optimizing the model parameter set from measured material characteristics are presented and compared to each other and processed for automated determination by the analysis of the electromagnets.
content.title_en: Electromagnetic actuator design taking into account hysteresis

content.text: A comparison of locally analytical group colomology and Lie algebra colomology and p-adic Lie groups. Summary: The main result of the work is a new proof and a generalization of Larzard's comparative isomorphism of local analytic group cohomology with Liealgebra colomology for K-liem groups. We show the following result: Be K a finite extension of the p-adic numbers and be G a K-liemology. Then there exists an open subgroup U of G, so that the Lazard isomorphism, which is given by the discharge of cochains, is an isomorphism. The proof of this result is independent of Lazard's proof of the comparison isomorphism.
content.title_en: A comparison of locally analytical group cohomology and Lie algebra cohomology for p-adic Lie groups

content.text: The effect of ultrasound on the microbiological diversity and degradation performance of a biological reactor for wastewater purification. Since the establishment of activated sludge in everyday life, it is possible to find new solutions to sustainably and economically optimise the biological process of wastewater purification. The use of ultrasound, as investigated in this work, has been shown to be a suitable technique. After the ultrasonic action, optimal morphological changes in the flakes structure are achieved, resulting in increased microbial activity in activated sludge. Furthermore, by the dissolution of a part of the activated sludge, a reduction in excess biomass is observed. Since the establishment of the active sludge process in everyday life, we are constantly in search of new solutions to optimize the biological process of secondary purification in a sustainable and economic way. The application of ultrasonic sound, which is investigated in this thesis, manifest itself as the optimal reaction in the evolved.

content.text: Self-organization in continuous adaptive networks. Complex systems can often be described by adaptive networks. These are characterized by the dynamic coupling of local and topological degrees of freedom, leading to a wealth of self-organizational phenomena. Analytical studies can contribute to the understanding of the mechanisms underlying the phenomena. However, the development of appropriate methodological approaches is difficult due to the need to take account of both the dynamic and structural characteristics of the network. This work examines a new analytical approach combining methods from graph theory and the theory of dynamic systems. It is our knowledge according to the first approach suitable for the analysis of continuous networks. We use it to investigate three emerging phenomena that are central to biological and social systems: synchronisation, spontaneous diversification and self-organized critique. <dt.>

content.text: Target-oriented detection and resolution of quality deficiencies in software systems using the example of further development capability. For enterprise-critical software systems, which are to be durable and expandable, the quality goal of further development capability is essential. Continuous changes and extensions are indispensable to adapt such software systems to new or changed requirements. However, these measures often cause quality deficits that can lead to an increase in complexity or a deterioration of the architecture. Especially quality deficits in the specification or architecture can severely affect software systems. To counteract this, a method is developed in this work which can evaluate the compliance with quality objectives. This allows both the recognition and the resolution of quality deficits in software development. Quality deficits are detected by a quality target oriented and rule-based analysis and corrected by associated reengineering activities. As an example of a quality target, the further development capability of software systems is considered. In order to validate the method, the quality deficiency was evaluated.

content.text: In this work, a measurement method was used to investigate the flow around a wind turbine (rotor diameter 116 m, hub height 102 m) with coherent Doppler wind lidar. For the first time, measurements were carried out on a wind turbine in the open field, which can simultaneously collect data before and behind a turbine until long-distance afterrun. Two different scanning patterns have been used to investigate the speed deficit in the downstream and the meandering. In addition, turbulence analyses (turbulence intensity, power density spectra, integral length scales) were carried out to investigate the influence of a wind turbine on the boundary layer. In the course of the turbulence analyses, the lidar data were compared with anemometer data. Furthermore, the measurements were compared qualitatively with follow-up models. <dt.>

content.text: Influence of presence of a heteroatom source on the synthesis of layered silicates : ilerite, magadiite and kenyaite. In this work the hydrothermal synthesis of Ilerite, Magadiite and Kenyaite is treated in the presence of a heteroatom source. The main objective of the study was to investigate the influence of the above-mentioned compounds on the resulting material and also the possibility of isomorphic substitution of silicon by tin atoms. The properties of the resulting samples were characterized using various methods. For comparison, non-modified samples impregnated with SnO2 and containing aluminium were produced and characterized using the same methods as for the Sn-modified samples. An appropriate split of the Q3 signal in 29Si-MAS-NMR measurements for tin-modified magadiite and its redox properties indicate the presence of OSn bound SiO2 tetrahedrons. Consequently, the obtained data seem to confirm that the silicon atoms can be subsiliated.

content.text: Age and method: a comparison of telephone and personal guide interviews with children. Children are becoming increasingly informants about their life world. Nevertheless, a methodological and methodological examination of this special target group is largely lacking. In this study, the feasibility of telephone and face-to-face guide interviews with children aged 5, 7, 9 and 11 is examined. Particular attention is paid to the verbal, interactive and cognitive abilities of children, who in turn have an influence on the data quality and the content of guide interviews. It is evident that, although partly with limited possibilities of knowledge, the interview is already possible in both interview modes from a young age. Building on the analyses, practical information for the interview of children is derived. content.text: The President of the Old Age : a constitution and his alternatives. Benedict Brunner compares, on the one hand, the historical, political, legal, personnel and communicative characteristics of the three main options for a parliament's opening.
content.title_en: The Old President : A Constitution and his Alternatives

content.text: Characterization of optical metamaterials : effective parameters and beyond. The present work deals with the characterization of metamaterials. For a more comprehensive introduction to the topic, refer to Chapter 1. As artificial media with periods smaller than the relevant wavelength, these are usually described as effectively homogeneous materials. This type of description and its critical analysis and evaluation are at the heart of Chapter 2-4. Chapter 2 lays the foundations for the description of artificial structures by means of homogeneous Maxwell equations and in particular the corresponding material equations. In this chapter, the description of artificially magnetic materials is derived on the basis of a complex, spatial dispersive material response. The material equations obtained for media with weak spatial dispersion are then used in Chapter 3 to determine the effective properties. The determination is made by the so-called S parameter retrieval, i.e. the inversion of the Fresnel equation for reflection and transmission on an optical layer. This method is also extensively considered by the point of view of general periodic media, whereby the basic relationships and especially limitations are used in order to derive an effective response to the metaparameters.
content.title_en: Characterisation of optical metamaterials : effective parameters and beyond

content.text: Active data and model-based sensor positioning for 3-D measurement. In the area of three-dimensional object reconstruction and inspection, the view planning is one of the central problems. It allows the determination of suitable sensor parameters to capture a measurement object with high precision and complete with few views. This allows shorter view plans to be created, which lead to more accurate and complete reconstructions. Traditional methods of view planning, the determination of the best next view (Next Best View, NBV) strive either to maximize completeness or minimize uncertainty. In contrast, the model-based multi-step planning presented in this work allows for the development of the eigenvector (so-called extended e-criterium) which is the largest intrinsic value of the estimated measurement uncertainty, the joint optimization of completeness and accuracy. To this end, the sensor used must be modelled precisely and its characteristic measurement uncertainty experimentally determined.
content.title_en: Active data and model-based sensor positioning for 3-D measurement

content.text: Glasses and glass ceramics in the system MgO-Al2O3-SiO2 with ZrO2 as germ forming agents. In the system MgO/Al2O3/SiO2 with the germ forming agent ZrO2 it is possible to produce colourless, transparent to opaque glass ceramics with good mechanical properties. For this purpose, the spinel and the deep-quartz are excreted in this system, which have a high thermal expansion coefficient compared to the residual glass phase. At comparable low crystallization temperatures, the high-quartz mixing phase is eliminated, which is stabilized by the installation of MgO and Al2O3 in the crystal lattice also at room temperature. If the crystallization temperature or time is increased, the concentrations of MgO and Al2O3 decrease and thus lead to the conversion into the deep-quartz mixing crystal phase. The transformation temperature of the glass ceramics increases with increasing crystallization time at 950 ʿC. Thus, a diffusion barrier is formed by the crystals, which slows further crystal growth. The conversion of the high-quartz M2 into the mechanical hardness of the Mg2M was achieved by a break-th.

content.text: Data assimilation in European regional and coastal seas (Black Sea and German Bight). The work is divided into two parts, which deal with the development and application of data assimilation approaches for the Black Sea and the German Bay. The main objective of the first part, which deals with the Black Sea, is an estimation of the stereotic heights in the region. A fundamental condition for the method used is the independence of the estimation from the observations on the Basin scale, which can be considered one of the main new developments. Furthermore, for this region it is the first application of a model based on the Nucleus for European Modelling of the Ocean (NEMO) framework system. The second part of the study deals with the German Bay. In it, the potential of FerryBox surface temperature and surface salt content measurements for data assimilation is examined for the first time. In particular, the "aliasing" problem in connection with the M2 tide is discussed. Furthermore, it is shown that different correlations have a strong influence on the quality of the state estimate.
content.title_en: Data assimilation in European regional and coastal seas (Black Sea and German Bight)

content.text: Planning for an ageing population: experiences from local areas in the United Kingdom. The majority of British communities are confronted with an ageing population, with coastal areas and rural areas being preferred as retirement homes. The British central government has started to address this challenge relatively early and provides strategic guidelines for the communities. Based on three case studies (North Tyneside, Poole and Wealden), the band examines the local approach to the ageing population. The participants and local forms of governance are analysed and local learning processes reconstructed. On this basis, challenges and perspectives of urban development for an ageing population are discussed. In addition to conclusions for theory and practice, what actors in other countries can learn from the British experience are reflected.
content.title_en: Planning for an ageing population : experiences from local areas in the United Kingdom

content.text: Although life competence programs are currently considered the most effective measures for preventing juvenile substance abuse, it is not clear how they work, which life skills are promoted and how they influence substance consumption. How young people apply the skills learned and whether altered behaviour affects substance consumption has hardly been investigated. The dissertation study examines the questions based on the German life competence program IPSY. The study combines quantitative questionnaire methods with qualitative observation techniques and is based on a one-group pretest post-test follow-up design. The sample includes N=51 students of the class 5 of an intern school in Thuringia, who all participated in the IPSY program. Data collection (studio questionnaires, saliva samples, video interactions) took place at three measurement times (pretest, post-test, follow-up after 5 months).
content.title_en: Factors of the school-based preventive life skills programme IPSY for the influence of tobacco and alcohol consumption in adolescence

content.text: The aim of this paper was to develop, implement and evaluate microreaction technology experiments for the university training of chemical students in the field of technical chemistry. By changing the specific training situation at the Institute of Technical Chemistry and Environmental Chemistry of the FSU Jena, students of chemistry are to be familiarized with basic fields of microreaction technology at an early stage, to identify potentials of microreaction technology and to promote and sustainably develop their interest in microreaction technology. The extended aim was to contribute to the reduction of the gap between the current market and workplace situation in the microreaction technology sector and the availability of qualified professionals in this field. Two microreaction technology experiments were developed, implemented and evaluated for this purpose, which deal with basic areas of microreaction technology (physico-chemical characterization of T-shaped microreactors, synthesis in microreactors). In Experiment 1, T-shaped micromixers are developed, implemented and evaluated in terms of mixing behaviour, energy input...
content.title_en: Development, implementation and evaluation of microreaction technology experiments

content.text: The analysis of complex systems with extensive data sets and the detection of relevant patterns require the use of modern statistical methods. DPLS models, a variant of structural equation models with latent variables, are expanded methodically to model several time lag stages simultaneously. The model results show that moods, i.e. the assessment of the current economic situation, are clearly related to economic variables, among others with investments, orders or stock market developments. Expectations, i.e. the assessment of future development, provide a medium to weak forecasting force for six to maximum eighteen months. For short-term trends, the forecasting of the current economic situation is based on the observation of the current economic situation, the forecasting of the current situation and the forecasting of the future. The forecasting of the future is based on the forecasting of the current economic situation, and the forecasting of the current economic situation is based on the forecasting of the current economic situation.
content.title_en: Moods and expectations in the market system: an analysis with DPLS models

content.text: The influence of active and passive navigation on spatial memory of active drivers and co-drivers. Research results on active navigation suggest that the execution of a movement could be less decisive for spatial memory than the active decision on the direction of movement. Consequently, an actively navigating passenger would not necessarily be disadvantaged compared to a navigation instruction following driver. This hypothesis was investigated with two experimental series. In Series 1 movement control was manipulated as the first factor in virtual environments and four other factors were compared (Experiment 1: learning intension; Experiment 2: instruction specificity and instruction control; Experiment 3: navigation control). Series 2 transferred these findings to a real context. The participants drove on the front or back seat of a tandem and received various detailed map sections to navigate through a park (Experiment 4 and 5). In another experiment without exposure, however, possible confining of the two previous experiments were excluded (Experiment 6). The present work confirmed that spatial learning in the research on active navigation is less of active movement control is obliging the participation of the relevant knowledge.
content.title_en: The influence of active and passive navigation on spatial memory of drivers and co-drivers

content.text: Ficucs - a constraint-solder for geometric constraints in 2D and 3D : algorithms; cases of use; modelling. The present work reflects the results of a long-standing research and development activity in the field of geometric constraints on standard geometries in 2D and 3D. The experience of constructive and numerical approaches for the calculation of constraint-based models was incorporated into the development of the constraint-solder Ficucs. In addition to the algorithms and data structures used in Ficucs, various applications, which use ficucs as a calculation module, and related models are described. The aim of the activities was to develop a constraint-solder that can be used in a variety of projects. Particular attention was paid to interactivity and the stability of the algorithms, which are very important for user acceptance. To this end, improvements were found again and again, largely implemented and thus verified. It was shown that the combination of different concepts in an application is often problematic. The present work should make the results achieved accessible to a more constructive approach and a hybrid approach.
content.title_en: Ficucs - a constraint-solder for geometric constraints in 2D and 3D : algorithms; use cases; modelling

content.text: Characterization of limiting factors in hybrid donor-acceptor solar cells. Hybrid photovoltaics is a new technology that is intended to combine the advantages of organic and inorganic solar cells. The dissertation here deals with the question of the causes of differences in the performance of hybrid and purely organic solar cells. Light-induced electron-spin resonance spectroscopy (l-ESR) as well as charge-based transient interference spectroscopy on hybrid layers were used to investigate the influence of organic stabilizer molecules on defects of nanoparticles. In the second part, the existence of charge transfer states in hybrid layers is shown by l-ESR. In the final part of the work, alternative concepts for the improvement of hybrid solar cells are presented and initial results presented. In summary, various limiting factors in hybrid solar cells can be found and characterized, so that these can be considered in future systems.
content.title_en: Characterisation of limiting factors in hybrid donor acceptor solar cells

content.text: Spectroscopic studies for the doping of polycrystalline CdTe layers for solar cells. Compared to the current industrial standard, significantly better efficiencies can be achieved with the semiconductor cadmium-telluride (CdTe) for solar cell applications, provided that basic physical properties of the material are better investigated. The aim of this dissertation is against this background the investigation of the photoluminescence (PL) of CdTe under the influence of chemical treatments, ion implantations and novel manufacturing methods and the correlation of the PL with the electrical properties of the solar cells processed from the corresponding material. In the PL untreated dTe layers a transition is detected for the first time, which can be associated with cadmium emptying. Furthermore, the phonon coupling of the dominant transition in the PL of chemically treated layers is correlated with the efficiencies of solar cells, which are processed from the corresponding layers. Also, connections with excitonic transitions in the PL are observed and interpreted. The ion implantation as a method of material modification allows the dotulation of the corresponding layering of the cell.
content.title_en: Spectroscopic investigations for doping polycrystalline CdTe layers for solar cells

content.text: Systemic risk in interbank markets. The aim of this thesis is to develop a better understanding of systemic risks on interbank markets. The importance of systemic risks for the stability of the entire financial system has become clear due to the international financial crisis of 2007/2008, which has led to one of the most severe recessions of the last hundred years. Starting from a crisis in the US real estate market, enormous distortions have occurred on the international capital markets as a result of the increasing interlinkage between financial institutions. These culminated in the collapse of US investment bank Lehman Brothers in September 2008 and led to an almost complete collapse of interbank credit markets in the following days. Banks rely on these mutual loans to compensate for short-term liquidity fluctuations on the pass-on side of their balance sheets and to sufficiently diversify the asset side. Without functioning interbank markets, banks cannot make time-transformation and provide the real economy with long-term loans. ...
content.title_en: Systemic risk in interbank markets

content.text: The thesis deals with the resistance behaviour of flexible, leafy vegetation and the resistance of the sole and vegetation in flowing fields. To this end, the research has systematically examined the vegetation density, vegetation arrangement, the roughness of the sole, the depth of flow and the plant structure in order to investigate the proportion of the resistance of the sole and vegetation in flowing fields. To quantify the resistance of vegetation, a new force measuring system has been developed which allows a direct and simultaneous determination of the resistance forces of up to ten vegetation elements with a high accuracy without affecting the flow field.In addition to artificial flexible vegetation elements, measurements with rigid, cylindrical vegetation elements have been made for better comparability with existing works.The results of the resistance of the sole showed that the proportion of the resistance of the sole can be in the same order as the resistance of the total resistance of the vegetation and not be neglected at all. The results also indicate that for the rigid and medium-flexible elements of the sole resistance are assumed to the total resistance of the flow.
content.title_en: Resistance to flexible vegetation and sole resistance in flowing fields

content.text: I am the musician with laptop in my hand!? : from the influence of technical innovations on the production process of electronic music; a review of the years 1997 to 2007. The focus of this work is the search for answers to the question of how technical innovations influenced the production process of electronic music in the years 1997 to 2007. In 2008, developers of technical innovations, specialist authors, artists and scientists from the field of electronic music were surveyed Germany-wide with the help of seventeen problem-centered interviews. This was connected with the aim of identifying and systematizing technical innovations in the production of electronic music and their influence on the production process in the sense of Grounded Theory. It was shown that the central innovations are the virtualization of the sound studio and the digital networking (peer production, democratisation of distribution, reputation economics, connection of supply and demand). Furthermore, this work offers a systematic differentiation of the concept of innovation as well as an overview of the development of electronic music from its beginnings to the present.
content.title_en: I am the musician with laptop in my hand!? : from the influence of technical innovations on the production process of electronic music ; a review of the years 1997 to 2007

content.text: Mechanical connections to the construction of optical high-performance systems. Optical technologies are considered to be one of the key technologies of the 21st century. The variety of optical systems and the requirements for these systems are constantly increasing and therefore make continuous development necessary from a scientific point of view. Optical systems are usually produced in multi-stage processes. Important process steps are the connection of optical components with mechanical components and the connection of already assembled optical components to optical systems. The present work shows the current state of development in the implementation of these connection tasks using optical high-performance systems and then presents possibilities for further development. The described viewing methods are transferable as well as the shown solution spaces generally to the design of mechanical connections and offer advantages especially for fine-work applications.
content.title_en: Mechanical connections for the construction of high-performance optical systems

content.text: The focus sensor of the nano-sensor is presented in a comprehensive way. The focus sensor of the nano-sensor is a practical focus sensor based on the focus sensor of the nano-sensor. The focus sensor is characterized by a high resolution and low measurement uncertainty. This nano-sensor system is primarily tailored to measuring applications in the nano-positioning and nano-sensor. A new focus sensor was developed as a base sensor for the nano-sensor system. The principle of this sensor is based on the focus measurement method developed for the DVD and CD player technology. The connection of both mechanical touch principles into the nano-sensor system is achieved by means of the developed focus sensor (base sensor). The focus sensor is directly connected to the focus sensor (cantilever or stylus) with focused laser beam of the focus sensor. The major advantage of the developed nano-sensor system is its modularity and versatility. The focus sensor of the focus sensor is presented in a comprehensive way.
content.title_en: Optical and tactile nanosensors based on the focus process for use in nanopositioning and nanometers

However, such names have only been preserved in the most favourable case to this day. Rather, a large number of still existing hall names are threatened with extinction. The present work provides a decisive contribution to the elimination of a research idea that exists in Thuringia. A methodological and factual basis is presented, in order to provide a foundation for research on the Thüringen land name, which has been conducted for decades only sporadic, uncoordinated and/or interested lay people, on the basis of which further projects can be started. ...
content.title_en: The Thuringian land name landscape : ways to explore

content.text: Opportunities and risks of commodity investments: a quantitative analysis of commodities as an asset class. Due to increasing correlations between traditional asset classes, historically low interest rates and high volatility of equity prices, alternative investments have increasingly become the focus of investors in recent years. Timo Klett conducts a comprehensive analysis of commodity investments by characterising yields in a comparison to traditional asset classes in a uni- and multi-variate context. The author develops a return model on which risk analyses and risk-adjusted performance analyses can be carried out. These illustrate in particular the diversification potential of commodities. However, the complexity and heterogeneity of this asset class must be considered, which high requirements on asset management make essential.
content.title_en: Opportunities and risks of raw material investments: a quantitative analysis of raw materials as an asset class

content.text: Support for children with a migrant background: an empirical study on objectives and measures in kindergarten. Kindergarten is generally attributed a central importance in the promotion of children with a migrant background. Through early educational offers and measures, it is intended to help support children of immigrant families in their educational and integration processes. Thilo Schmidt investigates, on the basis of three central migration pedagogical approaches, which goals and measures are pursued and implemented to promote children with a migrant background in kindergartens and in what proportion these goals and measures are related to each other and to specific framework conditions of educational work in kindergartens. The data were collected via a standardized postal survey of kindergarten managers in Bavaria. The statistical analysis of the data was carried out via multivariate analysis methods.
content.title_en: Promotion of children with a migrant background : an empirical study on objectives and measures in kindergarten

The mycotoxins citrinin, deoxynivalenol, ochratoxin A and sterigatocystin were quantified in the lower myg/kg house dust range. A clear link between a mold infestation and the detected mycotoxins could not be established. Using various LC-MS measurement methods, satratoxin G, H and their isomers of Stachybotry's chartarum were found to be less relevant despite the fact that mycotoxins are not present in the test of the test.

content.text: From supervised to unsupervised support vector machines and applications in astronomy. A classic problem of machine learning is the classification of objects. If there is enough training data, this concept often leads to models with excellent quality. However, the creation of a sufficiently large data set can prove to be costly for certain applications. Unlike such labeled training data, unlabeled data is often widely available. In order to include the latter in the learning process, the literature has included the so-called semi- and unsupervised support vector machines, but both extensions lead to difficult combinatorial optimization problems. The development of optimization approaches for both extensions is one of the central topics of the dissertation. Beyond these theoretical explanations, the application of machine learning techniques to current questions in astronomy is the subject of the work. <dt.>
content.title_en: From superb to unsupervised support vector machines and applications in astronomy

content.text: Synthesis of peptide mimetics and analogue compounds of heterocyclic imines. The focus of this work is the synthesis and derivatives of N,Xheterocyclic imines (X = O, S). Due to the reactive iminic double bond, these compounds are suitable as starting materials for various addition reactions. The targeted products are characterized by different structures of the peptide mimetics. In a UGI-3 component reaction, the representation of mono- and dithio-bisamides succeeds. A modified UGI-SMILES-3 component reaction with aromatic thiol compounds leads to N-Arylioamides. A two-stage synthesis consisting of an acid chloride addition and subsequent FISCHER indol synthesis, enables access to melatonin analogues, which contain a modifiable heteroatomium. Furthermore, the representation of bicyclic 2-imidazoles and imidazoles is performed. In addition, the addition, the addition, the addition reaction is examined under stereochemical aspect.
content.title_en: Synthesis of peptide mimetics and analogue compounds of heterocyclic imines

content.text: Social work in social assistance: a qualitative analysis of case processing. Rahel Müller de Menezes researches professional social worker/social pedagogical action in the administrative-organizational context using the example of specialists in social services in Switzerland. In the empirical study, four types of approaches in case handling could be reconstructed, which differ considerably in terms of their support potential for the clients. The lawyer type of case-specific fit corresponds to the criteria of social worker professionalism, but the other types are limited or not at all because the clients receive too little or inappropriate support or are penalised administratively and financially because of the non-compliance with demands. Rahel Müller de Menezes is a specialist high school professor at the Department of Social Work at the Bern University of Applied Sciences in Education and Research.
content.title_en: Social work in social assistance: a qualitative analysis of case handling

content.text: Intervention Study PRimus - Psychosocial Resources in Youth Sports : Methods and results of evaluation of programme implementation and program effectiveness. The concept "Psychosocial Resources in Sports" (Sygusch, 2007) establishes methodological measures for systematically promoting resources Self-concept, self-effectiveness, group cohesion and social competence. In the PRimus study, this concept was implemented in sports handball and gymnastics over seven months in the training everyday life of 29 training groups (age: 12-16 years). In an interview study with the trainers (N = 39) and a questionnaire study with the athletes (IG: N = 374; KG: N = 270) at three measuring times each, the implementation and feasibility of the concept was examined as well as the effectiveness of the targeted resources. The methodological measures are frequently and increasingly implemented in the sense of the concept during the intervention process and are assessed by the trainers in large parts as feasible.
content.title_en: Intervention study PRimus - Psychosocial resources in youth sport : Methods and results of evaluation of programme implementation and programme effectiveness

content.text: A probabilistic population forecast model : Development and application for Germany. Population forecasts have a far-reaching significance for the future design of various social areas of life, so the continuous improvement of their methodology is indispensable. Furthermore, the review of past population forecasts shows that their accuracy could not be significantly increased by the better data quality or by the previously improved methodology. For this reason Christina Bohk develops the probabilistic population projection model (PPPM) for the implementation of probabilistic population forecasts theoretically, implements it and applies it exemplaryly in a forecast for the population of Germany from 2007 to 2050.
content.title_en: A probabilistic population forecast model : Development and application for Germany

content.text: Family policy as a reform process: Germany and Austria compared. Family policy has been one of the policy areas with the highest reform activity in Germany and Austria during the last years. This was surprising for comparative welfare state research, since it has been regularly pointed out the inability of the so-called conservative, familial welfare states to reform in the field of new social risks such as the reconciliation of family and work. So how are these sudden, far-reaching reforms to explain? To answer this, Sonja Blum examines the reform processes in parental leave and public childcare, including the introduction of parental allowance in Germany in 2007 or the introduction of income-dependent childcare allowance in Austria in 2010. The book draws a comprehensive picture of the changed determinants of family policy in both countries, including new stakeholder constellations, new ideas and vertical and horizontal policy transfers in the context of an increased family policy commitment of the European Union.
content.title_en: Family policy as a reform process : Germany and Austria compared

content.text: Mentoring: Female Professionalism in the Beginning. Mentoring as a program has the potential to fundamentally renew gender constellations. Using eight individual analyses and the overarching consideration of an exemplary mentoring program, Christine Kurmeyer traces the internal structures and mechanisms of opportunities and obstacles in female career progressions. At the same time, she identifies potentials at the individual level, which demonstrate an overcoming of barriers to equal participation of women and men in professional and family work.Especially in the status passage of career entry, Mentoring creates security, especially for the female mentees, by confirming mentors and by supporting them in the first professional network with the other mentees. Mentoring offers guidance for all involved parties on role reflection - also the gender role stereotypes.
content.title_en: Mentoring : Female Professionalism in the Beginning

content.text: On the communication of risks: A study on social systems in flood risk management. Risks and the handling of them represent central challenges of modern society. Social relevance only becomes a reality by communicating risks. This also applies to natural risks such as floods. Swen Zehetmair gives a comprehensive insight into the various communication relationships that shape the social handling of flood risks and examines the social systems involved in flood risk management. Conflicts and cooperations, structural couplings as well as the problems of political control in flood risk management are discussed and challenges for risk management are illustrated.

content.text: Tool-supported development of secure wireless sensor networks. The development of safe systems is a very demanding task. In the field of wireless sensor networks, this is made even more difficult by the limited resources. This work is based on a tool-supported and model-based design process. This enables the automatic generation of applications based on finished components that meet the requirements of the application or application developer. In particular, this approach supports a holistic consideration and evaluation of safety aspects. In order to assess the fulfilment of the requirements, flexible exchangeable models for the evaluation of various functional and non-functional aspects can be provided. For the safety aspect, several concrete assessment models are evaluated in the work based on different views on a general safety model for wireless sensor networks and their modelling and application properties discussed. In the practical example of safe in-network aggregation, the quality and significance of the necessary modelling effort for each of these approaches are evaluated in the context of the work. This evaluation using the tools implemented in this work, not only demonstrates the general utility of the application tools, but also can help to implement the qualitatively-based approach of the problem of the use of the sensor networks in the future.
content.title_en: Tool-supported development of secure wireless sensor networks

Since then, several hundred people and horses have been infected with WNV annually, many with fatal outcome. In recent years, an increasing number of WNV outbreaks have been reported also in Europe. content.text: Realization of a voltage and current limitation control in the 3- and 1-phase insular grid with different loads with the help of the microcontroller XC 167. Then the control concept was developed and the control concept was implemented by using the microcontroller XC-167. content.text: A transformational approach to generic software development based on higher-order, typed functional signatures. This dissertation describes a method for developing generic software libraries based on a program transformation. More precisely, the signatures of generic, i.e. type parametric, functions are transformed from a functional language into an object-oriented language. Functional type constructs, such as functions of higher order and type constructors, are mapped on type parameters, which are specified with so-called terms. The method presented is independent of specific programming languages and can be formally secured on the other hand. This thesis introduces a method based on program transformation for developing generic software libraries. More precision, the signatures of generic functions, i.e., functions parameterised on types, are transformed from a function to a function to a function.
content.title_en: A transformal approach to generic software development based on higher-order, typed functional signatures

content.text: The simulation of the simulation of the plasma and ionized species is an overview of the simulation of the plasma and ionized species in micro- and nanostructured etching processes. The present work is about the spread of electrically neutral and charged particle species in plasma etching reactors under process conditions. To date, only simulations are able to obtain detailed knowledge about the species transport in microstructures. Therefore, the aim of this work is the development of simulation models, which can efficiently and accurately calculate the spread of the species inside microstructures. In the first part of the work, the physical properties, the generation of the plasma and the transport of species at very low pressure in the reactor are considered. To virtualize the processes in the reactor, possibilities of the simulation of material and energy flows as well as the state of the art in the field of plasma and topography simulation are outlined. The preliminary and disadvantages of various simulation techniques are analysed and the special requirements of an integrated plasma topography are discussed. The main part of the work is a completely new approach to the modelling of the propagation of the species in virtual scenes. In this section a general transport model is developed by the re-conducting of the microstructures.
content.title_en: Modelling of transport processes of neutral and ionized species in micro- and nanostructuring etching processes

content.text: In particular, the management of the task of the autonomous database tuning is being designed by the user. In recent decades, the administration of IT systems has become increasingly complex and costly. To ensure high availability and performance of these systems, continuous manual administration and optimization of the systems in ongoing operation are hardly enough. Initiatives such as the Autonomous Computing therefore try to reduce the administrative complexity of new systems by enabling automation of complex system management and configuration tasks and their subsequent transmission to the systems themselves. The present work aims to investigate the transferability of the concepts of autonomous computing to the database tuning and to design an infrastructure for automation typical database tuning tasks while reducing human interaction. As one of the basic prerequisites for automation of the database tuning tasks, the description and modelling of the tuning knowledge are identified here. The presented concepts therefore allow the administrators to capture both the problem situations and the corresponding proven tuning processes in the system. With the help of an architecture based on these concepts, the task of monitoring and pre-conducting the task of doing tasks are also being influenced by the task of performing tasks.
content.title_en: Description, management and execution of workflows in autonomous database tuning

content.text: The following examples are given: - Stability analysis of unconstrained receding horizon control schemes. The topic of this thesis is the model predictive regulation (MPC). In particular, neither end conditions nor end costs are included in the problem formulation. The aim is to show a relaxed Lyapunov imbalance in order to be able to follow asymptotic stability of the or quality estimates on the control circuit closed by means of model predictive regulation. To this end, based on a controllability assumption, a stability condition is derived, which is subsequently subjected to a sensitivity analysis regarding the predictive and control horizon. The latter leads to criteria for the design of appropriate step costs and also allows the detection of useful symmetry and monotony properties, which form the basis for the subsequent algorithm development. The use of the so motivated algorithms allows the prediction horizon to be examined with a view to reducing the guaranteed rule-level and thus significantly reducing the computational effort. Many examples of the parameterized rule-like analysis are derived from the derived from the derived function.
content.title_en: Stability analysis of unconstrained receding horizon control schemes

content.text: Binary and ternary lanthanum triel tetral-ide : synthesis, crystal chemistry and chemical binding. Summary: In this work, systematic preparatory and structural investigations of intermetallic phases of the systems La-Sn, La-Al-Sn, La-Ga-Sn, La-Ge-Sn, La-In-Si, La-Si-Sn and La-In-Pb were performed. The compounds were characterized by X-ray and Rietveld methods and the chemical binding was analyzed using band structure calculations. Summary: In the present work systematic prepariative and structural investigations of the systems La-Sn, La-Al-Sn, La-Ga-Sn, La-Ge-Sn, La-In-Si and La-In-Pb have been made. The structural characterization of the intermetallic phases was carried out by means of X-ray diffraction using Rietstal and singing on the mixture.
content.title_en: Binary and ternary lanthanum triel tetral-ides : synthesis, crystal chemistry and chemical binding

content.text: Competition law aspects of domains and search engines : the legal situation in Germany and Austria. Folding text: Discover the dark side of domains & search engines! The creation, application and operation of websites are often costly. To better understand the domains, legal aspects are presented and an overview of the domain name system, technical aspects and the procurement procedure is given. The work deals with the competitive framework conditions of domains and search engines, one of the most used services on the Internet. This is the decisive role in the search for relevant content and websites on the Internet. The procedural enforcement including the dispute settlement procedures can also be found in this compendium of domain law.
content.title_en: Competition aspects of domains and search engines : the legal situation in Germany and Austria

content.text: Calculation of the overlay in primary school : Solution behaviour of children in direct and indirect overlay questions. Calculation of the overlay is an important topic of primary school mathematics, which has hardly been empirically researched. Sabrina Hunke conducts an interview study with 42 children of the fourth year of school to investigate their solution behavior in the overlay calculation. To this end, tasks of the type "How much about?" and "Does money?" are used, i.e. direct and indirect overlay questions. The evaluation is qualitatively carried out in the areas of procedures, flexibility, components of the overlay process and errors. The author not only shows the great importance of rounding rules for many children, but also the specificities of the indirect type of task, and develops concrete consequences for the teaching from this analysis.
content.title_en: Primary school rollover calculation : child response to direct and indirect rollover questions
