content.text: The study examines the influence of microstructure (crystallite size and microdistortion), particle size and BET surface and bulk density on catalytic activity and the coupling behaviour in the microwave field. The parameters were varied by five different synthesis routes over three orders of magnitude. In the field of catalysis, both liquid phase catalysis and (microwave-assisted) gas phase catalysis are investigated. In order to determine the coupling behaviour in the microwave field at a frequency of 2.45 GHz, a measuring apparatus with a differentiated measuring position for the electric and magnetic field component of the microwave field has been developed. The microstructure of the catalysts clearly influences the catalytic activity, whereas particle size and bulk density play a greater role in the coupling behaviour and the microstructure exerts a lesser influence. The frequently found flat-rate neglect of the magnetic field component is not acceptable for magnetisable catalysts. The two-stage catalytic converters are optimized for the detection of the two-phase catalytic converters.

content.text: Evaluation, analysis and optimization of direct-push sensor systems. Global ecological questions regarding soil and groundwater pose a major challenge for mankind. The exploration of the surface-close earth body provides a significant contribution to the response, evaluation and derivation of solutions of essential environmental questions. Modern direct-push sensor systems are used to explore this, allowing rapid and efficient in-situ measurement in a vertical profile. For the future development of this exploration technology, a systematic classification and description is developed in this work. To evaluate and optimize existing sensor systems, a methodological approach is presented, based on the analysis of laboratory and field scale experiments and their mathematical modelling. This method for the analysis of direct-push sensor systems is suitable for the analysis of direct-push sensor systems in deductive form in the case of synthetic developments and implementations of physical, chemical or biological sensor systems. An essential application of direct-push sensor systems is the exploration of contamination in soil and groundwater. One of these sensor systems is measured by the membrane interface of sample (MIP) as a method of analysis for the use of the method of analysis, which is not reliably evaluated in terms of the analysis of the measurement of the measurement.
content.title_en: Evaluation, analysis and optimization of direct-push sensor systems

content.text: Total synthesis of the Marine Macrolid Palmerolid A : Access to a natural substance with a pharmacologically promising active profile. Palmerolid A was isolated for the first time in 2006 and showed a very strong and exceptionally selective cytotoxic activity compared to selected cancer cell lines in cell biology. As a 20-member macrolactone with five stereocenters, several isolated and conjugated double binding units and a dienamide-bearing side chain, the highly functionalized natural substance offers interesting challenges from a structural point of view for the synthesis chemist. In the context of this study, a strategy was developed that allows total synthetic access to this highly potent molecule. A remarkable amount of the natural substance could be provided via the synthesis sequence described here to examine its pharmacological and toxicological properties in detail.
content.title_en: Total synthesis of the marine macrolid Palmerolid A : Access to a natural substance with pharmacologically promising active profile

content.text: Multisensual design of the shop atmosphere for profiling store brands: a theoretically guided, experimental design for shopper behaviour. The focus of the work is the increasing displacement of the stationary retail through the Internet and the question of how physical shops can resist this. One starting point for this is the creation of a shopping experience that appeals to all senses and is also in line with the brand of the shop. Especially a brand-appropriate implementation of the shop design is often in the back of the list when creating shopping experiences. In the empiricity of the work a theoretically guided experiment is carried out to optimize the shop atmosphere in the stationary textile retail trade. The work focuses on the stimuli music, fragrance and colors: their effect on brand perception, buyer behaviour and turnover is examined in the business premises of a women's clothing chain.
content.title_en: Multisensual design of the shop atmosphere for profiling store brands : a theoretical, experimental design for shopper behavior

content.text: The global configuration of political cultures: a theoretical and empirical analysis. Can the global pattern of politically-following culture/s be described rather as unity, diversity or hybridity? This question fuels the sociological debate about cultural globalization, cultural circles and global mélange as well as the political-theoretical universalism-relativism controversy. Sophia Schubert establishes a separate research strand in the paradigm of political culture for its conceptually precise and systematic empirical analysis: diversity research. The central finding of the analyses is that none of the three theoretical positions (unity, diversity, hybridity) are sufficient to interpret the global configuration of political cultures alone. They are complementary.
content.title_en: Global configuration of political cultures : a theoretical and empirical analysis

content.text: Disease in the Center : Design of disease-oriented hospital structures from cybernetic - constructivist perspective. Astrid Peben develops a structural model of disease-oriented centers at university hospitals. The model is based on a cybernetic-constructivist perspective as well as the findings from extensive individual studies in Eusoma-accredited university breast centers. The author shows which structures an ideal-typical center should have for the purpose of optimal patient care and which are the main challenges in the change process.
content.title_en: Disease in the Center : Design of disease-oriented hospital structures from cybernetic - constructivist perspective

content.text: The interaction between entrepreneurial innovation and art: a scientific study in the Renaissance and the example of the Medici. The examination of artistic forms of work and expression promotes entrepreneurial innovation, since there is an inner relationship between both. Jeannette zu Fürstenberg follows this thesis by studying economic and artistic innovations of the Renaissance and by working out the role of the Medici as entrepreneurs and patrons. Due to a structural examination of princeships of entrepreneurship, innovation and art, she shows that the historical phenomenon can be instructive even for today's entrepreneurship.
content.title_en: The interaction between entrepreneurial innovation and art: a scientific study in the Renaissance and the example of the Medici

content.text: The internationality of top managers: share price reactions to the designation of international boards of directors and supervisory boards. Many German companies have long been operating in international markets. Following the demands of science and corporate practice, top managers should be led across borders, which in turn have a sufficient degree of internationality. But how can the internationality of a top manager be measured? And exists between the constructs "internationality of a top manager" and "company success" an effect relationship? Tobias Dauth contributes to the identification of international top managers - empirical results of the quantitative study - implications for corporate practice and future research projects. The content: The state of research on the internationality of top managers - theoretical conceptual basis for the analysis of the capital market reactions on the designation of international top managers - empirical results of the quantitative study - implications for corporate practice and future research projects. The target groups: doctoral students and students of economic sciences with the focus on international management and executives who are engaged in strategic tasks in the fields of diversity and international management.
content.title_en: The internationality of top managers: share price reactions to the designation of international boards of directors and supervisory boards

content.text: Measurement and control of communication efficiency : a theoretical and empirical analysis by using data development analysis. Increasing competitive pressure forces companies to use their marketing budgets effectively and efficiently. Especially in communication controlling, systematic measurement and control of communication efficiency is increasingly required, which is transparent and comprehensible. Jürgen Schwarz identifies a promising method and checks its applicability for measuring communication efficiency both theoretically and in empirical studies. The author derives recommendations for communication controlling as well as implications for measuring communication efficiency.
content.title_en: Measurement and control of communication efficiency : a theoretical and empirical analysis by using data development analysis

content.text: Analysis of strategies of the automotive industry to reduce CO2 fleet emissions and market launch of alternative drives: a system-dynamic approach using California's legislation. The requirements of the automotive industry are increasing worldwide in terms of reducing CO2 fleet emissions and market launch of alternative vehicle drives. Jörg Wansart is developing a simulation tool for the analysis of strategies of the automotive industry to meet the legal requirements of Greenhouse Gases (GHG) and Zero Emission Vehicles (ZEV) in California. The potential of the developed tool is demonstrated in the context of a comprehensive case study for the Californian market.
content.title_en: Analysis of strategies of the automotive industry to reduce CO2 fleet emissions and to market alternative drives: a system-dynamic approach using California legislation

content.text: Chitosan as a carrier material for catalysts for selected liquid phase reactions. In the present work, chitosan was examined for its suitability as a carrier material for catalysts. In addition, the biopolymer chitosan was modified by inserting side groups or by networking. This was used, among others, dialdehyde, diisocyanates, salicylaldehyde and other substances. The carrier systems thus produced were loaded with Pd(II) compounds and subsequently chemically reduced by NaBH4. The support and catalysts obtained in this way were characterized by IR spectroscopy, ICP-MS, TGA and elementary analysis. The catalysts were mainly used in liquid phase hydration of unsaturated carbonyl compounds, olefins, alkines and other eductes. A modern microwave reactor system was used. The activity of the catalysts was examined, while the selectivity regarding the hydrogenation of various functional groups was investigated.
content.title_en: Chitosan as a carrier material for catalysts for selected liquid phase reactions

content.text: Participation in the knowledge society : function and importance of discursive participation procedures. ?How can quality and legitimacy of political decisions be guaranteed and improved in contemporary (knowledge) societies? For some years now, the involvement of additional actors in political will-building and decision-making beyond representative democratic institutions and procedures has been increasingly demanded, not only in the Federal Republic of Germany. These demands are aimed at the inclusion of citizens with their specific knowledge, values and perceptions of problems in the sense of "participatory policy advice".
content.title_en: Participation in the knowledge society : function and importance of discursive participation procedures

content.text: The first time the information is given to the new world: the transfer of the transatlantic telegraph cable to the public is not the same thing. In the summer of 1858, the first electric telegraph cable was installed between Europe and America. The spectacular underwater connection was supposed to overcome space and time - a project that seemed to justify the greatest technical effort and considerable financial commitment. It is considered the birth of virtual communication. Christian Holtorf, however, with the first knowledge history of the Atlantic cable, shows that this company was initially a failure. The cable connection worked only for just under four weeks. His research in British, Canadian and US archives revealed that misunderstandings, errors and misconduct determined the technical development: The visionaries were deceived, the engineers ruined the technology, and the investors lost their money. "Holtorf creates a multifaceted and well-founded panorama of the transatlantic telegraph cable's relocation. Perhaps the first wire to the new world was therefore not a narrative of the triumph of technology over space and time, but a precise measurement of the frame of the assignment was only possible in the case of the current and of the time-round techniques.
content.title_en: The first wire to the New World: the laying of the Transatlantic Telegraph Cable

content.text: The practice of seeing: the interplay of bodies, artifacts and visual order. The debates of the Visual Culture Studies, which have been primarily oriented towards the theoretical aspects of images, are being extended to include a new dimension in this book: the objects of material culture. Sophia Prinz undertakes for the first time the complete reconstruction of a theory of visuals, which was not systematically developed in Michel Foucault's writings. This perspective is further sharpened in the examination of the perception theories of Jacques Lacan, Maurice Merleau-Ponty and Pierre Bourdieu and developed into a comprehensive dispositive analytical heuristic. With a view to the interplay between the world of things, the cultural perception schemes and the practice of seeing, seeing thus proves to be an active participation in the shaping of the world as well as in the shaping of one's own subjectivity.
content.title_en: The practice of seeing: about the interplay of bodies, artifacts and visual order

It is a sign of an aesthetic that is asserted precisely by the fact that it constantly subverts itself and challenges itself. Science is expected to divide it from this, but for several decades far-reaching attempts have been made in currents of cognitive biology and systems sociology to "observ itself from outside" (Luhmann). Unlike the literary ones, it seems to be primarily about ideological self-concertation. content.text: The city hall swimming pool in Germany from 1870 to 1930. The book deals with the urban indoor swimming pools built between 1870 and 1930. Its task was to provide the entire population with a covered washing and swimming facility in the form of shower, bath and sweat baths as well as swimming pools. - - The study is based on a broad material foundation. For the specified period, around 200 indoor swimming pools were proved, of which 55 baths were described and analysed in detail. - - The development of the architecture of the urban indoor swimming pool is presented and classified as a historical building. As part of the complex municipal construction task, the bathroom was in the tension field between purpose and representation building, whereby the decorative architecture corresponded to the conditions of the bathing facility and technology. - To draw a comprehensive picture, the economic and social framework conditions that were characteristic for the development of the municipal building task indoor swimming pool during the period considered are included in the study. - Until then the architectural development of the baths was not yet comprehensively examined and considered. Thus, the work makes an important contribution to the systematic research of the 19th century developed new types of construction architects and community-types for the new types of construction.
content.title_en: The municipal indoor swimming pool in Germany from 1870 to 1930

content.text: Time- and space-efficient self-stabilizing algorithms. Self-stabilization is an approach that enables a distributed system to tolerate arbitrary transient errors. This dissertation presents new self-stabilizing algorithms for known graph theory problems. In addition, existing procedures are examined on their complexity. The focus of this work is on the methods of proof used in complexity analysis, as well as on the design of algorithms. Self-stabilization is a general approach to design a system to to tolerate arbitrary transient faults. This thesis presents new time- and space-efficient self-stabilizing algorithms for well-known problems in graph theory and provides new complexity analyses for existing algorithms. The main focus of this thesis is on the proof techniques used in the complexity analysis and the design of the algorithms.
content.title_en: Time- and space-efficient self-stabilizing algorithms

content.text: The importance of the privilege under § 35 BauGB for the financing of biogas plants. Many biogas plants have been built in an external area prior to § 35 BauGB. The privilege status for biomass plants contains a variety of undefined legal concepts which can lead to legal uncertainties for operators and financing credit institutions. In this work the importance of the privilege is illustrated by the possibilities of a subsequent removal. Here, possible scenarios and the resulting effects on the financing of biogas plants are shown. In addition, different protection and solution options are presented. Through the evaluation of banking and public authorities interviews as well as the relevant literature, practical results can be obtained. Many biogas plants have been built in an external area prior to § 35 BauGB. content.text: Functional analysis of the anion transporter Slc4a8 with the help of constitutive knockout mouse models. The cellular pH regulation is of particular importance in the brain, as pH here affects the excitability of neurons, but neuronal activity can also cause changes in pH. The aim of this work was to investigate the physiological significance of the Na+-dependent anion exchanger Slc4a8 in mammalian brain and kidney, as well as the comparative analysis of the transporter Slc4a10. Slc4a8 showed a broad neuronal expression pattern. Hippocampal neurons of mice with a targeted deletion of the Slc4a8 gene showed a decreased basal intracellular pH and recovered more slowly from acidification. In accordance with the detection of Slc4a8 in presynaptic nerve formation, electrophysiological investigations also revealed a pH-dependent defect of presynapse. This was also characterized by a decrease in pharmaco-transcepts in the presence of pharmaco-in.
content.title_en: Functional analysis of the anion transporter Slc4a8 with the help of constitutive knockout mouse models

content.text: Mineral plaster and masonry mortars are proven building materials whose mechanical and structural properties are thoroughly investigated. However, little is known about their ecological behaviour under real climate conditions. In this work an experimental approach is pursued by exposing single and multilayer plaster and masonry mortar variants of different composition over three years to real climate influences. Rainwater, which is drained from the test bodies during rain events, is examined for summary parameters as well as inorganic and organic ingredients. In this way, selected single-layer variants are analysed by means of established laboratory methods for their release from substances when exposed to water. This results in comprehensive and systematic findings about the leaching behaviour of ingredients. The orienting application of the laboratory methods allows initial conclusions to be drawn as to how far the behaviour of irrigated plaster and masonry mortars can be mapped under real conditions with simple laboratory methods.
content.title_en: Environmental properties of mineral working mortar

content.text: Migrant workers in Beijing: spatial, social and economic aspects of a current migration problem in China. China's booming economic giant is getting more and more attention from politics, business, science and the public. At the same time, however, internal social problems and the major regional disparities of the country are also addressed. Reports on the situation of migrant workers in the country's major cities are also increasing. Although science has also taken on this topic, there is still a lack of research, especially those who study this phenomenon in depth and systematically with empirical surveys "on the ground". The dissertation by Ling He is thus a gap in the way it is designed. The focus is on the everyday life of migrant workers in Beijing. The thesis also addresses the advantages that the city, which counts about 17 million inhabitants, creates through the employment of the approximately 3 million migrant workers, and it points to the social and economic problems that must be solved in the context of migration.
content.title_en: Migrant workers in Beijing: spatial, social and economic aspects of a current migration problem in China

content.text: Pilot study on the applicability of an integrated concept for the decentralized treatment of wastewater and waste. This is due to a number of scandals that are shocking in Germany, such as the train accident in Eschede, the Gammelfleisch scandal or the smearing affair at Siemens. content.text: Investigations on the taxonomy of the genus Riemerella and diagnosis of Riemerella infections in domestic poultry and pigeons. Riemerella, Diagnostik, Taxonomy. - Riemerella anatipestifer (RA) and Riemerella columbina (RC) form the gene Riemerella within the family Flavobacteriaceae. RA has great economic significance as a pathogen of the "Infectious Serositis" of the water poultry, as well as as as secondary pathogens of other poultry species, especially the turkey. In Germany RA is particularly widespread in regions with high poultry density. In contrast, RC has been isolated from pigeons. The importance of the germ as a pathogen is still largely unclear, even if its detection in pure culture from pathologically modified organs of diseased pigeons suggests at least optional pathogenous potential. In spite of the great economic importance of RA, there are still many questions about Riemerella's diagnosis ....

content.text: The cult figure and nation : public monuments in Paris, Berlin and London ; 1848 - 1914. Not only nation states, but the idea of the nation itself has a history. The research of recent years has decoded them more and more as "imaginated community". Despite its undeniably sweeping and many evocative creative power, the modern nation is best understood as a cultural entity, as a complex bundle of drafts of order and collective affinities. Building monuments is a - decisive - characteristic of national identification. In a transnational comparison Helke Rausch spans up monument topographies in the metropolises of Paris, Berlin and London. She examines how monuments were used as iconographic means to create and cement the nation as a unit.
content.title_en: Cult figure and nation : public monuments in Paris, Berlin and London ; 1848 - 1914

content.text: Topological phase transitions of HgSe under uniaxial pressure. By means of initial calculations, the influence of uniaxial pressure on the strip structure of the zinc-blend semimetal mercury selenide (HgSe) is investigated. Both slight elongation and compression along the [001] and [110] directions open a band gap near the gamma point of up to 37 meV. Calculations of the Z2 invariant show that HgSe is in the phase of a topological insulator under uniaxial compression of about -5%. Both stronger compression and strain cause a transition into the phase of an ordinary insulator. Calculations on an HgSe multilayer system show surface states with great similarity to dirac-claws of known topological insulators. The work is divided into a comprehensive introduction, a chapter on the presentation of theoretical foundations, a part of results, and a final chapter on conclusions.
content.title_en: Topological phase transitions of HgSe under uniaxial pressure

content.text: Missing values in the social sciences: Analysis and correction with examples from the ALLBUS. Missing values have always been a major methodological challenge for quantitative analyses in the social sciences. Method research indicates that in some areas the problem of missing values will become even more acute. In this work, the most important theories on item and unit nonresponse are first summarized. Using examples from the ALLBUS, analyses on item and unit nonresponse are then carried out. In addition, correction methods for missing values are compared by a new method based on real data. In this context, the focus of the method comparison is on the multiple imputation as a correction method. The results speak clearly for the application of multiple imputation in Item nonresponse, especially in multivariate analyses. Although the results for unit nonresponse do not allow clear recommendations, the way to use multiple imputation there seems to be an alternative to weightings if the data situation is favourable.

content.text: Spectral gaps of indefinite storm-liouville operators. The thesis contains two main results: (A) For locally definable relations, it is shown that the finiteness of the number of eigenvalues in a real spectral gap of the essential spectrum is maintained under finite-dimensional disturbances. (B) For a subclass of locally definable relations, namely for relations with finally many negative squares, the number of eigenvalues of the disturbed relation in a real spectral gap of the essential spectrum is estimated upwards/lower by the number of eigenvalues of the undestructive relation and other correction variables. Here, only one-dimensional disturbances are considered. Furthermore, the evidence that the eigenvalues presented in this doctoral publication are sharp. content.text: The study examined the influence of individual media use on attitudes towards nuclear power plants, using the example of the planned extension of the duration of German nuclear power plants in 2010. The study was conducted in a two-method design. In a representative telephone survey, the settings and media usage behaviour of n=551 Thuringian were collected. The arguments in the reporting for or against an extension of the duration were collected by a quantitative content analysis of n=480 media contributions. In the data connection, variables on individual media input were formed from the arguments from the reporting. On the basis of these variables, attitude effects were examined. The findings showed that the individual media input of arguments influenced attitudes towards atomic power both in the medium and the long term. It was also clear that attitudes towards the extension of the duration were better predicted by general attitudes to atomic power, energy and politics than by the individual use of media communication content.
content.title_en: Extension of the duration of nuclear power plants - No, thank you!? : a communication-scientific study on the influence of media communication on attitudes towards nuclear power

content.text: In this work, various possibilities were investigated to increase the mechanical load capacity of optical coatings by selecting the coating materials and adjusting the coating design. The influence of the separation conditions on the load capacity of different coating materials was investigated by means of individual layers and the mechanical characteristics of the materials were determined. Comparative measurements on reflections with different materials and different layer thicknesses investigate the influence of the corresponding parameters on mechanical load capacity. Based on the characteristics specified on individual layers, the stress conditions of different layer systems were calculated under indentation load using an elasticity theoretic model. The stress loads encountered in the model provide plausible justification for the damage caused by experimentally produced layer systems. This stress analysis is used to select mechanical loadable layer designs with optical function. The layer systems produced in this way show an increased mechanical load capacity compared to the previously used dereflection systems.
content.title_en: Layer design taking into account optical and mechanical properties

content.text: Applying Markov for controlling abox abduction. The manual creation of annotations to multimedia documents is a time and cost-intensive task. In this work we define an agent for media interpretation that automatically generates annotations to multimedia documents. The agent's observations are given by superficial information extracted by means of modern media analysis tools. Based on background knowledge, the agent interprets these observations by derivating explanations on a higher level. Observations and their explanations form the notes to a multimedia document. To this end, we examine an abbation algorithm that determines explanations by using a logic-based knowledge representationalism. For certain media content, several explanations may be possible. As the agent is only available to determine the explanations, we must use a first order procedure in terms of the calculation process and depth of calculated results.
content.title_en: Applying Markov logics for controlling abort reduction

content.text: Violence, poverty and ignorance: the division of labour between the state and the private sector in the treatment of selected neglected problems - Germany in intra- and international comparison. Violence, poverty and ignorance can be considered as the problems that the society of the state needs to combat. However, the patterns of the division of labour between the public and the private sector differ from country to country and they are subject to change processes. This paper is devoted to six empirical studies of selected phenomena, causes and consequences of such variation, which have been neglected by political science, and such changes in six policy areas: asylum, protection of the population, protection of old age, biodiversity, education and research and development. A particular focus is on the absolute and relative position of Germany in all empirical individual analyses. In this case, the writing does not shy away from recommendations for reform. As a result, scepticism about the general state and private sector's ability to solve problems, but greater confidence about area-specific, quite differently accentuated work-sharing arrangements.
content.title_en: Violence, poverty and ignorance: the division of labour between the state and the private sector in the treatment of selected neglected problems - Germany in intra- and international comparison

content.text: The cultural and architectural history of the German crematoria. The changed burial behaviour since the end of the 19th century shows from the beginning a reordering of the rites and habits. Very close interweaving of art and architecture history with social history can be seen. Ulrich Hübner's aim was to explore the artistic and architectural diversity of the crematoria in Germany as a whole, with the Saxon crematoria forming a special heavy and high point. The author takes the interaction between art and the fundamental reformation of the burial culture around 1900 into his eyes. content.text: Fracture experiments of single grain boundaries in ductile metals. The plastic deformation of the bending beams was predicted by means of a finite element crystal plasticity model calibrated by means of pressure tests on single crystalline micro-bars. The fracture parameters of the grain boundaries were then determined within the framework of a cohesive zone model. A method to investigate the fracture of a single grain boundary in ductile metals is developed based on micro-cantilever bending experiments. The plastic deformation of the cantilevers is anticipated by a finite element crystal plasticity model which is calibrated making use of micro-compression experiments on single crystal micro-models. The fractures of the particles are determined by a finite element crystal plasticity model which is calibrated.

content.text: The present work deals with the development of numerical methods for the simulation of solidification processes. In the simulation of solidification processes, two major problem areas exist: a large need for computational time and an undesired anisotropic influence of the simulation grid. For this purpose, a modification was implemented, which reduced the increased growth of the boundary area in grid direction and at the same time strengthens the physical-pole preferred growth direction. Together with the high-level function method selected after thorough evaluation, for the calculation of the krümmungsmethode, which was not used in the solidification simulation, was implemented, the modification was simulated thedritic growth away from the grid direction. It succeeded to significantly reduce the grid influence and to achieve randomly stable progress in the field of analysis.

content.text: The design of a regulatory framework for selective damping of selected harmonics, taking into account permissible limit values for electrical energy quality parameters. It is known that the active filter against the harmonics is very effective and will eliminate the problems arising from this. However, the cost of an active filter to improve the grid quality is very high. To ensure the grid quality, the voltage effective values of each harmonics must not exceed a certain limit value. The utilization of these limit values requires a control method for the active filter, which finds the optimum between the grid quality on the one hand and the consumers on the other hand. The present work presents a control method, by which the voltage harmonics at the transfer point of a three-phase system are limited to a defined value. For this purpose, an impedance model with a fast current control is used. The model parameters of impedance are determined by a grid impedance measurement. In addition to the voltage harmonics, current harmonics in the three-phase conductor system cause many problems for the entire electrical energy system, in particular a neutral conductor can be used to compensate for the current frequency. The determination of the current can be avoided by means of a minimum voltage frequency.
content.title_en: Development of a control method for selective damping of selected harmonics, taking into account permissible limits for electrical energy quality parameters

content.text: Optimization of a cryogenic current comparator for use as a beam monitor. The non-contact, non-reactive monitoring of particle beams in the nA range is one of the challenges in accelerator technology. One way to solve this problem is to detect the magnetic field from the particle beam. In the context of this work, a detector system was optimized based on the principle of the cryogenic current comparator (CCC) with regard to noise-limited resolution. In the cryogenic current comparator, the magnetic field is measured by a superconducting pick-up coil and a superconducting current sensor (DC-SQUID), which are surrounded by a superconducting shielding. It can be shown that the noise-limited resolution of the detector is significantly influenced by the low temperature properties of the pick-up coil and thus the ferromagnetic core material used in the coil. For this purpose, extensive temperature and frequency-dependent pertoxicity of the reactor was reduced.
content.title_en: Optimization of a cryogenic current comparator for use as a beam monitor

content.text: The aim of this dissertation is to investigate determinants of the short-term and long-term use of smart meters and related products. The Rubikon model, as well as the results of technological acceptance research and environmental psychology research on energy use and lifestyles, is developed on this basis. The project uses the RESIDENS project to collect the data required by means of a panel design with three waves. In the process of data collection, a mix of methods is used to collect objective and subjective data. The examination of measurement models and the LIMA model is carried out by means of structural equation models and path analyses. With small adjustments, the models describe the empirical data relatively well. Overall, the study results show that smart metering and related products are accepted by a part of the population both on the current state of the art and in a future scenario with automated control of household appliances. These are part of the population using the first-nov technologies.
content.title_en: Development and review of a long-term smart meter model : a three-wave panel study

content.text: Intelligent electronic patient records: design and application of a model of action for the development of knowledge-based systems to support medical documentation processes. Medical treatment documentation is a key knowledge-intensive process for medical decision-making and for the control of patient treatment in health institutions. It requires the application of general medical knowledge, which is no longer available to the physician at the same time due to its power and dynamics. This information requirement has led to different forms of knowledge management and knowledge-based systems in medicine. Standards for methodological modelling and implementation of such software do not yet exist due to the research status of many approaches. The optical-bragg-gritters (FBG) are used as fiber-integrated reflectors in the laser-diameter process. content.text: Production of surface nanostructures by means of crystallizing diblockcopolymers. The self-organization of diblockcopolymers is a promising approach to the production of periodic nanostructures, which can also be transferred to surfaces by means of thin films. In crystalline diblockcopolymers, the shape and size of the nanostructures can be directly influenced by the crystallization process, which enables the production of adjustable nanostructures. The aim of the work was to produce defined adjustable surface nanostructures by controlled crystallization of semi- and double crystalline diblockcopolymers. The first demonstration was that in the context of a combined self-nucleation experiment, the surface nanostructures of a semicrystalline diblockcopolymer were controlled and pre-speakable by thermally induced thickening of crystalline lamellae. The realignment processes during the thickening were examined in situ, visualized and discussed at molecular level. The formation of crystalline double lamellae was also demonstrated for the first time. Moreover, it was shown that branching of the crystalline block was able to adjust the resulting nanostructures strongly.
content.title_en: Production of surface nanostructures by crystallizing diblock copolymers

content.text: Studies of selected breast cancer cell lines using Raman microspectroscopy and chemometric methods. Breast cancer is one of the most common causes of death in the world's female population with approximately 460,000 deaths annually. Detailed tumour characterization is necessary to develop appropriate cancer therapy. Raman microspectroscopy is used to objectively support pathologists during tumour diagnosis by providing molecular biological information. In this research, chemometric methods were used to evaluate the Raman data of individual cells, thereby realising classification and identification experiments. Here, cell nuclei spectra were correctly assigned to the breast gland cell lines MCF-10A and MCF-7 with an accuracy of 99%. Differentiation of Raman data from six malignant breast cancer cell lines showed that single Raman spectra could be correctly assigned to an accuracy of almost 100%. Classifications according to the cell line origin (pleural effusion and solid tumor) were shown to be of greater potential in the clinical field.

In this work, systems consisting of GaAs and ultrathin platinum layers are investigated using XPS, SPM and static and time-resolved nonlinear optical methods (SHG). The quality of the interfaces is characterized by different process parameters and their strong influence on the electronic properties of the space charging zone and thus on the SHG signal. Time-resolved measurements demonstrate the great influence of metal deposition on the dynamics within this surface-related sample range, both in terms of charge carrier processes and coherent grid vibrations.
content.title_en: Real-time investigations of energy dissipation processes at interfaces between semiconductors and thin metallic films

content.text: Global and first-mover benefits of internet-based business models. The question of pioneer advantages on the Internet has so far been insufficiently researched. Jantje Halberstadt empirically examines this question and shows that first-mover benefits exist in national markets, which is based essentially on the argument that national first-movers can combine the advantages of the first in the national market with the advantages of the successor from a global point of view. The first-mover benefits are more pronounced, the more intensive network effects come to bear. In addition, the first-mover hypothesis is often based on winner-take-all markets, in which a single provider prevails in the long term. However, the study shows that no sustainable monopoly gains can generally be assumed - especially the weaker network effects. The content: first-movers in Internet markets - global and first-mover network effects. The target groups: lecturers and students of business economics with the emphasis on management and entrepreneurship; business founder, founding consultant and practitioner are working at Tje Halbenburg University. The author is Dr.
content.title_en: Global and first-mover benefits of internet-based business models

content.text: The Bologna reform is a substantial transformation of the structures and contents of the study programmes offered by European universities. The reform of the internal structure of the study programmes as an internal structure of this reform is an immense challenge in terms of intellectual, temporal and organizational aspects. But how did the universities manage this task? Accreditation played the role of the problem causer, instead of guiding and orienting. content.text: Efficiency and effectiveness through defence cooperation: Impacts within the European Union. Defence cooperation can lead to economic and military advantages. Philipp Gallhöfer sets up a theoretical model to calculate the quantitative effects of defence cooperation. The model is used in four case studies, among others with the European Air Transport Command in Eindhoven and with the I. German-Dutch Corps in Münster. The case studies show that besides cost savings (efficiency) also better military capabilities (efficacy) can arise through international cooperation. Cooperation therefore offers the EU states an opportunity to react to the defence economy problem from declining defence budgets and at the same time rising defence costs. content.text: The process development for the chemical pretension of thin glasses. When the glass is preloaded below the transformation area (Tg), smaller ions of the glass (usually Na+) are replaced with larger ions of a contact medium (usually K+). As a direct consequence of the increased space requirements of K+ compared to Na+, mechanical pressure stresses arise in the near-surface volume ranges of the glass, which make it difficult to spread surface cracks and thus solidify the workpiece. As the current state of the art of the work results in the chemical preloading on an industrial scale over several hours of immersion of the glass into a potassium nitrate melt, it can only be inadequately integrated into the generally continuous process of glass production. The resulting objective of the work was therefore to develop a continuous process for the chemical preloading of thin glasses. A first basic process concept was developed from the variety of the solution variants that were in question, namely, that the coating of the glass surface with a potassium-containing salt in combination with a subsequent heat treatment of a tunnel furnace was intended for the process of testing.
content.title_en: Process development for the chemical pretension of thin glasses

content.text: Wave-current interactions in coastal areas. Many coastal areas are exposed to a risk of flooding due to rising sea level. In order to develop strategies that deal with these problems, a deep understanding of the physical processes in the ocean and especially in coastal areas is required. Wave-flow interactions describe processes and the exchange of energy between waves and currents. In coastal regions, these interactions, such as the so-called "radiation stress", can generate strong flows parallel to the coast. In this dissertation, the ocean model FVCOM, which is based on unstructured grids, is coupled with the wave model FVCOM-SWAVE, uses different model configurations and different resolutions to investigate wave-flow interactions in two coastal regions.
content.title_en: Wave-current interactions in coastal areas

content.text: The production of semiconducting transparent zinc oxide nanolayers under atmospheric pressure conditions by flame pyrolytic deposition. With its semiconducting properties zinc oxide (ZnO) is mainly used as a transparent conductive oxide in the form of electrode material. As usual manufacturing methods are used different vacuum-based technologies, such as chemical and physical gas phase separation. Based on the principle of economic efficiency, the change in the deposition process of the layers can contribute to the cost reduction of the respective optoelectronic applications. The method of flame pyrolysis used for this work is operated in an open atmosphere and does not involve vacuum technology or reaction chamber. It is also suitable for surface-like deposition and both temperature-sensitive and non-level substrates can be coated with this method. However, up to now only amorphous layers could be realized. The aim of this work was therefore to study the deposition of nanoscale transparent conductive ZnO layers with this atmosphere-based separation method. Using statistical methods, a suitable process window was found, in which a wide range of zinc oxides and a range of radiations were produced in the desired range of the chemical parameters.
content.title_en: Production of semiconducting transparent zinc oxide nanolayers under atmospheric pressure conditions by flame pyrolytic deposition

content.text: Personal social capital in urban societies. Network resources are helpful in diverse life situations but are distributed unequally. In this book a social capital model is presented, which describes and explains to what extent social resources from personal networks are available and used. Statements about the unequal distribution of social network resources are empirically examined for different urban societies. As a result, access to social resources depends on other valuable resources (knowledge, prestige, income). In addition, however, compensation effects between social and other resources are also demonstrable.In terms of the use of social capital, the value of situation-specific social resources is shown.The content of social resources as capital.- Action and structural component of the social capital model.- Access and mobilization of social capital.- Operationalization and measurement of social capital.- Social capital in large and medium cities as well as in urban populations.- Mobilization examples of social capital The target groups social, media and communication scientists The author PD Dr. Sören Petermann is research fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Multi-Religious and Multi-ethnic Societies in Halle-Prof.
content.title_en: Personal social capital in urban societies

content.text: Sound spaces of the experience society: a phenomenal investigation. We live in sound worlds that shape our experience of a living reality. The phenomenological investigation carried out in this book describes the aestheticization of life by means of the sound spaces of the experience society. It is an invitation to critical listening and a plea for the planning relevance of sound geographical realities.
content.title_en: Sound Spaces of the Experience Society: a Phenomenalogical Investigation

content.text: Looking beyond the conclusions : the consideration of alternatives in the planning and approval of port development in Germany and New Zealand. The consideration of alternatives as part of planning and approval processes of large-scale infrastructure projects has been firmly established in international and national environmental law for over two decades. In recent years, increased conflicts over individual projects such as "Stuttgart 21" and calls for a new culture of participation have raised the question of who should be involved in the development and selection of planning and project alternatives. This question is first of all conceptually addressed before it examines the anchoring of the alternative testing in German and New Zealand planning and approval law and its implementation in practice using two case examples for port development. The comparison of the two systems allows conclusions to be drawn on the added value of the alternative testing as an instrument of environmental law as well as the identification of favourable and inhibiting factors for its implementation.
content.title_en: Looking beyond the dreams : the consideration of alternatives in the planning and approval of port development in Germany and New Zealand

What strategies do women develop to deal with their numerical and cultural minority status in the technical field? content.title_en: The micropolitical situation of women in technical professions : strategic positioning in the non-habitualised field

content.text: Press freedom or xenophobia? : The dispute over the Mohammed cartoons and the Danish immigration policy. Burning Danish flags, devastated messages, hundreds of thousands of angry Muslims on the streets of Arab and Asian countries: The twelve Mohammed cartoons of the Danish newspaper Jyllands-Posten occupied the world for weeks in 2006. Jana Sinram sheds a detailed light on the background to the conflict, shows what happened in the years before the publication of the drawings and in the months after that in Denmark, and explains how the dispute could develop into a global crisis. It covers largely unknown connections with the restrictive Danish immigration policy, clears myths and misunderstandings and makes clear that the cartoon dispute was about much more than just press freedom. -- Publisher's description
content.title_en: Freedom of the press or xenophobia? : The dispute over the Mohammed cartoons and the Danish immigration policy

content.text: Imperial Border Areas : Population Policies in German-Southwest Africa and the Eastern Provinces of Prussia 1884-1914. Germany is one of the few colonial powers of the 19th century, which pursued an expansion policy in Africa and Asia as well as in adjacent territories of the Empire. With the colony of German-Southwest Africa and the eastern provinces of Prussia, Dörte Lerp first looks at two of these imperial border areas in a comparative way. It shows that there were indeed parallels between the population policies in both regions. In addition, Lerp refers to the specificities of the respective regions, especially the different forms of racism. Thus, the book contributes significantly to the integration of colonial history.
content.title_en: Imperial Border Areas : Population Policies in German-Southwest Africa and the Eastern Provinces of Prussia 1884-1914

content.text: The present work deals with the experimental investigation of the structural change of the semiconductor indium antimonide (InSB) after the stimulation by an ultrashort laser pulse (60 fs). The investigation is carried out by ultrashort X-ray pulses (around 100 fs). A laser plasma X-ray source serves as the source of the ultrashort X-ray pulse. In this source, an ultrashort intensive optical laser pulse is focused on a metal foil (intensity up to 8*10^16 W/cm^2), resulting in plasma emission of X-ray radiation. To characterise the X-ray source, a novel timepix detector was available, which enabled braking radiation to be detected up to photon energies of 700 keV. The penetration depth of X-ray radiation is usually several micrometers and thus much greater than the penetration depth of the laser pulse used for the stimulation of 100 nm. By using a highly asymmetrical Bragg-reflexion, the particle depth of the X-ray radiation is already measured by means of a linear intrusion depth of the X-ray radiation.
content.title_en: Time-resolved X-ray diffraction of single-crystalline indium antimonide

content.text: Optical characterization of selected defects in CaF2 single crystals. This paper investigates defects of the calcium fluoride crystal (CaF2) that occur after absorption of laser light with a wavelength of 193 nm. Calcium colloids that occur after long-term exposure with 193 nm laser light are experimentally detected in the CaF2 crystal. By means of the very sensitive Cavity Ring-Down method, defects are detected in situ and assigned to the MNa centers. The analysis of the conversion of MNa centers into F and FNa centers shows that a photodissociation of the MNa centers exists even in the case of low-power excitation light. The findings of photodissociation and association result in a new extended model of the MNa center.
content.title_en: Optical characterization of selected defects in CaF2 single crystals

content.text: The thesis describes the development of a new NPMM-200 nanopositioning and nanometer. The overall system is presented in an overview. The design and realization of the positioning system are discussed in detail. An experimental verification focus is the analysis of the performance and the limits of the positioning properties of this measuring instrument. In addition, the first results of the metrological detection are presented using a selected measurement task and several application examples. The NPMM-200 stands out from the current state of the art with a measurement volume of 200 mm x 200 mm x 25 mm with simultaneous measurement resolution in subatomic order and a desired 3-D measurement uncertainty of less than 30 nm. Currently, no scanning system exists which is universally suitable for handling the multitude of measurement tasks on micro- and nanostructures. Therefore, the NPMM-200 was designed for multisensory applications.

content.text: Magnetic resonance imaging with spatially-selective pulses using multiple transmission channels. Summary: In this work, the techniques of spatial-selective RF stimulation in combination with parallel sending for MRI applications in humans were analyzed. With the help of parallel stimulation, it is possible to limit MR imaging to any small area of the objects to be investigated. This technique offers numerous advantages for MRI and has been tested in both phantoms and in test subjects with two different MRI systems. The two MR systems had special apparatuses for parallel sending with eight independent HF channels. The advantages and disadvantages of the realized MR methods were worked out using experimental results.

content.text: The thermodynamics of the solid-liquid phase limit of the melting of metallic alloys is no longer available to all the theoretical aspects of the fusion, the solidification alone defines the resulting structure. Despite global solidification, the solidification of large castings can occur locally and the resulting structure can change. Nevertheless, the theoretical consideration of the melting has been largely neglected, but is essential for the correct modelling of the structure of real components. In this work, a model is set up for the theoretical description of the melting, which calculates the driving forces of the melting and the occurring particle flows and consistently links. Quantitative investigations of the relaxation of thermodynamic imbalance at the solid-liquid phase limit are thus possible. For two aluminium alloys, the solutal melting is calculated in a wide range of process parameters. The purely quantitative influence of mobility M on the temporal development of the concentrations at the phase limit is highlighted, while the additional qualitative change is demonstrated by the kinetic coefficient L. Thermal melting is calculated for different heating rates and the extension of the calculation of the experimental structure is shown in the second analysis of the solid-liquid structure.

content.text: Thin grid discretisation for problems with variable coefficients. Using thin grids, functions can be solved in several variables with a number of degrees of freedom, which grows much slower than with "full" grids, discretely. In simulation, it is a common problem to solve partial differential equations, which have been discreted with the finite element method. Here, the challenge lies mainly in the calculation of the residual, i.e. mainly the application of the stiffness matrix. Existing methods can only be applied to problems that have a tensor product representation, i.e. not to problems with variable coefficients above the area. In this work, the approach from the Bachelor's thesis by S. Hirschmann [Hir], which is based on the level-based representation according to B. Peherstorfer and Ch. Zenger, is extended so that it can also be used to solve such cases, thanks to the variable dimension of the solution.
content.title_en: Thin grid discretisation for problems with variable coefficients

content.text: Metallic nanoparticles in lithium niobate for plasmonic applications. In this work, the production of metallic nanoparticles embedded in lithium niobate is investigated. Lithium niobate is a material of great interest for optical applications, with the high optical nonlinear coefficients of importance. By combining lithium niobate with plasmonic structures, these coefficients can be further increased. As plasmonic structures embedded metallic nanoparticles are very promising, as they can be produced simply by the self-organized process of ion beam synthesis. In this work, silver and gold nanoparticles were produced in lithium niobate. In this process, the influence of implantation temperature and thermal post-treatment on particle size distribution and optical properties of the particles was determined. Furthermore, the production of defects in ion beam synthesis and the recrystallization of lithium niobate were investigated in various form methods. The optical properties of the silver nanoparticles embedded in lithium niobate can be modified by irradiation with high-energy ions.
content.title_en: Metallic nanoparticles in lithium niobate for plasmonic applications

content.text: The classic demarcation dispute between trick theft and fraud has been in place for over a hundred years now. Although the criteria of demarcation used by the majority of the authors appear consolidated, the author has been able to reveal practical and dogmatic inconsistencies in her work. This uncertain state is unacceptable given the brisdom of both offences. -- Under consideration of the weaknesses, the author exposes and rejects the traditional demarcation attempts in a first step as mere ad hoc constructs. In a second step, on the basis of the law-abiding interpretation, she develops a completely novel stringent demarcation concept, the so-called two-stage examination, which leads to a clear divorce of both offences.
content.title_en: The demarcation between trick theft and fraud

content.text: Card-based payment systems and consumer behaviour: a theoretical and empirical study. Card-based payment systems such as credit cards, customer cards, electronic cash and electronic wallets are increasingly replacing classic cash in our money economy. The focus of current scientific work in this field is on economic and technological issues. However, consideration of the social and psychological aspects that arise for consumers from this development is hardly considered. These include issues of impact on consumer behaviour, debt, data protection, loss of control in the handling of money and attitudes to specific forms of money. The present study tries to answer these questions and describe explanatory approaches. The results of the theoretical analysis and empirical analysis using payment data from a bank as well as experimental simulation and survey document that in order to explain the influence of card-based payment systems on consumer behaviour an interdisciplinary and inter-actionist approach is necessary as well as the influence of the payment systems on the payment systems are directly influenced by the payment systems and the payment systems associated with the payment systems.
content.title_en: Card-based payment systems and consumer behaviour : a theoretical and empirical study

content.text: In the shadow of Albert Speer: the architect Rudolf Wolters. Rudolf Wolters (1903–1983) was a pupil of Heinrich Tessenow and Hans Poelzig as well as one of the most influential architects of the National Socialist Germany. As a close associate of Albert Speer, he was, among other things, a major contributor to the designs for the "Reichshauptstadt" and wrote press texts and speeches for him. Acquitted by Albert Speer of every responsibility, Rudolf Wolters lived unharmed in his hometown Coesfeld after 1945. Thanks to his connections from the Nazi era, he was able to establish a network of architects there to build up the Federal Republic. The author evaluates the legacy of this busy man, who was able to establish himself in Germany sustainably after a stay in the Soviet Union from 1933 onwards. At the same time, he explores the lifelong relationship between Wolters and Speer and opens up further structures of the management levels of the "General Building Inspector for the Imperial Capital"
content.title_en: In the shadow of Albert Speer : the architect Rudolf Wolters

Instead of thinking in parallel societies, diversity becomes visible as a resource.

content.text: The protection of Natura 2000 sites in the construction and operation of offshore wind turbines: an examination of the scope of the Habitat Protection Law on granted and to be granted permits of offshore wind parks. The question of the protection of Natura 2000 sites in the construction and operation of offshore wind turbines links one of the most important problem areas of nature conservation law with the discussion about the use of wind energy at sea as a core component of the energy transition. The present dissertation examines the relevant regulations and their effects on the permits of offshore wind parks. In particular, the legal issues associated with the authorisation of offshore wind turbines and the identification and classification of the Natura 2000 sites created and protected in the marine sector are discussed. Another focus of the work is the handling of the protection regulations for Natura 2000 sites, which are based on Art. 6(3) of the Flora Fauna Habitats Directive, and the examination of the possibility of a derogation decision under Art. 6(4) of the Flora Fauna Habitats Directive, on the importance of the habitat plants, on the extent to which the protection of the habitats is already subject to the requirement of the protection of the environment.
content.title_en: The protection of Natura 2000 sites in the construction and operation of offshore wind turbines: an examination of the scope of the Habitats Law for permits granted and to be granted to offshore wind farms

content.text: The growth and competition in beech, oak and oak populations under changing climate conditions was analysed in a variety of ways. Summary: The question of the climate sensitivity of beech and oak trees is highlighted by various forest science disciplines. While site and vegetation-oriented work highlights the wide range of beech and oak trees and therefore concludes on a high adaptability of the tree species in changing climate, investigations based on physiological processes often show a higher dry stress sensitivity for beech than for oak.The present work highlights the question of weather dependence and dry stress tolerance of the two tree species against the background of retrospective growth analyses. Eight beech oak mixed populations in two different age classes (± 60-year and ± 120-year old stocks) and two different regions were selected (west fall of the black forest: well water-capped locations due to comparatively high medium precipitation amounts, Stromberg: temporarily tense water supply due to comparatively low precipitation amounts). Esgutica were selected for free-breed populations.
content.title_en: Growth and competition in beech, oak mixed populations under changing climate conditions

content.text: The preservation of digital information by defining significant properties. The archive world is facing the challenge of constantly changing technology in view of the rapidly increasing amount of digital information that digital archivists (e.g. electronic files or databases) are facing in contrast to analogue objects (e.g. pergament customers or paper files). These changes, which affect the hardware, software and/or file formats, can significantly affect the durability and on the other hand the authenticity and integrity of the information. An archivist must keep an eye on the technological change and react to it in order to maintain the digital information permanently and trustworthy. Thus, the unlimited preservation of digital objects requires active archiving – in contrast to analogue archivists, which, after conservation measures if necessary, can be largely statically archived. At the latest since the 1990s, numerous solutions for archiving digital objects have been developed in projects and publications.
content.title_en: The preservation of digital information by defining significant characteristics

content.text: Design rules for superconducting analog-digital converters. This dissertation paper provides a contribution to dimensioning aspects of the circuit design in superconducting electronics. To this end, superconducting comparators, i.e. Josephson comparator and QOJS comparator, are examined in detail in terms of speed and sensitivity. The influence of thermal noise on the decision-making process of the comparators represents the so-called grey zone. It is analysed in detail in the work as an important characteristic. Various parameter dependencies are presented from this. A modeling of a Josephson comparator has been experimentally confirmed. Based on this, concepts of superconducting analog-digital converters are examined in the work and design rules derived from it. By reducing switching egy, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the circuits and thus the reliability of decision-making processes and switching processes are influenced. For special applications with very high demands regarding speed or accuracy, superconducting AD converters offer excellent performance features. The work provides concrete correlations between the different design tools and thus the reliability of the decision-making process can be easily transferred to the user.
content.title_en: Design rules for superconducting analogue-digital converters

content.text: The non-act: a dogmatic reconstruction. What is a non-act? The general administrative law remains the answer to this theoretically and practically relevant question. This is all the more surprising because the dogmatic roots of this legal figure go back to the beginning of the theory of form and error. Nevertheless, there is still a lack of a clear legal contour of the legal figure. This has led to inconsistencies in the handling of non-acts. -- The dogmatic reconstruction of the figure shows that the non-act is due to the relationship between civil and public law and concerns the constitutional possibilities and limits of the assignment of actions to the state. The key to the material and procedural classification of non-acts is its delimitation of illusory acts: While the non-act only concerns imputational issues, the figure of the sham act develops the dogmatic tension relationship between legally relevant action and choice of legal forms.
content.title_en: The non-act : a dogmatic reconstruction

content.text: Building renewals and demographic changes in line buildings of the 1950/60s: the example of Hanover. Line buildings of the 1950/60s were built according to the model of the "divided and relaxed city", are located close to the city from today's point of view and offer compact, usually low-cost housing. Line buildings are attributed great development potential, however, a "double ageing" of residents and building stock, the concentration of socially disadvantaged households and sales of housing stocks to international housing providers can lead to upheavals and, if necessary, downward spirals. What contributes to whether there is a modernization or a devaluation? What possibilities exist to further develop this large housing stock of the post-war period? As small-scale quantitative studies on constructional and demographic changes have so far been lacking, an analysis of the type of building specific for line buildings of the 1950/60s was carried out using the example of the city of Hanover.

content.text: The manifesto as a medium of reception control in the architecture and design discourse. In this work, manifesto manifestations of the design and architecture discourse are examined in the situative, media, institutional and historical context. Based on an analysis of the etymology and the history of ideas of the manifesto, the thesis is shown by selected examples that the medium serves primarily the purposeful control of reception in the discourse. Furthermore, the ability and meaning of the manifesto as a mirror of past and present, but also as a pioneer of future discourses, is analyzed and developments of the manifesto as regards stylistics, content, function and meaning in the design and architecture discourse are presented. This study explores manifestos from the design and architecture discourse in their situational, media, institutional and historical context. Based on an ethical analysis and on the manifesto , the thesis uses selectable examples to describe the existence of the instrument of the perception and the perception of the perception.

content.text: Classification of lattice group models, high order discontinuizations of Boltzmann's collision operator and parallelization. This work is about grid group models (LGpMs). This is a class of deterministic discretization models, which appear to be related to discrete speed models (DVMs). Unfortunately, there are no convergence results for the discretization of the collision operator using LGpM. Moreover, it is unclear whether the convergence results known for DVM's convergence results are transferable to LGpM, since there is no exact classification of LGpM within the DVM theory. This work addresses these problems by proving a scheme for the construction of discretizations with any high degree of convergence and classifying LGpM within the theoretical framework of DVM. The logically following step is a look at a practical implementation and numerical tests of the resulting discretizations to numerically verify the theoretical results and a closer look at the time complexity. Finally, we examine the parallelization of general LGp-relation is a significant consideration of the usage of LGp-relationship.
content.title_en: Classification of lattice group models, high order discontinuizations of Boltzmann's collision operator and parallelization

content.text: Prevalences of animal welfare-relevant integument damage and contamination in dairy cows in dairy farms in Lower Saxony. Dairy cows, integument damage, pollution. - The aim of this study was to record the prevalence of Tarsal joint changes (TGV) and the contamination of lactating cows in dairy farms in Lower Saxony. The collected data provided the "Animal Protection Working Group of the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Consumer Protection of Lower Saxony an objective basis for discussion on the definition of appropriate thresholds (target/al alert values) of animal welfare-relevant indicators. These should be integrated in the future in the amendment of the "Animal Protection Plan Lower Saxony". The data collection took place on 160 dairy farms with boxing stables with a total of 13,985 lacticating cows, which were selected with regard to the stock sizes and the regional distribution (PLZ divisions) representative of the low-Saxon dairy farms.
content.title_en: Prevalence of animal welfare-relevant integument damage and pollution in dairy cows in dairy farms in Lower Saxony

content.text: Kinematic analysis of 3D reconstructed movements of the lumbar spine and the pelvis in the beagle in step and trab. Canis lupus familiaris; Locomotion; vertebral column. - It is generally accepted that the movement of a mammal consists of a complex interaction of limb and trunk movements and the composite movements of the individual vertebral joints contribute to the overall movement of the spine and thus also to the range of movement of the pelvis. Compared to the numerous studies which investigated the kinematics and kinetics of the limb movements as well as the activation of individual muscles of the limbs during the movement, the movements of the trunk, especially the movements of the individual vertebral joints and the pelvis, are so far too little investigated. The aim of this work was therefore to analyse in a vivo method the three-dimensional (3D) movements, which occur during the movement in symmetrical gangs in the pelvis and between the lumbar vertebrals, with a non-invasive method.
content.title_en: Kinematic analysis of 3D reconstructed movements of the lumbar spine and pelvis in step and trot

content.text: The search for transit time variations using ground-based observations. In this work, known transit planets were investigated to obtain indicators for the existence of additional objects in the system by precise measurement of the transit time point. To this end, the selection fell to seven known transit planets, which, due to their properties, suggested additional objects. Using the YETI network, 93 transit observations with a total exposure time of 291 hours at 17 different observation sites worldwide could be carried out over a four-year period. Due to various influences, significantly changing weather conditions, only 41 transit observations remained for further analysis. The remaining observations had to be either aborted during the transit event or subsequently sorted out due to too high photometric errors. In addition to the own data, published results of other research groups were also used.
content.title_en: The search for transit time variations by ground-based observations

content.text: The study covers approximately 67 km in the northwestern Harz foothills, between the northern edge of the resin and the mouth of the Innerste in the leash. The aim of the study is to determine the influence of different land uses on the heavy metal and nutrient balance in the soils of the Innersteaue. Differences are made between the inflows of agricultural use, settlement areas and nature conservation areas. In the study area eleven transects were determined across the river course. Along the transects, the innermost soil profiles were created at a distance of 2-5 m from the shore and half the extent of the aue. The analyses of the soil samples included the determination of pedological basic parameters, the total contents and the plant-available proportions of selected heavy metals and nutrient contents. The results were also shown in the range of the soils. The results were very low in the range of the soils. The results were obtained by correlation analyses (according to Spearman) and a nonparametric test (Cruscal-Wallis-Test). The range of the soils is neutral. The range of the soils are also found in the field of the study.
content.title_en: Impact of land use on the heavy metal and nutrient balance in the Innersteaue between Langelsheim and Ruthe

content.text: Characterization of the quality status of the Neckar near Tübingen on the basis of structural, limnological and ecotoxicological evaluation criteria. The ecological balance of the Neckar is strongly influenced by the intensive use as a domestic water resource and waterway as well as by hydroelectricity production and numerous sewage treatment plants. The aim of this work was to characterize the ecological and ecotoxicological condition of the Neckar. The investigations were carried out at several test sites in the Tübingen area, both above and below potential sources of trace matter.
content.title_en: Characterisation of the quality of the Neckar at Tübingen on the basis of structural, limnological and ecotoxicological evaluation criteria
