content.text: Legal issues of publicity in municipal company law. The presentation is dedicated to the topic of "publicity" which is, in practice, important and theoretically extremely complex for municipalities as a legal obligation for municipal companies and participations. The procurement of sufficient information is a prerequisite for a task-appropriate choice of legal form and effective management to ensure an uninterrupted legitimation chain between the sovereign and the corporate bodies in the field of corporate law confidentiality obligations to report obligations under municipal law and transparency requirements. The legal issues of publicity are examined in the aspects of local self-government law, the Union law on competition, state aid and public procurement law, the law on integrity and antitrust, as well as the company law and municipal law of the German Land States. The main question of the constitutional law is whether the case law of the BVerfG on the substance of the electoral law of Art. 38 GG on the responsibility for integration towards the EU is transferred to the municipal level. The author develops a subjective law of the elector as a sovereign by means of "the law" and of the effective control of his participation, which the municipality assumes sufficiently before the control of his or her decision to govern its company.
content.title_en: Legal issues of publicity in municipal company law

content.text: Thin-film Josephson contacts for characterizing iron-based superconductors. In this work, the electrical properties of iron-based superconductors were investigated. Hybrid Josephson contacts were produced and measured on the basis of thin superconducting layers in various geometries. The results were analysed using both Andreev and tunnel spectroscopy and Josephson effect. By characterizing the contacts, insights into the behaviour of different contacts were gained. Due to the variation of the barrier, a targeted influence of contact behaviour was possible. From the measurements made, statements about the order parameter and its symmetry could be obtained. Overall, it could be concluded that iron-based superconductors behave significantly unconventionally and therefore Josephson contacts, in which they are used, differ significantly from those from conventional superconductors. This concerned both the measured conductivity spectra and the current voltage characteristic lines taken in the Josephson effect, in which a clear excess flow occurred, as well as the temperature behaviour of the product.
content.title_en: Thin-film Josephson contacts for characterizing iron-based superconductors

content.text: The multi-purpose redundancy of mixed AC HVDC networks is implemented through fast corrective measures. Mated HVDC networks can be used to build an overlay network overlaid with the AC network. Operation of such networks requires a rapid response to faults in the AC and HVDC networks. To enable these to be quickly adjusted by HVDC converters, the inverter work points need to be adapted quickly. In order to meet the sometimes very time-critical course of such fault scenarios, a procedure is presented that enables a rapid correction of the inverter work points. According to a list of possible critical equipment failures, correct converter work points are created at central level by means of an optimal power flow calculation and stored at local level within the converter control. Local measurements allow identification of occurring critical failure scenarios and activation of the corresponding precalculated corrective measures. In this way, the AC HVDC network network connection can be implemented in the case of an equipment failure by corrective measures in the (n-1) secure state of the redundancy.
content.title_en: Diversity redundancy of mixed AC HVDC networks through rapid corrective measures

content.text: Photon management in thin film solar cells. In this work, various approaches to photon management in thin film solar cells have been numerically investigated. First, dielectric and metallic particles have been considered in periodic arrangement. The disadvantage of these approaches is the discrete response of periodic structures. It is evident that on the sun-facing side of the solar cell a good light coupling is required over a wide spectral range, whereas on the sun-facing side of the solar cell a narrowband response is quite appropriate around the absorption edge. For this purpose, especially inverted opals are well suited. In the second chapter, randomized textures have been applied at the front side as a result of this. However, due to the texture, opal growth on the solar cell back is initially disturbed. Only gradually, however, a perfect grid is formed. It is precisely this mixture of periodicity and amorphy that combines the advantages of both approaches. The third chapter deals with completely randomized structures. The aim is to describe a procedure which randomized textures with favorable properties for photon comparison is to produce a patterned distribution of a given size.
content.title_en: Photon management in thin film solar cells

content.text: Open quantum systems under coherent control with continuous monitoring and unitary feedback. Summary: To realize quantum technologies it is imperative to protect the necessary quantum properties, such as coherence and interlinking, against harmful environmental influences. To achieve a possible strategy this is based on coherent control, which is experimentally comparatively easy to realize, but which can only keep the desired properties limited. We investigate how the control possibilities can be improved by means of continuous measurement and feedback mechanisms by means of an extension. In this work we confine ourselves to the basic example of a single two-niveau atom, which can spontaneously relax in its basic state by emitting a photon into the environment. We find that only by post-selection of the measurement events can one stabilize any pure qubit state, which does not seem possible by coherent control alone. Using unitarian operators as feedback operations, every desired two-level condition can be fully consistent with the measurement possibilities, for example, the control errors must be improved in a realistic manner.
content.title_en: Open quantum systems under core control with continuous monitoring and unitary feedback

content.text: The author analyses the impact of congestion in the transport infrastructure sector and designs a regulatory policy framework for the more efficient use of these facilities. The economic basic proposal consists in the implementation of the price mechanism. The price would maximise the potential use of the infrastructure and make it transparent. Using practical examples (slots and road use), it will be possible to consider how prices can also take into account the specificities of infrastructure use, e.g. exclusion problems and sudden and short-term demand increases. In competition policy aspects, any monopolistic tendencies that might be supported by the implementation of the price mechanism (purchase of the relevant slots by financially strong companies with the aim of creating market power) and proposed rules that can solve the monopolisation problem. The author concludes that for infrastructure use a time and space-related price system, depending on the amount of use, a price system that is fundamentally more efficient allocating the usage rights. For the ideal use of the auctioning mechanism, the price efficiency is proposed for the typical use of the market, the price efficiency of the market, the price efficiency is considered to be the most appropriate for the use of the market.
content.title_en: Transport infrastructure bottlenecks

content.text: Cultural finance: a contribution to the reform of public museums and theatres in Germany. The book "Culture finance" presents a comprehensive economic analysis of the German museum and theatre landscape. After a description of the financial economy of public theatre and museums, it is explained and critically discussed why the public sector should be engaged in the cultural sector from an economic point of view. The main part of the paper is devoted to the question of how the "institutional-economic constitution" of the cultural enterprise influences the cultural political output. Here, for example, centralized cultural enterprises are confronted with such in federal and municipal responsibility, cultural enterprises are compared in direct and indirect democracies, self-organized cultural enterprises and those in competition with each other are discussed. It is evident that the "institutional-economic constitution" of the cultural landscape has a decisive influence on their performance. On the basis of this institutional analysis, five ideal-typical reform options for the theatres and museums in Germany are then developed: the state-of-the-art, the democratization, the self-financing and the non-reformative, the status options are proposed.
content.title_en: Cultural finance: an economic contribution to the reform of public museums and theatres in Germany

content.text: Rational social policy: the production of security and justice in modern societies and their implications for the economic theory of social policy. Through the day-to-day discussion of a "reconstruction of the welfare state" fundamental questions of social policy theory are neglected. The author therefore tries in this work to build a bridge between practical problems of design and fundamental research. Fundamental link element is the definition of practical social policy according to its goal to strengthen the inner, material connection of society. -- To what extent now the special, changed framework conditions of modern societies require a special expression of rational social policy? According to the three-step of rational policy analysis, the situation, goal and means of practical social policy can be derived in modern societies. Key words are, among other things, the normative and empirical loss of meaning of normality standards, center and periphery of social policy needs as well as the protection or bridge function of social policy instruments. - Before this background, scope and limits of an economic theory of social policy are examined until now unreservedly, whereby the emphasis is placed on a differentiation of the two basic paradigms - neoclassics and institutionalism - that is placed as a normative approach to the norm, but that both of economic policy can be applied in a form of the norm.
content.title_en: Rational Social Policy: the Production of Security and Justice in Modern Societies and its Implications for the Economic Theory of Social Policy

content.text: The author's main concern is to explain the medium to long-term development of the real external value of the DM in the last quarter of a century. After a brief overview of theories on exchange rate determination from literature, the elements of the theoretical model framework, the so-called NATREX approach, are described in detail. In the context of this approach, a concrete NATREX model is developed, which takes into account specific characteristics of the German economy, in particular its dependence on raw material imports. The medium and long-term reaction of the real exchange rate to a variety of exogenous disturbances is derived. -- The theoretical implications of the model are examined and broadly confirmed in an empirical analysis. This empirical analysis also allows for quantification of the theoretically only qualitatively determined multipliers as well as the determination of a time path of a real exchange rate of the DM in terms of the theoretical model of equilibrium. A comparison of this time series with the actual real external value of the DM often shows that the DM has been over- or undervalued (mostly the first DM) since the time of the conversion is dominated by the national factors.
content.title_en: Determinants of the real exchange rate : a theoretical and empirical analysis

content.text: The work is based on the criteria for assessing the appropriateness of the duration of the proceedings and the development of compensation systems through the case law from the solution of the procedure to the solution of the criminalisation to the solution of the enforcement, which is supplemented by the provisions of § 198, 199 GVG. The work concludes that individual criteria used by the case law to determine the appropriateness of the procedure are not appropriate. -- As regards the solution of the criminalisation, in addition to serious systematic concerns, the lack of transparency of the criminalisation solution is particularly to be criticised. Even when the solution of the enforcement solution is applied, compensation gaps remain, and the dogmatic derivation from § 51 StGB does not convince. Since 2011, the enforcement solution has been accompanied by a financial compensation scheme standardised in § 198, 199 GVG, which closes the remaining gaps and thus ensures comprehensive financial compensation.
content.title_en: Excessive length of proceedings in criminal proceedings : provision – compensation – legal protection

Summary: The present paper deals with the study of NAD(P)H-dependent oxide reductases and their role in the reduction of unactivated C=C double bonds.So far no technical biocatalytic process is known with an isolated enzyme for this type of reaction. Furthermore, the enzymatic reduction of allylic alcohols described in the literature has not yet been clarified. These facts serve as the basis for the investigations carried out.In the first part, the alleged reduction of allylic alcohols by the NADH-dependent oxide reductases alcohol dehydrogenase from Equus caballus (HLADH, engli. for horse liver alcohol dehydrogenase) and carbonyl reductase from candida parapsilosis (CPCR) is explained. By the use of purified proteins combined with the use of deuterium-marked substances, a side activity was detected which is caused by other reductasen of the expression organism.

content.text: Modelling and simulation of the dynamics of accumulation and penetration processes in particle-loaded coolant flows. A coolant loss disturbance case is a postulated incident scenario in reactor safety research where insulation material is assumed to be released due to a leak of plant components. In order to minimize the penetration of the insulation material into the reactor core, a measure of this should be retained with screen gratings. The resulting retention corresponds to the process-technical solid-liquid separation process of the cake filtration and has a high relevance in many technical applications. The aim of the present work is the modelling and simulation of the storage processes taking place with the help of knowledge-based methods. A detailed process analysis was carried out. Subsequently, the essential model components and behaviours were identified. During the modelling process, various models with different objectives were developed. This work provides a detailed overview of the approach of model creation and the finished models. Furthermore, the final placement model is analysed in detail.
content.title_en: Modelling and simulation of the dynamics of accumulation and penetration processes in particle-loaded coolant flows

These new model colloids must have a steric stabilization and on the one hand have a similar refractive index as that of the medium. The present work deals with the production of sterically stabilized, aqueous colloid dispersions on the basis of fluorinated materials for light scattering. The core-shell colloids produced by Wiemann et al. [M. Wiemann, R. Schneider, E. Bartsch, Z. Phys. Chem. 226, 761 (2012)] with a fluorinated core of 1H,1H-heptafluoroobutyl-methacrylate and a stabilization shell of polyethylene glycolization were investigated by the polystyrene-resynthetic reaction rate and the polystyrestyres.

content.text: A philosophical reflection on the alienation of sexuality. Summary: This work deals with the problem of prostitution, which can be regarded as a phenomenon of alienated sexuality in capitalist society, and tries to consider this subject from a philosophical perspective. In this work, the principle of capitalism is considered to be the principle that, for the purpose of increasing capital, everything becomes a commodity. It is not necessary to consider the sex industry as problematic when judged on the capitalist principle that the object of reification extends itself to the body of man and its sexuality. Contrary to this view, the questions can be asked whether the body and sexuality are to be treated as the object of purchase or sale, and what is the difference between the trade with this and that with the human being itself. This work represents the point that the body and sexuality cannot be exchanged as a commodity for money, because they correspond to the personality and dignity of man. Therefore, this work deals with the assertions that support the legalization of the prostitution and the expansion of the sex industry. In the first part, work as a pre-work reflection of sexuality, the notion of sexuality in the relation to the sexuality.
content.title_en: A philosophical reflection on the alienation of sexuality

content.text: The Weltansicht as an Ersatz Gestalt: a happy open-end-environment-design-science-fiction-image-story. «The Weltansicht as an Ersatz Gestalt» is the previously unpublished master thesis that Jan Turnovský submitted to the Architectural Association in London in 1978. The focus is on the philosophy of "Open Systems" inspired by Umberto Eco, which is transferred to architectural design work: The perception (construction) of figures (architecture) is a major part of world view (collective, contemporary, etc.). On the other hand, an individual world view offers the possibility to see figures differently than intended, to construct them from given stimuli differently than usual. Three types of "magical formulas" that were used in architecture in particular in the 1970s and which were also used to concur with each other are examined: the terminology and formulas of numerical aesthetics, ideology and semiology. The "Weltansichtung" is a wisely, critical and highly-critically applied to the reader's language, the new concept of the German language, and the language of the English language, and the English language.
content.title_en: The worldview as an alternative figure : a happy open-end environmental-design-science-fiction-image-story

content.text: Expanded museum: cultural memory and virtual realities. With the entry of digital media into the museum, a new mix of real space and virtual space is emerging. At the same time, under these conditions, the museum's own media heritage is clearly emerging. This advancing "automation of the museum", in which it is increasingly becoming the medium of presentation, leads to the museum itself being virtualized and thus decoupled from the real space or "available" to it. The volume presents numerous international pilot projects of the use of digital media in museums. It becomes clear how museums expand into virtual space using participatory and interactive strategies as places of memory and social memory.
content.title_en: Expanded museum : cultural memory and virtual realities

content.text: The network and virtual reality: for the self-programming of society by universal machine. Computer-based »new media« seem to have a radical revolution in society. But: The »new media« could have developed differently. Technologies change society, but are also invented and transformed by it. In particular, this applies to computers that are universal and programmable. They are subjected to social ideas about what they should be and do. The question is, how and why has society programmed itself through the medium of computers, especially through the constellations of the »network« and the »virtual reality«? Jens Schröter's answers update the established view of the relationship between society and computers. Numerous illustrations document the development of the »universal machine«.
content.title_en: The network and virtual reality: for the self-programming of society by the universal machine

content.text: InnenStadtAktion - Kunst oder Politik? : Artistic practice in the neoliberal city. Who owns the city? - This question is the core of the battles over the inner cities, which are increasingly becoming a contested terrain. »Security and cleanliness« are considered the top maxim of an attractive cityscape. What role does art play in this context? Where does it serve to enforce regulatory policies and what are critical artistic practices? The focus of this investigation is on the 'InnenStadtAktionen', with which artists, theorists and political initiatives intervened at the end of the nineties against »privatisation, exclusion and security delusion«.
content.title_en: InnerCityAction - Art or Politics? : Artistic Practice in the Neoliberal City

content.text: The study raises the question of the extent to which a pedagogical approach beyond the solidification in systemic structures can be flexibly and systematically thought. This paradoxical initial constellation can be met with the late system theory of Luhmann, which attempts to advance a differentialist shift beyond the classical concept of difference. The hitherto open ends of this project are further developed with Deleuze. In a topological reading - especially from the perspective of a topology of difference - pedagogy can thus be refigured as an expression system.
content.title_en: Passages of Pedagogy : to the version of the pedagogical moment following Niklas Luhmann and Gilles Deleuze

content.text: Doing images : on the practice of medical images. This volume is the first German-language ethnography to be used for imaging processes in medicine. The focus is on the production, interpretation and use of medical images as well as the importance they have in medical practice. The theoretically demanding study draws on concepts of scientific and technical research and cultural sociology as well as results of field research in Switzerland, Germany and the USA. It aims to promote a reflexive approach to medical (and generally scientific) images and to expand the analytical instruments in sociology.
content.title_en: Doing images : to the practice of medical images

content.text: Digital realism : between computer animation and live action : the new image aesthetics in feature films. Digital doppelganger and animated Hollywood stars, journeys through nerve pathways and skin pores, impossible camera perspectives and image spaces that continue indefinitely - in current feature films filmed parts of images and computer animations are often indistinguishably merged. A new category of »hybrid motion pictures« has emerged, which has produced a picture aesthetic beyond the effect cinema. Their staging strategies undermine our vision of realistic representations - they influence our perceptions sustainably and shape our view of the world. The book combines the presentation of the technical requirements of these new image worlds with an in-depth examination of their aesthetic implications. It thus closes a gap in the scientific examination of the digitization of image production.
content.title_en: Digital Realism : between computer animation and live action : the new visual aesthetics in feature films

content.text: World events and mass media: on the theory of world media events: Studies on John F. Kennedy, Lady Diana and Titanic. How can it be explained that the mass media report exclusively on the same subject over several days in all parts of the world? Christian Morgner approaches these »world media events« and gives sociologically convincing answers to the structurality of the phenomenon. By evaluating extensive television and newspaper material from different regions of the world, which reported on the assassination of John F. Kennedy, the accident death of Lady Diana and the sinking of Titanic, he develops conceptual means from empirical research. Thus, a rigorous media sociological study is now available, which impresses with its close combination of theory and empiricism as well as complex theory development.
content.title_en: World Events and Mass Media: on the Theory of World Media Event : Studies on John F. Kennedy, Lady Diana and the Titanic

content.text: The coordination of proceedings in transnational intellectual property disputes. Proceedings on intellectual property rights are often held in parallel in several states. Therefore, there is a risk that courts may judge essentially the same legal issues differently and thus take contradictory decisions. In a critical assessment of the Brussels Ia Regulation, the CLIP Princes and the ALI Princes, the author analyses how proceedings under these rules are coordinated by means of procedural rejection and suspension. To this end, she confronts the demand for stronger cooperation between courts. To this end, the author systematises various forms of inter-judicial cooperation and examines the extent to which they are capable of promoting the international decision-making process and at the same time upholding the sovereignty interests of the states concerned and the fundamental rights of the parties. However, the cooperation is countered by legal and practical difficulties that the author also points to intellectual the rights and the coordination of conflicts in transnational legal disputes on intellectual property rights.
content.title_en: Coordination of proceedings in transnational intellectual property disputes

content.text: Self-dynamic civil wars: the persistence and finiteness of domestic conflicts of violence. Even in the 21st century, the world is shaken by long-lasting civil wars - the most recent example is the unending civil war in Syria. Until the beginning of the 1990s, these domestic wars were mostly regarded as politically motivated conflicts of violence or proxy wars. Afterwards, with the end of the Cold War and under the impression of the genocide in Rwanda and the Bosnian war, new approaches are emerging, which lead the widespread violence primarily to greedy motives or traditional ethnic enmities. Against these stenciled interpretation patterns Stefan Deißler develops a perspective that comes closer to the complex complexity of the civil war phenomenon. Without neglecting the fundamental role of ethnic, economic or political social groups, the author focuses on the warring organizations themselves and makes the relations between combatants and civilians a critical observation.
content.title_en: Self-dynamic civil wars: from the persistence and finiteness of domestic conflicts of violence

content.text: Innovative and interdisciplinary crystal breeding : Materials with tunable quantum critical behavior. Natalija van Well focuses in her study on crystal breeding with different parameters and the characterization of the crystals of the mixing system Cs2CuCl4-xBrx. By synthesis, breeding and characterization of such materials, insights are gained about the systematics of the change of their physical properties. As a result, the author determines new schematic phase diagrams and characterizes newly discovered compositions. Magnetic properties of the materials can be influenced e.g. by the change of distances between the interacting units.
content.title_en: Innovative and interdisciplinary crystal breeding : Materials with tunable quantum critical behavior

content.text: Architects in the GDR: Reality and self-image of a profession. Planning and building in the GDR is primarily understood as "state architecture". The architects involved are hardly perceived. In many cases they are only considered executive organs of an overpowering building policy. But what role did they really play? Tobias Zervosen asks about the self-image of this professional group without losing sight of the importance of the political. He comprehensively shows that the architectural history of the GDR is also a history of the architects themselves: they shaped their course in a variety of ways – whether at the political level, in the concrete planning on site or in theoretical debates. The book is "a vivid study of the self-image of the architects in an epoch of German history characterized by diverse internal and external constraints".
content.title_en: Architects in the GDR : Reality and self-image of a profession

content.text: The impact of incentive systems to promote alternative drives on purchasing decisions and traffic behaviour. Market penetration of alternatively driven vehicles is progressing more slowly in Germany than the Federal Government hopes. According to current developments, the stated goal of one million electric vehicles on Germany's roads by 2020 seems to be unreachable. Voices of more state support to accelerate market penetration of electric vehicles are becoming louder. This work examines the influence of state incentive systems on car purchasing decisions regarding drive technology. To this end, a selection-based stated preference experiment is conducted on hypothetical purchasing decisions with around 1,000 people in the Hamburg metropolitan region. The elements of the experiment are previously validated by expert interviews. The purchase decision is simulated with a mixed-logit model, in which the traffic behaviour of the participants is integrated. The results show that there are large differences in preference for the drives in the population. Rebound effects are expected above all among users of the environmental network (ÖPNV users and cyclists). The work gives recommendations for action to policymakers and describes the action areas for further funding activities of the electric mobility.
content.title_en: Influence of incentive systems to promote alternative drives on purchasing decisions and traffic behaviour

With the increasing motorization in the first decades of the 20th century the question of the necessity of roads exclusively for road transport was posed throughout Europe. After numerous, however only partially realized plans in the 1920s arose during the rule of National Socialism about 3,900 km Reichsautobahnnetz, over 2,500 km were under construction - then the world's largest motorway network and leading in technical standards, at the same time an important element of the propaganda. The conception of the Reichsautobahnnetz was characterized by the tension between specific political and aesthetic objectives of the Nazi dictatorship and a functionality of the transport infrastructure that takes up the planning of the Weimar era. The work analyses the overall concept of the network based on its spatial structure based on the various motives. The focus is on the hitherto poorly investigated functional purposes of the network and the design. - Due to the importance of the Reichsautobahnnetz as a testimony to the Nazi era and as a transport innovation, the second part of the work is on the monument property of the existing network. Until now, however, the existing infrastructure functions are not explained by means of the Reich's autobahn.
content.title_en: The Reichsautobahn : Conception, spatial structure and monument status of a historical transport network

content.text: The ramga-theoretic complexity of automatic linear orders. Automatic structures are a much-regarded topic in the research field of "Logics in Informatics" for the first time. A structure is automatic when their carrier quantity, their relations and their functions are all recognizable by finite automats on words or trees. In particular, such structures are finally present. The main motivation for the investigation of automatic structures lies in the uniform decisionability of their predicative theories of first stage. In this thesis we examine the model theoretical complexity of automatic linear orders regarding the two complexity dimensions of condensation rank and ramsey degree. The condensation rank of a linear order measures their deviation from the property of tightness by means of an ordinal number. In addition, we show that the dividing line between the term and the linear order ranges can be distributed from the linear order.

content.text: Students' projects with original astronomical data for use in the upper-level astronomy class. In the work, students' projects are described on the basis of original astronomical data for use in the astronomy class of the Gymnasial Upper Level. The projects and their implementation in the classroom are discussed with regard to technical and didactic criteria. In the first part of the work, the technical didactical principles are presented in three chapters. This includes a theoretical consideration of the role of observation for the astronomical knowledge process and for teaching, a discussion of various teaching forms and concepts in which student projects can be realized on the basis of authentic astronomical observation data, as well as an analysis of the school books common in Thuringia for the astronomy field. The analysis reveals that the number of images showing authentic astronomical observations or observation results is negligible in the total number of images. The student projects are suitable for the quantification of astrophysical topics in the astronomy class of the Gymnasial Upper Level. They deal with the topics of verification of the second Kepler law (flat rate), exoplanet on orbital exoplanets, exoplanetal determination, dual orbital constellations, and exoplanetal diagrams.

content.text: Vision electric vehicle - and why it didn't get far: an empirical study on the non-diffusion of electric vehicle 1967 to 2012. The goal of bringing one million electric cars to the roads by 2020, which the Federal Chancellor has set out, seems hardly feasible from the point of view of many experts. What is it that the diffusion of electric vehicles is taking place so slowly? Why are they still a niche product that is accepted only in a few parts of the world, but has not yet achieved a breakthrough in individual, especially private car traffic? The author examines these questions in detail by following the distribution of electric vehicles between 1967 and 2012. To this end, he conceives electric mobility as a sustainability innovation that serves socially desirable objectives but does not get through self-running. In order to understand the impediment factors, the subsystems of vehicle, traffic and energy must be considered integratively, while taking into account knowledge, value and conflict of interest of the involved actors.
content.title_en: Vision electric vehicle - and why it didn't get far : an empirical study on the non-diffusion of electric vehicle 1967 to 2012

content.text: New product announcements: theoretical and empirical analysis of consumer risk perception. Product innovations are of great importance for companies for their long-term preservation of existence. Thus, almost half of all German companies are innovative and have high innovation expenditures. High innovation expenditures are countering high failure rates. One of the main causes are adoption barriers that prevent or delay consumers from buying product innovation. One of the most important adoption barriers is the risk perceived by consumers. Due to the shortened product life cycles, companies face the challenge of reducing adoption barriers before market introduction in order to achieve immediate adoption of product innovation. One way to minimize the perceived risk of consumers early is to provide information about product innovation before its introduction into the market. The tool for providing information before market introduction represents new product announcements. The question about the influence of the content design of new product announcements, in particular the information characteristics, is to reduce the perceived risk so far only insufficiently examined. Anne Michaelis views various information characteristics from consumer exposure to new product announcements.
content.title_en: New product announcements : theoretical and empirical analysis of consumer risk perception

In the work, students' projects are described on the basis of original astronomical data for use in the astronomy class of the Gymnasial Upper Level. The projects and their implementation in the classroom are discussed with regard to technical and didactic criteria. In the first part of the work, the technical didactical principles are presented in three chapters. This includes a theoretical consideration of the role of observation for the astronomical knowledge process and for teaching, a discussion of various teaching forms and concepts in which student projects can be realized on the basis of authentic astronomical observation data, as well as an analysis of the school books common in Thuringia for the astronomy field. The analysis reveals that the number of images showing authentic astronomical observations or observation results is negligible in the total number of images. The student projects are suitable for the quantification of astrophysical topics in the astronomy class of the Gymnasial Upper Level. They deal with the topics of verification of the second Kepler law (flat rate), exoplanet on orbital exoplanets, exoplanetal determination, dual orbital constellations, and exoplanetal diagrams.

content.text: The regionalist strategies of Graubünden architecture: from 1900 to the present. content.text: Design parameters and behavioural effects of ecologically oriented control systems: a case study-based study. This book therefore deals with the design possibilities of an ecologically oriented control system and its effect on the behavior in the company. content.text: Apparition, body, image: light darkness in painting and film. Common characteristic of the works from the painting of the early Renaissance and the film of the 1920s to 1940s is the perspective representation of physical and spatial structures. To what extent does the light darkness, also called chiaroscuro, evoke a consciousness for the living up of the image re-enacted? Nature is not only deceptively depicted in real terms, it is also the possibility of its experience. The tension between two aspects of light darkness is found in both epochs: the sculpture on the one hand, which dissolves the figure from the image's ground and gives its static strength, plasticity. On the other hand, the picturesque dimension of the ground, which defuses the objectification, embeds the figure in the depth space and makes it appear moved by the dissolution of the body's boundaries. This is even more evident in the film by the actual movement. Thus, the chiaroscuro is described with its possibilities in an area that has so far been little developed in art history.

On the basis of a laboratory experiment with n=48 students, two versions of the robot Nao were compared with a tactile interaction ability (Nao with tactile interaction vs. Naohone tactile interaction). Tactile interaction means the reaction of the robot to the contact of humans. Recently, an online experiment with a social appearance was performed with a social interaction capability (Nao with tactile interaction vs. Naohone tactile interaction).

content.text: Sensory processing in neocortical networks : randomness, specificity and learning. Summary: Perception, decision-making and language are among the most complicated functions that emerge from the biological structures of the brain. One of the most important goals of neuroscience is to explain how the brain achieves its function with the help of its complex structure. In this work we want to contribute to the research of this question by studying the neuronal mechanisms of sensory processing in primary neocortical areas. We try to analyze the cortical circuit of this process and to provide information on the underlying computational principles.

content.text: Berlin in the feuilleton of the Weimar Republic : on cultural criticism in the short essays by Joseph Roth, Bernard von Brentano and Siegfried Kracauer. The feuilleton, also called cultural department, has so far received little attention from the cultural sciences. In particular, the »Zeitungsstadt« Berlin, however, produced a fascinating fund of feuilletonistic short prose during the Weimar Republic, which characterized the cultural characteristics of the metropolis. Eike Rautenstrauch examines exemplary short essays by Joseph Roth, Bernard von Brentano and Siegfried Kracauer, published in the feuilleton, which are enrolled in contemporary cultural discourses by means of architectural configurations. The synthesis of literary essay research and cultural history of feuilleton research is a methodological novelty in this form.
content.title_en: Berlin in the feuilleton of the Weimar Republic : on cultural criticism in the short essays by Joseph Roth, Bernard von Brentano and Siegfried Kracauer

content.text: The present work examines in a qualitative research setting the complex process of distancing and exiting from the extreme right 'movement', whereby five biographies of former members from different parts of the extreme right are analysed in detail. Of particular interest in the examination of the individual exit biographies are the basic patterns, difficulties and problem constellations that accompany this process. The work expands the knowledge about reasons and triggers that can lead to a distancing of extreme right scene. Confirmed among other things, are the assumption that monocausal explanations are not suitable to explain the exit process comprehensively and satisfactorily: the exit is accompanied and dependent by a variety of problem constellations and accompanying effects. This is by no means a quasi automatic process, at the end of which inevitably a successful departure from the extreme right scene is inevitable.
content.title_en: To the exit process from extreme right scene contexts

content.text: The optical properties of substrate materials for future cryogenic gravitational wave detectors. Since the construction of gravitational wave detectors (GWD) began in the 1960s, the sensitivity of the detectors has been increased by several orders of magnitude. To the continuous optimization of existing detectors, a major step is being taken to further increase sensitivity by using cryogenic test masses. Silicon is considered as a material with best prospects for use in future European GWD. This leads to open questions about material properties at cryogenic temperatures. The aim of this work is to obtain a better understanding of the optical absorption in silicon. Besides the heat input by optical absorption, temperature fluctuations can also limit the sensitivity of a GWD. Temperature fluctuations cause thermorefractive noise via the refractive number. An exact calculation of the thermorefractive noise fails to determine the temperature dependence of the refractive number of particles and makes it necessary to perform an extrapolation of this at present. In order to close this gap and to perform precise calculations, a measuring system is set up to determine the frequency of the radiation of the radiation.
content.title_en: Optical properties of substrate materials for future cryogenic gravitational wave detectors

content.text: 2-blocks with defect groups with exactly three involutions. In the modular representation theory, group algebras are examined over bodies whose characteristic p is a prime number. The group algebra then decays into a direct sum of so-called p-blocks. In the study of the structure of the blocks a number of invariants is of interest. The most important of these invariants is the defect group of the block, which often allows conclusions to be drawn on further properties, such as the number of irreducible characters. This work examines the structure of 2-blocks for the class of defect groups with exactly three involutions. Here the focus is on such defect groups with non-trivial automorphisms of unradical order, which were classified by Craven and Glesser. The *-construction of Broue and Puig proves to be a powerful tool in the analysis for complementing and improving classical methods. In addition to the calculation of blockin variants, the important open assumptions of Brauer, Olsson, McKay and Alper are verified to the 2-block groups of defect groups.
content.title_en: 2-blocks with defect groups with exactly three involutions

content.text: Ant. Lafreri Formis Romae : the publisher Antonio Lafreri and his print production. The printer and print dealer Antonio Lafreri (ca. 1512? 1577) was one of the most successful image producers of the 16th century in Italy. His Roman workshop produced numerous large-format copper engravings and etchings on a wide variety of topics. His range included Roman antique and modern monuments, maps, ornaments, portraits and works of contemporary religious and mythological painting as well as illustrations on scientific treatises. This work first examines the entire production of the image publisher and examines the continuous thematic expansion of his programme as well as innovative sales strategies that contributed to the continued success of the workshop and the widespread dissemination of the engravings. Over 400 prints are gathered in a comprehensively illustrated catalogue, which were found in Lafreri's offer and which impressively illustrate the versatility of the available pictorial material in the 16th century.
content.title_en: Ant. Lafreri Formis Romae : the publisher Antonio Lafreri and his print production

The key component of the audience is virtual people, with them being as realistic as possible and intended to act. This raises a central question: What are the characteristics of a real audience and what do people do when they sit in front of a speaker? Two studies were conducted to answer this question. The first exploratory study deals with experts in communication training and VR. Seven experts were interviewed both about the role of audience adaptation, interaction, and group dynamics as well as about technical application possibilities in virtual reality. The results show that communication training programs require high audience adaptations and interactivity possibilities. In order to complement the results, a training seminar was observed. The results of the observational framework of a discussion session are analysed by the two study methods of a discussion.
content.title_en: Development of a virtual audience concept for public speaking training in immersive virtual environments

content.text: Phenotypic heterogeneousity in bacterial populations: a mathematical study. Summary: Heterogeneity is a phenomenon widely used in nature. Despite its homogeneous environment and identical genetic material, various living organisms, from microbes to mammals, have developed a variety of life forms. Unlike genetic heterogeneity, produced by differences in genetic material, this form is called phenotypic heterogeneity. Initial observations of phenotypic heterogeneity date back at least to the 70's as the paper "Non-genetic heterogeneousity: chance in a single cell", by Spudich and Koshland (1976) describe this phenomenon. Since then, scientists have been trying to find explanations for these observations. Up to now, some mechanisms that lead to phenotypic heterogeneity have been identified, from which two of the theoretical aspects of this work are examined. We investigate (i) intracellular fluctuations leading to stochasticity at the level of individuals and (ii) a specific model describing the cell-type of the individual actions that lead to individual phenotypic heterogeneity.
content.title_en: Phenotypic heterogeneousity in bacterial populations : a mathematical study

A fast, parallelized and quantitative concentration measurement of metabolites is one of the major challenges of analytical chemistry. Natural sensor systems for metabolites are predominant in macromolecular biology – these biological macromolecules have been created to optimally process metabolic information for the benefit of the cell. content.text: The Volkshaus of the workers' movement in Germany: Community buildings between everyday life and utopia. The Volkshause are the ?built heritage? of the social democratic workers' movement. With its community buildings, it created its own ?proletarian public sphere? as a counter-project to the ?bourgeois public sphere?. The meeting places and organizational centers were simultaneously venues of proletarian culture, education and sociality. Also, at the beginning of the 20th century, the Volkshaus played a considerable role in urban and social discourse. It was a projection surface for a variety of community designs. The study presents the varied history of this type of building against a broad historical background. The architecture of the buildings is analysed exemplarily in the context of the architectural currents of modernism. A catalogue covering over 300 entries reconstructs the existing stock of the Volkshause in Germany from 1890 to 1933 using extensive source material.
content.title_en: The People's House of the Workers' Movement in Germany: Community Buildings Between Everyday Life and Utopia

content.text: The model of the retraction behaviour in the padpolitur. In the context of this dissertation, a model is presented which allows prediction of the retraction of material in the padpolitur of surfaces. It allows prediction of the retraction of material on the basis of physical parameters. The calculation is designed for any surface geometry and provides location-dependent retraction functions. The model includes the geometry of the workpiece, i.e. the resulting change of the retraction function is an integral part of the simulation. This represents a significant improvement to commercially available polishing machines, which partly work with fixed retraction functions. Among the variable parameters considered are the local flow of the workpiece surface, the geometry of the tool, the speed of the tool and the force on the tool. The comparison of real polishings with the results of the simulation provides a high match with deviations in the range of 10% and below. The strong position dependence of the retraction traces in the retraction of the relapse is equally reflected in the simulation polish.
content.title_en: Modelling the removal behaviour in pad polish

content.text: The influence of the coordination of trace elements in silicatic and aluminosilicate melts on elemental distribution processes in magmatic systems. The knowledge of the local structure of rare earth elements (SEE) in silicatic and aluminosilicate melts is of fundamental interest for the geochemistry of magmatic processes, especially when it comes to a comprehensive understanding of the distribution processes of SEE in magmatic systems. It is generally accepted that the SEE distribution processes of temperature, pressure, oxygen fugacity (in the case of polyvalent cations) and crystal chemistry are controlled. However, little is known about the influence of the melt composition itself. The aim of this work is to establish a relationship between the variation of the SEE distribution with the melting composition and the coordination chemistry of this SEE in the melt. To this end, melt compositions of prowatke and clamp (2005) have been used, which show a significant change in the distribution coefficients between titaniumite and melt exclusively as a function of the melt composition, as well as haplogranitic and haplobasic fusion of the melt.
content.title_en: The influence of the coordination of trace elements in silicatic and aluminosilicate melts on element distribution processes in magmatic systems

In the case of the conversion of β-alanine under activation by iminium chloride, the amino acids (aluminum, β-alanine, L-lysine) are also found in the amino group. content.text: The design of travelling-wave tubes with folded-waveguide delay lines. In this work, the design, modeling and simulation of novel touring field tubes are treated with folded rectangular hollow conductors as delay lines (VZL). Such VZL for applications in Q-Band is designed, manufactured and electrically measured. Models for such VZL are refined, expanded and implemented into an existing beam-wave interaction software. This software is also modified to enable a more efficient prediction of the tube amplifier. A convergence study is carried out and a comparison with established software packages verify the method. In this work the design, modeling, and simulation of novel travelling-wave tubes with folded-waveguide (FW) delay lines are addressed. An FW delay line for applications is designed, managed, and electronically characterized. Delay outline models, processed in the assembly.
content.title_en: Simulation and design of traveling-wave tubes with folded-waveguide delay lines

content.text: Access to the software components of the Google search engine according to Art. 102 TFEU. The European Commission has been conducting several antitrust proceedings against Google, a search engine operator for several years. The aim is to illuminate the extent of the company's market power and to sanction any abuse of market power. However, there is no comprehensive investigation to see whether competition in the search engine sector can not possibly be encouraged by granting Google's competitors access to Google's algorithms and data sets. The work links aspects of computer science, internet economy and media antitrust law and, in light of the prohibition of abuse of Article 102 TFEU, is dedicated to the question of the extent to which competitors in the search engine sector should gain access to Google's algorithms and data sets of market rulers. In this regard, it comes to an independent dogma of market power abuse by "absolute business refusal" in the context of European case law, under critical assessment of the Essential Facilities doctrine.
content.title_en: Access to the software components of the Google search engine under Art. 102 TFEU

A conceptual model of trust in SOOC offers a plausible extension of the research on trust in communication science, which focuses on the users as the starting point of attribution. Traditional, communication-scientific research traditions, which deal mainly with the credibility of the media, are replaced by a user-centered approach, which can grasp the specifics of SOOC. In the functionalistic sense, trust in systems takes the function of reducing complexity and thus enables actions under risk. Example of risky actions is the use of online co-location portals here.

content.text: Aesthetics, politics and Shia representations in contemporary Iran. In 'Aesthetics, Politics and Shia Representation in Contemporary Iran', Christian Funke shows the interdependencies of politics, protest and Shia materiality in the Islamic Republic. The book presents vividly and multi-layered how the 2009 protests and the 'Green Movement' were linked with broader discourses on democracy, identity, history and present, as well as religion and politics. Funke's argument is based on interviews and intensive field research and covers a wide range of topics ranging from colours to banknotes to urban spatial planning. Funke offers a new approach to the theory and methodology of religious aesthetics and sheds a new light on the 'Green Movement' by exposing the Islamic resources through which its protest articulated
content.title_en: Aesthetics, Politics and Shia Representations in Contemporary Iran

content.text: The declaration of will is a central term of the General Part of the BGB, and the problem of the declaration of will attributed to it has been with the BGB since its entry into force. The investigation develops answers to the questions whether the declaration of will is to be recognized, which means acknowledgment and according to which criteria is to be attributed, by drawing on relevant ideas from the analytical philosophy. It is explained that the declaration of will is a tû-tû concept. It is further shown that the calculation is based on constitutive rules. Differences are made between the legal and the linguistic calculation of the declaration of will. The legal calculation is based on constitutive accounting standards. In the context of the linguistic allocation, the difference between the allocation by virtue of the conventional meaning of the used signs and the assignment by means of conversational implicatures is explained.
content.title_en: The Declaration of Will attributed : Existence, Structure and Criteria

content.text: Memories written in stone: traces of the past in medieval church building culture. For the first time, the material, spatial and design relics as well as references of the buildings to their history are collected, systematically arranged and finally placed in a holistic architectural historical context. content.text: The use of the standard distilled food sample is complicated by the use of the standard distilled food sample. Chemical analysis is essential for many areas of application of the life sciences. High requirements for reliability and accuracy are placed on the methods used. In addition, factors such as the time, personnel and financial effort as well as the suitability for the examination of samples of high chemical complexity play an important role in the evaluation of the analysis methods. A method with high potential for the use in the life sciences represents the surface-reinforced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). However, the low reproducibility and negative influence of the sample matrix on the results present obstacles to the application in routine analysis. To meet these challenges, experimental factors have to be addressed as well as the data evaluation. The central topic of the dissertation is the quantification of low molecular substances in complex sample matrices with the help of SERS spectroscopy. To address these challenges, an experimental approach adapted to the respective application area has been measured as a robust sample method.
content.title_en: Robust detection and quantification of low molecular substances by means of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy

content.text: Security at the station: Monitoring measures to prevent terrorist attacks. The prevention of terrorist attacks is a highly topical and practical topic. The use of novel technologies in particular should recognise the danger before its emergence and prevent potential damage. In this work, selected security measures of the danger for terrorist attacks at stations are examined for their compatibility with fundamental rights and legal requirements. The subject of the investigation are the classic video surveillance, the registration of the registration plate, the intelligent video surveillance and the use of drones, body scanners and other capable detectors. Although the new technical possibilities often contribute to data protection, the existing legal bases in most cases are not sufficiently determined and disproportionate for the use of new technologies. For this reason, the author has developed legal bases based on its investigation results that enable the use in these cases. / »Security on Train Stations« -- The work explores variable security systems to defend terrorist attacks on train stations wherever they are compatible with fundamental rights in the detail,
content.title_en: Security at the station: Monitoring measures to counter terrorist attacks

content.text: Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) : Legal issues concerning the use of employee-owned mobile devices in the company. The use of mobile IT devices is hardly to be thought away in private and working life. While previously a clear separation between private and service-based IT devices prevailed, these limits are becoming increasingly blurred. More and more workers no longer want to do without the use of their private mobile devices in the workplace, but rather do private communication and service tasks from a single device. Discussed and summarized this trend is under the slogan »Bring Your Own Device« (BYOD). -- Christine Monsch is dedicated to the problem of what legal requirements a BYOD conception and its design must be fulfilled in order to ensure a legally effective use of private devices in the company. The focus is on work-related aspects such as cost and liability issues, working time regulations and co-determination rights of the works council. The author also analyses the abundance of telecommunications and data protection issues as well as the licensing issues and regulations of the company.
content.title_en: Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) : Legal questions concerning the use of employee-owned mobile devices in the company

content.text: Evidence maps in the evaluation and communication of uncertain evidence situations: the case of "synthetic nanoparticles". Evidence Maps (EM) are tested for the first time on health-relevant effects by synthetic nanoparticles (SNP). It is shown that the method to scientific standards appropriate evaluation and graphical representation of unsafe nanotoxicological evidence situations is well suited. It can support the education of non-expert decision-makers. The empirical test of the comprehensibility of EM for lay people shows that the graphics are more of a more unilateral argumentation than narrative texts, but not conflicting evidence – even if the pro-risk arguments are weak. Nevertheless, the open presentation of uncertainties in the expert evaluation has a positive effect on the comprehensibility – the conflict aversion is therefore stronger than the uncertainty version. EM can support the clarification of uncertain health risks through SNP as online information and as ppt presentations at information events.
content.title_en: Evidence maps in the evaluation and communication of uncertain evidence situations : the case of "synthetic nanoparticles"

content.text: Middleware to support architecture-driven game development: Optimization of development effort for browser-based MMOGs. Game development is an extensive project and affects a wide range of disciplines. This provokes the question of redundancy, especially in the field of software development. With a focus on the realization of browser-based Massively Multiplayer Online Games, architectural characteristics for the provision of typical communication infrastructures are identified in this work, which can be found in different approaches. Using a realized middleware, for derivation and generic provision of an infrastructure, the effort to develop a game idea can be reduced to concept-related, technology-independent elements. Using the COCOMO II cost model, seven game concepts are analyzed, statements on effort development are presented and the possibility to avoid effort in the implemented middleware demonstrated.
content.title_en: Middleware to support architecture-driven game development : Optimization of development effort for browser-based MMOGs

content.text: Private and administrative enforcement in European state aid law: from indirect enforcement to cooperation principle. Whether national courts are bound by the classification of a measure as aid by the EU Commission in its opening decision is a matter of two problems: firstly, the relationship between private and administrative enforcement - competition actions based on the prohibition of implementation (Article 108(3) of the TFEU) are part of the private enforcement - and secondly, the classification in the enforcement of Union law. The Member States' courts are involved in the enforcement of Union law. The cross-cutting scope of these two problems lies in this investigation. In order to clarify this, a comparison with European antitrust law is drawn and the legal nature of the opening decision is analysed. The Member States' courts are not bound by the opening decision, but are subject to a prohibition of deviation from the principle of loyal cooperation. content.text: The Federal Government and the Länder pursue different interests in climate policy and the federal conflict management in a substantial way. The study traces the orientation and design of German climate protection measures in the period 1990-2014, using the three fields of action 'Renewable energies', 'Emission rights trade' and 'Building energy efficiency' as an example. It shows first of all why the relationship between federalism and climate policy is tense and secondly, what productive possibilities, however, also what limitations arise for effective federal climate policy. The analysis framework developed in the work enables the diversity of conditions in the associated party political, federal and European arenas to be mapped and, over the various conflict cases, explain overarching processing patterns and strategy options.

An appropriate spatial-time distribution of water resources is, in turn, an essential prerequisite for the socio-economic and ecological functioning of the region. Therefore, an identification of the development and quantification of water resources is required to develop sustainable adaptation strategies through integrated land and water resources management. This is addressed by the upper Zambezi, as it is to be considered as characteristic for many other catchment areas in southern Africa. content.text: God in the streets of Guayaquil: the interaction between public space and religion. This work, based on the case study Guayaquil in Ecuador, was devoted to the interaction between religion and public space. This was done using four research-led questions, which in detail were: (1) In what form does the religious in the public urban space appear in a secular society and how is this occurrence conditioned? (2) In what way does religious actors use public space or in what way is religion used in public space? (3) What consequences does a presence of religion in public space, which is ideally reserved for rationality, have for politics? (4) In what way does the simultaneous exposure of divergent world views in public space affect religious practice and religion?
content.title_en: God in the streets of Guayaquil : of the interrelationship between public space and religion

content.text: Neuropsychological studies on individual differences in emotion processing. Furthermore, the relationship between the estimated parameters and individual properties of emotion processing is examined, as well as the parameter stability beyond various emotion processing tasks, which result in individual response patterns. Finally, amplitudes from event-related potentials, specific amplitudes of the late positive complex, are identified as electrophysiological markers of the information accumulation rates estimated by the DDM.

content.text: Topologies of justice : a political-geographical perspective on the right to food sovereignty in Bolivia. In Bolivia, since 2009, attempts have been made to build a food-sovereign and post-neoliberal society and to free oneself from economic domination. In the context of this empirical study, which is based on two research stays in 2013 and 2015, the focus is on the state efforts, above all, civil society and small-scale peasant initiatives and activities. In this context, the questions leading to knowledge are raised as to how this dynamic is a political practice of self-determination and how spatiality or scale levels of content are demonstrated, used, produced or challenged.
content.title_en: Topologies of Justice : a political-geographical perspective on the right to food sovereignty in Bolivia

content.text: The functionality of the work certificate and reference system in the German-speaking and Anglo-American legal area: a comparative-legal economic assessment. The work provides a comprehensive analytical and synthetic representation of normative relationships between work certificate and reference systems in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, the USA and England and examines the impact of the legal framework conditions on the implementation of the respective legislative intention from a dogmatic, transactional and behavioural economic perspective. Within the scope of the legal comparison, material and procedural aspects in labour law, liability law and personality law are presented in detail. This also includes history, special features of the common law, compliance aspects, process cost factors and legal enforcement in the comparative countries as well as alternative suitability diagnostic personnel selection procedures such as integrity testing procedures and background checks in the social media area and data protection issues.

content.text: The use of the substance of the trial, which has been removed under §§ 154, 154a StPO, in the assessment of evidence and the assessment of penalties in criminal proceedings: an investigation from the perspective of the rule of law and procedural law. The latest developments in criminal procedure law are characterized by the criminal procedural interpretation doctrine of acceleration, effectivation and reduction. Against the background of this development, the provisions of §§ 154, 154a StPO are subjected to a comprehensive analysis of the maximum rate of acceleration of proceedings under criminal law and procedural law. However, the norms of §§ 154, 154a StPO limit the principle of legality of criminal proceedings based on considerations of opportunity and serve to concentrate the substance of proceedings. The public interest in a process-economic and resource-saving criminal procedure finds its limit where the acceleration aim leads to an infringement of the accused in his rights and the rule of law, although the sentence is certainly not applicable to the rule of law.
content.title_en: The useability of process material eliminated in accordance with §§ 154, 154a StPO in the assessment of evidence and criminal assessment in criminal proceedings: an investigation from a legal and procedural perspective

content.text: Models of Living: Interactions between physiology, biology and pathology from Boerhaave to Meckel. In a scientific theoretic discussion, the possibilities for describing preparadigmatic sciences in general and for medicine in particular are worked out through a model theory perspective. The models of Living are then identified as historically adult and correspondingly variable models of Living Beings are followed by their interaction with contemporary medicine to concrete actors. The interactions of Physiology, Biology and Pathology show the fundamental importance of the thinking figure of Living for theoretical and practical medicine in the modelling of concepts of Norm and Abnorm as well as health and disease. It is clear that the life of Science is only ex negativeo as a blind spot and thus only available as a model whose historical transformatability has fundamental meaning for medical concepts and practice.

content.text: Laser spectroscopy of uploaded bismutations for the test of quantum electrodynamics. The work deals with a test of quantum electrodynamics in strong fields with the help of laser spectroscopy of the basic state hyperfine structure of uploaded bismutations. The experiment was carried out and evaluated at the ESR storage ring of the GSI Helmholtz Center for Heavy Ion Research in Darmstadt. Space charge effects were systematically investigated and the wavelength measurement of the laser was verified by absorption spectroscopy of iodine. Ion speed determined by an in-situ measurement of the electron cooler voltage could be reduced by more than one order of magnitude the greatest systematic uncertainty of the previous experiment. This showed the necessity of establishing a permanently installed high voltage measurement on the electron cooler, which was advanced in the context of the work. The specific difference determined from the measured wavelengths deviates so significantly from the theoretical prediction that none of the investigated systematics is considered a cause of the deviation. In addition to doubts about the values from the theory, the literature value of the magnetic core moment of bismut-209 is cited as a possible cause and illustrated in the forecast, how this puzzle could be solved in the following experiments.
content.title_en: Laser spectroscopy of uploaded bismutations for quantum electrodynamic testing

content.text: From patient endurance to all-encompassing prevention: flu pandemices in the mirror of science, politics and the public. The Spanish flu from 1918-1920 claimed between 25 and 100 million lives. Subsequent pandemics did not reach nearly this dimension. From 1997 the possibility of a further influenza pandemic was extensively communicated. Subsequently, billions of euros were mobilised to counter this threat. However, the feared major damage event remained. In addition to a historical examination of influenza, the re-update and rememoration of the topic of influenza has been traced since the end of the Spanish flu. The fundamental thesis is that discursive processes shape the perception of influenza. Discourses feed on memories of previous pandemics and influence both the generation of knowledge about influenza and its perception of risk. A corresponding discourse offers the possibility to fundamentally rethink risk perception and communication for influenza.
content.title_en: From patient endurance to all-encompassing prevention: flu pandemics in the mirror of science, politics and the public

content.text: The work deals with the fact that the contractual agreements between mobile phone companies and consumers are subject to ever higher consumer protection requirements. Due to the differences in power between entrepreneurs and consumers, regulatory intervention by the judiciary is useful and necessary. Nevertheless, under the guise of consumer protection, the principles of private autonomy cannot be completely ignored. A comprehensive evaluation of the predominantly sub-intergovernmental case law shows at which points the supposedly weaker position of the consumer is based on mere carelessness or indifference. The author always takes into account the numerous technical and legal details, as well as the civil law dogmatic foundations and general principles of civil law.
content.title_en: Individual consumer protection in mobile communications

content.text: The truly royal city: the empire in the imperial cities of Augsburg, Nuremberg and Lübeck in the late Middle Ages. In 'A truly royal city' Daniela Kah describes how the medieval empire or its representatives, such as the king, were experienced and perceived for the contemporary inhabitants and visitors in the imperial cities of Augsburg, Nuremberg and Lübeck. First, the award of royal privileges led to large-scale representative construction projects in the cities that made the empire so recognizable in everyday urban life. From the 13th century onwards, the cities increasingly applied symbols and signs in the urban space that visualise their self-image. To be "immediately part of the empire?" or "privileged from the empire?" became an important reference point due to its political, economic and prestige-enhancing importance, which led to the permanent presence of the empire in the imperial cities.
content.title_en: The truly royal city: the empire in the imperial cities of Augsburg, Nuremberg and Lübeck in the late Middle Ages

content.text: The use of churches since the 1960s. The use of church buildings continues to decline in Western Europe. To preserve the Christian peasantry, the conversion of churches seems to be a tried and tested means. However, a new use of churches brings with it various challenges in an ideal and historical respect. The current problem has a prehistory after 1960 in the GDR and the Netherlands, which shows how demanding a sustainable, monument-friendly church re-use is. Eva Schäfer not only presents a critical history of church conversion, but also addresses the conversion processes of selected examples. It also establishes connections between the international church building discussion in the second half of the 20th century and the converted profanations of this period.
content.title_en: Re-use of churches : discussions and results since the 1960s
